i just moved to the area and have a new physician.  i saw him yesterday after having passed out in a store and getting an ambulance to st margaret's er. i was there 7 hours. they took an ekg and gave me one bag of fluids.  doc was shocked that they did not take at least a ct scan since i am post-stroke and this was my 3rd episode of syncope.  doc said avoid them if possible, but ok for imaging. he said he would never admit me there for anything overnight, especially surgery.

i was sent to the emergency room by my doctor. i had a very bad migraine and a blood pressure of 190/120. doc was concerned about a possible stroke and wanted my blood pressure to be brought down. i arrived at the emergency room at 1:30 pm. they immediately took my blood pressure which was 190/124. they immediately gave me an ekg, urine test, head ct scan and blood test. at 2:15, they then sent me back to the emergency room waiting area where i remained until 8 pm when i gave up and went to a real hospital. if i wanted to wait for freaking hours to see if i would have a stroke i would've done that at home in comfort where there's food. i was given no medication to bring the pressure down i was just told "we're busy, the wait is longer than usual." yeah, i believe the long wait is usual and so is their incompetence. if you are not good at the abcs of heathcare then you shouldn't be in operation. thank god for the university of chicago, a real hospital. fransiscan health hospital is a piece of shit.

someone close to my heart was admitted here into the psychiatric ward. however, i would not recommend that your loved one ends up here. it is extremely hard to contact the patient as you are told incorrect phone hours and are given the run around. if you are lucky enough to reach them, they can't identify the patient you are looking for. in my opinion, that is horrible being that it is a ward and the nurses should be aware of who is on their unit. after repeating the patients name several times, the man who answered the phone, hung up on me. i kept calling, but did not have any success. this man kept hanging up on me. i was extremely frustrated with how i was being treated so i put in a call to the nurses station. a nurse picked up and was able to identify who my loved one was, but told me "____ is sleeping". this seems to be their go-to when they don't feel like getting the patient. 
secondly, according to the patient, the nurses assumed he left the building and "couldn't" find him, however he was in his bed the whole time. this seems extremely unprofessional to me. also, apparently the food is not great. this person described this facility as jail, granted it's not supposed to be an all-inclusive resort, but they should have their ish together. 

overall, our family is not impressed with this facility and would not recommend it to anyone!

felt like a sheep when i was here as a minor. you get zero one on one counseling. a lot of the support groups, other then like arts n crafts, were you just sitting there having to watch a movie abt mental health. i feel like thats lazy of the staff. many kids that go there might have adhd and other problems effecting their learning and if youre making them watch old mental health movies created before the 90s,, do you really think youre making them care? staff also picked favorites of the minors. its also unsanitary but i wont get into that

i was at summit oaks on christmas eve morning. after reading these reviews i was extremely discouraged, but i was also desperate for immediate help with my 13 year old son. i decided to go there in person instead of letting these really bad reviews guide me. i wanted to see for myself what it was like. the location is very nice. every staff member was courteous, empathetic, supportive and professional. there are inspirational letters posted in the waiting area along with coffee and tea. we got a five hour evaluation and excellent direction on what to do immediately to help with my son's behavioral issues. he did not get admitted, but if they had admitted him i would not have been worried. i believe he would have been in good hands. we also were given free lunch and the food was fine. fresh turkey sandwich, graham crackers, an orange and an apple juice. if you are considering going here and you are local, i recommend you go talk to them. i am glad i did.

my grandson has not been feeling well for the past few days. we had brought him to the er late at night and was checked in quickly. the hospital was very clean. the staff was kind when checking in. he was then taken in to do his vitals shortly after and then to his room to wait to see the doctor on duty. we were then greeted by dr. richard tan who had listened to our concerns and went straight into running tests on him. dr. tan's assist, sgt calderon was very kind and very helpful while we were waiting for the tests to be complete and to wait for the results. dr. tan was very thorough in assisting my grandson. he had even stayed in contact with the pediatrician on call as well which had made us feel better with some of our concerns. once all of the concerns were met, dr. tan had informed us that my grandson's medicine would be available in the pharmacy at 1:20 a.m. when we had completed our visit. we were pleasantly surprised and happy that we were able to obtain his medication right away so that we could give it to him. overall, oir visit to this hospital was awesome! mahalo to everyone who assisted us with our visit.

is this place even open?  no one answers the phone, fax number doesn't work.  left on hold by an answering machine for 20 minutes then hung up on. no answer, time after time.  if this is government healthcare we should all be terrified.  i was trying to forward medical records for one of their patients from another hospital. shocking disregard for patient care.

by far the worst experience ive ever had in an er room in all of long island ! came here for chest pains, and waited threee hours to be seen . once i was seen it took another 1.5 hours just to get my blood drawn . then another 1.5 hours for the results . all of this for the pa to come back and tell me all of the blood work came back great, but my ekg didn't look normal . why wait 6 hours later to tell me this , when the first thing the lady did at registration was take my ekg ...

went here to visit our friends who got a baby girl. campus is no doubt big enough with many departments and enough outside parking too. however not so clear indication about which way to go to visit any department. we had to ask multiple places to reach to the labor ward. atleast staff on the counters were welcoming and helpful on asking them questions.

also, our friends told that medical staff were just fine. they didn't had doctor available and with just 1 nurse my friend did delivery. i would say little bit of carelessness from staffs end.

just delivered my baby on 1/18/20. although my delivery was unexpected and fast (checked into l&d at 8:26pm and had my baby at 8:57pm) the delivery team was quick to act and bring her into the world. poor doctor barely had time to get ready before he had to come catch baby. 

this was my second time delivering a baby at this hospital and i've never had anything negative to say about their maternity ward. everyone is always available if i needed anything and weren't pushy when it came to certain things (bottle/breast feeding, vaccines, etc) 

cary, the night nurse was such a sweetheart. she made sure she we were well taken care of before she left her shift. another nurse told me she even waited to go home so she could be the one to help us give our baby her first bath, and did this while off the clock. the whole team we encountered were just wonderful!

absolutely would recommend having your baby at this hospital!

i had my endo surgery done here, they took really good care of me. the wait time was unnecessarily long, not sure why they make you arrive 2 hours before they'll even call you up. one of the nurses didn't know the medication she was giving and all the nurses had never heard of my form of birth control. i'm really glad my surgery was smooth, 30 minutes in-out, and i'm delighted they didn't kill me like all these horror stories you hear.

please consider an alternative er room as i would hate to see anyone ever experience what i went through. they truly have no concern for your well being or pain. it's just another annoying day at the office for this team and er staff. 

it's very sad to see people who choose a career in caring for people when in pain and distress, completely disregard their medical needs and show zero obligation to help. 

do you research and please consider a different er room ahead of time as when the emergency comes that is not the time to research and abrazo arrowhead is not where you want to go. i swear on my life.

this is unreal  i can't believe this is still a hospital worst hospital i ever been to in my life the nurses can give two craps about you. they throw you in the waiting room in the back night nurse older lady. worst nurse god put on this earth she seemed like she didn't wanna be here and didn't even care about the patients

doctors are decent. front desk, office personnel and billing process are horrible. good place for employees to pass the buck to the next person when you have a question or complaint that's it's someone else's department. three previous visits only one was without incident.  had a 3:30 appt today and i'm still sitting here waiting after walk-ins and later appointments have been seen. no updates or contacts that i didn't have to ask myself. no common sense that if it's after hours for your workplace you're not going to get a call from them.  chastised for not giving information they didn't ask. won't see me apparently without talking to my employer when it's after business hours so i'm sitting in the middle of a flu season (their words) waiting room of coughing patients probably taking in the germs that will get me the flu where i will have to come back and go into the same crap routine as i've done twice before with no real assessment except i must have allergies for the first time in my life and for an injury i had an appt for two hours ago. today, if i could give them a zero, i would. and these people are actually taking care if people in an urgent care capacity that are depending on them to have some wits about them. i'm glad i'm not sitting here with something life or death because i'd probably be dead. oh, but they made sure i signed off on their coronavirus paperwork alright. probably to protect their own health. 

look at that one star in the review and think zero stars. don't be real sick because if you are pick a different place than the hunters creek loop advent centra care.

the kissimmee location is god awful! mri  ordered for family member at 11:00 pm satuday  and finally taken at 4:30 sunday afternoon. when inquired on a possible time everyone kept shrugging shoulders stating no idea but 3 people ahead. amazing how it was always 3 ahead from 17.5 hours from the time of order.  nursing staff did not come in each hour and instead let hours go by before making a quick appearance. iv bag ran out, seemed to be a hassle to even get pain medicine. hard to get any any decent respect and care for my family member. amazing though the person in the other bed was seen multiple times each hour by a nurse or 2 nurses at 1 time. the care and attentiveness was outstanding for them. thought was they were all the same ethnic back ground,  while my family member was not. it seemed and appeared that obvious. to even give a 1 star was more than generous for this horrific time here.stay clear and go to orlando health facilities such as dr. phillips.

my father-in-law was transferred here last night from clinton memorial for faster treatment. he was supposed to have test done at 12:30 pm. he could not eat before these test and was already very hungry this morning at 10am. 12:30 came and went with no reason for the delay it's now 4:05 pm and the still have not done the test. poor communication with family. he has had nothing to eat or drink since yesterday at 5:30pm now.

i had c diff (and got it again due to recurrence as of this moment). it was a 7 hour wait at this place when they got me a private ed room. the staff were all kind. only concern i have is that i suspected i had c diff a few weeks ago due to explosive diarrhea and abdominal cramping. they wanted to do a urine test and not a stool sample on me at first. eventually after me pushing the envelope, they accepted a stool sample (it was c diff positive). their ct imaging people are obviously a separate entity and my bcbs insurance denied the ct scan and the radiologist charged me over $500 for that scan (pitts radiology). they sent me home with a prescription for flagyl and other meds. let me make it clear: every healthcare institution should always be following the latest evidence based practice guidelines to ensure optimal recovery and a reduced risk if recurrence. this is something this hospital failed to do. flagyl killed it off and then a week later without the antibiotic (i had finished 14 days of it at this point), the c diff returned. surprise! i graduated nursing school and even i know better about keeping up to date on ebp guidelines. if it's the hospital policy to treat c diff with flagyl, someone needs to either get fired or do extensive ebp research. honey, nobody is using flagyl anymore. 

i ended up having to go to an urgent care center and explaining the situation and this time i am on vancomycin.  even the doctor at the urgent care clinic stated that flagyl is no longer the #1 drug for c diff treatment. this costed me a lot of money between er and the urgent care. 

beware that this er may not be up to date on their evidence based practices and may treat you with outdated and ineffective methods. consider yourself warned.

after having outpatient knee surgery on 11 november and having paid them my patients portion for the surgery. a tad over $4000.00. come to find out bcbs paid my bill in full due to me reaching my out of pocket at another hospital. i have the eob to prove it. i have been after them for a month to refund my patients portion with out success.  one excuse after another. all i can say is beware paying anything up front with these individuals.

review: staff are great, attentive and caring, management listens to concerns as well. my mom is currently getting her physical therapy and my family is very thankful especially for therapists - amir and francis who works with my mom everyday in getting her back to her baseline. they are very compassionate, caring, patient and fun to work with and really dedicated in what they do. i would definitely recommend this place!

my mother was a patient here. the nurses were good but administration and management are horrible. they promised us we can transition from ltac to sub acute with no problems when she was ready. this was not the case. once my moms insurance was running out for ltac they rushed us out with little warning and the case manager janice didn't work with us before initiating the process. they wouldn't let us stay at their sub acute because they only had x number of respitory beds.  this was something they failed to tell us in the beginning

we pleaded with them and warned them it wasn't safe for my mom to leave and asked them to honor their agreement. they admitted they handled the discharge poorly but only offered a "sorry". they also admitted that their reps make promises that aren't true often.

 my mom died the next day at the new facility.  case management here only sees patients as numbers or "open beds". they have little regard on how they affect patients and families. stay clear of janice, ask for another case worker if you decide to go there.

i regret transferring my father to this facility. my father had a trach, feeding tube and was bedridden. he would use the call button and nobody would come for 15-20 minutes. we capped my dads trach so he could talk for a minute and he said the nurse just comes on a speaker and since he can't talk, he doesn't get any help. i personally hit the call button while i was in his room and sure enough, the nurse came on the speaker. it took them over 10 minutes to come in his room even though they heard silence. the nurse coverage on weekends is ridiculous. so many call lights on when you look down the hall and nobody helping the patients. on two separate occasions i could hear patients screaming for help so i had to track someone down. i filed a complaint with the supervisor. this is suppose to be a hospital yet there isn't a doctor on site at all times. what hospital doesn't have a doctor on site? i spoke to the ceo on several occasions. he tried to make things right for my dad but really didn't take me seriously when i told him he had neglect going on in his hospital. he clearly thought i was just emotional. i had to follow up every day and night to make sure my dad got his medication. he had a few great nurses and a few terrible ones. i also called the kindred complaint hotline about a doctor not being on site. case managers were helpful and didn't minimize my concerns which i appreciated. my dad made the decision to stop all treatment and he passed away there. i would try to avoid this place at all costs.

from my arrival at the er bed until i finally had the iv, at least 2 hours had passed. i was vomiting in this whole period and lost track of how many times this happened. there was nothing left there, only the reflex of throwing up and at this point. i got so dehydrated at this point that (believe me) i could not even swallow anymore because my tongue and throat were too dry to allow this action to happen.

my question for the staff of this hospital is: given how many bad reviews you received through yelp beyond mine (not even considering the ones they might get outside here), would you bring a loved one to this er or would you be sensible enough to search for another hospital?

i came back to the er here recently in what was one of the worst decisions i could have made. i should have known better after my last visit.

what i experienced in icu here still gives me nightmares.

i waited over 8 hours after being triaged, with obvious symptoms of advanced pneumonia, including coughing up blood, shortness of breath and rapid breathing, severe and extreme confusion--all without anyone paying attention.

eventually, i started losing consciousness and apparently had gone into sepsis after waiting to be treated for so long.

the only reason i probably survived was that a hospital administrator (i believe her first name was sandra) happened to be nearby and intervened. she was horrified upon finding out how long i'd been waiting, and paged her medical director to see me. he showed up, then walked out when i had to go to the bathroom while talking to him. i forgot his name, but she fired him that same night after he refused to come back, and replaced him with dr. mathew.

upon my admission, a team separate from icu was assembled and confirmed a primary diagnosis of acute multi-focal pneumonia. despite this, a full course of antibiotics wasn't started until long after i'd been transferred out of icu. i was stabilized and given oxygen--for nearly 4 days--while still coughing up blood! dr. mathew was now supervising both critical care and icu, so there was no one watching over things most of the time.

now, i know how unbelievable it may sound, but my treatment was abruptly cut off and i was suddenly transferred to out of icu as a result of my bed in icu literally being sold to someone else.

this patient somehow walked into icu with his family and a lawyer, threatening to sue for previously poor treatment; they also offered an alternative: a huge sum of money just to get proper treatment. i overheard the panicked conversation, since my room was closest to the icu entrance, and all rooms there are kept open.

i was rushed out of icu under these truly bizarre circumstances.

this late-night, hushed maneuver must have resulted from a decision being approved at some high level by hospital administration. whether the motivation was money or fear of legal repercussions, putting patient care last is not only antithetical to the hippocratic oath, it's downright shameful, and the move was very likely illegal under state regulations.

i was so shocked by what i'd heard i initially said nothing when the nurse manager walked in and started to clear my room for that patient. she was clearly ashamed while disconnecting my iv line and oxygen (with my spo2 still dipping under 40%), then covering me up with a full bed-sheet.

i finally said, "i guess my my room is being given to someone else." she responded, "i guess you know everything." i was then told "you always have friends here," before being quickly wheeled out.

as deathly scary as that was, things only got worse.

once out of icu and out of sight of the new patient, i was handed only a small plastic bag of oxygen to breathe from. arriving in a medicine wing, the nurses alarmingly asked why there was no equipment to provide proper flow of oxygen.

as i found out eventually, i was transferred to a wing for palliative care; someone in icu must have been aware of this, since a portable oxygen machine was left anonymously in a plastic bag outside my room.

the wing i was transferred to was essentially a death ward. my vitals were checked only a handful of times in several days. the nurses' only job seemed waking me every hour, on the hour, to make sure i wasn't dead--there was no monitoring! i managed to negotiate a transfer to the main floor, 9, where actual medicine was practiced.

days later, when the cdc came back with results on the culture icu sent them, confirming a particularly bad strain of pneumonia, a full course of augmentin--a common antibiotic--was finally started.

to summarize, i nearly died in the er for lack of proper attention and treatment; was stabilized then received practically no treatment other than oxygen in icu for several days; had my bed there sold to someone else; was transferred to a palliative care wing--a death ward--before negotiating my way out; then was kept on medical hold, with my life upside down in the outside world, for 11 days--when i could have finished treatment at home.

the staff may mean well, but there's something very wrong with this place. the higher-ups seem either completely out of touch, or at least entirely disinterested in patient care, outcomes, any level of comfort, or balancing the needs of patients with real-world obligations.

it seems there is one thing they are interested in--money.

i'd say this establishment lies somewhere between a third-world clinic and a mortuary. there were some redeeming qualities--after all, i walked out alive. sarcasm aside, i hope this review comes across as factual, because it is.

judge for yourself, but take heed, and for goodness' sake, pick another hospital.

i'm coming out of maternity leave for a few minutes to write what might be my favorite review of all time. st. luke's and all of the nurses there made my childbirth experience so wonderful that there aren't enough stars in the world.

we chose st. luke's because that's where my ob is located, and we were really impressed with the maternity floor. there were always a couple of babies in the nursery, but it never seemed too crowded. we also took their childbirth class and knew at that point that st. luke's was where we wanted to have our daughter. 

my due date was close to christmas, so you can imagine my surprise when my water broke at home on november 19th. we weren't really sure if it was the real thing, so we called the maternity floor at st. luke's. they are always available 24/7 for questions, which was so helpful leading up to my daughter's birth, especially in this case. the nurse i spoke with told me i needed to just come in so they could figure out what was going on, so after a lot of scrambling and throwing random items into a bag, we were on our way.

if you are in labor after normal hours, you enter through the er and they take you up to maternity. i got checked in, and after only ten minutes, the nurses confirmed that my water did break. surprise! from there, there were a few hours of relaxation and then an insane amount of chaos. my labor progressed so fast that my doctor couldn't even take the elevator; she had to run up the stairs. a few minutes later, my precious girl arrived. thankfully, i had my epidural about twenty minutes before that happened. i was so happy that my nurse encouraged me not to wait; her exact words were "it's not the time to be a hero." had she not encouraged me to get it when i did, i would have missed my window.

i cannot speak enough about the nurses at st. luke's. they calmed my nerves. they always made sure i had what i needed. they knew when i needed a joke, and when i needed to be left alone. they anticipated my needs and hard moments. they genuinely cared about my family, and took such wonderful care of my girl. what i appreciated the most was that they took her to the nursery to make sure i could sleep... i've heard nightmare stories of nurses wanting newborns to "co-sleep" in their mom's hospital room, and honestly the rest that they gave me made the first few nights at home bearable. 

the house pediatricians on staff were also incredible, and stopped by each morning to update us on our baby's health and answer all of our questions. the lactation specialist, pam, deserves her own five stars. having pam there was like having the world's most loving and supportive grandma in the room. she had my daughter breastfeeding in no time, and was so encouraging and loving. we wanted to bring her home with us!

i was sad to leave the hospital, and i feel like most people can't wait to get home. we are forever grateful for our experience at st. luke's, and they should never be overlooked when considering a place to have your baby!

other than that, i cannot believe how difficult of a medical experience ours was with this hospital.  no one should have to advocate as much as we did at every single step to make sure our loved one was receiving responsible medical, and the hospital was following their legal responsibilities.  now if i wanted a waitress, this would be the place.  we were constantly offered coffee and "room service".  however, for the main things they are responsible for (and charging a huge amount of money to provide)- medical care following laws and ethical standards- not so much.  the administration dismissed concerns time and time again, and at one point left us in a waiting room after they said they'd be right out (later sending a poor nurse that never could have addressed legal missteps).  

i mistakenly thought it would be different with their outpatient offices, but it's similarly been painful with an equal amount of advocating required.  i've been waiting 3 weeks for a call back from a manager at one of the offices.   

as a medical professional, i cannot for the life of me imagine what this experience would have looked like for someone who is not in the field, and didn't know how to advocate.

i'm just floored by all of this

any good reviews this hospital has were paid for by hilton head hospital, i am sure. worst hospital ever - doctors have no compassion or intelligence, narrow and small minded with no ability to think outside a box. not thorough at all and extremely rude. dr. bauer and dr. baker should both have their medical licenses revoked, and are a disgrace to the profession. condescending and arrogant with no right to be. nurses are the only decent thing about this hospital but unfortunately they take order from ignorant and inexperienced small minded idiots for doctors. rude, unkind, and dismissive. i was told by one doctor to "find god," after he spent about 2 minutes with me - this after i waited 2 hours to be seen. blood pressure monitor never worked, and no one brought me one that did, after i asked twice. horrible experience and because of their lack of follow through have caused many people to become sicker. friend almost died from a lung infection there due to lack of sanitation in their ventilator.

i was taken to the er at midnight on 12/15. i was scared and hoping for kind people to take care of me during my short visit. although i was given the necessary tests (no bloodwork though) and x-rays, i felt that my main nurse (i think his name was robert?) and my doctor, dr. snowman, made my visit very uncomfortable. i am a calm and very easy going person and treated everyone who helped me very kindly yet i was made to feel like i was a bother or a nuisance. i told dr snowman that my new gp, who i happen to like very much and who he had never heard of before, had recently run blood tests on me but that she didn't run a full panel. he looked at me and told me "yes she did". i told him again, calmly, that she didn't and again he told me that "yes, she did", like i was an idiot and didn't know what i was talking about, and further said that if she didn't that she was an inept dr and that i should find another one. i asked him if i could have an x-ray of my lungs because i've been having upper back pain that i thought might be related to my lungs and he said that the chest x-ray they just took included my lungs and that everything looked perfectly normal but he didn't bother to offer to show them to me. my fault for not insisting that he show them to me but a caring doctor would have offered. if, god forbid, i ever have to go to this er again i will insist that i not have dr snowman. i felt like the step child he never wanted. this was quite contrary to the wonderful things that that the tech who took my x-rays said about him. i was looking forward to meeting him and discussing the outcome of my tests with him and after he left my bedside i couldn't wait to leave. maybe he was having a bad night but my experience with him and my main nurse was an experience i wish i'd never had.

worst. vacation. ever. like, you hear those stories of going off with a hooker and waking up missing body parts? think that but no preliminary hooker fun times. came here, woke up with less liver than i started with. i hear rumors that sometimes people leave with more stuff in their body than before. even crazier, sometimes they get exposed to radiation and don't develop superpowers (although surviving is a sweet side effect).

in all seriousness though, aside from having food that is so bad it may be a violation of the geneva convention, i've always received wonderful care here. nurses do the heavy lifting of health care and the ones on 8a are superstars. rachel, amy, denise, ellen, mandy, heck, even had fantastic care from a student nurse named gianna. hospitals suck. you really should avoid them if you have that option. however, if you need top notch care, agh kinda kicks butt.

my hospital experience here was... ok. nothing terrible and no bad wait times. cafeteria was predictably bad but what do you expect in a hospital? no, what places this at 3 stars is that it took an in-person visit and several phone calls just to get my medical records released when i needed them. it should not be that difficult. if they hadn't dropped the ball on that it would have been 4 stars.

this is the worse hospital i've ever entered in my life. my son got sick while visiting the county, and we took him to the er here. we were treated by dr. william bennett. dr. bennett was very rude and very ignorant for a certified "professional." my son was tested for flu and strep throat. during our consult with dr. bennett, he had no clue what was wrong with my son, nor could he medically answer any questions i asked. he only guessed and gave his opinion, no medical response. he repeatedly told us to treat my son with tylenol and gatorade at home. dr.  bennett didn't provide and diagnosis, cause, or check symptoms. he became so irritated that he walked out of the exam room and said he had other patients. i informed him that i would be filling a formal complaint, and he replied, "go ahead." he was very unprofessional. he lacked compassion. he was impatient, inconsiderate, and incompetent with my toddler son. sadly, he was the only doctor on duty. 

if dr. bennett is any example of quality and professionalism for this hospital, i understand why the reviews are low and the locals travel to other counties for medical care. we waited over 3 hours for him to tell us gatorade, not even pedialyte and tylenol. i will never return to this hospital for care, never. 

disclosure: we recieved exceptional care and a medical diagnosis at another hospital, after leaving this hospital. 

i rated 1 star because that's the minimum. my actual rating is 0.

san francisco va has the best hospital care in the country.  the facility is a training hospital and so your care is going to be state of the art in every way. the doctors work together to coordinate your care and keep you in the loop at all times.  my husband has received care that kaiser cannot provide.

the staff is great. that is if you are gay and democrat. republicans were rudely met at the front lobby and advised that they would like the va across from "kings mountain" much better.  i noticed the place for the president was bare.  a vet told me the picture of obama was up far past his time. if i ever need meds again in california i will hold off till i get to idaho. just an old (vet) truck driver. if you go to the new one by the bay, tell them you are democrat.

over the couple of years of living in area , this has been the hospital for emergencies! and we have had quite a few emergencies and some of them have been handled superb and others horrible.  
the emergency room is a serious place to go and we always call first before coming. if we don't call first and go then, we may be in for a great wait. so we usually don't come unless we are seriously ill or injured. i found that coming in sick in the ambulance does not make us get seen quicker. sometimes depending on the illness or injury, you could be required to take more tests. and that may  take hours on top of hours. if you have a spouse or family member please  take them. it helps because sometimes they are not clear what they doing to you.  and sometimes you maybe too ill to remember. i repeat do not go alone to this part of the  hospital! 

now i am not fond of using the emergency room but i like using their other services here. their imaging and lab services are good. the staff at both locations there are very friendly and professional . they go out of their way to help patients . those individuals have made experience at st clare better. so i even appreciate the extra warm blankets in imaging . and the i appreciate the lady at the information desk giving my son a "chupa"  translated  lollipop to keep him quiet while he sits with his papi . 

 this hospital has more than just a hospital! it houses physical therapy and doctors offices inside which makes it so easy to park if you drive. and it is very convenient for the bus too.  it has a nice cafeteria too. we have used it! but it is never open for late night. but if you have an dr appointment , it is perfect to have  breakfast or  lunch there! they have great pancakes there! i have not had lunch yet. the people in cafeteria are ok. they can definitely cook the pancakes!

this review made me rethink about this hospital a bit. it is not  perfect but it is my closest hospital and when i call 911 the medics will take me here. and not all visits  will be the same.

from the time we entered the hospital we had the most wonderful experience.  my son had a surgery scheduled on a fri at 10 and he went back on time.
the checking in, signing paperwork all went smoothly. great staff

if i could give 0 starts i would. the emergency room can't find out what's wrong with my boyfriends lungs & his breathing so they tell us to call the actual hospital. right when the nurse picks up the phone she has a bad attitude & is very rude. no help at all when i'm telling her what the emergency room doesn't do for us... so great job st.clare hospital.

was here for severe hip/back pain 2 x in last 2 weeks.  ran same urine and blood tests ea time.  x-ray wasn't given till my 2nd time.  but wouldn't do mri?  said wasn't emergency.  and i have good insurance!  scary huh.
physician assnt tj both times referred me back to my primary dr.  wow.  i didn't even see a real dr. four hrs ea time there and two $75 copay's later.
told me was related to my prostate biopsy 3 months earlier.  2 weeks later now, got mri from my dr and it's ilopsoas tendinitis of hip.
would've been nice to get thorough tests weeks earlier.   in extreme pain now, and finally can start treatment.
unless you're dieing probably a waste of time here especially on night shift w tj.
place is clean and semi fast w some pretty descent staff.
but that's all that's good

the director of patient relations, keven weindt, was the least compassionate person regarding the waiving of my deductable, $85.00. the issue was that i was at the hospital only a few weeks earlier for the same reason- kidney stone. bc of their failure to suggest my severe pain might be a kidney stone trying to pass i found myself back there again. i did have even worse pain. however, had i known what to expect, i would have stayed home, less than a mile away. i was there again only bc i was scared, blind sighted by what was happening to me. a little sharing of info w/patient would have calmed me, in my own home. the stone passed bf i got tot he hospital, which by then i was so anxious, a pain of sorts still existed. while in their care, pain faded away. the worst was over. their docs, medical staff, labs, were paid by my insurance. why would i pay for a visit i could have avoided.
now they'll send their stock response this comment however, no changes will be made.
5 stars for support staff though.

i had to go to the er yesterday as instructed by my doctor.  i had a high risk of obstruction, inflamed intestines and more. having already had my laaa he intestines removed, we know there's a greater risk of complications. 

they took me in immediately and i was back in a bed within 10 minutes of entry. 

the nurses, doctors and medical staff were exceptional. i would highly suggest to everyone to trust this establishment and it's doctors. 

usually with invisible illnesses in my experience you can be brushed aside.   they actively listened to my concerns and did everything they could to get to the answers.  

the catscan staff were welcoming and calming as well. 

my nurse hannah was the best of the best.  and i've had my share of hospital stays.  she had tough competition. and she is the best of them all. 

this er was so exceptional that i am even bringing in treats and thank you letters to them on monday. 

i have been to a lot of hospitals with my diseases and none were this fast, helpful and kind. 

ps the hospital itself is new and gorgeous. i had a private room and not just curtains.

stay away!!!! 
i am so disappointed in hoag 
this is the second time they have not treated my family properly and made us feel like they were annoyed we went there... 

so here is the story:

my brother went in a few nights ago having difficulty breathing 
they treated him with a breathing treatment   and sent him home with medicine and told him he has the cold he has to let his body fight it

shame on hoag for not caring 
and they are suppose to be the best
very disappointed ...

we visit a lot of er's unfortunately. i won't get into the details of why, but suffice it to say, i can tell you some horror stories.  last night  after  suffering through abysmal service at uci in orange (well let's call a spade a spade and admit we received no service for four hours after coming in by ambulance (which despite our frequent er trips we basically never need to do), we went against medical advice and left to go to hoag.

we have also been fortunate enough to get excellent care at various hospitals both here at home and abroad in our travels, however the care and attention we received last night at hoag er was beyond comparison. they took our medical need seriously and responded with appropriate haste and concern. they were swift, focused and capable. i would almost never write a review for an emergency room but if you have to go, go to hoag. i also have to give a shout to dr. ricci and his staff (thanks hanna and dan!). thank you so much for taking my wife seriously and acting. you are by far the most impressive, compassionate and thoughtful er physician we have ever met. while i hope not to return to your er, i will cross my fingers that you are working if i ever do. thank you.

the staff there is s far less superior to the staff at newport.  the attitude and professionalism is truly lacking.  had a horrible er experience and have noticed the quality of care declining with apathetic personnel over the last 3-4 years.  shame on them.  nor living up to "christian" standards.  transferred to newport and the difference is like night and day.  

if you can, don't go there.

i took myself and my 6 year old here and were treated very unfair. we were in a car accident 24 hours prior. they took my sons vitals and felt his stomach.  then i was told that they were not worried about him. tywn the took my vitals and i got an xray of my neck. but ny head, neck, shoulders were also hurting.  i had surgery 9 days prior so i showed my nurse he saud it hurt cause it was time for stitches to come out. and sent us home. today i go see the surgeon who does an xray to find that the rods in my finger had moved down. this er did nothing to help me or my child. they were very wrong for this. now on my way to take my child to another er he still complaining of pain. thanks hoag for the great care
amazing service . very clean . very helpful and informative . lovely place . i would go here for sure

first time visit to this hospital. got a release without any proper treatment , medicines, prescription etc. the ailment still remains after the visit but we keep receiving bills after bills. bed sheet was dirty which got changed on complaint. doctor was not even able to understand the root cause of the problem. 
so far we have already paid around $2500 and today we have received a new bill of more $1280. patient is tired, unsatisfied , leaving back to their own country for proper treatment. this is the worst experience we ever had with any hospital. god knows how many more bills are lining up in queue which we will receive in another few days.
we were at hoag for a week. the care was great!  it is the cedars sinai of orange county!  i would definitely recommend this hospital!

i visited this hospital not too long ago today, and the front  desk lady said i had to go to urgent care or the emergency room. i share with her that the hoag at woodbury shared that i could  visit this location for non-emergency and non-urgent matters. the caucasian lady still did not budge. instead she checked her cell phone. even after sharing that i had a fever and severely painful throat, she still states that there were thousands of doctors and i had to go online and book an appointment that way. never in my life have i had this experience with a medical facility. she even went on to say, "are you in college? they can see you there." i told her i am not in college, and that this was my 2nd day off from being sick. 

i enjoyed my visit at woodbury, but the sand canyon location needs a new receptionist that cares about patients, does not turn  patients back who have painful symptoms, and who cares about the hoag medical group business. i would rate this location zero stars if it was an option on yelp.
this hospital sucks stick me with an iv and did not even do the test ! and huge stomach and they sent me home

i was pregnant and experiencing flu like symptoms, so i went to the er early one morning. the waiting room was empty and the staff were caring and got be back into a room right away! i was treated wonderfully! i felt like they were going the extra mile to make me feel comfortable and cared for! i highly recommend hoag irvine!

i drive here from lake elsinore because it is worth the adequate services you get in regards to your health. despite an hour drive, i still spent half the amount of time here at hoag irvine than i did at inland valley medical (who misdiagnosed me), and hoag irvines proper diagnosis was life saving, literally.  everyone here is so friendly and in good spirits, they don't appear to hate their lives or jobs like i experienced at inland valley. i can't recommend this place enough, i am so grateful for the entire staff and wish there was a way to go above making a google rating to praise this amazing facility and their crew. ( have also been here in the past, and although they've been busier at those times, the quickness of being seen and accurately provided for, there is no one or nothing else comparable to hoag irvine, er )

generally, i try to take negative reviews with a grain of salt.  i genuinely believe that people who write reviews really love a place or really hate it.  
my goodness though, the negative reviews of this place are actually... pretty spot on.  
please note that i am only reviewing the emergency room.  we went to the er because my 4 year old was having eye issues.  he was expressing that his eye hurt, and was walking a bit funny.  so my husband took him and his twin to the er. i went and met with them there. 
the one that was having the eye issues wanted it to be dark, so i put a jacket over his stroller so it can be dark. but it was obvious that he was not doing well.  his twin wanted to get out of the stroller, so he got out and was running around. there was a lady with a dog there. my boy did not attempt to touch the dog or anything. he just pointed to the dog and said, "dog" and was looking at the dog, kind of near the ground. (but again, not touching the dog or really near the dog). she kept saying to him, "the dog isn't friendly." but then, she kept insisting that it is a service dog. i have no issues with that and i genuinely have no issues with dogs. (i love animals). the concern that i had was that she kept insisting to me that the dog is "not friendly with kids" and "doesn't do well with kids."  ... aren't service dogs trained to be ok with people in general? since they are supposed to be servicing their person where ever the person is?   also, she was the one that decided to sit near us when she saw that we had two kids with us?  ok, whatever, we moved to the other side, because clearly, she wasn't friendly with kids.   also, i get it, this isn't the hospital's fault. this was just a cherry on top.  
anyway, we had been waiting for an hour, when i decided "let me at least ask how long it maybe..." now, let me be clear. i totally understand that they triage care. i totally do get that.  however, some guidance would be nice.  so i ask the lady who is sitting there. she says that she "can't answer that question" because they "don't go in order of people who came in." then, i asked, "i totally understand that.  can you give me something like an estimate? or someone that i can ask to get some kind of estimate?" she said, "no."  okay...  so i asked, "ok, is there any where else around here that we could go to?" she then said, "i can't help you look for a place, but you checked in but you might as well stay. but i can't help you." so... why are you there?  i then explained, calmly, that both of my children (again, they are four) have autism. so i was a bit concerned about how long they would be able to last without having a meltdown. (which no one wants...)  i wasn't asking for special treatment- just some kind of information. if it was going to be like, 30 minutes, we could go for a drive. (or i could call around to other places to see how long the wait would be ....)  any information would have been nice. but no, she said that she can't help me.  it was so unhelpful and so unempathic.  a man came back to the table, said nothing to me, and just smirked as i expressed, "ok, that was not too helpful, but thank you."  
i ended up leaving with my other kiddo and trying to get him to bed because it was wayyy too long to wait.  he was doing well, but i could tell he was getting tired.  the reason why i didn't want to do that is because i wanted to be there for my other kiddo to make sure he was okay too.  going to the hospital with them is noooo fun. (and i'm sure it isn't too fun for anyone else there either. lol)  
finally, my husband told me that 9:15, he got in to see the doctor (over 2 hours later). he waited for a while again.  it seems that the doctor was pretty helpful when he was finally able to see the doctor, but i'm not sure about that yet.  i assume so.  

if you have little kids, don't take them to this er. they are awful and are not helpful.  i get it, people wait at emergency rooms. i get all of that.  but some empathy would be helpful.  we got none of that from the front office staff there.  and lets be honest- those are the people that we see the first moment we get in to the emergency room.  so... maybe better training of those people.  
i already called and left a message to the complaint line and will be caling them again tomorrow to talk to them.  this is unacceptable.

dr. hien h nguyen walked into my father's hospital room in irvine hoag hospital. when she walked in she asked for a briefing as though there are no patient notes. either way, i briefed her within our conversation she realized we did not live in irvine she asked why we're there as we need a reason to seek medical help at any hospital. i explain to her my father's urologist referred us to come to seek help here due to the fact, they have 2 urologists on staff that may be able to help my father. she then looked at me when the biggest most condensing grin on her face and stated well your urologist is in newport beach why didn't he refer you to hoag newport. again i told her we do not mind the drive and by again i specified this to her 3x regarding us not minding the drive we live 45 min from irvine. i also asked her why was she laughing i quite did not understand with my sick father laying in bed there was nothing funny. she stated i would not understand. my sister could not take her disrespectful beside manner and stated to her she was being very rude. at this point i asked to speak with dr. hien outside the room, so we wouldn't upset my father talking over him as he lay in bed.  dr. hien nguyen if your reading this let me tell you i have never felt so unwelcome in any place in my life and i have traveled to many countries. i have never felt so discriminated due to my zip code. i have never encountered such an inconsiderate medical professional in my life. i felt as though you found out we did not have an irvine zip code and at that point, you were disinterested in caring for my father and questioning why we were there.  why would you question a patient on why they choose a hospital in a time of need? i felt as though you thought our urologist located in newport dump us on hoag irvine. i hope that this will be a learning experience for you and you see beyond a patient's zip code and treat them for there concerns.

so glad i listened to my friend and came to hoag hospital in irvine. i was treated amazingly with honesty & respect in the er. once i was admitted, i got to see all the beautiful designs and fixtures in the hospital. the staff was friendly and courteous.  amazing experience and will definitely come back again!!!

even though i had a great experience at this hospital a year ago when i had to have emergency appendix surgery, my experience since then with hoag and its doctors and its labs and it various facilities tells me that they are taking on too many patients (it takes 2 months to get an appointment with my doctor) and are hiring inexperienced and inefficient staff.  they cannot seem to submit a prescription to the right pharmacy, they don't provide necessary paperwork at sign in at the imaging center so that results are sent to the doctor, and all in all, they just seem to have grown too big too fast to provide decent service any longer.  really - it's so bad that i'm ready to switch to kaiser.

as far as hospitals go i had a great experience here had an mri here and every person i care in contact was very pleasant from the check in lady  to the mri techs. clean and friendly is a nice change in a hospital     i would consider traveling the 25 miles to go back if need be

if i could give hoag hospital more stars i would. i arrived @ the e.r. via the ambulance. i came in with excruciating pain on the right side of my abdomen. with in minutes i was put in a private room. as the nurse was taking my vitals etc. the on call dr. came in & ordered some tests. including a c.t. scan. . in about 30 mins i had the results i was diagnosed with acute appendicitis. i was admitted and in about an hour and a half got my own room. they gave me strong antibiotics to keep away any infection. i had surgery the next afternoon. from the preop all the nurses and medical stuff for a very helpful kind and friendly. the anesthesiologist was very knowledgeable and friendly. he made me feel at ease the surgeon was just as great. when i was in recovery staff  was beyond wonderful once i got into my private room the care couldn't  have been better. when you pushed the call button for help help arrived  within minutes. once again very friendly and caring. i cannot say enough stuff about the greatness of this hospital. i would recommend it to my family and friends very highly. i hope i don't have to go to the hospital again but if i did hoag hospital irvine would be my top choice. i wish i could remember and give individual credit to all the nurses and doctors i had.  thank you for all your wonderful help in my recovery.

i have been to hoag hospital in both newport and irvine and they've always taken great care of me.  most recent experience was going to the er in irvine with high fever and  high blood pressure.   five minutes after checking in at the front desk i was talking to a nurse. over the next four hours i was seen by several nurses and doctors, i had a ct scan, blood work and i had an abscess removed from the back of my leg.  then i was admitted as an in patient where to good care continued.  i don't want to come back but if i have to go to an er or hospital i'd come here

i came to hoag hospital around 5am due to an extreme anxiety attack. my heart rate was at 100 and i was waiting in the hospital bed for over an hour. the nurse said i'd see a doctor in 20 min and no one came. after an hour i started to go crazy in that bed (having an anxiety attack in the first place is already bad). i couldn't wait there any longer and got up to leave. as i was exiting the hospital, i was scolded as to why i didn't wait longer and that there's patients ahead of me. i tried to explain that my anxiety attack was just getting worse and i needed immediate care. however i was just treated with terrible manners and judged. never coming back here again
sadly i've read some similar issues i've experienced with my families experience that's truly answered further feelings i picked up on.

i went there to pick up a kid to bring somewhere else and the staff was not only polite and willing but very helpful in giving me precise directions and help on how to get to the room. facility was very clean; and very warm for adults and children. i hope no one has to bring their child here for being sick; but if your child does get sick; this is the perfect place to make sure your child gets well taken care of. highly recommend.

if i could i would give this place 0 stars.  my sister-in-law had a brain aneurysm back in oct 2019 she made it through surgery and  was doing very well talking and moving her hands and legs.  we moved her to this facility for physical therapy and in 9 days she developed bed sores, a urinary track infection and she fell out of a chair on her head because they were to lazy to strap her in or supervise her.  two days before she fell we told them we were uncomfortable with her in the chair because she was moving around.  when my brother got there after she fell their response to him was "what you don't want us to put her in the chair" after that he had a few choice words and demanded they do a cat scan of the brain.   which lead to another brain surgery.  unfortunately since her fall she has not been the same she is not really speaking and not moving her arms and legs.  the staff's incompetence after she fell was unbelievable.  they showed no remorse and even tried to blame her for falling!  please please do not let them near your loved ones!!!!

i had my prenatal care and the delivery of my first child at norwegian. dr. jenkins was amazing! she was thorough, responsive and supportive throughout the entire pregnancy and into my postpartum care.

i was also followed by the mfm clinic and their support and guidance was great as we were potentially dealing with some challanging issues. 

the labor and delivery unit and mother-baby unit nurses and staff are so kind, attentive and supportive during this roller coaster experience. i was able to share special moments with each of them- talking about their experiences as a new moms and asking for advice and guidance. they really are a special group.  

the breastfeeding support is invaluable. i worked with all the lactation consultants while in the hospital and have attended their baby bistro class with norma after i was discharged. my bf journey has been challenging and it was very comforting to know that norma was only a call away. these ladies love what they do and are so committed to supporting their patients. 

in response to some of the other reviews- the maternity unit was recently renovated and is more modern than the other units. my room was cleaned daily and everything was in working order. 

in short, i would return to nah if/when we chose to expand our family.
garbage place. unsanitary. workers could care less. i even had things stolen from me. avoid if you can.

this place is absolutely horrible!  i went in for a second mammogram there because the first one was inconclusive!  they always say the order is incorrect and then they charge you anyway.  very rude people and staff.  i overheard three staff members arguing with patients on the way out!

the night rn's for the adolescences unit are super sweet and care a-lot about their patients. with all they have to go through and the time and patience they go through, they surely don't get enough credit.
the hospital cafeteria is a good place for eats. prices are dead cheap, and the food is excellent, with a wide variety.

the only reason i'm an giving them any stars is because the er doc and the whole icu team were amazing. my mother in law was removed from the vent in icu and was sent to the next dept down to pass away. she sadly passed and the nurse gave us a list of funeral homes to use, we decided to find our own. we tell the same nurse we found the place to use, i write down the name, phone number and said the place will contact her for further instructions. we get all the paperwork filled out and the home is on their way to get her. she is not at the hospital! wtf!!! that same nurse gave my mil to the wrong funeral home!!! the funeral home that took her didnt even know who they had! my husband, who just lost his mom almost blew a gasket. it was fixed and said nurse called to apologize. if i had gotten involved, there would have been hell to pay and they would have been paying for the cremation. just for the pain my husband had to go through. true story

after coming to the clinic for my appointment, the receptionist said that the appointment was cancelled and they tried calling me on the day of the appointment. i didn't receive a phone call and if ever i missed it. why didn't they leave a message??? do they really cancel appointment on the same day? they even sent an appointment reminder and cancel it on the day of the appt? and tell me that the doctor don't see patients for a particular problem/illness? what a waste of time and filing a sick leave for nothing!

great hospital with awesome doctors and nurses. the main hospital is so roomy and beautiful. this place has such an amazing staff and such a great values and vision. parking here is bad and can cost a pretty penny, but that's not a deal breaker. the food here is awesome too.

review: my father was taken to harris after suffering a stroke.  he went in on a sunday afternoon and was admitted into icu that night. he was transferred from icu to the 3rd floor on wednesday. at this time he was just coming off sedation. we spent the day with him on wednesday discussing with the nurses whether he would still need a sitter to keep him calm and how great it was that we were with him so he would understand that it was bed time when we left. the pt lady came in and said he was a high risk for fall, etc and would need therapy. she informed us a case worker would be coming to discuss this with us. this is where the nightmare began. when the case worker came she dropped off a walker and left; no further discusssions. the next thing we know the doctor comes in at 6 pm and asks if we have questions. he says he thinks my father can go home. what? we were never led to believe he was even near ready to leave. he came up from icu that morning. we start asking what bp meds he has been on because his bp is uncontrolled. the dr says he has to look. we ask a few more questions and get no answers; just side-stepping. then he says he has to print some scripts and leaves and never comes back. by this time we are panicking trying to understand what is happening. it is the night before thanksgiving. we have no clothes, no wallet with insurance info. it is cold. pharmacies are closing and they are sending an 81 year old man out without certainty he can even get his meds. his granddaughter had the foresight to grab the scripts and run to his house to get insurance info and then find an open pharmacy while we are at the hospital trying to understand what is happening. this man is a veteran and is accustomed to getting his meds through the va. if it had not been for the amazing pharmacist that night at the walgreens on green oaks i have no idea what we would have done. first of all the pharmacist noticed that the hospital included someone else's script in with my father's!!!!!!!!  that could have been a disaster!!!! then they went out of their way to find coupons to make the seizure meds affordable. one alone was going to be $500. we were also told by the pharmacist how important it was that he took those each day and night. (the nurse as we left simply wrote on a sticky note with a smiley face that he needed to take that one tonight). what if we hadn't been able to find a pharmacy in time? the next day was thanksgiving! we hadn't even aligned anyone to care for him that night, because we had no idea he was leaving so soon. his wife suffers from mild dementia so it took forever to even get her to understand what was happening. by the time the process was over we left harris the night before thanksgiving at 7pm with an 81 yr old man in scrubs that they rounded up for him and a hospital blanket to shield him from the cold. horribly bad medicine! going from icu to home in one day.  was it that they needed to make their thanksgiving plans on time? was it that the nurses on charge didn't want to deal? was it that they found his insurance wasn't adequate because he was a veteran? or is this just standard behavior for harris? i have no idea, but i am appalled.

almost an hour later, we decided to leave and told them we would get the results of the test later. we then asked and found out that he was not a doctor but a nurse practitioner, not even a pa!   one of the nurses apologized to us and said we could get the results later. this experience was very frustrating, demeaning and insulting to us.  to think this is how seniors are treated and coerced into getting treatment and unnecessary tests done. the way this np spoke to my wife was totally out of line. i did not appreciate how she was treated and will never expose her to this type of treatment again.

we recently brought an immediate family member here for treatment of an acute reaction to a chemotherapy drug.  she spent 3 nights in critical care (icu), followed by 3 nights in the oncology unit.  the quality of care and attention she received was exceptional.  the nurses and physicians who managed her care were highly skilled and compassionate.  this facility is up-to-date and immaculately clean.

but since my forte is restaurant reviews, naturally i'm going to comment on the hospital's food service.  upgraded since our previous visit years ago, it's ably managed by sodexo, the france-headquartered institutional food service goliath (indeed, the french do know a thing or two about food prep).  inpatients receive a menu which includes rotating daily specials.  it's like room service at a fine hotel; you pick up the phone and order.  i'm told visitors can also order food.  food arrives within 30 minutes.  michelin stars my foot, but everything looked and smelled quite appetizing.

the oasis cafeteria on the first floor of the main building is open to hospital staff and visitors.  the missus and i dined here on two consecutive evenings.  their well-stocked salad bar is superior to those at many restaurants and groceries.  a special callout to the incredibly good 5-bean soup.  entrée choices were limited to just one or two main dishes, but the grill offers a variety of freshly-prepared hot sandwiches and there is also pizza.  i had a rather good grilled chicken sandwich one night and a decent quesadilla the next.  prices are very reasonable.

my pet peeve (with so many hospital cafeterias) is their short hours.  they close ridiculously early.  we are late eaters, and the chow line here gets locked down precisely at 6:30.  arrive at 6:31 and you're out of luck.  the only other meal option, a single vending machine dubbed "farmer's fridge," was completely empty during our visit.  thank goodness, a portillo's is located close by.

my experience:

i was admitted as a voluntary patient seeking help for suicidal ideation. i was placed with other voluntary patients as well as involuntary patients. 

involuntary patients tend to be people who are court ordered to be there. the problem with this is that they can't really get kicked out unless they really cause problems. however, it means that they are incredibly angry and are not focused on recovery, while half the other patients are.

so you have patients struggling with anything from anxiety, depression, addiction, suicidal ideation, mixed together with people who have angry outbursts and staff that don't know how to manage them. 

my first stay there was a guy who kept trying to start fights with people. the staff then tried to put him in a room with the person he kept fighting with. everyone suspected it was because the staff didn't like either of them or because one of the nurses thought it would be funny to mess with them. it was immediately fixed but it just goes to show that they are either incompetent or are willing to mess with people seeking help with their mental health issues.

the second time i stayed i needed treatment and didn't have many other options so i stayed again, thinking that things would be better. they were significantly worse. there was a woman there that screamed at staff and humiliated other patients. she constantly insulted other patients, complained very loudly about all the ways she was abused, got in people's faces, yelled at the staff, and that was my whole stay for a week. the staff couldn't do anything about it so she got to sit in on groups and say whatever she wanted to other patients while they opened up about their struggles. because of issues i'd had in my past being around her was incredibly triggering, and i threw up during my whole stay. i kept wanting to leave but the case manager laughed and said i needed to work on healing.

you're minimum stay as a voluntary patient is a week, don't bother trying to get out sooner. you're labeled as a danger to yourself or others and they want you to stay that whole time, at least, just so they can "monitor" you and "help" you with your mental health. also, doctors are the ones who decide how long you stay and they're not there on weekends and holidays. you have to be cleared by dr and case worker. 

half the staff are genuine, the other half feel the need to put you in your place. if you're going because you are in a bad place, this place will do 2 things, make sure you're "safe" and make you beg to go home. i met people there that would have rather gone back to their abusive households.

if you do not  want your child who is suicidal or anything else, to get more traumatized do not allow your child to be put in this facility. kids are screaming  and hallucinating all night, not to mention the demons my son saw. my son who already has ptsd came out with anxiety attacks that he did not have before he went in. he was wearing the same dirty clothes he wore when he was admitted on his release. they took his toothpaste and never gave it to him. after the first night we went to visitation and my son was traumatized  and had not slept all night. we told the charge nurse that we were going to take him home she kept repeating that we could not take him. we found out later that she lied to us we had the rights as his parents to take him home, disgusting! he had to spend another night and they restrained him while he was having a panic attack. i am begging you protect your child from this prison. they call the rooms cells and there are lock downs. actually i would rate it zero stars but you had to have at least one star to submit the review.

i arrived in the er on 6/18 about 7pm with severe head and neck pain, and i was unable to open my jaw. people who criticize the er wait - what do you expect? it's queens nyc not backroads iowa... but yes, it's long - but they do move you as efficiently as possible. 

the nurses were wonderful - especially my nurse diane, who i could overhear make even the most fearful of patients feel comfortable. she was so attentive and pleasant that i even felt calm when she gave me a muscle injection (which hurts).

there aren't a lot of good er options in queens, but this one is my choice for the future.
