urgent care sent me here because my ekg results, along with my shortness of breath & chest tightness/pain, could have meant a blood clot.  it's a good thing i didn't have one, since i had to wait 5 hours to get the blood test.  took another hour for the results.  i understand that it's an er & things get busy, but come on- if it's suspected you might have a life-threatening issue, you really can't be waiting this long. 

not only will this hospital scam you after making you wait forever, but the care is just bad.  they did the x-ray & ekg shortly after i got there, but had me sit in the waiting room for about 4 hours after that.  then, they brought me back & had me sit in a chair in the hallway- didn't even get a room.  the nurse said he "needed to go check something with security" but he would "be right back".  i ended up sitting there for half an hour.  doc finally came & said they were going to do a d-dimer test.  i asked where i could get some water because i was insanely dehydrated, & he said he would bring me some.  then he was called away for an emergency.  so, from my chair, i asked the lady at the front desk the same question.  she said only the doctor can give me water because it might interfere with any tests they perform.  i explained that i was just doing a d-dimer & that the doc said he would bring me some but had to leave.  she seemed not to believe me and simply ignored me (this lady was also incredibly rude & unhelpful regarding my paperwork).  i was so dehydrated & felt awful.  i somehow fell asleep for a while until they finally came to do the test a while later. 

in short, this place just wants your money & doesn't care about its patients at all.  go to another er unless you have 5-6 hours to wait for rude & uncaring staff.

i arrived at hospital early am on jan 9th for chest pain by ambulance. i was seen promptly by er doctor and was told i was going to be admitted, but was unable  to get a bed for several hours because hospital was packed. i was well taken care of in pod 1 by nurses and dr salem. i was also fed well. once a bed was available on 3rd floor the nurse made me feel really comfortable. i was in hospital for 3 days but all my nurses on that floor room 369 were awesome a 10..i had a angiogram and the cardio staff and dr choudhary were great and walked me thru procedure and made me feel comfortable. no one wants to be in the hospital ill but  my experience there was a 10 and was treated great. i don't remember all my nurses names but i just want to say your awesome and thank you

terrible terrible terrible hospital. the er is so unprofessional, they hang up on you while you are asking a question, they laugh between them and roll their eyes when you speak once you arrive. front desk  is a little more helpful when answering questions but still careless, how can someone work here if they hate people this much?

what has happened to this hospital??  my husband has been here many times, and most visits were good, except for the extremely long waits in the er.  my husband had surgery on friday and stayed overnight.  he just finished chemotherapy, so his immune system has been wiped out.  they obviously didn't consider this at all, or didn't care; so they gave him a room in the old wing where more than half the patients in the unit were quarantined!!  there were warning signs on the doors, but the doors were left open, so germs and bacteria could freely travel throughout the ward.  the nurses were unfriendly and unattentive.  my husband had to go looking for his nurse, pat, twice, and found her visiting in the corridor.  he was released by the surgeon the morning after surgery, but it took several hours for the nurses to complete the paperwork.  he was given no breakfast, and no explanation, even though it was allowed.  he was told he would be given lunch before leaving, and he had to ask about it three times before he was finally given a tray.  his "lunch" was an omelet full of eggshells!  obviously someone's breakfast that they didn't want.  he was in excrutiating pain, but they refused to give him pain medication because the doctor's orders had already been written.  he told the nurse how severe his pain was, and instead of offering to call the doctor for permission to dispense more pain medication, she asked if she should call the doctor for permission to stay in the hospital another night, knowing that no one would volunteer to stay one more night in that terrible situation.  we are very upset and disappointed that the hospital has changed so drastically.  i see from the other reviews that this experience was not a one-time exception; it has become the norm.

i brought my son to the er and he was bleeding from his mouth i asked one of the nurses for a gauze and she told me to use a paper towel! wtf my sons bleeding and not getting any medical care! on top of i think he has a concussion and they dnt really seem to care

i spent almost 3 weeks at sarh. if i ever get sick again i might try go by helicopter or plane to a hospital that will put me in a single room. i had to leave that place before i was well enough. i could not stand one more roommate. it was sheer hell. they do not care how awful you feel or if the new roommate is contagious or even if i was contagious. you're separated from your roommate by a thin disgusting dirty germ carrying curtain. i had a new roommate every day. omg. i was so stressed out it was unbelievable. i had to get out of there. they told me almost the whole time that i was going to be put in a single room as soon as someone left.  i guess no one ever went home because i never got the room the : weeks. there were mostly nice and helpful nurses if you could actually get them to come help you. some of the nurses were not so great. but, i was taken care of pretty well so i can't complain about that.

the worst emergency experience/hospital care i have received, don't bother going to the er dept. for treatment. save your time or a loved one's time from having to wait 5 hours to be seen. i was obviously there to seek medical help, since i was feeling extremely ill. while waiting 5 hours, i was finally taken back to a bed in the hall way of the er department. i was giving no privacy whatsoever, not to mention the care or compassion a patient who feel's ill should receive while waiting. the dr. finally came over to speak to me, began to ask personal questions and began to partially examine part of my body, while other patients and people walked by and watched or stared. such a degrading experience, not to mention the dr. showed no compassion or care to help find out why i was feeling so ill. all to tell me, i looked healthy and nothing looks abnormal in my blood work results. tell me why a healthy individual would want to spend 5 hours waiting to be seen for medical treatment! i voiced my concern to him, that i had lost a significant amount of weight in the last month...his response, were you obese?! what!!! i was floored by how this dr's showed no tact, grace or compassion. his unprofessional conduct, ridiculous responses and degrading behavior was unacceptable and uncalled for. i could not believe that a hospital that used hold such a prestige regard and compassion for their patients, now have such a disregard for human life. needless to say, i will be filling a formal complaint to the er administration office and the state public health department.

i went to the er after an atv rollover accident in october (yes, i procrastinate) but i couldn't pass up the chance to let them know how much i appreciate their help. from the moment i arrived i was treated amazing, and every person  i encountered was comforting and friendly! i wish i remembered names, but i don't. sorry!!!! numerous people came into my room,  and every one of them was helpful and reassuring. my finger is not fully healed yet, but it is much better condition than it could have been because you all. thank you!!!

i have yet to come to barstow community hospital emergency room and receive professional service.  the director of the hospital needs to place a microphone at the nurses station and hear what is said about patients.  heaven forbid your assigned nurse goes to lunch,  no one else knows what is going on.  then when you finally have had enough and say something, then some action is taken.  that junk that they post on the billboard about wait times is just junk.  the need to have some sort of follow up system so that patients know what step they are in, if stays or some other tests need to be done then have a checklist.  very poor management.  too many people sitting doing nothing.

kids have in-toeing so we come here for xrays and observe growth development on their legs.  to be honest, i really wasn't looking forward to this visit because last year, it was such a huge confusing process, especially since it was new patient visit.  check in process has improved but not sure if it's because we are returning patient visit. 

you go to the front desk, check in at a computer and take a pager with you.  then they page you to a desk and do all the paper work there. after that, you sit down and wait to be called in to exam.  they check vitals and then you proceed to exam room.  then you go from exam to xrays, then back to exam room for consult. 

we did not have to wait long after checking in or waiting in exam room to be seen, or wait long for x-rays, everything was pretty quick today so i was very happy about that.  

shriners i believe requires a referral to be seen.  parents need to be on top of scheduling shriners appointments and not procrastinate with scheduling these visits, you schedule these appointments well out in advance. it is important for families to ensure they come here on time because there are families who travel a lot further away to be seen.

depending the date of the visit, if there's a holiday, like valentines, shriners had a ton of toys and goodie bags to give to children from generous donors. i wasn't expecting this since we are outpatient visit.  my kids were very happy with the goodies they got. last time we were there, there were tons of free snacks at the lobby.  it is a very kid friendly environment and the staff truly seem to enjoy working with children. they expect good commitment from volunteers too.  

i remember visiting shriners years ago as a kid with my parents to make a visit to another family whose daughter flew in from argentina to get orthopedic surgery at shriners slc. this family didn't really know anyone in utah so through some networking, my parents (also from arg) found out and we went to go visit them. we discovered they didn't have to pay for her surgery and stay. children are taken care of here. definitely consider making a donation to shriners.

this place seems to be right in the middle the meals provided to the patients are ok not great based on the individual needs. security is excellent as are the front desk i've heard a few complaints about wait times for staff especially at night. overall this place is alright not great but the staff is friendly even though not always attentive they aren't bad either.
this place is very similar to an asylum!!! go for a tour and you'll immediately notice patients yelling "help" and others falling. the food looks absolutely disgusting! check my pics

my father was less than 24 hours, my sister said when she arrived to him the following day he was found naked thirsty and with kitchen gloves in his hands! it smelled like urine once you walked in and the "nurses" were very unprofessional!! this is the worse place i have been in!! we are taking our dad to a different facility!!! don't let your loved ones go there!!

i gave this place one star, but that's because i have to in order to leave my review. do not bring your loved ones here. this place is horror like you see on the news. there are a couple caring nurses but that's it. if you tour the place you would think they are well staffed, but that is because they have tons of students walking around all day. none worked on my cousin i just saw them walking around. they should shift patients who can't move every 2 hours. i was there for 9 hours asking continuously for someone to help me move my cousin and they only came 1 time in 9 hours. my cousin ended up getting 2 bed sores. i filed a complaint with the patients liaison and she was rude. i doubt she even documented any of it. the place is filthy and they used the patients bathroom to store soiled bedding and i would get there and the bathroom door would be open and the room smelled so disgusting and my cousin had to sit in there and smell it. now let's talk about abuse. my cousin told her brother they tied her ankles tight with a rubber band. he looked and took a picture of her ankle as she had a huge bruise consistent with the yellow rubber tie downs that are on the beds. she could barely move her legs so there was no reason to tie her legs. no one could explain why it happened.  i witnessed cleo being rough with her and requested she not go back in my cousins room and i found out she was. my cousin was able to get off the respirator and they started her on foods the next day she had a seizure and it took her roommate 3 times to call for a nurse. we have no idea how long she was left unattended and the sad result of it she passed away. do not bring your loved ones here!

i'm updating my review of san ramon regional because they've taken several steps to find me and discuss my experience, and i think that shows a sincere effort to do their best to make sure that people leave as happy as possible after what  is usually a bad situation...a hospital stay (with the exception of having a baby!)

they contacted me here on yelp, and they also did some pretty impressive detective work to figure out who i was and contact me by phone based simply on a yelp! review with no last name or personal info. knowing that someone actually cares helped me to take a step back. things definitely weren't perfect on day 2, but it's  important to remember that the emergency room is just that, an emergency room, and they kinda have to run a bunch of tests to figure out what's wrong, especially if it isn't something that there's  a clear answer for. 

the moral of my story, though, is that you have to be an advocate for yourself or your child. if something doesn't seem right, step in and ask why. say no. ask if there are other options. i was there to do that for my daughter, and, to be honest, they didnt try to bully me in to doing what they wanted to do. they actually did listen and respond with alternatives when i pressed. 

i'm still keeping a star off for disorganization on day 2, but i really appreciated their  efforts to make things right.

i had surgery and had to stay over night for observation, by far the best experience in a hospital i've ever had. my parents were so impressed when they offered them coffee or tea and a roll away bed if they wanted to spend the night. the staff was super attentive to all of my needs. they all introduced themselves and listened to what my preferences were and remembered them. they made my room comfortable and offered me soothing food and snacks. never had i felt this comfortable/welcomed/safe/taken care of in a hospital before. thank you carly, suong, nelson, and  zulema for making my recovery so comfortable. i apologize to the other 2 awesome nurses who's names i forgot.
hopefully i never have to go to a hospital again, but if i do, i will definitely be going back.

this review is based on customer service. i called in for a service estimate, and the lady on the phone was polite and knowledgeable. i had many questions and all were answered in a timely manner. i believe sara, was the lady's name. she called me back, with a break down of the estimate i had requested. leaving no doubt in my mind, about the deposit amount and payments. outstanding service and professionalism.

although a representative posted publicly about reaching out and i gave them my contact info, i haven't received any calls however i have received my bill. again another horrible customer service and experience at san ramon regional.

i wish i could give this place 0 stars. i will keep this really short: i came here because i was in horrible abdominal pain and was unable to eat or sleep. initially, i went to the emergency room. i do not remember much of that experience because my heart rate and blood pressure were so high that a nurse immediately took me to a doctor to be sedated. what i do remember is my follow-up appointment, which was absolutely terrible. i went in to see a doctor (i don't remember her name but she was a tall, blonde woman in her 40-50s). this horrible, worthless woman listened to my symptoms and refused to run any tests or even examine me. within five minutes, she abruptly walked out of the room while loudly complaining about hypochondriacs and told the nurse to finish up with me instead because i was a "waste of her time." i was mortified and in tears. i hadn't been able to sleep for more than 2-3 hours for at least two weeks at that point because i was in so much pain. i hadn't been able to eat. even drinking water hurt me. i went to a different hospital because my symptoms did not improve and guess what? 

i had a tumor.

if you'd like to die, go to this hospital. the doctors here will do a great job of ignoring your symptoms and ridiculing you as you slowly die in front of them.

this hospital is run by crooks who want to use every tactic to bill customers with outrageous bills. my wife went to the hospital during the summer for some stomach ache, obviously nothing was wrong , then i got these outrageous bills,  i decided to investigate the bills "i usually do not"  although i know the entire medical, hospital and insurance is nothing but the largest scam in america. after looking into the details i found out they brought their out of network doctor in an in network facility, just because they think my wife can be billed by these scammers as they think it will go  unnoticed by theses crooks who come out of mba school scamming patient, by inducing and out of network doctor to triple the charges as if what we paid is small "greedy thieves". if you ever go to these hospitals make sure you don't get scammed as they will tape into your wallet and you be smiling to them, i am so disappointed by these thieves. again i am sure the majority of doctors and administrators are good! i am giving one start rating because a thief doesn't deserve anything.

i very much want to like and use this hospital. however their admitting and billing departments are horrible. 
in 2018 i delivered my baby girl there they had the wrong address on file. we changed this address with multiple hospital staff during my stay however it was never changed.  they sent everything to the wrong address all my bills i didn't receive any bills from them until i finally contacted them. at that point they had already sent me to collections, because of their error.  i then had to deal with collections and then the hospital finally after nine months of dealing with them came back and fix the issues i was taken off of collections and i was able to pay tge proper amount i owed.

i delivered my second baby this past week here and i can't tell you how happy i am that we changed our insurance and delivered here. my first child we delivered in kaiser and the experience was just awful. at the san ramon birthing center the nurses are just amazing. every single one of them are so caring, knowledgeable and just love what they do. they helped me with such great pointers for breastfeeding, encouraged me when my milk wasn't coming in and even took care of my baby in their nursery so that i could sleep for a little bit. they made my experience just amazing and were so quick to respond whenever i buzzed them (and i buzzed them a lot and had lots of questions and asked for lots of helped). i wish i had had my first baby here as well but we changed insurance based on our first delivery in kaiser. if you can, please have your babies here. these amazing nurses and lactation consultants are so invested in their mommies and babies. thanks debra, stacey, danielle, jules, briana, connie, sheryl (lactation consultant)(apologies if i missed someone) thank you for what you did for me and my baby.

i came to this hospital to recieve care through there emergency room. the place is clean the service was timely and i was ready to sit here for 6 hours or more due to previous er visits. by far this was the quickest service i have ever recieved. been here only an hour and already getting discharged with medication.

review:
ok so i'm a nurse and always give the benefit of a doubt when someone writes a bad review of  a hospital. well here's another one. 
i took my friend into the er monday morning to igor before shift change. i wheeled her in and we approached the counter, no line. we stood there for five minutes while the intake person said absolutely nothing to us. as a seasoned healthcare worker i quickly surmised she was checking in the daughters of one of their employees. there is, however, always time to say "i'll be right with you, i'm checking these kids in". say something! well after a good five minutes standing next to my friend with her head hanging low the receptionist looked up and said "which one of you are checking in?" really? great. you can't even tell who's sick...so she doesn't ask what's wrong or what brings you in, just asks for id. 

triage went by quickly and then my friend was moved to a small room with a recliner. i joined her after i moved my car. bright glaring lights were on, no one to be found, she wasn't even introduced to her call light which was tightly wound around a bracket on the wall...nursing 101, a huge no no. 30 mins later a doctor comes in and assess the situation, going to get iv fluids, an ekg and anti nausea meds. ok thanks. 30 mins later the door opens, "we are going to draw blood". i'm sitting in the wheelchair. the attendant asks if i need the wheelchair, i assumed they were coming in to draw the blood since she announced that, and that only. i said "well if you take it i won't t have anywhere too sit". she looks at my friend and says "do you need it?" she responded "i'm good here in the recliner". attendant "well do you wanna walk?" ummm where? ohhhh are we going somewhere? yes to the treatment room. ohhhhhh well you didn't say that. ok so off to the treatment room.

she gets wheeled to a little waiting area outside another room and told "it will be just a second". we wait, and wait and wait.  i ask the nurses in the née they room if my friend could lie down, "it will be just a second, just a second". 30 mins later she i is invited back to another recliner. the nurse is just new off of maternity leave.  i got that from another employee who gleefully tells us after saying hello to her. i just need to know what our plans are thanks. these people have no customer service skills at all. 

they start the iv, give her anti nausea meds and something to relax her then tell us, "if it gets busy we may need to put you back out in this waiting area" whuuut?! yes, turns out my newly drugged friend may have to sit up in a chair, straight up, in a waiting area if they need her recliner. i said "are you serious? she's been vomiting all night and is weak and now medicated" the nurse replied "yes". i said "that's unacceptable" she replied "well that's what we have here" or something to that affect. i was ready to defend my friend's recliner at all costs...

two hours later, after the fluid is done we wait for someone to tell us the next move. i'm trying not to be that nurse so i just wait. an hour later i finally ask what happens next "well the doctor notified me he's in an emergency so it will be awhile". three hours later we leave....unnoticed. 

this hospital has the worst customer service...inform your patients what's going on! where you're taking them! thank you for the care you gave, your kindness but tell your patients everything they need to know!

this hospital took excellent care of my mother in law.
she had failed quickly and was admitted. the doctors and nurses went above and beyond to see what her issues were.  they were non stop until they found what her issues were. 
the staff respected her and spoke gently to her keep her calm and made sure she was comfortable.  
sadly, she was eventually put on life support. the team who was assigned to her took such care, it was moving. 
even when she was in a medicated coma, they were gentle and kind to her and our family. 
taking her off life support was a hard decision...
they served food and made sure the family was comfortable as we went through the long process of taking our loved one off life support.  

the team was amazing. the doctors were very supportive and made sure the facts were delivered in a timely manner. 
this hospital is very highly recommended.

thank you all for making such a hard time easier to handle.

thank you to the obgyn staff and dr. parker for taking excellent care of my sister! everyone was so attentive to my sister, making sure all of her needs were met and that she was comfortable when she was delivering her baby girl! this was her first pregnancy and dr. parker and the nurses were explaining everything step by step and with care which made us all feel super comfortable. we now have a beautiful, healthy baby girl added to the family! and mommy and daddy are doing absolutely great! thank you!!
so much better than loma linda bs. fast, accurate, normal people. no crazy cult people here.

the nurses and doctors were great . the service was great , they nurses kept on checking up on the patient. they had great attitude, some workers were working for a really long time and seemed tired but however they didn't give out attitude they were super nice.

she was finally seen by the on call gynecologist who checked her, and gave her some meds and a special shot  to stop the bleeding. about a week later,again all the bleeding...she was waiting in a chair in the er, in a chair not even a bed was made available .. the checked her hemoglobin due to blood loss and determined that she needed two bags of blood!! great staff. nurses are caring, nice, and intelligent. clean building and a sense of safeness.

thank you for making this very scary experience a very relaxing time for my mother and i.

ppru thank you ! dr. ho, dr. kim, dr. mayeda and rn terry! thank you for all of your hard work and kind hearts!

this review is specifically for the emergency room.  i have actually had relatively positive experiences in other departments, which makes it all the more upsetting how bad the er was.

i had hit my head and had a cut that was bleeding.  it was in my hair so i couldn't really see it, but i didn't think it was too bad.  i hadn't lost consciousness or had any vision issues and the blood stopped after just a couple of minutes, but i knew i needed to be sewn up.  i spoke with the urgent care in the area, but they said i should probably head to an er.  "good" sam, here i come.

i got to the hospital and checked in to a basically empty er.  i told them what had happened, and since i knew i hadn't reached my deductible, i immediately asked how much it would cost.  well, of course, no one knows what the final charge will be, but they couldn't even give me a hint of the cost.  then i had to essentially sign away my life by saying that i would pay anything my insurance fails to cover.  i looked up the average cost of something that i had been through, and it was around $700.  here we go.

i waited about an hour in a dingy hallway.  there appeared to only be one doctor staffed at that point.  the doctor finally brought me into a room and looked at the cut.  we decided to use a couple staples to close up the wound.  she irrigated and put them in and off i went.  the doctor was with me for 15 minutes total.

cut to a couple months later and i get my bill. i was pleasantly surprised that it was only $500. incredible!  i paid it and moved on.  but then, another month goes by and another bill comes in.  this time for $900.  wait, what is this???  turns out the doctor charged me $500 for literally 15 minutes of service.  then this dirty hospital er charged me $900 so i could wait around for an hour and get into a room that had been used by two patients before me without being sanitized or cleaned at all. 
i fought the charges as much as i could for as long as i could, but of course i lost.  these people are all a bunch of money hungry jerks, taking advantage of people when they are in need.  it's pathetic.  i should have just gone to the urgent care and gotten faster and better service for $150.  

now let's see if katrina b. will try to help me out since no one else was willing to do anything to try and fix this horrible experience.

my best friend was squaded here for an emergency surgery for a perforated bowel. she woke up in the icu and stayed in the hospital for a month. the nurses and docs caring for her were exceptional!

after the second surgery, they payed more attention to the fact that she was npo for 5 days, and she couldn't keep anything down for 3 days before even seeking treatment. thats over one week without any nourishment! also, for someone as sick as she was, she probably should have had her picc placed much sooner because they were unable to draw labs and could not get her nutrition through eating or ng, which was only on suction. 

they gave her a picc and tpn after about 1 week of being there. she celebrated her 24th birthday shortly after being discharged and this wouldn't have been possible without this amazing team at riverside! three months later she was able to get her ileostomy reversed and she is doing great!

the reasons why i have rated riverside as a three star is for two reasons. 

1. when having my gallbladder surgery, i had to have surgery twice. everyone knows that undergoing anesthesia is not safe nor cheap, but i had do it twice. the first time was to remove my gallbladder and gallstones. when i awoke, i was advised that some gallstones had been missed and that i would have to undergo surgery again the next day to remove the remaining stones. let's not go into detail about that nor discuss my anesthesiology bill. 

2. the billing department for the hospital has some of the rudest and most non-empathetic individuals i have ever encountered! they would not work with me in regards to my $12,000 bill i had accrued in less than six weeks. i had a $4,000 deductible through my insurance so they charged me $4,000 for me when giving birth (in december), $4,000 for my daughter when she was born, and then $4,000 for my gallbladder surgery (in january). the only payment plan they offered to work with me on was a 12 month - $1,000 month plan. this also did not include the numerous separate bills that i received from anesthesiology and some other medical offices. they immediately sent me to collections after three months since i could not afford their $1,000 per month payment plan - especially with being on maternity leave for eight weeks. 

now that i am on a better insurance plan (far less deductible), i may consider using riverside again if for some reason any medical emergency arise. my tip to others is that you better make sure you're on a pretty good insurance plan before visiting riverside as their billing department is not one that you want to work with! koop

miami healthcare exec philip esformes found guilty of paying kickbacks and bribes
by jay weaver and david ovalle
april 05, 2019 10:15 am 
philip esformes is a miami beach healthcare executive at the center of a massive medicare fraud case.
philip esformes is a miami beach healthcare executive at the center of a massive medicare fraud case. rob latour rob latour/invision/ap
philip esformes, an obsessive businessman who built an empire of healthcare facilities in miami-dade, was found guilty friday of 20 charges, including paying bribes and kickbacks, in a scheme to generate streams of medicare patients for his businesses.

the wealthy miami beach executive managed his chain of skilled-nursing and assisted-living facilities with an iron hand, with prosecutors arguing he had billed $1 billion to the federal health insurance program for questionable services that patients largely didn't need or even receive.

esformes faced 26 charges overall. the 12-person federal jury, after three full days of deliberation, came back with guilty verdicts on most of them in what was touted as the biggest medicare fraud case in the country -- in the reputed capital of such criminal activity, miami. jurors, however, did not reach a verdict on the main count -- that esformes had conspired to defraud the taxpayer-funded medicare progra

 

esformes, 50, went to trial alone in february because two key conspirators -- a physician's assistant and a former larkin hospital administrator who recycled patients for cash -- had pleaded guilty. several other healthcare associates charged with medicare fraud in related cases had also pleaded guilty and cooperated with federal prosecutors, including some who testified against him.




 1:32feds break up largest medicare scam in u.s. history

the u.s. attorney's office held a press conference in miami on july 22, 2016, announcing the filing of charges in connection with a $1 billion medicare care fraud scheme. by logan riely
esformes, who was arrested in july 2016 and has been held without bond at the federal detention center, could spend the rest of his life in prison, even without a healthcare fraud conspiracy conviction. he faces a forfeiture hearing before the jury on monday. no sentencing date has been set before u.s. district judge robert scola.

one of esformes' defense attorneys, roy black, focused on the fact that the jury was hung on the indictment's main conspiracy count of defrauding the medicare program.

"for three years, they [prosecutors] have touted this case as a $1 billion healthcare fraud and they failed to prove it," black said.

"the jury was unable to reach a verdict on that and several other counts; however, they did obviously find him guilty of a number [of other counts]," black added. "it's certainly a mixed bag."

the deadlocked verdict on the main conspiracy count was puzzling to some legal observers because jurors found esformes guilty of bribery and paying and receiving kickbacks to generate medicare patients for his facilities as well as those of other healthcare operators. it is possible that some of the jurors believed esformes' facilities provided healthcare services to patients and therefore did not technically fleece the federal program.

despite the mixed results, especially on the hung healthcare fraud count, the justice department declared total victory.

"philip esformes orchestrated one of the largest healthcare fraud schemes in u.s. history, defrauding medicare and medicaid to the tune of over a billion dollars," said assistant attorney general brian a. benczkowski of the justice department's criminal division. "i commend our dedicated prosecutors and law enforcement partners for their professionalism and unyielding pursuit of justice on behalf of american taxpayers and vulnerable beneficiaries who, as a result of esformes' crimes, were denied the level of care that they needed and deserved."

at trial, convicted healthcare operators, the former hospital administrator and an ex-ivy league basketball coach testified that esformes paid them and various doctors hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes to buy and sell patients as well as to get his son into the university of pennsylvania. esformes himself made $38 million from medicare and medicaid payments between 2010 and 2016.

"ladies and gentlemen, the amount of cash was staggering," justice department lawyer allan medina said in a packed miami federal courtroom during closing arguments last week. "when you commit fraud of this magnitude, it's a win-win for all the partners in crime. philip esformes has a commodity, the patients. philip esformes has the doctors to do what he wants them to do."

thankfully, we did not need any immediate attention or i fear what the results would have been.  had i known we would have had this many issues, we would have gladly drove over an hour to another location that we know would take care of our family.

we visited two times prior to my baby's delivery for an infant cpr class and a breastfeeding class. the cpr class was great, but we didn't get too much out of the breastfeeding class (didn't love the instructor). it was great to visit prior to become more familiar with the parking situation (there is a large lot near where labor and delivery is which i prefer to parking garages) and all the different buildings. 

i'll spare you the details of my birth and instead focus on the amazing staff. every nurse we encountered was out of this world. i felt so taken care of over the course of the three(ish) days we were there, i didn't want to leave. even the security guards were funny and welcoming... giving birth can definitely be scary, but i felt very comfortable at baptist. 

when it came to sustenance, the food you could get delivered to the room wasn't half bad and there were always options. my husband made his way to the cafeteria a couple of times and they had even more to choose from and stayed open late. 

we had the basic room and it was tiny. i felt bad for my husband who slept on the squeaky pullout couch three nights in a row. i did catch a glimpse at the bigger suites and they looked very nice! definitely worth the upgrade if you'll have a lot of visitors. 

while i hope i don't end up at baptist again anytime soon, i'm happy that this was where i gave birth to my healthy babe!

unfortunately, going to the er at ojai valley community hospital (ovch) in recent years has become a little like playing a game of russian roulette with a couple rounds in the cylinder.  
   between 5 active, athletic kids and my own injuries, we've been there dozens of times over nearly 20 years. and in most cases it i'd describe our experiences as pretty good - as far as a trip to the emergency room goes. 
   however in the past few years that's changed, and seems to be getting progressively worse.  and our recent january 2020 er visit didn't help improve my opinion. 
   why the decline?  one big reason is that  ovch has been "contracting out"  it's emergency room services to what i'd describe as out of town medical "mercenaries" who come in and gouge the hospital and the patient.  they have no connection to the community, no affiliation with the hospital, and are essentially accountable to no one. they won't even tell you that your medical insurance is no good with them. it's insane. 
   even if ovch is part of your insurance plan and is recommended by your insurance carrier as your emergency care facility......even if you make your er co-payent to ovch when you check in at the emergency room desk..... these unethical parasite physicians will bill you separately for their er care because (as "contract physicians") they simply don't have to accept your medical insurance.  
problem is - you'll never know that until you subsequently receive their bill in the mail!  
   that's a sign to me that ovch has recently become hard-up for doctors / nurses and is failing the community with it's overall lack of oversight.  **the ovch foundation board needs to take action.   
   in fairness i'd say that as long as the er physician on duty happens to be one of the good local docs like doug nelson or gordon clawson (and a few others)  you're in competent care.  and if you're able to confirm beforehand (before any care is rendered) exactly who your er doc is going to be and that he/she fully accepts your insurance as full payment (get it in writing), you're probably ok from at least a billing perspective.
   if not i'd head immediately to cottage hospital in santa barbara or to saint john's hospital in oxnard where you'll get far more comprehensive (and much faster) care.  it'll be worth the drive and peace of mind.

review:
the good: the nurses, doctors and support staff largely make a herculean effort to care for those who find themselves at this ancient medical facility. hugely grateful to them for saving my life. 

the bad: this was, without question, the dirtiest, most poorly designed, badly run hospital, with the most limited facilities, i have ever witnessed. 

summary: 9 hours in the shockingly dirty er which seems to operate much as one would anticipate in a third world country. 2-1/2 days in an equally filthy er room, while going through a battery of tests. several hours in surgery, which was very professional on all accounts. 2-1/2 days on the first floor ward, which was (again) shockingly dirty and poorly outfitted.

besides the excellent staff, this hospital is terrifyingly bad. apparently, nobody ever takes a shower here, as when one can find a shower, it appears to have last been cleaned in 1998. everything about this place (besides most of the staff) smacks of stunning disregard for the patient's comfort and wellbeing. i never saw anybody cleaning, beyond taking out the trash. there was visible dirt everywhere, save for the surgery and scanning areas. the blankets are as thin as paper and threadbare. ditto for the towels, if you can get your hands on one. 

the business office visited me twice, while i was doubled over in pain, waving documents and asking for money on the spot, in spite of my $1160 monthly premium being fully paid up -- and offering no specific details about what i was being charged for. apparently, my hospital co-pay is $1400, which they wanted on the spot, with zero itemisation. 

though i am grateful to the nurses and doctors who saved my life, i hope to never return to this hospital again.

i'd been taking an herbal supplement that was recommended by a professional.  i failed to do any research; and, i just started taking it for pain and to relieve some long-term bruising caused by using prednisone for an auto-immune condition.

the doctors and nurses are very caring, very professional, super informative and want you to be comfortable and to heal.  they ran blood work 3 times, an ecg and then had ecg monitoring, a ct scan, and a chest x-ray, all because i may have had a heart attack, stroke or mini-stroke.

none of those things happened; but, i am glad they ruled them out.  i have knee surgery scheduled later in the month, so i didn't want to jeopardize that.  they did find two health concerns that i need to address; and, i will after my knee surgery.  these are long-term health improvement items; and, nothing that is acute or critical.

so glad that we were only 5 minutes away from ormc, the er staff was great; and, so was the hospital staff.  i really appreciate all they did for me.

hca must pay $162 million for charity care problems

healthcare giant hca, based in nashville, tn, must pay a kansas city, mo, charitable foundation $162 million and undergo extensive auditing after a judge found that the for-profit hospital operator broke key agreements regarding charity care and capital expenditures in its billion-dollar purchase of hospitals from health midwest in 2002.

judge john torrence, jd, of the circuit court of jackson county, mo, ruled that hca, the nation's largest investor-owned hospital company, did not spend as much money improving health midwest's existing facilities as it said it would. the judge also ruled that hca did not abide by an agreement to provide at least as much charity care to the community as the health midwest's not-for-profit hospitals had provided before the sale. that amount was said to be $65 million annually.

the health care foundation of greater kansas city (hcf) had sued hca in october 2009 to ensure that it had complied with its more than $950 million obligation to charity care in the kansas city area. the purpose of the lawsuit was to determine if hca had complied with its obligations to make $450 million in capital improvements to existing health midwest facilities and provide over $500 million in charity care. hcf chairman karen cox, rn, supported the ruling, saying "as a voice for the uninsured and underserved, the hcf board of directors felt it had the fiduciary responsibility to make sure that this population had been afforded the services promised to them through the sale of health midwest."

hca issued a statement saying it would appeal the decision. "rather than simply put money into the repair of old facilities, we built two new hospitals, spending hundreds of millions of dollars to ensure this community has high quality care," the company said in a written statement. "we believe we have complied with our agreement, exceeded our promises, and we continue to spend millions for the benefit of a community we love."

health midwest had operated 11 not-for-profit hospitals in missouri and kansas before the sale.

she quickly placed a catheter and gave my wife a dose of zofran and a dose of fentanyl iv, and started to leave (this was 1 hour after being placed in the room- this is a fact, there is a clock above the door). i asked if her pain is still not being controlled, what is the next step? they said they can give her another dose of fentanyl. i asked how long we should wait before seeing if she needed another dose. they said 15 minutes. we waited another 15 minutes and i again had to go out into the computer center area and tell the nurse that the first dose wasn't working. then our nurse (the one with the black hair) came in and gave her the second dose. my wife quickly calmed down and began to relax...we were both incredibly relieved...we thanked everyone we could for helping us. but in retrospect...why did it take an hour for us to get 2 iv drugs?? i understand that ers can get busy, but the people who helped us had been sitting right in front of our room on a computer the whole time avoiding me (i was never rude to anyone and never raised my voice, just pleading with them to help us). as we were waiting on the rest of the workup, we could hear them out there talking about facebook. the nurse came back in and said how much better my wife looked and later the doctor came in and said how much more color my wife's face had now that she wasn't in pain......(they both noticed how bad she looked when she came in! and still left us to stay sitting for 1 hour with her vomiting and in pain (and that's only because i was making a fuss) ...? excellent hospital for giving birth in the bay area

we had two of our babies born here (3 years apart) at the sequoia "dignity health" hospital. both times we had a very pleasant experience. we found that virtually all the nurses were very well trained and highly experienced. we found that they were very caring for the health of the mother and the baby. i know a couple of our friends also gave birth in this hospital and were very happy. generally, it is not super crowded like some other hospitals and feels very clean and premium hospital. 

nurses:
i believe that each nurse are assigned to manage 2 patients during their shift. and there are two shifts (7am-7pm and 7pm-7am). so expect two main nurse assigned to you each day you are there. there are also other nurses who do some specific things, who keep coming in-and-out during the stay. they also have monitors in their lobby areas where they constantly monitor all the patients. one of the things that really impressed me is their team work. all the nurses were genuinely helping each other even when they were not assigned directly to the patient. 

emergency situations:
giving birth is a very complex thing and is really a miracle! at any given point in time, there could be an emergency! each room is equipped with emergency buttons that the mothers can push and it literally creates an ambulance like noise in the nurses' break rooms and control rooms with red-lights blinking above the patient's door and alerts every nurse about it. and both times we were there, some patients pressed their emergency buttons in the middle of the night for different reasons and i saw all these nurses literally running and rushing to that room to help that patient! it was really amazing to see them caring so much! this is the main reason i gave 5-stars! 

they also have a couple of in-house obgyn doctor (at least 1, 24x7) and couple of in-house anesthesiologists to take care of things in addition to nurses.

birthing room:
each birthing room has a fancy birthing bed with a lot of special capabilities to help with birthing. the bed also has a bunch of buttons to articulate the bed, plus there is a tv that the mother (or spouse) can watch while waiting for the baby to arrive. next to the bed, they have a small bed for the spouse or relative to take some rest (if that's possible). 
each room also has an attached restroom with a toilet, sink and a shower.

hospital food:
hospital food, especially for vegetarians like us was pretty blonde and terrible :( we suspected it and so we actually cooked food at home and brought it to the hospital, so it was not much of an issue. i hope non-vegetarian foods are better, but i encourage you to do the same as we did :)

postpartum:
one thing i've heard is that during some months it does become quite busy and after the birth, they'll move the mom and baby from the main birth room to a different smaller room during the 48 hours recovery period. i know one of our friends were moved but we were not.

i believe the hospital also has other departments, and i don't know anything about them but if you are planning to have a baby, i highly recommend this center and am sure this is one of the best in the bay area. 

btw, after the birth, make sure to give the nurses cookies and chocolates to thank them!

review: my uncle has had 2 recent visits to this hospital. first visit would be 5 stars for er services. everyone from nursing staff, lab, radiology, md's and case management were amazing. more recent visit included an admission and the icu staff was very kind and informative. i'm a nurse and was blown away with care up to that point. he was transferred to 5th floor and care, communication and compassion seemed to be lacking. feeling frustrated with discharge process and lack of communication. being sent home in taxi with out keys to get inside and no family close by.

so i have to start by saying, er was busy peak flu season but that did not in anyway effect the courtesy and respect from this healthcare staff!! from the moment we walked in the door, the girl at the front was so sweet, respectful, understanding!! security was the same and between her and the two security officers they made things feel at ease in a hard situation. the triage nurse was thorough and understanding he was great! then, the doctor amazing his nurse desiree amazing ! the whole experience was the best possible scenario in such a awful situation that i have never in my life felt so pleased with an emergency room experience like this one!! stacy from registration was also great and helpful!! and so so kind !! i'm grateful for enloe!!! 

also our visit began over in urgent care earlier in the day and the rn named amber 
you were a blessing today thank you for your kind heart and the compassion!!

excellent hospital, my finance, went there for a heart problem taylor hospital couldn't find. they had to reshock her heart to bring it back in rhythm. taylor had no idea what to do.
stay clear of taylor hospital. 
go to this hospital instead.

out patient check-in personnel were friendly and helpful. the persons doing the transporting around the hospital were friendly and did an excellent job. all of the nurses, techs, pas and dr sandeep sharma were top notch. everyone listened to my concerns and responded appropriately. the technology was state of the art. the results of the procedure were excellent. discharge was within a few minutes of promised. it was first rate from beginning to end.

after having 2 kids at bryn mawr, was managed by crozer-affiliated ob practice for my 3rd. since i would turn 40 by edc, i was sent for weekly nst. tests were reassuring but i was cautioned not to go past my due date. remaining in close contact with my team, i was instructed to call and schedule myself for induction prior to my due date. my ob team cited increased risk for stillbirth the closer i got to my due date. so like a good patient, i did as i was told, and called for an induction prior to my due date, and after having had grab-onto-the-nearest-table contractions for a week the docs agreed i needed to deliver asap.

!!!!!! surprise !!!!!! no l&d bed available for me, despite the md's insistence that i be induced prior to my due date.

i came in anyway. i figured i would sleep in my car. i just didn't want my baby to be stillborn.

anesthesiologist who placed my epidural was excellent. 

nurses who took care of me on l & d were pitiful. i had bronchitis and after getting tired of asking for prn otc cough medication (coughing + recent vaginal delivery = really painful) and not having it given, i just asked my visitors to bring some in from home. i remember,too, my last morning there being in a lot of pain and calling my nurse for naproxen & being told my night nurse was in report with the day nurse and i would get it when report was over. guess what? no naproxen. i ended up running my bath towels under hot water and using them as heating pads because guess who didn't answer the call bell? my day nurse!!!!!!!!!

zero stars. zero. f-ing. stars. press ganey's gonna hear all about it.
these guys totally suck. they failed my sister and other people i knew. go to a real hospital. like riddle. too bad fedex goes to this dump. we deserve better.

my family and i called to check on someone. the receptionist put me through to the icu. after being redirected, i told them the patient i needed information on. they asked who was calling. then proceeded to say "his family is in the waiting room. call one of them.". the patient was proclaimed deceased shortly after this. i cannot give a worse rating for this hospital.

review: arrived at emergency room 6:41 pm due to prednisone reaction at 8:16 pm i was still waiting to be seen in er on 2/22/20. i then decided to leave went to er desk and asked to be removed from patient roster going to another facility. not one staff member knew how to perform this service nor responded appropriately to the issue.  i assumed the desk clerk was bothered since he was texting on his phone.  i was in the facility with another woman who had even been vomiting in the area only to see her sit and the mess only cleaned up.  the final straw was listening to a male staff nurse discuss private patient information.   this facility needs to train its staff on patient privacy guidelines immediately.  i left the hospital and went to owensboro.  never saw a doctor or received medical care.  this facility isn't fit enough to see a pet let alone a human being.  i asked for written proof showing i was being removed as a patient and i definitely don't want a bill from a substandard hospital of this magnitude.

both my grandparents were admitted to grand park and my family is thankful for the exceptional care they have been given. the staff are absolutely wonderful and have been very attentive to both the patient and family needs. grand park is one of the best short and long term rehab hospital in this part of town. the employees from social care, nurses (rn, lvn, cna), physical therapy, kitchen, cleaning, and much more are just absolutely wonderful.

grand park is very carring facility with hard working staffs and rooms are clean.
staffs works hard on individual careful for each patient.

my grandmother is currently hospitalized here. the doctors and nurses are all very kind and are always willing to put extra effort. the food is also very nice. my grandma has a hard time digesting hard food but all the food that they provide are soft. especially, the physical therapists team works very hard and my family is very satisfied of their support.

wow, some very low ratings for this hospital on yelp!  i'm actually surprised because our experience was pretty good.  from the front desk/security desk, to the floor nurses/staff, to the social workers; everyone was very friendly, helpful and accommodating.  

they were super helpful when my 85 yr old aunt and 97 yr old uncle, came to visit their son in the hospital.  they both have difficultly walking and the staff went out of the way to make sure they both had wheel chairs to bring them to my cousin's room.  truly professional and wonderful staff all around.

i have nothing negative to say, and appreciate the care and attentiveness they provided my cousin during a very difficult time.  big thanks to everyone!!

south miami hospital emergency room is now the worst around the area. in the past, it was one of the best. we have been there twice recently with serious conditions and they left us alone in the room for hours. the tests were spaced hours apart and they would not even give us a blanket. the first time the older male er doctor would not even come in the room and gave us incorrect information from the doorway. the second time, the female er dr. basically threatened my husband saying that if he left he would die. he is just fine weeks later. do not go there! doctor's er is by far the best and will treat you with compassion.

i moved here from seattle and the transition has been terrible. when you called for an appointment no one answers the phone the first time and they don't return the call for one to three days. i tried to make an appointment with neurology and was given an appointment 4 months from now. this is broken system here in denver.

very upset with bashir a certain group of students, surgical team....

i'd still recommend it, but just keep in mind er's are generally miserable anyways so word of the wise, always have low expectations for that mess.

if i could give this nursing home negative stars i definitely would. i worked here for two days with the alzheimer's side of the nursing home. one, in no way shape or form is there complete security doors are easily opened and the residents get out. the nurses are lazy and racist. they get intimidated by new  workers. they leave their pts in dirty diapers, bed sores. they are also force fed, i saw one nurse force feeding a woman that couldn't even talk, another nurse tried blocking the view but there windows all  around so you can see reflections . another pt was left crawling on the floor because the nurses said she was "hard headed and needed to learn" she would try  to charge her phone but the charger was broken.. she would want to call her daughter. at one point one of the rns in charge got in my face because she needed help.. there were over 20 pt i was an activities aid ... i had to watch probably about 5 people trying to escape.. one man walked around scratching like crazy like he had scabies.. this place  needs to be closed down.. this was reported but the owner did nothing i also reported to the hpd they also did nothing... the city and the nursing home both suck.

took my wife to the er and was very relieved we did not have to wait. the staff there are very attentive  and professional,. we were blessed to have frank rn take care of my wife. he checked up on her often to see how she was doing while doing his rounds. frank,thanks for taking great care of my wife and taking care of me with that sandwich. 5 stars to you and your team in the er.

this is one of the best hospitals i have ever been too. the love and the kindness from the staff working there is heartwarming. i will definitely recommend this hospital to anyone, one of the best hospitals in the country.... tall are amazing

the staff in the er are professional, caring, friendly and efficient. rudy in triage was my hero, quickly assessing my injuries and eliminating a potentially long wait time. suzanne was attentive and good-natured despite the er being short-staffed. they had several challenging patients with police escorts but they took it in stride.  this is a very hard-working crew. hats off to all of them.

i have filed several complaints against this hospital over the years. i have a physical disability and some areas of the hospital are not accessible to me. the requests i am making are or should be standard operating procedure for any healthcare facility and would benefit many patients with hidden physical disabilities. recently, i visited the facility - my doctor sent me over to mission laguna specifically for testing/imaging. i could not use the waiting room for radiology/imaging. there was no way to contact a manager from the front desk (they are all off sight).  i had two other appointments the following week and i was assured that things would be handled by a risk manager, gerri, who later admitted she did not follow up. on my return, the obstacles were still there.  premise disability accommodations (ada americans with disabilities act) are supposed to be handled discreetly (they are not at this hospital).  i have been referred up the line to the vp of patient care and to the st. joe's executive offices in irvine.  the management (and their attorney) is /are either stupid or abusive.

review:
efficient and helpful is all i can say after my first visit. staff was incredibly kind going to far as to walk me to the place i needed too go to.

facility was clean and not dated like so many other facilities i've been to. pharmacy had a short wait time. no problems with this va facility. yet.

i went in for a minor surgical procedure. i was very nervous, mostly because of a fear of sedation. but the staff was very understanding and took amazingly good care of me. i could not have asked for a better experience. i would have no hesitation to go back, should the need arise.

i delivered my first baby here back in november and it was the most amazing yet wildest experience of my life! everyone here is so heart warming and kind. they made me feel so comfortable and well taken care of from the moment i was admitted to the moment i went home with my baby girl! i want to give a special shout out and thanks to donna, jody, and osha! i wish i could remember all of the nurses's names because they were all so great! donna is the  coolest and she was my first nurse! she felt like family after we found out my husband graduated with her daughter. when it was time to move to a delivery room she made sure the best one was available for me! jody and osha were the storm troopers! they saw me at my worst when i was turning into the exorcist from those crazy labor pains lol but even then they were so calming, professional, and guiding my labor amazingly! dr. hernandez gave me my injection, he was so professional and quick. thanks to dr. northey, although she was not my ob, she was perfect and i'm so happy i delivered my baby with her. finally after my baby made her grand entrance, everyone i encountered during our stay were beyond amazing! oh and lily the lactation nurse! oh my god she was the sweetest and so helpful! the rooms are nice and big, the food is great, everything was awesome! i know i'll be coming here again if i am blessed with another baby in the future! thank you

i thank the ambulance drivers , emt, doctors , and nurses and the rest of the staff for all your compassionate help and professional service. i highly recommend this hospital and medical center !

ive had the occasion to visit a friend in this hospital for way too long and its a place i would never go and you shouldn't either.  the rooms always smelled like urine and or poo wheres the the cleaning staff or nursing to clean up?  the staff is clueless and a majority speak creole and like to talk about the patients and visitors they need to smarten up as i understood exactly what they were saying more than once!

i went to a cvs minute clinic with really bad symptoms and after being diagnosed there i was positive my vitals were not right so i went to the hospital. by the time i arrived my vitals were getting even more concerning and i was quickly admitted. the doctors and nursing staff were kind, proactive and diligent. i was quickly started on iv fluids and antibiotics. they made sure i was comfortable and continuously checked up on me. the doctor was young but i like that because i feel like young doctors are more concerned and do more testing to make sure everything is okay. turns out i was misdiagnosed at the minute clinic and ended up with a bad bacterial infection that could've gone septic so i'm grateful for the hospital staff for catching that. overall i had a great experience! thank you so much staff at wellstar cobb!

if i could give this place 0 stars i would. i came here with my mom to get an mri since she was in an accident, and the people are so rude. i work in health care myself, and i cannot imagine being like that. no one offered to help or get a wheelchair, and they almost treated her with no respect. the signs are misleading and it seems like it is run down. after seeing how they treated her, i would not like to be treated here even if i had to.

my grandmother arrived in the ed via ambulance after a fall at home left her with hand lacerations and a head strike. they did a head scan and an x-ray of her hand, sutures and closed the open wounds on her hands, and sent her home. they sent her with vague dressing change instructions and no supplies. when i took down the initial dressing, the fibers from the kerlex were imbedded into the wounds so deep it caused bleeding and pain to remove them, even after dampening. i redressed it with my own supplies and she said it felt better. two days later she called and asked if i'd change it again. the swelling in her hand and arm were worse so i recommended that she have it reevaluated. this time they decided to xray the arm and shoulder that they should have had x-rayed the first visit. it turns out she had a fractured elbow.  it really amazes me that an x-ray of the affected arm in a fall in any person wouldn't be part of the protocol. they totally dropped the ball and caused her to have to return to the facility for something that should have been caught the first time. not impressed with the quality of care.

my experience at providence st joseph was excellent. had hip replacement with a two night stay the nursing staff was wonderful- their care & attention outstanding. truly served as my nurse advocate when i needed one.  found the physical therapist to be great as well. this is my second time at this hospital - the other was emergency based - i trust them with my medical care

from the  gentlemen who replaced a white board in my room, to the lady cleaning it - right up to the nurses, physical therapist and lab technicians; everyone had a welcoming and supportive attitude.  it showed every time someone came into my room
given a choice, i will return to providence saint joseph medical center for any future hospitalization.

it's unfortunate that a 4 star , fantastic er and staff are attached to this hospital and related in any way. i've been in the er several times and the dr there is amazing.
unfortunately, for a heart patient with severe issues, this is downright dangerous stay if your admitted. 
mostly, this isn't a staff issue, as much as it is operations and lack of facility.
while suffering a severe heart issue , there was no available cardiologist on staff, they refused to talk to pahrump cardiology which treats me (dr arik is a real cardiologist ) and refused to review the extensive medical records from pahrump, and from cedars in la , all done within 30 days . 
i even had my hf cardiologist from la on the phone himself and they refused to speak with him. 
instead they wanted to do the risky stress test to a heart already damaged, echos, and angioplasty... again, without a cardiologist leading the team. that's very dangerous. the issue was being treated and an emergency happened, delaying my trip to get the procedure done by a world class hospital and staff.. i just needed stabilized
enter the emergency, what caused the problem was actually ketoacidosis! i was drinking liters of fluid per hour, urinating ever 10 minutes, smelled like "rotten fruit" , confused, virtually catatonic, sweating heavily, and had uncontrollable ketones and acidity in my blood... yet proper treatment (such as iv hydration and stabilizing blood sugar) was never properly ordered. so any doctor reading this knows what happened... my electrolytes went out of whack and heart destabilized. my bp plummeted ( at times under 70) 
my heart meds , entresto, are not cheap (about $30 each with a discount card) . they refused to provide them. they claimed amiodarone is just as good. if they would have checked my records they would have seen i react badly to that. so i went three days without heart meds when i needed them most.
i do remember being unable to stay awake while they got me to sign consent forms i couldn't even read. that is concerning. 
lets be real, if you have heart failure every facility wants to do their own cardiac stuff... stress tests, echo, whatever.. it's 10's of thousands of dollars billable for an hour basic work... it's also "use it or lose it" equipment and staff , which a 25 bed rural hospital gets some income... so fine... but when you don't have the expert cardiology lead, am unwilling to look at recent records, refuse to consult with patients medical doctors, and ignore blatant coexisting factors ... all at the risk to the patients life and health... then sorry, your a one star facility , and with no other option in pahrump... your dangerous.
i hate to be mean... but everyone that is staff there knows what i'm talking about knows i am right. policy and protocol needs massive rewriting there...

i went into dvh 3 days after i had my daughter because i was passing blood clots the size of my hand.. upon my arrival the person admitting me asked me why i was there, i told her why, even showed her vehicles get stolen and security is completely incompetent and they do not care nor do they do their job. we were there for a total of 8 days in the ltch acute care on floor 6 due to my father having a severe stroke. my mother stayed day and night with him, her vehicle was parked in the emergency parking structure and was stolen! review: dr. towers is a wonderful physician. she handled my son with autism with expertise and had answers to all of my concerns. she held specific knowledge about issues with his diet and development. she did not push me into any treatments i was not comfortable with. would highly recommend her to any parent w a kiddo on the spectrum or otherwise.

i got sick  and was admitted into the hospital for four days in december.  my nurse kelsey was very kind, caring, attentive and took very good care of me. my hospital room was very clean and nice. a lady came in and cleaned it every day.  everyone i encountered was very nice.
my family and i love simi valley hospital! the staff is wonderful and always treats us with respect.

not much of an expert in emergency room visits, however this was my 3rd er visit in as many weeks (3 different hospitals). no one could seem to, or want to, correctly diagnose my issue until i went to simi valley hospital. wow! in the door and through registration, and triage in no time. granted, i was there at 7:30 saturday morning, but there was no one in the waiting room. no snotty nosed, coughing kids. no sad adults with masks on. and, the place was clean! unbelievable. they had me in a room within 20-25 minutes, and instantly started working on trying to figure out what the heck was wrong with me that no one else could seem to figure out. super professionals. super comforting. super experience. i hope to never see them again, at least professionally...but if i do, i won't mind. these people do their jobs well. they ultimately got to the bottom of my issue, and i left with the peace of mind of a realistic diagnosis, and a path to fixing the issue that is actually working. amen for these fine people and their fine hospital. forever grateful.

i had knee replacement surgery in december 2019. from admitting to nursing; every single person i came into contact with was so helpful and kind. they have a nurse navigator, kathryn harada, who helps all joint replacement patients and ensures that we know what to expect before and after the surgery. further, she provided amazing support when i was not able to attend the normal class, she met with me individually. she cares about each patient and followed up twice while i was in the hospital and then gave a call to see how i was adjusting the day after i got home. the simi valley adventist hospital provides excellent care and i would never hesitate to use this hospital again in the future.

finally had time to write this review of my er visit this previous november, and it hurts my heart to have to write this but ...

long story short- people acted like they didn't want to be there, except a few. the x-ray dept seemed to be the most caring.

short story long- i went to the er on a saturday afternoon because i kept going in and out of consciousness. i felt as if i was having a stroke. upon stumbling in , i literally stood there for maybe 5 minutes while the security guard was using a wand on some guy that looked like a visitor, but had a wrist band. finally she sat me down in a chair, waited another 15 -20 minutes before anyone acted like they gave a crap. (from my memory, the only other people waiting was the dude standing there being searched by the security guard) my legs started to turn red from loss of blood flow. they finally got me inside, and started doing tests. the two techs that did the ekg were okay, but little did i know they printed out the someone else's test, and quickly switched it back. that's fine mistakes happen. so it took them until almost the end to hook up an iv... oh yeah when they wheeled me in, the first doctor just looked at me and passed through acting like he didn't have time and disappeared. meanwhile i'm panicking because my head feels numb, and people just seemed like they were doing other crap to be bothered. so after about an hour or so of laying there, the er doctor came in and asked some questions. i still kept going in and out of consciousness. when i finally was decent with fluids, i had to use the bathroom. i rang the bell, and the doc came in. i told her i had a diaper on (i wear them for emotional support, it's in my charts) but don't use the bathroom in them. when i notified her of this, she handed me the urinal, and gave me a wierd look and acted like i was a freak for my diaper. if that wasn't bad enough they wouldn't even close the curtain till i asked (the camera was there in plain sight) i told that to the doc, and she laughed and said they don't turn it on. i demanded she close the curtain anyways. hours went by then a smart alec er nurse came in and started doing other vitals. he really just acted pissed off at the world or something. so finally the doc came back and she said everything was normal, but it's an er so i'll have to go to a doctor to make sure everything is normal... are you serious????? you're a hospital.!!!!!!!! so whatever i just wanted out if there as soon as i felt somewhat with it. of course i don't have insurance, so maybe that is what alott of this boils down to. i made a payment on the beginning bill, but now for some fun reason they decided to get it into collections without any sort of acknowledgement of my previous payment!!!!!!! just really not happy with how things went, and i especially am not happy with how fast they are willing to send something to collections without my payment being recognized. sad sad sad, especially since i've been a cocoa beach resident for 31 years now. sorry... you guys screwed me some years ago, but this is reprehensible.

my girlfriend came in with the stomach bug and they had us waiting in the er for almost 40 minutes. i kept telling them she couldn't hold in throw up or bowel movements so they take us into a room just to get blood drawn and threw us back into the waiting room once again where she continues to throw up and shit herself after me
asking multiple times now to give her anti nausea and iv. she is passing out in the wheel chair in the waiting room as doctors and nurses walk by. the front part of this office is a joke i understand they take patients by who is the worse but there's literally nobody in here and my girlfriend is sitting in the lobby throwing up and dazing in and out of consciousness while we were in the lobby. this was the worst watching my girlfriend suffer like this because of lack of care hospital care. i unfortunately had to keep nagging the front desk lady for her to finally call up somebody and get us a room. when we get to back over 6 rooms were empty i was beyond confused. after having iv in her and given medication. a emergency doctor comes into the room without even introducing himself and says she needs to stay over because her lactic acid level is too high and she could die. i was upset and had all these questions plus i didn't even know this doctors name and instead of answering my questions and handling an upset patient he starts to argue with me then kicks me out of the hospital to leave my girlfriend there alone. she stayed the night and the next day the nurse left the iv needle in her for hours withoout twking it out they forgot she was in the room and one of her blood lab tests " got stuck in the testing tube shoot in the wall" this place is an absolute shit show.
