first and foremost, i understand and agree that for the majority of us the risk from covid-19 virus is very low.  i agree there is no need to panic.  however, this morning while making breakfast and lunches i spilled my coffee over what a doctor from lake forest hospital said. (i didn't catch the doctors name, however i'm sure it will be easy for the hospital to figure out who was answering questions on the radio.)  a woman called in  and was saying she isn't sure if she should take her family and young children on a plane to florida ( i think) for spring break because of the virus. the doctor told her that flying on a plane is perfectly safe....(next is what made me spill my coffee.)  the doctor stated that the air filtration systems on planes are much better than people think, and they remove the virus, so there is no reason to worry about catching the virus on the plane. a doctor said that.  you don't need to be a doctor to understand at this point that this virus is not being spread in the air.  it is being spread person to person, person to surface, and surface to  person.  lake forest hospital and its parent northwestern need to get a hold of this doctor and reprimand him for giving false information.  again, i understand for most of us, including a young family the risk is low.  however, stating that on the radio when there are possible seniors and others at risk listening is dangerous.  an elderly person with chronic condition may hear that and say "well, if a doctor associated with northwestern says its ok to fly because of the planes air filtration systems, then it must be safe.  i'm sure northwestern will reply to this with its usual legal speak of possible miscommunication by the doctor.  unacceptable, statements like that doctor made put peoples lives at risk, especially elderly with chronic conditions.  the is no air filtration system on any plane that can remove the covid -19 virus.  shame on lake forest hospital and northwestern

the doctors, nurses, technicians and staff at memorial hospital of gardena rock! can't say enough nice things about them. i have been to their e.r. twice in the last 20 years (most recently this past week), and my wife has been here 3 times in the last year 1/2. my wife took me to the emergency room because i kept having chest pains, tightness, palpitations and burning in my stomach, back and arms. surprisingly the waiting room was pretty empty, then again it was a wednesday morning. 

i was admitted pretty quickly into the e.r. had my vitals checked and given a bed. they did an ekg on me and i was "glad" i was having the heart palpitations right at that moment and they were pretty intense and nonstop. i figured whatever was going on, if it was heart related they should be able to see it. that's the tricky thing with heart palpitations, often times they don't always happen, so you might go to the doctors office and not be having the symptoms when they do the ekg or listen to your heart. but this time i was having the palpitations and the doctor said my results came back normal and good and that i wasn't having a heart attack.

dr. sean howse was awesome as was the ekg technician. the phlebotomist was the best i've ever had! i didn't even feel the needle prick, and that was the part i was dreading the most, because i hate needles! but he took several vials of my blood and i didn't feel a thing! even the receptionist and security guards were nice! overall it was a great experience considering where i was at. i mean, no one wants to really go to the e.r., especially me! 

after the ekg and the doctor talking to me, listening to my heart and me describing my symptoms, he told me i had gerd and gastritis. he was about to discharge me but my wife and i insisted they do all the blood tests, all the heart tests to 100% rule out that it was not my heart, since i kept having these symptoms. the doctor was like "you're fine, it's not your heart, but if it'll make you feel better i can do all the tests." we were like "yes please do all the tests." 

i also insisted on him doing an ultra-sound of my stomach and intestines, since i kept having nonstop burning in my stomach and chest area and striking pains/cramping. he agreed to do all the tests i requested. for some time now i had been agonizing over if something was wrong with my heart and since i suffer from generalized anxiety disorder it constantly gave me panic attacks. i really needed to figure out what the hell was wrong with me and try to fix it. 

so they drew several vials of my blood, gave me a chest x-ray and a stomach ultra-sound. the test results for my heart and all my blood panels came back good. no liver, kidney, thyroid or heart issues, also no infections. the doctor said "that's good news that you have no stomach infections, i was worried about that, and your pancreas is good too, which was another concern." he said "my test results came back better than his!" dr. howse was very funny and his anologies are hilarious. my wife had him on a previous visit. he takes his time talking to you, explaining what's going on and what the results and treatment options are. he didn't rush when talking to me like some doctors do, he was very patient and caring and answered all my questions. so was the ekg nurse/tech ,the phlebotomist and the lady who did my ultrasound.

there was no evidence for active cardiopulmonary disease. there was no evidence for congestive heart failure on my chest x ray. no evidence of pneunothorax (a collapsed lung), and the osseous structures are intact. he said i need to drink more water because my water levels were lower than they should be but otherwise "my tests results came back better than his." but i do have gerd, gastritis, and i have several small gallstones. the doctor said they're tiny but they're there. he prescribed me antibiotics and several meds for gerd and gastritis and recommended a follow up with a gastroenterologist. 

we got there at 4am and left at 7am. not too bad for an emergency room visit, especially considering all the tests i did. glad this hospital is only 5 miles from my house!

on march 6, 2018 my wife was admitted to amg on gibson, for recovery and rehab of her body, after beating the flu at presbyterian hospital - where she was for over three weeks in acu.

my wife was 54 yrs old and not of the senior citizen level - which their facility looked to have been the main type of patients in the rooms, so i really don't think they were qualified for the admittance of my wife.

the doctor who they assigned to her was a neurosurgeon and was employed with amg for only one day, and refused to look at her chart before he boldly and consistently refused me to speak for her.  i had to go to the ceo in order for them to understand that he wasn't going to do any work with her, until he reviewed her file.  he adamantly was angered that i stood up to him.  he even tried to leave the conference after i pointed out to the ceo what he was doing.

the same atmosphere was present with the supposedly "head nurse", who on the first day, gave me a list of things i was allowed to do - primarily, allowed to participate in every step of the care they were to provide.  she continuously was aggitated at my requested and constantly denied my participation.

even when my wife's eyes rolled into the back of her head and i screamed for help and no one came and then had to go and get a nurse to help myself, when i got back, and my wife seemed to have recovered from that moment, they looked at me and all they said was, "well she seems to be okay now."  they did not do anything but scoff at me and her.  even then, they had an intern stay to help my wife with a bed adjustment, and the same thing occurred again, while the intern witnessed it.  i again requested some help. and the intern looked at me with, "what would you expect me to do?" - and thus, did not even bother to back me up when i said it happened again.

the atmosphere i witnessed at this facility was totally against me and my wife's care. 
it was not in the least caring, supportive and helpful - and all i was trying to get the best care for my wife.

i will admit that the assigned neurologists and the nutritionists were helpful and took care of her as much as they could, but others - no they were not.

they failed time and time again.

after 5 days of this nonsense, i finally was able to speak with the ceo, kari, and we agreed that in two weeks time, my wife would be able to go home after her body had been rehabilitated.

the next day i video recorded how long it would take for the nurse to come and assist her.  after an hour of waiting, i had to go to the nurses station to ask for the help. so again, it showed me his much they really cared and how long they would take for them to respond to a "call by the patient".  one day i was escorted from my wife's side because of my requests.

my wife died in their care two days later on march 13, 2018.

i would advise everyone to either choose a different facility, or be like me, and show them that their own documents allow the family to participate in the care they supposedly say they offer.

keep them on their toes if you want the best care for your loved one - as they apparently don't think they should.

beware and think twice before you use this service.

dr. kosari is a terrible, careless, incompetent surgeon. do not trust him. i've made that mistake twice, so i'm not sure which of us is the bigger idiot. i've tried to summarize my experience with him below, but happy to describe in more detail through message for those considering a surgery with dr. kosari.

in 2013, i started to develop an umbilical hernia just above my belly button. it was never that noticeable, but in the spring of 2019, it had grown just enough to always be noticeable to me. i was referred to dr. kosari. i thought that the reputation of cedars-sinai would hold, but i was wrong.

in the examination, dr. kosari was friendly, but clearly rushed. he let me know he only had about 10 minutes. i explained i'd had the hernia for a few years and, while seated, he asked me to lift my shirt, briefly touched the belly button (literally for less than a second) where it was visible and that was it for the exam. he said he'd recommend doing the surgery with stitches, not mesh. knowing nothing about the difference, i trusted his judgment.

the day of the surgery, i was a bit tense as this was my first surgery. i was also concerned he had not adequately inspected the hernia (and he had not ordered any type of ultrasound). i waited for about 2 hours and then they took me in to prepare me. when i saw dr. kosari before the surgery, i explicitly asked him, "so you are going to be able to fix not only the part below the belly button, but also above it, right?" dr. kosari responded, "yes, don't worry. once we're in, we'll be able to check it all to see what we're dealing with."

i woke up after the procedure and went home. i had the surgery on friday, sep 13. i removed the bandage (which was covering the belly button and surrounding area) and showered on sunday, sep 15. by monday, i felt the hernia above my belly button exactly as before the surgery. panic immediately struck. i called cedars-sinai and was able to tell dr. kosari's nurse i felt a bulge exactly like the hernia, and she told me to just come in for my checkup in 2 weeks for dr. kosari to examine it.

when dr. kosari examined me, he tried to say there was nothing wrong, or that it was something else (like a result from the surgery or a problem with "skin" being "detached"). i told him, "no...i am 100% sure this is the same hernia i've had...it feels exactly the same." he told me to come back in 4 more weeks after the recovery period "to see if it's still there." that really aggravated me, i left the appointment knowing i still had the hernia, but he wouldn't acknowledge it.

at the next appointment, he acknowledged i still had a hernia, but never acknowledged it was because of his carelessness. compared to the first surgery, he was pushing much more strongly for not operating again. i think it's because it would make him look bad to have to repeat the exact same surgery, but i scheduled a follow up surgery for dec 3 anyway to get it dealt with once and for all (had already pretty much met my out of pocket max, so thought why not - and couldn't get in to ucla before the end of the calendar year - book ahead!).

on dec 3, i had the second surgery, and this time we did an ultrasound before the surgery. again, he did not recommend mesh, just a single stitch he said. this time, i didn't notice the hernia for a few weeks, but could definitely feel a slight bump, which i thought might be the stitch or something. now, just over 6 weeks since the second surgery, i still have the hernia. i can feel it exactly the same as i used to.

after one surgery, i'd expect a hernia to be fixed, at least for a few years before it might recur. after two surgeries, i would really expect a hernia to be fixed. now, after spending thousands of dollars, taking months off from the gym for two separate recoveries, and still having the problem that was supposed to be fixed, i'm so filled with anger and frustration about this "doctor." he is careless, negligent, or uses poor judgment in making choices for his patients' care. 

please, do not select this doctor. i will be seeing dr. chen from ucla instead....happy to compare my experience after my third hernia surgery for the same hernia. in my last check-up after the second surgery, dr. kosari told me, "if it comes back let me know and we can go back in there with the mesh." to myself, i thought this moron will never touch my body again. don't let yourself become another one of his mistakes. i will forever regret it, but hopefully i can get a successful surgery from ucla and eventually put this behind me. but i'm sure i will continue to live with the nightmares about the hernia problems that i've had ever since the first surgery was unsuccessful, i hope you can learn from my pain and experience to avoid the same experience with this terrible doctor. cedars-sinai should not allow this man to be operating under their name.

as they say, "fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice shame on me." he won't be fooling me a third time.

we tried to explain this to the charge nurse pearline o'connor hill (middle aged white woman with straight brown shoulder length hair and black glasses). she angrily blurted out, "the new patient!?" and when we looked at her in confusion, she asked "or you're the new patient!?". we confirmed that he had just been admitted, and pearline commanded a younger nurse to get the a.m.a. form. it was presented on the desk and he was repeatedly urged to sign it. we didn't know what the form was and pearline refused to explain it. we tried to ask again about returning for the next round of antibiotics, and she said "you want to leave the hospital and then come back to the er!?" and stared at us with furious disgust. she wouldn't listen to us or answer our questions. i realized that we would need to get away from his woman in order to seek medical care. he did like she wanted and signed the paper, at which point she commanded the younger nurse to remove his iv and cut off his hospital bracelet. we quickly went to the elevators to escape the furious charge nurse who angrily stared us down as we walked away. 

my boyfriend was exhausted after already having been at the hospital for 5 hours and just wanted to go home and get some sleep. i insisted that we return to the er doctor to ask him what to do. it felt absolutely crazy that i was having to help my sick boyfriend around the hospital building through the parking lot in the middle of the night to seek medical care! when we returned to the er, the er doctor was confused to see us, but when we explained what happened, he was shocked and appalled. he said my boyfriend wasn't even eligible for an a.m.a. form because he has sepsis, and that he would make some calls. 

while we waited, many other medical professionals were confused to see us in the er again but were shocked and apologetic after learnging what had happened. eventually shelly schwartz arrived, identifying herself as the head of nurses. we explained what happened, and asked again if he could go home to rest and return in the morning because we never got an answer to that question. she said that since he was admitted, he needed to remain under hospital care. that was fine, at which point we asked if it would be possible for him to get a quieter room. at about 3am we were taken to another room. he was hospitalized for 5 days and underwent surgery. 

we have no complaints about the care received from that point on, although the hospital visit was spent in fear of pearline o'connor hill showing up and what she might do, since she was clearly unstable and my boyfriend was in an extremely vulnerable situation. 

pearline hill's inexcusable and outrageous behavior could have resulted in my boyfriend's death. she was inexplicably furious at us and aggressively demanded he sign a form she refused to explain. who knows how many patients she's done this to, people who were alone or too sick to persist to receive medical help. my boyfriend was exhausted and confused, but thank god i was there with him to guide him back to the er to find medical help. had i not been there, he would've gone home to get some rest, gone into septic shock and died. i cannot understand why an otherwise friendly and professional hospital would employ someone that is such a clear liability and danger to patients.

staff friendliness is the first thing that stood out on a recent visit to a family member. 
excellent location, right off major expressway with plenty of free parking. secured facility, that i found to be clean & quiet. the staff was very attentive, thorough yet, gentle attending to the needs of my family member. they were constantly checking vitals, providing treatments, changing bedding and made themselves known & available to the the family.

my father was at the rml pulmonary rehab facility in chicago recovering from a triple bypass that was done on him. i came after work to visit him on august 22 as i did daily and i arrived about 715pm. when i walked over to my dad, i found him covered in a thick substance, which my husband realized was his feeding tube food. the feeding tube was supposed to of been flushed every couple of hours because of how sticky the substance is. the nurse was not following protocol and was not flushing, which resulted in the tubing to clog and explode all over my dad, and him laying in it for hours. he was calling the call button, but they were not responding physically. they would respond with "what can i help you with?" he has a trach and was not able to talk! which they should of known! i even hit the call button to see if the would come. someone came on the microphone but i wanted to see if they would respond to knowing he was a trach patient, so i kept silent. they turned off the microphone and light, and never checked on him. i was beyond mad, and ran into the hall and yelled for a nurse. 3 cnas attempted to "unblock" his tubing which was obviously completely blocked at this point, and all 3 of those cnas looked very stupid. finally his nurse arrived and realized the issue. than they all left the room to let me father continue to sit in his "food". after 15 more minutes of him sitting there and no one taking action, i took it upon myself to start cleaning him. he had been sitting in his food for 3+ hours at this point! once they realized i was taking things into my own hands, they rushed into the room to clean him up. this is completely unacceptable of the nurse, who should of known better. this is completely unacceptable of the facility as a whole to treat their patients this way. i guarantee this is happening to other patients, as the staff there had horrible bedside manners rn & cnas. luckily, i was able to complaint enough the following day to get him moved immediately. we had constant visitors the next 24 hours on my dad to watch the staff's actions to ensure this didn't happen again. my heart goes out to all the patients and their family's there. i hope they are able to leave that horrible facility asap. but this rn & facility need to be held accountable for their actions!

i wish there was no stars on this hell hole on yelp cause this place doesn't deserve any!

thanks to the extremely kind and attentive doctor who examined my friend's leg, he quickly realized the blood supply to her foot had been cut off and in a very short while she would lose her foot altogether.

the e.r. staff sprang into action, there must have been 10 people cutting her pants off of her, hooking up her i.v.'s, having her sign papers, dispatching an ambulance to transport her to pomona valley hosp. trauma unit (which seemed to arrive within minutes), cleaning her wound, etc.... they were all extremely kind, understanding and very very professional.

my deepest gratitude to each and everyone of you at queen of the valley as well as at pomona valley for taking such great care of my friend. the surgeon at pomona valley was able to save her foot.

recently  my daughter  stayed in icu. i witnessed  mso many mistakes. meds were not given according  to doctors orders be abuse shift change nurses were  not organized. when my daughter  was struggling  and trying  to get out of the bed and i reported  it i was told they were allowed  to move around  until  someone  finally  got around  to checking.. one nurse aid named samantha who was lazy left my daughter lying puddled up in the bottom of the bed several times and she had ard time breathing and not resting and she said to leave her like that so that she would  not be able  to get out and she would  not have to check on her at the same time. all night long she was lau6 with her friends and they even kept me awake and i was not a patient  who needed to rest because  they became  easily  agitated.  i was there for a week and saw so many things that made me sad...but there were also many more who were caring . i do not ever leave my loved ones alone e in the hospital  ever.

review:
i can't say enough good about university hospitals. i recently had a major surgery at this location. all of the doctors, staff, anesthesiologist, etc were beyond wonderful. they really are genuine, caring, patient and i had no doubt that i was in the best of hands. 

the food choices were actually vegetarian friendly and really tasty for a hospital. and the elder brit volunteer by the name of jean calmed everyone in the pre-op waiting area. chatting with her really put my mind at ease, she was so lovely. 

i have to say that i was absolutely scared out of my wits that i had to have a surgery. it was my first one ever with a 6-8 week recovery time. now i have a better idea of what to expect should there be a next time. i will continue my relationship with uh hospitals as long as i live in northeast ohio. they really are top notch. (alot more compassionate than cleveland clinic).

i have heard some horror stories about the place, but after my wife had a devastating stroke, and spent two weeks here, i found nothing to complain about.

staff was totally compassionate and professional. they quickly did her cat scan. she had a massive hemorrhage, and they thought she would die in the emergency room. they arranged a video consult with a neurosurgeon in albuquerque, since there is none in taos. he explained there was nothing to be done as far as surgery...we could only wait and hope she would recover.

for a week, she drifted in and out of a coma as almost a dozen friends and family streamed in from around the country to be at her side. the hospital took incredible care of her, and all of us. they made us feel so comfortable, people kept referring to it as the hotel, instead of the hospital. when i complained about the fold out chair i was sleeping in, they found me a better one. staff was caring and compassionate. doctors were accessible and informative. i can't think of anything i wish they would have done that they did not do.

at the end of the first week, when most of our friends had to leave, the cafeteria manager helped arrange a thank you gathering and provided snacks at no charge. the meals there were cheap and excellent. 

after the first week, my wife came out of the coma and started to get better. they arranged for her to move to a skilled nursing facility in albuquerque. her recovery has been miraculous.  

i love our little hospital.

i am pretty amazed at some of the bad reviews here. at least two of them are from people upset that the hospital did not provide them transportation home. looks like a lot of people just don't understand that, in the er, its not first come, first serve. they treat the sickest first. we've been the the er 3 times, and found it totally professional.

if i could give zero i would. my daughter got stomach virus. the wait has been two hours and we r still waiting!!. people rude. avoid!!! they are the only hospital in town snd they know it. waiting room full of people and they just don't care. my daughter just throws up every 15 minutes. shame on any doctor who works here. we are from austin,tx and have never waited this long. they say that the rooms are full but i have gone to our hospital at home and they would line us up in the hallway and treat us there. do not retire in this town! you will likely die in the waiting room. what a nightmare.
the doctors and nurses- aside from one exceptionally rude er nurse- are great. the registration folk are across the board (pun intended) a nightmare.

on sunday, dec 1st, our daughter's friends brought her to prisma health baptist, after bringing her to urgent care, which they were not able to draw blood and test it. they were worthless. 
when they brought her to prisma health baptist emergency room, the staff was rude and so unprofessional to the group of girls, saying that they were "sorority girls". they would not test our daughter and the doctor did not believe she had mono. they did not take the girls seriously at all. this was extremely upsetting to us, since they are of age college students! they should be treated as adults and taken seriously, especially when they are sick!   we drove from summerville, sc to columbia, sc an hour and 30 minutes away. they started drawing blood and testing her when we arrived in the emergency. this is totally unacceptable and should have been done when our daughter was first in with the doctor! the doctor brought back the results and our daughter had mononucleosis. they only said that she should take motrin and extra strength tylenol every 3 hours switching off when she has a fever. they said if she has any symptoms, such as vomiting, jaundice (yellow) face and skin, dark urine, pain in abdomen to bring her back. we left and brought her back to her dorm room.  on tuesday, dec 3, our daughter's roommate called and she had all the symptoms that the emergency rooms said, so i drove up to columbia, sc and brought her to musc in charleston, sc. they admitted her into the hospital and tested her and diagnosed her with mononucleosis and cold agglutinin disease. 
we will never take our daughter back to prisma health baptist emergency room! we will always bring her to musc from now on, since they have the best doctors in the state and took the best care of her, which was so much appreciated. they were so professional and caring and updated us on our daughter's status regularly.

your better off dead than going to this place.

my 90 y.o. mother and her 97 y.o. husband are residents of an assisted living facility. on sunday 2-9-20 my mother couldn`t get out of bed. my step dad called 911. she was taken to nfrm by rescue at around 8:00 am. by the time i drove from jacksonville, picked up my step dad and got to the er it was close to 11:00 am. they had sedated her in order to examine her as she has dementia and becomes agitated if her husband is not with her. upon our arrival she was sedated and sleeping. their test could not find anything wrong with her but they wanted to admit her for observation. we asked when she would be admitted and moved to a room. they told us the did not have any beds available at this time . we were concerned  and didn`t want to leave her but didn`t want to watch her sleep for hours. upon my request the er nurse gave me her cell phone # and told us to call in a couple hours and she would let us know if she was awake. i called the # at 2:00 and no answer, 3:00 same results. finally at 4:00 we just showed up. she had been moved to a different room and was basically unattended as she was waiting for a room to become available. we asked the staff if her husband would be allowed to stay with her in the room as she becomes agitated and uncooperative if separated from him. we were told by a couple er nurses that it wouldn`t be a problem and they would put a recliner in the room next to her bed. so here we are in a er room awaiting a room. one chair for us to sit on  which we gave to my step-dad while my niece and i stood. mom was still out of it. still waiting for a room to become available. a board in the room shows that some test were ordered and completed and others were pending. we asked about which test were done and the results but nursing staff was unable to give us answers. we asked which test were pending and the answer was the same. we are getting mad that we are just in a room with no idea whats going on or when a room will be available. finally about 7:00 pm they told us a room was available but it had to be cleaned. we waited and waited. finally the nurse tells us that because multiple room became available at the same time housekeeping had to clean them in the order of the vacancy so we had to wait longer for them to clean her assigned room.

i don`t remember what time we got to the room but i again asked the guy transporting her about her husband staying in the room. his response: that`s not a problem. in the process of transferring her to the bed it was discovered she had been laying in her own urine for quite awhile. i then asked her nurse about her husband staying in the room and the answer was "absolutely not". this is the women`s floor and no men were allowed to stay in the room. they said he could sleep in a recliner at the end of the hallway, in the visitors area. i asked to speak to the charge nurse and she reiterated the same thing. she didn`t get that i was upset because everyone up to this point had stated "no problem" and at the last minute she says no! major communication breakdown. this lack of communication causes us problems and get my mother and step-dad to become upset. in addition, even though they had a list of her meds it took them until the next day to admin. to her.

because they found no medical reason to treat they ordered pt to get her up and moving. i spent 2 whole days next to her bed and never saw a physical therapist. i spoke to the case manager about transferring her to a rehab facility and she stated she sent referrals to 2 places and has not heard from either. 

in the meantime my mother becomes delusional, agitated and "talking crazy" i told the nursing staff i believe my mother has a uti as i have seen this behavior before and know it can be caused by a uti. the nurse stated she was checked for a uti in the emergency room and was negative. talked to the dr. about it and she denied a uti stating my mom`s dementia along with a new environment caused her to be confused.my niece along with her father refused to accept this explanation and demanded she be tested again for a uti. guess what ? positive for a uti. antibiotic iv was administered and she is slowly recovering from the delusions.

still haven`t seen the pt. follow up with the 5th floor case manager revealed that we didn`t hear from terrace view rehab because referral was not submitted.

my mom was finally transferred to a rehab facility where she can get the help she needs. all of my family agrees that the hospital experience at nfrmc was terrible and if my mom had stayed there any longer they may have killed her. i have never been a patient in a hospital but  i have been in a bunch of them. this was the most disorganized and neglectful place i have ever been. we were angry when she was sent there by brookdale because our hospital of choice was shands.

the second time i had recently had a very long flight and had swelling in one leg and was concerned it could be a blood clot. i was quickly called back for a blood test to rule out deep vein thrombosis and ended up waiting in a back staging area for about an hour and a half for the results. again, a super friendly pa introduced herself and explained what they were going to do and what the tests were for. much appreciated. 

eventually, i found that i was going to also have a vascular ultrasound of my leg to rule out the blood clot which was about another hour or so and then i was just waiting to be discharged or find out what was happening from there while the radiologist read my scans. 

the internal waiting room was a bit cold and uncomfortable but it is what it is.  it's a hospital. 

this er is pretty fast and efficient and the staff are friendly and seem to really care.  my only issue is that both times i've only spoken to a p.a. or a nurse.  while i understand the doctors are busy, for the cost, it would be nice to be seen and spoken to by one of them.  on the most recent visit last week, my discharge was done by the nurse who didn't really answer my questions and said they didn't actually know what was wrong with me, but they had ruled out a blood clot so good luck and follow up with my pcp.  

for however many thousands of dollars i spent - that was disappointing.

my mom had to have a small surgical procedure for trigger finger at noon, but had to arrive at 11:00 am. the night before, dr. hubbard's office called to say there was a cancellation so come in at 10:15 am, which we did. 

after checking in, we sat for quite some time before she was called to go into the surgical area, about 45 minutes. after some time, about 30 minutes, a nurse came out to say, "your mom is still waiting because someone is ahead of her, and yeah, i know, they had her come in early, but the dr ran around for 45 minutes cause that's what they do. so as soon as she goes in, we'll let you know." at 11:55, another nurse came out to say she was going in, but according to my mom, it was actually another 20 minutes in a freezing cold room before she was taken in for the procedure. 

here's what seems so purposely sh***y to me, coming out to say my mom was nowhere near ready to be operated on, we were made to come in 45 minutes sooner just to be told the dr ran around for that time, and she wound up going in later than she was originally scheduled. anyone familiar with gang stalking knows this is common behavior for us ti's to put up with. 

on top of all that, when my mom saw the dr. at his office, she had told him about severe pain in her thumb joint. instead of telling her she could get a cortisone shot, he said it was arthritis and nothing could be done except wear a brace, which she paid $60 for and it makes her hand hurt more. before she had the surgery, she told him about the brace not working and the pain so he gave her a cortisone shot. gee, nothing like taking advantage/milking an 84 year old woman on a fixed income.

i was at this hospital for 8 hours waiting for a loved one after surgery. the care seemed to be good but i'm having a hard time getting past the filthy unsanitary bathrooms. i have never seen bathrooms like this in any hospital i've ever been in. i used three different bathrooms and each was as dirty as the next it was truly disgusting. every garbage pail was over flowing. this was in the millstein building.
fac_name: Milstein Building - New York Presbyterian Hospital

review: don't send your loved ones here, go down to weill cornell. the hospital is quite dirty and the staff is rude. more importantly, they are very slow to communicate about a treatment plan and in fact slow to administer anything beyond the most basic of care. my relative has not received any treatment beyond palliative care in almost 2 weeks with absolutely no communication from the care team as to options. don't go here if your life depends on it - they aren't willing to take heroic measures to save lives here. truly a terrible hospital.
fac_name: Milstein Building - New York Presbyterian Hospital

review: while waiting for my mother in the patient waiting area in millstein 3rd floor. i went to use the restroom and it was disgusting. to think that this is suppose to be such a great hospital. the toilet and even hand washing sink was full of scum and mildew. the trash bin overflowing. where is management. this is totally unacceptable. to add on top of that the number of visitors and visiting hours are ridiculous.. you cut off visiting hours and on top of that only two visitors at time.
fac_name: Milstein Building - New York Presbyterian Hospital

review:
this was the first time i have been to the hospital. i was here for the woman's and children's department. the parking deck was pretty hectic and you have to exit the deck by going to the top floor. you also have to pay for parking - they take cards.
i was a new patient here. i arrived early for my appointment and the receptionists were kind. they were very thorough with labs and their questions. i waited 45 minutes in my room for my meeting with my gynecologist and the nurse came in and told me they will be another hour and a half because of emergency surgery. so, after driving a hour for this location i was not seen by a doctor unfortunately and had to head home and reschedule my appointment, which is a month from now. i get that things happen and doctors have priorities; however it was extremely disappointing. thank goodness my symptoms are manageable! i look forward to having a better experience in a month.

i'd give this place no starts if possible.  my son went last night to the er there as he was in terrible pain and thought he had a kidney stone.  he begged and begged to see a doctor while vomiting on their front desk.  no one ever saw him.  they said they had no rooms.  he didn't need a room.  he needed someone to look at him.  it might have been food poisoning as he finally felt better after throwing up there four times.

how the hell does this place not send a doctor to look at him after an hour of being in pain?????  so much for the south.  i'm in ny and trust me this wouldn't happen at my er room.  this place sucks the big one.

this hospital is the worst!!!  ridiculous wait time in the er with uninterested, unengaged staff...we couldn't get anyone to come help us while we were waiting on a doctor and my poor elderly mother peed in the bed!!! no one would make eye contact to help us. and when she was admitted to the hospital, it wasn't safe for me to leave her by herself because the staff wouldn't come when she called and she kept having to poop and pee on herself, waiting for help. furthermore, she was an extreme fall risk, and the staff disabled the bed alarm in her room and just set up a portable potty by her bedside for her to use. also, both her arms were bruised badly up and down because no one could get a decent pick line in. rather than call on a pick team to come do it professionally, they kept sticking her over and over and over and over. i've never met so many unprofessional, uncaring hospital staff in my life. i would never take someone i love and want to survive to this hospital!!!

went to aspirus to visit with lynn kern for my first obgyn appointment. this is my first pregnancy so i was excited but nervous. the nurse who greeted me was very much robot-ish. not the most friendly to start with. when i was met with lynn she stated she need to be fast because she had another  patient she was helping.. granted i was early for my appointment and this was my scheduled time with her. anyways i proceeded and didnt ask much because i'm still very new to this all. once she start the bedside ultrasound she asked if was still pregnant.. obviously i was confused but said yes. about a minute and a half rolls by and she decides this was taking too long and to send me to an ultrasound. i cried the whole way there.. finally in the ultrasound they confirmed a valid pregnancy. however i'm so upset she couldnt have taken a few extra minutes with the bedside ultrasound.. i'm now stuck with a $700 ultrasound bill that i believe was not needed at all. i'm with marshfield clinic now and much happier!
room was filthy. staff overworked. no customer relations. only good thing was our surgeon who goes other places also. check it out beforehand if you can.

did something to my knee so went in for an x-ray after visiting primary care.

very small hospital but super pleasant front desk and no wait for imaging

i'm waiting for insurance for updates soine mri so i was glad to hear they have mri as well

was accused of only wanting drugs and shelter after being sent to their emergency room from a doctors appointment. it was extremely offensive not only because i am not a drug user, but also because i was dressed professionally (i was supposed to go into work after my doctors appointment that morning) so clearly i'm not living on the streets. the doctor that accused me of wanting drugs never came back in after my pee test came back clean, but the doctor that took over was no better. they discharged me while i was still actively showing the symptoms i came in for and shortly after leaving i lost consciousness, but refused to go back. i will be using my secondary insurance to receive care at ahn hospitals from now on.

worst service from the front counter lady at the er. i was rushing to take my brother when his fever was 105 degrees and asking for the paper work to fill it out for him. i had politely asked for the paper that we need fill out in order to check in and she very absurdly just said "first of all who are you?" and held it down and said "my brother is having an emergency can i get the paper that we need to check in?" and she decided to reply rudely with " that's not how we say it here, you're not saying it right." what if english was my second language or if i had speech impediment. this looks very bad considering she is working at a hospital. i didn't catch her name considering she was turning to the side with her name badge but it was the african-american lady with glasses.

this place is a pit, filthy & disorganized. the staff are rude & hostile. no one knows the answer to anything. my spouse has been waiting on a gurney for 2 hours for a bed. our hoc is st. jude but they were full. he will be transferred asap. choosing this dump was a huge mistake. stay away!

well besides one rude er dr me whole experience was wonderful. not even in my room yet all the staff making jokes making me feel welcome. props to su in icu. your the bomb. all of you guys. i felt like a king there. to all the icu staff. i b.v wish i could give this experience  10 star. huge rooms nice po privacy.  i hope i get dick again just to go see them. i

only reason i'm writing this review is for the rn silvia . the dr was so unprofessional and disregarded me and made me feel stupid for coming in. but then this wonderful nurse came in and made me feel heard and comfortable and she reassured me. she is someone who does this job because she generally cares for the patients unlike the dr who does it for the paycheck. thank you silvia

wow wow wow!!! 
best service ever!!! 
had my baby here 2 weeks ago and i can see why everyone on the big island recommends having their baby here. 
can't review the whole hospital but the women's center as well as the birthing family unit is amazing! so coordinated.
all my pre pregnancy was managed by the 4 midwives and the 3 obgyns here. they try to get you to meet everyone because everyone takes call and who knows what day you will be in labor. 
thank goodness we live 5min away because labor is no joke. 
akiko and dr. kong were life savers! didn't take a birthing class because i knew my birth wasn't gonna be like what they said. as soon as i arrived they pushed for me to get a epi because i wanted one and i got one within 15min of arriving. thank the lord. but this hospital is well known for having a major percentage of non anesthesia and non c section births. to each their own! 
after 12 hours in labor with 2 hours of active labor, i had round the clock service for 48hours by multiple nurses with great food! 
skin to skin contact immediately with 1 hour without any measurements or doctors. just me my hubby and our baby interrupted. we even got delayed cord clamping. they are very attentive to what you want with your birth plan. 
i hope to have another child

good for routine things:  immunizations, sinus infection, urinary tract infection, general checkups, physical therapy, etc. they also have an er.  staff is friendly, patient, and calm, the interior has beautiful hardwood floors and you can see hawaiian quilts and other displays on the walls.  like any hospital, they serve the entire community from infants to elderly, but because it is a smaller community it can have a more comfortable feeling, like you are not just a number. because it is a small community and facility, expect to have a wait. bring a snack and some water if you are the type to get hangry (hungry+angry).

sometimes chronic symptoms or conditions/diseases that need specialists take a long time to get taken care of, or to find the right treatment. you may have to wait for a specialist to come in from honolulu or for an appointment to open up on a lab's fully booked calendar, so there also isn't a lot of choice in this area as a whole.  

i would recommend going to a bigger hospital for rare and severe conditions, but in general this hospital serves a vital need in the community and i'm glad it's here.

had an er visit yesterday due to a sever allergic reaction. it was probably the shortest er visit iv ever had in my life. the doctor and nurses were extremely friendly, helpful, and thoughtful. i'm visiting the big island from the mainland for unknown amount of time and didn't bring any warm clothing on our trip. a nurses brought me multiple blankets to keep me warm and comfortable. hand down one of best er visits i've ever had.

first i must start by saying that i am  picu nurse in new york city so i was not sure what to expect when i needed to go to the emergency room here on the big island bc i thought i may have a blood clot in my leg after the long flight . to my surprise i received excellent, efficient & quick care , even better than i have received in some of the hospitals i have been back at home . dr gary goldberg was amazing , he was in to see me right away , kept checking on me & had impeccable bedside manner. he updated me on my results as they came in & luckily everything was negative. my nurse ashely was also just as terrific, attentive & kept me updated too. the us tech, x-ray tech & everyone i came in contact with was so professional that i felt the need to commend them & write a review. my standards are very high & you guys all rock , thank you for the excellent care you gave me ! mahalo! don't be fooled by the small town vibe , they really know what they r doing up in waimea!!

best children's hospital in lubbock!!!! we've always had wonderful experiences there!!!! they have the best doctors!!!! kind of sad that my son will be turning 18 soon and won't be able to go here when he needs to. but he can go to the covenant medical center hospital for adults, which is just as great!!!!!

st. luke's is the reason that healthcare in this country has such a bad reputation. my daughter and i got the flu while on a ski vacation at tamarack and unfortunately the only thing open in the area was st lukes. we spent about 20 minutes waiting for a doctor and when he came in he spent abut 5 minutes telling us that we definitely had the flu but did no tests and gave us no medicine. we just received a bill for over $1200 after insurance for the visit, an amazing rip off. we will never use a st luke's ever again and i suggest you never attend their if you are in central idaho or any area they serve.

i rarely would dive into being happy about being in a hospital. however i really think this place deserves to be recognized. from the moment i came into the er to being admitted and being in the main hospital, i have been treated like i'm a guest at a 5 star hotel. doctors were methodical, listened, patient, and not in a hurry. the staff and nurses have been exactly the same and incredibly personable/friendly. they have gone out of their way to keep me as comfortable as possible and treat me like i was the only one that mattered. when was the last time you could say that about a hospital visit? this is a remarkable hospital and team. thank you leeza, laura, rebecca, and dr. lewis for the amazing care you've been providing me. it is truly appreciated.

happy holidays! the best place to bring your children for medical needs!  !
a safe place to be. merry christmas

it's got to be one of the dirtiest hospitals i've been in understaffed not enough rn  nurses my father stayed here different doctors all the time never knew what medication he was really on worst place i wouldn't recommend it

p.a stephens decided that having labs drawn on my son in the e.r were not important. he is 10 years old have chest pain it was hard to breath shaky dizzy yes it was slightly better since we were in the room but she didnt want labs. she said he looked fine, yes someone may look fine but until labs are drawn you wont fully known unless your a mind reader..... i used to work here very disappointed.  i work at moffitt now an we  dont asses people by assuming.  we actually get evidence to help dmfind a solution

i went for my first mammogram at memorial hospital west and was highly impressed!! check in was fast and efficient. i was personally walked to the area to wait by a nice lady. i was explained every step of the process. they had a nice changing area and even had coffee and little cookies/crackers in the waiting area. the woman who performed my mammogram was so professional. she explained everything and told me she has been doing this for 30 years. i was amazed how quickly i received my results, which revealed no cancer thankfully. i was treated very well and not like just another number. 

a friend of mine was diagnosed with breast cancer and was very impressed with the care at this hospital. her nurse was truly caring and made my friend feel as much as ease as you can in that situation.

went to the hospital because my big toe was cut badly and it needed mending. the emergency room was excellent , the doctor and nurse who helped me had really good bed side manners. my big toe was glued and
bandaged up and off i went home. thank you for the excellent care and for attending to my bleeding toe promptly. parking was easy.

came here hoping that i would be able to give birth to my daughter. after moving to miami  at 32 weeks, no obgyn would take me in because i was so late and the hospital i was affiliated with in hawaii didn't have any nearby hospitals in miami, their nearest location was in  jacksonville. however, when i felt contractions coming, i waited about 5 hours until they were more consistent and closer together and checked into the hospital. they immediately took me in, i had to do some paperwork, give them my prenatal records from hawaii, and they didn't give me a hard time at all. everyone was nice and expedient and they assured me that everything was going to be okay. i was in labor for 12 hours and they didn't rush a c-section and didn't try to transfer me anywhere. they were persistent ad supportive and the nurses made sure i was hydrated and gave me a clear liquid diet (i didn't eat  since the day before). when my daughter came they moved me to a room within hours and made sure i was comfortable the whole time. nurses and doctors were very informative and they were strict to make sure i was feeding baby on time and that  she was able to come home with me within the 2 days (she was coombs positive and had to be put on the blanket for jaundice). i love this hospital and the people in it. definitely recommend!

i was in the e.r. two days ago.  the staff was absolutely wonderful.  janelle, karen, elvie and jessica were all very pleasant, caring, considerate, used good infection control technique and i truly felt well cared for. they all deserve a 5 star rating.    this evening i called and the "nurse" by the name of seneca was arrogant, rude, condescending, uncaring and had a very nasty tone of voice.  my fiance heard the conversation and was shocked that a nurse from santa ynez cottage hospital would treat someone that way.  her tone of voice made me feel like a child who was being scolded. my discharge papers stated that if no improvement to return to e.r.  my call was to confirm that even though i have an appointment with my primary doctor on thursday that i could come back in.  she told me that i should go to marian hospital closer to my home if i felt it was an emergency. i told her that it is not an emergency but am still in severe pain and the ibuprofen was not working.   myself and my entire family always go to santa ynez cottage hospital because of the kind way that we are treated by staff.  not any more.  this person needs to find a different profession because of the way she speaks to the human race

excellent er doctor and nurses
thank you so much for the great care for my husband

my mom had a heart ultrasound done 9 days ago, and when she went to her the follow-up appointment with her cardiologist today, they said the report had not yet been done.  her appointment with the cardiologist was originally scheduled for yesterday, so we called the afternoon before to make sure they could obtain the report.  we also called advent health to ask them to fax over the report.  i've had a lot of imaging, and i've never known a report to take more than 48-72 hours to write.  if the report truly hasn't been written by the radiologist, that's dangerous.  if it's been overlooked in terms of getting it to the doctor, that shows incompetence.  i tried to call 407-303-4025 to get an explanation and i didn't get an answer after about 25 rings.

beautiful hospital but questionable care.
 i have had problems with every provider.
i keep getting a bill for my primary care annual physical when i have a no co-pay coverage for annual physicals. 
 the gastro-hepatology group was difficult to contact. they left a message at 4:55 pm that there was a problem with my prescription.

  they also gave me a referral to the ent group at advent health for throat problems.  i waited a week and contacted the ent group.  they said they did not understand the referral since the doctor i was referred to did not handle throat issues.  wrong referral and no call to let me know that?

my father stayed at this location for only one night, we couldn't let him stay there any longer, as soon as i entered the facility it was loud, there were random patients everywhere in the hallways unattended, the facility was old, small, looked very ghetto and depressing, you can hear everyones conversation out in the hallway. my dad was unable to sleep the first night there because that place was never quite and it was either his roommate was on his phone 24/7 or the smell and rude nurses barging in out loud with out considering that the other patient might be sleeping. there were loud beeping sounds that the nurses weren't able to turn down. my dad is the type of patient that needs a lot of attention he always needs help to do anything, he called out for a nurse multiple times so someone can help him go to the restroom and no one showed up until he tried doing it himself and accidentally flipping over the table and they still didn't show up. there was no place for my dad to leave some of his belongings and his over head lamp was taped together from falling apart and a broken tv that was wrapped in a plastic bag, how can anyone get better at this place when it's literally a hell hole for sick patients! do not let your loved ones into this place! when we took my dad out the nurses warned us if he left no other hospital will accept him as a patient!! what kind of bull sh*t is that!?!

where to start. this hospital is filthy dirty. they keep the medicines for all patients in the room with the patients in a cabinet that has a lock with a note saying by law it must be locked and they cover the lock with a towel so it won't lock so they don't have to use a key. in addition all the meds are mixed up and not kept separate per each patient and they keep digging trying to figure out what belongs to what patient. the other night they could not find my mother's insulin and after 2 hours had still not found and and she did not get her insulin.  in addition protocol is that insulin should be kept refrigerated and at this hospital it is not. today they had the wrong patients medicine on my mothers iv pole and had it administered and going in her veins. thank god it was the same medication she was on as they could of killed her but it had another patients name on it. my mother has mersa and the nurses and doctors are not wearing gowns, masks and/or gloves. the hospital she came from nobody could enter her room with out putting on a gown and glove and taking them off before you left.  now 2 days ago she was just diagnosed with cre and still nurses and doctors still  have no gowns, gloves or masks on and she is still in a room with other patients and not isolated. they are passing germs from patient to patient.  this place is a shit show. i want my mother out of this place now and moved to another hospital!!!

review:

review:
i came in for outpatient colonoscopy today. it could not have been a better experience. from the lady that checked me in, to all the pre-op, surgery nurses and doctors and recovery crew, everyone, without fail, was kind and friendly, and very helpful. even staff that weren't involved with me said good morning or hello. that attitude makes a huge difference, especially if you are nervous about a procedure.
i was very impressed indeed. i give 4 stars because the place is old and a little worn around the edges. but i saw people painting while i was there and the lobby is very nice so it seems they are trying to upgrade the ambiance.

review:
there is absolutely no customer service at this hospital.  many times  throughout the six day hoslotalization for my mom, the  right hand didn't  know what the left hand was doing.  there is no protocol in communicating with patients when they are first admitted to the hospital  from the er.  you can wait for 6 hours without hearing from a physician upon being admitted; during regular business hours. 
the fax machine and phones don't work.

review:
i was transferred here from cedars due to some insurance issues. the transfer required me to be open minded as this hospital is visibly older so i gave it a chance. there has been a great lack of communication between the team of people responsible for my case. at first there was uncertainty about if i could eat or not due to a procedure i was supposed to have, the only thing is i wasn't scheduled for any procedures so they had me fasting from 3pm one day until just about 3pm the next day for no reason. i had asked about it and they kept saying they would get ahold of the doctor to ask and find out more information but it took for me to call patient support for them to figure it out. i am in the hospital due to my oxygen levels dropping while ambulating which is a scary thing in itself so they were trying to figure out if i had another blood clot in my lungs that is causing it or if the hole in my heart that is the cause. i have not seen any sense of urgency to try and figure it out. every other doctor that comes in here has said something different, one will say it's a pe the other will say it's the hole. i'm on day 3 no with no definitive diagnosis and it is beyond frustrating. i could keep writing but i'm still here and getting more and more annoyed by the minute. i have encountered 2 nice nurses who did their rounds when they were supposed to but some other staff are not as great. avoid this hospital if you can!

i'll be updating this post until i leave. i'm not getting any answers. these doctors are lazy. i'm asking questions and all i'm getting is "i don't think so"when it should be answered with either yes or no. if you don't know do more research and/or consult another doctor and figure it out!

upon discharge i asked for a work note and the doctor literally said "you work at a clinic, your boss is a doctor he should know". my mind is blown. i should have said and yes i'm a nurse and the way you all operate around this hospital needs to be reported.

review:
below is a detailed description of our experience giving birth here: 

my wife received a total of 18 excruciating cervical checks within 1.5 days of trying to induce! she received 4 doses of cytotec inserted vaginally which caused her to be so sore and sensitive that each cervical exam was beyond painful. several of these could have been eliminated but the hospital was out of the applicator. i mean come on, how do you run out of that? i offered to drive to another nearby hospital to pick one up but they wouldn't allow it. 

because induction didn't work, she had a c-section. the hospital was out of something called a joey pack so they refused to do skin-to-skin once baby was born. after talking to them for awhile, they agreed to allow it. but once baby came, they ignored this request and didn't do skin-to-skin as promised only moments before. 

baby couldn't latch and the nurse told us to feed newborn only 15ml (1/2 oz) of formula at each feeding. this is way too little and is why she lost over 7% weight within 1 day! why would they have purposely told us to under feed her? they also strongly discouraged us from using our own formula since it could only be mixed with sterile water (according to them). even though the nicu had this water, they flat out said the nicu was closed and it was too difficult of a process getting permission to open it. even after waiting until the next morning when the nicu was sure to be open, they insisted it was too difficult getting permission to use the water. really, i mean come on, you've seriously got to be kidding! 

although almost all of the nurses were great, one latin nurse in particular was very rude to us and just unfriendly. i won't post her name here but she was the only nurse at night so we couldn't switch. she is specifically the one in question who gave us all the issues with using our formula that i mentioned above.

instead of getting all the blood work needed at once, they kept forgetting necessary tests which caused our baby to get multiple blood draws that were not necessary. these could have been taken at once to avoid pricking her with the needle so many times! again, communicate better and get your shit together! 

after talking at length with the hospitals pediatrician, we agreed to not administer the hepatitis b vaccine at the hospital. we had to sign papers, talk with several people about it, but it was all agreed we would do it in a few weeks with our own pediatrician on our own schedule. however, after we were discharged and at home, we read through the hospital paperwork and it says that they did administer the hep b vaccine. did they do this behind our backs without our consent or is their paperwork incorrect? how can a hospital make this kind of mistake?

overall, even though we were mostly satisfied with the level of care we received, i would not recommend good samaritan medical center in west palm beach to give birth based on all the issues i mentioned above.

my husband came down with a severe case of the flu three days before our unfortunate experience with good samaritan. his sore throat got so bad that he wasn't able to eat or drink more than occasional small sips of water. he was getting really dehydrated and wasn't able to get fluids down, so we went to good samaritan at 10pm. after waiting for three hours, we finally got a bed and the staff refused to administer iv fluids because (quoting one of the nurses) "this isn't some fancy iv lounge. fluids actually aren't that good for you." we explained that he hadn't been able to drink very much in almost three days, and no one even brought him a cup of water. we sat in the hospital until 2am and only received a steroid shot that was supposed to help his throat. it didn't. we were told there was nothing else they could do and they discharged us. 

overall, staff was flippant, condescending, and inattentive. facilities were dirty (blood spattered on the wall) and treatment was disappointing at best. 

if you're looking for efficient, high quality care, look elsewhere.

they treat black people differently than white people! i heard it with my own ears. they assume black women who are legitimately in pain to be addicts trying to get drugs, so they let them cry in agony for hours before any meds are given. this happened to the woman in the bed next to me. 
lach is the hospital that they send folks with
 medi-cal or no insurance. it's the place where all the negative stereotypes about how women, especially black women, are all perpetrated with abandon. if you think there's no such thing as "white privilege" your dead wrong! i'm a white female, i speak the queens english and i was not subjected to that treatment. even though that woman was literally 4feet away from me. if the nurse was late with my meds, i just had to remind them and ask them to please go get them. and they would. anything i asked for, if they hesitated, i could insist, raise my voice, argue, and it would get done. i had that privilege. at 11pm i could get a cup of tea while the woman in the bed next to me was screaming in pain as several fibroid tumors tried to exit her uterus through her cervix and out her vagina. they gave her a tylenol while they waited for the dr on call to answer his page to approve a stronger med. it was horrific, and in a gd hospital no less. where all life should matter, and keeping to your solemn oath is a privilege

worst hopspital ever!
don't know how people last a night here it's disgusting! if i could rate it  0 stars i would! they let any random homeless people stay there with who knows what sickness they have + not to mention everyone is smoking cigarettes in there! what kind of hospital is this? 3 people in 1 tiny room? & they have machines from the 1900s so glad i left under my own will they wouldn't let me leave & didn't even have a case manager! i still have nightmares of this place

terrible place. my mom was discharged from being in there with hypertensive complications and when she went to the pharmacy to get her much needed meds the doctor had not sent the prescription in yet. she was told it would be in tonight or tomorrow. someone who is prone to hypertensive attacks can not wait until the next morning for their medication. when i called the discharge nurse in unit 4, she was very rude and disrespectful. she actually had the audacity to tell me that if the doctor doesn't send it tonight and she has an attack then she could come back to the er. what????? wth kind of answer is this. it is unethical for a patient to have to wait for their medication to be sent to their pharmacy because the doctor hasn't done it yet. this is ridiculous. patient care should be 1st. i am shocked by this response from the nurse and the doctor's lack of efficiency in his work. not ok! i have never had to wait for a prescription to be sent because the doctor had not done it immediately when getting discharged from an er or shortly after. i now understand why this hospital has a very low rating. terrible. just because this hospital services predominantly the  low socioeconomic class does not mean care should be overlooked! this is outrageous. if my mother has a hypertensive attack tonight due to her medication not being sent in a timely manner, this will not be the last this hospital and it's organization hear from me. get it together people. if you could help it, please do not go here. request another hospital.

christmas holidays will never be as exciting as the time i ended up in the er in 2019 and finding out i needed emergency gall bladder surgery. woo hoo!

my surgeon and anesthesiologist were caring, told me everything that was going on and came to see me post op.

4 stars though: when we did get help, everyone was so nice and helpful. much appreciated..

i have no issue with anyone or the care i received in the emergency room. my issue was the first person i spoke to when checking in. the place was all but empty and she was cold, robotic and about as friendly and courteous as a rock.as i sat & waited to get vitals checked,apparently someone she knew stopped by for a chat, she was all smiles and laughing. very disappointed that the first person you come in contact with is so unfriendly.  your going to an er because your  you should get a new receptionist.  everyone else was kind and professional.

review:
this is regarding the kaiser south sacramento infusion center an rheumatology clinic. 
several months back, i took my sister in for her infusion. she had an anaphylactic reaction to the medication being infused. the male nurse (who transferred in from the ed)  was excellent. he knew what to do and took good care of her. this was supposed to be our last visit under the care of the rheumatologist who ordered the medication. we had, had enough of her poor practices and decided to transfer care to ros. kp.
somehow, because it was the middle of the month, she superseded the new rheumatologist we were transferring to. my sister went in for what we thought was a new medication to try (to get her disease under control). 
i dropped her off and told her i would be back after i picked the kids up from school. within minutes of me getting home, i received a phone call from my sister. she was whispering "can you come back and take me to the bathroom". i asked her to repeat it several times because i could barely hear her and i couldn't believe what she was saying. nevertheless, i rushed back, in rush hour traffic. her door was closed all but a crack. anger came over me when i saw her condition. she was horribly swollen with a bright red face. her face was so swollen her eyes looked closed.  she had a bath blanket over her chest with spit all over it. she said she felt like she had to have a bowel movement and urinate. she said that her nurse told her it that they don't take people to the bathroom. i was stunned, shocked and in disbelief. just then, her rn walks in and says " yeah, um are you the family"? i said "yes". to which she replied " yeah, so we don't take people to the bathroom so if she's going to need the bathroom when she's here one of you need to stay with her and help her to do that. this is an outpatient clinic, this is not inpatient hospital we do not transfer or take people to the bathroom". "if she is gonna be needing to use the bathroom then you're going to have to talk to her doctor and see if she can be admitted to the hospital for these infusions and then discharged when she's done". i was speechless. i looked at her probably with disgust and confusion, then looked at my sister, then looked back at her. she then went on and said "oh yeah she went into shock again we almost had to transfer her to the er". i said, she's allergic to the new medication to? the nurse replied, "her rheumatologist, wanted to try the medication again from last month. we thought that if we front-loaded her with as much steroids as we possible could that she wouldn't have a reaction. but, she did and because we had already front-loaded her with all the steroids; we couldn't give her anything but iv fluid. hence, that is why she is so swollen." i said oh, so you have her the medication that she had known anaphylaxis to. she went into anaphylaxisi again which is why she has to use the bathroom and why she is whispering (swelling in the throat). i said, and which md ordered this? the nurse said it was the md we had just transferred away from. i have since spoke to two separate providers and both agree that the massive amounts of steroid that she was given pushed her into cushing's disease.
in my opinion, the the doctor needs to be reviewed for unsafe medical practices. and the nurse should be reviewed by the nursing board and perhaps have her license suspended. regardless of if a doctor orders a medication or not, if you know it is unsafe for your patient you should not be giving it. thank god for the medical assistant that heard my sister trying to call out for help over her swollen vocal cords and alerted the medical staff team. that is a huge problem with kaiser. they want people that bsn or higher behind their name regardless of how they obtained it and what experience they may have. 
btw, i tried to file a complaint on my sister's behalf because she was too ill to do it herself and kaiser would not allow me to. i was told they have to come directly from the member or you have to be the dpoa on file to file a complaint on their behalf.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Sacramento Medical Center

may to accommodate his busy schedule so he could perform my knee surgery.  i called soon after to schedule the surgery since he wanted me to think about it first.  i was told by scheduler to wait another week for him to put surgery on order then they would call me to a schedule.  waited another week, called again because no call from anyone.  was told "oh, he's going  to call you".  well it's week 3 and no phone call!  talk about unprofessional!  i should've left my appointment initially after waiting that long.  $40 wasted on a visit with this place!  there's no reason to wait this long after an initial consultation with doc saying yup, your bone on bone, you're out of options!
