in 2009 when this hospital first opened, it was very nice.  the doctors, nurses and staff were professional and courteous.  things have changed dramatically over the years.  my mother was admitted to the hospital in 2015 after a fall on our veranda which left her with a bruised and swollen leg.  they performed an mri of her brain along with xrays. i thought an mri was a bit much but she was 78 at the time.  the doctor just discussed the bruising on the leg and never mentioned the mri results.  i didn't ask because i assumed if the mri showed anything bad, they would have told us.  boy was i wrong!  fast forward to end of 2019.  my mother had an infection that had developed in her leg so she was admitted to hospital for iv antibiotics.  by this time, she had developed vascular dementia unfortunately.  the er doctor was curious about her mental state so he went back thru her records.  that's when he told me that my mom had suffered a stroke in 2015 along with other vascular issues in a different part of the brain.  the er doctor never told us about any of this in 2015 when they did the mri.  in my opinion, the lack of information sharing on their part was medical negligence.  i could have made an appt. for my mother to see a neurologist whereby her further stroke risk could have been assessed and treated.  i will always wonder if her vascular dementia could have been postponed or prevented if she could have started medications sooner.  we'll never know.  on a separate note, i was in the er a few months ago due to ms issues.  the doctor told me that they do not have a neurologist on staff, only one on referral phone call. he also said that they do not have the ability to do an mri from the er. he followed up with a comment about st. anthony's only being a community hospital.  unbelievable!  i did phone the administration office the next day and was told that the er can order an mri but the patient has to be taken to a different part of the hospital. the scan has to be truly an emergency because of already scheduled mri appointments.  i've always been a patient of swedish in downtown seattle so perhaps i've been spoiled.  i enjoy living in gig harbor but may not stay much longer if the hospital situation doesn't improve.

i was there tonight, because i've been having flu like symptoms. i swear none of the nurses in the er wanted to listen to me nor help me... i still feel the same if not worse than i did before i got there. absolutely terrible. i will go to st. clair from now on. as for the rest of the hospital, i have no complaints, i had both of my kids here and labor and delivery is great! but i will never go back to the er here! drive the extra distance and go to st. clair!

i had surgery yesterday and everyone on the 2nd floor was absolutely amazing. the professionalism, care, and attention exceeded my expectations and especially with yolaine and gina.
yolaine brought my medications on time, made sure i wasn't in excruciating pain and walked with me. she is really a gem and can't thank her enough .
javier from the nutritionist department was a blessing as well and helpful with what i could eat.
an administrative staff would come by the room and ask how they were treating me and if she needed anything.  they provided the highest level of care and compassion.

do not go to this hospital! my 90 year old father went here for heart failure and water in his lungs. he was there for a week and i was by his side every day. i only spoke to a doctor twice. you might get lucky and have a nurse that's compassionate or you might get one that is rude and unhelpful. when he was finally discharged, an ambulance brought him home at 12 midnight!!! no one bothered to call a family member to let us know he was on the way home. what kind of hospital discharges a 90 year old man at 12 midnight?!!! will never go here again.
it s a joke. nobody can give your folder. i speak to ten people and nothing move! to bring your money there s no problem to  explain you what s wrong! nobody. a shame...

luanne s laprade is truly the most vile human being i've ever had to deal with. my grandfather is dying of cancer and i asked her for a bandage as i just burnt my hand and i can't really just go home and get one when it's my grandfather's last days on this earth. well, before i could even finish my sentence luanne cut me off and loudly says "no we do not treat anyone unless they are a patient" and then she walks away.

i was so taken aback by this behavior by a healthcare specialist in response for a request for a bandage and neosporin that i was going to put on my own hand - you know.. things that are provided in a basic first aid kit. i then heard her repeatedly talking about me to fellow nurses and when i was walking by to go to the cafeteria she was looking at me and giving me a really rude look. 

i don't want to be that person but i really think she was treating me this way because of my race because i am of a middle eastern background. they didn't have any first aid kits on the walls or anywhere in the the hospital so i had no choice but to ask for it. it seems illegal that they refuse even bandages or neosporin. it seems more illegal to even allow luanne to have a license to practice with the lack or compassion, odd childish behavior, possible racism, and neglect she displayed.
great hospital awesome care.  i have new signature doctor and i will say he is very thorough.

since i got older,  i need to follow up every two years with an easy peasey test.  this was the first time i got it here in boise and st luke's imaging center is where they sent me.

i was greeted immediately by miranda who knew right away what i was there for and quickly and efficiently got me in and out. poof!  miranda also stayed with me to make sure i did not get lost in the hallways (it could happen) 

i walked to this appointment because i could and my results were in my email before i got home.  what?  i was sure they said i would get results "tomorrow".
several years ago i had bilateral knee replacement surgery at holy name with dr. hartzband. i have to say that i received excellent care in the orthopedic section. i even had a private room!

i have had multiple out patient scans and treatments and have nothing but good experiences at holy name. i am a former medical x-ray technician(never worked at holy name) so i have seen it all the staff were great. i recently was involved in a motorcycle accident with multiple injuries and was treated well by the er for broken ribs. i have not to date had a bad experience at holy name.

yes this facility like most va medical center is overwhelmed with veterans. for my experience here so far i think a four star rating is more appropriate. like most hospitals, there are isolated and unfortunate incidents that take place. the staff that served me are very caring and professional staff. the nurses went out of their way to make sure i understood why they asked me their questions and i understood my health concerns and what to expect. 

the pharmacy tech personally came and explained why it will be a longer wait for my meds. 

also, the doctor saw me in a reasonable amount of time and came 3 times so far to make sure i'm being taken care of. so if it's warranted, i will update my review but i think the staff here truly do their best to care for everyone.

the doctor care is wonderful and they know what they are doing. i'd give it more stars if it wasn't for an rude staff member in the icu. and the lack of empathy for family staying in the waiting room over night. there was no compromising with this person which made it feel like they are only here for a paycheck. this person is in the wrong line of work. when you get to the point of just being rude then it's time for a change. i hope ut southwestern realizes that this person represents them as a facility and they aren't giving your facility a good name.

the absolute worse place to go to. went in for strep and what i thought was an abscess. got admitted and taken to the second waiting room pretty quickly (7:00pm) wasn't called to be seen by the doctor till about 10:00pm. went to the room to see the doctor and didn't see him till about 11:00pm. only saw him for less than 5min and that's the only time i saw him. asked 3 different nurses for something about the pain (never got anything until after i was discharged and that's  only because pain medicine was prescribed to me). went to the reclining area and got some blood work done and a strep test. wasn't called for a ct scan till about 12:00am. said it'd take about 15min (took almost an hour) was in the waiting area for about 2 1/2 more hours. didn't get discharged till about 2:15am. got my prescription at their pharmacy and didn't go home till 3am. i was handled by nurses the whole time only seeing the doctor once for less than 5min, never got anything for the pain i was in, never got my results for my strep (was written off as sore throat), and am currently still in the same health i was when i went in if not worse. **also noticed a nurse being extremely rude to a patient who was struggling to speak with her (clearly there was a language barrier) and made no effort to try to listen to her and spoke down to her***

came for my appointment this morning and the check in process was fast and efficient. i saw the doctor and the procedure was painless, fast, and easy! i even got a few goodies to take home :-) my surgeon is amazing and lives up to his awesome reputation! kaiser exceeds expectations and i did not feel any pain during my procedure. i was honestly scared for nothing.

staff is beyond spectacular. nurses and receptionist are friendly and helpful.

i also had a 3:00 appointment and checked in early so the other doctor was able to see me sooner.
they addressed my concern and i was out in no time living my best life.

kaiser is absolutely the best! parking was a bit busy for  10:00 am but i was able to get in and out fast.

review:

review:

you really need to fix this kaiser!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: i was there a few days ago in the emergency room, i was in a lot of pain and feeling so much under the weather. from the moment i walked in till the moment i left this people were the most professional and nice team i ever met. nurses would come frequently to my room to make sure i was confortable, dr came and talk to me and he took his time to make i could be treated right away. i had some issues with my insurance so social worker came and helped me enroll for financial assistance so my visit to the er and my prescription to take was all free. thank you so much for everything

review: i had very severe bronchitis during the winter that caused me to have to see a doctor so many times... some don't seem to take the time to find out the root cause.. even had one doctor. in the er be outright rude.. listen to the patient issues and not what you think is best and the outcome will be more positive .. hopefully my experience with kaiser will be better going forward
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: kaiser wla is the best!  i've been to several emergency rooms -- ucla, cedars, st. john's due to a chronic health condition -- and by far and away, kaiser treated me like a queen.  fast service, polite staff, clean accomodations, easy parking, very efficient, great communication!  i grew up hearing horror stories about the kaiser system, but it is unfair of me to be stuck in a past iteration of it.  clearly, they have upped their game!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: this was hands down the best experience i've had at a hospital!!!! from the time i was in the er until they admitted me and i was finally discharged after 3 days. they gave me a private room!!! i've been to cedars 2 times w my daughter and they had her on a bed in a hallway for 3 hours and forgot we was there. when i arrived at kaisers er, it was a minimal wait( maybe 30 min) then they put me in a room. the er doctor did thorough test!!! x-ray, ultrasounds, ct scan, blood work, everything until she could find out what was wrong with me. she did not treat me like a second class citizen( i don't have kaiser as a insurance)she kept coming in and checking on me up until i was admitted. the social worker called my doctor to see if i should go to. once i was admitted the nurses were wonderful!! they ask me questions to get to know me and as the days went by, they greeted me with respect, dignity and compassion!!! i want to change my insurance!!!! before i was discharge social worker came in and told me they would schedule my follow up w a pcp. once i got home we found out the insurance didn't pay for a med nor the machine i needed. kaiser's case manager sent some company to bring me a machine and they made sure i had medications. again, i am not even a part of their insurance family. they treated me like family!!! it was amazing and i'm grateful  it was very clean too!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review: kaiser is by far the worst hospital ever. they are under staffed and are always booked. the people working there are brain dead.  everything takes forever. they need to get there act together and hire more people. i wouldn't recommend kaiser to anyone.

review: had to go in for the flu and received absolutely the best care imaginable. dr. overman, her nurse helen, and everyone made sure they checked everything, were so kind and considerate.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente West Los Angeles Medical Center

review:
my husband recently had spine surgery here and i have to say i was above and beyond impressed. 

-very clean waiting room with good coffee and granola bars. private rooms when your doctor comes out with surgery results. 

-amazing cafeteria. the food was delicious. i couldn't believe a hospital actually has good food. i ate there 3 times in 24 hours. my husband loved everything they fed
him. 

-nicest nurses ever. my husband's nurse julie was so sweet, accommodating, informative, and took great care of my hubby. she was awesome. 

-spacious, clean rooms with updated fixtures and very nice tiled bathrooms and direct tv with all the channels. i was so impressed. 

overall a really great experience and i am so glad he had his surgery here. we left very happy and he felt very taken care of the entire time. i wish they delivered babies here/did c-sections because i would love to have my
next baby here lol!

recently had knee replacement surgery. the staff is great! very friendly and helpful. nurses were great, especially lindsay. they answered all my questions and seemed to really care about how i was doing. this is a small hospital so the nursing staff isnt overloaded with patients. great hospital and if given the choice i will always choose to go there for future needs.
dr. sore was great!  all the people there were nice and attentive.  highly recommend if you need emergency care, like i did.  dr. sore was funny and has a great bedside manner.

i needed some blood work done and  someone told me about this place. it doesn't look like much from the road as it's small and the building looks a lil dated.  when you pull in off rt 6, parking and the entrance are around back.  holly and maria(?) were very professional, friendly and quick. holly drew my blood i hardly felt the needle go in my arm. she was a very pleasant woman with a good personality and she made the experience go smoothly.   i'm a big fan of "bedside manner" in situations such as this-- i mean, who likes getting blood drawn??!  great experience here!

helped me to find out what was wrong w me. was fast and effective. 5 min wait from check in to being call back. dr came in 5 min later took care of me. was there totally 1 and 1/2 hrs from start to end. very good experience. would recommend them to anyone who asks. they also have valet parking for all. this is an added plus.
fac_name: Brigham Health & Brigham/Mass General Health Care Centers

review:
here for surgery unfortunately. the nurses pacts, transporters, housekeeping and all other staff has such great customer service. being in the hospital is usually not pleasant but everyone i have come across has been caring and helpful. 

the room is spacious and welcoming. i really have no complaints. i hope i don't need to come back anytime soon but if i need hospital care i will come here!
address: 155 E Brush Hill Rd  Main Campus

review:
this review is specifically for the er department at elmhurst hospital. i had to bring my toddler there and was nervous because i had never been to this ed before. the triage nurse, alan, was very calm and compassionate, which immediately put me at ease. they took her back to a room right away and the next nurse, brittany, was amazing at getting my fussy toddler to take necessary medicine and quickly did the procedures she needed. nina was our main nurse. she kept us well informed and was patient allowing my toddler to pee on her own so they wouldn't have to do an invasive procedure to get it. my daughter cried every time someone walked in, but nina was able to get her to warm up to her by giving her a sticker and talking at her level. the pa and md who saw her were also very gentle, and they ordered the necessary thorough testing so we found out what was going on with my daughter. 

my only concern has to do with the office nurse. i called the day prior to going to the er concerned that her fever was over 105. she told me to bathe her, which did bring her temperature down combined with motrin. i just felt like she didn't believe that the reading was correct and my concerns were dismissed. i know i also should have pushed for her to be seen.

over thanksgiving, i was experiencing a migraine so severe i ended up at the er. i have ankylosing spondylitis which causes major flare ups around my major joints and back. sadly to say, this migraine was a result of my disease. morphine wasnt touching it. i was in such excruciating pain in my head, opening my eyes and light would cause it to go worse and me to throw up. the staff at erh was so kind, professional,  courteous to my disease and very thorough. they were doing everything possible to get me to feeling better.  i ended up staying thru thursday,  friday and mostly saturday. i just wanted to say thank you for the support and care i received from these wonderful people. iy seems all we here about any more is the negative experiences. i wanted to give a positive one.

once again i thank hemal parekh and her team for fixing my dad's heart issues.

review:
the only reason this medical center has any stars is because we are forced to give at least one when reviewing. please consider this a negative star rating. 

where to start????  

i live in oakland. i know what you're thinking?  why go all the way to kaiser santa clara?  trust me, this was not by choice. after having my appointment scheduled in san francisco (my oakland kaiser is not equipped for this procedure) i was later informed that the scheduling department made an error, in order to be seen in sf i would need a referral, and that i was really scheduled  to be in santa clara by 8am. if you know, you know... traffic! 

a little about the procedure. a capsule endoscopy. not sure how many are familiar with what these require so let me give you a little background.  basically i'm swallowing a camera so they can look at my small intestines. in order for this to be successfully done i would need 1 gallon of the ever delicious gavolite (lemon windex. flavored poop juice that literally makes you pee out of your ass for hours to the point your shit is clear).  

now to the next debacle, the pharmacy (different kaiser location) received a  notification that my doctor had ordered my poo juice, shortly after i received a notification staying that it was ready for pickup. i arrive to the pharmacy, wait 30 minutes in line in a cesspool of germs to be told that it was not ready and the ready for pick up notification was sent in error. after one hour of being subjected to a number of nasties, poo juice was finally in hand. 

so let's fast forward to yesterday. i am not allowed to eat at all!  i am a big guy, eating is the most important part of my life, forgive me i have yet to eat and i am quite hangry. recap of monday, no food, drinking the delish poo juice every 15 minutes (did i mention i had to set an alarm for 2 am and start my second round this morning), and lack of sleep, by 5am i ready to hit the road, jk, i have to poop. 

anyways, get on the road around 6 from oakland and finally make it santa clara. check in at 8 as instructed. what would you know, the computer system is down. we are in the fucking heart of silicon valley and you make billions of  dollars with on-site it, what do you mean your computers went down?  they take me back, my blood pressure  is looking "awesome", computers are still down, but they tell me i will be out the door by 9:20. all i can say is, lol. 

at 9:20, nothing has happened, shocker. here's the real kicker, santa clara being the only facility that's can  handle this procedure forgot to charge the fucking battery!  are you serious??  why wasn't it on the charger, i bet your phone is charged?  get this, they have 2 batteries, one is broken, the other dead!  i mean, i really have no words. 

then they told me i could wait a few more hours so the battery can charge. i have a few issues with this: 1. took off work. 2.  fiancé took off work. 3. most important, i'm fucking starving. 4. i would have to come back again tomorrow?!?!? 

obviously i didn't have the procedure and i'm gonna go stuff my fat face while i file a grievance with member services. i'm sure that will go smoothly.

review:
*kaiser permanente santa clara clinic* 
i've been to the evening clinic thrice so far when skyport, where i usually go for routine health care & generally like, didn't have any appointments. each time, i've been disappointed with the quality of doctors at the clinic. granted it is just 3 different doctors so there may be some sampling bias. but i will promptly update this review if i ever visit this location again (& i hope i don't have to).

*kaiser permanente santa clara emergency room*
skyport doesn't have an er so my nearest er is also santa clara. this week when i needed to, i was hoping that their er would be different - at least as good if not better than any regular er (eg. kp oakland) - from its evening clinic. after all, they're two different buildings, adjacent but on the same campus. but i was just so disappointed. at the er, it was an experience, just as bad if not worse than some civil hospitals. first, we couldn't find parking & there was no one available at the valet. it took us 10 min to find parking, but far away. registration took us another 25 min. i was in pain but there was also another patient behind me on a wheelchair who appeared either passed-out or in deep-pain so had just put her head down & was being assisted by another kaiser helper waiting their turn. long lines & only two nurses to register & only 1 nurse to take the vitals, who was also a part-time helper if a patient needs wheelchair assistance, after. it appeared that they had no sense of urgency or emergency, sometimes even chit-chatting & laughing amongst themselves while we were still waiting in the line, in pain. in fact, most of the er medical staff including the doctors & the nurses seemed fairly junior & disorganized too. as you'll read further, all of them (from the nurses that registered to the doctors & nurses who diagnosed/treated me) were asking me the same questions all over again, yet re-typing my responses into their computer, not realizing i was in pain & frustrated, repeating the same responses. for example: 
-what brings you in today?
-when did you start feeling this way?
-on a scale of 1-10, how would you rate your pain?
-have you seen a doctor for this & when?
-is this your first time at the er for this issue?
-have you had any medication recently?
-other personal questions, already on my chart
after the registration, i was sent to the waiting room & after another 30 min, into the screening room - the first point of medical triage. in the screening room, the nurse first asked me the same bunch of questions that i had already answered during registration. she hadn't read my chart nor my earlier responses to these questions. then after about 5-10 min a doctor came by & asked most of the same questions, again, without having read my chart, but a few new too, related to my pain:
-do you have any sensitivity to light?
-do you have stiffness in your neck?
-have you been already tested for this infection? (no. but as you will read below this somehow got interpreted to yes!)
he then told me that some other doctors would examine me further and i was sent to a patient room at the back of the er. after waiting for 10-15 min another nurse came in & asked me the exact same questions all over again. the room was very cold, so i asked her for a warm blanket which she quickly got for me. 
then after about 5 min, a doctor came to see me. she asked me most of the same questions again & ordered bloodwork, saline water, & other pain medicines through an ivr. finally reading into my notes, she thought that i was already tested for this infection earlier. (remember my answer above was no.) i said no again, and she said she'd order it - she didn't. the nurse inserted an iv needle to draw out blood & then administer saline water & pain medication. but while inserting the iv needle she wasn't gentle -showed her inexperience. she inserted the needle so hard that a lot of blood spilled over the sheet & the floor below -by the way, not the cleanest i've seen in an er. instead of apologizing, she asked me:
-have you had any alcohol or use blood thinner? (no.)
she just smiled & told me that i have a lot of blood that just oozed out so quickly (ok! what!?)
i was administered the saline water & some pain medicines. after 30-min, another doctor came in. he also assumed my infection test was done but i said no yet again but he said that it didn't matter anymore!  he suggested some otc medicines, assured me that i should feel better soon & left. after about an hour i started feeling better due to the pain medicines but during that time a lot of people were walking & talking pretty loudly outside. i overheard an entire conversation of a random nurse who's soon moving in with her boyfriend (good luck, but this is an er!). then my nurse came back with my discharge papers, went over them, wished me well, & then i gladly left. at least no longer in pain. at least i'm not mad at yelp for not letting me leave them 0 stars & they get 1.

to sum it up - yikes. 

went  to the er on thursday after class for severe lower back pain that extended into my legs. 
the moment i got there, the triage nurse quarantined me out of suspect of corona virus. mind you, their only basis was that i had a fever (which i didn't even realize i had) and i am a japanese american. no other symptoms. they had someone come up to me every 5min (often the same person) to ask me the same questions (did you travel  abroad in the last 30 days; do you have a cough?) as if they would get a different answer. my answer was a hard no  each time. meanwhile i was in severe pain, and my chief complaint was not addressed until several hours  later. 

after a couple hours waiting in a quarantine area, they took me to what i thought would only be temporary accommodation. it was a patient bed  in a cramped hallway, and the bed was too short for my legs. it turned out to be the only patient bed i'd see in that hospital. pretty sure that was a major hipaa violation. 

my first nurse was absolutely atrocious. he did not smile. he was rude. he was in no way gentle. he missed my vein 4 times when placing an iv, which judging by the vein he  used, did not seem possible. when i had to give a urine sample, he made me hold my urine specimen for 20 min until another nurse came by and asked me why i was still holding it, and then he would not help me back into my  bed. i was in so much pain. the icing on the cake: he gave me a flu test and jammed the stick so far up my nose that i got a nose bleed. i didn't even know i had a nose bleed until the mri tech took off my mask and asked me why it was bleeding. after i told him, he shook it off as no big deal. i've had a couple flu test before -- none of which caused this much discomfort. 

at the end of the day, the docs couldn't figure out the root of my pain and gave me a referral to a spine specialist. they didn't give me a number -- the told me to wait for his call the next day. the specialist waited until the end of their business day to call me to schedule an appointment. i missed their call but called back not even 10min after their initial call. and they were already closed! i had to wait until monday (today) to try to book an appointment. i've called them 8 times and left messages. it is absolutely amazing and appalling to me that someone can seriously stay in business if they don't answer their damn phones. i probably will not be wasting my time with them.

when i visited the hospital on tuesday. feb. 18th, it was disgusting that antibacterial dispensers -- one in front of the au bon pain cafe and the other right near the main entrance next to the info desk -- were empty at a time when the us is trying to prevent a pandemic. particularly as people with compromised immune systems visit hospitals, but even in light of the hospital's simply being a place that is supposed to stop-- not spread -- infectious diseases -- this was surprising. however, more astonishing was that when i notified the woman working at the info desk that morning, she appeared uninterested. i then went to patient family services. two people-a young man and woman -- were  chatting behind a desk. when i explained that there was no antibacterial soap in main area of the hospital, they did nothing. i explained that it would be very helpful to fill the soap dispensers in the main area of the hospital right next to the front info desk as well as the dispenser that was in front of the au bon pain restaurant café.the young man named joel explained that when the custodian did his rounds, they would let him know. he did not know what time that would be, but it would be in the morning. this had nothing to do with keeping the hospital clean and  safe but everything to do with minimizing one's work for joel in the ambivalent young woman.  the young woman behind the desk who had been chatting with joel prior to the interruption of work giggled. i suggested that since dispensers were empty, that it would be good to call custodian services now to fill, but joel said he would not do that; the young woman was also ambivalent to act.

i called several offices. thinking that those whose job it was to take care of these issues were ambivalent, i asked the switchboard to connect me to secretary to the president. the  switchboard rep stated that these calls went to (the (ambivalent) patient services. meanwhile i saw many people trying to wash hands when entering the hospital and the restaurant -- only to find empty dispenser. i finally called the director of nursing, explain that i knew nurses cared-- and patty in that office was great.

but -- it is disgusting that the other staff members seemed to act -- or not act -- out of ignorance. i did wonder if such a basic step in patient care could not be taken, what happened with more complex issues. i have found care to usually be excellent at the hospital, but this was negligent. there was the same issue of empty dispensers at brigham's fish center. the hospital needs to get with its own program.

brigham and woman er is terrible for many reason. the first one, i do have health insurance but there is $150 co-pay for the er i was told when i walked in give us a credit card or a doctor will not see you that was one visit in may. i had a terrible fibroid and was in a lot of pain and they would not help my pain or me or even figure out what was wrong without a credit card and i have cancer there was no extra consideration for that. i had a surgery done at that hospital and was sent home to early and the surgeon made a big mistake and cut my yard line and cost me to have a kidney problem i had to be admitted and have another surgery to fix it after that surgery i woke up something was wrong they ignored it i followed up

not good follow-up. they do not check on the chart before seeing their patient - causing for the patient to share the history. they seem to not care. i get it that they have lots of patients but sorry you go in to get care not to be treated like a number...bad all together i am planning on switching care at this point for primary care and specialty.

my son was brought by ambulance around 3am in the morning and tested positive for influenza b. they were quick to get him fluids take give him meds and a chest x-ray. they staff were amazingly friendly and kind and very supportive and encouraging it's a long drawn out flu and very scary. loved this hospital and had a excellent professional experience.

the night crew in the er are horrible they pick favorites on who they give their care to... annie needs to retire she's bitter and treats patients like they're garbage.. we had teri m all day she was amazing and when her shift was over everything went to crap... you might as well stay home and suffer rather than being ignored for 4 hours...

i got in a  bad car accident and burkowitz is my primary. he wasn't available for over  5 weeks to see me so i scheduled with irizari who had more availability, i live an hour away and had to get around a car accident on my way to the appointment- it ended up making me 13 minutes late but i notified the office which i was on hold with the call center for 15 minutes before they were able to transfer me. then when i got to the office i wait another ten minutes before getting checked in for them to ask the doctor if it  still works. he said no, to reschedule. i work full time and can't afford to take time off because a doctor doesn't feel like seeing me for 15 minutes. the girls at the front are nice but i couldn't say  the same for the doctors. very upset

on the position side of gwinnett medical center (gmc) i am a fan of their women labor and delivery unit (gwinnett women's pavilion). we had two children born here one back in 2012 (before the takeover) and in 2018 when northside hospital just started taking over gmc. all of the nurses and doctors were pleasant and i liked that they changed their policy to keep the babies in the room with the parents.

i'll give 4 stars for the women's pavilion.

now on with the emergency room...

my biggest complaint is the gwinnett medical emergency room center. the wait time here is extremely long (about 3 hours minimum). my wife is on the clinical side of healthcare and i used to be so we are consider ourselves very understanding.

we decided to here as our daughter who was 12 months came here to visit as she had an extremely high temperature of nearly 104 that would not go down using acetaminophen, ibuprofen, or liquids. nothing would lower her fever after about 3-4 hours, so we came here.  after hours and hours of waiting, we were seen. the nurses ran several tests, one after another and they found nothing, as we thought maybe it must be a viral infection or a uti, but it was neither.

we went home and after a month received a bill for $3,469.00 and our insurance picked up a little. gwinnett medical center now is under northside hospital, so all of their bills are under northside hospital now.

they apparently have a financial assistance program to help patients who are in a certain income bracket, which we qualify for. after speaking with their financial assistance people we have been told they would call us on the phone and not to call them. they insisted they would call us and after waiting and waiting... we have called half a dozen times with them telling us to keep waiting. yet, month after month we keep getting this extremely high medical bill saying our balance is delinquent - pay immediately. why have a program that does not work? gmc/northside you guys can do better.

the bill: 

$3,469.00 - 2 hour room rental, 2 saline iv's, 1 uti test, 1 blood test, 2 nurses (est. 20 minutes), 1 amoxicillin rx and 3 freeze popsicle's.

honestly, i really thought having northside hospital take over gwinnett medical center would be such a blessing for all those who live in gwinnett county. my professional advice is if you have an option (non-life-threatening) to take your children to choa (children's health care of atlanta) and stay away from the (er) gmc/northside hospital unless you have health insurance benefits that pay 100%. if you are an adult with non-life-threatening issues, more than likely, one would be better off to just visit an urgent care facility. my personal experience is they are cash base ($100-$150) and that is all you will pay if treated in their clinic, of course, that depends on what one needs (specialists refers...)

it stinks i had to write this, but i thought it was important to inform others, just so there is some transparency. do not expect the same as it was under gmc. when it was under gmc ownership the reviews here were mostly extremely good.

[review #608] (34th review of 2019)

i brought my child there to gwinnett medical's children's emergency room due to a broken arm. we arrived and they performed an x-ray. the physician came out and informed us that she did feel comfortable performing a reduction and said they will transport him to choa. we received a bill for $2500 after insurance and of course got another emergency room bill from choa. i don't understand how you can advertise a children's emergency room and can't perform a fracture reduction. now i stuck with 2 emergency room bills.   business office staff also very rude. i will never nor any family or friends be coming to this hospital. 

fyi: any children's issue: go straight to choa.

this hospital deserves a no star. took my mother here to have her little pinky finger check due to ulcer. her illness history are hypertension and hyponatremia, and we all are know that. we even show them the medication and dosages. in this case they don't even bother her pinky, but keep drawing her blood every four hours for 4 tubes (3-10ml size) each time, and my mom is a very tiny vietnamese female. they diagnose her with of the following: diabetic even though her blood lab results low in sugar, finger injury even though my mon bed ridden more than 5 years (she has no chance of falling or hit herself to anything), speech disorder and they order speech therapy for her even we refused because my mom doesn't speak english, but it does not work, also dementia even though my mom know and remember everything. they keep her there for 3 days and 2 nights to give her intravenous fluids and antibiotics. they discharge her with the pinky ulcer still there. 
what do you think of this?
this is a horrible experience.

i had to come here for some labs, and i was very pleased at my experience. 

like any big complex, i had to find my way around, but people were very nice and helpful. the wait was very short, despite the fact that i had been sent here (along with i am sure many other patients) due to issues at another campus, so they were likely a little overloaded.

everything was clean; the staff was friendly and knowledgeable, the process was minimal.

this was also during the covid-19 epidemic, and they were screening anyone who came through the door to try and keep the facility uncontaminated, which while not perfect was a good gesture for sure.

i would happily come back here again in the future for other procedures based on the quality of service i received.

cpmc has great facilities and friendly/helpful staff. 

the parking rates seem a little steep for those wanting to visit a loved one in the hospital. i spent $20 for 2.5 hours. you can enter the parking garage through two, one way streets.

picu. 

pediatric intensive care unit.

you hope you never know that acronym.

the nursing staff is wonderful, so attentive, sweet and sensitive to their small charges. a series of locked double doors open only for cleared parents. you walk through the maze step-by-step, one door to another - for security. 

i was reassured by it, as much for the protection as for the routine and monotony. when you're panicked and worried, any structure is welcomed.

i'm grateful for the staff at cpmc's new hospital. they were kind, always gentle and sweet to my littler. 

doctors were a bit of a mixed bag, one who scared the tar out of me when he called me at home at 11:30 pm and told me my son might be transferred to a new facility- at midnight. 

the new hospital is gorgeous though a few doctors (all men) really need a refresh on bedside manner. 

nurses a+++

the staff that helped deliver and care for our son here was amazing. for that i'd give 5 stars.

however, the day our baby was born, 34 hours after we arrived and an absolute hellish labor for my wife, they refused to deliver us each an entree to the room. the day he was born. the staff simply told me that they will only feed the mom. go take a hike, dad. now, i don't expect things for free, but i was incredibly offended at the absurd lengths this hospital nickel and dime'd us. not even a pregnancy day meal to keep the family together? i would never have a future baby here. friends of mine, who have delivered at ucsf, have stated that all meals were provided for all their guests, which is about as far from cpmc as you can get.

this hospital is clearly for profit, despite their claims.

recap:
5 stars for medical service
1 star for the policy makers with their heads up their butts

the labor and delivery team at cpmc van ness is amazing. every nurse that we had supporting us was better than the next -- and we had an amazing nurse to start so it's easy to say that their staff made the entire labor so positive, stress-free and enjoyable!

we cannot thank the staff enough! tori, ariel, angela, rose, jasmine, sheila, deb o and mary o were all wonder woman - thank you so very much!!

we also highly recommend golden gate obgyn as obstetrician practice -- their doctors and staff are truly wonderful!

ugh, where do i start. radiology mri has always been bad from this group. now hospital that has all the charm of a maximum security prison. everything is on lock down. the furniture is not friendly or comfortable. not a magazine to be found. my tech who was supposed to be the iv guy previously did a bad job x2 so i asked for someone better. they send a worse tech- she jammed in the iv wrong and in the wrong place. tech #2 fails again. try's for the third time against my better judgment and we finally succeed. i asked for a nurse to do it in my prescreen call. they don't care. my cost for all this $1,750 with insurance. the mri - two gowns and and no socks - not sure what the hell i am supposed to do with that. i was spoken to like a child on many occasions. infuriating "experience ". you need to work on your eq skills when it comes to patient care. it is seriously lacking.

stellar drs, stellar nurses.  have absolutely nothing bad to say.

was in for surgery, icu for a day, then a little over a week on a regular floor.

i was in the er today.the physician dr amin was the rudest and most condescending of all the people i interacted with.she stood talking with me with her arms tightly folded across her chest which is a position that someone takes to assert their authority and superiority.
she disappeared and did not return when i asked numerous times to speak with her about getting an iv as i felt really dehydrated.
she exhibited absolutely no empathy or concern whatsoever.i hope her behavior is not representive of how the other physicians treat the pts who come through the er.

the nurses where nice to my wife while she needed care. and  she felt safe and well taken care of. but the er staff are overworked and working at a high volume patient to nurse ratio. they dont have enough beds. so be prepared to wait in the er for days. the nurses in the er need help. hire some techs or more nurses. dont forget the wait. 3 to 4 hrs wait in er and days before being brought upstairs.

spent a few days here having a baby. this place is amazing. staff are wonderful, they took amazing care of us. the rooms are fantastic, the rooms are big, the service is great. we got so much help and support here as we had our kiddo. 

well done to all the pediatric staff, they are amazing. we had such good support. great to be able to just hand over the kiddo when you wanted some sleep. 

very high tech stuff everywhere. this was one of the nicest hospitals i have ever attended. 

less awesome - some of the food is not amazing, but they have lots of options for people.

our daughter fell down. her top teeth hit the upper lip. the bleeding could not stop. we went to the hospital, cpmc van ness campus emergency. doctors and nurses help us a lot because our daughter is 4 years old, she cried all time. they tried to make our daughter stop crying. so, they blew balloons, gave the stickers, brought the dog to help, and turned on tv. they was very patient with our daughter. we are thankful to all of you. thank you very very much.

this hospital is clearly understaffed first of all!!! there seems to be a lack of compassion as well and one nurse with major attitude problems!!! i can't believe the lack of personal around this place it is just astonishing horrible!!! and when it comes to pain meds that i have to have while in a flare i feel like i'm treated as though i'm a street or homeless person seeking it for thrills......ummmm yeah no i have actual pain and a disease that's been diagnosed for over 15yrs!!!! our healthcare system is a joke and this new fancy hospital is all money and looks and zero feel care gor the patient in need!!!!!

i had the worst experience in the new cpmc medical center er.  the staff was inattentive and basically ignored me.  
my vitals weren't taken when i checked in and they never followed through with taking a urine sample that i was supposed to have had.
all in all it was very unpleasant.

valet parking do not use. they would not give me my car back. the orange tag i needed to retrieve my keys was in my car where they left it. i was trying to leave at 9pm with my one yr old grandson. they detained me for over an hour  & made me feel like a criminal!

checking in my dad at the er.  kelly got a condescending tone w/ my dad who's obviously  struggling to answer her.  raising your voice at him won't make you hear his response better.  he is in pain.  struggling to breathe.  and you want him to explain why he didn't come in 2 weeks ago???  does that matter right now?  does it change why he's here now?  and will the answer make any difference to you and how you perform your job??  here's the answer, kaiser and cpmc can't get their shit together w/ his referral.  for god's sake you work for a medical facility.  and you can't even help him w/ his clothes??  maybe a different job where you don't have to work w/ people is best.

this is my second visit (taking a relative) in the past year and both times have been horrific. my mother has a serious medical condition and both times her doctor had called ahead to warn the er we were on the way in an ambulance. my mother is very elderly, frail and weak, and both times they treated us as if she was not important, or imagining her symptoms. the nurses are invisible- they stay in a pack in their office, if you need anything like a blanket or the saline the dr ordered 2 hrs ago (they never ask) you must hunt them down. furthermore the hospital has a constant stream of od patients from the tenderloin ... and on this occasion the staff put my mother ( confused, barefoot, dressed only in her nightgown & shivering) having just had a siezure - in the waiting room filled with coughing homless for over an hour.  this night was a horror - mostly due to the oddly empty feeling of the hospital. you never see nurses or doctors. the place just feels filled with homless. aweful.
emergency service which has 7 hour waiting time to get checked in. if you want to land up in a worst hospital you have ever been in your life then this is it.

i love the nurses and staff on the ninth floor, they took care of my client so well. everyone is nice to everybody, nurses, patient assistant, cleaners and all the staff... they are compassionate, kind, respectful and attentive to the patient needs and the guest included. im so happy and grateful with them. however, i wasn't satisfied with the service by a nurse who was assigned to us on the pm shift at the er. she didnt even introduce herself that shes gonna be on duty replacing the am nurse. its not that they are over staff, when your rude it does shows. she doesnt want to go to our room, she doesnt inform us whats going on with the patient, did not check his vitals, luckily another  nurse pass by help us and took his temperature, he had a fever. our patient needs changing, i called 3x and they sent an assistant... since when do you learn how to change somebody's pad sitting up? ....well not everyone is bad, some people just dont care, good thing we move upstairs so we can have a good service.

i've had a hard time trying to find a primary care doctor that was a good fit. doctor roberts has been the best by far. she is patient, attentive,  knowledgeable and very thorough. i've been to offices in the past where the doctor stares at their computer the entire time, that is not the case here. she makes eye contact, listens to your concerns and treats you like a human being, rather than just a chart on her desk. she also answers her messages promptly and when she isn't in the office, dr. yee is very responsive in her absence. i haven't had any issues with the staff here either. everyone that works here is competent and that is hard to find these days. if you're looking for a good doctor, dr. roberts is a great choice.

was admitted through the emergency room.    all staff very caring cheerful and made a nervous patient relaxed.   a  few tests and a good diagosis.    everyone on staff treated me with respect and caring.    the hospital was clean and comfortable.   although spending a night on an er bed i could have done without.    hospital was full and i was awaiting a room   when i got to my room,  it was very comfortable and i forgot about the er stretcher/bed.   i was on a limited diet but what food i could have was very good, arrived hot and tasty    they have an interesting food service they call it room service and for me it worked well.    on my discharge day,  the room service person called me to remind me that i hadn't ordered lunch   just another nice touch

i took my daughter to anna jacques er three weeks ago for a finger injury. i paid my 100 dollar co pay and this week received a 250 dollar bill from the attending doctor, who we never saw. this is the second time this has occurred  here and i am told the doctor does not work for the hospital and that he gets paid to review the case. it is very upsetting that patients are not told that the doctor bills separately and patients will end up owing much more that their co pay. this has never happened at beverly hospital. anna jacques touts itself as a community hospital but seems to forget the common courtesy of laying out their billing practices.  i was truly disgusted when i received the second bill and will never again bring anyone to anna jacques.

on february 5 i was admitted to gbh for elective cervical disc replacement & cervical fusion acdf. i just can't say enough about how well i was cared for from start to finish. i've been using gulf breeze hospital for well over twenty years and it's just the best of the best, bar none. dr. mark giovanini has done three surgeries on me over the past 15 years and he's absolutely the best at what he does. during this past issue i suffered for two years four months with chronic neck pain causing numbness, tingling, and pain jolting through my arms, post surgery my neck feels 100% better, and i haven't lost feeling in my hands, no more tingling, no more jolts of pain. other than the aches of post surgical pain i feel great and suspect i'll continue to improve, i feel like i have a new neck. i can't thank the staff at gbh enough, from tammy who started my iv, to the pre op staff that joined in prayer with my son before they took me to surgery, to kristi m, rn in post op she was wonderful very kind, kept me out of severe pain no breakthrough pain. i just love michael d., nprac  just a great guy, i just wanna take him home, he's a gem. i was in room 219 & lori rn my daytime nurse was very very nice kept me informed and comfortable, very sweet rn. my physical therapist was great- cameron very informative and super nice. we laughed and just built a rapport. my nighttime rn- stephanie was so sweet, she found me sherbet to soothe my throat, and last but not least dr. gio what a fantastic neurosurgeon and sweetheart, he has the best bedside manners and was very attentive to my concerns and questions. peeps don't settle for good, settle for greatness, go to the best of the best gulf breeze hospital. i'm 7 days post op and feeling brand new

- i might add i live in fort walton beach, i'll never go to any ed or stay anywhere but gulf breeze a hospital they are that good at what they do, i think i'd know as i'm also a paramedic and have worked in escambia county, santa rosa county, and okaloosa county, i know hospitals and i know who i want taking cars of me, keep up the great work gbh and crew

times are tough!  the er cannot afford kleenex in the rooms, a rolling table to assist nurses with all the medical items they need to do their work on you and no pillows at all.  looking for new medical providers this year

i'm literally sitting in the ed and having a panic attack because of the breathing treatment i was given....hr spiked up to almost 140 and all of the nurses and doctors are sitting!!!! i pressed the call button 3 times only to be told that i need to calm down. no, i don't especially when i've been coughing up blood. as a patient this is never how i should be treated! i am also a healthcare professional and would never treat my patients this way! i pray that o never need to step foot into this hospital ever again. instead of remodeling they should consider tearing it down or maybe simply firing the entire ed staff since retraining clearly never happens.

i underwent a pre-scheduled cervical spine surgery at gw by way of a neurosurgeon.  the pre-surgical and post-surgical treatment at gw were fantastic.  the doctors and nurses were attentive and detail-oriented.  the head nurse in charge ensured everyone did their jobs.  five stars if you require surgery or longer-term hospitalization at gw.  

now i turn to the emergency room (er) of gw university hospital.  in contrast, the er receives one star.  it was horrible.  avoid the gw er if at all possible.  the nurse assigned to me had a bad attitude.  i was experiencing severe cervical spine pain.  i asked for an injection.  the nurse claimed she had injected me with morphine, but i felt nothing.  then she disappeared for 2 to 3 hours.  no pain relief was provided.  it was chaos.  when i was discharged, there were patients waiting for a room.  they were laid out on gurneys.  peeing in their pants.  yet there were over 12 nurses joking around on their computers in the triage center of the er.  these nurses were ignoring the patients.  no one appeared to be in charge.  poorly run er.  avoid it.
i have been at the er now for almost nine hours. nine hours!  i have a terrible flu. average wait time is not an hour. and i'm still not treated.

i went there tonight because i hit my head on double pane glass wall when i fell and they didn't even see me...precedent was me was given to a woman with a broken hand; i was horrified, horrible hospital they don't know what the hell they're doing there!!!!.  

the hospital is dirty and run down and has derelicts at night, it's not a safe place to be, nor do they have good and timely care.

go to sibley hospital
excellent, expedited treatment. discharge 90 minutes later. thank you, gw hospital - er staff for taking good care of me.

don't come here to the er if you can help it. the place is under construction and it takes hours to be seen. it's full of people who come in for colds so no one takes you seriously. you can hear the nurses telling each other how dangerous and incompetently run the hospital is. to make it worse i got home and realized they had given me 2 other peoples' signed discharge papers, which i'm pretty sure is a hippa violation.

took my daughter into the er as she was having a severe allergic reaction. they rushed her through the doors and immediately started working on her.   totally pleased with the attention they gave her during this medical emergency.

this poor review is against ssm and not the people working at the hospital.  
after getting a massive bill for a er visit i have been making payments on my own $200+ a month.
today i got a call from ssm that they were going to send my account to collections if i did not make payment arrangments.  
ssm are a bunch of money grubbing suits... go anywhere else!!!!

i live 3 blocks away and they say they accept my insurance. but i call and call throughout the year and they never have appointments available to enroll with a primary care doctor. 
i wonder where my tax dollars are going with this place.no one is ever in there.
this facility cares about the old people but the dietary manager "tera" is so rude and disorganized. wtf is she doing?!? why is she even there. she needs to be reviewed.

do not come to this hospital if you can get anywhere else. you will wait forever & the people up front are extremely rude. i get this feeling they look down on certain patients and it's very annoying . and the treatment isn't much better . after waiting 2+ hours to even be seen you're usually thrown in a hall or even if in a room it takes another few hours to get anything done and another few hours for results . trust me if you can get to milton hospital it's way more worth it.

day surgery is a nightmare if your time is scheduled in the middle of the day. staffing is short and scheduled times are just a suggestion. plan on waiting and running late. oh, your blood pressure will be up due to the added anxiety. 

robin in surgical reception needs sensitivity training. i arrived to pick up my husband after a day procedure and was told by his doctor when i should arrive back to the hospital. i did as he said and i walked up to the desk when i arrived back. she was talking to another woman and abruptly stopped, looked at me, and asked "do you need something?" i explained what i stated above and she told me to take a seat and she would be with me in a minute. five minutes later she came over to me and said she is not supposed to call back and he just got out of surgery. not true! i volunteered to show her my phone with the time the doctor called me. she told me it would be about a half hour longer, which is now close to 2 hours for recovery before i could see him. the reception desk is less than welcoming in fact i received a chilly reaction given what we were going through that day.

if i were able to give no stars that would be more accurate!! i was in the er in april of 2019 and received probably the worst care i've ever had to encounter in my almost 25 years of being chronically ill. i called the very next day to submit a formal complaint which was just handled by even nastier people and swept under the rug. billing has been an absolute nightmare. claiming i owe a certain amount after both my insurances and myself has contacted them several times saying this is not true. ssh apparently only goes by the first page of an eob. i've never had any of these issues with any other ma hospital. if you value your life, sanity, and money, you should find a different establishment because between the incompetent er staff and billing department, i'm surprised they haven't faced medical malpractice lawsuits out the ass. i'd rather drive 45 minutes in an emergency to bwh or mgh than the 10 minutes it would take me to get to ssh.
"frances farmer will have her revenge on seattle" nothing more than a snake pit that needs to be shut down and it's workers arrested and jailed.
