review: army tricare isn't the best insurance out there but when i delivered my baby, the staff were pretty good at what they do! my baby was sunny side up. i was pushing for an hour and a half and they had to call a doctor since my body was weak and baby wasn't budging. major (dr.) tillman gave me the options of forceps and vacuum and he recommended forceps. i went with it. within 4 pushes, my baby was out! and i was expecting a bad marks on my baby's face but it was barely noticeable and went away within hours! after delivery, nurses are in and out to keep me and the baby in check. the next day, the same dr. (tillman) came to check on us again. thank you major for being extra cautious! i heard the worst outcomes from forcep deliveries but you made mine quick and didn't harm my baby!

dr. lionel savadier, md, is a diagnostic radiology specialist in hollywood, florida. he attended and graduated from medical school in 1968, having over 52 years of diverse experience, especially in diagnostic radiology. he is affiliated with many hospitals including memorial hospital miramar, memorial hospital pembroke, memorial hospital west, memorial regional hospital. dr. lionel savadier also cooperates with other doctors and physicians in medical groups including radiology associates of hollywood inc. dr. lionel savadier accepts medicare-approved amount as payment in full. call (954) 987-2000 to request dr. lionel savadier the information (medicare informatdvice, payment, ...) or simply to book an appointment.
dr. savadier is the kind of rare physician that makes a rather unpleasant test seem like fun because of his warm sense of humour and the fact that he actually talks to the patient. memorial west needs more quacks like dr. savadier.
address: 601 N Flamingo Rd Ste 104 Primary Care Physicians of Florida

review: i was seen today by mr timothy hartzler, nurse practitioner, at the gastrointestinal practice in the main building in room 505 on the 5th floor. the receptionist, diamond, was professional& efficient. mr hartzler listened to my complaint patiently & with interest & then examined me. he answered all my questions calmly & i was very happy with his treatment. i highly recommend this practice. also the hospital & office are beautiful & clean. thank you.
fac_name: Bon Secours Saint Francis Medical Center

review: my sister visited there last week via rescue squad into the er and was treated immediately and then admitted.  she has been given the best attention and offered several specialist to deal with her cardiac issue. the staff has been incredible and they are currently working to restore her heath so as to do another procedure when she is able.  most of the nursing staff were attentive and compassionate and kind (those that were not know who they are). the setting is beautiful and one of peaceful prayer and reflection. every evening there is a prayer/meditation that is  broadcasted over the speakers which is a godsend to patients and families. the doctors seem to really care about the outcome of the patient. i especially want to  mention dr. robert omuria, hospitalist, who went above and beyond in helping our family understanding my sister's condition and the steps moving forward.
fac_name: Bon Secours Saint Francis Medical Center

review: have yet to find a better dr.  been a patient of his since 2000.  amazing, smart, professional yet personable.  takes time to listen and always makes you feel comfortable. excellent diagnostician.  only drawback - very busy!!!!
our family has always had great success with the staff and care at valley springs med center.

i have to share my experience here. my daughter was admitted here wed am with a pe (blood clot) in her right lung. childrens er was great. however, once moved to 6th floor for inpatient treatment we have been suffering. last night was the hardest due to lack of adequate staff. our nurses mentioned walkie talkies being removed monday & transitioning to a mobile app for all correspondence regarding patients  as being the cause. they are stretched very thin as it is and this change has caused great difficulty for nursing staff, but more importantly patients . 
my daughter had an iv bag empty for an hour last night. it took me 2 calls and finally walking up to a nurse station before we received assistance 45 min later. she got to level 8 pain during this time as well. this morning the imperative injection for her condition was 30 min late & her pain meds were 45 min late causing another level 8 pain for my daughter along with an empty iv bag for an hour again. 
i spoke to the nurse leader for the floor and let her know i was going to leave my daughter for 4 hours to work but didn't trust the staff to care for my girl so i called in sick instead. she said lots of changes with radios removed and staff reduction but she will "look into it". i know her power is limited, we all do our best.
although my daughter is 17, she needs help. she deserves attention as much as the infants and toddlers. i am blessed that my employer allows me sick days to be here with my daughter. i feel so incredibly worried for other kids here whose parents cancanbe here to make sure their babies have iv & medications timely. the staff appears to be depleted and rushed to the next room, again, a few staff mentioned the need to skip breaks to keep up & losing staff when they need more. 
the children deserve better, so do the staff in the trenches. upper level "decision m as kers" have created a safety concern in my heart for my daughter & the children here with us. pray we get good care as we are here until monday at minimum.....

absolutely terrible er experience and was shocked at how uneducated the doctors seemed to be on what i thought would be very simple and common medical questions. in fact, when asked about the risks of certain medical procedures, they went so far as to tell us there were none (which is not just unethical, but illegal since that was not the case) and then were not honest with us about the results of other tests. and when we questioned all of this, they threatened to call cps on us and said they were the doctors and they were the ones that knew what was best for our child. unless you want to be bullied and threatened with your child being taken away for asking simple questions about how certain procedures could affect your child, i would not go near this place with a ten foot pole. 

i also had asked multiple times to speak to the director of the er and was told i would be receiving a call each time. i have yet to receive a single call. so much for caring about feedback, so unfortunately i'm leaving it here to hopefully save other parents the distress and heartache we had to experience, at a time when what we really needed was support, guidance, and help.

you know it's bad when i am writing a review while i am still at the hospital. i am currently in the emergency room helping my uncle. they have taken the x-ray and told us the results (in this case nothing major was wrong). the nurse then said she'll get the discharge paper for us. it's been almost two hours and i haven't heard anything from anyone. the staff was friendly, but it really should not take this long to get discharge papers. extremely disappointed. i should also note that it does not seem super busy either. i've seen other nurses going in and out of the other patients' rooms in a timely manner, so i really do not understand what's going on.

good overall staff are nice although one was
not very tolerant.
that aside the doctors are very good.

between the aggressive insensitive ems agents that showed up.the lack of attention from the hospital staff. my father fell down stairs and they treated him as if he was a liar or not in as much pain as he claimed he was. as if we want to call them, as if we want to spend 8 hours in a emergency room surrounded by other sick people, we just had a sudden death in the family. and not 30 minutes later my father misses the steps and falls forward with a sharp pain in his leg he screams out like i've never heard him before and can't get up. ems get there and i promise, i will be following up with their names and filing a proper complaint.they begin to speak rudely to people asking my father confusing questions.insulting the pastor to be quiet while he translates to his asshole partner meanwhile we all speak english.no sense of humanity or care for the situation. i'm sure they encounter chaotic scenarios and maybe they've dealt with people so long they hate them now. but that isn't my problem.one has the nerve to say excuse me and grabs my arm and pushes me aside and claims ignorance to what he just did. had that not been my father it would've been a very different outcome.we get to the hospital and he begins to explain to a nurse who just walks away mid talk and gesture wit her hand to just place him on the side. ems guy tries to find empathy by saying " u guys get mad at us but look how they treat us " i even apologized to the guy because i refuse to let their sad negative energy affect me in the slightest. from there they ask my dad very casually the pain meter question 1-10 which i assume based on the treatment we received is what determines priority. while my dad has his leg straight the pain is a 6 but if they understood the situation or read the notes the ems took down they would see when he attempts to bend it the pain is a 15! we get there at 530pm an hour later we see radiology and then from 630- 1130pm we just have to wait.we see doctors walking around were being very patient and every hour ask if there's any updates i was told by 8pm the results were in and viewed and all it needed was a doctor to confirm it. if that's the case then why did we have to wait almost 4 hours more. from what i perceived we were ignored because we weren't deemed a high priority. i have no doubt that there are other people in much dire need of assistance  but when i see the doctors laughing with each other and standing around ( never to deny someone a break especially them since i have just experienced the high strung attitudes of some ) while i was just told all i was just waiting on was a was doctor to view the results is highly upsetting. my father had a pain so sharp he almost fainted from it. he was trembling from the shock. plus dealing  with the death in the family. but all this isn't found on paper it's found through real conversation & a real interest. treating every patient with the care & attention you would want ur own significant loved one to receive. its disappointing the whole hospital system is but a greedy corporation.keep them as long as you can ensuring the maximum insurance charge.finally by 11 i can't take it anymore and begin to complain and i ask how long are they planning on keeping us waiting for the sake of waiting. i get two nurses to run around and  literally grab the same doctor i have  seen walk past us numerous times seen standing around seen laughing it up and chit chatting. walks in and says " you're all fine nothing is tore or broken, maybe it's bruised we'll give you motrin for the pain and you should use ice packs " and that was it, 1 minute and done. before my dad can even ask him a full question he's walking away. if i tell you my blood pressure was going to go over the roof at this moment is a understatement, i call out to him to come back and make gesture my dad still has questions in regards to what he said vs what my dad feels. he dismisses his questions saying he's fine and looks away then looks back at us and says " all good? and you know what let's get you a cane ". walks away. we wait for the paperwork and the cane and surprise surprise he's disappeared no one knows anything about the cane they can't find the doctor or a cane and in frustration my dad just wants to leave. with the same pain he came, the quality of work at this hospital is lacking to say the least. but you know what out of total fairness because we're decent people who believe everyone should be treated with the same respect and kindness we expect of others. there was a guy in radiology, benjamin. what a saint, he actually managed to make me laugh. made my father feel at ease and comfortable with his personable personality and smile. whatever benjamin is taking it needs to be given to the rest. 2 more nurses checked in who were nice. besides benjamin i can't name one other person,u ask who's the doctor on site and no one knows. and i see why, they don't want the complaints compiling.

the worst experience i have ever had with doctors. i was there for over 10 hours, mostly ignored, and yelled at when i tried to inquire what was going on. i came here for excruciating pain after a doctor gave me medicine to take to prepare for a procedure; my dr. told me to go to the emergency room. two doctors finally did a vaginal ultrasound, but they would not talk to me. then they turned off the light and *left* the room, leaving me in a corner. after a few hours, i forced myself to walk into the hall and ask someone wtf is going on - they forgot about me. they finally told me to just talk to my doctor (!) and gave me pain medicine. no one called me to follow up. they should be ashamed of themselves.

came to the allen pavilion because my mother was throwing up due to an adverse reaction from a procedure she had that morning--while we had no problem waiting to be seen because we do understand that there were others who may have to be seen immediately  because of their severity --what i have a problem with is that a another patient in the waiting room apparently texted a friend who obviously works here --she comes in  --because her friend who's sitting said when he saw her "i didn't expect you to come" and she answered i'll be back i'm going to the back --she comes back a little later to her friend after standing in foyer joking with security guard and proceeds to tell her friend you're going to be called next--"what's your last name again? castillo? right?" within 5 minutes they were called --mind you we've been sitting here going on 5 hours --they go in and she leaves 10 minutes later --we go to inquire when will  my mother be called -they said there's no specific time depends on severity of patient--so we continued to wait --mind you now it's 2 hours later again i go to front desk to inquire and there's no one there i waited there for about 15 minutes and no one came out not even the security guard was there --at that point we were getting very frustrated and decided to leave and take her to another hospital

i had the absolute worst experience with this doctor. i unfortunately had a miscarriage and had the sad luck of having to see her for my confirmation of an unviable pregnancy. the first words out of her mouth were "i don't think we've met before".  unfortunately for her, we had met, when she delivered my baby only 6 months prior. we have electronic medical records these days use them. she then asked my husband and i if we were trying for this pregnancy. i am still confused as to why she would ask such a question when we just found out we lost the fetus. the appointment got way worse and it would take too much effort to type out the rest. long story short, stay far far away. she needs to retire or learn how to treat people. she was upset i would not consent to a procedure to remove the pregnancy surgically 2 hours after the diagnosis and refused to come back in the room with instructions. she had her two nurses do it. this left us with more questions than answers. northwestern should be ashamed to have sole ohs like her oh staff.

carrier clinic is not the same since hackensack meridian took over. a family member was there is 2017 and it was a wonderful experience for him. patients could go to the dining room and play cards. go off the unit and explore the beautiful grounds. it felt happy when you went on the unit. he was there again recently and its feels sad and pathetic. patients cannot leave the unit at all.  they eat all meals on the unit. patients pace the hallway all day and it feels like an insane asylum. everything has to be approved, even a weighted blanket. thank god my son connected with a wonderful nurse.he was moved to a different unit and his room four times because he couldn't sleep with all the chaos. his experience there was traumatic. people screaming at night saying they want to die or just screaming in general. if my family member needed inpatient mental health help, i don't think i would want to send them to carrier. hackensack meridian needs to reevaluate their methods of treating patients because it could be so good. it was good. now, not so much.

my child was a patient here on the adolescent unit in the middle of october 2019 and i found the staff to be polite and very hellful both in person and ln the phone. they have grewt weekend visiting hours although i thought the 6 day stay for my child was  a little rushed

during our visit to breckenridge we went here at 3am because one of the members of our group suffered from altitude sickness, dehydration, hypokalemia, hypoxia and gastroenteritis. the hospital is located in frisco, just a 15 minute ride away from breckenridge. we were attended to quickly and all of the staff from receptionist, nurse, phlebotomist, radiology tech, respiratory therapist, and er physician dr. adler were professional and caring. we received clear discharge instructions and they also made arrangements for home oxygen that we could use for the week. copies of all the test results were given to us. because of their prompt and expert care we were able to enjoy the rest of our vacation. thank you to everyone in the er- you were all great!

my stanford health care affiliated doctor referred me to stanford healthcare facility for a simple audiogram, yes, hearing test. this was just to get a baseline hearing loss for my 10 year old tinnitus.  

stanford healthcare pulled a bait & switch scam on me and blue cross insurance company. two weeks after the audiogram test i get a bill for $700; $250 already paid by blue cross... i effectively am supposed to pay the rest.

i was floored, so looked up general costs for audiograms.  results show audiograms cost about $40-70, with average full blown hyper-testing at $114 average across the us.  evidently hearing aid companies even give free audiograms if you are considering hearing aids.  

in the 1950's-1960's every kid in every school in my town got the same audiogram that i just got, every year, free. it was the same test and same results that i got from stanford healthcare last month. it was just ear buds, a laptop, a button pusher with beep-beep-button pushing.  

$700? - i am not paying these scam masters at stanford healthcare. 

i raised the issue with their billing and escalated up their chain. but after 2 step-ups they will not even call me back. the last one flat refused to escalate up their business chain.   
i essentially got, "we performed the services and you have to pay us."

and now, just a month after the test, they are starting with the billing collection threats, already, and payment is not even past due.  

i am asking all of my family and our friends to pull out of stanford healthcare primary care offices and never use higher services. 

i am not paying this bill. i am also reporting them to blue cross for potential fraud (bait & scam switch is a form of fraud). if they push me to pay that bill, i will sue them in small claims. i'll pay $5k not to pay stanford healthcare a penny. 

recommend you get out and/or stay away from stanford healthcare.

almost all of stanford healthcare facilities get about 2 of 5 ratings in yelp... mostly because of their scam billing and insane, unscrupulous pricing practices.  look it up. 

this crap is what is going to get the us onto national healthcare faster than anything else.... which i am ok with.

it's called children's hospital but the thing you need to be worried about is losing your life savings to them.

my son had a 5-minute laser procedure administered by dr. anna bruckner. a no-risk laser treatment. we've had it done for years.

what did they charge for this procedure? well, dr. bruckner charged us $2,688. what?! even better, children's hospital charges us separate from that $1,102.

$3,800 for a 5-minute procedure. the system is broken, and people like dr. bruckner perpetuate this. our insurance company, aetna, saved us about 25% and my total bill is now $1,700.

for a 5-minute procedure.

make sure you get the cost of your procedure in writing before going forward with anybody here. i will never give them my money again.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review:
took my son for a consultation and it was a good experience. the doctor was knowledgeable and very good with my son. he made sure we were comfortable with everything at each step. 

parking is always a bear, but the computerized check-in process they have now is super handy.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review: i have 4 kiddos and all of them have been patients at children's at some point. the staff is attentive and willing to help. i've learned that i need to be super clear about my expectations and my child needs. we have dealt with a lot of medical issues and i feel as though the staff and our family are a team working to get the medical issues resolved. my one criticism is the dental department. i have waited in the waiting room for extensive periods of time and it is always overflowing with people. we scheduled a dental surgery and were given a price for the procedure and then were charged almost triple. that was extremely frustrating. i give the hospital 5 stars and the dental department 2 stars.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, Aurora

review:
this place is the reason i am still alive. after being sent home from the er with a diagnosis of anxiety dr pradip morbia found three blockages in my heart. he would not stop until he found out what was wrong with me. 
people who complain about having to wait in his office need to understand if you are not seen at appointment time it's because someone needs him more. if i woke up this morning feeling bad i could go to the office and be seen today. this man gives his cell phone number to his patients. he answers any time. the health and well being of his patients is his number one priority.  
as a bonus he gives god all the glory for his healing abilities.

i brought my elderly grandfather into the emergency room because he was having severe issues breathing. mind you he's had a 5 way bypass and cancer in the previous years, and recently diagnosed with dementia as of 2 years ago. i expressed to the woman at the front that he could barely catch his breath nor even walk in the building due to being out of breath, they didn't seem concerned and told us to wait our turn. ok, totally fine we can wait not a problem in any way. 4 hours later during which my grandfather struggled to breath the entire time to the point where other patients actually expressed their concern for him to the front desk. once again we were wrote off, and i never once complained. we finally were sent back to a freezing cold waiting room where we waited for another 2 hours. at this point my grandfather is impatient and scared due to his dementia. when nurses finally came in they told us we were going to have to go back out to the waiting room where i finally said absolutely not. there's something seriously wrong, she agreed and said they would set up a chest x-ray. long story short he was admitted and his heart was failing! they kept us in the er for the night which was miserable my grandfather is completely restroom incompetent  and i was the one that had to change his diaper and clothes! we finally get a room the next day and majority of nurses yelled at my grandfather and talked so loudly in his face he was terrified. the next night was the worst i had found out the nurses were giving my 81 year old grandfather and entire vile of adavan for no reason except they didn't want to deal with him. i finally asked a nurse why he looked so out of it and she told me they had been giving it to him and it was never once discussed with me. i never left the room after this unless absolutely necessary. fast forward to 10 that evening my grandfather was out of diapers and i needed to grab some out of the car. i requested a nurse to sit with him (mind you he was completely passed out sleeping) i specifically instructed the charge nurse and my nurse to not give him anything at all while i was gone. i timed myself- 11 minutes, when i got back they had dosed him again! i specifically instructed them not too. at that point i was absolutely disgusted and completely upset. your staff needs a significant amount of training when dealing with elderly people, and especially ones suffering from dementia. there was only one nurse who didn't scare my grandfather, and he absolutely loved her. she talked calmly and quietly and he even would joke around with her. i had to ask someone to help me bath him 3 days in which i once again had to do. it was a terrible experience really. i absolutely do not recommend this hospital to anyone suffering from dementia/alzheimer's.
avoid at all costs. this hospital lot my records, ran extensive tests on me, only to tell me nothing    and that they want me to have procedure redone at my cost!
fac_name: Three Rivers Community Hospital & Health Center

review: do not go to this hospital! dr. alicia sanders negligent care could have killed me! i went into this facility with a 4mm obstructed infected kidney stone with hydronephrosis (fluid backing up into kidney). i have documented history of chronic kidney stones (that is shown in their system) and had ct from the previous week showing the stone available for them to see. doctor sanders was very aggressive and negligent in my care. she refused to believe i had a kidney stone despite it showing up on her x-ray that she ordered and accused me of being a drug addict. i asked multiple times for a different doctor to be assigned to my case. the male nurse that treated me said there was another doctor and he will see me. the female nurse sandy and doctor sanders lied and said there is no other doctor. the doctor wanted a ct and i said i would consent but that i was in so much pain i would not be able to hold still and asked for pain medicine. i was in 10/10 pain and in so much pain i could barely even speak or walk. (imagine someone cutting you apart with a chainsaw, that is what an obstructed kidney stone feels like).  no one cared and continued to deny me care or acknowledge i had a kidney stone despite it showing up on the x-ray she ordered and previous ct i provided.  dr. sanders fabricated events to have me removed from the facility because obviously her ego had been offended when i asked for a different doctor. she accused me of cursing when i did not. she bumped shoulders with my mother as she came into the room and then tried to accuse my mother of hitting her. she said i was refusing treatment when i was not. the female nurse forcibly ripped out my iv and roughly grabbed my arm to throw me out of the bed. this later resulted in scar tissue in my vein making its future use difficult and painful. they had a police officer escort me out. they made me walk to my car even though i was in 10/10 pain, very unstable physically, and almost passing out from the pain, the police officer was pounding on my car door only minutes after i left saying i had to leave now, even though my mother was trying to put the new hospital in the gps. all of this horrible treatment was in front of my two young children and mother.  i subsequently went to a different hospital, community hospital, and was immediately treated correctly. my case was so severe i was hospitalized for over a week. i had a massive infection, the stone was blocking the flow of urine to my kidneys, and my pain was so severe i was on iv pain meds around the clock until my surgery. when i told my urologist what happened he said to never go to st. vincent's again and that this previous doctor's negligence could have killed me.

i am very thankful that you are in my area to care for my family when we are in need. the hours that you are available makes it easy to be seen. the staff is courteous and professional and always makes my visits comfortable as they can. nancy is sweet caring and always smiling treating  you well in your time of need. i have always been able to talk to becky and get my problems resolved. coming here is like dealing with trusted family. so grateful to have a quality provider so near to home. thanks for being available for the last 15 plus years.

the clinic can get pretty backed up and you may not get appointments in a reasonable amount of time but you can always leave a message to your provider. the staff is pretty helpful when they are available and the new kiosk check in process is pretty convenient. we love dr. mandebach in pediatrics! he's the best pediatrician my kids have had in our 6 years of clinic visits. the pharmacy staff is super slow i wish they could get some up training or something in the process to make it quicker for service and pick up.

been going to the davis monthan afb pharmacy for years with good service. over the past year, have seen the support given to retirees go down hill. in addition to federal holidays, numerous down days are now added to the times the bx pharmacy is closed.

but today was a sad situation for all retirees. most folks know that on the 3rd thursdays of each month the pharmacy opens at 12:30 not early in the morning.

this morning my wife forgot the policy and arrived at 10:30 to get some prescriptions. she then realized her error and saw all the signs saying open at 12:30. she decided to wait rather than come back.

around noon while waiting she saw the numerous folks coming into the waiting room getting ready for it to open at 12:30pm.

then a young lady in her af uniform, just before noon,  came over and posted a notice that the bx and clinic pharmacies would be closed all day.

now if there was an emergency this is totally acceptable because the support is for our war fighters not dependents or retirees.

but if was not an emergency, this is totally unacceptable. there were no notifications on the phone or at the pharmacy saying they would be closed all day.

i would hope our base commander would take a look at the operations of the bx pharmacy and hopefully prevent this from happening again.

we took our son for surgery this morning at newport beach surgery center on 19th and newport boulevard. our experience was so amazing that it prompted me to go write a review which is not my norm. the attentiveness of the registered nurses and debbie. and several other but i regret not paying better attention to their names, because they were absolutely gracious and kind from the moment we went back they played with my son they removed all of his fears from a scary situation for a little guy and made it as pleasant of an experience as having your son going to general 
anesthesia could possibly be.


thank you so much for the kindness you showed my child and my wife and i

i am a bit confused by the bad reviews. this is just a facility at which respective doctors have operating rights.  they pay for the privilege to use the facility.   it seems like most of the bad reviews are based on the doctors who are independent of the surgery center, and thus not relevant 

i recently had elective surgery at the surgery center and spent the  night in recovery.   the staff was amazing  from check in to check out.  the night nurse was there for me within seconds every time i needed her.  everyone was friendly  and so helpful.  these are the people hired by and work for the surgery center, not my doctor.  in addition the facility is clean and comfortable.   

there was some confusion about my appointment time and i did have to go 24 hours without food (which i need to do more often) but not anything drastic that  would cause a bad review.  if your doctor uses this facility for surgery, be rest assured, it's a clean and friendly place.

clean, friendly & efficient! all the nurses and docs were super attentive and made sure i was comfortable before and after surgery! i appreciate the smiles and being around a team of medical professionals who seem to enjoy their work and environment! i just received a follow up phone call this morning which is icing on the cake! 
thank you nbsc!

had to go to st joseph to get a procedure for my heart. after reading some of the reviews i was really worried.

the check in desk needs a big sign that says ..." please sign in and have a seat until we call you" there is a sign in sheet but you can't see it unless you are at the counter. so myself and everyone else ask the same question intruding on the check in nurse.

2nd check in on 2nd floor went off with no problem. everyone was very good and very informative. doctor came in and plainer what they would be doing and the options. 

i don't have any issues with st. joseph's

i've been here in the er tonight for hours with the loudest, angriest, screamiest, most vulgar person i've seen/heard in a long time. er is packed like sardines and staff overwhelmed. i foresaw countless more hours of misery in my future....

until nurse celilia noticed my misery from down the hall and came to our rescue. pretty sure my patient was not her responsibility this evening. but she recognized the need and swooped in seconds before i broke! a tiny piece of my life was made infinitely better because she helped us. :)

so today i went to ca urgent care this morning and they sent me to the er at st joseph's for a possible appendicitis. i got called back at st joes er fairly quickly and thought i'd have a good experience, especially after the awesome experience we'd had at the santa cruz facility with my grandson previously. once i was called back all attention stopped. while the nurse working was seemingly nice,  he kept ignoring a lady that had been there all day and was just waiting for a room so they could admit and transfer her. she kept saying in her weak little elderly voice, "i'm diabetic and haven't eaten all day!" even after hearing a doctor ask him to help her he didn't. i finally got up myself and asked him a second time if he could help her. he didn't. it wasn't until i asked to speak to a supervisor an hour later that he sat down beside her and explained to her what was going on. i was being poked on as they tried to draw blood and get an iv started, which took them six times! two they couldn't get because i was so dehydrated, once they infiltrated a vein, then they hit an artery on each arm!! yep! two arteries they hit! they finally got the iv going on my wrist! after i had the ct scan i was put in a hall, sitting up, in a chair...for almost five hours! as i sat there in misery i had to be alert because there were so many nurses, doctors, other employees, gurney's, medical records computers carts, wheelchairs, and many other things and people zipping down the hall past me. at one point there were three nurses trying two wheel three separate gurneys, in two directions, by me and i had to stand, pull my iv cart backwards, and stand inside the curtain of the patients space in the bed behind me. as i sat there nurses lined a hallway on stools, propped up against a wall, with their computers in front of them, they laughed and joked, one guy even making a sexual comment where i could hear!! as if all this wasn't enough it was disgustingly dirty with two tourniquets on the floor, dirty kleenex's, candy wrappers, and cups on the floor. it can't be good for all those nurses to work in an environment like that with no set place to sit and record their medical notes not to mention it's extremely unprofessional to be discussing patients medical conditions and test results in front of every eavesdropping ear...right there in the hall! the doctor nor one nurse ever came back to check on me or update me on anything let alone see if i was okay. it wasn't until i saw the doctor come walking by and i asked for my results and if someone could remove my iv that anyone paid any attention! i had to get upset and tell them i was going to remove the iv myself so i could go home because i wasn't a priority to them and they weren't doing anything at all! i will never go back there which is sad because st. joes has always a good reputation! when you come to a hospital and voice your concerns, you should be taken seriously, and treated with respect. the lady in the front office found my mother's predicament amusing just by seeing how she smiled. the nurse who came to help my mother and relieve her of concerns went above and beyond. i guess it just depends in the individual health staff.

my husband was transported to this hospital after a traffic collision on a santa paula highway . the accident occurred in the mid afternoon when i arrived to the hospital after a 2 hour drive my husband was sitting in his clothing with lacerations from broken glass hitting his face  a swollen knee, pain to his shoulder, neck and back and side waiting for results from x-rays ... we sat and talked and we discussed some details about his treatment in emergency room department my husband was traumatized, tired and confused from the accident . when he asked a nurse on duty for some water he was told " i'm busy and i'll get to you when i can". it took the department 4 hours for  them to x-ray... the front administration was rude, callus, and unprofessional and her only concern was if i had our insurance card , the x-ray tech was insensitive to the pain and at one point hit my husbands knee against the wall ... i eventually complained and requested to speak the supervising nurse on duty i instead spoke to the attending physician i deeply expressed my dissatisfaction with the treatment provided my the nurses and other staff ... winding this all down ... it took the emergency room staff 4.5 hours to give my husband water 3.5 for them to x-ray him the results of x-ray were 3 broken ribs and a very bad experience at santa paula hospital

emergency room/west ashley. be very careful about using these services. they appear to have limited access to knowledgeable staff. i got the feeling that doctors who work in the hospital are not available for emergency consultation in a timely fashion. in my case i was sent home with a kidney stone. i almost died and had i not been transported to roper downtown, i feel sure i would have. all because there was no one available to read a cat scan. 
roper/st francis downtown is amazing and i cannot sing their praises loud enough.

after years of suffering from back pain due to degenerative disc disease i went to see doctor samip morker and i can't believe how amazing dr. morker and his team were able to put together a plan long term plan to help me be pain free. all you will say is "why didn't i do this earlier!" thank you doctor morker and team.

i followed up via phone and email and never received even a generic response.

so i went in for a d&c, which is a fairly standard operation. no matter how i tried, i couldn't get them to put into their medical records that i'm allergic to some antibiotics--one severely. my primary care doctor told them. i believe my ob-gyn's office told them, but friday afternoon before i was to have surgery, they called me on an old phone number i haven't used for fifteen years (somehow, it still put a notice in my email), and when i called back, they had no record of these allergies. 

what they wanted (it was a nurse who didn't seem to care about putting in my drug allergies) was $4,000 upfront, or they wouldn't operate. i needed this operation to rule out cancer, so i argued them down to $1,000 upfront.

the medical information they had on me was 20 years out-of-date, including illnesses i hadn't had since my 20s. i'm almost 50. 

spooked by this horrible record-keeping, i made sure to walk in on the day of my operation with several printed copies of the medicines i was taking and the medicines i was allergic to. i gave these out to several nurses. (it was never clear to me who was a nurse and who was a med-tech. they should introduce themselves better.)

on intake, they mentioned that they gave people lavender essential oils as part of pain relief. i told them not to--that i was allergic. lavender gives me asthma. remember this....

so i gave out my sheet listing my medications and allergies to several people, but when i got into the operating room, one of the last things i remember the surgeon saying was, "so, no allergies?!" i told him then and then--they were already giving me things through my iv, that i had a severe reaction two two common antibiotics (clarithromycin and cirpo) and could not take them.

this was after telling seven people that i had these issues.

so i woke up in recovery, and there was the nurse, trying to give me lavender.

i told her to go away.

i was in pain, but only accepted an extra-strength tylenol because i was afraid that, if i was out-of-it, and they screwed up and tried to give me something that would make me sick, i wouldn't be able to stop them.

harbor hospital is not a safe place to go because they can't get basic info about your drug allergies into their system.

getting money out of you is more important than taking care of you.

i went to the sleep clinic which is a building on hospital property by the parking garage in july.  it was just my initial office visit with the doctor to see if i should get a sleep test.  i have insurance and received a bill soon after from the dr for her charges as i would expect.  fast forward to jan and i receive a $300 bill from exeter hospital for a facilities charge.  what!  the dr bill wasn't even that expensive.  then i received a $600 bill from exeter hospital from a mammogram i had in june, 6 months ago!  how can they do this?

this review is for the nurses and staff who helped my son this am during his surgery (outpatient). not only was everyone welcoming, but they thoroughly explained everything, were kind, efficient and compassionate.

save yourself injury, chronic pain and suffering. i got injured by a physical therapist at this location. no one took accountability for their actions. practice manager backed up the therapist who performed unnecessary manipulation on me and caused an injury. i will not recommend this practice to anyone. irresponsible, poorly trained and unethical therapists are employed here. go somewhere else to get treated but not here!

i was a high risk pregnancy and had to go in twice a week to be monitored, plus multiple stays. i got to know the staff and they each hold a special place in my heart, from registration, to my ultrasound tech, to the nurses and doctors! they all worked together amazingly! they each went above and beyond for my labor and delivery and it was a wonderful experience! i would highly recommend this hospital to anyone!!! the ob department is the best and since it's a small hospital the nurses are able to be right there and help you at the drop of a hat! i couldn't say enough good about them!

i went into penn choking and doubled over in pain. because i had a temp of almost 102 at home, and hadn't decided to go to the er, i took tylenol. when i got worse, my husband took me to penn. they didn't check my lungs despite all the coughing, and they didn't believe me about the fever. all they did was labs and an abdominal ct. when that came back okay, the nurse comes in and says i can go now. i asked what's wrong with me and she said "nothing." the doctor never even came in. i was very sick and angry. i got my blood test results with bad cbc numbers. i called out, "what about the bad labs?" the dr yelled back "follow up with your primary?."when the nurse handed me paperwork that had a diagnosis of constipation, i threw the papers on the floor. they called security who booted me onto the street where i waited in the freezing cold a half hour to get picked up. i got home and passed out. my adult son came in from work  hours later and checked in on me. my temp was nearly 103. he ran me to the virtua er where i was evaluated and admitted 2 hours later for pneumonia and influenza a. i was 4 days in the hospital and 3 weeks in medical rehab.  i'll never go to penn again!

as with most hospitals i've had good experiences and bad experiences i am a sickle cell patient and those with sc know exactly what i'm talking about. but my last visit doctor rico was the doctor who took care of me during my admission. i have to give him all the praise that i can give to a doctor he made my stay pleasant,no stress at all, in fact his bedside manner was more healing then anything and i thank him. i just wish more doctors would treat sickle cell patients with the same amount of caring and respect that dr rico showed me. again thank you dr rico i know i rated three stars but that's because of other stays some good some not so good that i had at paoli hospital, but this last stay and doctor rico really earn a five star review...mike w.

i live in california and had to come to houston for a family emergency. i've been undergoing a new depression treatment in california called spravado. this is a brand new drug and must be administered in a doctor's office. i've been having great results and was disappointed that i would have to miss two of my weekly treatments. i called around on the off chance that i could find someone here to do the treatment, and i was a little doubtful it would work out since it was the week of new year's. i got a list of local providers from the internet.  a very nice lady named jenny called be back from houston behavioral healthcare center. jenny worked overtime to quickly process my insurance and was able to get me in for a treatment. jenny is a wonderful and caring lady who is truly committed to helping people. she also runs the ect department there. jenny welcomed me and and happily provided the treatment i needed and i'll forever be grateful to her. i hope anyone who suffers from severe, treatment resistant depression will reach out to jenny and consider trying spravado. thank you so much jenny and houston behavioral healthcare hospital.

review:
been at this hospital's er 5 times in the last few years due to reoccurring medical coonditions.  the er wait times to see a doctor are ridiculous. every time we come here with an emergency, it takes hours to see a doctor.  6 months ago my wife was having 10/10 pain due to a rare medication side  affect and they couldn't persctibe pain medication  until she saw a doctor. it took 3 hours to see a doctor after we got a bed in the er!  she was in 10/10 pain for 3 hours!   now i'm sitting with  her again in the er 6 months later due to another rare reaction. it's 7:30am, we've been here for  1.5 hours already and we haven't seen a doctor yet. she's in 8/10 pain weeping in pain and there seems to be no sense of urgency from these doctors. 

if i could sue this hospital, i would, but i don't know if i can.

went here last year for my annual mammogram. the tech did not seem to know what she was doing and had to take a few slides over again which i'm sure you ladies understand is not fun. then, a few weeks later, i received a letter from them saying i was going to need to come back because of an "architectural distortion" on one of the slides for my left breast. i have no idea what that means and they gave no explanation. i made the appointment right away and yet i received at least ten (10) further exact letters (not exactly eco-friendly!). i called to confirm my appointment and they said it was on the calendar. i then received a registered letter from them with--you guessed it--the exact same information as the previous letters!!! i went for the appointment on the scheduled date (7/25/19) and there was nothing wrong with my breast. what a scam! but it gets better. they then billed my insurance $751 for the appointment of which $201.31 was my responsibility since they stated that that visit was "diagnostic"--not "preventative" even though it was coded the same on the bill. i disputed it and they sent me a bill for $160.28 and then another for $77.56 due on 12/27/19. i paid the amount before the due date but before then, i received a collection notice dated 12/24/19. they didn't even give me a chance to pay before the due date and the collection company is asking for the original amount--$201.31. so now i have to deal with them. my purpose for writing this is to warn you how shady this hospital has become and to advise you to go to any other women's mammography center other than this one!

i had an amazing fibroid surgery and 3 night stay here under the care of dr. michael randell. the nursing staff is amazing! every one we interacted with in 7west was so patient-focused, caring, responsive and everything you want out of a nurse.  my husband and mom stayed in the hospital with me 24 hours a day, and the nurses never seemed annoyed or bothered by them.  the rooms are on the smaller side, but doable. we got a cot off amazon for my husband to stay in and my mom stayed in the recliner that comes in the room. if you have any questions, i would recommend you contact karen lynn at 678-843-5889. being an out of town patient and someone who had literally never been in the hospital, i had a lot of logistical questions that i was having trouble getting answered and being put through to various departments when i called the general line. i finally found karen and she was a lifesaver!  the only negative about this hospital, which isn't enough to make me take off a star, is that you have to pay to park, and it's hard to understand how to get a day pass in the lot.  here are my best directions on how to do it:  1.) when entering the blue lot (not purple!) for the very first time, push the button and take the ticket. 2.) when leaving for the first time, put your ticket in the machine slot and press the all day pass button before paying anything. pressing this button will spit your ticket back out and this will be all your day parking pass. 3.) when returning to the blue lot, press the only button and get a 2nd ticket; keep this ticket just in case your all day pass doesn't work. however, this ticket shouldn't be needed again. 4.) if you're staying overnight, be cautious because the all day pass only works till midnight.

my recent stay on cvu was exceptional. corrina, michelle, leilani, erin, sarah, alfred, nicole, and victoria were all so compassionate and practiced with professionalism. also the staff in the gi lab, stephanie and toni were kind and informative and helped to ease me through my procedure with patience answering all of our many questions. the director of cvu roxy is a great leader, as is reflected in those in which she leads. the bedside care i received made a significant impact on my stay and i applaude this hospital, as they are fortunate to have such an amazing staff.

horrible er....
4 hours in severe pain put in a room and go a blanket 1.5 hours later after no contact. my boyfriend had to go ask why none had been to see me.  i have been down 5 days with my back, they finally came in, explained how i was hurting to the np, she sent a pain pill for me to take, had a 1 min cat scan and was sent  home with eleven and a muscle relaxer.
i will never go back....

went to the er for horrible side pain at midnight (on my birthday mind you) and had to wait over an hour and a half in the waiting room, doubled over in pain. it wasn't until i threw up that they finally got me a room. then i laid in a hospital bed for another hour and a half. they only took me for the ct when a surgeon i know called and told them to and after i threw up again. they finally gave me pain medication, told me it was a kidney stone, and sent me home at 4am without any sort of strainer or anything so they couldn't study the kidney stone and tell me how to prevent another one. $6,000 for all of this.

horrible experience at this  er.. i would strongly advise anyone seeking care to avoid this hospital like the plague. i was seen by dr tubbesing who brought a whole entourage of people in the room with him without introducing any of them or even asking for my consent. i had no idea who they were?? meanwhile, i had to tell him of my female problems in front of him and all these people in the room and listen to him as he belittled me and told me that women bleed and it's never determined why. and my perception of him and his attitude was like - why are u here??? this is not an emergency. you are wasting my time. he then proceeded to make me feel bad for coming to the er by telling me that this is handled outpatient. i turned crimson red. how would u feel in my situation when a doctor is downplaying your situation in front of all kinds of people in the room??? he later came in to apologize and said, "i'm sorry if it offended u that i asked questions to learn more about your condition." the whole situation was disgusting. i will be reporting this to the medical board and i will fight this because i do not want any other patient treated in this manner. there was such a lack of respect and dignity it was really unbelievable. how a doctor can treat a patient like this is beyond me. i had not been to the er since 2012 and i will never return to this er again, but nothing will be said or done b/c he is a director and probably tenured.  he will continue treating patients like something he stepped in (dog poop) and everything will be swept under the rug. that's just the way these egotistical doctors roll. if it won't be handled appropriately internally, maybe i can get the medical board or even news media to listen. thanks for nothing north central baptist. please please please for the love of god, do something about this doctor!!

my family has come here numerous times and have received excellent care. the other day their care topped them all. i had some sort of eye infection, but the doctor prescribed an antibiotic and said that i should follow up with an ophthalmologist if it got worse. then she called from her cell the next morning saying she was concerned about my eye and that i should see an ophthalmologist that day and gave me a couple of recommendations. it's a very good thing she did that. i would have had terrible issue with my eye and they caught it just in time.

incredible! the staff, the facility and the doctors are outstanding. such a professional and excellent organization. i received the very best care. these are the doctors to see. thank you everyone for making my surgery go so smoothly.

best urgent care visit i have ever had in my life? which is ironic because when you very urgently need one, you always seem to have the worst experiences. or at least i do. i came here after i fell the night before and am aching in my shoulder just kept getting worse and worse. i walked right into an empty waiting room and they took me right away. doctor came in before triage was even over and they took me back for a precautionary x-ray. no fractures in the shoulder just possible soft tissue injury. they gave me a sling and sent me on my way. every single person i encountered was highly friendly and lightened the situation in a great way. i have only knocked this down a start because it wasn't getting better and i ended up going to my regular doctor who did a more thorough exam to find that i had shifted my rib out of place during my fall causing the referred pain. i wish this would have been caught during my initial urgent care visit but i'm also glad i didn't have to pay a large er visit bill to find this out. would definitely come here again but hope i won't have to.
records department does not answer or return calls.  tried to call admin and always received  message that receptionist was away from desk and i should call back later.

i could write a short novel on this establishment, but i don't think i have enough space.  anyway, i was admitted after a cervical surgery to this hospital on nov 18th and stayed for 5 days and 4 nights.  i have been in other hospitals recovering from other surgeries, but by far this is the best that i have ever been in.  each and every one of the employees (from the front desk to my room) that i met (and can remember, lol), were extremely nice and caring.  i got to know a couple of them pretty well in the few days that i was there and must give kudos to one of the nurses that i met.  her name is jetta (i call her vw or volkswagon as a nickname, she'll know who i am).  her attentiveness and care-giving was over the top.  i do miss her and her teammates a lot.  not that i want to spend any more time there, but i think that i will drop in to say hi.  in fact, i will most likely be volunteering once i get better.  thank you jetta and your team for making me feel "at home" in a place that not a lot of folks would want to be.  another individual that was quite knowledgeable is eric.  he had great answers to all my questions and did a lot to make me feel better when i was uncomfortable.  he taught me some massage techniques that will really help me - and it has.  i highly recommend this hospital and staff/surgeons to each and everyone that reads this review.  if i ever need another surgery i will definitely, without hesitation be back.  all of you are "second to none".  happy holidays to all!!!!

i had to go to er on a tuesday morning because i fell and felt i broke my arm. the wait was unbelievable but everyone was amazing! my rn was anna, she was wonderful! the doctors, x-rays techs, check in people, check out people, even my splint maker, and especially the nurses were so friendly and helpful! made the wait so much better!  i did break it! ugg! 
they still need to work on the wait times but the people are outstanding!

this is the story of banner hospital emergency room.  i and my boyfriend arrived at 9:00 a.m., we waited for five (5) hours and no one came and gave us any type of update on our long wait.  robert approached the orderly at the lobby door about finding out approximately how much longer we would have to wait.  robert is 70 years old and he has had two hip replacements and 3 heart stents in addition to high blood pressure so by not eating anything he has become a little anxious, but when he approached the orderly and the orderly got loud, robert became loud but this orderly didn't know how to control the situation that he had created so he just calls out some security goons to beat up this old man.  i had just walked outside when all of a sudden five security personnel have hold of robert and takes him and deliberately flung him into the exterior wall of the facility and busted open his head; i ran over and yelled 'what the hell are you doing to him?' everyone stopped and looked at me ( i guess they thought that i had gone) then one of the guards run over to me and tell me to go sit on that bench, i responded that no! i will stand here where i can see what you are doing to him.  housekeeping came out with a bucket of water to wash the blood from the pavement.  now that his head is busted wide open he is taken straight into a room (could i possibly have been treated in that room so we could have been gone?)  banner then charges his insurance $20,000.00 for injuries that they created and we had to pay $250 cash.  today i received a letter from the city attorney's office where banner filed a police report against robert.  banner why don't you try giving your employees some sensitivity training instead of showing your brute force, robert has never had a police record until your little exhibition. not a veteran friendly facility.

this is the hospital we always go to. excellent experience until today 11/8/19. my mom was brought in this morning by 911.  nurse that took care of my mom was so irritated every time i try to approach her something concerning my mom. being also a nurse my self and in the medical field i would never ever raise my finger and point it around to tell someone to hold on. and this was not only one time incident. then when second time i asked for a bed pan, the nurse "angel"  is her name said again ?!!!   if you are so unhappy with your job, no one is forcing you. i hope no one else experiences this. especially in an emergency situation like this.

we were in az visiting family when my daughter fell and split open her chin.  we went to the er at 3am.  we waited over an hour to see a doctor. dr. simran kapur came in looked at my daughters chin and said we should glue it, but she had no idea how to apply the glue!  the nurse ended up doing it, but three hours later (when we were driving back to co) the glue came undone.  i got a huge medical bill a month later for this.  seriously??  this place is a joke along with their non competent doctor.  dr. kapur go back to medical school!  steer clear of this place....it is all about the money for them, not patient care!

it's a plain out horrible place to be at if you get into a altercation with anyone earthier it be physically or verbally they with give you thorazine. thorazine is antipsychotic medication even if your depressed and just depressed nothing else no history of self harm or anything they will give you a dose of that i don't know about the adult unit but on the 14-17 unit they have these things called quite rooms they are pretty much solitary confinement i had to stay in there for at least 30 minutes and it was the longest 30 minutes of my life i never put a hand on anyone there but they still gave me thorazine if your child is depressed just get them a counselor and if that don't work just go anywhere that is not wellstone i will never go back ever and they have a school but all you do in there is learn basic math read a few things then you're done you can have you're child's school work sent over there but it took a week for mine to get there and when it did the school teacher couldn't even help with it. your child will be behind lock doors that a little uneasy feeling when your not used to that and my family has a history of seizures do to a medication that we informed them about and told them not to put me on so they disregard that and they still put me on that medication it was not a good place to be at
great hospital and staff. location is convenient to many places in the new river valley.

i have been in and out of culpeper hospital er 6 times in the past 3 days.  the nursing staff there was wonderful. they were so caring and kind to my husband who was the patient. i'm terrible with names but one of the er docs was the absolute best. very laidback and matter of fact and you just felt like you were in good hands. salt and pepper hair and a culpeper native, he was the best!  we had to leave their care and go to prince william hospital. whereas i easily gave culpeper hospital 5 stars, i would give 0 to pw.

this place is understaffed. my mother in law was sent to the emergency room, because they did not have enough oxygen. it was bought to our attention, that the overnight staff is the worst. they at times don't administer medicines to their patients, but of course they will hound you to pay your bill on time. this place is a joke, and they should be fined and or shut down. veryyyyyy dissappointed with their services.

i spent the day feeling terrible, then this evening i headed to hospitality er. i felt like a queen! they were quick, attentive and very nice. between free snacks and drinks, comfortable chairs, tips on making treatment easier, a shoulder massage, and access to their netflix account, being sick got a whole lot easier! i left feeling much better than when i walked in and the staff called in my prescription promptly. i would highly recommend this establishment to anyone needing an urgent care visit.

everyone should know that this place doesn't treat the elderly or i rather say if you have medicare and a supplement. as the cute blonde at the check-in desk told me, we are privately owned and have the right to deny medicare patients. so don't waste your time at this establishment of no care for the elderly unless you pay cash.

this place is absolutely amazing. they were so caring. the staff kept checking on me. when i came in i was immediately addressed very respectfully and compassionately. dr constante and his nurse were amazing and took the extra step to figure out what was going on with me. i recommend this place!

been here with my grand daughter since 7pm, zahed has not yet been seen, it's now 9:15 pm we still sitting in theater same spot, the got people sitting out here with iv's in their  arms, coughing, old people sitting in wheelchairs, then they keep coming out here calling people that left from waiting to long without being at least triage, this is by far the worst hospital i've ever been in, if you sick do not come here, this fools busy.......they don't get no stars not

this hospital is discussing and should have its license revoked. the lack of care my grandfather received was appalling. he left the hospital in worse condition then he arrived. he went to the hospital because he was having problems standing and walking. his vital signs were good. they were so good the hospital refused to admit him. they put him in a room and kept him on outpatient status for a week. they eventually had to formally admit him because he started having kidney problems. on the day he was supposed to be discharged they left sitting in a chair in a cold room with nothing on but a night gown from noon until after 1:am the next day. our family got a call at 1:am saying he would not be discharged because his blood pressure was too high. (i guess so, he was cold and stressed from sitting in chair for over 12 hours). the nursing staff was dismissive, unhelpful, unengaged, and ineffective. sara and alice are two of the names  i remember -- alice was the one who let him sit there all day and night. sara was rude to my

staff is extremely friendly, competent and professional. i was actually given time to rest. never waited more than 5 mins after ringing my nurse bell. bed was comfortable. i appreciate the gentle treatment.

in the er with an elderly person second time in a month. you know how you walk in and assume - bad night. once was a friday abd then monday. the worse place to be if your sick. no organization and the training is crazy. i felt like i was in jamaica bidding in an auction.  lack of follow through , no bed side manner. have ass er attention.  est thing that could happen is having a better medical facility take them over and train / fire where appropriate

i have been going to the colony er for years. this er is the best hands down. unfortunately for me i have a very complicated medical history that consist of a lot of chronic illnesses. i choose the colony er because of the of the best doctors in the metro area and the great care that i receives. dr. wendie williams is an outstanding doctor that will provide you with excellent professional care. she was my doctor on my last visits and she is absolutely amazing. she is an awesome listener and she have excellent bedside manners. she is so caring and compassionate. she discussed her plan of care and kept me informed of my test results. she explains my test results in a way that i could understand them. she has a clam demeanor which helps me to stay clam. i trust her diagnosis and she also gives recommendations of doctor's to follow up with. she is truly god send. she really knows her stuff and she is a top of the line doctor. i appreciate her so much and her commitment to provide me with the best customer care. from the time that you walk in the doors you are greeted by the most friendliest front desk staff and they are always willing to help you.  nurses like candice, lauren and the other great nurses goes above and beyond the call of to duty to provide you with excellent care. the radiologist and techs/ paramedics are all stellar. dr's. holland, petersen, laseter, carlos and bennetsen are all top notch. going to regular hospitals and waiting in the wait room for three hours is a thing of the past. thank you the colony er hospital for being the best neighborhood emergency room.

the bad news is that i now have a $7,000.00 dog.  the good news is that i have a $7,000.00 relatively healthy dog.

lucy presented in kidney failure (long story--regular vet problem) with bun and creatinine off the charts.  lucy's body temp was 91.1 f, and she was extremely lethargic.  

staff--all of them--were thoroughly professional and compassionate.  lucy was in critical care for a week; was returned for an additional five days three days after original release.  had nasogastric feeding tube initally; replaced by esophageal tube on second admission.  first admit was spent under heat tent.  daily kidney values.   

during both admissions, a vet called me every morning with a progress note.  because of transportation problems, i was unable to visit daily.  when they called, they were able to describe exactly where she was physically and were able to answer all of my questions.  i felt that lucy was getting individual care from vets and vet techs/nurses.  

when lucy was discharged, she was provided with a good supply of liquid diet for use with her feeding tube, and six cans of wet kidney diet dog food.  instructions for tube feeding were provided.

i took lucy to see my regular vet for follow-up yesterday and she's doing much better than expected.  her bun is normal and her creatinine is barely above the normal range.  she's eating and she's gained 0.3 lb. (which is pretty good for an 8-pound dog.)  her behavior is almost back to normal, which i feel is very good for a dog who was practically dead a month ago.

yes, med vet is expensive, but my furbaby got excellent care and, when you consider that she was in critical care for 11 days, the cost isn't totally unreasonable.  i feel she got excellent, life-saving care from a thoroughly professional, competent, and compassionate staff.  everyone, including the receptionists, was concerned about lucy and me.  

the only reason i gave a four-star rating instead of five is because i think her original release was too early and that she should have been  kept a couple of days longer, which would have eliminated the second admission.

it'll take me a long time to pay my credit card down, but i have a happy, relatively healthy dog because of it.  she'll be on a special diet for the rest of her life but, with reasonable care, she should have a normal lifespan.

really disappointed in my experience with med vet.

woke up tuesday (mardi gras) to my cat having gotten sick allover the house. i found her to be lethargic and lacking her usually healthy appetite. this led me to be super concerned and call her regular vet. they were closed due to the holiday so my call was routed to this facility. the receptionist was super kind even after i hung up and tried to call around for a closer clinic. with none open we loaded her up in the car and headed over. 

5 hours later we left with a one thousand dollar bill and a cat who was overall in no better of a state than how we arrived.

long story short the vet became convinced our cat required xrays and then ultrasounds as she was in search of a large obstruction in the cats stomach or intestines which neither test revealed to ever be present. we were so convinced surgery was going to be required that we called family members to tell them and ask for help watching our other animals. our cats condition got worse by the hour, all 5 that we were there, until the ultrasound was conducted and the vet told us it didn't reveal anything "of concern" we were so beyond frustrated at this point i was honestly a little speechless. i asked if our cat could get an iv at this point and i'm honestly not sure why fluids weren't an option earlier. the vet had the nerve to suggest she stay overnight for "monitoring" at this point we were told our bill would be $800 and we declined 

she has since improved and is her normal self again. this seems to have little to nothing to do with the vet visit. 


truly my frustrations are with myself for allowing this emergency clinic to play into my concerns of my pet. moreover we have yet to receive the standard courtesy call after the visit to check on her. this leads me to assume this is not a vet that actually cares for patients not their owners.
