they towed my car!!! i visited and needed to be transferred for emergency surgery. i told them my car was out front and they told me it was fine.... i haven't been able to walk let alone drive so i was concerned. i had to go back to the emergency room due to blood clot from my picc line and asked them again about my car still being there, again they reassured me and told me it was fine. 5 days later i get a notice in the mail that my car is towed and impounded. still unable to walk and drive i was told i had to get all the way downtown and get it myself. oh and pay the $500 bill! ridiculous!
then after speaking with sandra the hospital director she didn't know who authorized that (which i beilive was a lie) and she was going to get back to me, i tried following up and i still don't have an answer: it's been 4 weeks now and nobody ever got back to me as promised! oh but they can sure harass and call me everyday to tell me about the $1200 i owe them!!! i would advise avoiding this place. they overcharge you and clearly don't care about their patients. there's a much nicer place to go in stone oak!

i was taken to the er the second week of november 2019 after having an allergic reaction while donating. pros: the staff was extremely pleasant and respectful and attentive. to be honest, it was the nicest and friendliest experience i've had with medical staff in a long time. way better than university hospital. and the care and attention that i experienced with everyone i dealt with really made me feel comfortable and taken care of. especially when i was provided with warm blankets and tucked in lol. 

cons: the staff and nurses weren't  the best about cleaning after themselves or really lax about clean up. there was a point when i had gone to wash my hands in the sink in my er room and there was a cup full of blood with bandages completely open and exposed just sitting in the sink from who knows when. it wasn't until i notified another nurse that she said, "oh yeah, gross. let me clean that up for you." that it was taken care of. had i not said anything who knows how long it might have stayed there. another thing i noticed is the nurse who came to give me my discharge paperwork and remove my iv for saline left it on the chair beside us (this is in a discharge waiting room, mind you) and it stayed there until i asked another nurse about it, to which she replied "oh yeah, you can just throw it in the trash right there. it's not a needle."  


so overall, 3 stars for how nice and friendly everyone was and the care provided felt very ethical. like asking before lifting my shirt or a sticking me with a needle. it's been a while since i had people describe their every step to me as a patient and treat me with such humanity, vs being treated like just another #. 2 stars knocked off for cleanliness. other than that the beds and rooms were clean everywhere i looked. and the er waiting room even had a water dispenser, coffee maker, and snacks available- which is the first i've seen compared to santa rosa and university hospital er waiting rooms.

completely disgusted with this hospital. husband finally discharged on christmas day with home health care. have we heard from anyone four days later? ofcourse not. case manager in room 12/24 to get authorization. home health place we were assigned to has never heard of my husband. our insurance has called the case manager 3x and been told "working on it", nurses say case manager aware and working on it. so unbelievably negligent! if one does not show up today i'll be filing complaints with every regulatory agency i can find.

er staff was really good. they would get a 5! hospitalist doctor good as well. however once family member was transferred to inpatient, definitely things changed. floors in room very dirty. cna's nice and tried to help but clearly very short staffed, and dad sat being wet and ignored for extended periods. workers don't even make eye contact, most are glued to computers, and definitely give the vibe to just leave them alone. no one asks if they can help even if you walk to nurses station. could hear patients ringing the nurses desk and it took a long time for anyone to answer, even with multiple employees sitting in the nurses station. care providers etc. come in room expecting elderly father to sign all kinds of paperwork that he doesn't understand instead of waiting for a family member. very very disappointing. wouldn't go here again! please fix!!

after posting last review, some one claiming to be from hospital asked for more info and promised to have someone contact us with help. well, no call, but my son now has 120 point ding against his credit score by some visiting doctor who is not on staff at hospital. his office never filed with insurance, but sent the bill to collections agency.
that place is out of control and an administrative mess.

labor and delivery was truly a blessing and took very good care of baby and me, even my husband. i enjoyed all my nurses and the doctors i met along the way. i delivered via cesarean with dr. schectman at acacia obgyn - my last birth with a different dr and hospital.  i was concerned with delivering at this hospital considering the reviews but after having a last minute tour (they made time for, with the lactation consultant) i felt comfortable in doing. i literally have zero complaints. they took my baby so i could have some rest, and treated us like we were family, it was incredible. my last birth at stone oak was a nightmare, i had twins, a careless dr, spent 5 days there with little to no sleep, and it took me two years to recover. this birth i was feeling better by my 6th week. like i didn't even have a caesarean. anybody wondering about this hospital know that it's old. but the staff here is wonderful.
i have a bill from this hospital charging $809.00 for a bag of saline. northeast baptist billing department refused to adjust the amount. stay away.

visited in 2018 because i was exercising and my chest got super tight. i was advised by a friend's wife who is an employee at this hospital that i should go in and have it checked out. this is a hospital that specializes in cardiac care. upon arrival i sat in the lobby for some time before being seen.  i finally went back and saw a nurse and they drew blood and got my vitals and did an ekg and i went back and sat in the lobby. after waiting well over an hour i decided that if i was at risk they certainly would've brought me back by then so i left. i got an outrageous bill. i never saw a doctor and never got the results to my tests. i had to go back to a cardiologist just to verify things were ok. never go here as a walk-in if you are experiencing any type of heart issue. they claim they followed protocol but it certainly doesn't feel like it.  still fighting them over the bill. i have sent an email in to the address provided for other complaints. this is after over a year of going through a dispute process which no one seem to care about my concerns. please read your email so that you can address this appropriately.

horrible unorganized emergency room with a wait time of 10 hours while i had a fever of 102.4. the man who did my blood draw calapsed my vein right in front of me. he left the tourniquet on while pulling the needle out i almost threw up. i'm a phlebotomist and that is the number one thing you don't do to a patient. crazy that they let someone this inexperienced be the person to work on someone who is so sick. never will use anything with wake forest's name on it again.
fac_name: Wake Forest Baptist Health - Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center

review: you have no right to privacy when going through the er at this place. expect at least 4 adults male and female to be in your exam room while you fully disrobe right in front of them. if you ask them to please step out while you change in to a hospital gown... expect the reply to be it's not like we have not seen it all before. unprofessional, disgusting and wrong on every level. i give my dog more respect while relieving himself. when this female made that ignorant statement to me i picked up my purse and walked right out the door. sick with pneumonia and could hardly get a full breath i refused my rights as a human being not to be abused. i went to medical city dallas and was treated with the utmost respect and dignity. was admitted for 4 days and could not find one negative thing to say about this hospital. thank you medical city dallas for being the professionals that you all truly are. your care and respect speaks volumes.

thought this hospital got better but noooooo. where do you even start, the receptionist was so rude, major attitude, she makes you sign papers and doesnt explain what the hell  you are signing, fortunately i know what those papers where, second we have been here since yesterday 7pm, it is now 5am we where suppose to be discharged an hr ago and we are still here, ohhh by the way they lost the urine sample obtained when we arrived. point of this story dont come to this  hospital, travel a little farther for better care.

i love santa anita! the location across from  the park is ideal for bringing recovering family members out to enjoy a peaceful place while participating in rehab.
staff is very attentive and caring. amazing nursing care and therapy staff.
many employees always ask if i need anything when i enter the assisted  living and skilled nursing. 
i have visited many post acute facilities and santa anita is special! attention to communication and families love the care!
if you have a question or concern,  the staff is ready to listen and help.

do not bring family here. i would give negative stars if i could.

my grandfather almost died due to their negligence. he clearly needed to be rushed to the hospital a week before but they continued to say he was fine and he had no infections. when he eventually went, he was diagnosed with pneumonia and had to be hospitalized! he's now recovering in a different nursing home because we would never want to bring him or anyone back to this place.

they are also way understaffed, overworked, uncaring, especially lazy, and unorganized. every time i'd ask for my grandfather's status on how he was eating or his health (mind you our family would go visit everyday), they would say it's fine and when i'd ask to see his charts, they'd make excuses and say he was fine. clearly he was not. the care provided was negligent at best.

not only that but there was constant bribery. i would see patients getting basic care and attention from staff only after they would receive a red envelope or a gift card. this is unacceptable.

moreover, the social worker who visited in the hospital was absolutely unprofessional. she showed up several times to invalidate how my family was feeling and trying to gaslight us into believing it wasn't the nursing facilities negligence. on one occasion, she literally mocked me and laughed at me when i expressed my concerns with why i did not want my grandfather going back to their nursing facilities. honestly, she should be fired for the lack of professionalism and for her condescending behavior toward families that are already going through a difficult time while in the hospital with their family member facing life or death.

no one ended up reaching out to us to apologize or make things right. i believe they were far too afraid of their negligent behavior and receiving a lawsuit knowing they were wrong. it was clear to me they were faking nice while trying to gaslight us. and the fake nice honestly i feel it was because they'd get a fat check from insurance because my grandfather needed extra iv care and breathing machines once he was discharged from the hospital to a nursing home and they wanted to get the money for that since my grandfather would be an "expensive patient." it's clear to me they don't care at all about people. it's just money to them not actual compassion for their patients.

they really need to do better to improve their facilities by taking responsibility for their wrongdoings, hiring employees that have professionalism, and not treating patients like cash cows.

my wife marcie h was at this facility for 5 weeks in dec19 thru jan20....at first we hesitated to go to this type of facilities because of all the negative things you hear from the main stream. we decided to try it since this one was the closest to home. rehab patients have their own building. it has  been remodeled and it's nice. long story short we were very sad to leave because of all the great people that helped my wife and the friendships she built with some of her caretakers.  not everything went well sometimes but by speaking up to the right people we were able to change things for the better we hope. we would like to thank the wonderful people in the admin side and please forgive us for misspelled names.....justin,  marissa, brenda, dr. o and kendra. rehab crew: chantelle, ludy, dax, luisa and mary jane.
building 700: nurses...marlo, rene, vicky, jessica cna's: xianmei cao, grace, suechi, oscar, estevan...a very special thanks goes to this next 3 cna's for really caring and showing it everyday ...their love for what their job requires when dealing with patients. they went over and beyond for caring for my wife with all her needs. elida zavaleta, kathy carino and margarita mendoza. thank you ladies from the bottom of our harts. we will go back and visit when my wife is back to herself.  thank you again. gracias.

my 77 yo mother was admitted through the er for low sodium levels and a uti. after spending several hours in triage, she was admitted. while i really liked her attending dr (dr. barrella), i only spoke with her twice in 7 days, once in the er and again at discharge. information was never communicated to me so the attending nurse paged the dr and spoke to her supervisor, as i was very upset that mom was being discharged without me knowing the results of some tests. hence, the dr came to talk to me. mom already has dementia and lives in a memory care home. her dementia and confusion was exacerbated by the uti and low sodium levels. i visited her daily and she was awake and alert only 2 of the 7 days. apparently she was trying to get up at night to goto the bathroom, asking for food, etc, so she was given ativan 5 of the 7 nights she was there, which created a comatose state of sleep. she could not be woken during the day and was still in this state at discharge. it was like trying to put a dead body in a wheelchair and into my car!  and she barley ate during her stay (bc she slept through every meal), which resulted in her electrolytes being very low. she was never given a bath and her hair was a matted mess from lying in that bed for a full week. we are still trying to untangle it. one med tech was being very rude and short and told my mom that she needed to be nice. i can only imagine what was said to mom when i wasn't there. i would never return to this hospital or recommend it to anyone i cared about.

this hospital has the worst post-op care of any hospital i have ever been to. i had a two level spinal fusion and i was refused any iv pain medication after my surgery. i laid in the hospital bed for two days crying and writhing in pain and they did nothing to help me. the "nurse" that discharged me slammed my foot on the ground because she was angry with me for asking for medication. i had to walk myself out of the hospital with a walker two days after my spine was realigned with hardware because she was being so rough with me. please be aware of you are having surgery here-you will receive no iv pain medication post surgery no matter your procedure. you will be given shots in your butt for pain control which does nothing! please have your surgery at the lake. there is also no icu or critical care floor if there is a complication. i have made complaints with the nursing board, ohh, and frog to investigate this facility. please do yourself a favor and choose the lake where you can get the medications you need post op. horrible horrible facility. never again will i have anything done there!

easy five stars for this emergency room!  my five year old had a face plant which left a hole in her forehead. contemplated taking her to childrens because i knew they used nitrous to stitch, but stuck with my gut to go to my local er. so glad i did. the entire crew was so kind. my daughter got her stitches with a little medication and no drama. i wish i could remember everyone's name, but her nurse leah, with her horse pictures, walked that amazing balance between professional yet we felt like we were with someone who genuinely cared.  thank you so much again. everyone from registration to ma to rn to pa were phenomenal! so happy to know my local er is just as talented with children:)

woke up with extreme back pain and unable to walk normally--thanks body! the er got me in within a half hour and i was on my way to feeling better. the nurses were friendly, listened to my concerns, and discharge was easy. i was there for four hours and things seemed to flow smoothly. considering other er's have much longer wait times, it was nice to have treatment so quickly.

i'm waiting for a doctor to look at a cut finger and this place seems very nice. polite staff, clean facilities, and they even got me a cup of water. my primary care doc is at swedish next door and that office has also been good to work with. can't say i'm looking forward to any future visits but it's nice to know i'll be well cared for if it's necessary

swedish hospital ballard clinic discriminates against elderly and disabled. they refuse to put the person in a wheelchair on the exam table and will even write it down that it's against their policy. when the elderly person needs a bladder bag changed, they refuse to do it and state they don't have a bladder bag in the clinic. it seems they don't care if anyone is complained against, this continually happens but where else are wheelchair people supposed to get care from, i thought this is what doctors and nurses are paid to do? the same thing has happened at university of washington ballard clinic and university of washington medical center er.

there was an er doctor there who chastised my daughter who came in the er with kidney stones. instead of giving her pain medication , he began calling her a brat and told her to apologize to a nurse  who was her "life line". he treated my daughter like garbage. he defensiveness was even 
more bizarre because nothing was a problem except for the fact that they were withholding her pain meds during this. i am going to be requesting the medical records and will make sure he is called out for this. shameful, unprofessional and not his lane.

had a definite, verified, horrible heart attack. was treated like scum and called a "homeboy" (f*ggot to a gay man). 

healthcare is abuse. i left untreated, in medical trouble and in fear.

a very disturbing aspect is isolation with no call light/assist when needed, cell signal, tv, and all other employees completely ignore kindly nurse requests.

if on any of my jobs i ignored a customer, i'd be rightly fired, in healthcare it's encouraged to do to wounded patients.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: so far so good. went to the er during my first trimester. was worried i'd be there all day but considering the severity and treatment i was out in about 3 hours which was far less than i planned. the obgyn department is also very efficient. they always have a full house but tries to honor everyone's time. i've gotten blood work and visited the pharmacy at this location its all been pretty decent. i would say to anyone skeptical abt coming over here 1.) know where you are going as far as the building and floors 2.) try to arrive early to allow for parking and walking 3.) grab a face mask to decrease your anxiety 4.) check in on your kp app and keep a your phone charged in case its a busy day. 5.) always treat ppl on the job with respect. it comes with perks.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
making an appt now typically requires a wait of 35 minute on hold. rep on phone was a jerk with an attitude when i asked him several questions. 
care is substandard with you now seeing pa's and not dr's. went for months and the pa wasn't proactive and my shoulder worsened. she didn't even request an mri after i told her about my preexistíng issues. the dr's are too conservative, unproactive and allow your concerns to linger on. never going back to this outfit next enrollment. my health needs have never been met with this organization. they don't listen to their members and disregard their requests.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
it was my first time here at kp south bay! the encounter with so many dr. , nurses, and staff members. dr. zane was my surgeon he very polite, informative on how process was going to take place.  he's chief over the bariatric department. i was able to pick my own surgeon and dr.zane was surgeon. dr. tim was the one who was putting the tube with cameras down my throat. 
,  dr. han was the one who gave the injection to put me under while the surgery in process. this kp in south bay is hugh medical building. the nurse who took care of me in the recovery room was rhonda, alice and many several nurses. they were accommodating to my needs. i very blessed to have such a awesome team. then i was taken to the floor was i was going stay. the staff members were excellent. mabel , bryon, to many to name. they were on it and taking care of the patients. i was truly blessed to be apart of awesome team. thank you kp south bay for great service and hospitality.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
mom mom had pain on her chest that radiates thru her back and left side, short of breath, the guy took her vitals, my mom went to the little room for ekg and guy inside said wait for 5 mins for the md. til now we're still waiting, it's almost an hour. mom's pain from 5/10 when we got here, now it's 9/10. are they gonna wait til their patient collapse? my mom has afib and hx of heart attack.
if only urgent care is open, atleast there, they attend to her right away because of breathing and circulation issues. this er sucks
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: i dont do reviews normally but holy hell this place is a hot mess. be prepared to wait until you drop. this place is just wowww.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review:
my dad is a chemo patient and he had fever over 100.6. we went to kaiser harbor city urgent care first couple days ago and the staff are super friendly, the dorctor prescribed antibiotics but unfortunately the fever did not go down after 48 hours. we decided to go to the er this time because it passed the urgent care hours. it turned out a nightmare! the staff from receptionist to er nurses didn't smile at once. the x-ray tech is friendly though. in harbor city urgent care, the receptionist gave us a heads-up the possible wait time. in here, they replied they don't know and kept my dad waiting. my dad expressed several times in the waiting room that he felt chills and fatigue and wanted to go home, all he wanted is something that can reduce his fever and safe to take during chemo. but the doctor kept him waiting and waiting. the blood test was taken and so did flu test. we went in around 1030pm and got out at 5am, almost 7 hours wait and in between the doctor shifted. the first doctor didn't carry over all the notes and my dad had to repeat everything again to the second doctor. the flu test was still not ready by 5am in the morning so we decided to leave. by 6am in the morning, i finally got a phone call from dr. nguien confirmed the flu test came back positive, which i appreciated him calling very much. few hours later, my dad's oncologist doctor called and told me he could not find any doctor notes on the system so we had to repeat everything again...

i am glad this nightmare is finally over. i understand er prioritize the worst case first, which is fine i understand. however, i was just at harbor city urgent care coupledays ago: the pharmacist sincerely apologize for the wait if you've been waiting for more than 30 minutes, but here in the er, instead of explaining, they asked my dad to sign an agreement form before he leaves the hospital without any explanation. really? 

if the staff in harbor city urgent care smiles and gives you heads up, then why can't here?! if the staff went through the same basic training, then a little care to your patient won't hurt. i assume you will not treat your parents like that but why do you think it is ok to treat other people's parents like that? 

we would never come back to this er.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: kaiser emergency department sucks ! worst than the county was here for 5hrs waiting to be called just to be placed in a bed and waited another 1hr for md. the check in desk ppl are no help  either . horrible
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: i have heard about kaiser nightmares as far as wait times. we were visiting relatives during the christmas holidays and my wife was experiencing chest pain and heart palpitations. we waited almost 5 hours in emergency to see a dr. absolute joke to run an emergency room / dept this way. i will never come to this hospital again! i'll make the 2-3hour drive to see a dr and will still come out better time wise.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente South Bay Medical Center

review: i hardly give feedback but i must commend this hospital for employing not just intelligent medical doctors but m.d that has good relationship with her patients.  i dont know her name unfortunately but my visit was feb  10th at the dental pediatric emergency. she did an excellent job. she saw my baby had a swollen figure she was concerned as if it was her own child that really touched me. we were not familiar with the hospital as it was our first visit, she took us right to were we are to be registered to see doctor for my baby finger at the emergency. this warm reception made me love jamaica hospital. this doctor deserve an award, she was soo friendly. god bless her soul. please keep employing people like her. i can tell she love her job. the lady at the reception also  did a good job. when i told her my daughter gum bleeds  when she starts crying she ensured we were attended to very quickly. god bless her. i love jamaica hospital.
i recently spent 5 days there ,and 12 last year. the quality of care was excellent from the hospitalists, nurses cna,s and the techs. the er was excellent also. would highly recommend.  thank you

i love plano medical center, mainly because my life was transformed in that hospital. my name is isaac castro, and i'm considered the miracle child there. i survived a severe traumatic brain injury, 6-7 week coma, and lost 273+ pounds all muscle. but i woke up from my coma there and taught myself close to everything at plano, baylor medical centers, and at pate rehabilitation. i was close to death, but jehovah woke me up for proper reasons on earth. amén

we walked into the er and within 3 minutes we were being triaged and taken to a room. heather came in immediately and did a history. she was very caring and kind. next the dr came in and told us he would try and make my daughter comfortable,and boy did he. less than 30 minutes after we got here she was feeling so much better. 
 if you ever consider going to a stand alone care center,don't. they cannot provide you the level of care an emergency room can. 
i am not always a fan of er's, however medical city ofplano did and outstanding job of making our daughter feel better.

i was involved in a car accident about 24 hours prior to my visit and i just wanted to get checked. i've never been to an er where they make you feel bad for being there. pa bethany wood in the er treated me like absolute sh*%. she did not care to hear about my pain, told me to go home and take some ibuprofen and then left. when i asked the nurse to see her again, she came back and was even more rude than the first time. i told her about my pain and she told me i didn't tell her that, when i did. she downplayed my whole situation and pain. i told her she was being rude and she argued with me and i asked for someone else. in a even more rude way she said "i'm all you got". i told her i'll just go somewhere else and she said ok and walked away. never been to a hospital where the staff shows no type of empathy. avoid pa bethany  wood!

after seven years and three visits to this er, i have now been diagnosed with diabetes.

 my latest visit i came in with 400 sum blood glucose after being denied treatment at a local urgent care and sent to the er. 

the er took blood after searching for a vein three times.  i waited tethered to an iv and sensors needing to urinate for about an before the closed the door so i could collect the urine. 
 waited about 45 minutes before 10 units of insulin were administered. wait another 45 minutes they check my blood glucose which is at 363. wait a few more minutes a rude doctor rambles off that i neeed to see my primary care physician and have a prescription filled all in what seemed like less than a minute. 
keep in mind i'm disoriented, dizzy with blurred vision. i mention the vision to the dictor. he says that's normal because of the corners and the blood sugar. this is sunday night the er isn't very busy, one pharmacy 10 miles away is open and  it didn't have the medication i needed. so the doctor discharged me with 363 blood glucose, disoriented  and blurred vision to drive myself home.
my first visit to this er in 2013 with an entire body rash was treated with a steroid shot followed by a $2500 bill. this is with insurance.
my second visit to this er was with the all over body rash in 2016. steroid shout and $2500 bill. 

the rash is candida albicans an infection caused by diabetes and lowered immune funxtion. medical center plano failed to diagnose this rash all three times i was treated.

in 2017 i lost a toe joint to gout caused by the diabetes medical city plano failed to diagnose not once but twice.

i've followed up with my primary care after each if these er visits.

i'm searching for a the best medical malpractice lawyer i can find at the moment

this hospital is amazing. hands down i would absolutely trust this hospital with my children's lives. i actually have, my 1 year old got so very sick once and they went above and beyond to assure she was alright. they were going to release us but then she developed a fever and we ended up staying for a few nights and they made sure she was hydrated and tested every possible issue there could be. the wait time is barely there, like 20 minutes max. would definitely recommend.

i came today to this hospital expecting for a great service and what i've received is al the contrary they came saw my daughter and its been over three hours and the doctor is nowhere to be find its a children hospital top 10 and i do not see how come they r top ten when there is no attention to the patient and the wait is extremely long when there r only 3 other children

after calling the oncall doctor from my pediatrician, who works at the childrens hospital,  she advised i go to the emergency room after hearing my babys abnormal fast paced breathing from over the phone. upon arrival we were checked in and seen within 15 minutes. the nurses took quick action to get the right care for my child and very friendly. facility is spacious and clean. thank you to all who helped and to those who continue to dedicate their time to these precious gems.

i want to thank the entire staff of nurses, medical assistants, doctors, security, and lovely volunteers at calvary for their compassionate work and professionalism during the most difficult time, the last days of one's life.

patients are treated with respect, given the utmost in comfort and medical care. family and friends visiting are treated with tender genuine compassion as well.  

the facility is kept clean and well run, tightly organized 24 hours of each day and night.  all questions and needs were addressed immediately and respectfully. 

every staff  member we met the past two weeks, was truly wonderful, thoughtful and sensitive to our needs during the last days of my mother-in-law's life.  her wishes were honored and met with utmost compassion. 

we know of calvary through those we know who have familiarity with the facility as their choice for hospice and palliative care.   we recommend calvary highly.

my name is sheila r.

i cannot express how grateful we are to calvery for the exceptional end of life care my mother received there. she was a long-time supporter of calvery through the years because of friends and family members relating stories of caring and compassionate staff. the medical and nursing teams were top notch, the facility was comfortable and not institutional, and visitors were treated with great compassion and kindness. my mother never had a day of discomfort or anxiety for her 2 weeks at calvery. we will continue out financial support for this important community resource.

kootenai healths discriminatory treatment practices strike dark totalitarian undertones that places big pharma, and their bottom line above patient care.

my wife and i had our second child delivered at kootenai health. during our newborns first physical inspection the doctor discovered our child was born with ankyloglossia (tongue-tied), and at that time it was recommended that it be clipped as is routine. this is a common procedure at kootenai, and the for mayo clinic which it is a part of. 

however because we opted not to have every shot and vaccination administered kootenai refused to perform the procedure. the labor units head physician told us directly that had we accepted all the shots they have performed the procedure, and that he had done so on numerous occasions. although we asked for studies indicating our newborn was more at risk than any other child the physician told us there were none, and that no such information existed. 

despite the fact  that we were troubled by what this meant for our newborn my wife and i remained civil, and kept cool heads. as our meeting came to an end i made the attempt to shake hands with our proudly out of state physician as we parted ways he refused. in idaho that speaks volumes.

i fear that kootenai's good name no longer means what it used to; beyond that i can't help but feel terrible for many of the incredible nurses, and doctors who work there but are obviously unable to speak out in against kootenais one size fits all approach to health. it is only because of those hard working individuals that kootenai health earned two stars rather than one.

kootenai medical sucks. had a sleep study for take home cost me almost $600. the payment people told me i had months to pay off.  been getting calls from a 1 888 974 1235 , no message left. turns out to be them. i paid 250 and 117 off from that balance  in november now they have called me 2 times about my remaining balance  of 223.  wtf kootenai!!!!! there are people who owe thousands and u gonna call me about 223.00. will not go there for any reason. yes rumors are correct.  they suck!!!!!! paid balance off today so i don't get harassed by them again. please people go somewhere else!!!!!!!!!

i had a planned day surgery in late november. i have insurance. i was hounded by billing to prepay what my insurance didnt pay. i ultimately caved and paid $500. i paid december, january and now its february 20, 2020 and i get no less than 1 call every week. some as early at 7 am all for payment. i've never missed a payment. i have yet to receive my february  bill. i was told it went out yesterday but they called me?. i asked for the bill to be emailed so i could make my payment and was told they would do that. nothing! i was told it is "customary" for calls to be made until paid in full. give me a break.  it's not an issue with staff but billing. i'm  not a deadbeat quit treating me like one.

the sole reason i've given three stars is because the majority of the staff are phenomenal and caring. i have the most experience with the few rns they employ since i require central line care and all blood work ordered by my primary doctor has to be done there and i've never had a problem with failure to use aseptic technique, which not all nurses ensure they follow when doing central line care even though not doing so is incredibly dangerous. however, the best care couldn't make me blind to the fact that the hospital desperately needs to be updated cosmetically and otherwise. supplies in exam rooms are stored in sterilite containers found at walmart, the en-suite bathrooms in each exam room are so small that you couldn't fit the iv pole in with you if you were getting something intravenously, and everything from the vital sign monitors to the thermometers are woefully outdated. i can't understand how this is the case when they've managed to acquire a facilities in both cushing and jenks.

i would never go anywhere else!! i had to bring my daughter to get her ankle checked since she fell down the stairs, i wanted to make sure she didn't tear anything. from the time i walked in the front office was helpful and welcoming and super nice, to the nurse how was so sweet and really nice to us showed my daughter how to use crutches. then the p.a. came in the room to look at her ankle, he was nice, knowledgeable, and answered all my questions.i even seen him the next day and he asked how my daughter was.she had to get some x rays and the tech was nice and explained everything she was going to do. thank you all  for helping my daughter and making her feel at ease.  even though she really don't like to talk much..i would only come here!!

i have never been so frustrated in my life! i came in thursday evening in so much pain. my nurse was extremely rude and had a nasty attitude. she was very condescending to me. i was there for two hours and they refused to give me anything for pain (they stated they needed to get blood work first). that's a bunch of bs. i was only allowed tylenol after two hours of begging and mind you i'm crying out in pain at this time.
the bmnext excuse i got from her was my bp was low (mind you, she had an xl cuff on my arm and last reading had been 50 mins prior) i ended when rechecking it correctly myself and what do you know, actually a little high (hmm probably due to the amount of pain i was in)
when i requested to see a doctor vs the pa, she got an attitude and started sending a different nurse in, yet no one let me know i would be having different nurse... finally after a couple hours of going through this, i told them i would like to just leave. miraculously, at that point they finally send someone in to do an ultrasound so i agreed to do it because i just wanted to find out what was wrong. the ultrasound tech was the only nice person of my entire visit. that was done and of course they still refuse to give me anything for pain and i just continue to sit there. 
finally i was done sitting there and excruciating pain  oh, i could have done that at my house so i called them back in there  take my iv out  and instead of the nurse coming in to do that, she sends some kind of tech or scribe in there  to bring me ama paperwork and take my iv out.  first off, the rn treating me should have been in there doing that discharge paperwork  oh, it's part of her scope of practice (which obviously she doesn't seem to know much about her role i guess) and second, this tech that comes in here tells me when i ask if i needed to sign that "you have to sign this if you want us to take your iv out".. he just screwed up by saying that. totally not even legal to hold someone where like that. they were trying to put me in a position to either leave with it so they could call the police or feel stuck to stay there. i'm not an idiot. i'm a nurse myself and i know my rights as a patient. i also know how someone should be treated in that setting and i can tell you every bit of treatment i received there it's the complete opposite of what healthcare professionals stand for.

i ended up going to methodist freestanding er about eight hours later and received phenomenal treatment. have they just given that to me they may have caught the fact that it was my gallbladder and i ended of being transferred from methodist to main methodist for surgery. instead they wanted to sit in question me and make me feel like what i was feeling wasn't real and more worried about ways to not give me anything for pain vs just trying to make me comfortable and being good, ethical staff.
complaint filed. i dare them to send me a bill, i will have a lawyer ready.
stay away unless you want rude staff, slow and inefficient care

i am actually really surprised that the reviews aren't higher. i was just at the er, which even though is under construction, i was very happy with my care. they treated me as a human and listened to me. the ultrasound technician was incredibly kind and thorough. i would recommend going here over parker adventist any day. the only reason i am giving them four stars and not five is due to the construction and overall appearance. i was very pleased with the care i received though.

whatever you do, if you have been a victim of assault, do not go to this er. i had been to this er the previous year for other reasons, and the care was decent. this time, i returned two weeks after being assaulted in a doctor's office, with the headaches, blurry vision, and jaw pain not subsiding since i was hurt. my provider told me to go to the er to get checked out. i got stuck with dr. mary sprinkel, a woman who knows little but professes to know a lot. with such hubris dictating ability, it is no wonder that as a victim of physical assault that caused me injury and pain, she willfully ignored the incident i had reported (there's a police report, too). she concluded, it must my tmj acting up, and even had the audacity to print out tmj exercises (that i've already been doing for well over a decade!). i'm not sure where dr. sprinkel attended medical school, but they should be embarrassed by this ignorant and arrogant graduate who did me (and every other assault victim) such a grave disservice. now, after "being seen" by dr. sprinkel, i can conclude that she aggravated me to the point that i am now back to clenching my jaw, which hasn't been an issue in 6 months, but thanks to dr. sprinkel's inability to listen to the 51 year old patient who's been dealing with disabilities since birth, the problem that wasn't a problem that the dr. insisted was the problem is now part of the problem.

i'm still receiving bills from a visit in early 2019...a whole year later. please pick a different healthcare provider if you're considering sutter.

this review is due after i've been shafted by sutter health a second time. 

i have a health plan that covers preventative care at 100%. last year i went in for my first annual physical with sutter (i had a kaiser plan prior to this). during this appointment, i mentioned that i had chronic back pain and we talked a bit about it for a few minutes. after our conversation, the doc mentioned that i might be billed for this part of the conversation since it's not part of a physical. no treatment was given for my back pain. 

sure enough, i received a bill for hundreds of dollars for that part of the conversation. i was irritated by this, but a doctor's time is valuable, and i was the one that brought up the topic. i pay this bill. 

one year later, i go back in for another physical. this time i'm careful not to mention anything outside of answering her questions about my health. she mentions that i had lost some weight since last year and i tell her that i've changed my diet. 

months later, boom. i get hit with a $400 dollar bill for this check-up. some phone calls with my insurance company and the billing department later, i'm told it's because the doctor coded the appointment with a code for "abnormal weight loss".  the same lab tests that would have been covered under a check-up were then not covered by my insurance because another topic was discussed during the visit.

so that's how it works here. the doc slaps a code for whatever she decides to say to you and you pay the price. i can't be the only one they're shafting, right? so i google something like "sutter health coding error", to find sutter was just fined 30 million dollars 8 months ago for exactly what they're doing to me, and they're still doing it!

the issue has not been resolved as of this review.

man do they suckkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkkk! no explanation of services administered. started talking to my dr. because he asked me probing questions. ended up upping the "level" of the appointment to a "level 4" (why? who knows) costing me $500 instead of $90... so pathetic...

never go to sutter health or dr. lovett. during an annual exam, dr. lovett instructed me to come back for a follow-up vitamin d lab test. i asked if that was part of my annual exam, because i am lower income (on food stamps, housing insecure, etc.) and can't afford any out-of-pocket doctor's visits, despite being a full time grad student and working four jobs. he insisted that it was part of my annual exam. this was also my mistake for trusting this doctor instead of double-checking with my insurance company beforehand, but now due to his fraudulent counsel, sutter health is claiming that i owe them $150. after months of contesting this bill through my insurance company and through sutter health (dozens of messages, letter of appeal and phone calls) they are still charging me for this bill even though their physician, dr. lovett misinformed a patient. again, i'm lower income and i'm sure this doctor makes quite a bit more money than i do, and should be more up to par about billing etiquette, especially if it can come at the expense of his patients who are struggling just to pay for groceries.

from the moment the ambulance brought me here, to the exam, x-rays, being admitted, surgery, different floors based on my condition and operation prep, not a single person let us down. the nurses, doctors, pa's, surgeon, all introduced themselves, all explained what was going on, kept us informed, and demonstrated true empathy and concern. it was if i walked into a place with long lost family. this hospital managed to hire people in every field we came in contact with that had a great sense of humor and willingness to help.  if i was wealthy i would want to give them all gifts. they truly made a horrible situation of my breaking both ankles, the best it could be. way to go baylor!

giving them even one star is being generous and perhaps only because the nursing staff and the one doctor i have spoken to are kind and doing their best despite a severely broken system. this hospital's issues run deep and i could go on forever, but there is a big disconnect between the telemetry floor (which is a misnomer) and the radiology department. my dad arrived via ambulance to the er department on wednesday at 7 pm. he was admitted thursday morning to the hospital. we literally got our very first report from the radiologist on sunday at 11 am, despite my father having multiple x-rays since being admitted on thursday morning. he should have had a confirmed diagnosis within one or two days....not five days later. it was one series of errors after another. we waited from friday afternoon to saturday evening for a radiology report that we would truly never receive as the final x-ray was never performed...and no one even knew it! it took me calling the house supervisor, speaking to a doctor and demanding he call radiology. they have no intenal process in place to know when something hasn't been competed as ordered?! heaven forbid you need a radiologist over the weekend, as they are only staffed from 9 am to 3 pm. i thought hospitals should funtion 24/7? global is too cheap and/ or dysfunctional to pay onrad  (their contracted afterhours radiology department) to read a report, despite all the previous blunders and the doctor specifically requesting it asap. as a result, my father has been in the hospital since wednesday night.... paying per night for their incompetence and getting increasingly exposed to numerous other potential issues. 

i will update and revise this review when the hospital administration has reached out to me and satisfactorily resolved these issues. it's a miracle that they are still accredited by the joint commission and are capable of honestly receiving medicare payments.

my father was brought in by ambulance on friday 11-29. i ran into the er upset and frantic. clearly how someone whose parent just had a massive heart attack would behave. i was asked by the security guard my father's name. i told him and he said no one was there by that name. i was confused how that could have been the case. i couldn't possibly have left the scene after the paramedics and made it to the hospital before them. the security guard said maybe but did he give them his name. i said no we didn't because he was unconscious. the guy said maybe he is in the system as a john doe. so i naturally asked well can you tell me if an 80 year old john doe arrived here with cardiac arrest in the last few minutes. the nurse at the desk behind him said "jesus" and scoffed and rolled her eyes at me. clearly not the response someone trained in this field should have. i wasn't the least bit ok with her response and got agitated. the security guard said if i don't calm down i would have to leave. i said i will calm down but this clearly isn't ok and you can't treat people like this. all i want to know is if he is here. after about 30 minutes the guard came back and said he was here and someone would speak with us shortly. another 20 minutes or so went by and a woman came to gather information. after that another person came and said that he is bed 11 and we can see him in a bit. which is hopeful right. after about 10 minutes we were called back. the man ushered us into a room with 3 chairs facing the door. no clue what us going on but it didn't feel good but they said he was in a bed so maybe it's not bad. they said a doctor will be with us shortly. after about 20-30 minutes of watching nurses walk by joking and laughing a doctor walked by. my husband got up and the doctor said how's it going to him. he said well fine i guess just wondering what's going on. the doctor said yeah i'll be with you in a minute and walked away.  finally he came in and sat down said said well he didn't make it. we shocked him with the paddles and he didn't respond. he literally just kept repeating that and offered no further insight or explanation. then he and his nurse said we will get him cleaned up so you can see him. we waited and waited and waited. finally we were called back. my dad still had the iv lines and some sort of mouth piece in. clearly he wasn't cleaned up. there was another nurse in the room going over the details with someone on the phone. i asked if they could talk about it elsewhere since it was highly distracting and desensitizing. they said well we tried to get you back quickly. i don't call nearly 30 minutes or more quickly. i asked twice why can't they make the phone call from the nurses station plus this whole time they were supposed to be hospital sells and/or gives your number to other places or affiliates. this way they can try to profit even more off of your loss. if there was such a thing as negative stars this place would get it. absolutely horrible from beginning to end. you should be completely ashamed of the operation you guys are running. despicable!!!

review:
i have a trained service dog for mobility and medical alert. while my disabilities can be invisible, it's usually not as you can see i have a major walking issue. i worked with a local service dog training organization that meets assistance dogs international standards to get him. he is legit, no amazon certificate or anything. he took 2 years of training and cost tens of thousands to train.

his mobility vest is made of leather. it doesn't fit currently (we think it shrank due to rain and not having proper care taken of it) and we're waiting on his new one to come in (takes up to 8 weeks because it had to be custom made as it's a mobility/guide vest). still, he was leashed to his collar and had a couple leash wraps that showed he was a working service dog. we even put on his working booties (they're heavier duty than what you can get at petco and meant for working dogs). we have the laws printed out and highlighted and i/my boyfriend both know how to answer the required questions.

yesterday, i had three important doctors appointments. i've waited several weeks for them (about a month) and they were supposed to be a new step in figuring out my chronic disability. they were also about a 40 minute drive to get to them. between the first appointment and the second, i thought it would be a good idea to get a printout of my medical records, as my new school was requesting them.

this meant going from the clinic side to the hospital side, where they had the hospital administration who dealt with these requests. while waiting to see someone, i noticed a bit of commotion going on but decided to focus on filling out the paperwork. i had noticed someone called the cops or security, but i was entirely oblivious to why. when i was called back i was told they would get my paperwork filed but i would need to leave as the cops has been called, so if i protested they would escort me out by force. this entire time, my dog hadn't even lifted his head from his nap, tucked beside my feet and out of the way. the administrator talking to me told me it was bs because she knew me and my dog and has seen him vested before, but they'd had five complaints about him (particularly his size) and so i'd need to go. the administrator confirmed it was due to his size/not being vested and that his behavior had been perfect.

i pulled up texas state law on my phone as well as the ada. they said it didn't matter as it was hospital policy. i left, unable to go to the rest of my appointments (missed ), obviously. they told me i wouldn't be welcome back to any of their hospitals or clinics until he was wearing his new vest (takes about 2 months to get). 

i called the head of hospital administration, michelle, to get a copy of the policy. she confirmed it and said by it saying she didn't care what i thought the law said. she refused to hear me out and kept talking over me any time i tried to say it was against the law. she also started talking about how my dog was unleashed and causing issues (wtf?!), which is completely untrue and i have several witnesses that can attest to that. even the doctor i saw earlier today told me she was afraid of dogs, especially big ones, but she was beyond impressed with how well behaved mine was. he was completely leashed and i can show you a picture of everything he was wearing yesterday.

to make this story even worse, this is the second time they've done something like this to me. the first was in the exact same department about 9 months ago. the greeter stood up as soon i walked in and screamed "get that thing the fuck out of here!" i spoke with hospital administration after that incident and they told me they had dealt with it and will provide better training for their employees and volunteers on service dogs.

ada faq on service animals (pay special attention to q1, q2, q5, q7, q8, and q14-17): https://www.ada.gov/regs2010/service_animal_qa.html
ada on service animals: https://www.ada.gov/service_animals_2010.htm
texas disability law on service dogs: https://gov.texas.gov/organization/disabilities/assistance_animals

review: north coast used to be sagamore hills children's psychiatric hospital in the 80s. it was horrible and you didn't get to leave the locked ward. in fact, you couldn't even leave the building. you were always locked down and don't get me started on mandatory drugs! no one was trusted with pills, it was all liquid. other patients were allowed to instigate trouble and very little was done to stop it and you wonder why some of us used to stay in our rooms and lash out at staff who would try to roast us out of our rooms and on ward. this would be a nasty physical confrontation usually initiated by staff. as soon as they put their hands on you and you happen to be combative, it was a bad day for them, and i mean terrible if you happen to be a born fighter because you knew how to draw blood even with nothing but your teeth. you got dragged to the qr, which is really the quiet room, and empty concrete room that was also also locked. school was mandatory but some of us played sick. we were able to successfully stay back from school as long as we had a fever. i learned how certain peers were able to constantly stay back from school. all you had to do was stand on your bed when no one was around and hold the thermometer up to the hot ceiling where the heat came from, but don't hold it too long or they might get suspicious. the ceiling could be used to our advantage anytime we wanted to stay home and fake sick, the ceiling was also a heater vent. one time i almost got caught but thankfully i never did. i hated school anyway and i hated the disrespect i got and uncaring nature of the teachers. it was hard for kids who did nothing wrong to be locked up so bad. the only times we had access to the hallways was when we were walking in line escorted by staff to and from necessary locations elsewhere in the building. if you try to fake something needing a regular hospital, it may not work because  any ambulance ride and regular hospital could easily be used for and easy escape plan. you take the ambulance ride to the hospital and when no one's looking, just run from the hospital and wherever you want! that would've been fun but i never got that chance. then you had no comfort items, which made an already bad problem far worse. when you're coming out of a severely abusive home, having no love or nurturing even in the new places and especially no comfort items is enough to make you go mad. they punish you when you lash out over unfair conditions and then leave you locked in the qr until you calm down. at some point you break and eventually start calming down, you can't stay in there forever. i don't blame people for lashing out because such living conditions, especially for abuse survivors who did nothing wrong really don't deserve it. when you're forced to live as though you were a criminal, sagamore hills now known as north coast was really a children's prison. when you have to live like a criminal, that makes an already bad situation far worse for an innocent person who did nothing to deserve to be locked up

the primary reason i'm giving this er only one star has to do with the er doctor  who i saw and their billing practices.  she was despondent throughout my visit and the entire brief time she spent with me. it was like a cold wet towel on a rainy day. after learning who she was i was not too shocked to learn she wrote two books about reconsidering being in the medical field. she lives in a 700,000 home. 

her billing practices are to turn over patients within 60 days of treatment. not from the time the patient actually receives the bill and knows of the debt. i was turned over to collection for $53.20 and had only been given two weeks to pay this invoice before i received a notice stating that i would be turned over for collection for non-payment.

the medical industry will never get better in this country. the truth behind all of the issues we face when seeking medical care is greed. we have fostered a belief that monetary success is what all should seek at the expense of others and now our medical practitioners do not enter into their careers due to a love of science and caring for others but simply so that they may live in million dollar homes, take luxurious vacations, and show off all that monetary success at the expense of their patients. 

the hospital claims it has no control over the billing practices of their doctors.

review:
sorry for the length  it's copied from the letter send to our congressman. 

   what can i say, this place raises my blood pressure like no other.  a few years ago i had issues with my father and the va which is a story in itself but i ended up talking to cong. ralph abraham. 3 years later i'm right back at the same spot. the community choice program was enacted approx  4-5 years ago to allow vets to see outside pcps & specialist when they live over 60 miles away. va not only wouldn't recommend this service but dissuaded vets by telling them their request wouldn't be approved. we bypassed that with help from cong.  abraham and for a couple years had no issues seeing outside drs. it was a nightmare to get the referrals and approvals but was doable if vigilant.  if a vet doesn't like his team dr( there are approximately 8 teams at this location) they can request a change. we request a team change in august of 2016, it took 13 months before he was changed. his only options were to continue to see the dr that he was unhappy with.   he would have to go to urgent care to be seen during this time had he not been on the cc program. they way it worked, you contacted triwest(whose in charge of referrals and approvals). if you don't get these prior approvals in hand it's likely they won't pay. they worked fairly quickly by va standards.  older vet wouldn't be able to get this done. after seeing outside drs we had multiple issues with the va team. despite telling the team dr and every nurse we encountered, do not change their medications or treatment without seeing the vet or consulting the cc pcp.  dr. kept changing medications and treatment without seeing the vets or consulting with cc pcp. the cc pcp had to call and change everything back.  this program also takes almost a year to pay so many drs don't want to mess with them. but after lots of work we got it done and it worked reasonably well for 2 years. 
   typical day at the va. we could no longer contact triwest to get referrals and their cc primary care dr could no longer request referrals to specialist or drs. we were told by triwest and va staff that from that point on to see an outside dr. the vet must drive to the alex va to see team dr to get a referral to see his pcp. no other way to see an  cc pcp.  have to wait wks/mths to see the team dr, must see va dr or specialist to get the referrals to an outside specialist. to be clear,  we drive over 65 miles, see 1 dr wait for appt with va specialist to refer to cc dr.   one vet had a diabetic ulceration on his foot that had reopened after a 16 months of extensive treatment, contacted his team dr, yellow team, dr santiago. to next available appt was 4 mnths.  advised to go to urgent care. cc is essentially useless now. at the last primary va appt, put in for the referrals to continue his care with his pcp and cardiologist but don't expect it to be approved. the rn said she  had never had a single request approved to see an outside dr, never.  we did get approval to continue to see their outside cardiologist, but no news on outside primary care.
 need diabetic shoes. 6 appts in 8 months. 1st apt, get boot for the foot with ulcer.  2nd , pick up and have boot fitted.  i expressed concern for the other foot that's bearing all the weight to ensure it doesn't develop an ulceration.. 3rd apt,, measured for shoes, did molds for inserts. 4th apt, shoes but no inserts.repeated molds & reordered.  5th visit,  inserts in new shoes, way too tight. the inserts weren't taken into consideration when measured. 6th visit...that was today. 
this is a typical day at the va.  had an appt for the cc cardiologist. he had ran out of 1 medication. previous day i contacted the  pharmacy to order the refill. told the script was expired. called the ccpcp to get a refill  since we would be close by. arrived at pharmacy next day, told that it hasn't been sent in. went outside to call dr since no reception inside va. dr said they did send it but would resend it and call them.  told that they did have it but refused to fill it because the referral to his cc program had not been completed, no emergency supply either. told to go to uc, crammed full.  contacted cc  pcp to call in script.  then to prosthetics dept as they were calling us to set up an appt. knocked on both doors in prosthetic dept no answer. i saw the prosthetics dr in  hallway & explained we were in town and had a call saying they were in.  he advised that he could see him. provider opened the shoes to unlace them at which point i told him they were supposed to be velcro he cannot tie his shoes the provider continue to loosen the laces and try to put the shoe on his foot. at this point i told him, as did the veteran that these shoes would not work.  the provider stated that he ordered shoes with velcro but that's what they sent, so here we are.....

i mean seriously who likes going to the doctors!  but when we have to go ... it's nice to know that those who are in charge of our well-being and care go the extra mile to make sure we are taken care of, comfortable, and well informed.  kudos to cy-fair surgery center.   i came here for some medical procedures and from the moment i walked in and dealt with laura (who was a consummate professional, not to mention helped ease the anxiety with her awesome demeanor and comedy), instantly made me feel like this was going to be an awesome visit.  if there was ever a frontline hero to represent your organization, she was the perfect example.  next i dealt with keny, who continued the excellence and professionalism that laura exuded and while taken my vitals, etc. made me feel like she genuinely cared about my well being.  and although i was feeling happy and comfortable up to this point, the second laura and natalie just further upgraded my comfort level and mindset that i had chosen the right place for my procedure.  thank you all for an awesome experience ... and although i may not have gotten the names of the other ladies who helped, everyone involved in my care was amazing!

i was treated at this facility on december 8th for what i thought was a heart attack, so naturally, i was terrified. when we arrived here, we were greeted by a male nurse at the window who upon seeing my wife and i exclaimed verbatim "you came to the wrong damn place!"  

i told him i couldn't breath to which he made us aware "we're not set up for that here" (even though we were in the emergency room) and "you're going to be here for a while".

we were blown away by the callousness of the response and momentarily considered going to another emergency room, but because i was having trouble breathing we decided to stay. 

i was then seen by a bunch of other staff members, that ran various tests. all of them were courteous and professional. in particular, the gentleman who ran the ultra-sound machine to check for blood clots. i was never given a diagnosis of any kind, but i made the safe assumption i was having a panic attack ( i had never had one before, and apparently they can feel similar to heart attacks). 

when the doctor, allowed me to go, i was not prescribed any medication or given any instructions, and i wasn't told what had happened i was just told to get dressed. i took the tape off from spo2 monitor so i could get my shirt on more easily. the male nurse came back in and instead of getting some new tape, he once again looked at me like an idiot and he asked: "why did you do that?". everything he said and did was full of resentment at the fact that we were still there.

people have bad days, i get it. but when your job is to help people that are having the worst day of their life, a little compassion might be in order. you should never greet any person that is scared, or in pain with "you came to the wrong damn place". even if you personally can't help, it is incumbent on you as a decent human being to help get them help. this is especially true when your job is to "help" people.  

i went the next day to make the hospital aware of how my wife and i were treated by the nurse. the would not let me speak with him directly, nor would they grant my insistence that he apologize to my wife and i. i was told "something" would be done and i would hear back from the hospital directly; i never did. 

then the day after christmas, i get the bills. they hadn't run my insurance (even though they had it on file) so i received a $6,400 bill for all my tests and scans and $460 for imaging. so now i get to chase around the hospital and the insurance company to get it all rectified. 

again, most of the staff seemed compassionate and professional, but the first impression was impossible to overcome. add to that no followup and now having to chase around to settle the bill; i cannot recommend this hospital.

i've had three experiences with beaumont's er over the past twenty years. two were minor home accidents that required some suturing, and the third was a gall bladder attack that required emergency surgery. i've always been treated well there, and over the years i've observed a lot of improvements in both the physical infrastructure and the quality of care. on my last visit i showed up just before midnight on christmas day (!) when the er was very short staffed, and it did take me a while to get pain meds- points off for that. but once the necessary staff were available, i was quickly admitted and scheduled for surgery the following morning. that morning i was visited before surgery by both the surgeon and anesthesiologist, both of whom took time to explain what was going on, and to ask if i had any questions. following surgery, the nursing care i received was exemplary, and the follow-up care at the hospital was very good as well.

there is a total lack of communication between departments at beaumont. as patients get passed from one department to the next, they are given incorrect information about the time things will take.  when the "receiving" department is told the timing that the previous department indicated they blame the other department saying "they should have never said that." with the exception of the gi pa (tara karmo) who stuck to what she promised and got back with me in the 15 mins she said she would, all others failed.

my saga...

beaumont urgent care sent me to beaumont emergency due to a possible foreign object in my throat and to get my throat scoped.  i arrived around 3:00 pm in the afternoon.  at the time, there was not a line for checking, but there was a number of people waiting.  after waiting about an hour and a half, i was taken to triage where i was asked a few questions and was told by that person i would be taken to er shortly.  an hour later or so later, i was taken to er and was told they wanted to do a cat scan rather than a scope.  at that time, i was told the wait would be about an hour.  3+ hours later, i was taken for a cat scan. the cat can people said i would get the results within the hour.  4 hours later, around midnight, someone came to take me to my room  as they were admitting me ????

when i questioned this the response was "hasn't anyone talked to you?"  when the resident did talk to me, she indicated that nothing came up on the cat scan and they needed to scope my throat (which is why i was there in the first place) and all the ent people were gone by then.  i asked if i could just make an appointment for the next morning and come back for the scope and they said if i left, they wouldn't be able to get me in. so, i asked for them to confirm that if i stayed, someone would be able to do the scope first thing in the morning.  they assured me they would do it first thing in the morning.  i finally had the scope done around 1:30 pm.
around 3:30, the gi pa (tara karmo) told me that the ents did not see anything on the scope, but the scope wasn't able to see into the esophagus. the ent wanted to do a barium swallow but she didn't think the test would give the information.  to get the right information, an endoscopy would be better. but, it was too late to get that done and i would need stay another night.  i said there was no way i was going to stay another night for a "timing issue" and we needed to come up with another option.  she said she'd get back to me within 15 minutes, and she did. she had some meds prescribed for me and got me an appointment at her office a few days later.

i have just finished six weeks of outpatient rehabilitation for a bi-lateral knee replacement at the rehab services department at broward health in coral springs. 
  
everything - from the warm and compassionate greeting from joanie who answered my initial, very  nervous call - to the sessions thrice, then twice, then single weekly sessions paul mcgowen have been noteworthy for his skill, compassion, encouragement  and knowledge of various physical therapeutic exercises.

understanding that i have made years of accommodations for my fused knees prior to my surgery, paul incorporated hip and lower back exercises into my pt plan.  he gave me exercises for home and followed up each session with a progress report.  he told me what to watch for - how to correct myself.  in short - he cared.

bhcs rehab consists of an incredible group of people - and for this, the program director, ms. pomerantz should be recognized.  she has put together an incredible team.  it was not unusual for any of the other therapists - edwin, amanda, allison and monica - to stop by me (either on the table or on a machine) to cheer me on.    youlanda was always ready provide heat and ice and tell me how great i was doing.

i have been to other facilities for physical therapy.  i know what it is to be treated as a case number.  i know what it is to be viewed as an insurance claim and nothing more.  this is not the case at broward health coral springs.  my experience with paul and his colleagues has completely "etch-a-sketched" those very negative experiences from my memory. 
 
my life has changed dramatically for the best - and i owe much of it to paul mcgowan and the rehab group at bhcs.  i thank them all.

on friday february 28th at about 8:30pm my daughter and i took our 18 month old grandson to the emergency room on bee ridge and cattlemen.  

1.  my daughter was holding the baby who was crying - he had been bitten on the hand by a dog.
2.  the security guard never looked up from his computer and mumbled for us to sit down - "they know you're here."  we were the only people in the er, so i'm thinking "who knows we're here?"
3.  three women were behind a desk and did not make eye contact with us - no concern for a young woman holding a crying baby.  they just talked to each other - nobody told us anything.
4.  five minutes becomes 10 minutes and nobody said anything to us.
5.  after about 10-12 minutes a door marked triage opens and some patient comes out.  the triage nurse asked us to come in.
6.  she did not wash her hands, use purell, or wear gloves.
7.  she had to do all the typing to get us into the system (i guess the other three women were busy not helping)
8.  after about 15 questions - she finally asked why we were here.  we told her he had been bitten by a dog.
9.  when she reached for his hand - he of course screamed - so she reached for an unsanitized teddy bear on her desk and gave that to him to quiet him down.
10.  she dabbed the wound clean (did not rinse it) and moved us through some double doors into another waiting room with about six chairs - again we were the only people there.
11.  about another 10-15 minutes later a nurse came in and confirmed the baby's name.  then she asked us if he had a fever?  no?  a cough?  no?  we told her he had a dog bite.  (i wonder why she hadn't read the triage report??)
12.  she asked my daughter a dozen questions which had nothing to do with the dog bite, including vaginal or c-section delivery?  i'm guessing that is a priority when treating a dog bite.
13.  another 10 - 15 minutes and a doctor came into the room.  and here's where i started to question this whole operation.  he never came closer than 10 feet from the baby - never looked at the wound, let alone cleaned it.  from 10 feet away he then described what he was going to do - he was going to order an x-ray and then give us some antibiotics - because he told us without antibiotics the risk of infection is very high.
14.  another 10-15 minutes and a guy from x-ray came and told us he had been instructed to an x-ray of the right hand.  "is this _____?"  good guess!

did you ever see the movie zootpia where she has to go to the dmv to get her license?  that's what this experience brought to my mind.  they were like the sloths but without the smile and the compassion.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drhsktakrzc 

15.  another 30 minutes and the nurse came back asking us what was happening.  that is when i got a little frustrated and asked her why the doctor had not even looked at the wound?  why hadn't the wound been cleaned?  she seemed to think that the doctor had looked at the wound.
16.  i could go on and on...

finally the nurse came back with the prescription for the antibiotic - it was now 11 at night.  i asked her if she could call in the prescription so it would be ready when we got there.  "we don't provide that service."

this is a perfect example of an organization which is driven by procedure - and has absolutely no focus on patients.  no compassion, no coordination, no communication.  the system these people work in has crushed their humanity - and this is with an empty er.

all the while i'm thinking to myself - "omg imagine if there was a corona virus outbreak in sarasota and there were five or six puking sick people in the er waiting room?  this hospital is completely unprepared to handle anything like that."

come to find out two days later that there was a corona virus patient in the hospital that night - and i thought back to the people not washing their hands, etc. etc.  i pray that my grandson, my daughter and i were not infected.  

and hannah b. don't respond "i am so sorry to hear about your experience..."  if you gave a damn, you would go to the er yourself and see what your customers see - it isn't pretty.  if you did care, it would either be fixed, or you wouldn't be working there.
