review:
original review ~ dec 2019

my experience as a patient at kaiser permanente: in 2018, i scheduled a preventive care checkup with my primary care physician, collin reed, md when it was due. his office canceled my visit less than 24 hours in advance, leaving me unable to, instead, schedule a client in my business. i rescheduled my appointment with the doctor. and again: one of dr reed's assistants canceled less than 24 hours before the appointment. concerned about the delay i chose to meet with another physician in dr. reed's office. however, i was only allotted 5 minutes for an entire yearly check-up that year. come 2019, i again scheduled my annual checkup with dr. reed. as in 2018, his office canceled with less than 24 hours notice. two more times this year i scheduled with the collin reed, my primary care physician, and those appointments as well were canceled with insufficient notice to fill the allotted time with clients in my business. in total then, dr. reed cancelled five physical checkup appointments with less than 24 hours notice during 2018/19. i consequently incurred hundreds of dollars in lost income. if i ran my affairs as dr. reed handles his appointments, i would lose my business, and certainly my clients' confidence. the strong message of these events is that kaiser does not value patients' time. if the organization invested a quarter of

the money it spends on tv advertising on customer satisfaction, kaiser might run more productively.

update jan 27, 2020:

after registering a complaint with the member services team at kaiser for the series of canceled appointments with my primary care physician, (see below) i was assigned a representative. she told me that my experience with kaiser was 'abominable' and then asked me what kaiser could do to ameliorate the situation. i suggested to be reimbursed for my out-of-pocket expenses that resulted from the series of late cancellations. she got back to me a few weeks later with the happy news that i would be reimbursed for out-of-pocket expenses and that a check would be issued.

no check arrived for those expenses and the member services representative subsequently rescinded the promise to me in an encrypted e-mail.  one might imagine that maybe kaiser's law department reversed the decision, putting the member services representative in a bind. if that was the case, i would have appreciated an explanation of this fact. as it went, the retraction of the promise of reimbursement for out-of-pocket costs was cold and without explanation. after announcement of the reversal of reimbursement, i reached out to the representative through e-mail and voice mail and there was no response. i have no insight as to what caused this reversal.

my doctor, brian schulz, explained the procedure effectively, and had a great bedside manner.  he's friendly, caring, and puts the patient at ease.

all in all, the day went smooth and i left feeling like i had visited old friends.

i had my baby here back in july! and this hospital was beyond amazing. i had read the reviews prior and they had me on a 50/50 on weather this hospital was going to be good or not. but they exceeded my expectations. i can't remember my nurses names but i loved them, especially the one who was with me during delivery. i wanted an unmediated birth and towards the end i started second guessing my decision but my nurse kept telling that i could do it. and i did it. best decision i've ever made was going to texas children pavilion for women.

i kind of didn't want to leave a review because i didn't want to let the secret out. dr. raine is amazing. each time after i see her, my husband and i talk about how much better she is than my last ob from four years ago. 
dr. raine sits and talks with us, i never feel like she is rushing. she encourages me and if i ever have any worries she is quick to set my mind at ease however she can. 
she allowed me to try for a vbac (which i successfully had unmedicated) after my last ob gave me a csection after seeing me push twice, and told me i would never be able to have a child vaginally because it was too dangerous. 
i'm always looking forward to my appointments. my only issue is nurse bridget who is awful. i'll message or call which a concern and she always tells me it can wait till my next appointment. she's rude in person too. she's just one of those people. 
looking forward to having my next baby delivered by dr. raine in a month or two.

left in tears if that tells you anything. had an appointment to be seen by a fertility specialist for two months. took off work on a wednesday, navigated all over houston, paid for parking, etc., just to get told by the rude, apathetic reception desk that "they've been trying to contact me to tell me my appointment was cancelled since the provider is out." i then state i did not receive a message and she said my voicemail was full. i am sorry but this was an extremely urgent message to get out to me before i go through the hassle. i told her it is very hard to answer the phone during the day because i am a teacher and have students all day, everyday. we asked if they email or text notices and she said not for cancellations. i find that ironic because i sure did get an email for everything else they needed for me such as a confirmation of apt, billing, etc the morning of the apt. i couldn't even reschedule, i had to walk out because this is a very emotional time for us and it was handled very unfortunately and unapologetically.

i gave 4 instead of 5 only because my sister had a different experience while we spent some time here. we brought my mom in they emergency. everyone to me was extremely friendly and helpful. our nurses once my mom was admitted where also helpful, friendly, and comforting. there was only one assistant that came across that you could tell she just showed up because it's a job. but everyone else made me feel like they truly cared about there patients. and even cared about us the visitors.

i gave birth here on 10/20/2019. the doctors & nurses were amazing, i was induced so i was at the hospital for a while. this my most favorite nurses during that time was i think her name was manuela( not 100% sure ) , and another nurse i forgot her name but she was vietnamese and she was also the nurse helping me practice pushing ( probably my most favorite of them all ), and another nurse whose name i forgot but she was blonde they're  the reasons why i'm giving 2 starts and not 1..  after i gave birth everything for me went horrible. the postpartum nurses were rude and mean they just seemed like they did not give a fuck. i stayed at this hospital longer than i thought because my blood pressure would not regulate, but honestly in my opinion it was probably those damn nurses that were so mean, which made me not want to stay there anymore despite the status of my health, so i told the nurses i wanted to leave and was willing to sign the paper about leaving against medical advice. it took the whole ass day for the paper to arrive to me, but before that dr. short came and had a talk with me to convince me to stay but i obviously didn't. i knew for a fact that i would not get any better if i stay at this shitty ass hospital. don't get me wrong, not all the nurses were terrible but i was at my most vulnerable time and i could not stand any bullshit. i wish i had spoken up when i was there and ask for different nurses but my mind was only focused on going home. when i was finally able to leave the hospital, the nurse made me walk from my room to the car, keep in mind i had a shitload of stuff i'm my room because i stayed there for week, i also had many pillows because those hospital beds suck. there was 3 of us, my step dad carrying my baby in the car seat to the car and my aunt holding me bags and me holding the rest. i literally had just given birth two days prior the least they could've done his help us to the car or i don't know give me a damn wheelchair?! even the nurse at the front & the guard was wondering why i was let to walk to the car and no nurse pushing me in a wheelchair. they even told me a nurse is supposed to assist me out. the guard and the nurse at the front had gotten me a wheelchair but i was already at the lobby when they saw me so it didn't make a difference that i walked the whole way there but yet i am still grateful for them because i was in a shitload of pain, even when i got home i couldn't walk normally for days, i'm not even being overly dramatic. when i got the the car, the nurse that was supposed to assist me out ran back to me only to cut the hospital bracelets off me, which i was hoping to keep as a remembrance of my birth. long story short, i should've chose sharp mary birch hospital instead of this one. i thought i had made a good choice choosing this hospital to have my son at but i was terribly wrong. i will not come back to this hospital and go for my gut next time and choose another. if you've made it this far, thanks for reading and i hope you don't get the same experience i do.
janice , claudine and the crew in the gastroenterology dept rock!!!.thanks for making my mom comfortable during her procedure ...keep up the great job!!

came in for extreme abdominal pain. they insisted that i filled a form while i couldn't even stand and had to kneel and write on the ground because of the pain and then waited 20 min for admission. while inside, long wait after long wait. doctors were ok and seemed caring. but after the visit i received a surprise bill because of an out of network doctor (one of them). several tests were double charged on the out of network doctor. my insurance refused to pay the duplicate charges so the hospital billed me for it because the charged items were part of another covered test. the hospital didn't listen to any reasoning and was unprofessional in that they told us to call back in 10 days because they needed time to review, yet on the second call 10 days later seemed clueless and apparently nothing was reviewed at all. all they said was go talk to your insurance. they are a rogue organization and don't go!

this is a very hard review to write as i sit and wait for my loved one to pass . 
i find it necessary to write this even in these difficult times as that other family's will not be put in the same situation that we have . 
first i will say care is very inconsistent. my loved one was not in the best of health but by all means able to treat and save based on multiple doctors on staff but then when you have other doctors and nurses have different opinions or don't want to do the work to treat your loved ones suffer . 
lack of staff to do a life saving treatment and working equipment is everywhere in this hospital and quite frankly should be inspected by state . when you have a nurse shaking and sweating so bad and unable to perform a needed medical treatment they need to go back to school . even when you advocate they will fight you every step of the way . you are frowned upon when asking questions and when you can't get answers then we the public frown upon you the hospital, medical staff and medical system. this hospital was in network per the insurance company and our medical system has become so much about making money and not the care of the patient . where's our ethics and moral obligation to do the right things , well it's not at scripps hospital chula vista ..... please by all means stay away from this hospital for the health and well being of you or your family .

i was in the emergency last week there was so many patients.. let me tell you they keep that place moving..out of about 20 patients in front of me i was done in about an hour and half very satisfied... comepare to hillcrest ucsd that place is dirty in the wait room when i have went there like maybe 8 patients in front i would wait about 8 hours just to go to the back

i took my mom here the day after christmas. she had fallen and needed to check for breaks.  it would have been 10 days to get in to see her regular doctor. they were so busy but everyone was patient, caring and efficient. their triage system is good. i could hear a few patients who were not being cooperative nor civil to the staff and yet they remained professional. what i anticipated to be a day long endeavor turned out to be a couple of hours. .  don't want to come back but if you have to be in an er this is great.

i have never seen such poor care in any hospital. i am only familiar with the labor and delivery ward here. i am not going to go into the many many details, but they failed in so many areas that i will give a couple of examples. my daughter had her baby there, so i am referring to her experience which i was there to witness. from not bringing the small necessities such water, tissues or a toothbrush to bigger things such as not believing how strong her contractions were or believing that she was even having "real" contractions to letting her sit in her own puddle of blood for hours, they were awful. and certain nurses telling her to let her newborn baby scream because he needs to learn how to soothe himself; ridiculous. i will say that there were a couple of lactation nurses that were very caring and supportive, but the rest are only there doing a job. had i known, i would have never let her have her first (or any) baby there.

this is the worst hospital  you can go to. they don't  care about  the patient  only the money. i was coming  to  scripps  for a pain on my r.leg  according  to  them it was nothing. only  xrays were taken.  went to  sharp lst  and they sent  me right to e.r to  get  a gown put on. ct scan was taken  n there was blood clot on  that had already  traveled up to thigh.they admitted  me and was put under  blood thinners  when at scripps by xray nothing  was found.  went  in jan.3,2020 taken by paramedics n nothing but  xrays  were taken. i was taken  there cuz sharp  didn't have any  more room  for patients  brought by ambulance. for a person with  osteopenia  and had a past head injury, arm surgeries rotator cuff surgery  ct scan  was the  correct thing to do.  dr.did what he wanted  not  caring  what  i wanted. i had a fall due to a know  brace  that i have to wear. strap became undone and made me lose my balance. so if you care about your self ans relatives  go to sharp. tlc is given at sharp  n radiologist  are professionals and  smart n so are e.r. doctors.  worst nightmare of my life!  i'm only giving a star to get out review not because  scripps  hst chula vista,ca  deserves it!

i had genetic testing, today i spoke with katherine, and dr. rana both where very polite,explain what was going to happen and what test there where going to do and what test to do to be proactive. very happy to have the genetic team working on me, thanks

called in for an appointment, and i love the new phone system that gives you a call-back option, so you don't have to wait on the phone for three hours. 
after hearing my symptoms, the nurse got me an appointment a few hours later at 4:30pm. plenty of parking in the garage.

i checked in early and waited with my boyfriend in the waiting room. perfectly at 4:30pm i was called in. the doctor took a good 40 minutes to come by, and finished my check up in 5 minutes. 

the pharmacy was also quick. i got a text notifying me when my prescriptions were ready to be picked up, about 5 minutes after paying.

overall, very friendly just like the pensacola location, but i wish i didn't have to wait so long for the doctor, especially since my appointment was at 4:30.

i have been dealing with kaiser for a few years now because i am a caregiver to a family member with kaiser. i wish my family member did not choose kaiser.   like most businesses, it's hard to find good customer service or service nowadays.  there are a few "gems" who work at kaiser, but there are also a bunch of duds, from nurse aides to doctors to administrators. 

here are a few examples of the recent/past negative experiences (it's getting worse):  

1.  we had a cardiologist who went mia (he was here one day, and abruptly left back to the mainland...). there's more on this cardiologist....tmi      it's not easy to see a cardiologist--problems hiring/retaining.

2.  a fiscal office who hounds family members to pay the bill for elderly family member.  no kidding--most recently, a kaiser employee "happened" to be near my family member's er room and offered to escort/follow us out of the er only to demand payment for the er visit, cat scan, etc. before we could exit with our (still) sick family member--no invoice seen, but demands $$$!!!  family member did not expect to go to the er as it was an "emergency" so $ was not transferred and was not ready for payment. soooooo they looked at others to pay the bill for our family member!   we were told blood tests will be invoiced.  the family member has never been delinquent $.    kaiser has no shame$$$ and seems to care more about $$$!!  

does kaiser hound the emtala patients? #harassment

3.  a fiscal office calls family members (goes down the next-of-kin list, power of attorney, etc.) to call to pay the invoice for a current hospital stay for a family member before leaving the hospital--kaiser likes to equate it to a doctor's visit copayment.  no invoice. see #2 $$$$$$$ 

how does one know this is a "verified" caller from kaiser asking for a credit card# over the phone?  see #4 how do i get on the "no call" list?

4. a family member with power of attorney cannot email kaiser on behalf of a family member's account, but has to "jump through hoops" to set up a (so called "verified") separate account to email kaiser on behalf of the family member.  yet, it's okay for doctors, nurses, social workers, patient coordinators to call/speak/meet with the family member with power of attorney.  yet it's okay for the fiscal office to call family member with power of attorney for payment...just not email. who's to say who we are via email, phone, or  in-person?!

5.  we were once assigned a clinic doctor so perplexed with family member's ongoing health symptoms that "hospice" was this recommended solution instead of any attempts to fix the health issues. 

6.  where can a non kaiser member file a complaint, comment or suggest improvements on behalf of a family member?  better yet, try getting someone at kaiser who cares about what you think!!!  you are at kaiser's mercy and cannot just go to another doctor, hospital, etc.--and kaiser knows this! you are just a number--pick a number.  what quality assurance?

concerns fall on deaf ears--so get the word out and yelp it or post it online. otherwise "what happens in kaiser stays in kaiser!"

7.  it's not hard to find sassy/rude nurses in ambulatory, patient care coordination, etc....  instead of practicing "health" and "wellness" --it seems as though kaiser adds to the stress of patients and (for sure) the stress of family members.  lack of communication and lack of trust does not help.

8. double occupancy hospital rooms have no privacy whatsoever. what hipaa? 

i (unwantingly) know my family member's hospital roommate's name, date of birth, medications, medical conditions, doctors, visitors, etc. 

9. a roll of a dice--you may or may not be assigned a competent hospital or clinic doctor.  the hospital doctor only stays at the hospital. the patient's assigned doctor at the clinic does not come to the hospital. sometimes, there's a disconnect in communication between hospital and the clinic doctor. they really don't care--no trust established between temporary hospital doctor and temporary patient. for kaiser---it's seems like "next!" $$$

10.  parking usually suck during the weekday. there's been times when there are no stalls.   it's slippery when it rains in the parking area, elevators, sidewalks, etc.  what osha?

11. it takes a long time to get a bed from er to hospital. not enough beds.  certain er rooms/floors tilt, uneven--crappy builders.

here are recent examples of recent/past positive experiences;

1. family member does not seem to mind the hospital food.  patients are given a menu to order their food for delivery to their room.

2. for the most part, the er medical staff have good bedside manners.

3. on occasion, you will find a "gem" of a nurse or er doctor or staff (john l, etc.) who are knowledgable and actually seem to care about the patient--who actually seem to enjoy their job. 

4. family member likes current assigned doctor at the clinic.

my husband was brought here by ambulance because of chest pains earlier this morning (about 3 hours ago).   when i got here, they were drawing blood then took him to xray.  waited a while for the doctor.  in the meantime, i wanted to ask for ice chips since he is not able to have anything.  well, when i finally found his nurse and asked her, she was not the friendliest.  of the times we have been here, she is the worst and that is why i am on here writing a review  i understand that this is not the easiest job, but you are here to help those who need medical attention.   we got the ice chips, and i asked for more.  no one checks in.

they say either you love kaiser or you don't.  all i can say is that i am glad i do not have kaiser.  only giving 1 star because the security guard was super helpful and so was the greeter.

i love kaiser permanente as our health care provider! they are all in one , i can even book a few different appointments one after another on the same day at moana loa or koolau. the staff are always so nice, my primary dr. is dr mia hawkins at koolau and she is amazing! so is dr. patel & gyn dr lawrence.  our eye doctor michelle okabe in waipio is so nice & a sweetheart. my ortho is dr. santi for my knee, dr. matthews for my hand & dr. vasconcelos for sports med. dr. santi runs a great ortho dept and his assistant claudia is awesome & caring. dr. greninger in general surgery has been a surgeon since 1985, pa sara palm is young, nice & patient. the icu nurses are the best in their field. peter q. is so nice & good with his patients and their families & brian h. & luis p. are also good. i've brought my dad several times to er and they are very efficient. i've had quite a few operations as you can tell with my knowledge with the staff lol and everyone is attentive and very nice.  and believe it or not their hospital food is so good it really is!  check-in is quick & they have a self serve stand if there's a line. nice gift shop, cafeteria ok, the vending coffee is too expensive, i usually get mine at the outside stand paradise coffee stand. moa has farmers market, i think on wednesdays. the only complaint i have is that i wish they had more handicapped stalls you would think being a hospital they would. and that they revamp the kailua clinic. i would definitely recommend kaiser as you're primary health provider.

this is one review i wish i didn't have to make, but my adult daughter came down with severe abdominal pains and due to the hour i had to bring her to the er. i drove up to the er entrance and was assisted by a security staff member who made sure she got up to the check-in desk while i parked the car.

parking was a breeze and when i walked back into the er lobby, i was pleased to see that the staff was already getting her information and vitals. once they were done, she was assigned to an exam room where more questions and tests awaited her.

throughout her time in the exam room, she was visited by no less than 4 employees for administration of iv and meds, lab work, escort to x-ray, etc. everyone was extremely professional and constantly checking to see how she was holding up. we were there for at least 2.5 hours, and to be honest it felt a lot shorter.

it's experiences like these that make me proud to be a kp client.

love/hate relationship with this place. husbands eczema flared up pretty bad friday evening. (his face was super red and swollen!) we called to make an appointment with after hours but they were booked. so we opted to seek advice. first person we spoke to transferred us to a nurse, who then told us she was gonna talk to the doctor. was on hold for a bit and nurse says a doctor would call us back. guess what? no calls....


saturday morning we called again to make an appt. they asked what was wrong and whatnot and person said she was gonna send his symptoms to a doctor and a doctor would call back to make an appointment... well, we did not get any call back and at this point i was getting annoyed because my husband was miserable. i opted to take him to their damn er instead because i was tired of waiting. thankfully they weren't busy and i was finally glad he got seen and was given steroids! now i would just hate for the damn bill to come in.

the er visit would have been avoided if they just called back or made an appt. right away!

the people are so nice here. they have this wonderful routine before you have your surgery and they walk you right through it very efficiently and quickly so you are in and out of there in no time with no hassle. there are many volunteers here and they are absolutely delightful. there's also valet parking and i feel like they do whatever they can to make what could be a very negative experience into not so negative and experience and i very much appreciate that.

been here a number of times and feel it is really a wonderfully managed and organized health center. the 300-bed facility is built on 130-some acres of property, and replaces the old silver cross hospital that used to be in joliet. 

as you approach, the main building is the hospital center, and on its right is a separate but connected building that houses most of the testing and other diagnostic capabilities. nicely organized in keeping testing away from the busier hospital itself. we utilized the testing rooms, and felt the scheduling and organization was perfect.

have also had occasion to visit patients in the hospital and it is clean, roomy, wide-aisled, and up-to-date in almost every area (it opened in 2012). it seems that most every room is now a private one. this hospital is an anchor in will county, and is easy to get to in being right off i-355. 

never had the opportunity or need to use the emergency care facility so don't have a comment on it, but understand that it is a level ii trauma center. this is a nice addition to the area and a wonderful replacement for the old joliet facility.

yay. very nice staff all the way around. been here three days and not a single bad exchange with any staff member. from checking in to being discharged this has been the smoothest visit to any hospital around. it amazes us that there are so many negative reviews (mostly emergency room and at night though).

this place is a joke. came here by ambulance otherwise i would  have gone to loyola. i have a disease called pseudotumor cerebri. i came in with migraines and urine problems. they help with the migraine but when my bladder started acting a fool they refused. i'm in massive pain and they don't care. next time it's loyola. when i asked for a social work they told me they leave at 3. doubt that. never again will i come here.

review: allow me to introduce myself as a registered nurse, board certified by the american board of quality and utilization review. i attended the care of an 86 year old alert and oriented senior who came to this emergency department for relief of pain in her prosthetic hip. she remained in the emergency room from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. during those eight hours, she was never assessed for pain, nor was she offered or administered pain medication. the physician appropriately ordered a ct scan, blood work and a urinalysis. eventually, a young female physician reported to my friend that the ct scan revealed two hematomas, typically caused by a fall / trauma. my friend had experienced neither. following the initial ct scan, the same transport person came to my friend's cubical to transport her to a repeat ct scan. there was only one ct scan ordered, and it had been done. in addition, the rn suggested a straight catheterization urinalysis. i suggested that my friend first try to provide a voided urine sample, which she did. the rn chose not to respond to my friend's call light, which was  "blinking" for quite some time.  the rn reported that the original specimen had been "misplaced". huh? then, it was found. excuse me?  my friend remained in the same position for eight hours, more than enough time for a pressure ulcer to develop. i requested water and for some sort of nourishment to be provided. finally, she was given a dry turkey sandwich that had to have been days old. it was embarassing and disgusting.  at del webb,  seniors are disposable. my counsel would be to get the hell out of that hospital ed as quickly as possible.

review: this is the absolute worst hospital ever! i brought my 12 year old daughter here because she was having stomach pain.  the nurse asked her if she was sexually active. my daughter told her no. the dumb nurse then asked my daughter if she has ever had anal sex!!!! my daughter looked at me confused and asked me what that was. she also told my daughter that the doctor would most likely have to do an inappropriate exam on her. we were both wondering why this idiotic nurse only thought that this could be a sexual problem. my daughter got nervous. the doctor came in after a very long wait and started asking my daughter questions. nothing sexual or inappropriate.  i told him what the nurse had asked and also told him what inappropriate test that the nurse said that he would do.  his face turned red and said that it wasn't something that he does and wasn't planning on doing that.  the doctor said that he couldn't figure out what was wrong with my daughter and that she should see another doctor to follow up.  they had poked her with an iv needle and we waited 30 minutes for the liquid. i asked one of the nurses how much longer it would take for the liquid and he with attitude told me that if the doctor ordered it my daughter should get it soon. we waited another 30 minutes and still no liquid. i walked out and asked another nurse when she will get the liquid because she was in pain. she also had an attitude problem and said that it should be soon. 1 hour later the idiotic nurse from the beginning walked in and i told her that what she told us wasn't true about the test and she laughed it off like a dumb b! i told her that we were still waiting for the iv and she said that she thinks that the doctor didn't order it. the doctor then came and said that he forgot and that he would order it now. ummmmm really??????? 1 hour later and no damn liquid for her iv! i told the nurse that my daughter was in pain and tired and to get the damn needle out of her arm.  we walk out and we're were told that we needed to pay $1200! for the f'ed up service??????? wow! i told her that i had insurance and she told me with the insurance it was $1200. i asked her what a cash patient would be paying and she said $900. i said then consider me a cash patient and we received the worst service. they are so lucky that i didn't sue them. i took my daughter to another doctor that was able to figure out her problem without it becoming sexual.  this hospital should be closed down. i called and complained several times and was told i should also call other departments, but anytime i called back i would be told that they never received my complaints. they supposedly had no idea that i had complained and one of the idiots told me that those were normal questions that the nurse was asking. one more thing!!! i had asked for an itemized bill and one of the charges was $250 for a pregnancy test on a child that has never had sex!

review: my dad was here for open heart surgery so i had to come and go for over a week. it was a pleasant hospital with a nice valet service if you're handicapped.  there's a cafe and coffee shop on the first floor and i think a cafeteria elsewhere in the building. it's not about hospital i'm really glad i don't have to come any more.

how? first off the staff both in the ed and the icu were fantastic. the ed was swamped yet they still managed to get someone to escort us to where we needed to go (the last thing i want to do is to wander about a unfamiliar hospital with all of my gear trying to find where my patient is) 

once we got to where the we needed to go in this case the icu, again the staff was friendly, professional, prepared, and went above and beyond to help us get the patient and family ready for the transport. i cannot say enough about how good they were. 

thank you to the entire staff at mercy and your community is lucky you all are there!!!!!!!

communication between nurse to nurse, physician to physician, and staff to family members is terrible and irresponsible. my father was under care here and inappropriately discharged to home which was not a safe place for him due to multiple medical issues and safety concerns (high fall risk and dementia). we spoke with multiple staff members and were never told the full extent of his injuries until after he was already discharged (neck fracture and swallow difficulties requiring a special thick liquid diet). he was discharged suddenly and late friday night which left little to no options to pick up his required medications (antibiotics included). they made no efforts to assist in this matter. my father is a military veteran and medicare eligible yet no plans were made to set him up with the resources available to him to help with physical and mental recovery. this is unsafe practice and needs to be fixed immediately. they need to do better.

the university of iowa hospital commits criminal acts to protect its highest-paid surgeon, dr. patrick william hitchon.  after dr. hitchon intentionally paralyzed me and stitched me shut with a broken spinal cord, he lied to me and refused to release my medical records.  he lied to me repeatedly.  i unknowingly lived 18 years with a broken spinal cord until dr. sergion mendoza saved my life.  beware of dr. patrick william hitchon and the university of iowa hospitals & clinics.

review: delivered my baby here and i only have good things to say. it was a rough go around and i was considered a "frequent flyer" since i was high risk and was constantly in and out on weekly 24hr observations. they allowed my professional photographer in the room to capture our baby's birth story. i want to start with the anesthesiologist cory who did my epidural. he was great and i hardly felt a thing aside from his cold hands which i warned  him would be in my yelp review lol. they say cold hands, warm heart. cory informed me of everything that was happening and made me feel comfortable and relaxed , literally. now onto the nursing staff- with being a "frequent flyer" the nurses never once made me feel bad for coming and spending the night  to check on my baby- in fact the encouraged it because i was so high risk. the nurse michele that took care of me all the way up until i pushed (her shift ended)  was phenomenal. she informed me of everything  that was happening and reassured me everything would be okay because i was having a premature birth. it felt like my sister was in the room y'all! she's amazing. she even came to visit me in recovery & gave me a hug. she has so much passion for what she does and she is right where she needs to be in life. since i progressed quickly after my epidural my doc didn't make it so the laborist on call delivered me. i  didn't catch her name but she was awesome too! on the postpartum side i'd like to thank dr. abdulla and dr. lamotte for performing a frenotomy on my baby at just hours old so it didn't effect breast feeding/latching. all the staff made sure to accommodate  us with anything we needed/ wanted. they fed my hubby each day we stayed so he never once had to leave our side and they also gave us a celebration  dinner with steak, shrimp, a baked potato, a bunt cake along with two bottles of sparking cider. the kitchen staff was amazing and so kind and all the food was on point. i have nothing negative to say about my experience. i will have all my babies here in a heartbeat. thank you for making our experience unforgettable while we welcomed our double rainbow baby into the the  world.

the thing i don't like about coming to this office building is the parking. the parking structure can get completely full, but they do have valet parking on the top floor. the problem is that at times the valet parking is full as well and they won't take any cars. becomes a problem when you have to look for street parking and you have an appointment. the worst time to have an appointment is in the middle of the morning because good luck finding a parking stall! it's too bad because i actually like this office building but they don't have sufficient parking compared to the offices.

the medical care here is the gold standard!  at least in the saperstein icu.  

my family member is very ill and of advanced age. they take a team approach to figuring out your diagnosis. now that she is at home, medical personnel is still showing up to follow up with her!  

they are even doing follow-up testing to ensure that she is improving and to prevent a readmit.  the care at cedars completely reassuring and gives one confidence that one can overcome illness even in ones 80s. 

the only concern i had was my observations that 2 of the security guards have very obvious signs of untreated thyroid disease. surely some medical professional there has noticed. i hope they take interest in their staff as they are the face of cedars and your first encounter before one is allowed upstairs.

i have had a number of bad run-in's with the health system here in the central coast, but i have also had some good ones so i have always held off posting anything.
my interaction this past week changed that completely though.
back story - i have been on topiramate for around 3 years, which for anyone who has never encountered this medication, is an extremely expensive medication with horrible withdrawal effects and not very fun side effects. one 30 day supply costs me around $250 since i got laid off and lost my insurance. i can't afford that and don't want to stop cold turkey so i have been trying to wean myself off since december. (i was on 400 mg).
on thursday night, i had a partial focal seizure. i was awake for the whole thing, screaming but could not stop myself, it was by far the most terrifying thing i have ever dealt with. i couldn't think straight after for the next 24 hours.
my partner called 911 and they asked me to go with them to the er because i couldn't stand without getting extremely dizzy and my blood pressure dropping.
i was in the er until 6 am, and the doctor tested me for a uti. and then told me i fainted because i have a blood pressure issue.
i would like to hit on the point again that i was in no place to advocate for myself, and neither was my partner. he didn't fully know what happened, and i couldn't think straight. i couldn't even explain it fully to my partner for 2 days. but this doctor decided, despite being told i was getting off a medication that has been known to cause seizures, and that i had a seizure like episode that i might have had a uti and blood pressure issues. (spoiler, i didn't have a uti).
he kept coming into the room to ask me "if i was ready to go yet", like i was enjoying having a nurse watch me pee when i needed to go. finally, we just left because it was obvious that he was not going to help and i was exhausted.
i am terrified to see the bill for this useless trip. i only know what kind of seizure i had from my own research. i don't know if it hurt me at all, seeing as i was awake the whole time, or if anything else happened.
that doctor doesn't care at all. it makes me sad. if i have another seizure, i'll just let it play out and hope i survive. that's all that will happen if i go to the hospital, except they will charge me money if i do.

i was the support person for my daughter's recent labor and delivery. the labor and delivery service was mostly good, but the time after the delivery was awful.
we came to the delivery room around midnight and my daughter delivered at 2:30 with an uncomplicated natural childbirth with no pain medication. the delivery was very smooth and the dr. was skilled and personable. i thought it was a wonderful delivery.

because i was my daughter's support person, i was there for the entire 31 hours after delivery. and this is my story. 

we got in the recovery room about 4 and the nurses began their protocol of patient care. my daughter was not allowed to sleep more than 2 hours at a time, plus she was caring and feeding her newborn. nurses continued to wake her up over and over for some sort of patient care, that was in my opinion mostly unnecessary. at one point a nurse came in to wake her up and ask her if she wanted a pain pill. where is the common sense in that?
i got her out of there as quick as possible because she needed rest after being exhausted by delivery. she guesses she got 3 hours of sleep in the 31 hours she was there after delivery. perhaps this is a way to get new mothers out as soon as possible?

the sad thing is many new parents don't realize how abusive this protocol is and just accept it as normal. even the lactation specialist i complained to said she had her baby at home for that exact reason. a natural, un-medicated delivery is a normal part of life. and in my opinion the hospital's patient care is abusive.

we all joke that new parents are sleep deprived, but in the hours after delivery a new mother should be allowed to sleep if baby will let them. i worry about other mothers who may have had complication. they need the rest more than anyone and i know they will be denied rest by hospital patient care. 

we asked to be left alone for a few hours for sleep. the staff agreed then just continued on with all the things they are required to do. 

we left a day early so my daughter could come home and get some rest and she has been doing that. she would have liked to stay the full time because she has another child to care for and she is a single mother, but she told me she was so exhausted, that she needed to leave. she said she couldn't keep her eyes open and i saw that every time her eyes closed she would immediately be asleep. how is a person that exhausted able to care for a newborn or even herself?

i'm sorry for anyone who delivers at a hospital especially this one.  patients are trusting your hospital with their health and a very very important part of health is rest.

a close family member ("cc") was involved with this program for a little over 2.5 years. after "graduating," cc then relocated and continued in outpatient therapy with the same psychiatrist. a few months ago, we terminated treatment with this provider. we finally realized that the provider was squirrely at best and only sought to make messes for cc that he would have no part in cleaning up.

prior to entering treatment, cc was on zero medications, had zero hospitalization, and zero history of drug abuse. cc was in school full time, working part time, active in our church community, and generally managing. following a traumatic life event, we voluntarily chose to have cc enter the retreat on the recommendation of our home psychologist. 

after a series of: 
-tms (junk science), 
-ect (victorian, invasive shock therapy), 
-2 years worth of toxic medication trials, and 
-1.5 years of outpatient group therapy
-relocating cc several states away to continue treatment, 
we are at a massive loss emotionally and financially.

the retreat psychiatrist (who led our family member's care) had far too much faith in his own capabilities. he had a deceptively closed-minded focus on his personal field of study, which we know now, doesn't really help with the functional treatment of complex trauma. we didn't get to choose cc's providers, but knowing what we know now, we never would have chosen this path for them. 

you practically need a phd in psychiatric practice to understand how this program works. we were very blindsided to learn that the arcane psychoanalysis was the foundation for the retreat's programming. they tout dbt, but it's two sessions per week, which are confusing and disorganized at best. 

the treatment team routinely exercised poor judgement in assessing the dynamics of cc's complicated trauma background, which continued throughout the entire course of care. they essentially allowed cc's biological parents (and main payors) to dictate the care and treatment strategies used, which resulted in a series of misdiagnoses.

it's a rampant issue in healthcare, but the providers are wholly protected by the system from bearing any consequence for their "firm suggestions." they put the onus on the patients and their families to be the ultimate deciders, but it really became a toxic cycle of the blind leading the blind. we didn't feel like we had a choice at any point if we wanted cc to get on a path to recovery. 

think of sinking an average year's salary for a 3-week-long diagnostic workup by a supposed "team of experts." a mix of art therapists and social workers will work with your psychiatrist to strong arm the patient into a desire to "get better" and then coerce the family into refinancing their home to get the recommended weeks to months of extended care at over $2000 per day. this includes an intensive regimen of loosey-goosey therapy groups, bizarre binders full of self-help jargon, and patient-guided group therapy. they are trying to be progressive, but it's a classic case of poor administrative controls and defaulting into letting the inmates run the asylum. it honestly feels like some of the providers get a kick out making things messy and watching us drown while we try to clean up catastrophe after catastrophe. they just smile at us and placate us with politicized psychiatric jargon.

once we pursued outside consultation, we realized we'd been completely, wholly, massively duped by these supposed "experts" and gamed by a very unregulated rehabilitation system. unless medication management and positive talk therapy are the $200,000+ boost you need, these people constantly come up short.

after all is said and done, we were dealing with an entirely different medical and psychiatric picture than the providers were willing to treat or even investigate. hundreds of thousands of dollars later, and hundreds of hours of travel, family therapy, and the many years cc devoted to their own therapy, we have very little to show for it. 

we are left with immeasurable pain and suffering, a heap of debt, and a solid education in the toxic dysfunction of the behavioral health system.

speaking from my own personal experience, if you are a person of color seeking care of any kind, run. my mother always had our family at ucla. as a teenager/young adult, i begun to see how my primary care doctor at the iris cantor women's center seemed to really be less than interested in my health and health concerns. as an adult, i have a different insurance and i've had to go across the way to the 200 building where the care is worse. the doctor i ended up meeting with tried to convince me blood tests were not necessary when i was concerned i might be ill. turns out i tested positive for the exact test i came in for. i have attempted to find a black female doctor to try and ensure as best i can that i have a doctor who cares about my health, but instead i have been given the run around as my health has declined. the only black doctor in the clinic is not taking any new patients and her referral for another black doctor was "a new female doctor in century city but does not her name". apparently that doctor, along with the only other black doctor, have both quit and their last weeks are next week. it is really disheartening to see for myself exactly how difficult it is to get a decent level of medical care as a black woman, and probably just as an average income level human being, in this country. just terrible.

i had been seeing ucla doctors in various locations and willing to travel once i find someone i like.  my kids see a ucla pediatrician in santa monica and we have been so happy with them.  the medical center, however, was a nightmare for me, with fragmented services and information, nothing seems set up from the patient's perspective, no one knows the whole picture of your health.  the physicians based here are impossible to schedule with, and if you are lucky to get in, they run late. once i waited 1.5 hours before getting up and leaving.  of course they are busy with lots of patients but my time is valuable too.  but they also botched a biopsy.  tried several times until they had to quit and asked me to come back for another try after i healed up.  no thank you.  i went to the other reputable, nationally-ranked hospital in town and my experience was completely different.  i am a huge ucla fan, but i won't be back to the medical center if i can help it.

i took my husband to the er last sunday. he received excellent diagnostic care and was admitted to the hospital with pneumonia. from the time he was admitted until his discharge on thursday he received excellent care. the nurses on the 6th floor were superb.

cannot speak highly enough about the emergency care that i received at this hospital.  on 07/14/16,  i arrived at this hospital by car unaware that i had suffered a fluke "plaque collapse" and had no blood flow to the right side of my heart.   i was going to die without immediate emergency medical treatment which required inserting a stent to reestablish blood flow.  

from the moment my wife pulled up to the hospital emergency entrance at which point i realized i could no longer walk on my own, the professionals at littleton adventist went into action. 

i was immediately wheeled into the hospital and surrounded by a team of professionals who determined that this previously very healthy patient was in the middle of a fluke major heart attack.  i was dying.  they stabilized me and immediately took me into an operating room where i was surrounded again by an incredible team of professionals.  a cardiac surgeon who was already at the hospital performed the procedure and i had a full recovery.  

in fact, felt great right after surgery when i once again had blood flowing to the right side of my heart.  spent the night at the hospital where everyone who interacted with me was a+ wonderful.   my surgeon told me days later on follow up that there was no residual damage at all to my heart.  he attributed that to my regularly working out for years while i attribute it more to the incredible skill of my surgeon and all of the amazing professionals at littleton adventist who worked with superb teamwork to save my life.

i can't say enough about nurse steve in the icu! my mom was in there for the last three days and we were fortunate enough to have him take care of her all three nights. steve was very compassionate, understood my mom's needs when even we did not, and made me so comfortable knowing that my mom was in his care overnight. most of us wish for our parents to get out of icu, but i was sad knowing that such a compassionate nurse would no longer be taking care of her. this is not to say that the other nurses and doctors have not been great, but steve was exceptional and i wanted to extend my deepest gratitude to him!
thank you steve. i truly appreciate your dedication to what you do and for your compassion to your patients and their families. enjoy your long weekend off. mrs. "z" and family will forever be thankful.

sue terlap

very very disappointed in this hospital. my adult son attempted suicide by overdosing on alcohol. bac .45. hospital kept him for less then 24 hours.  "evaluated" and released him  while he was still intoxicated.no one seemed to  care. i told  psychology he wanted to go home so he could  to finish the job and i was told that is his right.  what really??

i feel bad giving hospitals bad reviews, but this time, it's necessary. i brought my son in with severe back pain and sciatic leg pain. we got here at 2:15. got into a room at about 3:00. a nurse came in and asked all the usual questions and said "ryan" (pa) would be in to talk to my son. one hour goes by. no one.  nothing for the pain. it's about 4pm and my son hadn't eaten anything. i went out to the nurse's station and asked if i could get something from the cafeteria for him. 'nurse one' says probably, but he needs to be seen by ryan to get the ok. i go back to his room and we wait. another hour goes by. i return to the desk and ask, "when will ryan go to my son's room?" 

nurse one - oh, he hasn't been in yet? i'll get him in there.

ten minutes later, ryan shows up, asks my son what's happening and he tells him about the severe sciatic pain and low back pain. 

ryan says, "so, what do you want us to do for you?" 

i'm shocked. he says,  well we can give you muscle relaxers. or, i guess we could do an mri." um, yeah. thanks, we'll take the mri.  and something for his pain right now? thanks....

i went to get my son something to eat and someone came in and gave him a shot of valium. valium? he's not having a panic attack... his disc is blown! 


we wait.

we wait. 5:30 a different nurse comes in and says they'll be taking him out for his mri soon - remove all metal etc. at 5:40, ryan comes back in and says, "well, its gonna be another couple hours until we can get you the mri, so if you want to go home, i can give you a prescription... you probably won't get the mri till 8 or 9."

at first, i'm like, yeah, we're going home this is bs. we'll  just go home and try to make it through the weekend. then i started to think about that.  if we went home, we'd go through the wind with him in pain. monday, try to get an appt with a surgeon. prob won't get an appt for that week. meanwhile, we still can't get an mri because we haven't seen a dr. to authorize it. weeks will go by without any help. 

so, i go back out and tell ryan we want the mri after all. he says he just cancelled it. i said reschedule.  

in less than 10 minutes, someone comes in to take my son to get the mri. really. 

i'm figuring ryan was trying to clear out the room my son is in without doing anything for him. its friday night and they need the room. 

this kind if care is what i'd expect with socialized medicine.  this is unacceptable.  i'd give a zero if i could. no attention, no urgency. they act as if severe pain shouldn't be an er visit,  make you wait long enough and maybe you'll just go home!!

we wait.

my husband had back surgery.  this has been the best hospital, best service, and most comfortable hospital room/ accomodations i have ever seen.   very attentive to the patients.  their whole team has been amazing.  incredibly impressed and well pleased.

by far the worst of the major hospitals south of downtown denver. have waited for tests in conditions that resemble third world countries. use any of the other available hospitals. have given them second chances through the years and nothing changes. generally disinterested personnel and frequent confusion.

i had a wonderful experience in the er at this hospital recently.  i arrived there at 5:30 pm on feb. 13. i waited less than 30 minutes, and a nurse apologized for my having to wait!  every single health care worker that helped me was wonderfully kind, compassionate and informative.  the pa that took care of me was skillful and made me feel safe.  i had a ct scan in the er, and the pa told me the results 45 minutes later.  i was given treatment, monitored closely, and helped in every way to be made as comfortable as possible. i was home 6 hours later and have been recovering well.  so grateful to the amazing staff at littleton adventist er!
still have not received my records. don't ask me too contact littleton hospital i receive them.

we had another great experience. i have had 2 knees and one hip done here and my right thumbnail put back on after it was ripped off in a work accident. all these were terrific, but my husband and i went in because we suspected he may be having a heart attack. ten people leaped on him and sprang into immediate action. he was stabilized then whisked to the cath lab for a stent. they were all amazing providers and made sure we knew what was happening. they took terrific care of him and really made us feel better while not sugar coating the seriousness of the event. always caring and totally professional and informative. would always say go here for any concern or condition you may have to get the best care.

did my homework to make sure scripps was identified by my insurance provide as in network before needing their services.  went to the er for a non life threatening injury in october with the peace of mind knowing i was in network and costs would be covered for treatment.

2 months later the surprise/balance bill arrived from pacific emergency providers.  apparently the hospital is in network but the doctors are out of network, and i am responsible for paying out of network fees at this in network hospital.  i didn't go to an in network hospital for the cafeteria and waiting room, i went for in network care by in network doctors.  after contacting both pacific emergency providers and my health care insurer, neither would budge and the bill is mine to cover.

avoid scripps mercy or expect out of network fees, aka balance billing regardless if your insurance identifies them as in network.

apparently congress is working on a solution to curb the practice of balance billing, until then i'll just plan on using youtube to repair future injuries.

this is my first appointment at lancaster general hospital for a bone grafting procedure and staying overnight for recovery time. i am going to be a new patient. i never been there before as a patient.

this is the sorriest excuse for a healthcare organization i have ever seen. went to the chantilly facility to become a patient and transfer my car from atlanta so i could get care. doctor acted as if i was a bother, they never contacted me with lab results or been contacted me since for follow on care. i contacted them to voice my concern on 10 different occasions, each time i was told that someone would call me back in two days. i still have not received the first call back. stopped by 3 times to ask for care was told they would call me and no one has, heck i could be dead right now. i got two out of my three medications mailed to my home, i did not ask for them, i had plenty on hand. and here it is 3 months later and no one has ever called. they need to close this place down, doctors are uncaring and incompetent and no one cares if you live or die here. treating patients actually seem to bother them. va clinic and doctors in atlanta are like the mayo clinic compared to this crap-hole.

i have never been so disgusted and disappointed with st e's as much as i am now. 6 days ago i had an incident with my 70 pound dog and an incredibly heavy kitchen stool, the result being a smashed shin, swollen, black and blue with a strange hard bump to the left. 3 days after the swelling and bruising was covering my whole leg and ankle and foot. an er visit was inevitable and i've always preferred st e's in the past so it wasnt a question.  the receptionist wrote on the paperwork "swollen and sore ankle", even after i repeatedly said that wasnt the point of impact, but just a by-product.  i was sent to fast track. and was seen by calin b. ostler, pa for about 60 seconds. she ordered an x ray of my ankle, and the wrong side of my leg. over and over i said to 4 different people, my ankle is not the big issue but the massive, hard, painful bump to the left of my shin. after the xray they put me back in a conference room.  30 minutes later a nurse comes in with my discharge paperwork.  i let her go through her shpeel and then say, "the doctor hasn't even come to talk to me about the xray yet so how am i getting discharged". shes clearly embarrassed and goes to get the doctor that had no intention of talking to me again.  calin b ostler came back in the conference room, said she would give me an air cast for my ankle and to take motrin and quickly left. the nurse came back with the air cast and i said again that it's not my ankle and that the air cast will be incredibly painful on the bump since it would rest directly beneath it.  so she wrapped it and sent me on my way.  i was absolutely, positively livid. not only was there no explanation to what the hell was wrong, i felt i was being rushed out. so, 2 days ago, no improvement, i decided to try iu health.  which is where i still am, writing this review in a hospital bed.  they admitted me immediately, i've been here since the 10th with a hematoma in my leg(that would be the weird bump), a stressed out heart (it was 140 bpm when i arrived), and blood clotting.  i have to have the hematoma drained and physical therapy and heart medication. they could not believe what st e's had done. or rather, not done.  if the blood clots made it to my heart i could have died. not to mention telling me to take motrin when nsaids like that can cause further harm with blood clotting.  why this very serious problem was completely and blatantly ignored by calin b ostler,pa and the folks at st e's i'll never know.
what i do know is i will be filing a serious and formal complaint and i'll never, ever put my trust in st e's franciscan health ever ever again.  
(as a side note, iu health have been positively amazing. i'll be writing a much brighter review for them)

review: as a patient as well as someone who has done numerous clinical rotations here, i applaud this hospital! every single staff member i encountered from nursing to housekeeping was amazing. the establishment is always very clean & comfortable. their er specifically was great about getting me right in, and quickly diagnosing as well as making a plan to help with my issue. i highly recommend st. clare's of denville!

just wanted to add a few words to  my last review. my family and i (mostly me lol) have been to st clair's many times for many different issues. 
we have always  received excellent care. my son and daughter where both born in st clairs hospital and sometime in may my daughter will be delivering my first grandchild at the same hospital.

i had fallen in my home and dislocated my shoulder. needless to say, it was extremely painful.  an ambulance was called and i was transported to st. clare's denville.  first of all the two emts were really wonderful. their names were nicole and ahmad.  
they even stopped into the er later in the day to see how i was.
all the staff were absolutely wonderful.  they all were so caring. when i was waiting to be transported back to the er from x-ray a nurse passing by expressed concern for me and brought me a heated blanket for my shoulder.  she also was very kind.  i can't understand the negative reviews.  my nurse was lorrie...again very kind and caring.  i wish i could name all that took care of me.

the absolute worst scheduling department services i have ever experienced and i have worked in healthcare for 40 plus years. never able to have a human answer the phone,always informed the call volume is heavy , and you can expect a return call within 24 hours. not so easy when you have cancer and waiting for your insurance company to approve a scan for a month! either the scheduling staff at st clare's is too sparse to handle to number of patients calling,or they just could care less about the community trying to utilize their services. think i'll go elsewhere in the future.st clare's,you need to up your game!

update. i had a billing question and spoke to jill in billing. after about 15 minutes, she could not find any record of me having surgery. she found my account because she had a different visit, but had zero record that i had a full surgery. tell me again that you don't lost medical records?

literally almost killed me. had an infection from the head orthopedic that gave me an infected dirty needle in his private practice. i go to the er, after complaining, they send me home. go back to the er because they wont prescribe meds over the phone, and had to be checked in. they never admitted that they gave me an infection spreading through my body, because the orthopedic i visited, is a head doctor at st claire's as well. if the 3rd party infectious disease people didnt help. who knows. milked my insurance. doctors pop on a waive hi, not leaving a name and bill you. the staff is kids, the doctors are horrible. the kids are good. food horrendous. the religous facade is a front. only reason i went.

i went to the 5th floor for pain management, a bilateral medial branch block in lumbar 2-5. hayley checked me in and took my vitals, then quickly took me back to room #21. karen, the rn, got my iv hooked up perfectly and me sign some pictures, then i got undressed and put on the hospital gown, and gave her my urine sample. immediately another nurse came in and updated my medications. next, some men came in to take me back. one of the guys was joking with me as he hooked up some numbing medicine in my iv. the procedure took about 15 min. then they were taking me back to my room. everyone i dealt with was so nice and thoughtful and everything went as smooth as it possibly could. i know a lot of yelpers gave them bad reviews but this is my second time here and the pain management staff rock! it's clean where i was and i really don't have anything negative to say. hopefully the whole hospital has stepped up their game and they can get more positive reviews. i'll be back for more procedures so if everything keeps going as good as my last two visits, i'll be alright.

cafeteria review

i'd like to take a moment to complain about one of the employees in the cafeteria. i don't know her name. she's african-american and wears colorful eyeshadow. she is one of the most intensely rude people i've ever met. it's common knowledge throughout the hospital about her being so rude to people as well as habitually over-charging  people. i know this because i was warned about this and was told i'd better request my receipt, which i do. i once brought it to her attention that she double charged me, she immediately got an even bigger attitude and told me it was my fault that she had over charged me. recently i was getting an item out of one of the refrigerators when she cuts me off, steps right in front of me, blocking my way to the refrigerator. she didn't even acknowledge my presence which she  knew full well was there. i hope that something is done about this woman's bad attitude. it's not a good representation of the hospital.

brought my dying mother in from her doctors appointment to be admitted. doctor called ahead to let them know she was coming and in bad condition. too say someone in that amount of pain looking the way she did should have to wait 3 hours is outrageous. idk what you guys do back there but i sure know when you have people sick the way she and several others were waiting that long while everyone of your employees seemed to have a zero sense of urgency is just a disgrace. fix this before someone dies waiting on you in your emergency room lobby.

arrived with my mother at the er. asked for a wheelchair, as she couldn't walk. the front attendant, while remaining seated and on her phone, said "we don't have any down here". what? an er with no wheelchairs? she responded that they were probably all upstairs because "they get lazy and don't bring them down". asked if she could get someone to come get my mother. she was in a lot of pain and  2 weeks post heart attack. attendant replies "ok. just a second" and proceeds to look at her phone and close all of her apps. mind you, we didn't just casually walk into the er. i was practically holding my elderly mother up. when a nurse finally did arrive, she had to chat it up with the desk attendant, talking about when  they go on break, where to meet. i will never ever set foot in this hospital again.

we always have an excellent experience with st. john's . 

the er staff at st. john's got us through admitting & into a room probably within 2? maybe 3 hours . 

the doctors who are on staff , the nursing staff is wonderful no nurse ratched's at this hospital. my fiancé was in for several days with cardiac issues . we switched his old long term cardiologist from cedars sinai (nightmare hospital ) to now dr grifka . dr grifka is another 5 star cardiologist . he has the best bedside manner and it's the same in his office. he's very clear & cautious. they don't care about managed care at st. john's . they don't let the insurance companies dictate when to discharge a patient . the nursing staff was terrific to me even offering me linens to spend the night in my honeys room and dinner with him. i passed on the hospital food and most of the days we ate from the cafeteria salad bar . im not too hip on hospital food .  
valet is convenient but pricey so if you can find street parking i'd highly recommend it, i used the valet when i was arriving later in the afternoon leaving a night . what made me mad at the valet , no one was waiting except me. instead of putting on the rear defogger they wiped the inside of the window smearing the back window so badly i couldn't see behind me . long drive from sm to sfv not being able to see out of your rear view window. what's the hurry? i tipped accordingly the second day .

i'm torn between five stars and one star, so i felt that two was sufficient for my wife's experience. i'm a proud father of a new baby girl who came into this world over one month early!! 

the labor & delivery staff were great except when it came to having my wife's food delivered. at first i thought it was the dietary staff but i later learned that the food trays are left at the nursing station. why? i have no idea but i can tell you that the trays sit for at least a minimum of one hour before the trays are delivered. i'm sure it's not the nursing staff's job to deliver food but why continue this practice if it's a problem?? 

as i mentioned before the staff are great when it comes to patient care but this one little detail of not delivering a pregnant patient's food is truly a horrible practice!! what makes it the absolute worst is that my wife spent one week at the hospital dealing with a difficult labor and now she has to eat cold food that has been sitting out for over an hour... 

after being transferred to the postpartum unit, it was extremely noticeable how much more attentive and helpful the staff is. everyone from the nurses to the unit secretary were beyond helpful. the dietary staff delivered breakfast, lunch and dinner to the room every single day!! the few days spent there were great!! the young man who conducted the hearing test was very professional and handled our baby with such care. i don't know his name but he definitely deserves recognition!! 

overall, our experience was good up until we were discharged... as we were being transported out we passed the security staff. there were three black male guards hanging out at the desk in the er lobby area. as my wife was being rolled out on a wheelchair one guard shouts out "what did you have"? i nicely replied "we had a baby girl" and i smiled because it's our first child and had been trying to have a baby for several years. as we reach the automated doors the guard yells out "good luck" in a sarcastic manner! 

this is exactly what i needed after spending an entire week in the hospital watching my wife struggle with a difficult birth, every meal being served cold and possibly bordering on bacteria contamination; all to be topped off with some contract security guard expressing his personal feelings on how he feels about having a baby girl. this is what you have to look forward if you're a patient here!!

i remember when this health center was run by the sister of charity of leavenworth. it was as professional as you could ever expect but for whatever reason it has lowered its values and you'll probably get a similar experience or worse!!

allied security is the contract company providing your sarcasm and er hangouts. i was informed that it's managed by the dietary department, not even sure how that makes sense?? when i inquired i was also told the dietary department also manages the valet parking operations. maybe it's downsizing at its best or worst??

i do want to thank;

marcel loh - chief executive
paul makarewicz - director - mission
carol o'dea, administrative director - quality and patient safety 

for not doing your jobs and especially for allowing these experiences!!

i had some testing and surgery here. everyone that i came in contact with the hospital was wonderful and incredibly helpful. the nurses in pre-op and post op and the radiologists were just incredible at explaining everything and anticipating your needs. my stay was 3 nights in the hospital and the nurses were very friendly and great at keeping me comfortable. they listened to me and tried to help me with any complications that i had. they even let my kids come visit me one night, then they went on lockdown and they had to help me leave the hospital. they were also very good about helping me get in contact with my surgeons when i needed too.

i recently was diagnosed with breat cancer.  i utilized the services of st. john's health center receiving excellent care in their breast center.

the staff i came into contact with were amazing. from first contact onwards all the staff made every step as easy as possible.  

i am an rn by background so my obserations were very keen throughout the entire journey.  i have the greatest regard for this system and the indidivuals who provided such prompt diagnosis, treatment, care and support.  i compliment all the professionals who were not only skilled but professtionals with compassion.  i have felt confident about the advice i received as well as the treatment.

the staff did everything they could to make a difficult time as pleasant as possible for me, the patient.  the appointments and treatment were well organized so they were one after the other with a minimum of wait time.

i am amazed by the high quality of care i received from the oncologists, the nurse navigator and the hospital staff.  the attitude everyone exhibited daily is something i could never duplicate.  any patient going through cancer treatment needs all the pleasantness, positive attitude and care this center offers.

i highly recommend this facility for treatment.  most of all, i am thoroughly satisfied with the results from my surgery, a partial mastectomy with reconstructive surgery.

i was seen 12/14/19 in the er and was not taken seriously when i told staff i was confident i was having a miscarriage. i was brought in by ambulance and they told staff i was "having a heavy period" i was put in a room with 8 other people separated by curtains so everyone could hear everything. i was not given a bed i was given a chair were i remained sitting in pain for hours. staff was rude and not compassionate at all. finally a doctor came in and told me they could confirm i was pregnant but couldnt confirm if i was miscarrying or not, couldnt give me anything for pain, couldnt suggest anything or anyway to manage the bleeding and sent me on my way. i paid the hospital bill that night. which im sure was more than they got from the homeless and drug addicts that i shared that room with that night. i had more blood work done the following tuesday that confirmed i did in fact miscarry. not that any staff or doctors at this hospital would give any sort of concern. you guys need to do better. be better. try harder! no one should ever have to go through that horrible situation ever again. it was devastating to learning i was miscarrying at the same time as finding out i was even pregnant after being told my entire life i couldnt get pregnant. then to also be put through the treatment that i received at this hospital at such a devastating time. the doctor was so up beat and happy to come in and deliver this news to my husband and i. i will continue to tell my story and let others know how horrible my experience was at this hospital.staff and doctors at this hospital shouldnt be allowed to treat anyone.

first off, babyline is a free service that hoag provides for new mothers. 5 stars should be awarded for that alone. it's incredibly helpful and has been literally lifesaving for many new mothers.

i had my first child a couple of weeks ago and had difficulty feeding her enough without injuring myself (she has a really strong latch and i was unable to correct it). freaking out and afraid i wouldn't be able to feed her, i called babyline as a last ditch move. the nurse on the line was really helpful and answered all my questions. i took her advice, got the tommi tippee bottles (baby loves this bottle!) and the medela pump -- this changed everything. using the pump every 3 hours as per babyline's advice helped my milk come in, and i no longer needed to supplement with formula. my baby gained such a healthy amount of weight by her 1 week appointment that her pediatrician had to do a double take, she was so impressed! my daughter is happy, healthy, and well-fed thanks fo babyline.

i highly recommend calling babyline if you have a new parent issue with your infant. it's a free service, for goodness sakes! we're lucky to have it available to us. if you don't agree with their advice, don't use their free service anymore. there are plenty of lactation consultants you can pay hourly for advice elsewhere.

nothing has changed here. same old bullshit treatment. zero stars for this place would still be an exaggeration of less than stellar service. poor service leaves you wondering why these people are always providing mediocre service. at the time of checking in, the lobby was empty, we asked about wait times and they said 11 minutes. what a sad lie that turned into.
