review:
my doctors are rock solid, i have zero complaints about my doctors. my complaint is for clerical. billing services / clerical are a joke. i have to file taxes, and as a disabled person, i have spent a lot of money with kaiser.  i have attempted to get copies of all out of pocket expenses for calendar 2019, and have received the run around at every turn. i have received incomplete information on my co pays, i still havent received pharmacy bills, and i have been re directed for premium bills. i have been attempting to collect this information since 12.30.19, and it is now 1.22.20. i filed grievances today. what is the response time on a grievance you ask? 30 days. i spend $720 a month on kaiser. that is $23.67 per day 365 days a year. kaiser has regularly tried to refer me back to the website which is strong in some ways, and very weak in others. if i go buy a printer, i could print out my co pays. i cant download and save it like people do in 2020, but i could print it if i went and bought a printer. they cant just print in the office for me. they sent me incomplete bills, they couldnt send me anything that just shows out of pocket. the website does not provide my out of pocket prescription payments even if i went and bought a printer. they failed to send me a copy of pharmacy records. the website does not provide payments made for my premiums over the year. they failed to send me a copy of the premiums i paid, and went on to tell me i need to contact a different department by phone. i filled out all of the paperwork, and explained clearly what was needed in the office on 12.30.19. when kaiser ca sales people sold me this plan, they told me that my records from kaiser hawaii to kaiser california would transfer seamlessly. they do not. i needed to fill in all of my new doctors on the info i was told they would have. i needed to get my kaiser medical records from hawaii, and give them to my california doctors so they could have my medical records. that is purely for medical records, and making sure my new doctors would have a list of ailments.  what does that mean for billing records? that means i need to go through all the same run around with kaiser hawaii since i moved to ca halfway through the year. if you are moving state to state, and you are considering sticking with kaiser for the convenience of record transfer, and the kp.org website, dont bother. their systems are not connected regardless of what they tell you at the point of sale. i am giving serious consideration to dropping kaiser at my next open enrollment. there are far cheaper options, and the whole benefit of kaiser to me was supposed to be convenience. here is what i have asked kaiser ca member services for, and cant seem to get:
1. complete neat statement of out of pocket expenses for co/pays
2: complete neat statement of out of pocket expenses for pharmacy
3: complete neat statement of out of pocket expenses for premium dues. 
i am literally asking for basic receipts, and they have terrible response time/turnaround. by the time you find out they have failed to provide information and you let them know, you need to start over at step 1. good doctors, garbage clerical system (not the people, the system), misleading sales department. i really wish i would have put all charges on one credit card so i could get my own receipts without relying on kaiser to give me a couple simple printouts. everybody i have spoken to at member services and billing was very polite, and incapable of  providing me with receipts due to the system. why cant i just look up, and save a file of this basic info on the website they so proudly use as a selling point?  what a mess.

 i am looking at the responses to the negative reviews from other customers. i have noticed that they are generic responses stating that the review will be discussed, but i dont see any that show kaiser taking any actual action. my problem is ongoing. any response that doesnt show them taking immediate action, and eludes to discussions with senior staff members is really just an example of the run around and ineffectiveness i am explaining.

i want to commend and recommend dr. sanjivan kohli. dr. kohli was the physician who oversaw my husband's treatment for four months at kindred hospital. dr. kohli embodies the best of medicine both from a with his medical expertise and his empathy towards patients and their families. i feel without dr;. kohli i would not have my husband at home with me now. he was the instrumental force in achieving the positive results and successful outcome of my husband's stay and his life during the long road to recovery. dr. kohli was always reachable and talked to me during my darkest and most fearful periods of my husbands treatment. he was extremely knowledgeable, kind, understanding and comforting. dr. kohli is the best physician and treats the whole patient as an human being of equal status to his own. he understands the medical and psychological issues that come from a serious and life threatening illness. i consider dr. kohli at godsend to us and he was the driving force in saving my husband's life and my sanity during a serious life threatening period. he is associated with uci. kindred hospital and has a private practice in south orange county. look no further for the best it is dr. kohli. i want to express my eternal gratitude to him.

review: what an amazing place. as a resident of northeast ohio we are so blessed with the amount of high quality health care that we have available for us. one of them being the world ranked rainbow babies ants children hospital. they truly are remarkable and go above and beyond to make the children comfortable and the parents comfortable. thank you rainbow babies for everything that you do.

this place is callous, to the degree that i've never experienced. i was a patient of a doctor who had prescribed me thyroid medication. she left, and i continued to get my refills from walmart. 
     unbeknowst to me, my doctor had ended the refills after a year. it makes sense, i understand that they'd want fresh blood work, but i was now high and dry without my daily medication.
     i explained how i was going to need time to find a doctor, schedule an appt., and get blood work done, and requested one more refill to tide me over, as this process would take at least a week or two, and i was scared to go that long with my daily thyroid medication. 
     they kept telling me that it was my fault, that i should've found a new doctor already, that it wasn't their problem, etc. 
     they were content to leave me high and dry, and only because the pharmacy at walmart in lisbon, took sympathy on my plight, was i able to get a 5-day supply, and had to scramble to find a doctor. 
    as a result, i have to miss a day of work, to oblige the busy doctor's schedule. 
    i wouldn't expect this type of customer service from any type of business, let alone one that is supposed to tend to peoples' health. 
    i don't write yelp reviews, i don't care about most of my consumer experiences. but if i'm able to stop one person from dealing with these sob's, my effort is warranted.

i have taken my toddler here twice and both times were great! the wait was not long and the staff was so sweet. they are very thorough and do not rush. it is nice to be able to go to find this type of experience
fac_name: HonorHealth Urgent Care - West Bell Road

review:
i was referred to honor health about 3 years ago & i will not be going back after several issues. back in may i had bronchitis, my primary doctor there wasn't available so i had to see one of the other doctors. she was very quick with our appointment & when i asked her to fill out my fmla form for work she told me my primary doctor had to fill it out (she was saying this as she was walking out the door), i asked if she was sure because my "primary" doctor was on vacation..she said yes & to make an appointment to see her when she gets back. fast forward to a week after saw my primary doctor just to have her fill out the fmla form she started questioning me like why didn't i get it filled out when i saw the other doctor last week, the other doctor was the one that's suppose to fill it out since she saw me. she made it seem like i was the one that did something wrong and i felt like she was talking down on me. she spoke to the other doctor, filled it out and told me she would not do this again for me. on top of that i got charged $80 both times when this should've been handled at the first appointment.
now at the beginning of this month i had laryngitis, lost my voice. i saw a different doctor in the same office. i asked to fill out the fmla form he told me i didn't need it all i needed was a doctor's not excusing me from work. i asked him he was positive (like 4 times) because i have no sick time & i don't want to lose my job. he said he was sure & that i wouldn't lose my job. next day i call my hr & they informed that indeed i needed the fmla form to protect myself & the doctor's note just combines my absence into 1 day! and without the form i could be considered for termination since i didn't have sick time. so i had to take the forms back to the doctors office but the doctor i saw was out for 2 days. when he did get back into the office he did fill out the form but he put the wrong date for the first day i was absent from my job, which would've been the day prior to my appointment & i even told the doctor that at my appointment & even left him a note with my fmla form when i dropped it off. this all could have been avoided if the doctor took a couple of extra minutes to fill out one form form at my appointment. i could've lost my job over this! i just feel like the doctors there are in a hurry, want to get people in & out, and overall don't actually take care of the patients needs. on top of the front desk nurses have no customer service, i think there's only one there that actually smiles, has a pleasant tone and is welcoming. after all this i will be searching for a new doctors office.
fac_name: HonorHealth Urgent Care - West Bell Road

review: dr. duke you would be so disappointed in how your hospitals have become and the lack or patient care. i on more than one occasion saw you fire people over lack of care and complaints. half of this er would and should be fired tonight! it should not have taking me making 3 calls to the hospital administrator to get a basic answer. then the er staff gets pissed because i called him and they were written up. i tried for 4 hours to get answers!!! it was not until they got their hands slapped they decided to check on patients instead of sitting at the nurses station clearly and loudly joking and playing while patients were being neglected!
fac_name: Memorial Hermann The Woodlands Medical Center

review: this hospital is amazing! every time i've had to come here, i'm treated with kindness and respect from the doctors and nurses. this goes for the er and the maternity ward. i had my son here two years ago and felt so relieved at how comfortable the nurses made me feel. i should have written this two years ago. one nurse stood out because she sat and talked with me as if i were her friend. her name was alice. thank you to her! also, the head of the maternity department at the time, billie. you guys were just all so friendly! i have a reoccurring condition which, unfortunately, means i have to make several visits to the er here. every time the staff has been extremely kind and made me feel at ease. i absolutely love this hospital!

both of my labors there were horrible. both times i asked for an epidural and both times they refused to check me until it was too late. 

more recently my 2 month old swallowed bath water and we rushed her to the er and they barely checked her out because we don't have insurance. the next night we took her in because she was wheezing, congested, bad cough, and her oxygen levels were low. and once again they did almost nothing because we don't have insurance. the next day i took her to her doctor and found out she has bronchiolitis. now she's on 3 different medications. they could've killed my baby. this place is horrible.

i cannot believe how messy and unprofessional this place is. we checked into the er around 11:40pm today (1/25/2020) and it's now 2:00am . honestly we could of been done and out of here since an hour ago.. but the nurse and the doctor did not communicate with each other so we sat here waiting for discharge papers. when i finally went out to ask (twice) .. she had the nerves to tell me.. no one informed her of anything. what?!!!! so this whole time.. why didn't they follow up with each other... omg. i'm just so annoyed. and on top of that everyone here got attitudes today. no friendly vibe. i feel so uncomfortable when trying to seek for help... this is unacceptable.

i have to give the labor and delivery team and postpartum nurses 5 stars. i had my son there in august and my daughter had my grandbaby there in october. although it took my daughter 50 hours in labor they took really good care of her. sy was one of my nurses and she was awesome. i really liked everything about that hospital because they're labor and delivery isnt busy like other hospitals and they actually get to know their patients which is great. if i were to ever have another baby i would go back there. thank you to all the ladies in labor and delivery and postpartum for making mine and my daughter's experience great!

my experience started out positive.  pre-op prosedures ,ekg, blood work, and staff were wonderful.  my bariatric surgery went good but then staff forgot to notify my husband that i was in recovery already 2 hrs. my surgery was scheduled as was another lady and yet they didn't have beds for us up stairs. we remained in recovery from noon until 7:30!  my stay was overnight only and yet not once did anyone have me do the breath machine or get me up to walk.  i had assistance once to go to the bathroom and after that i unplugged my machines and took myself not once but 4 times to the bathroom. no one instructed me on proper drinking amounts that were so important.  i'll never return.

this was a very pleasant visit walking into the doors. passed all of the heartache that came with the visit, the staff was very accommodating and took care of our loved one with the utmost respect. thank you guys!

i have been here twice and the first time
with my daughter for a broken arm and the service at the er was pretty good and welcoming. unfortunately the billing department lacked knowledge. i have receiving bills for that day from various different companies. i am new here and have not experienced this before. i have been with my kids to other hospitals and all i pay is my co-pay and they never sent me anything after that. this is 3 months later and i still have call these people to ask why my insurance was not charged, and they tell me that they didn't receive my insurance information for the er. as i have mentioned earlier i have recently moved here and i have always considered the services and people here in manteca to be better than those in the bay area. it is really unfortunate that i have experienced this and hope that they figure out a better way to handle their financials better so that people who visit the er don't have to deal with calling these companies but focus on healing.

had a dislocated shoulder. they were very professional and fix my shoulder very quickly. they sedated me which made the setting of my shoulder much easier the staff was excellent doctor was very professional. was there for about  2 hours.

horrible wait times and they have made several medical errors several times to several of my family members.

if you have a choice to go elsewhere?

go elsewhere.

as long as they don't "need the bed" you might be fine. it's absolutely ridiculous that they would discharge us with my daughters urine being completely red with blood. they couldn't get an iv in, and when they finally were able to get an iv in her upper arm (with the  help of ultrasound) then they claimed that  the iv antibiotics  wouldn't "go in", even though they were able to flush with saline and get a blood draw.  no follow thru to determine if she had kidney stones or anything else.  then she was literally told by a nurse that "she had already been there too long and they needed the bed".  hmmm...maybe because she has medi-cal?? if you really want competent care go to french hospital. shameful.

the nurses and doctors in the labor and delivery department are down right amazing, the care and compassion they provided was second to none. when complications arose they were phenomenal both with the mother and myself, if you are deciding where to deliver your child this is the place, hands down.

communications are terrible. the surgical orders from the doctor were out in the computer system wrong in two separate occasions. following the procedure my wife was placed in a 4 person room in the med sure department. the staff support was terrible. one nurse assistant assisted my wife to a restroom and then left her there. another time my wife called for assistance to get to the restroom and nobody ever showed up. a nurse named shane came into the room at 2:00 am and proceeded to talk to another patient in his outside voice. then at 3:00 am my wife had to call the nurse for a third patient in her room who was yelling for help with no assistance for around 15-20 minutes. then at 4:30 am they decided they needed to draw blood from my wife for reasons unbeknownst to her doctor. we are currently waiting for 2 hours for discharge paperwork to be "located" terrible customer service and support.

my mother was admitted here for hospice care.  a nurse named jamie overdosed my mother on morphine not once but twice.  instead of 2.5 ml she gave her 100 ml.  my mother was never responsive again.  my mother had heavy breathing and lots of mucous and her blood pressure dropped.  this woman made my mother suffer. this nurse told us my mother was showing signs of imminent death and to prepare ourselves.  nurses started rushing in and we thought it was the end.  after checking her they told us about the overdose.  this facility caused so much pain and torture during an already sad situation.  when this was caught they didn't even send the nurse home they let her finish her shift and we had to see her every time we left the room. they caught the error at shift change when the evening nurse was coming in.  my mom passed two days after this.  even after she passed there was someone from house keeping banging on the door arguing with us to come in and get the trash bin.  then 3 people came in to clean her, change her and reposition her.  we had to explain she passed though a nurse already came in to pronounce her.  there is no communication at this facility and they only showed some care and concern when i alerted them i filed a report with the state department of health.  we felt they were just trying to cover themselves and weren't truly sorry.  we were told the hospital would have given her more morphine then us.  trying to justify it.  they kept coming in with food trays to feed my mom who was unresponsive.  again lack of communication and just staff not all on the same page.  the day this happened we asked for administration to come in.  we were told well it's the weekend and people have plans set up and we're trying.  when i mentioned getting an attorney that is when they got the ball rolling with people coming in to explain how this could have happened.  they said they didn't know if it was deliberate or human error.  but would investigate so they can prevent this from happening again.  absolutely horrible situation and i feel so sorry for sending my mother to this facility in her last days of life.

the staff here is more than amazing. i had a procedure done on 04/2019 and i was quite nervous about the process and it wasn't cheap, but from the moment i arrived the payment process, the actual procedure everyone was extremely attentive and genuinely concerned. sometimes you can tell in the medical field when people don't really care but that is not the case here! thank you to all who helped me during my time of need! if i need anything else that can be done here, this will be my first choice hands down!
fac_name: Methodist Ambulatory Surgery Center - North Central

review: i would give give dr khoury 0 stars if i could. i read all the reviews prior to meeting with dr khoury and they seem to be 50/50. unfortunately, my experience with dr khoury was appalling, he is the worst dr i've ever met in my life. i had a late second trimester loss and he was very cold, showed no compassion and lacked bedside manner. he refused to see me as a patient due to the high risk of any subsequent pregnancies even though he is a high risk dr!) his treatment plans are "his way or the highway." i would not recommend him, there are plenty of other high-risk drs in the area that are empathetic, compassionate and caring.

excellent, attentive, caring staff. i had full tracheostomy and was in critical condition after an accident. vibra kept me positive and helped me recover nicely. cheers to all staff at vibra, i can never repay you for your kindness and appreciate you so much!

the staff was great. service was great. administration is horrible. billing is not following the laws. after they submit the claim to insurance and in return receive request for supporting documentation, they do not respond and provide this paperwork. instead, they sell the bill to a debt collector. this is despicable, especially for an organization pretending to be faith based. make sure to report them to the department of insurance and bbb for fraud.
they are very slow with the process of doing things compared to other hospitals.. plus why is it texsan? i'm confused.. if you're trying to combine texas and san antonio that's weird

the worst hospital!! horrible rude ass nurses that don't know what the fuck they're doing. nurse abby and nurse assistant michelle felt bothered when we arrived late afternoon. we felt like an incovenience to them. nurse abby said it herself in her thick heavy accent "nobody sent me a report this is ridiculous". they can't even tell you what the medications are for. nurse chika just hands you a cup with 10 pills and says with her thick heavy accent "most of them are for blood pressure". got mad at my brother for asking her why so many pills. told him who was he to question her. we we're kicked out on nye by a "nurse supervisor" by the name lola, very ghetto btw and unprofessional. told us "uhh this too many kids up in hea yall got 60 seconds to get up outta hea.the day before my loved one got discharged nurse elizabeth poked an iv canula on the hand and caused my loved one excrutiating pain. the line was even leaking blood!! but tried to clean it and kept tugging on it causing more pain. im not a dr, but nurse elizabeth doesn't know how to poke!! all she said was "im gonna poke you huhhhhh" sounded like an indian ritual. not the way you help a patient brace themselves before a poke. nurse supervisor chuck comes in and dismisses the pain my loved one was in. said he would document the request for removal of iv. this place is a fucking joke. do your research before accepting your loved one to be transitioned here. i read so many bad reviews online/social media and dind't think it would be that  bad. these people are here for a paycheck, they give two shits about the patient. no wonder locations have been shutting down. i pray to god this location is next. this hospital is a fucking joke

i went to this er on monday . and i have nothing negative to say about any of it. i got in a room within 10 minutes after getting checked in up front . they found out why i was in so much pain and also told me a few other things that i didn't know was also affecting my health . so i give them 5 and the pa i saw that afternoon amy she was awesome and very sweet and caring and she also personally called me and told me about another concern . so i thank them all so much for getting me back on the right track!!

i have lived in 7 different states and have been to hospitals in all states. this is the worst hospital possible. terrible care, 8 hours of waiting for one iv and 30 minutes of care added up together in those 8 hours. this is not the first time. i hate that this is the closest hospital. next one is 2 hours away. i hate this place, i hate this place. i'm pregnant and my clinic wants me to have my baby here -not happening over my dead body. 

do not go to allen fletcher hospital this place is disgusting with their money and no care whatsoever.

from my first interaction with the reception area,to the person who wheeled me out the door, i received kind,warm,caring and professional attention.
the past reputation of this hospital caused me to hesitate to utilize its services over the years. recently my doctor, who is associate with hospital, felt i needed a procedure done and i acquiesced to have it at emerson.

i sensed these nurses enjoy their job and enjoy working with each other and the feeling trickles down to the patients and makes it a much more pleasant experience.

when i called a few days later about a few concerns,i received the same amount of caring and friendliness, which impressed me.
i now speak,after personal experience,highly,about the medical care and emerson hospital.

review:

i understand being skeptical when you're an expert and someone's coming in with their own information, but the absolute contempt shown to me by the staff there was outrageous. of the 8 nurses/pas that i had contact with 3 of them were kind and sympathetic to the fact that i didn't feel well and came in with some of my own research/information.

fac_name: Legacy Good Samaritan Hospital & Medical Center

review:
i have been going to the callahan eye foundation for over thirty years.  i had a detached retina while i was in my twenties and have been a regular patient ever since.

pro: this is a cutting-edge (no pun intended) research hospital for eye research.  this is where uab trains its eye doctors.  here, you will get top notch physicians and staff who are among the best in the world.

pro:  eye trauma emergency room.  if someone you know gets an eye injury from an accident, go here.  24/7/365 someone is available in their er to treat an eye injury or problem.  if they need to call in a doc for a surgery or second opinion, there are specialists in that same building.

con:  the parking deck is a nightmare, especially for visually impaired drivers.  awful, just awful.  i wish uab would move the eye foundation to the highlands campus just because the parking is so much better.

overall, if you have an eye issue -- retina, cataract, vision problems because of diabetes, any eye related health issue -- this is the world class hospital where you need to be.

nobody is paying attention. spending so much time talking to each other, they forget the patient is right next to them. nobody uses their "inside voice". while trying to move me with a broken hip, two people were flirting like it was a singles joint. was asked by 3 people to go over my meds list but nobody bothered to order the drugs to give me before bed.  the staff appears to be running on industrial strength caffeine and are rushing about without any focus. when i asked a doctor whom i had never met to speak up a bit since i am hard of hearing, he told me he was tired and had been working for 12 days straight. he went on to say he was  speaking low since he was exhausted and it was obvious he was annoyed by my simple request. if i could be at any other facility right now, i would go in a heartbeat. the staff needs some training in decorum and manners and maybe some yoga to relieve the mania.
address: 2100 SE Salerno Rd  Martin Health System

review:
ut southwestern dallas- great doctors terrible billing.  we have outstanding health insurance.  ut's billing department should be removed/fired as they are extremely incompetent in their billing practices. i have received bills that are well over a year old.  they are a joke in my opinion almost criminal in their billing practices.  the way they bill you often months later in a helter skelter fashion is pathetic.  i have plenty of $$$ but dealing with ut requires a full time cpa.   baylor does not demonstrate such extreme incompetence.  suggestion- fire the director over medical billing.  then fire two board members for not firing the medical billing director sooner.  i believe a class action lawsuit should be launched against ut southwestern medicals billing practices.  

best option is to use baylor dallas.  free publicity rocks. the truth is out there.   fire ut  in my educated option they are definitely "wallet rapists"
fac_name: UT Southwestern University Hospital St Paul

review: had a good experience this time. thanks to the expresscare staff for expediting my visit so that i could make it to the pharmacy before they closed. the desk staff, nurse, and np were all efficient in addressing my immediate needs.

amazing hospital, amazing staff
very compassionate care here
neurosurgeons dr. s. murthy, and chief of neurology dr. richard johnson performed surgery on a herniated disc in neck for my son.  
not only are they experts, they took time to explain everything to us, and followed up quickly after surgery.

thanks to everyone who took such good care of us

aa

sat in the emergency room over 7 hours with my daughter who had a fever. her private doctor sent us (we were not a walk-in). right away they told me it was a virus. but it took them 7 hours to get a doctor, do the bloodwork, put in the saline, while all around us the emergency room emptied out. i guess if you're not truly an emergency you sit and wait and wait (but there's no one else here!) i can't help but feel like i am being suckered. if she wasn't sick when we came out, she'll probably be sick by the time we leave.

it's a small hospital i'm told, only 275 beds. not sure what kind of a heart hospital it is but the emergency room is run like a one-room schoolhouse.  northwell is just 10 minutes away. i'd go there.

my mom was brought to st. francis after having intermittent chest and left arm pain despite her ekg coming back clear. she did not have to wait long from coming in by ambulance to start receiving care. immediately her information was taken as well as her vitals. within 5 minutes, she was in a room in the er. once in a room, her blood was drawn and she was kept informed about what the status was. she was very hungry(and the cafeteria was closed) and a nurse brought her a sandwich. she was admitted and within a few hours was in a room(much better than if we had gone to northwell).

once in a room, her nurse took her information and explained how things would go. a nurse came a few hours later to draw blood and get more detailed information. all of the nursing staff(as well as the pca's) were excellent and call button time response was excellent. the night nurses(which is when i was there) were all excellent. asking if i needed anything. the communication between me and the nurses was excellent. the board was always up-to-date with your nurse and pca's names as well as if you were having a procedure that day when you could have your next dose of pain meds as well as your estimated discharge date. 

for a hospital, the food was very good(even having a guest tray for $15). to get your food, you dial 5555 and order from the menu. that is nice because the food only comes when you are hungry(during meal hours) and doesn't just show up when you could be sleeping or not want it. if you miss a meal, they will call you to see if you want to order food. if you haven't ordered dinner, they will call before the end of dinner(6:30) to see if you want anything.

a sister came to visit my mom(when i wasn't there). she asked if my mom had any visitors and my mom felt had she said no, she would have stayed and spent some time with her.

south bay cardiology in west islip is a part of saint francis. their incompetence is surpassed only by their greed. don't use these "doctors" under any circumstances. their only mission is to bankrupt you.

avoid this hospital at all cost.  they are extremely disorganized. my father went for chest pain and their incompetence was evident immediately.  no doctors to be found.  the place ya run by pas.  cardiologist saw him hours later. mind you he was taken by ambulance for chest pain.  we can't even get our medical records from them. avoid at all cost especially for heart related issues.  don't buy that they are a heeled hospital.  it's all marketing.

ive going here for my prenatal care over the last few months. being african american we knew the statistics with childbirth in regards to death rates being much higher and wanted nothing but the best for our unborn child. we did research and read tons of review on hennepin healthcare. the reviews were not   the best and definitely hightened our concerns.  the midwife care we received was pretty good. we had a really great midwife who was able to listen to our concerns. 

my biggest problem was with the nurses. i needed some paperwork completed for my job. the nurse that saw me expressed her disapproval with needeing this paperwork completed at this stage of my pregnancy. it felt that she was downplaying some serious symptoms that i was experiencing.  this type of attitude is a huge reason why you have to be your best advocate.  we decided to change our healthcare providers.

the front desk was very helpful and upbeat. 
the best medical assistants i've met so far and for as young as i am i've met a lot, not by choice.
if i had to chose any place it would be honor health arcadia 100 because of wondeful people  like theirs.

i called this hospital and had questions because i didn't know how insurance companies work. it was a female who answered the phone and was very rude to me, and i decided to hang up because of how rude she was to me i had questions that i wanted to know, and she was making me feel like i was dumb for not knowing the answers. i thought that the people that worked in hospitals wanted to help people for both physical and mental health. 3:16 pm today. shame on you

my daughter was treated and really not tested properly for stomach pain. i was working with her insurance and trying to apply for charity care last call was february 8 updating them about the situation and when i called them yesterday february 21 i was told my case was transferred to collections. how do you send someone to collections if you just resend them the charity application because the 1st one was missing information.  ?? worst experience i had so far.

horrible attention!!! my appendix almost burst while they had me sitting in the lobby waiting for assistance. i begged the lady from there to please get me medical assistance and they gave me attitude! my friend took me out of there to st. mary's hospital in hoboken and i where i received medical assistance and had surgery.

my dad was sent to encompass after suffering a heart attack and stroke.  i want to complement the staff there on taking great care of him! first let me say that one of his nurses, orlinda is the most caring and helpful lady i've ever met in any of these places. from dr yang, occupational therapist thad, speech therapists miriam and samantha, case worker sherri,  to mike at the front desk, everyone we came in contact with was super warm, friendly, and helpful. the facility is clean and well maintained and i would definitely recommend encompass to anyone who's loved one needs short here rehab. thank you encompass team!

my particular horror story happened on a saturday morning when i began feeling a crippling, agonizing and debilitating pain in my abdomen, getting worse and worse. unable to move and barely able to stay conscious, i called 911 and an ambulance took me to the nearest hospital -- king's county. 

i was wheeled into the er on a gurney, crying and screaming in agony. after several minutes, someone asked for my insurance card. thinking that i was about to die, i cried and used profanity to plead for help. she said she didn't like my language and simply walked away.

i lay there, crying in agony and fearful that i was on death's door. i thrashed on my gurney, pleading for help. a full hour went by as i cried and pleaded for help, while the staff all around completely ignored me. i listened through my pain as they gossiped, engaged in long discussions about what they would have for lunch, and as they answered phones from people in distress and then joked about how "stupid" the callers were. after an hour a doctor happened to walk by. i reached out for him, pleading for help. he took one look at me and shouted at the staff that i should be a priority patient. 

i lay in the lobby for another 20 minutes, feet away from the open door in the middle of winter. 

finally i was wheeled into the hospital by a staff member who slammed my gurney into each and every door and wall, furthering the worst agony i had ever experienced. he ignored me, stopping to have a casual chat with another staffer about the upcoming super bowl. he then wheeled me into the middle of a busy hallway in the er, locked the wheels of the gurney, and left me there. for the next half hour, countless people bumped into me as my cries for help went unanswered. after vomiting several times, the pain became so unbearable that i lost consciousness. 

i woke up to a woman asking for my insurance again. i begged her for help, and she just walked away. 30 minutes later a friendly doctor (the only positive part of this experience) briefly examined me in the hallway (where privacy was nonexistent) and said they needed to run tests. after an endless wait, a horrendously mean nurse withdrew 5 vials of blood from my arm (i was later told this was a mistake and they only needed 2, so the others were disposed of). she hooked me up to an iv, left a bunch of literal garbage (wrappers and packaging from needles, etc) on top of me, and left. for 2 hours, no one would acknowledge my presence as i cried in pain. my questions went unanswered. it had been hours since i had anything to drink or gone to the bathroom, and with an empty iv bag connected to my arm, i was literally trapped on the bed, unable to move. 

i asked everyone who walked past (or rather, everyone who bumped into me) but i was ignored. occasionally, a nurse or staff member would walk by and treat me with about as much respect as they would give a stray animal. the staff here have no business dealing with patients, let alone other human beings. interacting with them was undoubtedly the single most dehumanizing experience of my entire life. 

after hours of this agony, of being ignored, of being literally denied the ability the use the bathroom or access to water, i told a staff member that i was on the verge of calling the police to report that i was being held captive against my will and tortured. this got their attention. the doctor came back, surprised that no one had spoken to me, surprised that i had been tied to this bed for so long, and very surprised that the nurse dumped her garbage on top of my lap. she ordered more tests and unhooked my iv. i waited 17 minutes to use the only available bathroom, peed into a cup, and held onto the urine for another 30 minutes until someone took it. after another endless wait, she came back to say she thought i had a kidney stone and suggesting i get a ct scan. well i finally got that scan, but they didn't bother to walk me back to my bed so i got lost, wandering the sprawling hospital halls... 

after a full day of being abused, abandoned, restrained, ignored, and borderline tortured, i wad diagnosed with a kidney stone, given a prescription to pick up from a pharmacy that had already closed, and sent on my way. look, no er is a fun place, and i understand that this one is working under exceptionally difficult circumstances out of their control. but there is simply no justification for what i experienced. i once visited a hospital in an impoverished, rural community in china, and the people there were treated with infinitely more respect and dignity. king's county er resembles a hospital from a post-apocalyptic zombie movie. but in a world without zombies, there is simply no excuse. shame on them. shame! you've been warned.
