this review is for the er. i went in because i had the most excruciating stabbing headache. i had surgery here a week ago and my discharge papers said to go back to this hospital if i had complications. i went back, the two front girls that were signing me in were too busy talking to each other. then once i was called in the guy taking my vitals, older, really tall man, white hair, was rude! he literally made me feel bad for going to er for just a headache. he then got a text message and took this phone out in front of me, stopped doing his job and just started texting ! i can't imagine what they do when patients aren't around if that's how he acted. i was like hmm maybe it's just the people in the front that were off. nope then once i went in, the nurse( don't remember her name but blonde, and had a really bad orange tan) asked me my pain range, i said 10, she then said seriously 10, like the worst? i said yes this is the worst headache in my life!!!! i can barely open my eyes, or walk, why would i come in here for something non emergency. she then said okay i'll give you some medicine for the headache? i asked if she will do any testing or ct scan, she said no it's way too much radiation for something non emergency. so what does it take?????  me to flatline????? anyways, i ended up checking out because i heard her go back and tell the other nurses " i have a headache too" and they all laughed. wow just wow: i then asked to be discharged, i didn't tell them why because i already felt like a laughing stock. i never imagined going to seek care and feeling like crud because of people who's job is to care and help.!!! they literally talked about a patient in front of others! i should've read the reviews before i came in!!! anaheim global fix your staff to have some bedside manner !!! listen to your patients and reviews!!!! never coming here again!!! wouldn't even bring my worst enemy here !!!

nurses were turning around and gossiping about patients with mental health disorders security guards standing around not doing anything front desk staff was absolutely deplorable i am definitely filing a medical with the medical board of the state of california on this hospital

this review is for the er, specifically for the nurse named malinory or something like that from last nights shift. you shouldn't become a nurse for money, you should do it because you love helping and caring for people who are in pain and need. i've never felt so ignored by a nurse in my life then last night. why do i have to ask to go to the restroom 3 times before i could go? and when asked where it was she replied "where it is". does it look like i know where the room i was put it  is at and where the restroom is from there? very very rude nurse. acted like she didn't know anything when i asked. after waiting and waiting and nothing, i asked to be released. it took more then 30 mins after asking her to just release me so she could come with the clipboard and make me sign. i was reading and she kept saying sign here and i told her i'm reading what i'm signing. she just stood there then. why did i have to be flagging her down every 5 mins to come give me the paperwork. she would acknowledge me with just a nod when she saw me out of bed and keep sitting down. she told me i would see the dr. before leaving but that never happened. she just kept me there to ignore me more. wasted hours here. never again going to this hospital or recommending this hospital to anyone. if you want medical attention don't waste your time here.

this review is specifically for l&d. i was visiting a family member who was going into labor at night time. there were a couple of older nurses who were extremely unprofessional and lazy. just standing around gossiping. at some point during the night, one fell asleep at the desk and another came back from outside reeking of cigarettes. there are pregnant mothers and newborns around, come on.. management needs to do something about these unprofessional nurses.

this hospital has helped a loved one more than words can imagine. they saved his life on many occasions.  many thanks to the lady i met there who is by far superior in nursing betty on 6b and hannah.  many thanks especially to housekeeping they have who is simply the best on floor 4b when our loved one was down there.
dr. jalal was so helpful, and dr. joseph o'gorman,  do.
words cannot express gratitude in this condition.

i would rather die than go back to the emergency room here. not one bad experience but two! er staff has no compassion of patience, the blankets are always dirty. they need to fire everyone and start fresh

good medical care, probably the worst customer service in the industry. we were making regular payments on a successful procedure performed at memorial, but they turned us over to a collection agency anyway. they will be several months sending out a bill and then if you don't pay it off immediately they turn you over to a collection agency. when my father was ill they actually wanted a quarter of a million dollar lump sum payment upfront. there is no defending their business practices

it's a shame this is the only hospital in carthage. not happy with it at all. will drive to freeman in joplin from now on. i had a massive blood blot in my leg, couldn't walk, couldn't bend it. they gave me a shot to start blood thinning and a percocet that did nothing for pain. if i go to an er it's because i cant take it any longer. i hate hospitals and will likely just stay home next time. i guess addicts are making drs so scared to treat patients they'll send ya back out in the same condition you arrived. makes it pointless to even go to a dr anymore. when ask why not was given for pain he said the dea told him they'd rather 1000 people od on heroin than one person on pain meds. people aren't dying from prescribed pain meds. they're dying from meds not prescribed and fentanyl. but that's the american way, make everyone pay the price because the dea cant stop the bad stuff so they stop it all.

this er is absolutely rude. they are not helpful at all. there is an employee by the name of kent who is probably the rudest person i have ever encountered. i called to complain on him and nothing. of course he is protected. i will not send my people back to this mercy until he is gone. poor care, they don't even know their own policies and they have no idea about the hipaa laws. not a clue. but trust me, kent knows everything! he refuses to send information even with a release signed. i was talked to like i was a child and hung up on. deal with someone else when you go to the er. he is horrible to deal with.

these people don't even deserve the 1-star i have to give them! my child who is in lubbock going to school at tech went to this emergency room twice in one week with gastric distress. the 1st time they threw antibiotics at her but in the same sentence told her she just had a virus. the 2nd time (one week later) she returned with the same symptoms but they were much much worse. the dr. entered her room with a finance person and stated 'this is not an emergency' and he wouldn't treat her until she handed over her credit card and paid $200. the dr. gave her more bogus meds. 12 hours later she was admitted to umc for five days!! so much for not being an emergency. 

and to come at a 21 year old kid demanding money who is very sick and has great insurance that does not require a co-pay is a jerk move. save yourself and go somewhere else. i'm so angry i want to scratch all their eyes out.

very happy with the care i've had and continue to receive at norton brownsboro. in september i was there for brain surgery, performed by dr. sun. it was a success. i love having my follow up appointments at the cancer center on mondays because the hospital has tomato soup and grilled cheese that day. 

i'm telling you right now it's the best tomato soup in the city! creamy with tomato chunks. as for the sandwiches you get your choice. i always get the alabama slammer, minus the jalapeños. chicken, gouda, sautéed onions, and a creamy bbq sauce. so good!!! a nice meal for 7 dollars. can't beat it!!!

lots of new construction going on, probably contributed to the problems below. personnel issues and privacy issues need to be corrected.

the good: some really great doctors do their thing here. super nurses/staff in the orthopedic surgery ward - before, during and after. second floor nurses were truly exceptional.  the medical staff can and does take minor issues in stride and takes action to make things right. a newer facility. the hospitals food is good, not great but good - i ate everything i could and would have eaten more if it was available (and i didn't even try the jello). you can get your prescriptions filled and brought down to you, and they make sure you have everything you need before you leave.

the bad: they don't have enough regular rooms for their post-op overnights. they have converted exam/prep rooms - bed, sink, tv, and equipment; i also had a door with a large window looking down the hallway. shared bathroom (multiple rooms) has toilet and sink. the rooms work, i was only in there for 24 hours after surgery. they are expanding to meet demand. parking is also insufficient, however costco parking in close by for overflow.

the ugly: early (before 7am) registration. one person checking me was plainly unhappy to be working, directed me to another building (i was right she was not), and was rude. they escort you to an elevator 20 feet away to a desk 10 feet out of the elevator on the 2nd floor. the patient advocate, located in an open space on the second floor, discusses medical information related to the planned surgery (hippa violation) in front of everyone waiting to talk to her before going in to surgery.

i have had several procedures at brownsboro   i have some very specific medical issues and they have always worked with me. i  can't say enough about how well the staff worked with me to keep my  conditionn as stable as possible. from the receptionists, nurses, anesthesiologists, and physicians they all worked with me and my family and made me a part of the team instead of a patient with a number. i'd like to hand out kudos to everyone there. thank you all for taking such good care of me and getting me home by the afternoon. this has been the  shortest procedure stay i have had in a very long time! 
thank you'

a children's hospital?  their priority is computer and paper forms. we have been here for over an hour with a twoweek old to repeat some blood test from the hospital. what about limiting risk?  even worse there was no other choice almost no patients... where is there staff? sad

can i give this er zero stars?  three plus hours with my husband in the waiting room.  we were just getting ready to leave and go to another hospital when his name was finallly called.  he then spends 11 more hours until he gets a bed.  ultimately spends 5 days in icu and 7days total in hospital.  they almost kill him treating the first problem.  no attorney wants the case since he lived....  i would not take any of my dogs here.
fac_name: CHRISTUS Spohn Hospital Corpus Christi - Shoreline

review: the wait time to get admitted is horrendous. we waited 6 hours to get a room.  the volunteers, nurses, & dr's are extremely nice, however, some of the security guards are extremely rude and can't even say hello or crack a smile, which is unacceptable. the rooms do not have blackout curtains, so if your child is used to sleeping in the dark, good luck as it is a challenge and naps are impossible in these rooms. definitely prefer going to the cm in op, ks.

veterans beware !!!

i am a veteran  and prisma health or whatever they are calling themselves today does not honor veterans.

i've had three procedures done by prisma health referred by the veterans health admin and each time prisma has tried to bill me when the va was clearly responsible for the charges. once i received a bill a year later after the procedure was performed. each time i've had to prove to them that the va was responsible for the bill when my procedure was  approved and prisma notified by the va before any appointment was even set up. the accounting dept of prisma has no clue or maybe they do, maybe this is normal procedure to only scam and try to get more money from patients. i would not be surprised if billing was at both ends. surprise billing and ignoring the va seems to be the norm at prisma health. this hospital is just a huge corporate profit enterprise who does not care about patients.

strep throat is no fun, especially when you develop a large and painfully swollen bump on your neck/jaw line. and when it's one of your littles whom is experi coming these symptoms, it sucks even more. i'd like to thank the staff over at peyton manning's children hospital for being so great, pleasant to work with, and very sweet to my daughter during our er visit. the hospital is no fun, but after many hospital visits over the last few years i'm starting to notice the cleaner and more better equipped hospitals. if you need to take a minor to the hospital i highly recommend peyton manning's children hospital. having been to the other children's hospital in the area many times and having many issues with their staff, i can safely now only recommend this local children's hospital. way to go peyton manning's children's hospital! thank you for having a medical facility where parents can actually trust the medical staff on board is giving your kids the best medical treatment available to them. did i mention it's also a teaching hospital? even their students are very well spoken. thank you!
fac_name: Peyton Manning Children's Hospital at St. Vincent

review:
whatever you do, dont go to this hospital. the doctors are clueless. last 2 times i was there were for emergencys in the middle of the night. the first time after 8 hours we were sent home, drove straight to morristown and the had my daughter diagnosed in 1 hour. this time after 14 hours we were released with some joke of diagnosis. went to overlook and they had it figured out in 1 1/2 hours.
dont waste your time here

came in with left arm pain, waited a entire hour for ekg , then another hour. spoke to triage nurse, just to tell me that they still have patients before my nana. which is 84 years old with signs of a stoke. never in my life have i seen such poor care! to top it off they asked for the copayment as soon as we got in the room. just sad.
fac_name: Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital - Hamilton

review:
my last trip to erlanger was short, but was memorable.

i work at a hotel and one of our staff members fell and needed to be taken to the er so we used our shuttle and i took her. kellie the valet over at the emergency room was a perfect example of what a valet should do to go above and beyond the job requirements. she assisted with getting a wheelchair for our staff member so she didn't have to walk, she didn't mention my shuttle being in the way (which it very much was) and she did it all with a smile on her face.

from one valet to another. thank you if you see this kellie. i will definitely be using that trip to the er as an example on training people at my hotel.

peyton rose allison wright and christina went above and beyond helping me and my 82 year old mother. the valet service has the best employees. friendly, competent and courteous. they made my mother smile before she went in for her surgery which lightened the mood. thank you!!@

we chose to use the valet services at the emergency room as we were rushing to get inside, the valet attendant katie was extremely helpful and seemed to genuinely care about taking care of us. she was very polite, thanks katie!

kelsey hoskins ran in the rain to get our car from erlanger children's as valet. she was so sweet and awesome! a smile goes far. thanks, kelsey. we appreciate your work today especially with the rain.

my sister had her baby at this hospital. the stay was from sunday- should be wednesday. i was there on monday. 
this hospital is breath taking from the street view. beautiful lights, fountain and a nice parking lot. you walk through the door and automatically you are stopped to get you id scanned and a visitor badge. i really loved this part! safety is number one especially by the labor and deliver department. 
the nursing staff was absolutely amazing! my favorite nurse was the wonderful beautiful intelligent aussie   bernie. she was open and took the time to explain everything as well as answer every question we had (which was a lot). the pediatrician was extremely sweet i feel bad bc i didn't get her name but she has blue end in her hair. dr. young was quick and responsive. it seemed like everything went smoothly. 
the only down side is that it seems this hospital spent majority of their funds on the façade of the building. the rooms and the beds need to be updated! 
other than that it was a great experience.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review:
hi mom has been in and out of the hospital recently , her primary care doctor is dr nelson at highland but she is in the process of finding a new doctor and a new insurance, county or state medical
benefits give us  nothing  good to choose from because the whole system is corrupt as fuck.  this building is nice but i liked it better when it was just eden not
sutter, they are too busy and understaffed at this hospital, the rooms
are nice and roomie, it's  welcoming, thier  communication skills leave a lot to be sesired
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review:
i wasn't going to write a review. but i wanted to tell you guys regarding my experience at icu eden medical center.

my father was hit by a car. was admitted for severe brain trauma. i'm thankful that eden took my father in and that the neuro / trauma doctors did the surgery to release the pressure from his brain. the specialist doctors were awesome. there was a few nurses that were wonderful in taking care of my father. but some of them would make really bold remarks. yes, i do know my father is in a coma and might never wake up. but the way one of the nurses said it was not a good. they would make comments when they thought me or my siblings were asleep "i heard that we done everything and there's nothing more we can do" that to me sounds like you are giving up on my father and even if you done everything you keep on trying. the nurses who cared and they didn't treat my father like "i'm just doing this because is my job" would ask me how my father was. what would he be doing right now? what were his days like? i work in the medical field. but this was just disappointed. we already have mix emotions and to top it off with the remarks some of the nurses would make. it was totally uncalled for. 

also dr. ghandi would talk to us about if it was her "very spiritual" and if my father knew in the state he probably wouldn't want to live this way. i fell like she wanted us to take my dad off the ventilator. i hope am wrong. but either way it was to soon to have that conversation. it was barely a week and half from the severe brain injury and she wanted to have this conversations. 

thank you to the case manager. they were very helpful. help us with work letters and if we approve or deny certain things. they also help us in transferring my father as soon my father was okay to be transferred. 
the security staff were friendly.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: every time when you coming to emergency they just spending your time the nurse is going to the break you are thinking someone will become somebody come no one is coming to helping you every time you have spent five hours in the emergency room the doctor will be show after 4 hr this is the very best emergency in the area
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: went into the emergency room to see my little sister after her requesting to only see me when she was in the ambulance. arrived at the er after a 45 minute drive to wait an additional 1 hour and 40 minutes to be told i could not see her. this is the worst hospital ever and i can't even see my little sister. security and nurse were terrible!
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: wait time was not too long and it was very fast compared to other hospitals the nurses were amazing i felt safe and cared for.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: terrible! all the people that work in the emergency need a better attitude!  they tried the wrong family! i promise you , if i ever end up coming back, make sure the workers have a better day. we all have bad days but if you know this is your field of work, make sure you have a better attitude before somebody get slapped!
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: i've been hospitalized once here and visited urgent care twice. my hospitalization was very comfortable thanks to the outstanding team they have there, no complaints. the cook even visited patients to see if they want something off menu. the urgent care visits had very little waiting time and both times my problems were quickly diagnosed and solved. if i was going to have a problem it's that one of the doctors tried to tell me i had the dt's. i had to inform her that's impossible, i'd just had a 4 beers.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: poor communications. poor medical care. doctors hampered by management. hospital makes appointment follow ups with specialists while you are waiting to be seen in emergency. no specialist visit in er with injury.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: this review for emergency center. my dad had a stroke and ambulance took him to the emergency center. i was so worry and i rushed to the emergency. because i was so worry, i did read the "please wait here sign" and ran toward to receptionist. the receptionist was helping another patient to check in. as soon as i try to say something, she looked at me and told me that i cut in front of the other lady and i need to step back behind the sign and wait in a very mean way. this black shirt hair lady with glasses was very mean, she made me look like i did it on purpose or didn't know how to follow the signs.. maybe she was trying to tell the other people that i don't know english? she didn't have to humiliate me in front of other people.
address: Sutter East Bay Medical Foundation 20103 Lake Chabot Rd

review: the only reason i even gave this facility two stars was for cleanliness and the front desk staff. as for the doctor i saw, he doesn't even get a star. to be polite, i won't name names, but he was awful. i went in with my main complaint being chest congestion... he didn't even listen to my chest. i don't even recall seeing him have a stethoscope. i am not a doctor, but as a patient, how am i going to feel secure in my treatment when the doctor doesn't even check the main source of complaint? not only do i feel like i wasn't given the proper time and look over, but his personality also wasn't his strong suit. front staff was great, but actual doctor was sub par.

do not... i repeat do not go here unless you want sticker shock on your bill. my bill was 3 times higher for something relatively minor than if i went to another major hospital er down the road. i would hate to see how high my bill would be if any tests were actually run. they advertised these neighborhood hospitals as affordable and that is so far removed from the truth!!!

treatment was as expected. however i will not ever go back due to the high costs associated with care. it is much cheaper to go to st francis hospital down the street.

awful service! 
we are still waiting and we've been here for 3 hour and the waiting room is so empty; so there is no reason for this wait time. do not come here.

if you have a choice, avoid this hospital until they resolve their patient drop off and pick off bottleneck due to their on-going construction. the system they have in place is an embarrassment - either stage additional satellite parking locations, shuttles, valet stations - whatever it takes to remove the congestion on reservoir rd. just a horrible, horrible experience before you even set foot on the property. and today the parking attendants are only accepting cash because their credit card system is down. what a joke. avoid this hospital.

how can i say georgetown hospital has gone down! do not ever go to this hospital for an emergency.  i repeat...don't do it to yourself or a loved one. i spent over 8 hours in the emergency room.  i could have traveled to at least 8 different hospitals during my wait.

how does a hospital allow a patient to sit in the emergency room for over eight hours after telling the triage nurse that their symptoms include a head spinning, and periodic sharp pain in the chest, leg, arm, and neck?  in the meantime at least 5 people that arrived after me with what appeared to be common cold/flu symptoms were sent back for treatment.  the last time i checked cold symptoms were not considered an emergency.  

what type of triage is this? hell, what type of hospital emergency room is this? if an experienced doctor is not available to diagnose and treat patients with diverse illnesses, staff could have at least communicated this to me so i could have chosen another hospital.  

also, i need to know why in the world are staff taking vitals, blood, and urine right smack in the middle of the er waiting room next to the registration desk. talk about no privacy and just down right inconsiderate.  i just cannot with this hospital at this point.

now lets get to the lackluster registration staff including the nurses at the front desk.  please train your staff to be empathetic and show at least the slightest bit of concern for patients.  please remember that me and my  insurance are paying good  hard earned money for my er visit which in turn is paying your wages.

get it together right now georgetown hospital! we can not wait for future renovations just to see the basics achieved.  your name should be changed from medstar to medbelowpar!

this hospital kept us in the waiting room throwing up and very ill. even after i was seen, they put me back in the waiting room and did not take care of us with a needle in their patients arm still. i do not recommend it at all  and they do not care about their patients.

if i could give this place 0 stars i would. i left work early after waiting 2.5 months to obtain an appointment with the doctor i had researched online. upon arrival, the gentleman at the front desk told me that i was not in the system for an appointment and the doctor i was supposed to see was not there. mind you this is after 6 or so received confirmations.  he told me to have a seat to see what could be done  10 minutes. 20 minutes pass. i finally come up and he tells me there's nothing that can be done and i'll have to come back. i said that that was not an option and he went back to meet with the team. a lady then comes out and grabs me... no new patient forms or anything as everyone else was completing and starting conducting what she called an "interview" on a random paper she grabbed of her desk.  i have never seen anything like it. she then told me to go back and wait and the patient manager grabbed me back into this office to tell me that no one will see me today and they were going to ask me these questions anyway that they wrote on a random paper that anyone can see and that because i was in for a regular check up as a new patient it was not urgent which they outlined on the paper. then she wanted to set me up to come back. i will not be coming back here or seeing their doctors. how unfortunate.... i just wanted to make sure i was healthy.  do not go here. what a waste of time.

this is for one recent excruciating experience, although i've seen gu perform better in happier days.  a loved one recently tripped and fell down a flight of stairs and hurt her elbow, and we just went in to confirm whether it was a fracture, a break, stage iii pancreatic, or just something to put some tiger balm on and rest up.  after an hour+ in the rather slow-traffic waiting room filling out some pretty scintillating paperwork, we were ushered by the qualified powers that be into an area resembling a world war i field clinic and sequestered behind some flimsy curtain for at least two hours while these brainiacs sped around looking at various (others patients') charts, provided zero updates unless proactively solicited, and barely made eye contact with us even though they were obviously over-staffed and under-patiented.  we got one personal visit from the head cheese who then went on to bigger and better things (perhaps a head cold for the gent over behind curtain 5a) and couldn't be bothered to convey to us what, in what, after a likely three hundred years of experience in this practice, she could've told us in about 20 minutes). meantime, the purple scrubbed worker bees were busily buzzing around alternately looking at various charts on various computer screens and, um, checking their latest like, coat of nail polish.  (how many gals who just graduated with a pa license from strayer online does it take to manage an er full of, say, 5-7 patients?  15-20, apparently.  three to four illustrious worker bees for each patient lucky enough to end up at this underwhelming facility - not a bad ratio, in theory, but practice falls short, believe you me.)  no bedside manner (the key, glaring deficiency), sparing smiles, more or less basic command of verbal communication but nothing to write home about.  thankfully the news was good, but we would have appreciated it a couple of hours earlier.  and, hey, i'm not a medical operations specialist or anything, but perhaps an emergency room operation can optimize efficiency and effectiveness by clearing easy cases out sooner rather than later?  disappointing experience.  we'll opt for gwu, sibley or the effing minute clinic at pentagon city mall the next time around.

i can't say enough good things about dr eric anderson of pulmonology and dr. margolis and the thoracic surgery team.  the best nurses on c4-1 ever we're lou, stephanie, and erin.  they made sure to communicate with my mom what was going on and took the extra time with her when she needed it.  communication included things like, i am busy right now, can you give me an hour and i will walk with you.  the reason i gave two stars is for the communication between the depts, the nurses and the doctors as well as the parking.  the doctors would tell my mom one thing and not communicate it to the rest of the staff.  prime example my mom was to be ready to go by noon on the day of discharge and she was no where near ready.  getting medicine when she needed it to was another pain in the neck.  parking sucked! i found out that there is a pass for people who have family members who are staying for an extended time three days before shelby mom was discharged.  and this is after almost two weeks.  do you know how much money that is?!?!  not one word from the nurses, the parking staff or anyone who saw me on an almost daily basis.  as for the er, wonderful care from the start.  from liz who took us in to the nurses.  i know from other reviews that the er got a hard knock, but please remember, as much as it sucks being in pain, it is an er and they triage

harlem hospital is the worst hospital.  unprofessionalism is rampant at this so-called hospital.  tried to call to cancel an appointment. each time i call, there is always a busy signal.  typical ghetto hospital!

the best of the best. my doctor here was wonderful, staff were wonderful, security was always helpful with questions, and they had tons of information desks, maps, and wow the food options were not just plentiful but good. i always find it a tad chuckle worthy when you go to a hospital and all they are serving is unhealthy food in the cafeteria. like... huh??
northwestern talks and walks with the same intention. yes, there is unhealthy food, but the plethora of options of fantastic healthy food is just praiseworthy. this location is so nice sometimes i would work remote from their lobby when i was in the area. 
also! they just announced they are putting 78 million into an emergency department expansion to cut down on wait times. 

exceptional, and that's just the facts

have been debating leaving a review on here but i see others have had a similar experience so here goes...

many years ago i went to the er here because of a debilitating headache that came on suddenly. despite that fact (and the fact that i told the attending doctor that i had a family history of cerebral aneurysms) the doctor literally treated me like i was a crackhead chasing a high, even asking me if i ever used cocaine before prescribing some ibuprofen. not sure if this hospital just has issues with treating "certain people" but i went to another hospital that not only treated me decently, actually ran tests to make sure that what i had wasn't life-threatening just based on my family history. i don't ask for much, but being treated like a human being is at the top of my list. not only will i never go here again under any circumstance i won't recommend it, either.

nmh is such a comfortable place for a hospital stay in downtown chicago. it's clean without feeling "too sterile" and the artistic installations throughout the building evoke a sense of home. there are about a dozen restaurants on the 2nd floor at reasonable prices. thank you to our amazing surgical team led by dr. gregory dumanian! we loved our 12th floor nurses including, alyssa, ro and lindsay. the pre-op nurses and pcts were also all-stars and the 12th floor chef monica made a delicious dinner and husband for my husband who has a ton of food allergies. 

pro tips:
- all ride shares can be accessed in the gelter pavilion by the arrivals entrance
- the walgreens pharmacy on the 2nd floor has everything you need for an unexpected overnight stay

top quality medical care. 
i came back here for hip replacement surgery instead of getting it done in my home state of louisiana.  (no duh)!!
they are meticulous,  super professional,  polite, knowledgeable.
i can't say enough. 
if your insurance allows it, i recommend 
northwestern without reservation.

this the second time i had the unfortunate experience of bringing my wife to northwestern emergency room. 
average wait time is between 6 to 7 hours. 
i came in at 11am and was not admitted until 3am the following day. 
my wife had an acute condition and was told by her primary go to northwestern er, but we still waited.
there should be an acute er for individuals with acute conditions and then another er for the individuals that have strain/sprains and head colds.
after the second er experience i changed my medical group to doctors out of university of chicago. much better and professional experience. and actually it is a much higher ranked hospital. 
also the gate keepers gals at northwestern er are rude and insensitive.

very unprofessional. i actually took myself out of their program due to very poor communication. if you have a terminal illness you would think they would at least contact you about results? think again. you have to call, write, beg for a call and usually get someone who has no clue and will 'send your questions on to the people who know'. then never get a response....again.

the only time you hear from them is when they schedule you for another vastly expensive procedure or test. and even then its just a mychart notice. 

they have some good nurses onsite when getting something done but it ends there.

but all they care about is cramming scans, exams, procedures down your throat without giving any more information. it is chaotic, a keystone cop act. left and right hand have no clue what the other is doing. transplant team rep? keeps making promises that never come through. 

team social worker? unbelievable at best. abrasive, condescending and useless. even she said transplant was not an option but i needed to keep coming back for tests and scans? not even a doctor and making prognosis?

each doctor gives different information.they keep swapping people around and never tell you. 

transplant team nurse is haughty and unfeeling at best. i have a friend who underwent a transplant 4 years back who had the same issues! they get mad at you for asking for information, but never remedy the issue.

her reply when i said i wanted out of the program? "ok. it's done.". nothing else!  lol

it is beyond ridiculous. looking at the top transplant hospitals in the usa they cannot even make the top 15, what does that tell you?

it's all about the money. we refuse to give you the exact prognosis but just keep spending a couple hundred thousand on useless tests and procedure we know will not work or give more information. they know those things will not fix anything but they can grab tons of cash from insurance either way.

i ended up moving my entire transplant plan to another hospital. now i can get real updates, no 'i don't know" garbage, and real information i can use to plan for future possible events. after talking to 5 different doctors from 5 different sites they were concerned i needed better treatment. not to mention a doctor in my own family and some nurses as well.

wouldn't recommend this place for anyone with transplant needs.

shout out to dr. mark agulnik in heme/oncology and his fabulous team!!! my wife is under his care and she has been so well cared for. northwestern is a world class sarcoma center. we are so lucky and grateful to have been directed to northwestern!!!

i have been going for 3 years. procedures, surgeries and inpatient stays. 
this is not a place to go to be cared for. they do not listen to you. it is disconnected patient care. all about money and procedures,get you in and out. have an issue good luck. you are on your own. 
i often referred to it as prison care. meaning, i felt like a prisoner without support of anyone. i had to be hospitalized after surgeries my heart was stressed afib. 
they scared me into getting on a medication that i would need to be inpatient to get on. 4-5 days. the 4th day i was so over medicated my b/p 90/40 hr 40s i pleaded with them to lower the dose. it's too high. not comfortable taking it. 
they did not listen. 
the next day.  i was to be discharged, i was told i need to stay another day and medication needs to be lowered. 
prison care. locked down in the system for another day and night. knowing, i was unheard. did they care? no. after, i was so upset.  stating, i begged no one listened. one dr said i would of listened to you. ok sure. i don't believe you. 
i have many more just like this i'm going to continue to share so others do know we have choices. northwestern is not the best. and patients do not come first. 
rush
loyola
lutheran general 
and more other hospitals in chicago area. 
if we continue to give this hospital business
they will continue to think they are doing it right. 
do your research. know that just because it's on tv and has lots of money for marketing. that doesn't mean it's good. it means they are doing and pushing lots of surgeries and procedures. like me. i got sucked up into that system.

the care at the hospital is good, as are the doctors, but the admin is disastrous and can actually affect the care! not only can't you get in for months to see the doctors for months but it will be a full-time job for you to make an appointment. their policies about this are ridiculous with time frames of 72 hrs to just get an answer, not even appointment. but once you get there, there will be confusion as to the diagnosis, the billing etc. once, prior to an appointment i struggled for months to make, the doctor was unavailable! once the billing was listed incorrectly even though the doctor corrected it twice. once they weren't sure of the side the procedure was needed! there are great doctors in other systems. meanwhile, recommendation for northwestern . . . fix your admin systems and processes and hold it to a higher standard.

exasperating er visit yesterday. confusing signage, my grown son was taken to the hospital with a dislocated shoulder, which he has done several times before. he was in a tremendous amount of pain. when he got to the hospital the only thing they wanted to know was his insurance information and he didn't even get to see a doctor until about 20 minutes into his trip. over the course of 3 1/2 hours they took an x-ray and he was seen by a physician's assistant. we saw a nurse a physicians assistant twice and the insurance and payment guy four times. it's odd that they seem to spend more time and effort making sure that they get paid, rather than making people better.  oh, yea and to add insult to injury and  $1100 later, they charged $35 for parking. fairly certain that cost 3x more than o'hare. didn't know  the hypocratic oath includes price gouging?   our medical system needs an enema!
excellent staff from check in to discharge.  can't say enough about the nursing staff - great people that really took care of me.

dr. sandeep samant, the best of the best surgeon in my opinion, removed cancerous tumor with tors and performed neck dissection surgery on my husband.  he is an incredibly gifted, experienced and knowledgeable surgeon who's goal is to make his patient cancer free.   in addition to this, he is the kindest, most empathetic doctor who puts the patient at ease.   he is a rare gem.  we have full faith and trust in dr. samant and his team for my husband's care.  his surgical team and nurses and staff are amazing and top-notch.  my husband also received excellent care at nwm hospital chicago for pre-op, anesthesia, surgery and recovery.  thank you to everyone and highly recommend dr. samant and northwestern, wish we could give them 10 stars.

i've had nothing but great experiences & northwestern is the only hospital i'll go to for treatment. neurology specialists are great. i had seizures over 20 years & after having tumor completely removed there, i haven't had any in over 8 years. they have good orthopedic & physical therepy dept & also work with shirleyryans orthopedicdept (formerly ric). gi doctors helped get rid of my ulcers. i even had my kid at prentice. i've been to the immidiate care clinic & got treated right away, without having to wait in the er.

a nurse,  so sorry i didn't get her last name, named laquisha in same-day surgery was unbelievable! she attended our groen daughter who's had many hosputal stays in tge past 15 years, including two brain tumor removal surgeries.  early on, daughter was a military wife but for the past 8 years, as a now civilian-exwife, she's been a patient at st. thomas medical rutherford co. or another lical large hospital.  bless her heart- she truly struggles with her health issues.  at every hospital, tgere has always been 1 or 2 good-great nurses but sadly more "not good at all" nurses in their knowledge & treatment or professionalism.   but rarely have we incurred one like today! hopefully the administration knows the last name of whom i'm speaking but i'm certain god does!  this precious angel nurse, laquisha, was so knowledgeable,  professional,  compassionate,  helpful and i could choose many more adjectives & adverbs to describe her but would like to simply sum up as "unbelievably,  truly,  caring, awesome"! i hope this fine lady is commendedby her superiors but ifnot, she has our highest commendations and i know god will bless her & her career...which is without doubt, one to help others first-job/income after.

i want to start this off by saying i don't write many reviews and the ones i usually write are good ones. my father had surgery with dr. rodney bensley in cardiovascular last wednesday 1/22/20 the care that he has received since then has been less than mediocre. the nursing staff on the 2nd floor dropped the ball several times, and  he was moved up to the 4th floor where things just got dramatically worse. i am not a complainer, i am kind and respectful to anyone who cares for my family.  i believe medical care is tough,  however there is no excuses for the amount of laziness on the parts of some of these nurses. 
i also understand with any major surgery there is lots that can go wrong, i am not unaware of these facts but i have stayed at more than 20 hospitals across the country with my father due to his health and have never been afraid to leave my father alone with the staff. i was afraid to leave my father alone here.  i have never felt that about a place! the manager of the 4th floor came to speak with me her name is jessica. i expressed all of my concerns and she was being very attentive. at this point dr. bensley showed up because the nurses could not get the ng tube back in (which was taken out prematurely to begin with). he finally got it back in and came into the hall where jessica and i were finishing up. he began saying in a loud voice "what is going on,  what is your problem,  what is the problem here" then he began to accuse me of questioning things "why are you asking questions" he was practically yelling "he just had major surgery it takes awhile for things to go back to normal" i said "i wasn't questioning any of that the nurse was" he responds"you don't speak to anyone about his care except for me" at this point i would like to point out that now the nurses refuse to give us any updates about anything going on with my father and dr. bensley is not very accessible. i personally have never been so embarrassed, intimidated, or dissatisfied with medical staff as i have been here and if i could have transferred my father safely to another hospital i would have!!! i will say he has had 1 very wonderful nurse on the 4th floor named meghan. jessica the manager had given me her number to follow up while she was doing an investigation. i have called and left her a message with no return call. if you are looking for a hospital that cares for your family be very careful. since ascension has taken over st. thomas and the nursing staff has been cut back they cannot possibly care for you or your family well unfortunately.

i was restrained for 3 days both hands and feet for  pneumonia now how do u get restrained for pneumonia.everytime i have been there something has happened. i would not go back to that hospital sucks was.

recently had a medical procedure here, the doctors were great and most of the nurse's were fantastic but some of the tech's need to learn some bedside manners. the food wasn't terrible like most hospital food but nothing to brag about, all the staff was extremely nice and helpful. big rooms and all but it's still a hospital and no one wants to give a hospital 5 stars, it sucks even to visit one.

hospitals have come a long way over the years. this hospital's outpatient surgery center is phenomenal. from beginning to end, each employee was attentive and professional. the care i received exceeded my expectations.

horrible er. save yourself some time and go somewhere else. it says here average wait time is 24 minutes.  that's a joke! more like 6-8 hours and then when you are seen they do absolutely nothing to help. i've had my son there about 5 times in the last 6 months for a few different ongoing issues and each time they ran a couple little tests but when they came back normal they just shrugged their shoulders and said he'd just have to see this doctor or that doctor. they left my son in pain. i asked wasn't there something they could do and each time i was told no. last time he was there he sat in the waiting room for 6 hours. they ran 2 tests and said he'd have to see a urologist. we already knew that and he had an appointment but they weren't able to get him in for a week. he was in a lot of pain so we went to the er thinking maybe they would help since that's what we are always told to do by the doctor when they can't see him. the er did nothing. they just expected him to sit at home in pain for a week and wait. they wouldn't even make him comfortable while he was there or at least for the night. they shouldn't get paid for making people wait that long to end up having no treatment. they are insensitive to people there. they just don't care. last time we were there a lady waited for so long she got frustrated and threatened to slap the nurse if they didn't see her soon. she had been waiting in the waiting room for 8 hours! i've been there twice where we were never in a room and were treated in a hall on a gurney along with others. there was a lady there once that had to have her ring cut off her finger and they did it right next to us in the hall. the  employees aren't in a hurry for anything. i once saw a man in there waiting for hours to be seen while he was laying on two chairs rolling in pain. he looked deathly ill. they just left him there. nobody came to check on him. i've been there when there were so many people in there we had to sit on the floor because there were no empty chairs. i was once left in a room in excruciating pain after i had been vomiting and having severe stomach pain. i was alone and too weak to move and in so much pain i was calling for a nurse but nobody heard me because they put me in a room to far away for them to hear. nobody came to check on me for a few hours. i ended up being admitted. i could go on and on about how terrible this hospital is. they should be shut down. horrible excuse for a hospital. we are going to travel to a different one from now on. 6-8 hour wait time for them to do nothing to help is just unacceptable. if i could give a review with zero stars i would.

so here i am again this time my gallbladder ruptured and had to have emergency surgery late thursday night. had to have an ambulance bring me in bc i can't see to drive plus i couldn't walk the pain was horrible. anyway the surgical staff jumped in fast to fix me.  i also found out after surgery by the awesome anesthesiologist that when i go to sleep i stop breathing,  so he set up my next appt for that issue. i had no idea i did that needless to say i'm pretty scared about it. 
floor nurses and others have been awesome getting me whatever i need. pain is sharp but they are quick to give me my pain meds. definitely glad i chose this hospital and staffing unit for my care!
zero stars. horrible nurses. waiting in my 7th hour and the place is dead, computer glitches seem to be the excuse. it's horrible here. still haven't been told what is  wrong.

i came here because let's face it.. the pain i was going through was nearly in tears due to the pain associated in my back that only has been getting worse. i have been to hca hospitals across the country and this one was one of the worst  i have ever been in. currently starting to get comfortable but can't because of the pain. congratulations northeast you just proved to me that it's not an er but a general care place that can't handle inflows or walk ins

i cannot say enough good things about select and their staff. my grandfather was not given a good prognosis. ltac was our last resort - it was either that or hospice care. being a nurse myself i knew it was important to tour their facility despite another rehab being closer to us we went to select- based on not only their community reputation but the cleanliness of their facility and attentiveness of their staff. 
my grandfather recovered and went on to live with us for many more years. i feel like i owe those extra years to select. i was reminded of his stay recently as one of my patients daughters was deciding on the right rehab for her mom i felt it was my duty to share our experience

against my request i was taken to piedmont medical center via piedmont owned ambulance. i was suffering yet again of falling asleep on my feet however this time while awake i had no control over my upper torso, my body would just flip over.  once at the hospital i immediately realized where i was. 
the next thing i know i'm laying on this plastic bed type of thing in a room similar to an x-ray or cat scan room.  immediately i became uncomfortable and then as the machine tells you i felt like i was on fire.  the electrodes were burning and shocking me.  this went on for longer and much worse than a chemical stress test.  when i asked why they were doing that the reply was, "you wouldn't stay awake when i was trying to get your information so i had to do something".  there was a diagram of my body on this monitor showing where and what i was doing on this machine.  first only skeletal showed up, however when my leg slipped and my knee went out my back lit up bright green.  they told me the machine was a cat scan.
thier diagnosis at that time was that i overdosed on my pain meds.  but that was quickly ruled out once they realized that i had only taken less than allowed and half that was prescribed.  the next diagnosis was after my episode with their nasty machine.  yep, you guessed it, a broken back.
once admitted into piedmont's observatory floor it just got worse. nasty impolite nurses too busy to help and a definite racial bias that let you know they didn't care. 
i signed myself out of that hospital for fear they would only hurt me worse. i wonder how it i will get a nasty virus from being forced to walk over dried and wet urine barefooted in order to use the bathroom!
the icing on the cake,  my drivers license which had a very prominent place in my wallet is now gone and i know it was there only hours before i went to piedmont because i pulled the twenty out from behind it while still at my home.
piedmont medical center do you not believe in the hypocratic oath,  "first do no harm"?
never ever again will my shadow fall upon piedmonts doors.

this hospital is by far the worst i have ever experienced in my life. i have been a patient here and got absolutely zero diagnosis. the doctor actually said her staff didnt know how to take blood pressure correctly. cost me thousands for absolutely nothing. i watched a senior gentleman constantly throwing up for over 2 hours in the waiting room and still wasn't taken care of. another woman was having  serious chest pain and complete numbness of her left arm. she waited 4 hours in the waiting room. fast forward to today. my wife is going in to be induced. we just moved here so we have no friends or family and they refused to allow my 10 year old kids to at least go up to the maternity waiting room while we checked my wife in because they were not 12. i said the will mask up and rub sanitizer all over. i was expected to leave them in the main lobby with no security and a senior citizen that can barely see over the counter to watch my kids. who also said she wouldn't watch my kids. i ask if a security could at least come stand with them for a few minutes so my wife wouldn't be alone.. again told no.. complete shit

i recently had shoulder replacement surgery at welia. i was greeted and waited maybe 5 minutes. i was informed through the whole process. all of my questions were answered. dr. lamps and his assistants(whom i know) were professional and wonderful! i spent the night in the hospital and was treated with the greatest care. from the top to the bottom, all of the staff were wonderful and made the whole process easy to handle. we in this community, should be thankful for this health system. thank you welia for the great care!!

last time i use upmc for reimbursement of out-of-network claim and the staff was nice and helpful. so i'm updating my review about their customer service through the phone that is in the back of the card. i'm glad they have improved their customer service with training and also are requesting to reviews the staff after talking to him/her. i like when the company/ business wants make sure that you have received great service.

very poor experience with this hospital. i was scheduled to have an mri done today the 29th of january. i arrived  on time, was checked in, and right before i was supposed to have my mri done i get a phone call from the scheduling department while in the waiting room! they told me that i would need to reschedule and even had the audacity to lie to me over the phone. not only did i have to drive 20 minutes one way but i didn't get an mri done due to the poor work provided by staff/scheduling. i won't be coming back and will wait to find an alternative even if it means driving much  further to a different hospital!

if i could give this hospital 0 stars, i definitely would. i brought my boyfriend into their emergency room this afternoon and i can promise you i will never go back. not only does registration have no idea what they are doing when it comes to directions - after waiting for a bed to be available, we go back into the room to find someone else's blood in the sink and on the sheets. (picture added below). if you think that is bad it only gets worse. out of respect for her i will not add her name to this review, but the nurse he had needs to go back to training. i watched her take the iv in and out of his arm/vein 6 times. even as he was shaking and saying ow she didn't stop. i'm no doctor but that it not how the hell you do an iv. you never fish in someone's arm. so because of her ignorance, she blew threw his vein, which at that point blood started pouring out of his arm. he was sweating, in pain, and ready to pass out. do you think she had remorse? no. she asked if she could try the other arm immediately which at that point he said no i need a second you just blew my vein out. once a successful iv was done we didn't see her again for about an hour. to add to all of this, my boyfriend had a bad ibs flare up yesterday which they didn't care to look into at all. he was given fluids for hydration and anti nausea medication. worst er and hospital period. i highly don't recommend and definitely don't think we should have to pay the bill that's coming for that awful and disgusting service.

i was admitted to spectrum health for a serious respiratory infection. the staff were mostly very helpful (a few were outstanding!!) and i liked that i could pick up the phone and order my meals when i was ready to eat. i would love to give them 4 stars but i just can't. we have been back and forth with the billing office since before i was even discharged. we don't have insurance and are thus  required to pay cash for my visit. when i called the billing office, they were absolutely unwilling to work with me. at all. they told me that my bill was too big to be put on a payment plan  who does that? and they expected payment within the month. who has thousands of dollars just sitting around? we work with an agency who will work to get a reasonable payment based on the fact we pay it all ourselves. spectrum wouldn't budge. spectrum health is all about the money, not about  patients, they were unwilling to work with me in regards to my bill. so, 1 star it is spectrum.

i gave birth to my 3rd child here at sutter davis birthing center. i preregistered so when i came in my delivery room was ready. this was a big concern for me because my last birth very fast and i want able to make it to the room and instead i had my first son in the checkin room. for my 3rd delivery i planned a water birth but when i got to the hospital this time my contractions where so close meaning that there wasn't enough time to get to tub filled. even though i didn't get to have a water birth like i planned i did have my son natural and the experience was amazing thanks to lois, kathy and sandy. addition to them are the wonderful nursing staff, techs, ped doctors, lactation consultants, midwives. i appreciate their thoroughness, kindness and professionalism.  they made my for day stay feel like a vacation. with their help i was able to transition into breastfeeding postpartum care and study for an upcoming exam.

the e.r.  staff is kind and they really care about their patients. they are all efficient and they made me very comfortable during my visit. it was not busy when i arrived and i was only there for two hours. i felt safe at this location. there were two police officers parked outside. i will come back if i have another emergency.

irecently had knee surgery at menorah medical center the staff and everyone involved in my care was absolutely amazing i have had many other procedures in my past and this is by far the best hospital i've ever stayed at.
medical errors, disinterested doctors, some mediocre nursing, yes menorah has it all.  unless you have a minor medical problem you are likely to fare better at a major medical center.

my father in 2013 was there twice the first time was ok he had a bag and did not need personal care. the second time was a horror. i walked in he was nude laying in his waste door closed. i know the knew his room was right outside the nurse's break room and the respiratory tech was to come at 6:30 each day and i got there at 6:45. they said he was released to go to rehab on thursday. i got a call from the rehab place that he had pneumonia saturday morning and needed to go to the hospital at 8 am when i got there at 9. they said he was septic and would not make it through the day. he was dead less than 48 hours after they said he was well enough to leave. must go every day. do not be fooled by the floors for transplant patients ask to see other floors.

my mother in the hospital, i called the front desk to transfer my call to her room the person answered the phone insist that no one was there by that name. the security desk on the previous day didn't have a problem finding her name in the system. the call center/ receptionist didn't know her job!! and she was rude!! incompetent as hell!

i have never experienced such an incredible experience. this is the most wonderful team you will ever encounter, this place is truly a gem. if you are looking for a way to birth your way, have midwives that are all actual nurses but are the jack of all trades and still have all the security of a hospital and emergency care this is the perfect combination. from the moment i called, the whole team took my situation seriously and got me in quick for induction. they were so loving and kind! dr. blake was incredible. he was patient and efficient and allowed me to push for 2+ hours to deliver a higher risk baby that very well couldve had to be a c-section baby at any other hospital but thanks to him and his team and a lot of hard work, he came out safely and beautifully.  they truly fought for me and my baby and treated us like we were top priority from the very first phone call. they did an amazing job at delivering our baby boy and handled everyone of my concerns with so much ease. dr. blake and his team truly care about us moms, they are their biggest advocate. i cannot reccomend this place enough. we truly felt like family. 

 plus, what hospital let's their patients sleep while the incredible nurses tend and rock baby outside in the hallway? (just an extra little perk;) ) 


also, we werent kept any extra time and didnt have a ton of interruptions from random county services like bigger facilities and the food was awesome, best authntic mexican breakfast burritos!

can't say enough good things about the wilmot cancer center; everyone we've encountered so far have been a super positive and helpful doctors, nurses, physician assistants, patient care technicians... everyone we've met have been dedicated to making a difficult phase of life less onerous. i really can't say heap enough praise about the attention to patient care here and the extra effort that everyone has made so far. 

while every individual experiences their own journey towards a cure, the wilmot cancer center has been, for our family, a very positive step in the right direction.
fac_name: James P Wilmot Cancer Center At Strong

review:
after an unexpected turn in my health over the christmas break i found myself a customer/client/patient of the james p wilmer cancer center

the care and attention of everyone from the person who takes my garbage and linens to the doctor who performed my surgery has been nothing short of wonderful.

kudos all around for everyone!!
fac_name: James P Wilmot Cancer Center At Strong

review:
greenville is blessed to have st francis.  fortunately, i only had to use them for their er after a three day case of food poisoning.  the er was easy to find and had plenty of parking for family.  the er was spotless clean.
after walking in and giving them my name and birthdate they had my info including insurance within minutes.  i was moved to a room in less than 5 minutes.
an iv was started and vitals taken within minutes.
the staff working the front were kind and efficient.
the staff that put in the iv was a super pro.  it was comfortable the entire time i was being treated.
ever member of the staff had a kind and  warm smile.  everyone seemed to genuinely care and love their job.
everyone worked in harmony and made me comfortable and made me feel like i was going to be ok.
my doctor had a great bedside manner.  he was bright and wanted me to feel better fast.  i felt so blessed to part of the bon secure family and would recommend this hospital until the day i die.  which could be here in 50-60 years, lol.
i'll be a patient here for life.
thank you everyone at st francis.  i really am thankful for all you did for me.

i had a good experience at this er. 
i came in on a thursday at around 1pm with really awful pains in my chest and upper left shoulder/back and there was no one else in the waiting room. i immediately got checked in by the initial info. taker and looked at by the first nurse who checked my basic markers like blood pressure, temperature, reason for coming in, etc. he told me to take a seat and that they'd call me in "if they had room". which was a little worrisome, but i actually only waited for about 15 minutes or so before i got called in. 
i was taken to a private room by one nurse, met by another, and got changed into a robe, and started the process for my specific issue. the nurse we met in there was really rushing (the other nurse even pointed it out) - not even leaving the room to let me change into the robe - just holding it up and telling me to take off my clothes behind it - and asking me questions super quickly without even waiting for my response. i'm thinking and hoping that she just had something urgent to get to, because it was a little unnecessary, but nothing terribly awful. i took my time and made sure to get all my answers out before moving on. the other nurse was very kind asking if i wanted a warm blanket, etc. they were out the door in about 5 min after i got in. it took around 45 min or so before the dr. came in. 
he was really great. dr. mccall is his name. great bedside manner: calm, kind, allowed me to ask all of my questions and say all that i wanted to say. he took the time to thoroughly explain the results of the tests the nurses took, going into more detail about how to read it and what certain markers would and could mean, etc. he did a physical examination, as well, and explained everything as he went. explaining why i was probably feeling the way that i felt and what would cause it. i didn't feel rushed with him, and i felt like a person.

i was in and out of the building in about 2 hours!
and, parking is in a parking garage next door that was free (gate was open and there were no tickets) the day that i went.

i will have to see how billing goes, but in-person care was pretty good and thankfully much better than other reviewers' on here.
fac_name: PeaceHealth Sacred Heart Medical Center University District

review: went in early in the morning, was seen by erik poyourow, md. he was condescending, practically sneering. i hadn't been to an er in over 10 years so it's not like i was overusing services. he managed to insult my gender and age in one statement. "mocking" best describes his attitude. i got in to see real doctors later that day, who did an xray, found a kidney stone. apparently they can exist and cause the symptoms i had without  intense pain. those providers were surprised erik had not done imaging. if he had tried harder to diagnose my problem and less trying to impress the nurses with his cleverness i might have gotten some help. $250 to be basically laughed at. i'm a provider also and he was just unprofessional. i'll be going to mckenzie-willamette in the future if i have to. get some cmes in ethics, doc. the nurses were nice.
fac_name: PeaceHealth Sacred Heart Medical Center University District

review: my dad is here now and has been for at least 4 days and he feels the staff on the second floor have been "excellent."  no complaints at all  great job second floor staff from gary in room 227!!
this is the worst emergency room i've ever been to, i've had the worst experience here in my life please do yourself a face and go somewhere else

took my girl here because she was having heart problems and we waited about 4 - 5 hours and they werent busy. staff full of lazy people that dont know how to do their job. by the time they saw us, my girlfriend didnt even feel the symptoms of what she was feeling anymore. never coming back again and if you have an emergency i suggest you dont come here. if i could give this place no stars i would.

i've been dealing with chronic stomach issues for going on well over 6 years now. occasionally i have terrible flare-ups that i just can't get under control at home sometimes that involve uncontrollable vomiting and i usually am extremely dehydrated by the time i get to the er so i always request getting iv fluids as soon as possible because it helps me so much. 
i spent an hour in the er waiting room(technically the er bathroom since i couldn't stop vomiting and didn't want to disturb other patients in the waiting room) and was finally triaged....then sent back to the waiting room for almost another hour of waiting.

intro
this review is a commentary on the staff and administrators at 
usmd/mcnt, not the doctors. all of the information contained in this review is verifiable. 
backstory
i was a patient of the mcnt practice for many years and had my annual physicals there many times over the past decade. the annual screening is used to discount my insurance costs. three years ago my screening form was "misplaced". last year i was told it was faxed however, they could not provide the transmission report. to ensure the form was submitted on time this year i planned to pick up the form and submit it myself.
current events 
when i arrived at the office for my appointment i explained my past problems with the screening form to the nurse (rachel) and the doctor (hyatt). they assured me the form would be completed and they would call me as soon as my blood test results were in and added the test results normally came in three days. since my appointment was on friday i contacted them twice on the following tuesday. i received no response. i called twice on wednesday. i did receive a  message from the nurse on wednesday afternoon reporting the test results were in and awaiting the doctor's signature. i called twice on thursday and once again on friday. i did not receive any responses to these messages. i arrived at the usmd office friday afternoon around 3 pm. i explained that i was upset at not having received a response to my numerous messages and that i needed my screening form that afternoon to meet the deadline. a short time later i was ushered into the vacant hematology lab by rachel and told my form had not been signed and that the doctor was on holiday. i was furious! i explained loudly but respectfully that i needed to leave the office with the form to meet the deadline and requested that another doctor sign the form. i was then told no doctor would be able to sign the form that day and that their responsibility did not include notifying me or completing the form. i responded that i would not leave without the signed form. i received the signed form around 4 pm. i left, commenting on their horrendous customer service and poor communication skills. on my way to fedex, i called the usmd administrative offices in irving, texas. i was greeted by a very polite administrative assistant. she patiently listened to my comments, explained that most of the senior staff was gone for the day but that someone would get back to me on monday. this was  november 22, 2019. i never received a call.
closing
as i noted in the introduction the doctors at this office are outstanding. fortunately, my gp left the practice so i do not need to find a new doctor. having said that i will only go back to this office to retrieve my medical records. the customer service is deplorable, some of the staff are incompetent and certainly shouldn't be working with people. the usmd offices are no better since they were "unable" to return my call. i would avoid any usmd offices, specifically the mcnt office in flower mound, texas.
