i just wanted to add that i am not just some butt hurt person that got charged a big bill or am just out to get this business, i genuinely have had horrible experiences with all things inova. i wish i could say otherwise. i have had others tell me they do not like inova either.

i have an elderly godfather who has been in and out of the hospital for the last few years.  last week he went in by ambulance and was released several hours later too weak to get up.  the next day he was back in by ambulance and he requested that he receive no further treatment but wished to enter hospice.  the hospital kept trying to do blood work and x-rays despite this request.  the er doc spoke with us and insisted he could make him better.  he would be in the hospital another 5 or 6 days and probably get out for a few and be back but he would have time.  my godfather stated repeatedly he'd had a good life and enough time already but wished to die and have no further treatment.  we repeated this scenario several times.  we were visited by hospice and told he would be moved in the afternoon.  he waited from 9 am until 4 in the afternoon for transport.  from the time it was determined he would go to hospice the er offered no more care.  he remained in the hospital bed with an empty iv attached, on bloody sheets.  no amount of pleading on my part got him any comfort until he reached the hospice center in aldie where he lived only 24 hours.  i can't say enough good things about capital caring.  the horror of the day was the treatment in the er with the insistence that they could prop him up for a few more days and then ignore him from that point on.  they could have removed the iv from his arm, cleaned up the bed and allowed him some comfort but that is not what transpired at all and i am sorry he had to spend one of his last two days in that situation.

my dad stayed in the burn unit because he required an icu bed and they had an extra bed in the unit that they use an an overflow bed. we had been having a lot of problems at regions because the healthpartners doctors refused to treat his underlying problems. instead of just treating the problems, he had to keep getting admitted to the hospital for the same thing, sometimes within 15 minutes of discharge. they would pressure us to end his life claiming that he is so sick, yet they refused to treat the problem. age and disability were constantly discussed. most nurses were awful. they would come into the room to change the sheets while we were trying to have discussions with the doctors. they would talk and laugh over us. i discovered in the medical records that the nurses were refusing to let the hospital volunteers in his room to provide light physical therapy and companionship. how awful. they were so cruel. they obviously hated my mother and i because we were begging for medical treatment. they made constant notes in the record about us...lying, ridiculing, etc. they played a dirty joke on us. they claimed he had a terrible disease. the nurses on another floor didn't understand why they said what they said. this hospital was terrible. terrible.

my mom suffers from a mental illness. if she is given her mental medication then she stabilizes and is conversational, eats and sleeps properly. she was admitted to this hospital about two months ago and even though doctors had a record of her mental health issue they have not prescribed her mental medication...instead they let her suffer in mental anguish, put a feeding tube in her and try to get permission from me to not resuscitate her as they prepare her for hospice euthanasia.

i probably saw my mom for this last time today. i walked into a miserably hot room with bright lights shining down on her to the point that she was traumatized and would not remove her hands from covering her eyes even when the lights were turned down. her last thoughts will probably be through a broken mind that was denied medical relief as it tries to make sense of evil/incompetent doctors and idiotic television programming blaring from the corner of the room.

if my moms insurance had not run out then they might of tried to relieve her mental suffering and saved her life.

goodpersontest.com

my mother was nearly euthenized!!! she entered due to mental health issues and nearly left in a casket. they stated since she wasnt eating that they suggested expedited hospice! her mouth was covered in scum and dried blood inside and they where constantly asking me to deny the right to resuscitate her until i showed up in person. i made it clear she was to be treated instead. suddenly she was on her way to recovery and then cleaned properly. i have no respect for physicians that side eagerly with death. she has been there for two months yet still has not been given her proper mental health medications. the psychiatric dr. has yet to respond at all to at least half a dozen inquiries. without her meds she is highly depressed and gives up on life. it appears thats exactly what they want.  beware, monitor your loved ones closely if they end up in this horrible place. we have resulted to legal action against this elderly abuse/death row.

i honestly don't understand why this hospital has such a low score. i have been to the emergency room several times in the past and i haven't been there for more than a couple of hours. and that is all the medical staff testing blood work and scans. if you're from los angeles you know that a trip to the er can take up to eight hours. 

yes this hospital being renovated now and has needed an update for years. but just because it looks old, you cannot take away from its medical team. yes i do understand that other hospitals look nicer and better. that is one of the reasons this hospital is not getting an update. but you cannot let the appearances take away from the service and medical care that you can receive there. 

most recently i have been going to the labor and delivery room twice a week. i can honestly say i have been treated very well, with outstanding service. the nurses and the staff have been very supportive and explain everything that is going on in detail. i also have gotten the opportunity to see the labor and delivery room with ease and i feel more comfortable now. i definitely recommend this hospital and i would not judge it from the outside.

wow! i'm here for an emergency room visit today and the staff (from the transport staff to the nurses) were are caring, kind, thoughtful, professional and properly cared for my condition. nurse mena, respiratory therapist tim, and nurse practitioner diana have been just fantastic! i hardly ever get sick and i don't like going to hospitals but they made me feel at ease. they were thoughtful in their explanations of my prescriptions and home care. "....you were loved by someone, touched by someone...you can look back and kniw you were loved..." is my sentiment for today's visit. i didn't want to let the day pass without complimenting the wonderful people who took care of me today. lots of love, protection, and blessings of the most high to all of you.

i called the director of patient services as directed by business owner ofst johns regional medical center in response to my negative review concerning emergency room triage and wait time while i was having a stroke in er.

i called and left message . no response in 5 days!

this hospital is not responsive .

the hospital manages the emergency room as a urgent care.

hope you do not have life threatening emergency.

sandra in the medical records office was extremely helpful in correcting information in my er/hospital stay.  someone put i had been drinking and that caused blackout.  i've never have drank nor smoked or done street drugs.  this was a heart related problem, bradycardia/syncope, 2 strokes and 4 silent heart attacks.  thank you sandra for correcting miss information on my er/hospital records.

the nurses who took extremely good care of me and really took the time to help me: wade,andrew, jamaica, laura and poola.  thank you..  the doctors: bond and khatore, thank you for saving my life and to continue my care as its a long road.

back in mid september my wife was refer to st. john's medical center' labor and delivery dept. for some ultrasounds and tests because she was having some pregnancy concerns. from the very start to finish the support she received from everyone involved was above our expectations. they provided her with all the support she needed even though my wife did not have insurance at that time. my wife's insurance was not set to start coverage until oct 1. 

she was given all the necessary tests to confirm that the baby was okay and analyzed for contractions. turned out she was having contractions and was given a pill to stop the contractions and prevent a pre-mature delivery. 

a month later we received the bill for $1855. we applied for the financial assistance program and two weeks later we received a letter stating that we qualified for 100% discount care and our entire bill was covered by them.

most people complain about hospitals but they do not take the time to educate them selves on the financial programs that exist. not everyone will have their bill 100 percent eliminated, but will see huge bill reduction with payment plans. the hospital makes it easy to apply by including the application along with the bill.

my wife's delivery was fully covered minus our co-pay by kaiser in october at cmh.

honestly i have been very pleasantly surprised with the care i have received here.  starting from the minute my boyfriend brought me to the er.  i was having horrible chest pains and they took me right back to do an ekg.
the er doctor was extremely kind and patient with me.
i was admitted and have been here for 3 days now and have zero complaints.  the nurses (especially julie she sunny on the 4th floor) are amazing.  they have gone above and beyond to make sure i  comfortable and have everything i need.  the doctors assigned to me have also been incredible.  very thorough and patient with me and my anxiety which consists of hundreds of questions.
i typically would go to los robles in thousand oaks if i was having an emergent since that is my "home" hospital, and truth be told i was a little reluctant to come here.  not anymore!!  in fact i would come back here specifically because of the amazing care i received.
thanks again julie and sunny for making my stay more comfortable and enjoyable.  2 words one would not normally use to describe a hospital visit

i'm the caregiver for my mom. she was sick so i took her here. i waited in the waiting room because i trusted the nurses and/or doctors know what they are doing. i was wrong. i should have went in with her. they bruised her badly and she developed an infection from the work they performed on her. apparently they forced the wrong sized needles in her arm which ruptured her blood vessels and she bled under the skin (causing hematoma), now she has to take antibiotics. it would be nice if an er had experienced, professional staff instead of ones that don't know or care. you should be able to trust an er. don't go here. this place is a flipping joke.

this hospital appears to be understaffed...long waits for help when needed...medications are not given when they are supposed to or missed alltogether after 6 days and many tests...they discharged my wife still vomiting and cannot hold down food...didn't do her any good there except kept fluids in her.....now she's dehydrating again....if she continues to get worse...not sure if i will take her back there or to sarasota if she can handle the trip....also...no follow-up call from the hospital or one of her doctors there to check on how she is doing....it only reflects on a poor administration!.....up-date....today friday 1/30....she's been home 3 days now....still vomiting & diarrhea...soonest appointment she could get with our primary care provider is monday...hope i don't have to rush her to another hospital before then.....englewood community hospital is not a first class hospital by no means....my wife is worse now than after a 6 day stay there....should be rated zero stars!

i would give this location zero stars if possible! 
i called several times to make an appointment for my 15 month old to get his flu shot (pediatrician's office is currently out) & to confirm insurance. 
cindy at the front desk was very pleasant she said yes please bring him in. 

we get there & after a question of has he had any vaccinations in the past 28 days i said yes, he has had his 15 month old vaccinations the end of last month. 
nurse practitioner christina kapfhammer came out & said no i will not be able to give him the flu vaccine that two live viruses can not be done in the 30day time frame!

as a nurse practitioner you dont know what vaccines can be done together?!?

do not bring your little ones here! wait for your pediatricians office! first time mom here so thought a simple flu shot would be okay to get here. wrong!

as a canadian family on vacation, i never thought i would have to bring my daughter to emergency in the middle of the night. what originally started out as a fever on dec 23rd, turned into a coughing fit with shortness of breath by the 27th. my wife woke me up at 3am to check on our daughter and we could clearly see something was not right. as someone not from this country, i had no idea where to go for care and started researching multiple facilities nearby when we came upon this hospital. 

now that we have been discharged and resting at home, there is no doubt in my or my wife's mind that we made the right choice. from the moment we entered, we were quickly expedited in the back and saw a doctor within a span of 15-20 minutes. while i appreciate our medicare system in canada, this was a a completely new experience to me. anyhow, the all the staff that saw us provided my family top notch service and completed the necessary tests to ensure that my daughter was going to be ok. at no time did i ever feel there were going to be  unnecessary tests or that we weren't being taken care of.

at the end of the day, my daughter was diagnosed with pneumonia and we were sent home with medicine so that she could rest easy and recover. i am glad to have met the staff at the hospital and can't thank them enough for all their work. god bless you all!

review: it was nice clean environment except the restroom but i can understand that a little. however. the wait wasn't long they treated us with kindness and respect. they treated us and let us go. this is a nice facility to go too for emergencies. if u like me i like to read reviews before i go to a new place. from my experience it's a go too.

around 0100 i couldn't take anymore of my back pain and went to the er. in august we had the annual triathlon(atv and dirt bikes) which consists of motocross, flat track( both on saturday), then the harescramble(sunday and my preferred discipline). anyways, the first moto these guys were talking a bunch of crap so i signed up last minute and jumped on my sons buddy's quad and smoked those guys pretty bad! during that first of two moto's, i came up to a small triple, approximately 50'-60'(fishing story, prob closer to 40' max) and came up short casing  the third jump due to the quad falling on its face when i went to burp the gas right before take off. it's been a struggle since then. so anyways, i was coughing pretty bad friday and ended up i thought i pulled something and then stayed knocked out friday night to last night. i couldn't control my bowels and pissed myself once. they at first want to run me to a neurosurgeon so they could start cutting into me, not sure what they were thinking but them scrambling around didnt make me feel any better. they ran me to x-ray to see if there was a broken bone in my back. they gave me 3 shots and some other pills, then sent me on my way. they said there is nothing they can do for me other than rehab..... i'm home and finally got a few hours of sleep..... 

the two male doctors were ok, short but didn't give a crap really. the nurses were seriously ignorant and short! my fiancé, who is very skinny due to crohn's, went to find me a blanket that i asked for about 45-55 mins earlier and to get me a cup of water since my throat was very dry since couching so much. the staff acted like we were drug addicts constantly telling us they don't prescribe narcotics there that i would have to find a family doctor. i never asked for any pain pills, i wanted something to help me stop coughing or too see if i was getting pneumonia. i've been here multiple time with my family and never had any issues or was made to feel like we were drug addicts.... i tried calling the number listed and it kept ringing. the only nurse that was good was the x-ray tech who went right away to get me a blanket. the other nurse came in and said she was still looking for a blanket even though i was covered up. she never noticed that i was already covered. she never brought a blanket back.... also, it was not busy as there were maybe three more people in the er other than my self so it's not like they were busy. everyone made me feel like crap, like i was being profiled, and i know it's because i'm self pay, thanks to the rising rates from obamacare i can not afford insurance premiums now. i should've stayed home and saved myself aggravation and money since i left there with some muscle relaxers that i told them i can't take because pills upset my stomach... i was hoping for a stronger cough syrup so i would quit tweaking my back. sorry for the lengthy rant, but i'm embarrassed and still in pain. that trip was a waste of time and money....

it's not common to leave an emergency room experience and feel that it was phenomenal; however, that was the feeling i had after our experience at tulsa er & hospital.  the facility is brand new and was spotless.  the nurses and doctor were caring, knowledgeable and attentive.  i highly recommend this facility.

go again? no. avoid if possible. my wife was brought to the er by yosemite ambulance even though they had no available rooms. 
2 hours later she was still in the hallway in a wheelchair and they would not let her use restroom! she remained in the wheelchair for over 6 hours. and, they would not let me inside to see her. we could only communicate by cell phone. the ambulance should have taken her to a hospital in merced rather than take her to a hospital that was way over-booked! later, the hospital was very helpful in faxing a report to my wife's primary care doctor and i changed the rating from one star to two stars.

a quaint mariposa non-magnet hospital paying their experienced registered nurses low wages for decades to include expecting experienced rn applicants to accept lvn wages. interview summary: no clinical situational questions. expect questions relating to co-worker and managerial dissension, unrest, an atmosphere of unhappiness, and misery bar none. 
no thank you !!!!

i can't imagine any other business where you are spending thousands of dollars at an establishment and the people working there treat the clients like they are trash, and are annoyed with them for existing.

i met the doctor for the first time during my stay in the er when he burst into the room saying, "i'd like to know what possible reason you could have for holding up a ct scan!"  not, "hello, how are you feeling?" not, "hi i'm dr. gionis."  i'd been waiting literally hours to see him the middle of the night, after a day spent throwing up with a fever. it was 3am.  i deserved kindness and gentleness, not being attacked.  that is an incredibly rude way to treat anyone, period. second of all, when you're the doctor and a large tall man, and your patient is a young woman, alone in the room, who is so sick she can barely speak, it's absolutely unacceptable.  

i was able to articulate to him that i had wanted to see the results of my bloodwork before further testing.  i have been in the er many times in my life for various issues including gastric related ones, and i have never had anyone order extensive imaging before even examining me.  this clinic ordered an x-ray and ct scan, in addition to a urine sample, blood panel, and other tests,  before anyone had even examined me!! i had no unusual symptoms of any kind and in all my er experiences, the imaging comes when something shows up in bloodwork or due to symptoms noted in the exam with the doctor.  they claimed they needed imaging to see if it was appendicitis or other internal organ issue.  yet no one had even palpated my  abdomen to check for localized tenderness.  so i felt like this was a racket and i had every right to request to be seen, examined, and to know if any results in my tests indicated the need for imaging.  they had already swooped in and x-rayed my lungs and i didn't even have a cough or any symptoms remotely related.  

i was there because i needed intravenous fluids and anti-nausea meds so i could rehydrate and take tylenol, get my fever down, and be well enough to drive the next day.  i was of course willing to be examined and appreciated them looking for signs of something other than food poisoning or the flu, but this was excessive and i had every right to question them and to want to talk to the doctor about why the hell a ct scan was being ordered before anyone had talked to me. 

when my mom and i questioned them on all the testing and why we weren't being seen by a doctor, we were treated horribly.  we were gaslit, and shamed.  they then kept me there for 5.5 hours, 12-5:30am, citing being a small clinic in a rural area.  it was a monday night in the off season.  there were one or two other patients the whole time i was there and yet we went hours without being spoken to or seen. and when my mom tried to get someone's attention, to get me a blanket, or some ice chips, or any info on when we might be seen, she was told she was violating hippa laws.  by walking outside the doorway.  

anyway, this place is awful.

review: ascension brighton center for recovery is an excellent recovery center.  i was there for 9 days to get off suboxone 20 years of being on opioids for chronic pain. all the staff there were amazing.  everyone was very professional and compassionate.  the care i got there was wonderful from drs to nurses and support staff.  sure the building is old and in need of some updating but that did not take away from the excellent care i got.  my only wish would have been that i got medical care on returning home because i've been sick at home 5 weeks since leaving treatment.  it's one day at a time and i pray i start feeling better one day.  thank you ascension for the excellent care i received while there.

i have been seen at upper chesapeake hospital er 2 times for severe migraines. i was always treated with upmost respect and cared for with kindness and understanding.  i was given the meds needed to stop the migraine.  my last visit for a migraine they found aneurysm (which they were not looking for).  i was then referred to a specialist at the main university of maryland hospital.  i was seen and treated for the aneurysm and no longer have that aneurysm. thanks to the doctors and staff at the upper chesapeake hospital a potential problem was eliminated. the doctors and nurses at upper chesapeake were very professional and top notch.  i highly recommend this er.  awesome experience and outcome.

good patient service, but hard to navigate. i visited here for some extensive testing my doctor had ordered that was not available at the hospitals closest to me. i had looked online at the virtual map to try to plan our visit which turned out to be not very helpful at all. i was told to park in the garage by the main entrance by preregistration, which we did. this is also know as the visitors parking garage. this was a big mistake. we ended up walking all over the hospital and finally getting to our destination on the other side of the hospital. we would not have made it had there not been so many nice employees willing to help.

i also wish i could give zero stars.  i am a former rn at mvh.  i have never seen an environment so stacked against success for providers and nurses.  my experience was this:  there appeared to be understaffing and lack of positive communication between departments because of this burden.  in addition, in an overburdened environment, mistakes can happen. they can and do. nurses carry a lot of liability, for this reason, i would not advise working at this hospital.  leaving my position at this facility was the best decision of my professional career.  the nurses and providers at mvh strive to provide great patient care in the face of a lot of deficits (of the facility).  it makes me sad to see that nurses and doctors get blamed for a lot of things that the facility is responsible for.....until this facility improves the work environment for nurses and providers, there is no way in hell that i would take a family member to this facility for care.

best hospital ever! the er is amazing! i was treated so well. my wait time was maybe 10 minutes. i was very happy with the staff. everything was done quickly and professionally. i will definitely come back to this hospital and refer others as well. the care was phenomenal! thank you!

to whom it may concern,
wanted to give my complaint to this hospital. i had the worst experience i have ever had with any hospital. i was seen on january 3rd-4th as an outpatient blood transfusion. not only was i poked 10 times to try and get an iv started but when i told my nurse that the pain was unbearable she was hesitant on starting a new iv. i am a stage 5 kidney failure patient and i should be respected when i say the pain is unbearable. they should have listened and removed the iv. after the transfusion they sent me home with my arm swollen and bruised. the pain was still unbearable that i had to go to another hospital and turns out that the iv that was placed in dameron hospital infiltrated and all the fluids went into my tissue. i am so angry not only because this happened but i am already going to the worst pain in my life because of kidney health. i am highly considering filing a malpractice lawsuit so this won't happen to another patient again.

took my boyfriend here for emergency at 11pm, it was the closest er so we had no choice. the wait was way too long we didn't leave till 6am!!!! like wth? i honestly would've drove somewhere else if i knew how bad the place & staff were!! worse place ever! they do not care for their patients, the 2 nurses that were in charge of my boyfriend were very aggressive. people in front desk weren't friendly at all, no "hi" nothing just plain rude! all they did was gossip about people. they were even making fun of patients falling asleep in the waiting room & rudely kicking them out. oh & to add to how bad this place is, they really tried to charge us 4,000!!!!! lol we called and the person on the line said they charged us for something severely life threatening--deadlly!!!?? lol it was just the damn flu!!! thankfully we didn't have to pay that shit!

the best hospital in town. i've brought my self and kids here after hours. they are fast with handling patiences  faster than st joseph i will tell you that forsure. gotta love anthony ambrosino best doctor their.

why is it that this female security guard at the er thinks she can keep asking medical questions? if i told you that i'm here to be seen for my back, that's all you need to know. you are a rent a cop fake ass cop... you are not a medical provider.. according to the hipaa law i can sue the hospital because you are violating my privacy. if i tell you it's none of your business how i hurt my back then it's not your fucking business.... why do they hire nosey people like that. and on top of it all bitch had the nerve to give me a dirty look when i was walking with the nurse. what kind of establishment is this hospital running when a rent cop thinks she has every right to but in on your privacy?? so fucking disappointed in this hospital privacy standards...

we showed up in this emergency room in june 2019 when my son was badly scalded on his legs and stomach while camping at folsom lake.  we don't even have sutter insurance, but kaiser; this just happened to be the closest er. the waiting room was overflowing when we arrived at about 9:00 pm, but we were triaged within just a few minutes and admitted right after that (my son was in a bad way).  kat, the charge nurse on duty that night, was awesome; she was a calming, knowledgeable presence, and she immediately started a course of treatment.  within two hours of our arrival, the staff had stabilized my son, gotten him admitted to the burn ward at shriner's hospital in sac (also awesome), and arranged for an ambulance to shuttle him down the hill.
  
to the er staff at sutter auburn faith, thank you so so much.  this was the first stop on the road to recovery, encompassing the most critical minutes after the injury, and we could not have asked for more.  my son is doing very well now, and he also thanks you from the bottom of his heart.

review of doctor tiffany ginger may liean hue and the sutter  auburn faith emergency   department  .
i love auburn, i was blessed to have been able to spend most of my 54 years here . i'm proud of this community and our rich heritage  and when it comes to health care my famiky and i have always turned to auburn faith . both of my /kids came into this world via maternity ward and i have seen more then a few nights in the er getting stitches or having a broken  bone set . 
the emergency room  is staffed by gifted doctors and dedicated nurses who provide a place of compassion . safety and healing ,  it's doctors like 
kevin owens md. , dr. andrew prince m.d. and dr. brian stamper m.d, that i can personaly  recomend  as five star  winners.

i came here yesterday after getting hot coffee on my hand the staff working was very great i didn't have to wait long to be seen the nurses and emergency doctor working where very great the first thing i noticed when i came in was how clean this establishment was very clean atmosphere very clean exam rooms this establishment is very well taken care of with the very friendly helpful staff they made me feel very comfortable with the medical attention i revived and made me feel better today after coming in yesterday my hand is back to normal with no blistering and doesn't hurt that much :) this staff is very knowledgeable on there jobs and they take pride in what they are doing i highly recommend this establishment for anyone looking for medical attention the staff is very knowledgeable and friendly and very helpful i would definitely recommend this establishment for anyone in the area they are awesome thank you sutter faith hospital for being so helpful and so great with me i appreciate it
thanks to all doctors and nurses for taking care of me last wednesday when i was in for knee replacement surgery. flawless stay. thanks again.

my husband has been a regular patient here since sept 2019. they are all very nice, from er doctors er nurses to hospital doctors nurses aides dietary housekeeping transportorting. lab and social workers. my husband been in the icu unit a few times they are great. i stay with my husband 24 7 while he is here they make me comfortable and welcome here . yes they have some flaws but who doesn't. but their patient care is number one in their list. thank u guys for everything

my husband was diagnosed in september with sepsis. he's been in and out of sutter auburn faith and sutter roseville for over two and a half months. there was only one hospitalist and one nurse that i had a problem with but the rest of the doctors and nurses were excellent. i especially want to thank the wonderful nurses in sutter auburn faith icu. they made a difficult time bearable.

i spent a month there. 2 weeks in icu on a ventilator.  the staff in the icu was the best. the middle care unit was also good but not as attentive to progress. the physical therapy unit was amazing. especially dr schwartz. they keep you moving and improving.  everyone was very friendly and encouraging. the speech therapy folks also took great care of me. i am grateful for this hospital.
fac_name: The Moses H Cone Memorial Hospital

review:
glad i arrived early for my test today. there is valet parking and 30+ year employee spaces that take up the first 3 decks of the parking garage. wow! i have never seen anything like this before. this place is also very confusing to navigate. i asked about 4 times how to make it to the right place.

i finally have found where i need to be. the customer service has been great so far. waiting patiently to be seen.

review:
last weekend, my mother sat in the er for 5 hours in excruciating pain.  cone er did xrays, claimed they couldn't find anything, gave her some morphine and released her with no plan, no nothing.  this was one of several trips to the er she took over the past 3 weeks with this horrible pain.  finally being totally fed up with cone's mess, my brother took her to his doctors in d.c. a few days later where they immediately found a significant compression rib fracture.  what the hell is wrong with you so-called doctors at cone er?  seriously..........how do you miss a significant fracture and you claim to have taken xrays???  shame on all of you for making her go out of state for decent care.

cone health received my online complaint and sent a pathetic letter to my mother trying to cover themselves.  they tried to say they gave my mother adequate care while at the er.  yet the facility in d.c. even acknowledged their care was terrible.  other good doctors saw through their mess and their lies.  we see through it too.

do not let your loved ones go to this hospital!!!!   drive a little further.  go anywhere else.  this hospital is a joke and will treat your loved ones as such.

review: staff for er was young but quick & efficient. i was in and out under 3 hrs. the room was clean, staff was affectionate and helpful to me during a quick time of distress for an infection i had. i'm so happy i came here instead of a quickcare.

they found a way to kill their guests quicker at the hospice. i went in here last week to see my uncle and some bald old white guy was walking around with a chicken. feathers were falling on the ground. the nurses were letting him walk around with it. i was shocked and asked for an administrator and was told they were at lunch. i am not a doctor but spent some time on a farm, and chickens carry more diseases than a daycare. i have pictures if anyone wants them.
fac_name: CHI St. Joseph Regional Health Care Center

review: on wednesday night i was at church when i began to experience severe chest pain, being an emt and a high level cardiac patient i made the choice to go to the er. when i arrived at the er (chi st. joseph, bryan) the visit started out as good as it could, my ekg was abnormal along with labs. i was rushed directly to an er room. doctor conrad and doctor tuckerton were the two doctors in the er at the time and thank god. issues started when it was time to start an iv. i know i am a very hard stick so i told the nurse to get the ultra sound, despite that 14 sticks later still no iv access. the nurses were doing what they could, but due to hospital staffing no one qualified to complete advanced iv procedures was working. finally, doctor tuckerton established it, during the testing i was told i was being admitted, but no beds were available so i might be in er all night, i was being kept very medicated and comfortable so no problem. finally, i was told that due to labs i was being taken to icu, again okay. this is where the part starts that results in a one-star review. again amazing nurses, but the doctor! i made the extra 15 mile run to this hospital due to my now former cardiologist, doctor marc schwartz being on staff. the first issue came with initial admitting orders; it took him over three hours to enter them. when the nurse went to get pain medication for me due to severe chest pain, surprise no orders for it. as a reminder my history includes five heart attacks, 6 stents, a quadruple bypass, 3 strokes, and afib. oh and i am 42.  i had not been given anything tor pain control for now going on 8 hours, when the cardiologist doctor marc schwartz was asked for the orders from the rn he said pain control was not his problem and walked off, thankfully the icu doctor took care of it. several hours later the pain control issue came up again. the previous order was a onetime only order, again doctor schwartz would not take care of it and relayed the message i would just have to deal with the pain. at this time my blood pressure was 179/99 and my pulse was back up to 140 due to the pain. once again the icu doctor fixed the issue. now for the crown jewel. doctor schwartz comes into announce that the severe chest pain and symptoms are due to the plumbing around my heart being very bad. we know it's bad, but something has to be done. i am on every medication i can be to manage the symptoms. he made it clear he does not know what to do and until the heart muscle starts to show damage he is not interested in any invasive procedures, his answer is, i will have to live with the pain and associated symptoms for now, playing the er round trip game, his attitude is why i will start going to the hospitals in the woodlands. his lack of empathy and his attitude are my deciding factors in filing a formal complaint with the hospital and the state of texas. i strongly encourage everyone, if you have an issue with a hospital or doctor, speak out! speaking out advocates for other patients and helps protect them and until enough people speak out against a doctor of facility a change will not happen!
fac_name: CHI St. Joseph Regional Health Care Center

review:
came here to meet my friend for lunch at the cafe.  there was a variety of food but we went to the grill for burgers and fries. didn't get to check out other parts of the hospital. there was a hand sanitizer and a box of masks by the entrance in case anyone needs it. 
the bathroom was clean and stocked with toilet papers. i parked in the scurlock tower garage and it was $7 for up to 3 hours. not terrible in tmc.

writing a yelp review for a hospital seems silly since your review will likely depend on how your visit went and your diagnosis, but here i am. methodist is an excellent hospital in the greatest medical center in the country, and that's that on that. the complex is expansive and offers everything you need, plus more - an imaging center in the same building as a bank and jewelry store? sure, why not. i have only encountered friendly staff here and there are plenty of information desks scattered around to help you navigate the numerous towers. valet and self parking are offered and a fairly reasonable rate when you consider you have to pay to park anywhere in the med center these days.
no wonder united healthcare dumped you and was trying to get you to adjust pricing. ultrasound at methodist $1,240. exact same ultrasound elsewhere $120, yes 10 times as much as methodist.  #thievery

i'm giving them a 2 because i got out alive!  never go to the emergency medicine stand alone houston methodist clinic on voss road.  i came in dry heaving with chills and stomach cramps as symptoms i know to be moving into an adrenal crises.  i was too sick to talk and told them i live with addison's disease and they needed to talk to my medic alert team.  they refused to call the number on my medic alert bracelet!  then they took more than 40 minutes when standard protocol is 15 minutes to get me my emergency stress dose via iv.  they didn't even know if they had the drug!  the rn didn't even tell me when the emergency stress dose was put in my vein and refused to ask the doctor to give me the only anti nausea drug that works for me.  it was a horrible experience with zero management of my juvenile diabetes and at discharge they insisted i take the hotel garbage can with me that still had my stomach bile in it!  go to a full service er and not houston methodist when you have an emergency!   i did a review with their quality control patient services department and they stated i didn't require acute diabetes management, which i know from other similar emergencies with juvenile diabetes and addison's i absolutely required close management of both diseases.  incompetent doctor on the day of and no endocrine doctors on the review team, so how could they have the knowledge to judge what happened to me and what i required.   they couldn't.   this location moved like sloughs when i required emergency care!!'

my stepfather was admitted via the emergency room last weekend and spent four nights as an inpatient. he and my mother and i were treated wonderfully by so many people there. he was given the thorough and expert workup that he has been needing for months but could not get in his small town. everyone treated us kindly. as we try to find places in the hospital, hospital staff were constantly stopping to ask if they could help. and when we asked for something, the attitude of staff was to see if they could make it happen rather than two be annoyed with us if we wanted to do something differently. for example, i was standing in the hall outside my stepfather's door to give him privacy and to be available when needed. instead of telling me to move out of the way and go to the lounge, a staff member offered to go find me a chair. that kindness was so precious because of all the fear and pain we were going through. our hospitalist, dr. patel, investigated everything and answered all of our questions patiently. we left the hospital with confidence in the diagnoses that were given and the diagnoses that were ruled out. 
the only service that did not serve us very well was psychiatry. this was far short of the level of care we received by the other specialties.

poor excuse for a medical facility! my god mother was rushed by ambulance to the emergency room due to a tia. i left the area to make a private phone call and when i got back she had climbed out of her stretcher/over the bed rails and was leaning on a chair confused. i alerted the closest nurse whom responded with, "she is not my patient." i could not believe what i heard. what happened to the days when nursing meant that every patient is your patient especially in an emergency room setting. i could go on and on about the filth of the hospital and the rudeness of the staff but i'm going to end it here i give it zero stars‼

this hospital was detrimental in my father's health and basically killed him. he entered healthy and just needed help from geriatrics with medication side effects but they instead administered heavy duty psych drugs. dr scharma in the geri psych unit would not listen to me when i said my father has never been in a psych unit and was in a delirium from other medication. he administered new meds, more
meds, anti psychotics and the staff put my dad in restraints. my father was unable to talk, feed himself or speak after that. i had to hold a meeting with this incompetent doctor and the staff and demand all meds be stopped immediately. my father had no clinical
diagnosis for these meds. they made him so sick he ended up having heart problems and in a delirium for weeks. 

eventually he went into respiratory failure. he was trapped in bridgeport hospital for two months straight. he lost his bed at his long term care facility (he was only 74) and due to psych notes he could not get rehabilitation anywhere. but my father did not have psych issues. he had blood poisoning from his co2 build up from the respiratory failure his stay in psych did to him and from being bed ridden so long. bridgeport did no tests for this!! they let him stay in a room without tests being done as if he was fine. yale new haven ran the tests and  saw what was happening. he suffered immensely from bridgeport hospital , the staff was incompetent, un-empathetic and dr scharma is not fit to care for the elderly or anyone that needs  close attention. didnt matter that i was the healthcare proxy and knew my fathers entire medical history. my father needlessly suffered and went back and forth in and out of hospitals for months after bridgeport. 

he died december 2019, unable to ever get back to  
his baseline , and only with suffering propelled by the terrible two months of mistreatment in bridgeport hospital. i saw my father the first day he arrived at bridgeport and i saw him during and i saw him after. he went into a hospital that made  him worse than before and ultimately propelled him to death. 

no response from patient relations. i will be taking legal action. keep your family out of here.

this is the worst medical facility anyone can attend.  my wife has been there over a week.  they can not agree on a treatment plan.  never volunteer to be treated at this useless facility.  they should have their accreditation revoke. how can i send a reply. there is no link.  patient is in room 348a.

serious safety concerns. i tried following chain of command to resolve issues and it is near impossible to get leadership to talk let alone take ownership for their mistakes. staff doesn't wash hands and staff didn't check basic safety items like a name and date of birth when giving medications. multiple doctors with poor bedside manner. after surgery the surgeon never came out to let the family know the patient was out of surgery. 
 we observed the surgeon talk to other families and let them know their family member was out of surgery. we found out our family member was out of surgery when we saw our family member wheeled down the hallway to go back to their room. within an hour of  reaching the floor our family member was unstable and neededd to  be transferred to critical care.  so many other  safety concerns about dmc.
horrible horrible  hospital er is so bad my mom has been waiting for 3 almost 4 hours and still waiting for a doctor to see her and she's been in severe pain and still hasn't been seen

my husband and i were there on new year's eve. he had an aggressive infection and in a lot  of pain . the er staff took care of him immediately,  
with just a few questions from him and they knew exactly what to do to ease his pain and took great care with much empathy and kindness on their part . i cannot praise them enough. thank you with all my heart to the er people.

my aunt has been diagnosed with kidney cancer and the staff at doctors medical center have been very supportive and understanding of our feelings. the nurses and neurologists have been so informative and honest. the hospital as a whole is clean and quiet for the patients. the care has been so great everyone is helpful, patient, and very attentive to our needs. i want to send a special thank you to rebecca and brad in the e. r.  they were so respectful of our privacy and genuinely concerned for us and treated us like we were friends for awhile.  we can't thank them enough.
they literally saved my life and the care i received was fantastic. medical staff  could not have been any better.

i recently broke my hip and when i arrived by ambulance i was made to wait in a hallway for quite awhile amid police and people in handcuffs before being taken to a room for evaluation.  while in incredible pain, i was largely ignored, and finally taken to surgery after 26 hours, with the explanation that i was an "add on".  following surgery, patient care was minimal.  when i'd ring for a nurse during the night to help me get to the bathroom, i sometimes waited 10-15 minutes.  i was often told that they were understaffed, and rarely saw a nurse between 10pm and 7am.  the food was awful, and there seemed to be a disconnect between the hospitalist and my surgeon.  on the day i was to go home, they ordered my walker from the wrong company, causing me to wait an additional 6+ hours before i finally borrowed a walker from a friend and went home at 6pm.  no one ever informed my primary care physician of what had happened, and i was given little discharge information (like whether i could shower) - all in all a very disappointing experience.

recently had unilateral thyroid removal surgery at this facility.  surgery results were satisfactory (kudos to surgeon) but experience will cause me to not repeat using this facility:

before the procedure i told the surgeon and anesthesiologist that i had anxiety about the procedure and requested a pre-op sedative. my request was denied because i had to "walk to the operating room" (guess they don't have wheelchairs?). in the pre op area i sat in a recliner wearing my surgical robe. i walked to operating room #8 passing 7 operating rooms while on the march. once in the operating room, staff had me lay flat on the  operating table, put compression inflatables on the calves and tightly strapped me to the table in varies areas. i was in a near panic mood. when i came out of the anesthesia, i felt like my frontal lob was going to explode and had lost hearing in my right ear! thankfully my spouse was with me to instruct the nurse to relieve my severe pain with medication. 

yesterday my brother had surgery at scripps memorial, la jolla. i was with him. while in the pre op area on a gurney, the  anesthesiologist asked my brother if he wanted a sedative for anxiety? while waiting for his surgery, they kept him comfortable with a heated blanket, socks, and head cover. the nurses were friendly and attentive. after the surgery my brother told me that he gave the entire experience 5 stars; wish i could say the same for sharp.

absent few nursing/group exceptions, disconcerting empathic vacancy and deep defensiveness pervaded. sought alternative options starting day one, ultimately too far to be logistically feasible, after meeting the seemingly inculpating, difficult internist. folks are advised not to file complaints. instead, they're asked to speak with staff first; who were then entirely unwilling to hear feedback that wasn't per se congratulatory. literally unwilling. saw counselor rachel, the subject of a half dozen concerns, angrily approach and ask a 60 year old client in the waiting room, in front of 18-22 seemingly traumatized others, why he missed an appointment - instead of abiding by confidentiality laws (and instead of inquiring if he was ok)! consistently impervious to their impact on others in acuity, from intake forward. patient told (in voice mail, by a grumpy nurse manager) to call intake for an appointment. after complying, with five contacts over 2 weeks, there were zero return calls. patient left with no response or plan or information. what do they imagine is the experience on the other end? weeks of sleeplessness and confusion, hour after hour, visited on an historically at-risk client; all of which could have been eliminated with one call. reckless disregard for the person they purport to treat: the leading cause of death met with striking disregard for safey. rachel also oddly talked about another staff member leaving, after disclosing that she had been struggling for a while -- dumping the work load on rachel. there were too many areas of concern to adequately address in this forum. walked on eggshells around her and a few others. having seen/worked with/known myriad clinicians over time, this institution felt consistently maligning. perhaps elephants don't hire giraffes. please be on notice for recapitulative power dyad sequelae (e.g. waiting room antics' ramifications for witnesses). agencies of salience will be sent specific concerns, memorialized over time, as a last resort. first non-positive review for this author. upsetting treatment for those statistically at risk by the internist, p. a., intake, et al. will not refer here without systemic changes. felt compelled (morally obliged, perhaps) to turn some tables around this organization. having both earlier worked in excess of a decade in the mental health field during and after university, and also having earlier been treated absent reportable incident, this reluctant reviewer was struck by their dearth of psychological-mindedness and callousness. experienced them generally absent insight and palpably pathologizing, even as iatrogenic injury is the third leading cause of death. resent feeling obliged to obtain assistance in reporting as they were not receptive to any feedback. disappointing at best.

avoid this hospital's ct scan dept.  i accompanied a syrian refugee yesterday to get a ct scan. they had gone on their own before two weeks earlier and were told that the procedure was not authorized. his letter said to go to his doctor's office in the main hospital by 9:45am.  we did and were told we weren't supposed to be there, to go to the boyer bldg. we did, logged in, waited, saw the intake clerk and were told the procedure was not authorized. i indicated that was unacceptable because we had been told to come for it. the clerk went away, came back, and said it was okay, to go to the ct scan waiting area. a staff member took out paperwork.  we waited over two hours before i let them know we seemed to be overlooked. i was told our appointment was for 3pm. how is that possible, to have a doctor's appointment to evaluate the results at 10am and have the scan being evaluated at 3pm? again they relented and took the patient next. we then went back to the doctor to get the results of the scan. there i spoke to the patient relations mgr and his boss to get them to not put others through the same thing in the future. it is so stupid, incompetent, and bureaucratic it is almost hard to describe. the hospital botched the appointment telling us to go to the doctor first, not having the authorization, and not spotting or letting us know the appointment was at 3pm, and this was the second time the refuge had been told there that the procedure was not authorized.  it was authorized, at least once and most likely the earlier time also when he was told to go home (after a difficult trip to the hospital).

it's mind boggling how disorganized the place is.  somebody should be fired.

minus stars better describes this hospital. after my daughter aged out of a children's hospital, we were sent to this cesspool. i think she would have received better care from the corner crackhead. besides the one nurse who helped me change my daughter, the night nurse (male) the night before she died and the day nurse, the day she died, no one seems to know the meaning of care, compassion or dignity. seemed like my daughter was more of a nuisance. it's easy to see why this one nurse won the daisy award. one evening, my daughter was the only patient to one icu nurse. my daughter had wet herself and i asked the nurse for assistance in changing her. i see the nurse with her feet up on one chair, sitting in another on her cell phone. i decided after 15 minutes to ask again. she came back 5 minutes later handing me the linens and said she was getting a new admit and i could go ahead and change her myself or wait till she was done with her new patient whom wasn't even there yet. while you were reclining on your phone, maybe you should have been doing your job. at that point, i requested another nurse. that's  what i mean about giving someone their dignity. since my daughter was on a respirator, had many iv's and monitors, changing linens is a 2 person job. all the things i witnessed could fill a book. because the lack of care she received, her father, a nurse and myself, also in the medical field would tag team so she was never left alone. i feel they don't like when you are involved with your loved ones care. i guess you may see how terrible things can be. i think they make you as uncomfortable and unwelcome as can be. trust me, i slept on the floor that first night and would do it all again. i always thought family involvement is important to a patient's care. sadly my daughter did not make it out of there. it all went downhill when she developed sepsis. my advice to families, be involved, ask questions, be that squeaky wheel. to temple, i sure am squeaky and i promise not to stop squeaking
i had an amazing experience at st luke's. everyone was respectful and caring and allowed me the best recovery and outcome for my surgery! i will recommended them everytime

very unprofessional. the hospital is in the red and is currently dealing with issues concerning their financials. there are management issues and staffing issues due to the lack of professionalism in management. discrimination is also present. i would reccomend finding a better facility for care considering all of this affects the quality of care that is to be provided.

if you need a great pacu nurse i recommend marissa she is very conscientious and has a great caring persona

review:
i wouldn't go here if you have an unknown emergency, especially if it requires deduction tests to be run to find out what the underlying issue is, because they are only going to do minimum procedures, except for performing and charging you for major procedures like an mri if your insurance allows it. 

they also are not going to listen to what your medical allergies are and they're just going to prescribe to you whatever it is they want to give you.

next they're not going to give you any pain medication because they're going to say that you're a drug seeker or a drug addict, even if you need pain medication, which all is completely unprofessional and irresponsible.

furthermore my insurance company paid banner over $6000 for my er visit, where they ended up making me more sick than when i went in there, and when i disputed the additional $1200 they said i owed them they told me that the doctor did not prescribe medication to me that i was allergic to and i told them they did and that it was in my medical records. they sent me to collections!

instead of looking in my medical records the director called me a liar - well i have a picture of the medication showing that he did prescribe me medication that i was allergic to. andi wouldn't believe a word they have to say

so it looks like yelp removed one of my complaints regarding banner emergency and also remove the response from banner emergency representatives after they requested information from me and then failed to do anything about the situation, again. my review stands.

review:
i anonymously donated a kidney in january of 2019. the process was smooth until right after surgery. communication was lost and no one, because of the anonymity of the donation process, could tell my wife where i was. at one time, telling my wife i wasn't at banner. then, there was a three hour wait to get me a room! in this whole process i wasn't a vip...i will get to this issue later. the nursing staff was horrible. i am a medic, so i do understand the issues of working on a ward and the short staffing problems. i also have seen nurse burnout, but there are patients who love to complain about anything and everything - that is not me. i was a military medic for a decade and know there are things we can do in medical to help. i've also seen people on medical wards that can't make it in the ed, icu or any other specialty and show up on medical wards. my pain management was the worse i've ever seen, and i was in enough pain to regret donating. i didn't sleep for 48 hours because of the incredible pain i was in.
dr. harland assured me that he - because he was opening me up inches from my umbilical hernia, that he would fix that. i had an incision there, but it seems nothing was done/fixed. surprise!  
to spit in my face, i was recently sent an anesthesiology bill from the hospital! donners are not supposed to be billed for donating! hello! i've been told that this is "common"! your assured that this will not happen prior to donation. so, my issue is this - kidney recipients use their insurance, so they are the vip. i've ran into two other anonymous donners and they echo my feelings of the process..." thanks for the kidney, bye, bye". i can't prove that they "skimped" on my care, pain meds, etc., but i went home with less pain meds from the kidney transplant, than the meds i got months earlier from a tendon reattachment. thankfully i only used three days' worth and had leftovers. i don't know if the recipient received vip care - i will never know, but i can only hope she (i know it was a 30ish female) is doing well and did received great care - i did not. 
while the shortage of donners that is needed grows, i wish they could incentivize people to donate. no, not monetarily, but by insisting doctor, nurses and the process of donation makes you feel like a vip. i don't need someone fawning over me, but if i felt like a patient that was doing a good thing through exceptional care, i would have appreciated my donation more. if i were you - i would go to the pain/travel of donating in phoenix and stay away from banner umc.

i arrived at 10:30am, they drawn blood, left me in the waiting area. currently been here 3 1/2 hours waiting to be seen and i told them i  am in pain. if i could give negative stars i would. they claim they have rooms for every body so patients won't leave and that's bull crap and now people are piling in. no one will give a answer to when i will get seen.going on 41/2 hours still not seen still in pain and point out to them that my urine cup has been sitting on the desk for almost 2 hours. this place is a freaking joke.

this company is entirely unethical and unequipped. 

administration and practitioners shared my medical records with other parties without my legal authorization, thus breaking patient confidentiality. 

administration and practitioners scheduled appointments for dates that i was unaware, and sent bills when i missed appointments i had no idea i was supposed to attend. 

administration and practitioners repeatedly made false claims about my insurance coverage (i.e. assured me that ear wax removal was included in co-pay, assured me blood work was covered in full by my insurance at the time). 

administration and practitioners were not transparent about policies, and this led to large bills for unnecessary procedures (i am in great physical health) that i cannot fully pay due to poverty-level income. 

practitioners provided insufficient treatments and diagnoses, which then exacerbated symptoms, on top of aforementioned administrative tomfoolery (i.e. inappropriately sharing records, scheduling appointments without notifying patients or even seeing if patient is available for scheduled time). 

any company that is not transparent about policies to clients is negligent and unethical. maine medical acts in accordance to negligence and unethical practice.

i have been visiting folks at maine med for years, in my work as a pastor i visit folks here several times a year. the staff have always treated me with respect and are very helpful. the care of the folks i have visited has been second to none within our state. it's clean, and although it can be hard to navigate at first but the signage is great so if you take your time you will find where you need to go. parking is easy and usually not hard to find. if you or a loved one has serious health issues that need medical attention this is the place in maine you want to be.

we could not believe how dirty this hospital is.  first off, everyone going from the parking garage into the hospital has to go to p8 level, when you get off that elevator there is not even a trash receptacle before you enter the hospital.  
in the entry hallway, there is a hand sanitizer dispenser on the wall along with a box of tissues.  but no wastebasket in which to place your used tissue, so they either end up on the floor or you can take the germy mess into the hospital with you. 
inside, the trash receptacles are often overflowing.  
the patient rooms are too warm so they have portable fans.  if you have lung surgery they might as well just shoot you dead, because the fans blowing on your face are so filthy....they have dust imbedded onto all the blades and cobwebs and dirt on the fan grill.  f i l t h y and d i s g u s t i n g and i have sent two photos to the health department.  no wonder the poor patients are all coughing. 
and one final note....the cafeteria is an embarrassment  nothing has changed since we were there 20 years ago.  no healthy entree options just burgers, pizza, hot dogs and grease.   the hot dogs are tri-colored...grey, brown and greenish.  the burgers are definitely not all-beef but made of gristle and fat and leather.  yes there is a salad bar but who would dare go near it?  
the waiting rooms for ccitu are overcrowded and disgusting. there is a dusty dirty vacuum cleaner sitting in the waiting room corner, it looks like the dust bag hasn't been emptied for years.  ....apparently we visitors are supposed to vacuum the place ourselves when things get too germy and  unacceptable.  mavis was an old lady visiting her husband.  we all had to lift our feet every two hours whenever mavis decided to vacuum the joint.

i was seen in the ed of mmc located in ptld. i have been seen there many times over the years. on this particular occasion,  the ed was extremely busy so i was placed in the hall.  i was not given an iv. i wasn't given anything really,  just waited for  ct scan. several hours later,  which i do understand given how busy the ed was,  i got the ct scan,  was told i had kidney stones and was referred to follow up with my doctor.  the  pain had subsided on its own.  when i recieved the $3000 bill,  i was astounded.  i was charged for a room,  iv, nursing care,  e.t.c just as though i'd had all those services.  it's "bundled billing" but i literally had none of those services.  just by being "admitted" to the ed you are charged $1000 (just under actually,  about $980) for a package of services. i have a deductible,  like most folks.  i'm now playing about $1000 for services i never recieved! i disputed it and my dispute was denied.  thank you maine med,  for stealing from me. i understand this is common hospital practice but it's wrong,  it's unethical,  it's stealing. what is a person left to do but pay it? it's not okay! our system is so broken!

longest wait in the er ever.. before checking in, there was a bunch of questions needed to be ask i really didn't have the strength to do so. i was completely exhausted i could stand, but barely talk. it took more than 2 hours to get checked in, so i'm like really? didn't have that patience right now.. i did what i had to. i did have a pleasant interaction with sandra though i believe that was her name. i got here with my aunt around 11 or 12. check out completed at around 8 p.m. felt better after taking some iv. took a lloong time.

going to the er is the worst. it's loud, stressful, and you have to wait forever. so i wasn't exactly thrilled to find myself in the er on a friday night in need of emergency surgery. but even though i was stressed, sore, and miserable this was still one of my best hospital experiences. from the moment i was checked in everyone did their best to make me as comfortable as possible, frequently going above and beyond the call of duty. they were attentive, friendly, listened to my concerns, anticipated my needs, and cared just as much about how i was doing emotionally as physically. my wife was allowed to stay with me the entire time (with the exception of the operating room of course) and hold my hand as i went under anesthesia which made things so much less stressful. the doctors also included her in all the discussions about my healthcare and called her on her cell the second i was out of surgery, which helped my wife feel much less scared. 

the room i was put in to recover was really nice (nicer that some hotel rooms!) and even had a pull out bed so my dad could spend the night with me. the food at lgh is also really good (and cheap!) and both my wife and father enjoyed eating there. my wife was especially thrilled they had a milkshake machine. ;) my dad is a doctor and can get super judgey when it comes to hospitals, but even he was impressed by the quality of care (not to mention my room and the cafeteria food lol).

highlights of lgh include:
- when i developed a migraine the nurses turned down the lights and put cloths on my eyes in addition to giving me pain meds.
- the cafeteria was closed but i was famished for the nurse got me easy to digest food from her break room 
- they also made sure my wife was comfortable and would bring her chairs and blankets while she waited with me
- both the er doctor and the surgeon were willing to call my dad and give him updates (with my permission of course) even though he was being a pest. the surgeon even gave my dad his personal cell so he could call with questions.
- the er nurse basically hunted down the or folks when she felt they weren't getting to me fast enough, and would go out of her way to find the answers to any questions i had
- they heated up the blankets so i was warm and toasty and basically made a comfortable little nest of blankets and pillows for me 
- the staff ordered me a tray full of clear liquids to eat right after my surgery since they knew i'd be hungry, i didn't even have to ask. 
- everyone was friendly and funny, which really put me at ease. even in such a miserable situation they were able to make me laugh. 

definitely a five star er!

checking into the er was the worst experience. not only was i having issues with breathing, the bigger lady was completely rude. and then, it took almost 2 hours to be seen by a doctor, while i see people that checked in after me, get called in to see a doctor first. hello!! i can't breathe!! did you guys forget about me!? or did the bigger lady at the desk just not give two sh*ts? you're better off going to a different hospital.
it's all about the money even with insurance they are now using nurse practitioner in place of drs yet charging drs prices. stay away from this hospital

my husband was brought to the hospital by ambulance because his primary care staff thought he was having a stroke. the doctor ordered a ct scan where it was shown that he did in fact have a stroke. they put him on the machine to watch his blood pressure,and ordered a mri. the dr came in and said they were giving him a new medicine and wanted to watch his blood pressure because it was 200/103. the nurse( sarah) came in at 6:30 and gave him the new medicine. they came and took him for the mri and he got back to the room at 7:30. we  never saw a nurse again that night. we repeatedly rang the bell and stood in the hall and everyone walked right by. i finally stopped someone because it was now 12:00 midnight and he hadn't been hooked up to the blood pressure machine this whole time. a nurse from another area came and hooked him back up. my husband's pressure was still very high. we had also asked for some food for him around 7:30 which never came,my daughter went out and got him something. at 12:30 i asked who his nurse was,i was told jo. i said i wanted to see her (it was now 1:00 in the morning). she finally came in! she proceeded to tell me that they were very busy,and this is what happens when they leave patients who were already admitted in the er. they don't have time for them because they have their own patients. she left never to be seen again. at 4:30 a nurse kelsey and an aid molly i think came to take my husband upstairs to d4. they were so nice,and took great care of both me and my husband. i was in tears by then. my husbands treatment on d4 was amazing. all the staff was great particularly his nurse kirsten the next day. we both would never go back to this hospital again however. we usual go to the saints campus and will continue to do so.
actually i like the doctors and nurses here. but the receptionist on the second floor is such a nasty man. i don't know how he  can keep his job.  just be aware!!!

went to the er new years eve , the time in was fast and my wife was taken right away, infection in jaw dr prescribed antibiotic ruled out wisdom teeth , saw slight blotches may be on set of shingles did ekg just to make sure nothing else was going on .recommended to see family dr asap. satisfied!! saw family dr after new years day.. and she determined shingles on side of face prescribed the proper treatment .in the process 1 day later my wife got bels palsy  . face drooped and we headed to the er. let me tell you , the nurse treat her to the upmost of seriousness ,took her right away, the dr checked everthing to rule out symptoms other than shingles , i always had a negative to say in the past, but these 2 experiences  have been so positive, thank you dr slagel & dr o'shura. for your  help , we left here with the upmost confidence, this place has come a long way to reach this level of service , thank you staff,walter schilling.

at rehab hospital they expect you to work hard with your therapy. three hours a day of pt, ot, st, but they get you better. he complained a bit about the therapy, but i know it was the best for him! 

the nurses were very friendly and came in a timely manner. we also appreciated the updates with dr. nomura. overall a really great experience and i highly recommend them if you qualify for inpatient rehab.

used to be a hospital that gave me a profound experience to being one of my worst stays at a given place, ever. i was under a voluntary stay at the bhs unit, and what i witnessed under sane conditions was tremendously scary/awful. not just towards myself, but seeing how the nurses treated disabled patients was so heartbreaking. 75% of the staff were overtly aggressive towards every patient for no apparent reason. i understand they get dealt with a lot of crazies, but people like myself do come in to heal themselves. dealing with the same environment they are with harsher terms being under medications that destroy your mind. (ativan) my last stay i went under a stressful situation, every time i spoke with my assigned psychiatrist, i stated i wasn't suicidal and that i was just tired from the medications. ativan has a negative after effect on me, and i told them that. they proceeded to do their "im's" because i called out a nurse on her abuse towards a patient and i was aggravated they were talking down on me for asking for basic clothing necessity. the nurse that i am referring to literally pushed a patient. i saw it with my own eyes. this time at the hospital i wasn't "delusional" or under an episode. i just voluntarily checked myself in to reprogram my thoughts considering my first experience was beneficial. welp, yelp reviewers, never again am i coming to this awful hospital. that goes to anyone who cares for their family member or themselves. make sure you understand that nurses can be equally as traumatizing and horrible as the people scrutinized inside these facilities. be careful who you trust, because i was mortified my entire stay at mission community. you guys suck.

my son was born in the hospital and had to spend over 80 days in the nicu since he was 13  weeks early . let me say, if it wasn't for the nurses and doctors i don't think he would have made it . i would recommend this hospital for anyone's maternity choice. the labor and delivery room was big . every thing was modern . the nicu was great , they also have separate rooms to pump as needed .  i still take him to all the doctors associated with westchester medical

unacceptable care and behaviors for an er emergency facility. zero sense of urgency coupled with a rather blasé and detached view of patient care from professionals. 

my wife had a level ii trauma and was sent via ambulance to westchester medical. we enter reception and guess what?...no one is there. we stand around and wait 5-10 mins for someone to show up which is just unacceptable for an er. 

we finally get admitted, get my wife a bed and the place looks like a third world trauma center after a disaster. patients moaning and groaning with beds cluttered in the hallways and basically no one attending to them. then nurses and doctors with loud conversation about their weekend plans and quite literally all of them (some 7-8) sitting behind their computers all day vs looking after patients. if i took a picture of this, you would not believe what it looked like. i couldn't help but think how much more effective these people would be if they were actually attending to their patients in their rooms vs tweaking patient's records behind a computer. it was very disconcerting to say the least. 

then each time my wife needed anything, it was quite literally a 1-2 hour delay for the requested item. wife asks for ice chips...45 mins. wife is in dire pain and in need of pain meds...1 hour delay and being told in a very nasty tone about how they had to get approval for the meds even though just hours before another nurse had given her the exact same meds. then xrays done without any pain meds in her and even though my wife is tough as nails, she is literally screaming and shaking in pain based on her injuries. why didn't they give my wife morphine or fentanyl prior to moving her around for xrays when the staff were fully aware of her pain level??

wife is finally stable enough to get cleared for a bed in the main hospital and even though we were told beds were ready, they couldn't get a porter to transport her for another 3 1/2 hours. 

further, each and every time i interacted with the staff they were nasty and condescending. is this what they teach these people in nursing or med schools these days? then a doctor is dictating notes to a more junior staff and within earshot of every one in the er about someone they were admitting that had issues with suicidal tendencies amd ideation and was giving complete details on some very personal stuff. where is the professionalism here? what about a patients right to confidentiality? 

i have to ask, where is management here?? didn't see any sign of a head nurse or anyone with any real authority managing staff and ensuring that patients were given proper treatment. 

the icing on the cake was that my wife never even got to see a dr for her trauma...only a pa and that's after being in the er for about 10 hours. 

on a more positive note, when we did go to the main hospital, they were terrific in all respects except one. the one exception was promises by the case worker/social worker to followup with us on after care and basically never did even after we made 2 followup calls to her and still waiting for a response from her. also told by pt group and acute care facility that they also reached out to her but no response. 

never thought i would be writing a yelp review on a hospital, but that er experience was just bad enough to warrant a review.
