worst hospital ever.  care there is terrible, especially on the 7th floor.  god help the patients who have to go to this nightmare of a place!  something needs to be done and quick!

worst experience in the er. i got to the hospital around 7:15am. nobody was in the waiting room. they took my vitals and the lady walked me into the hallway and had me sit on a bed and said, "you can stay right here someone will be coming to get you very quickly." over an hour goes by and nobody had even approached me. meanwhile i am right by where all the nurses are on their computers. i can hear all of the conversations going on about what they ate the night before, about a guy dying in the trauma unit, the weather...one lady was on her cell phone and another twerking in the hallway. i couldn't even believe my eyes. i was so sick and nobody had even come to ask if i needed anything. finally a doctor came to me and asked what was going on, mind you this was his first day. he checked my breathing and discussed my issue in the hallway. i was never given a room or anything. he sent me for x rays, had to wait close to another hour because nobody was there. they took my x ray and walked me back to "my bed" in the hallway while i was in a gown. i was so uncomfortable. then the doctor comes over and diagnoses me with upper respiratory infection, prescribed me no medication. 3 days later i was getting worse and worse. i went to urgent care by my house where they took way better care of me (did a proper check up and a flu test). they told me i had bronchitis and now i'm on medication and feeling better. i will not be going back to westchester medical. they are unprofessional and i did not feel i was cared for at all.

disaster!  terrible environment from the moment you enter the main hospital.  employees who appear miserable and the total aura is a disregard for human dignity.  if i could give zero stars, i would.  myself and family members have been a patient of several hospitals in the tristate area, and i have never had reason to complain regarding the treatment or the overall experience from these other hospitals. we were sent to wmc by another local hospital that felt a traumatic pelvic fracture would be best treated there.  once we arrived and she was there a day or 2, they questioned why she came to wmc.  trust me if i could have magically returned my mom to the previous hospital(not far from wmc,  off of i 287 and an amazing facility) i certainly would have.  there are too many issues to describe but suffice it to say, my main complaint was a total lack of empathy shown towards my 88 year old mom.

i have lived in many states and i'm over 60 years oldand work as an x-ray technician in many hospitals throughout my life and i have never seen a hospital as disgusting or poorly run as westchester medical center the building looks like a 1950s insane asylum that they just pulled the bars off the window last week the staff could care less my father was extremely sick in a room with another person who is also extremely sick no single rooms so i guess if you want your roommate's disease you can have it my dad's roommate coughed on a constant basis i overheard the doctor say he had pneumonia i guess they didn't care if my dad caught pneumonia from his coughing also the blood pressure machine heart monitor and other equipment did not work so the nurses had to bring portable machines in to check his blood pressure every once in a while and when i say once in awhile i mean not very often at all for a 90 year old man in the hospital for bad blood pressure they alsoleft my father with staples in his leg after surgery for almost a month staples must be removed within a week or they start to scar and become infected not to mention the scar left is worse members of my family requested they attend to his staples and surgical wound many times with no response or even interest they told us maybe they'll take the staples out out when he goes to the old folks home i thought he was in the hospital i guess i was wrong  i work in the medical industry and i know what's good and what's bad i would rather go to a veterinary hospital than this mess ps there's no parking

review:
my prior foster daughter is currently in icu.  she was pregnant and roofied and went into a coma.   the baby was born deceased yesterday.  there is a homicide investigation.  her body is filing up with fluid due to kidney failure and she is not urinating, so it is getting worse.  

it is now almost 2pm, they were supposed to do the mri yesterday.  every day that goes by they tell us they will do an mri and dialysis, but keep telling us more urgent cases are coming in and being moved ahead of her.   the doctors are very dismissive.  

the doctor just told the family there is nothing life threatening about her current kidney failure.

to make matters worse, my foster daughter was married years ago and never did the paperwork (nor did her x) to dissolve it.   they are in a ferocious custody battle and there was abuse involved.   

he is now making decisions for her life.   we sent all of the criminal records to the hospital to fix this so that we could obtain emergency guardianship and her biological sister could take over making decisions to save her life.  the doctor has to sign the paperwork for her to take to the courthouse and also has not had time to put the pen to the paper.... so if the lack of medical care doesn't kill her, the x-husband may.   

if a fatality occurs, i will hire an attorney and report it to the joint commission.

if i could give this place 0 stars i would! my father is currently at this hospital in the observation unit. the doctors ran a stress on his heart, and the nurse informed me after i called to check on my father, that the doctor found some ischemia in his heart, and therefore might need to perform surgery. 

however, my father was never informed of this!!!!! it wasn't until i spoke with him and told him myself!!!! i'm out of state stressing over my father's health thinking he may need heart surgery, my father is clueless about what's going on!!! 

furthermore, after waiting a few hours i called back up to the hospital, to find out if my dad is going to have surgery and the nurse told me that the cardiologist told her no he is not. but no call to me nothing, and no information about why no surgery will be performed if he's doing better or not! i just called my dad myself and told him that the nurse said he not about to have surgery now.and like me hes wondering what's going on because no one is telling him nor me !!!!

i sympathize with all the negative reviews here but honestly this has been the best hospital experience i've ever had. if they suspect that you have a serious condition, they will take great care of you. the care and kindness of the staff was fantastic and i only wish that this hospital would be in my own home town.

i arrived at er with my family around 5 am because of suspected food poisoning. after a short 10 minute wait, i was able to see the triage nurse and after telling her my symptoms and some of my past health problems i've been facing the past year. she immediately ordered a blood test and an abdominal scan. i was also given an iv drip and medication to help with the nausea and pain while waiting for the results. after an hour and half to wait for the blood test and scan results, i was diagnosed with a serious condition that would require surgery. 

the nurses and doctors were very patient and professional with both mine and my family concerns. we were considering driving home to our city to have the surgery done because we were planning to return home that day if not for me getting sick and the staff were really accommodating in trying to help us prepare myself to get home with medication/paperwork if that was our choice. in the end, due to the seriousness/pain of my condition, we had the surgery done here and we were able to be booked into surgery by that afternoon!

each member of the surgery staff introduced themselves and answered every question about my procedure. the nurses even brought multiple warmed up blankets when i mentioned i was a bit chilly! the rooms in pre-op and recovery were comfortable and generally pretty private, though we were separated by a curtain. 

the procedure went without issues and for my overnight stay, i was well looked after and monitored. if i had any issues, the nurses came within moments after hitting the call button. i feel so much better now and i can't thank the staff at sunrise enough for their care.

im soooo frustrated! my dad has been back to this hospital for the 3rd time today in the past 13 days. his first visit he was diagnosed with epididymitis of the scrotum. he wasnt sent home with antibiotics. the second day came around just 2 days after and was given an ultrasound and they diagnosed him with an abscess of the scrotum. they admitted hiim to the hospital to wait for the  next day so he can see a surgeon who specializes in urology. today is the day of the surgery we saw the surgeon who explained the procedure as an i&d which means incision and drainage. hours later he was brought up to his room nurse said that the procedure went well with no concerns.  my dad was kept in the hospital for 2 days my dad was still complaining about testicular pain but they assured him and fourth i told him what the surgeon told me before he operated on him he stated that what i was saying was false because he saw the surgeons clinicals and they didnt not expressed that. i told him dr now told me that it is not an abscess that its an infection with cellulitis!

review:
i'll start by saying i very rarely get sick. i got strep throat a month ago, and never really feel like i made it back to 100%, which is unusual for me.  i went in today for an appointment due to spitting up blood with a severe sore throat. coincidentally, when i woke up this morning i had a nasty rash on my arm. my job requires me to work around the homeless population. it's not super uncommon to come into contact with someone with mrsa, so i figured i'd get that looked at as well. 

when the nurse took me to the room, which was relatively quick after i checked in, she asked me what i was there for. i told her my throat, but that i also wanted to get my arm looked at. she tells me i can only discuss one medical complaint, and that i'd need to come back to discuss the rash on my arm with a doctor! i was completely taken back by that. she said i'm only allotted 15 minutes with the doctor.  so if i have four complaints, do i need to make four appointments? she offered to assist me in setting up another appointment...

a few minutes later the doctor walks in. he's talking with me about my throat. about a minute into the conversation, the nurse knocks on the door. the doctor  welcomes her in. she says "doctor, the patient in room ___ was waiting here first." she literally interrupted my 15 minute appointment to tell the doctor someone was waiting  before me. what a joke.

so the doctor tells me everything is fine with my throat. i mention the rash on my arm. he tells me he suspects  it is mrsa, but tells me they don't do anything to treat it. he tells me  "people just kinda live with it."  uh...pretty sure people just kinda die from it. no antibiotics prescribed, no cares given. this was absolutely ridiculous. so now i have to make another appointment and pay another co-pay to get this looked at by someone else. absolutely pathetic.

review:
the hospital is recently new.  the facility is immaculate.  the staff is personable and many are very compassionate.  the food trays are excellent and have a good variety.  guest trays are reasonably priced.  a pullout bed is available for spouses or caregivers to stay overnight.  parking is a bit of a challenge due to the number of people being served.  usually, the doctors are tops. however, i doubt that i will ever go there for care in the future.  they are clearly understaffed.  

example #1:   my wife has a bladder problem.   she had just come out of knee replacement surgery.  about 3 hours later, she wet the bed because the nurse or aide did not answer the call in a reasonable time.  other calls were made.  my wife told me that she laid in her own urine from 7:00 pm to nearly 7:00 am.  it appears that the night shift may have had too much to do.

example #2:  one of the doctors decided that she was getting too much pain medication.  without contacting the surgeon who prescribed it, the doctor adjusted (reduced) the medicine to fit his wishes.   my wife subsequently complained of severe pain.  after over an hour of intense pain (she said the pain was a 12 on a scale of 1 to 10) she was finally told that a nurse would be in in about 20 minutes.  prior to that she had also called because she was wet again.  it was about an hour and a half before she received additional pain medication and about two hours of laying in her own urine again before they came and took her to the bathroom.

example #3  while i was taking my wife's suitcase to the car, the discharge papers were being given to my wife without my presence even though i would be the caretaker for the next few weeks.    when we got home and i started reviewing the information, the names of the  drugs on the paperwork didn't even match those on the pill bottles, and the amounts were duplicated.  i literally had to write down the scripts of ten different bottles and their bottle directions so i would know what and when to give.  

example #4:  as stated above, pain did not seem to be an issue for the staff.  upon discharge, my wife was taken to my car in a wheel chair.  as soon as she was pushed to the car, the attendant left.  my wife was in so much pain and so stiff from the bandages and surgery that she was nearly unable to get into the car.  we had to have her scoot herself along the back seat with me on the other side of the back seat helping to pull her in before we could even get the doors closed...all this without anyone from the hospital staff helping.  i almost took her to back to the hospital to be readmitted as she was in so much pain that it appeared that i would not be able to  accommodate her needs.  it was about four hours later after giving her the drugs that should have been administered in  the hospital that my wife was finally relieved of much of her pain.

i started by saying that the staff is compassionate.  when someone finally did come to my wife's aid, they were very kind and willing to assist.  so was the staff guilty of  incompetence?  doubtful?  lack of staffing?  likely.
one more note.  after my wife had laid in urine for an hour and a half without assistance, i arrived in the hospital and went into the hallway to solicit help since the pager on the bed was soliciting no response.  two women (nurses or nurses aids) were sitting together talking to one another right outside of my wife's room.  one did tell me that she would get a nurse, and she also helped take my wife to the restroom and clean the bed.  but why did it take an advocate to get help?

iu claims that newsweek has given them a top ten rating for hospitals.  my experience with the care given to my wife would say the bottom ten.

i wish i could give zero stars. i have been here twice and won't be back every time it's a beyond ridiculous wait time, rude staff, and provider patient communication is always terrible you sit there forever just waiting not knowing what's going on. it's a shame especially with it being fairly new

maestro!!! the best surgeon one can ask for.  dr. magnant is quite simply an amazing surgeon.  as a cancer patient who has been on a journey from diagnosis to surgery with dr magnant and her team for the past 6 months, i can not ask for a more compassionate human being, one who truly cares about her patients and one whom to put your total trust in through the journey.  she has a delightful sense of humor and has the gift of making the otherwise arduous journey tolerable. she is a dedicated professional and follows up to check on her patients and never let's you feel alone in the process.  there is nothing more one can ask for in a surgeon.  top notch!!

review: i have chrohn's, and heard that the gastro department at methodist is awesome. while there were more tests run, i don't feel like any better value was given. the facilities inside seemed about the same as most hospitals. nothing better. a few honorable mentions-tracy in ct was awesome and caring even at 3am. roxanne in x-ray made sure i was comfortable for the hours long series done, and jessica young, went above and beyond to clean the bed i was assigned that smelled awful when i got it. she sanitized everything. also, superior excellence from chris, who corrected my iv, and stuck a new one on the first try with no machine! so glad he wasn't a digger like the others. keesha answered my questions well, and was a thorough nurse. the er triage was nice, not very thorough, but once in a room they got things recorded. they used a machine to look for my vein. they dropped the alcohol swab on the floor, used it again with dirt specs and all for the second go round on the second dig for an iv. on the whole, i have more tests to take back to my doctors, i was pushed out faster, i don't feel i gained from the experience, and this flare isn't over. they have some great staff, and some that should leave healthcare. staff seemed happy, though. on providing holistic care, and follow through with all of the tests, i don't think that goal was accomplished for me. overall, they did their job, and have some great community resources. i was hoping for a more connected experience.

the rehab facility does look good, so for an outpatient or a patient who can already get themselves to a restroom it is probably ok.  the check-in staff is nice.

if you bring a loved one here as inpatient you have to advocate tirelessly for them to ensure they are clean and to support their dignity and recovery.

review:
the layout is confusing, signage mediocre at best, and parking can be baffling and frustrating as all get-out (especially near the er). the er has a door wide open to the outside world, so patients and visitors in the waiting room freeze their tuchuses off. the bureaucracy can be frustrating.

so why four stars? mostly, it's the people. nearly every person i've encountered there over the years is competent, helpful, friendly, and willing to go out of their way. it's a beautiful facility in nice surroundings, somewhat conveniently located (route 68 can be a bit hairy). and as others have mentioned--the art on display is awesome.

review:
sitting at work one fine day, when sudden pain in my chest, hard to breathe, sweating, dizzy... yup, major cardiac event. dr. guru khalsa was and is an amazing physician, with an excellent bedside manner and a good, keen head on his shoulders. he made a good call on the diagnosis and subsequent surgery, and i'm here to write another epic review.

the nursing staff at chomp is beyond compare. in all the years i've lived here and visited this facility, i have never had need to say anything but the absolute best about these dedicated, hard working  linchpins of medical support. always cheerful, always going the extra mile, always doing way more than one could possibly imagine to make a difficult situation as easy and pleasant as possible. really, i could go in for days about the stellar care from the nursing staff here. just beyond compare in every possible way, in every department.

doctors are very much a personality based, subjective judgement. in my experience here, 99% of these hard working folks are exemplary across the board. they always seem to have all the time you need to understand where you were, why you got where you are, and the best possible way forward.

i'm not saying all this great stuff just because i'm feeling euphoric over having my life saved. these folks are the absolute best i've encountered anywhere.

of course, every rainbow has a shadow (not literally, but...) and at chomp you will find that all that excellent, high end care comes with a supremely high end price. they say good health is priceless, and chomp billing takes that to the extreme. still, what's your life worth? 

i happen to be lucky enough that i feel i have a really great life. so i'll pay that price, and be grateful that i'm around to pay.
fac_name: Community Hospital of the Monterey Peninsula

review:
nice fish and art, but......my brother is there for acute pancreatitis, then kidney failure, sepsis, big stuff!! 

many issues with care. there are good folks there for sure and many of the docs were fine, but the communication between not so good. brother's girlfriend had to tell them about his blue feet & disorientation that turned out to be sepsis. understand, with acute pancreatitis and kidney failure sepsis is to be looked for. you can die 12hrs! many hospitals have a sepsis response team for just this situation. someone not in an icu, regular bed, but can turn bad quick. chomp does not.

blood sample from the wrong room, directions by doc not being followed or relying on patient on pain meds to track??! they did not consistently track & measure urine in a kidney failure patient, fed him foods he was not supposed to have..basic stuff. these were things after being told twice or complained about not doing by doctor and friends who were trying to track.

i think most of you know, but always have friends\family there with someone in the hospital to be their advocate. chomp, you can do better.

identify the ones not paying attention, treating hurting patients roughly, follow protocol and get rid of the ones that don't care. they sure seemed to care about themselves when my brother got c.diff (hospital bacterial infection by the way they are required to report) due to his lowered immune system. certainly isn't helping his other medical issues! 17 days and counting..

review:
took my husband back to chomp er this evening.  while the triage nurse, registration and the er tech who takes vitals are fantastic!  they know us by sight!  on the other hand, the er doctor, dr. collins, is a joke.  

we experienced some horrible care by this doctor over the past couple of months.  my husband has several bulging discs in his neck and bone spurs which are pressing on the nerves in his neck for which i've taken him to chomp for help.  

so this evening, i took my husband to the er, like i said, and dr. collins came into the exam room, even after we said we wanted another doctor.  he went on to say that he was the only doctor back in express care.  wrong!!!  dr. ellison was there and so was the physician's assistant.  dr. collins then said "well what are we supposed to do for you tonight?"  i explained that my husband was experiencing some urological problems and could they be caused by the bulging discs in his neck that are pressing on some nerves. dr. collins said "the mri didn't really show any significant problems".  he needs to go back to school and learn how to read. 

we then asked him to try and contact the neurologist and he blatantly lied and said that this doctor didn't have privileges at chomp.  wrong again!!  according to the neurologist's profile on the hospital website, it clearly states that he has privileges at chomp. 

i then asked dr. collins about a recent discharge summary and he said that he never did these reports.  well, i located it in relay health portal and showed it to him.  i won't go into what it said for privacy reasons.  he read it and said that he stands by what he said.  one thing it did state was that my husband was trying to take out his iv.  my husband isn't stupid enough to do this.

chomp has this program called edie which stands for emergency department information exchange.  according to an er nurse, this is something that automatically tracks the number of er visits you've had in a short period of time.  well, if you're a senior citizen without a primary care doctor, what the h**l are you supposed to do when you're in pain, can't swallow or pee?  they don't tell you about this program and even the people in the administration that i talked to, didn't know anything about it.  

we left when it was clear that nothing was going to be done.  after we got home, i pulled out the after visit summary and under reason for visit, dr. collins put down neck pain.  wrong again!  we went in for a urological problem.

the er tech didn't even clean up the room that we were in.  i saw a bottle of a numbing medicine that's injected on the tray along with what looked like bandaging strips.  i did take pictures but i won't post them. i'm keeping them to show the administration when i talk to them tomorrow.

came to this kaiser panorama city pharmacy for an emergency medication written by my pcp. thankfully, i looked at my member benefits and it said no charge for this medication. however, when i went to check out i was informed by the pharm tech that i need to pay retail price for it because she said it's not emergency and that routine medications are consider emergency. uhh, no sweetie, when the medication has the word "emergency" on it, it's considered emergency and medication you take every day to prevent something is not considered emergency. kaiser really need to look at education when hiring their pharmacy tech. anyways i told her to bill it to me. she said she can't do that. she finally had to ask someone else. thankfully a pharmacist who understand kaiser's policy, acknowledged that i can be billed. so when i got my bill, i was able to dispute it and got the charge removed because i quoted from the member handbook including detailed information on exclusion and inclusion and kp acknowledged it was an error. so takeaways from my experience are:

1. know your member's rights. you have the rights to the latest copy of your member handbook/member benefits. make sure you ask for it with information on all the inclusion and exclusions. it's alot of pages but read it so you can be informed of what's covered. ask for a translation in your language if you prefer (it's part of your rights).

2. if you question the cost of something and you're a kp member, ask them to bill you so you can dispute it.

3. if kaiser charges you for something that is a covered benefit, it's considered fraud. file an grievance and/or appeal with them first. if it doesn't get resolve or address within 30 days, you should notify dhcs (for medi-cal), cms (for medicare), and/or dmhc in general so an investigation can be opened. let these organizations know as well if you see quality related issues. if they get fined, they lose fundings and accreditation.

be your own advocate and know what are your rights as a patient!

if i could give this emergency room negative stars i would the woman at the front desk was extremely rude she didn't listen to anything that my son was saying about him having flulike symptoms instead she took one of the symptoms he had his blood drawn we sat in the waiting room for over two hours waiting for a room to open up within that time they could've taken a urine sample but they didn't until we got to the room when i told the second nurse he had flu like symptoms she tested him for that i spent six hours there just to find out he had the flu and if they would've listen from the very beginning i would've had to wait six hours to get that information... even the doctor was rude as if i had the audacity to bring my son in on the fourth day of being sick and not getting any better....this is probably the worst hospital i have ever been to i will never go back and i would never recommend anyone to be treated here

sisters er and their obgyn clinic is absolutely awful. i've been deathly ill with gi problems for several months. i have been told that unless my baby is in danger they can't help me. they refuse to treat me or run any tests other than sonograms and i am rarely able to keep water of food down. my heart rate and blood pressure has become abnormally high and i have been there over 13 times in the passed 5 months. nurses and doctors have treated me with such disrespect and unprofessionalism. hearing nurses and doctors laugh loudly and ridicule and make jokes about sick patients (myself included) is cruel and inhumane. honestly i'm terrified to deliver there i'm considering delivering at home because of the negligent and cold hearted treatment i've received in sisters er. oh and i also went into preterm labor and they refused to check on me and made me sit in the regular er without calling labor and delivery...i had to go to another hospital to have my labor stopped. i will never go to this hospital as long as i live so help me god. they don't even deserve one star the deserve  to be all unemployed.

stroke survivors need 100% perfect medical care 100% of the time. reading surgery center has provided that for me in 3 visits over the past two months, for 3 different procedures, and 2 different surgeons.
check-in has been fast and thorough, pre-op is well done, and or nurses have been alert and attentive. some or nurses are friendly and chatty; some business-like. all have been extremely competent; perhaps i should mention that all 3 procedures at 1280 broadcasting road were done under local anesthesia; 10 days in a coma, from a stroke 3 years ago, left me without my 'self'. i had gallbladder surgery using general anesthesia a month after discharge from rehab... but prefer local anesthesia. drs schlechter and tinsley understand my preference and both agreed to work with me. recovery has been equally free of stress (stroke survivors don't need stress).

i had my daughter here at a little over 5 years ago.  i was only in labor for two hours total, and the nurses recognized that i needed to be admitted right away.  a doctor was woken up (i've since learned that he passed away), and he was so calm and caring while delivering my daughter.  she had feeding problems at first, but the nurses again recognized the signs and sent a physical therapist to work with her while we were still there.  breastfeeding became so much easier after that!  i do wish they had something like quiet hours so that you can get two or three hours of uninterrupted sleep.  besides that, i really liked this hospital, and plan to have my third child there, too.

the hospital staff was great until .my wife got a room upstairs.
then the place became a prison . they searched her belongings like she was being arrested. they went through her purse,without her permission when i asked what they were doing they told me they were searching for drugs or weapons.they found a bottle of tylenol and a blister pack of zantac handed them to me and said i had to take them out of the hospital or throw them away. i took her for a walk around the hospital , after asking the doctor if it was ok since she had been in a hospital bed in the emergency room all day. he said it was a great idea and he approved. first they sent security out to find us then yelled at her for leaving her room and told her if she wanted to walk around she couldn't leave the floor.when i came back the next day my wife was crying and wanted to leave as soon as we could . she said in all of the hospital visits ands surgerys she'd ever had this was the worst.the nurses were also giving her medication and checking her mouth like she wasn't taking her meds. i am very disapointed in this hospital. and the way they treat their patients.i could hear the other patients complaining to their families.so i got her released as soon as i could

my husband spent 3 weeks here recuperating from a fall in which he suffered a complicated break of three ribs.  i can not express our gratitude for the wonderful care he received from the time he entered the facility, until the time of discharge....the entire staff was wonderful to both myself and my husband...thanks to them he is on his was back to normal...if you, or anyone you know are looking for a facility for a loved one don't hesitate...kearny mesa nursing center and rehab is wonderful from beginning to end...
fac_name: Kearny Mesa Nursing Center and Convalescent Hospital

review:
had surgery with dr. karram about 3 months ago. i can say now i am completely recovered. i am completely satisfied with my surgery. i definitely recommend dr.karram. his staff was also amazing. they call you a day after surgery to see how you are doing and to offer any advice with concerns you might have. a special thank you to cynthia for helping me coordinate my surgery also for being so thoughtful in contacting me to see how i was doing. i appreciate you and all the staff. dr.karram is absolutely the best.  i love the results. 
thank you once again for a job well done!

coming to the hospital as a child was always fantastic. when i officially "became an adult" with not the greatest insurance the care changed and i never felt the same care. my father has also had multiple surgeries that have never seemed to go right because we are always back "having it fixed." i guess it's like everywhere you go though, it depends on the people helping you and how much they care.

so. we were told to be here at 8:30 this morning. upon arrival, they took us back and let us sit for 3 hours in a room before the doctor came for pre-op consultation . he didn't even know what exactly was supposed to be done . he had to call his office to find out what he was doing. 
while waiting in the waiting room, they called me into a room so the doctor could tell me how the surgery went. i sat in there for an hour waiting until i finally just left and went back to the waiting room. 
the workers were talking loudly about how this was the worst job they have ever had . says a lot about the hospital. i wouldn't come here again if my life depended on it!

dr. pritchett was great- very professional, knowledgeable & kind. nurses were wonderful too! check-in was terrible. was sent wrong address for appointment, check in ipad lost battery, medical assistant called my baby girl a mister, was unable to use digital insurance card, and there was no smiles from anyone at front desk. as long as you can make it through the office door everything is awesome!

i checked in at the emergency room at south shore hospital at 2pm. its 715pm now and still waiting. 3 other patients waiting with me. nobody can give answer as to what the delay is. and why aren't they passing out face masks to these patients who are coughing up their lungs? just spray the flu virus all over the hospital why don't you? i should have made the trip to hammond st. margaret or south suburban. never coming back to ssh ever again except to visit someone i may know

where to start wont take comp cases unless you have case number,back in  the day they used your primary insurance until they got the case number and changed it over , front desk was rude on the 4 floor manager was useless no help they just want there money,then front desk girl starts raising her voice to me and threatens to put it in my chart amazing how ny is so messed up and ass backwards a shame used to be a great place for health not no more run from this place.

came in with a broken wrist. i was seen within 15 minutes. all the staff was incredibly informative and friendly. dr. seefeld set my wrist and did an incredible job! i went home to boston and the surgeon at tufts said it was some of the best work they've seen. would absolutely recommend!

i have always received good care through east jeff.er.about 12 years ago my son was given an antibiotic by a male nurse before a spinal tap caused him to spend a week in children's hospital. what do you expect from a male nurse who's busy flirting instead of doing his job.

i recently took my mother to the er.  as a former healthcare executive with responsibility for multiple facilities across the u.s., i was incredibly disappointed with the facility.  the ramp to the enter the er is filthy and extremely patient unfriendly.  one patient registration kiosk woefully inadequate.  if i were the administrator i would be ashamed of how patients are greeted and taken through their care.  the staff were fine and i feel sorry for what they have to contend with facility wise.  to say that this is an incredibly inadequate facility would be an understatement!

horrible emergency room...they do not communicate ur chart symptoms and medication u r on to dr.when u get in a room  r shd i say behind a curtain decided by 6..r he just didnt read them ..he was rude..nurse was great..hospital er was filthy..i was given injections then bp and heart rate sky rocketed with no dr ..r nurse in site..bp beeper stayed on..blood pressure and heart kept rising i honestly thought i was about to hv a heart attact had to send my husband to find nurse ..they didnt even know i was on bp meds r didnt read chart.i thought i wasnt coming out of there alive...this er use to b a lot better it has hone downhill bad..really bad...will not go bk there ever i am changing all ej connected drs to oshner drs..and i always pay my bill's on time but they harass u to death even when u do...so goodbye ejgh...poorly run..oh and time b4 that they only had 1 non working bp cuff in er and laughed about it....sad.....

i arrived with a pain in the belly at 7pm i gave up and i was although at 10:30 without being attended!  really horrible hospital trash care at the reception grumpy people!  dirty bathroom!  it's worth driving 30 min and going on cha revere!

do not bother to go here if you have an emergency. the er and staff are the absolute worst. you're more likely to die waiting, than getting any sort of decent human interaction. no one cares about you, they see you as just work. and clearly they hate their jobs. the wait is ridiculous. not worth your time. go anywhere but here, no matter how urgent your case is.

my daughter had her first child here last week and this hospital is fantastic.  the hospital is easy to navigate, super clean/modern, great lobby cafe and cafeteria with excellent food.  super friendly staff everywhere.  not matter where we were, staff always said hello and went out of their way to be friendly.  lastly and most importantly the maternity center was fabulous.  all nurses, workers were unbelievable.  especially, ariel who was my daughter's nurse the day after she gave birth.  what an amazing, caring and genuine person.  she was just the best nurse anyone could ask for.  i can't say enough about this hospital!
fac_name: Childbirth Center at St Joseph Hospital

review:
i just delivered my baby here in labor and delivery monday, march 2. the customer service, level of communication and knowledge was top notch. i had some of the following request and i was concerned they would judge but every one was so nice and understanding. 

1. no bath. they actually encouraged waiting as long as possible anyway. they were happy when i requested this.

2. no hep b vaccine. they had zero issues with this. 

3. delay cord clamping. they were all for this until he was born with shoulder dystocia. it was panic for a while and once he did come out, they immediately needed to cut cord and start working on him across the room. 

4. do not take baby out of room unless medically necessary. the only time this was done was during his circumcision. they prefer this. they really are about skin to skin and baby never leaving mom. 

i also wasn't aware the law changed regarding the "eye antibiotics". i thought it was required still, as it was a few years back. it's not. i would have denied it. he had a reaction to it and didn't open his eye for the first 24 hours.

if i had to find a complaint, it would be that a ton of people come in and out of your room non stop. the second day, my husband and i counted over 12 people in a 3 hour time span. but that night the nurses all knew how exhausted baby and i were and they all got together and coordinated their visits so it would be all at once and not staggered. 

i seriously can't say enough nice things about the entire staff at clr l&d.

the most disgusting, careless hospital i've ever been to in my life. the entire hospital is filthy at all times. the pictures are not enough. you aren't even able to sit down. i waited in the icu lobby. i didn't even attempt to stay in there

horrible place to be a patient. i came in with a minor head injury. i was told that i could leave the next day in the morning by all the doctors involved with the injury. a dr. kareem gadelmola came into my room. he said that i can go. then, he retract what he said. bugged me for 20 minutes to stay for one more x-ray. i screwed up and stop arguing to leave. i wanted to go see my doctor that i was more familiar with. after, i took the stupid x-ray. i kept having the nurses page him, so i can go home. after, he left was when i was told that i had to stay there till the next day. that no one could release me. now, i'm fighting the hospital to not be charged for him not doing his job. and, coming back to sign me out. dr. kareem is a horrible person. don't let him do this to you. because, this hospital is an expensive hotel to stay in for no reason..

went to this "hospital" for blood work. it looks like a hospital from the outside but inside there is one woman at the "emergency" entrance receiving everyone, many people just didn't wait and entered the hospital without checking in, i wandered down the halls and found the lab and rang the bell, no answer. then i waited in line and tried not to hear  while patients had to explain why they needed medical attention in public. shameful. 

and even though the computer 
generated ordered were from another uchealth  hospital i was told it needed a signature from a doctor. i said really? it must be in the computer system.  she left and went into another room and came back and said yes we can't give you the test. 

ok......you mean there are people back therewhile people wait on line for the emergency department and they are waiting behind me while we figure out a clerical problem.

so i just leave, no problem, it's routine blood test. 

i thank god i wasn't there for anything serious.

i was visiting my family from out of state and had severe back pain for 4 days. i know my body and knew something had to be wrong as i couldn't even move anymore. i visited this location at 5am. i was the only person in there so the snarky comments from the nurse and doctor about "being an emergency facility" numerous times was obviously a big turn off and they rushed me out with a "you should visit your primary". once again.. i'm from out of state so i don't have a primary nearby. i told them i didn't want pain meds, i just wanted to understand the cause of pain so that i could address as necessary. i'm not a pain pill girl... they prescribed me some extra strength tylenol and pain patches. i asked the nurse if he knew where i could fill the prescription nearby and he said "we aren't a pharmacy". clearly that's not what i was asking... i was just from out of state and was hoping with his knowledge of the area he could recommend a 24 hour pharmacy to help. i don't go to the doctor often, but this might be a great example of why.. incredibly dismissive and disappointing. now that i read reviews, i'm looking forward to dealing with the billing side next. do yourself a favor.. pick a different hospital. i wish i would have researched this place first. after all of that, i ended up at the grocery store with icy hot and lots of tears until i could fill my prescription.

the best hospital in all ventura county and san fernando valley.  ici and ccu are supported by best doctors and nurses.  dr. tahki  and  dr. zohdi the best in every regard.  diane, teresa and ashley rock. best nurses ever. my son passed away 3/04/20. but i know he received the best care possible because of the staff, neuro treatment and nurses.  this hospital deserves a 10 star.

after going to the er at los robles last night i'm telling all of my family and friends, "if i'm seriously hurt or it's a life or death situation let me die in peace rather than take me to los robles."

other than the nice person who checked me in and took my presenting symptoms, the doctors and rn's there don't want to help people, and shouldn't be around humans because they don't treat you like one!

the trauma doc didn't want to take over another doctors case and he said he wouldn't be able to see tests and labs already ordered so i should just wait. even thought my doctor told me to go to the er! 

the doctor then tells me i'm not dehydrated but orders an i.v. bag of fluids. which is it??  he also ordered two meds through i.v. that are pointless because i already take them orally.

a newbee medic tries to find a vein for the i.v. and proceeds to go in out and through my vein to the point that i start passing out.  they don't listen or help me, they keep trying to poke me and get an i.v. going in my other hand. as i beg them to stop, "give me a minute. get smelling salts my body is going  into full shutdown mode and i'm seeing black."

they put me in a bed and two nurse come in and immediately want to put an i.v. in. they don't want to help with the passing out. i ask for a mint as i'm shaking, sweating and still seeing blacks. the nurse says i'm "refusing service and he has other patient's he could be helping! he'll come back but it wont be in a timely manner!"

i was treated as a hostile patient there on out. it took a different nurse 2 more tries too get a vein. and i told them i was allergic to laytex and she used latex tape to tape the i.v. down. so when they took it off it ripped off a layer of skin. 

today i'm bruised and swollen and in worse pain then when i went in yesterday. 

the people that work there need to remember why they wanted to be in the health care field, non of them should be allowed to work on or around humans.

my experience was disgusting and they should all be ashamed of themselves!

do your self a favor drive e few miles more to any of the neighboring hospitals if you need er attention 
this place makes you wait over five hours to be seen. 
doesn't have to be this way regardless of how busy they are.
your emergency room doctor was mean to my 90 year old grandma. staff needs to learn compassion for the elderly

im still traumatized until this day from my stay at this place in 2012. they treated me like crap, they are racist and abusive. if i knew better back then i would have sued them big time. they gave me heavy opioids even though i requested to not be given drugs and i was not in pain after my accident. yes i was treated and my fractures were fixed, but they physiologically caused unprepairable damage. they were pushin for surgery instead of a fixture device to mend my broken bone to milk insurance. case manager and i wish i can remember her name was mean and unprofessional,  she has mental issues. i was in my right mind until they overloaded me on deloided i became addicted to it. this is a serious problem,  if you love someone and you care about never let them go to this hospital. it was not my choice, the ambulance was paid to take patients there, man that lawsuit would have been endless if it wasn't for statue of limitations and too long of a time has passed already.

los robles from entering door of er through admit, tests, treatment, meds, referrals and even paperwork and discharge continues to rock the 5 star rating and above!! i simply could find nothing to complain about or be critical of. i'm over 60 with a myriad of health problems and very much have been "around the block" at other medical facilities that do not even approach the "parking" lot when it comes to complicated patient care. everything falls into place like a well-rehearsed script. after all the opioid talk lately, i was especially afraid this time of begging for pain control and being left with next to nothing. i do have a number of chronic pain conditions for which i do take pain doctor supervised pain meds. the presenting problem i was here for also involved more than the usual level of pain. my fears were immediately put to rest with immediate and appropriate pain control. when i shared my concerns with the doctor about this, they said they know the difference of drug seekers/abusers for no reason compared to patients with long records, histories and tests that are proof of legitimate pain conditions. all of the personnel from doctors, nurses, er staff and just everyone were consistently good listeners, helpful, kind, quick to perform services and displayed a high level of empathy, respect and support. i continue to be dazzled by this amazing hospital!

my husband went to pinnacle urgent care for a swollen, red ankle.
doctor diagnosed him with cellulitis, and he admitted him.
during my husband's five day admission, the care he received was good.

when he was discharged, he didn't receive any after care instructions.
they gave him a light  compression stocking  to wear. i asked the nurse if the sock had to be removed when he went to bed  . she said: patients sleep with the soon on here.

well, that was the wrong answer. he was home for 2 days, & when he removed the stocking, his shin/ankle was so much worse. we went to community hospital, where he again was admitted for another five days!

he lost 3 weeks of pay, because he had to keep his leg elevated 90% of the time..

if he got accurate discharge instructions, he wouldn't of been hospitalized a second time, not to mention all the additional hospital/doctor bills.

i went to pinnacle to have a venogram.  i had no idea this hospital even existed.  i'm so glad i do now!  most places i have been are so overcrowded and the wait time is unbelievable.  everyone there really has it together.  i was totally impressed!  3 nurses to one patient....what?  it was insane!   great job pinnnacle you made a very scary procedures a piece of a cake.

i was having strong pains in my back on the lower left side and thought it might be kidney stones. i went to the er and they were very friendly and efficient.  they did all the necessary tests and found nothing and said it was probably a muscle pull.  i was in and out of there within 2 hours.
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Hinsdale

review: we arrived at 10:50pm after my 73 yr old mom had a severe head injury from a fall with blood streaming down her face.  we explained she fell and saw stars and had a deep cut and may have cracked her skull. 55 minutes and we are in the waiting room with people with colds and fevers going ahead of us. we asked for a sterile towel as the bleeding was not controlled and the front desk representative pulled one from the drawer next to him! ugh.  isn't er supposed to be a place to sort out injuries by severity? this place should be reported.
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Hinsdale

review: my son has been admitted with rsv.  the care has been excellent so far.  the doctors and nurses have been extremely attentive and informative.  they have answered all my questions and then some.
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Hinsdale

review: when having your first child, things can be quite stressful. this place made the whole experience a nightmare. we were told we needed an emergency delivery. during the actual delivery the midwife was texting 10 inches from my wife's vagina. i really can't believe it. then with the head expose, they invited a young girl from gwinnett tech to come in and shadow, they had her come all the way in while my wife was exposed a pushing and asked if she could shadow?? we obviously didn't care cause it was too late, she already saw everything. we were kinda busy trying to deliver a baby. after the birth we were transferred to a dingy and filthy recovery room. dust all in the hvac, just read other reviews. the nurse forgot about us for many hours. my wife did not get her pain meds for at least 6 hours. imagine that. and here's the kicker, i went to complain privately to the midwife on our 2nd day. my wife was so upset that she was crying. i threaten them with litigation for all of there wrong doings. instead the held me against my will with a security guard outside, and try to create a scenario where i was a drunk abusive partner cause significant commotion. i literally looked at the midwife name sarah who was acting as the lead or supervisor and said, i'm not the one who is loud or out of control you are. they were trying to build a defense against me, suggestively saying things that would seem to incriminate me. she even insulted me when she asked what type of doctor i was. asking about my credentials. i told her i was a dentist and she made a remark like i was inferior. last time i check, you still are less educated than me and you still have to call me doctor. obviously, nothing happen because i'll do anything to stay and with my newborn and support my partner. but now that i'm home, i can only spread my experience. there are plenty of other hospitals and better rated. don't choose gwinnett northside or gwinnett physicians group. it's not worth it. these are the type of people who have ruined healthcare.

top notch specialists and doctors. horrible nursing, staff, amenities and overall facilities. i only chose this hospital because i wanted to be seen by a highly recognized surgeon for my extensive acl repair surgery.

my encounters with the amenities and the majority of the staff outside of the surgical team, were very disappointing. the hospital bathrooms, cafeteria, and waiting room appeared less than sanitary. the nursing staff/administrative staff were incredibly dysfunctional. for such a nationally recognized hospital, we expected more.

i went in for surgery at 2pm. at 4:45 my mom told me that all the staff in the waiting area got up and left to go home. the receptionist told my mom that if the surgeons needed to get ahold of her they would call the desk phone and that she can go back there to pick up any calls. that is outrageously unprofessional! after no updates around 7pm she had to call the general hospital front desk for any updates.

when i woke up, i felt the nurses were very aggressive in my handling and seemed rushed. there were several moments where i started sobbing after the operation. i was super parched and hadn't had water in almost a day. i would ask for ice packs for my sore arms and no one was listening to me or helping me or even looking me in the eye. people were talking at me but no one was listening to my immediate needs. i was constantly asking to see my mom because i knew she would advocate for me, and they kept saying she was on her way or that the surgeon was talking with her (which was not true, they lied) and time kept passing.

finally, when i was about to get released, the hospital pharmacy was already closed but were we instructed to take pain medicine that evening to help me get to sleep which was very frustrating. if they anticipated surgery to end before the pharmacy closed they should have given me a few pills to take home or given the prescription to my mom to fill while she was waiting. after we got home, my mom spent two hours running around dc at night trying to find an open pharmacy that would give her oxycodone at like 1am. again, for a highly recognized hospital, we expected more. we paid so much money for this procedure. i recommend going to a cleaner facility where they have a proven record of showing respect for patients and their family members.

do not go there even if you are dying
i wish there's a rating below zero to give to this dump of garbage. everything here sucks the service the nurses the admins the hospital is dirtier than a hospital in a third world country. the wait is forever and everyone is rude as fuck.
by far the worst i've ever seen, it shows what kinda shitty university and even shittier med school

i arrived at 8am for an imaging appt. at the womens imaging center; first stop admissions.  they were very helpful & accommodating; moving swiftly considering i had been given the wrong "script" as they called it.  once they rec'd. the correct "script" for them they processed me extremely fast-i thank them.  unfortunately, when i got to the womens imaging center no one was at the front desk, but i begin to complete the paperwork i see re: the nature of my appt.  no sooner than i finish a lady by the name of "ms. blake" comes out.  she dies nit speak, not even a hello.  unbothered (as ive just come from childrens hospital w/ a child having a 104.3 fever. i couldn't cancel this appt. b/c i made it back in nov. of 2019, yes!) i handed her my "script" + admissions docs+ the ones i just filed out.  i attempt to explain to her, ive been here since 8am; i have an 8:30appt.  oh you're the one (so shes aware) yes.  (theres like 6 women in front of me-we all came from admissions; & its 9:19am)  well, shes says holding up a stack of patients paperwork, youre going to have to go to the back b/c you're late.  placing my paperwork underneath the others, while holding them uo in front, of my face.  she then gives me a look, as if to say, bye-bye, go & sit.  i do.  a few minutes later i ask for the mngr. "she is busy, "ms. blake" states.  you know, the one that came out?  that was her."  shes by the elevators, pointing behind her as if i know where "the elevators" are.  well can you let her know a patient would like to speak with her, i say " i will let her know" she says as she remains in her seat.  i ask for her name, & she turns her badge around for me to see: "beverly blake"  i never, saw the mngr.  not sure if she was even made aware?  i finally got seen; the other staff in the back were very, nice & pleasant; & left the imaging center at 11:42am.
i say all this to say, customer service comes with, the job.  customers dont ask to be at a particular place, but they are.  if you can't treat someone how you'd. like to be treated, dont be there.  you dont know what-people are going through...  be the person that uplifts not makes people have to report you, or want to slap you b/c you make things heavier, or worse.
"ms. blake" did not have to act like that, or treat me indifferently.  however, after, i asked for her name.  she did a 180° to all the other patients which let me-know, she was aware, if her behavior & conduct.   unacceptable.

the parking does not have enough space. i visited oncology in november of last year and the building for that department is okay, the room is descent.
i visited a loved one who had cancer and his bed had no sheet, no pillow, no blanket and both of his socks had holes. he was mainly lying down on a mattress and it was winter.
a nurse, particularly with the name of kim in oncology seemed unknowledgeable about how to deal with cancer patient and their changed behavior. i believe that medical staff like her should be trained on how to handle the emotional trauma of cancer patients to have better understanding of their behavior.  i never had any good impression in this hospital since i was hospitalized here in 2000 once and never wanted to be back. i just had to visit a loved one who unfortunately was hospitalized and passed in this hospital in less than 3 weeks of hospitalization and was very disappointed to see his bed condition and experienced an inefficient nurse with the name kim. i believe that nurses should be trained on emotional behavior of patients particularly cancer patients to have better understanding. or it maybe that they already are, but was just unfortunate to get an inefficient one for my loved one.

this place is a joke. receptionist not very friendly and seems like providing the minimum of professional customer service is the norm. very silo orientated department. if you are stuck using this hospital i feel for you. if you have a choice do yourself a favor and and go somewhere else , i'm sure you will receive better treatment. sorry for interrupting you while you gossip about your cousin with your co worker miss receptionist. 
on the bright side there was martha in the ct department that went above and beyond to help out. i wish our appointment was in her department. great job martha and thank you.

so that's my story i hope it helps someone.

you better have your wallet ready. i went here for my back, i was having muscle spasms that were quickly getting worse. it was your basic visit, iv, pain meds, run some tests, did a cat scan to determine a bulging disc. the place was empty, not a single other patient in there, which i figured was a good thing. they got me right in & there was a steady stream of medical staff coming in to offer helping hands, need a blanket, want some ice chips, etc. each one asked the same questions & were given the same answers, apparently nobody was taking notes. got my pain under control & sent me on my way. over the next few months, we received a bill from the hospital for over $12,000.00. yes, we have insurance. thereafter, one after another came bills from each of the doctors or medical staff for their charges, because that's not included in the 12 grand. we submitted the bills to our insurance & after their network discounts and other insurance nonsense we were still left with nearly $6,000.00 that was still our responsibility. we had several other large medical bills in the past 6 months within our immediate family. one of those, "when it rains, it pours scenarios." at any rate, every other medical office allowed us a negotiated, reduced final bill if we agreed to pay it all at once or in several lump sums, rather than monthly payments. not the er @ gv. the attitude is, oh well, not my problem. pay your bill or we're turning you into collections and we do not accept payments.

i created an account, just to let people know if they do not feel well, have an illness etc? not sure where to go?  i felt safe and taken care of here at this er. a bit too much tmi, but due to the nature of this service, i have to let you guys know? i had severe vomiting, upset stomach, cold etc and was really worried about myself. i was dehydrating and couldn't keep treating myself and be ok. i goggled this er and drove over late at night. they have a "non-emergency appointment request" online on their website. it is not required, but you can go on your computer and let them know you will be arriving. i got there and they already had a room waiting for me. the girls and guys were amazing, the dr. was very nice. the beds had memory foam and they kept bringing me warm blankets. there was also a tv and remote and it was quite relaxing considering lol! :) they saw me right away and pulled blood for labs. i was stunned that within 15-20 minutes, they had it all figured out and got me on an i.v. and some meds to treat me. they did have a pediatric emergency, which they kept apologizing for as they didn't come back for a while ( that was totally fine, i was fine). they even offered to get me some food they have on hand for patients after administering the i.v. and medication, as i had not eaten hardly anything for 2 days due to stomach upset. they wanted me to see if i could eat with the meds settling everything down. the only "tiny" issue, was that due to the fact i was throwing up, they never gave me a "throw up tin" lol! so, i got up and went through the cupboards and found one myself. that and the new girl taking out my i.v. at the end? pulled it too fast and i did bleed out a little bit, but no big deal. she felt really bad and a senior nurse stepped in and assisted her. i was just fine, i was happy to be feeling better. overall? this e.r. team did their best and treated me very well, the e.r. was comfortable, very clean and accommodating. for having to go to the e.r.? i was really impressed. if you don't feel well? understand they may have serious emergencies that you get back burnered for a little or they make tiny forgivable mistakes, but overall? if you don't know where to go? go here. they also had security running the front desk and they can see right out in front where you park. i did feel safe, taken care of and had great results! thank you so much to the e.r. team at green valley e.r.

basically, i was denied adequate service for hyperemesis gravidarum. the "midwives" and "doctors at this location denied me access to good health care. i believe it is because i am black american. numerous studies have shown that health care providers do not want to treat black women in pain. recent "studies" have shown this is because they "don't believe" black women/people when we say we are experiencing pain. but countless experiences have shown it's simply because these individuals are racist and don't care.

unfortunately, i would not recommend this practice for a multitude of reasons. if you have any type of trouble with your pregnancy, the midwives and physicians here are not that helpful or knowledgeable. personally, i had hyperemesis gravidarum and in writing the message, i am already crying as i think about the pain this disease causes during pregnancy. i was hospitalized 5 times. unfortunately, the individuals at this practice are not trained in this disease, and refuse to learn about it, or listen to the patient.

one day early in my pregnancy, i came to see a midwife named jodi, and after explaining my situation of not eating for a week and throwing up blood, she sent me to the emergency room, (one of my 5 visits during my pregnancy to get fluids because i was severely sick and dehydrated) yet only wrote me off work for two days. when i confronted her about my need to heal and be off work, she had a cavalier attitude and would not extend the letter. i finally mustered up enough energy to call a couple days later and request an extended sick leave letter from a physician whose name i can't remember and when i went to pick it up, it was not even written. it was horrible. also, if you have a severe pregnancy disability like hyperemesis, they will not sign off on pregnancy disability. i am not sure if they didn't trust me or my multiple hospital visits, or the fainting i had endured during my last pregnancy, but they think that continuing to work outside the home with hyperemesis is okay, which was a harrowing experience for me.

i went to the emergency room for a searing 9/10 hip pain, in tears and hysterical. i wasn't really aware of my surroundings but i did have my family with me. the only thing that helped was pacing, then laying in fetal and pacing again. they put me in a room, i paced out front of it crying quietly. then a nurse at the desk told me they preferred me stay in my room. i pleaded to her hysterically that it was the only thing that helped. she rolled her eyes at me so i kept on pacing. i was in front of my room, it's not like i was freaking out walking the hospital- i don't even believe i was sobbing loudly. 
when the x-ray team arrived they were so ginger and careful and understood me. however, they found nothing. not a darn thing. so i'm here. no answers, being told i'm fine, as i experience what feels like some on twisting a pitchfork in my hip and pulling my quad muscle from my femur and knee. pleasant yes? 
at this point my husband left me with my teen son to go get our other children from school.
a woman whom ,i'm assuming was a doctor, later appeared. and at this point i was in the phase of fetal rocking. she asked me to feel around on this lump on my hip. does this hurt? no. she pushed with moderate force on my hip, triggering a dull ache, i started to cry. she proceeds to tell me i have a lipoma, a fatty tumor, that doesn't really cause pain. then she disappeared after telling me they'll get a referral started and get me discharged. that's really all i could comprehend.
i started to pace again trying to relieve the agonizing pain from the area. i think i placed myself in the floor  sobbing. now thinking back was probably the grossest thing i could have done. a lady appeared, not a doctor. she began to tell me something about orthopedic and scheduling. i told her i didn't understand what she was asking. she asked me if i could schedule a visit. i told her i didn't know. she proceeded to say dates and times and i simply could not hear her over the pain. my son handed me my phone while i lay on the floor and i opened it. i clicked on some apps, i forgot what i was looking for. i asked again what i was doing. she told me dates. i couldn't for the life of me figure out what i was supposed to do so i started to cry again. she said something and left. i now realize that she was trying to schedule me an orthopedic and follow up appointment.
i started to pace, the fetal phase was no longer working, back to the hysteria walking phase. it had been 2 hours of hell. pure hell. someone showed up, a nurse i believe. she handed me some papers and told me to stick to my appointments and to go through the doors to the right. my son grabbed my items and i lead me down the hall. suddenly we were outside. i suddenly realized- they discharged me. i kept to my pacing and fetal on the bench. since my husband left to get my other children, my son and i stayed outside with no way home. turned away by the hospital, no relief from my living hell and no way home.

i'm an internal medicine physician (m.d; board-certified)
visiting from los angeles and was finishing dinner at a restaurant in boca with my 85 year-old dad on a saturday evening when he suddenly collapsed to the left and was having a stroke in front of my eyes. 

rushed him to boca regional medical center where they were already on high alert (we called ahead) and they implemented their "stroke alert" protocol with all hands on deck. 

on arrival, the (terrific) nurses whisked him directly from the front door to the head doc in the er (david leeman, md), he did a quick but thorough neurological assessment while dad was still in a hospital-provided wheelchair and sent him immediately to the ct scanner for a sophisticated brain perfusion scan. mind you, this all took no more than 6 minutes from er door to ct scanner (!).

ct scan showed no major blockages (thank g_d), but did show a small area that had subtly narrowed blood vessels and wasn't getting enough blood/oxygen to dad's brain for a short time. thus, the stroke symptoms at the restaurant. 

here's the best/mind-blowing part: within minutes, they had dad back from his ct scan and into one of the er's "critical care" beds, wheeled a two-way video monitor to dad's bedside and a top cleveland clinic neurologist-stroke specialist appeared live on screen and she did a remote bedside teleconsult (freshly-done ct brain perfusion scan on her computer) and chatted with/"examined" dad on the spot. 

she determined that dad had a "tia" (mini-stroke") but did not need (effective but sometimes dangerous) clot-busting drug treatment. after a team of (incredibly kind/efficient/competent) nurses took a detailed medical history, drew blood and did an ekg, they wheeled dad directly to the new marcus neuroscience inpatient unit of the hospital, where another team of great nurses attended to dad, gave him his evening meds and got him properly tucked in for the night. 

bottom line: from initial stroke symptoms to er admission to completed ct scan and expert consult/diagnosis to monitored inpatient bed, the whole process took less than 90 minutes. as stated above, world class care!

my mom came in with the fire department through er in cardiac distress.  she has advanced heart failure and wears a pacemaker.

we were left in the a hallway for almost 6 hours. we were told that her ekg can't be read because of her pacemaker, but it wouldn't be until the next day that an integrated ekg could be done.

after 5 hours in the hallway, the er admitting physician dr. bernstein came around. he asked why we were in the er today. omg. so, i told him mom has heart failure and he said, "ok, we'll admit her."  i never saw him again.

about 2 hours later we were in a room. i asked who her doctor would be. no one was sure. two residents were roaming around.  i grabbed them and took them into a quiet room on the floor to explain mom's condition.  of course, they told me i wasn't a doctor so i should let them figure out what was wrong with mom. (i have been her only caregiver for 20 years. i know every med, all of her numbers, and am very aware of her heart condition.)  they said the best they could do was brief "a doctor" in the morning.  when i asked if he/she would be a cardiologist, they said, "no."

we waited until 7a the next morning. dr. foster spent 5 minutes with mom. he is an internist, not a cardiologist. the rest of the day we waited for an echo cardiogram or some diagnostics to be done to asses her condition. it never happened.

the nurses couldn't do much, since there is no doctor on the floor (no doctor on the floor) and nurses advised that internists are only available by phone and only in case of an emergency.

my mother was dry heaving, unable to swallow, short of breath at rest (all signs of late stage heart failure) and completely unattended to except by helpless nurses.  i called my brother-in-law in pittsburgh who is a well known gerontologist and read the blood results to him.  he was appalled that there hadn't been a cardiologist in to see her, nor one assigned to her. 

i asked mom's nurse dinesha to contact the two young residents who i had learned were on duty in admitting.  she called them at least 3 times over a period of 4 hours.  finally they arrived. they asked me the same questions over and over and over again. i was losing hope and patience.  i told them i wanted a cardiac consult now.

my mom was nothing more than a school project for them. one was a junior resident, dr. awadallah, the other a senior. said they would order an echo cardiogram and assured me the cardiologist would see mom in the morning. they kept telling me, "none of this is in our control." i believe them.

finally, the patient in the room next door had to be moved to icu. the icu dr came up to our floor.  he was the only doctor i'd ever encountered outside of the residents. i asked if he was a cardiologist and one of the nurses asked me, "why do you want to know?" while a compassionate nurse named ernie, quietly told me, "yes, dr. louis is a cardiologist." 

of course, i threw myself on dr. louis' mercy. i begged dr. louis to order oxygen or a diuretic to relieve her labored breathing and his exact response was "no. i will not help your mother. it's not an emergency." he wouldn't even look at her once the emergency patient next door was moved to intensive care.

my mom was dry heaving and had extreme and advancing dyspnea (breathing distress), heart palpitations, dizziness, halos around her vision, tremors, and high anxiety. all i could do was stroke her hair and watch her gasp for air.

a kind young male nurse and a super nasty female nurse reluctantly gave us oxygen, while saying, "but she doesn't need it."  as soon as the oxygen was placed, mom felt slightly better, but still shaking, dry heaving, unable to swallow, get out of bed on her own, to toilet and generally feeling very sick.

this morning at 7a an echo cardiogram was administered.  i still do not know who the cardiologist assigned to her will be. i looked up in the directory of affiliated cardiologists, for any name i might know. i found my husband's cardiologist practices with dr. rudolpho carillo who is affiliated with boca regional and we called his office. we couldn't even get a staff member in the office to pick up a phone.  we were just left on hold for 20 minutes each time we called.  we called 3 times.

so as of this morning, she hasn't been seen nor has the echo been read.  there is no one to talk with to help relieve the immediate distress let alone discuss a prognosis.

we have now called mom's cardiologist who does not have admitting privileges in this hospital.(boca regional is simply where the fire department took us.)

our cardiologist is currently searching for an available colleague with privileges at boca regional to intervene.  mom calls me just now to tell the her roomate is still screaming and she can't take any more.

i hope we can move her out of there today.

this place was very professional and comforting for my spouse who needed his procedure. it was great that his actual doctor did it and spoke to us in español.  ! so that great!

the staff was  also very informative about everything that was going on. so the communication was incredible.

the only downside is there are a lot of divided curtains so it makes me wonder about privacy. but if that is an issue your doctor will call you about any issues. and there is a consultant room that is private that patients may talk to someone if it is necessary.

are the people who work here/answer the phone always so fucking rude and difficult? it's quite shocking how terrible the staff can be at this facility. especially around the holidays, when we are trying to check up on our loved ones who are under your care and supervision. it's disgusting and disgraceful. i can hardly get ahold of my family member, because the nurses are always too busy to help me get in touch with them. "i don't have time to help you." really? i'm at a loss of words.

had some chest pains that i could not explain.  being older with a family history of cardiac disease i decided to have it checked out.  went to this facility since i have been very pleased with the service i have received previously here.  no one was in the waiting room.  it was about 7:00 pm on a  monday evening.

before i could even take a seat in the waiting room a nurse was calling me to take me to a room.  two other nurses came to the room and i was quickly hooked up for an ekg.  they took my blood pressure and temperature.  they soon put in an i-v, took blood for tests and gave me something to lower my blood pressure.  the doctor came in and told me my ekg was a little abnormal and my blood pressure was high and with that and my family history they wanted to admit me to their in-patient hospital and do more tests.  i was very pleasantly surprised at the prompt and exceptional attention and care i was receiving.

over the next 21 hours i had a chest x-ray, a scan of my legs for blood clots, several blood tests,  a upper body cat scan and a chest ultrasound.  the nurses were all very kind and professional.  they kept us informed and often asked if we had any questions.  i had breakfast and lunch and was able to choose what i wanted from a few selections on the menu.  whenever i called for a nurse or aide they promptly responded. after all tests i met with the staff doctor via an interactive video screen and he reviewed their findings and recommendations with me.

having been to other hospitals recently with family members and putting up with non- responsive nurses and aides, baylor scott and white was a blessing and could serve as the model facility for how patients should be treated.
