review:
the absolute worst medical "care" i have ever received. the receptionist was nice and quickly got me back after recognizing possible stroke symptoms. that's where it stopped. the nurses were not friendly or sympathetic.  the doctor's visit was maybe 5 minutes. a ct scan was done that showed nothing. now i know after talking to many doctors afterwards that a brain mri is the preferred test for diagnosing a stroke. the er doctor released me after an hour and a half and in so many words, said don't come back here because we won't be able to help you. 

even though the baylor name hangs on the building, they aren't connected to baylor's system. i went to this location because of the baylor connection because my primary and many of my doctors are in the baylor umbrella. turns out, this location and burleson are owned by a different company that it sounds like just paid some extra $ to have the baylor name. they had none of my medical records or even my list of regular medications. 

thank goodness i continued my medical treatment elsewhere (this is how i learned of the baylor non-connection). i just hate that i spent $250 for an er visit here and had to turn around and spend another several hundred dollars for an mri. needless to say, i wouldn't recommend stopping here to anyone for anything.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Emergency Hospital - Mansfield

methodist hospital is a product of living in california so i understand a lot but at the same time i feel that there is a strong lack of empathy in this place. my fiance had to visit 3 times in 24 hours because he could not breathe due to asthma. the two previous times they sent him home because his oxygen levels were "ok" (about 94). but the third time, after being told to go home and "stop having so much anxiety" 6 or so hours later i had to call an ambulance because he was unable to drive and was really struggling to try and push through. this third time, the shifts had changed and he was admitted for a few days. they gave him treatments, though often late, and he did recover so i do really appreciate that he is still around today because of that. there were some during his stay with medication which were worrisome but either way he is breathing now. 

a few weeks later, after a heavy dose of antibiotics i got my second kidney stone. i came to the er in terrible pain, and it was a long process but they did give me prescriptions to take home, and while i was their my pain wasn't strong enough for me personally to need medication. i went again about a week later for what i though was another kidney stone. this time while i was waiting in the waiting room for what felt like hours, i went through what i thought was the worst pain in my life, and then by the time i was seen the pain was mostly gone. i got a ct scan and the kidney stone was confirmed to be there, though too small to treat with anything but flomax. i declined pain meds because i had leftover from the first visit.  

one week after that, i feel the actual worst pain in my life and take one of the last pills left of my pain medication, which offered me little relief. i go to the er again. i give a urine sample that wasn't moved from the bin until 2 hours of me waiting there. i know the sample testing takes at least an hour. they sent me out in the waiting room for 3 more hours, and in those three i could do nothing but cry from the pain and wait. i called my fiance over who helped to get a nurses attention. when he asked if he could talk to the doctor she said "we don't make calls like that". he brought me my very last pain pill so i declined when she said she could ask about something for the pain.  when i was finally seen again, i was discharged, and was to be sent home with ibuprofen. i immediately responded saying this is not going to be enough for the pain. the pa came out and prescribed me a less stronger medication but told me she couldn't prescribe me the pain meds i had because she had to watch  what i was taking. i get there is a drug epidemic here in sacramento, but a kidney stone is extremely painful and when i had my first one in my much smaller home town, they immediately got me a room and medicated me with what i needed. experiences like the one i had at methodist er make me miss home badly. 

i don't want to name any names because i know it is hard to make a living here and i know that the attitudes of these doctors and nurses are swayed by the many drug addicts that come in to get a fix. 
i know it is too busy to get a room but i find it astounding that they moved me out into the waiting room with a kidney stone. i'm not coming back here for my next emergency visit, though i don't think there is a hospital in sacramento i can go to that will give me the care i need.

i learned a big lesson and so i am sharing my experience so others aren't as naive as i was.  i was referred to the physical therapy group within presbyterian hospital dallas by my internist after having repeat back issues. i had to check in with hospital services, which should have been  a red flag since hospital charges are often much more than a private practice. i had a 1 hour evaluation where i was told i needed to work on my core muscles. i was encouraged to sign up for 1-2 sessions per week. i signed up for two per week, so i had one 1-hour evaluation and five 45 minute sessions.

i really liked the physical therapist. she was wonderful to work with. but if i had known the bill would be $3237 for these six sessions, i would have gone elsewhere. the bill was submitted to insurance, which was then  adjusted to their agreed upon price. i have to pay 100% out of pocket until i reach my deductible, so my 100% was $1578. that's $263 per session. i realize that the evaluation should cost more, but the five individual sessions included 5-10 minutes on an exercise bike -- something i could have done at home prior to arrival. this is such an insane amount for what was delivered in return and i'm no better than i was when i first walked into the place. i could have purchased at least a year's worth of exercise classes that focused on building my core instead.  

i sent an email to texas health voicing my frustration with not being told up front what my cost would be, but i haven't heard a word back, so i'm going to share my experience and hope others learn from my mistake. i'm guessing they don't care because i have to pay regardless and they're not going to do anything about it.  so... be forewarned... unless you have excellent health insurance coverage or medicare that will cover a certain number of visits, this is not the place to go for physical therapy. there are private practice physical therapists who charge much less so you can get more sessions for your money.

i am paying it down over 12 months, but it's the equivalent of having a car payment again and i really didn't need this expense right now. in addition to still having back issues i came here to address, i now have a huge amount of stress trying to figure out how i can come up with these monthly payments. lesson learned.

after we consulted with a friend of the family who is a plastic surgeon i continued to press the nurses to get a surgeon to sew her up because of the possibilities of infection, it still took another hour until a doctor came and closed the incision.  i'm concerned that if my daughter who is well educated and economically well to do individual had to endure such a horrible experience, what would a less fortunate patient have to suffer or die because they may not be aware of their rights.

so into the iv it went.... i got foggy & didn't care. . then, time to go. i sent my friend a text & he was there in a short while. 
i must state that - yes, i've had better experiences at other hospitals. but this one at lawrence general was very good. i believe i got good care in regards to what was wrong with me. the hospital was clean and anyone i interacted with were very professional. now all i need to do is get better....

this hospital legit sucks so bad. the people in the emergency room have no clue what they are doing and are not helpful at all. the wait is terribly long when they tell you it is going to be only 1hour at most. all i need is to get 3 stitches taken out and i have now been waiting here for 3 hours.
i was having breathing and chest issues and both the entire er, staff, nurses and doctors were fabulous.   top notch hospital.

this is a review i didn't want to write again but here i am. on november 10 2019 my father was brought here once again due to the fact he'd been feeling off for the past few days. as we would learn later between that friday and sunday the day we brought him in he'd had 3 heart attacks. they were able to catch the fourth and final one on an ekg. he had 3 stents placed that day and came back on december 5th for a fourth that was less severe. i want to thank the er staff for treating us with compassion and allowing so many family members to pack into the er room with my dad. i would also like to thank dr. terrie gibson for treating my dad, if it wasn't for her quick treatment and my mom finally convincing my dad to come in. we may not have him anymore, thank you baptist heart hospital! and thank you to the er staff

so very grateful to everyone at bolingbrook! the level of care my son received was  amazing. the level of professionalism from everyone during this difficult time for our family was above and beyond. i cannot thank them enough
fac_name: AMITA Health Adventist Medical Center Bolingbrook

review: one of the best sleep centers i have seen or had a study in by far! the staff were super friendly and helpful from scheduling to the end of my study! everything was quiet at night and i feel i slept well! highly recommend!

so i feel like leaving a super positive review here... the staff here did everything my father in-law could dish out int he form of both passive aggressive comments and little and loud demands. they went above and beyond to make sure his stay was comfortable and when my son was fairly sick a few months back they were super accommodating to us on the children's ward...

here on sunday early afternoon brought back to the small room been here for 45 minutes.  no one to check on is.  listening g to the staff talking about their cars.  last night.  deja. vu.     they dont care about anyone but them selves.   they are not busy at all. there is empty rooms

er is an overflowing cesspool. people are being treated in the hallways because they come here instead of using a primary care physician. if you weren't sick when you came in, you will be when you leave. there were bloody paper towels overflowing in the bathroom trash can.
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital Of Orange County

review: they charged me 686$ for washing my kids wound with water and soap!!!! i just called them to get itemized bill to describe every thing's bill separately and of course nobody is there to explain me...  prices are ridiculous!!!!
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital Of Orange County

review: this place is horrible. they do not treat their patients correctly. i have a family member currently admitted and she never gets the care she needs and deserves. whenever she asked the nurses or aides for anything she gets an attitude or is made to wait hours before she gets any type of answers. i do understand that she is not the only patient and that there maybe other patients with more severe problems but this is an on going issues and happens every single day.

i wouldn't bring my dog to this hospital if it was hit by a car in the parking lot.  none of the staff are properly trained to deal with non verbal autistic people,  which today 1 and 140 children are diagnosed a year, with autism.  statistics such as that would be essential in properly training hospital staff to special needs patience.  the on staff doctors have a god complex and expect no one to question them. i myself was given a cat scan and found that i had a thoracic ascending aortic aneurysm of 4cm.  how was i given the news?
doctor:
did you ever hear of an actor named john ritter from three 's company?
me: yes , why is this relevant to me?
doctor: 
because he died from the same thing you have. 
that was on august 31st 2019. recently i went back. saturday january 2020  ( yeah why go back?) but i did because i was suffering severe back pain  ( a serious symptom of a possible dissection of an aortic aneurysm) was given another cat scan and my aneurysm was now 4.3 cm which clearly states that it has grown . what does the doctor do? he informs me that nothing has changed,  and it's a descending aortic aneurysm not ascending? apparently this moron knows more than a renowned thoracic surgeon at westchester medical?!!! he hands me 2 pieces of paper . the original findings as 4cm ascending aortic aneurysm,  than another with the aneurysm at 4.3 cm.  he sends me home with 3 xtra strength tylenol and tells me to follow up with my thoracic surgeon.  my thoracic surgeon was appalled at this and plans on taking it up with the chief of staff. 
fyi 
a voodoo doctor would be better than these buffoon 's.!

i brought my fiancé in, and was allowed to stay with her. getting a good attending physician is a crap shoot. she had a history of head injury and was in pain. they sent her home without doing xrays or a cat scan despite having a positive loss of consciousness a few days before. a break of basic medical protocol, and the doctor was rude and dismissive and accusatory for refusing pain medication.

if it was possible to give zero stars i would. dr. did not even check my blood pressure or listen to my chest? he was supposed to write me a prescription to help persistent hiccups; never did. called to follow up next doctor said she would; never did. call to follow up next doctor said i would need to come back in to be examined. are you kidding me? spent hours on the phone i cannot get back and still have hiccups, for 7 days now. definitely not paying...no service. 
please spare yourself the aggravation and go anywhere else! a kindergartner could do more for you.

first time i came here i came to see a podiatrist but the receptionist was so rude to me and made me feel so uncomfortable i left before i could see the doctor and be treated. 
my second attempt coming to this hospital was worse. it was hard for me to get out of bed and i got lost getting there and was 15 mins late to my appointment then made me wait in the waiting room for another 10 mins just to tell me i'm too late and can't be seen. 
so i had to go to the er to be seen for my health issues. 
because their specialist have egos and their receptionist are unprofessional. 
especially the neurologist dr. schloss, i told them it was hard for me to get there and i was ill and crying and they still denied me. 
i'm currently at the putnam er. i wonder how i will be treated here.

had horrible pain in my stomach and lower back that increased throughout the day. had not engaged in any physical activity and was concerned that could possibly have some form of an infection or possibly my appendix . went to the er at putnam hospital. waited for over 2 hours despite the increasing pain and barely an ability to walk. after 2+ hours was ultimately brought to a room where i was left laying on a gurney for over 1 hour (so 3 hours + from when i first arrived at facility). was never triaged by a nurse or doctor to determine whether something more significant was going on which may have required more immediate assistance, was given no medicine and no medical attention and/or care. was not even given a pillow to lay on to try to help make me more comfortable. my husband complained and inquired for help with my increasing pain numerous times and was basically told that it was too bad i was in pain and we just had to wait. he was told that his repeated requests weren't "going to make the doctor see me any faster." a nurse practitioner...lorie gauthier...entered my room and when i expressed my frustration about being left for so long and in tears with increasing pain, she walked in and out and told me too bad, she wasn't going to "deal with me" and "i could wait for a doctor to come and see me when he had the time." at that point i left and my husband drove me to another hospital 25 minutes away...northern westchester hospital...where i was greeted with a wheel chair and received immediate care and support. i was at nwh for 3 hours start to finish including tests and medications provided...and this was the length of time i was at putnam hospital just waiting to be seen in the er. 

this is not the first time i have had this experience with putnam. my mother who is in her 70s was having chest pains, cough, confusion and significant pain in her leg and was left to wait in the putnam er the same way i was and they assumed that she "had the flu" given her age and symptoms. it was discovered that she had a pulmonary embolism and it was only my intense demanding that she be assessed that they discovered she was in more significant need and required more immediate care which she then subsequently received. however the nurses were not kind to her and were annoyed at my insistence that she be seen. 

despite its proximity to my home and being the closet place to access care i will never step foot in that disgusting, backwards, deplorable hospital again. northern westchester hospital exemplified what proper medical care should be and god willing in the event of an emergency i will be able to make it the 25 minutes to be seen there for care.

my son was injured at a high school football game, although it turns out the injury was not serious.   we nevertheless went to the phc emergency room to have him evaluated.  it was quiet and we were out of there in a reasonable time.  the staff was great.   phc is "in network" for my insurance.    four months later, however, we got a huge bill from a doctor we never saw who was a contractor to phc and therefore "out of network".   we didn't see her, but rather a physician's assistant who, we're told, was under her supervision.  nevertheless, we had to pay a huge bill to her for her supervision of a pa who did work for phc.   we were never told that anyone we were seeing was "out of network" or being supervised by someone "out of network", but apparently i signed away my right to object to this on one of those forms that you're shown but not really able to read.   such a scam.

should have trusted the mediocre reviews and my better judgement and gone to a different facility. we were out of town and needed emergency blood work done of our neurologist, to treat my wife's dizziness and head pains due recent adjustments in her  seizure medication. the basic problem was her meds were imbalanced and we needed  help getting our neurologist what she needed - blood work. my wife's medication was off balance and needed to be adjusted. carolyn the pa who was in her late 20's was ready to do a cat scan until we were able to finally get our doctor on the phone and share that it wasn't necessary. the initial nurse maura lacked empathy and cut off my wife several times as she tried to explain the details that led to her current condition. my wife is very  sensitive to blood work, and maura  was so sloppy they had to send in a second nurse to draw more blood because the first test results were incomplete. to his credit, joe, the second nurse, was nicer but basically rationalized the sloppiness and behavior of the previous nurse. long unnecessary delays didn't help either as we had to wait long periods of time between visits and had to ask several times for attention.

basically simple blood work that should  have taken less than an hour turned into a 3 1/2 hour unpleasant experience.

trust the reviews. don't make the mistake we did. thank goodness it wasn't more serious.

*update 11/21* family member is happy with the therapy that comes in and most the staff is friendly. said it does take them 30 minutes or more to get to their room. the food service often 4/5 times sends food that they can't eat. on the whole they said the food isn't bad but it's not great. very salty, no fruits or veg mostly starch and meat. 
one thing mentioned was the staff here talk about each other and complain a lot about each other and basically talk personal matters with the patients or within ear shot. my family member knows exactly who is who and what's going on in this peyton'
so far not impressed. a family member of mine is here and the hospital seams really uninformed, anytime a question is asked no one seams to know anything. this place is always dirty. spills on the floor, items not being swept up for several days. came in today and here was a pool of water just chilling, actually ruined a bunch of personal items like cards, flash cards to assist my family in communicating. i asked my family member who is in here they said it's hard to get nurses to come in and she said they aren't very attentive

this hospital is wonderful.  the staff is wonderful and the care given to my mother is outstanding.  after many fumbles and bumbles by other hospitals, this hospital saved my mother's life.  they were extremely thorough in all the test to determine what was wrong with my mother.  i am so grateful for finding this hospital.

brought my mom to the er for various heart related issues. long story short, she spent a total of 4 days in the hospital. needed a stent in the end.
we love this hospital! all nurses, technicians, doctors were very friendly, attentive and knowledgeable. all rooms are private too. on top of that the food is excellent. we had been to baptist in stone oak in the past for my sister and did not like it at all. that's why we went to methodist this time. really glad we did.

went to er at 5pm. it is now 3am and was just told after asking when will we get a room. answer we are booked no rooms available.  why you didn't say this at beginning.  
sleepless in a chair. sux

only go here if you want them to kill you. my husband was seen here in the er. he was septic and they called an alert for it. five minutes later registration came in and found out we didn't have insurance. a few minutes after that the nurse came back in and said he was being discharged for the common cold and was told to buy his tylenol at the local drug store. we left and he was still very ill. took him to another hospital where he was immediately seen and was once again put on sepsis alert and ended up staying a week in the hospital! 

this hospital should be ashamed of themselves along with the doctors who just want to make a buck! if he would of went home and stayed there he would be dead! 


update: they are still trying to bill us $3000 for what??

these yo-yo's will send a bill to the wrong address, and when they don't get paid, they take you to court thru a collection agency. i would suggest double-verifying any information they have for you before you spend your money on lawyers and court fees, or go somewhere else.

i highly recommend methodist hospital stone oak if you are in need of a hospital stay. yes he entire team is courteous, professional and caring. i have had to come here on multiple occasions and it has been as great an experience as a hospital stay can be.

really disappointed in the emergency care.   been here going on 7 hours.  if my 88 year old mom is sick enough to need to stay in the hospital for shortness of breath and afib - how can sitting in a hallway "bed" over 3 hours waiting for a "room to be cleaned" be the best attention she can receive?   pretty much told to suck it up we have one housekeeper and you'll get a room but we can't give any idea of when it might be - it could be midnight/it could be 3:00 am.    it's not like anyone is even checking on her.....   she's missed all her evening meds;  thank gosh i brought her some food!

the security guards are my methodist are rude and nosey. after being admitted to the hospital for 4 days i really needed a cigarette.  so on the 4th night around 2:30am while things were slow, i hopped into my wheelchair (safety first), got a family member to push me in the wheel chair outside away from any nonsmoking area signs and had 1 cig. after i was done, my family member rolled me back up to my room, i was gone exactly 5 minutes, with no issues. the security guard stopped me on my way back and wanted to see my id (mind you he saw us go outside, we both had visitor id stickers on our shirts,  and i have several iv's and medical equipment attached to myself & my wheelchair). he insisted on looking at my id, and my medical wrist band. the guard sees our id's and everything, then calls up to the charge nurse on the hospital floor my room is on, just to tattle on me and try to get the nurses in trouble. smh so now i can't go grab a smoke if i get the nitch to do so in a few days. the security guard comes off as a wannabe cop with a chip on his shoulder. i can say this because i am a fra, k9-unit. instead of cutting a person like me a break, seeing how much physical & emotional stress i'm going through, and understanding 1 cig never hurt anyone (special when i went out my way to go smoke beyond the no smoking signs) he has to act like a jack-ass and report me and my family member to several others. 

i want to add that this security guard was rude while he questioned myself and my family member. not only that but there was 2 other elderly gentlemen filing a complaint for a sinus .

i was seen in november 2019 to remove a hernia and they discharged me too early. i had to urinate before leaving and i told the nurse it was only drops not a full amount but she ok y'all are ready to go. so we left and by the way i live 2 1/2 hours away so we ate real quick and left. once we were halfway home we stopped in another town and i realized i could not urinate. so we went to the er their and they said if i had gone all the way home my bladder would have exploded because the previous hospital didn't make sure i could pee. i had to have a catheter in me for 3 days so now i am stuck with even more hospital bills than i can afford and i cannot pay. i have tried contacting the hospital but have had no response. maybe this will help. i do not blame the doctor i blame the hospital because they need to implement a better procedure or something.

this was absolutely the worst experience i've ever had. my 4yr old daughter was in a pretty bad car accident and she was taken by ambulance to this butcher shop. she was bruised along her shoulders was having trouble walking and was complaining of having a bad headache then she threw up infront of a staffer, i'm not a doctor but that to me is definitely a concussion. still we waited around 3 hrs in the er waiting room before being called in. still 1 more hr passed befor a doctor even saw her. through out this i'm trying to bring attention to the issue and no one gave a fuck. what upsets me the most is that they tried to say that her throwing up was probably due to a virus. they should be shut down.

they saved my boy.  brought my 4 year old son in here past midnight for severe rash, bloodshot eyes and high fever he had for about 5 days.  we went in during the wee hours of the night so we were taken care of and triaged right away.  even though we had done endless research on his symptoms at home and had a gut feeling he had kawasaki disease, it only took 2 mins for the doctor to examine him and confirmed the correct diagnosis.  i was emotional.  the next 4 days in the hospital were exhausting and trying for the family but the hospital doctors and staff were nothing short of great.  my son including us were all comforted and taken care of tremendously well.  we were put in a nice big room.  the only negative thing for us was that we must've seen 20 different or same doctors repeating and asking the same thing over and over again and at the end we were billed for all.  we felt that was a bit of an overkill and unnecessary.  

follow up appointments were all great.  doctors are really fantastic and know there stuff.  nurses were very attentive and caring.

premier birth center was the best place i could have ever chosen for my birth! i entered not knowing much about the birthing process and felt educated and confident going into labor. the midwives get to know you and truly care about your wellbeing in every interaction. i had the birth i wanted with the help of an amazing team. i would truly recommend this place to anyone and everyone!

terrible from the start the birthplace is so not where u should go for best birthing care. 
i had epidural way too soon was there 2 days then emergency c section. ignored my pain when epidural was gone .  my baby was perfect no issues. the rushed her to springfield because they couldnt read an xray of her belly. they put iv in wrong on her foot i tood them it was wrong when my baby was screaming when they flushed the wrongly place iv. then her leg swelled up i said it's wrong take it out. so then she had to suffer through it again. springfield des came and got her. did tests there in nicu for 2 days and no problems. none. so 2 weeks of a terrible worried start that i'll never get back when all was good. they seem under qualified sorry to say but i never thought i'd have to go through what i did if they would have listened the epidural would have went right. the epidural woman was rude and when she mailed a mistake and had to do it again said it wasn't her fault . even the nurses knew it was her fault. best nurse is kim she works 12 hours 2 days a week and if it wasn't for her i would have not made it. thank you for being a light in a dark place. thank you. sorry for typos i get going when i'm angry.

i was in hosp for three days and was generally satisfied with my care for high blood pressure. i was less satisfied with sanitation in the shared bathroom and there is no privacy in double room. nurses were !mostly ok but forgot things like relaxing compression cuffs and putting on heart !monitor for a few hours. seemed uncoordinated.

i was seen for 2 ovarian cysts (1 ruptured) on 12/02/19. both caused bleeding, pain and nausea not managed by naproxen, diclofenac, or promethazine at home. i was vomiting and crying from severity of the  pain. when i attempted to explain this to dr. donald, an older blonde pa cut me off, snatched my paperwork from my hands and abruptly said, "leave." i had seen this same nurse/pa on the left side of the of the candler er treating obgyn issues and she was disrespectful and unprofessional during my exam and even misdiagnosed me with a disease i never even had. 
dr. donald and the other nurses, however, were excellent and very respectful, knowledgeable, and kind.

i worked for this organization and i absolutely loved  it . i was going through a lot of personal issues regarding my living situation. my supervisor knew i wwas going to be homeless and he didn't bat an eye. i continued on and a few days later i did resign from the position because i did not have a place to go after work to lay my  head to rest and i was on my 90 day probation so i knew i was not able to get days off yet . i ended up resolving my issue the day after i resign so i quickly called my boss to see if there was any way to get my job back. prior to me leaving , i had an conversation with my boss explaining to him what was going on and why i needed to resign and he assured that if i ever did come back i would get my job back. i received a call a couple days after resigning and trying to get my job back, stating that i was not able to get rehired at any st joseph candler. i was super disappointed because i really enjoyed my job and the people i worked with. one of the reasons why i was drawn to working in this hospital because of its religiousness. i am disappointed because when i was in need of help no one helped me and doing the right christian thing you should help individuals that are in need. i have lost so much respect for this organization as an employee. they like to push the fact that their so religious but i was completely lied to by my boss and i was let down by this organization knowing my living situation.

despite coronavirus and all the crazy people coming to the hospital. i came in for surgery.
they are very very prepared at this abrazo. as soon as you walk in hospital someone is there with gloves mask telling you to clean ur hands and take a mask if needed. went to admissions got all that taken care of and went over to out patient surgery. again asked to clean my hands and get prepped for my surgery. it was empty when i was there since it was only 5am. by the time it was go time it was packed!!!
all the nurses, the surgery techs,my anesthesiologists and my amazing gyno all took great care of me. we laughed i got a great cocktail in my iv lol. after surgery the nurses in recovery were just as amazing took wonderful care of me until it was time to go home.
went home and had to come back bc i started to bleed. how "scary " i had to wait in the er for 5 hours even those nurses not to nice they are very rude and snippy!! like a completely different style of nurses form outpatient surgery to er( those ladies need a nice lesson lol)
so my doctors all knew i was in the er. but it was slammed. anyway got seen got a pressure bandage put on my stomach and went on my merry way.
this abrazo is great!

i am completely frustrated with this hospital and their staff. i visited this facility in may 2019. when it came time to pay, i gave them all of my insurance information, paid my copay, and was good to go. or so i thought. i have been trying since may (it is now february 2020) to get this outstanding bill taken care of and they are making it impossible. i have called several times and am getting different information each time. not to mention the staff are extremely rude (when i call in january 2020, the woman i spoke with hung up on me). all they needed to do in the first place was rebill my insurance. this is completely unacceptable and i am horribly disappointed with the service i am receiving. it suffices to say that once i have this bill taken care of, i will not be returning to this facility. 

i do not recommend abrazo west campus. 

as a recommendation for the hospital, i believe it would be in your best interest to higher staff members that possess some semblance of professionalism.

sent an employee that was injured on the job to have a minor injury cared for. it is required of our insurance that she has a drug test when work related injuries occur. the front desk was notified as the office manager came with her. the nurse was alerted as well as the physician. the test was not done and coming to abrazo 30 minutes after she left to get the necessary drug test was billed for an entire new admission, new physican charge and nursing fees. complaining does not help. i was given multiple excuses. doctor wasn't told. doctor deemed medically not necessary.  patient refused (she did not and was tested on the second admission) and finally it wasn't written in the chart. they are more than willing to double bill for their error.

back in january i visited abrazo's west campus after having been sick for a few days. i had woken up shivering and unwisely jumped in the shower to warm up ending up passing out. went to urgent care and due to me being extremely weak and scared of me passing out again they sent me to the er. we chose abrazo for the location. our troubles started when we first got there. as i was extremely weak from my sickness we thought i should be wheeled into the er. the lady refused to come get me but gave us a chair to use. i luckily got right in. once in it seemed that their equipment needed updated as the machine to pump fluids kept malfunctioning. they gave me fluids and pain meds even though i didn't mention being in any pain. our biggest issues was with leaving. at the end of my stay is when they came to take my insurance (this should be done at the start of a visit).  she came back saying i was out of network and would have to pay $4000 before insurance would cover (this for a flu test, fluids, pain meds, and xrays). she asked if we could pay that right there. thankfully we couldn't as i got my bill finally and only owe less than $400. i am happy i don't have to pay $4000 but feel that your employee in charge of insurances should know what insurances will and will not cover. after this i was discharged saying it's not the flu but just something viral and i'm free to go. keep in mind i still feel like crap and extremely weak. i asked for a dr.s note for the next few days and was told "we don't do that". when i got home my temperature was still at 103 degrees and shivering uncontrollably. so on top of being super sick for days. i got to go to the er, be told i have to pay $4000 (luckily didn't have to pay that) just to end up feeling how i did when i came in.

my 89 year old father fell at home in the pm.... called 911 and they were there within minutes. they checked him out on the outside with an  ekg and all was well, despite the blood and a knocked out  tooth  and the  passing out! paramedics said to bring him to er to get a cat scan of his head. because i feared the worst, i brought him to abrazo er on a monday night. had someone help dad out of the car and into a wheelchair only to find out his emergency was not bad enough to be seen right away. of course we're thinking a brain bleed because he hit his head so hard. after an hour or so finally got to triage where they took vitals...just as the emts  did when i called them to the house. then went back out to the lobby to wait with the about 30 other people in the waiting room. i accessed the damage to my dad and figured if he had a brain bleed here...right now in the waiting room....i'd rather him be comfortable in his own bed at home with us! i knew from experience that he wasn't  getting inside to be treated for many, many more hours. and that doesn't even count trying to get him in room to be admitted. so, my dilemma....89 years old , head injury, nobody paying attention to him, my call was to go home to his wife and his own bed and relax and sleep.!...long story short...thank god so far he is good!!! but what the hell is going on with our neighborhood er? there were people before us that was waiting over 4-5 hours! that before getting through the double doors to even see a doctor.
what does abrazo need to keep up with demand of all these emergencies?

to the reviewer richard m.

i've been a nurse for 12yrs, and been at abrazo west for 8.
i've worked side by side with kelly for six years, and find him to be without question one of the best rt's i've ever worked with.
i've seen him hold the hand of a woman dying that had no family there.
i've seen him not only skip lunch several times, but buy lunch for a family member that had no money. every viet nam vet that comes here, he makes it his mission to visit with them. he's also a very talented song writer, and gives each vet a special song on cd he wrote about their sacrifice and patriotism. he has been recognized many, many times in his six years here. an rt for decades, i wonder how many in total.  patients actually ask for him by name.
he has also been nominated for a daisy award, due to his understanding and compassion. the daisy award is for nursing excellence but, administration deemed it necessary to recognize an rt.    (amazing man)   i showed your grammatically incorrect review
to every employee on staff today, and 100% of them know him and worked with him extensively.  they think you're just an unhappy man.
god blessed this man with the talent and every facet of people skills
for any type of patient. 
sadly, he has moved on to another abrazo facility. he will be greatly missed by co workers and patients alike. 

p.s.  i hope your family member or friend is doing well in spite of kelly

stay away!  we spent 7 hours yesterday at this facility, 4 hours in the waiting room and 3 hours in the er room.  this place is more like a medical providers office.  the staff is cold and unsympathetic to the pain and discomforts of the patients that have come in to see them for help. during our time there was a stroke victim came in and was left in the waiting room for 3.5 hours before being seen, a young man with, what i suspect was a broken ankle (swollen and discoloring quickly) was put in a wheel chair that was placed by the sliding door that remained open throughout his 3 hours before being seen (it was 51 degree outside). the young man sat there shivering and covering his face with his hoodie in an effort to stay warm. he had shorts on and sat directly within eyesight of the registration desk. the room was very uncomfortable hard chairs, food crumbs and half drunk coffee cups with a tv that remained off. when it was your turn, you knew it as well as everyone else.  the medical providers would remain behind the reception desk yelling your name out and if you didn't appear within a few seconds, another yelling out of your name would be called out.  most of the times that patients in the waiting room would respond by stating, "she's coming" as we did for the stroke victim who's daughter moved her slowly in her wheelchair or we would call out the person's name as the room was a long narrow curve that some from the back cannot hear the yelling's from behind the desk.  when we got to the back, my husband who was experiencing severe abdominal pain was brought to a room with a chair, not a bed. due to this he remained in a uncomfortable state. the pa that attended to him was very nice, this is my only compliment to this place - we liked her a lot. she was genuine, caring and friendly.  the chatter of the rn's in this facility was horrible. they spoke of birthday parties out loud, almost yelling to one another. they spoke loudly behind the drapes to the patients of their diagnosis. there was no respect for patient privacy here. after my husbands cat scan was done we were told we needed to move to the waiting room.  i immediately stated, "are you kidding me? he's finally in a comfortable state laying down after 4 hours in your waiting room." she stated as my husband got out of the bed slowly and with much difficult, "we need the bed".  at no time did she even offer assistance while he struggled to get up. in addition we still didn't even have the results of the cat scan and when i asked how long that would be she said "it could be hours".   it made no sense to me. when we got my husbands diagnosis the lady said, "its just a piece of fat, you can go home".  i felt like stating and per the previous pa, its a piece of fat that has been advised needs surgery asap or it could become a blockage, but i hesitated to be as cold and rude as her.  there was so much that happen at this place yesterday, but these are the ones that i have the time to write down.  please take your loved ones somewhere else. i know their response will be to send an email to their patient care team as they have in all their other negative reviews.  my response for them now is, "how about making changes, instead of the same generic response you have given so many already."  i told my husband, while we were there waiting for the results, "if you need surgery it will not be here" and "if i ever need an ambulance or care, do not ever take me here."

do not recommend abrazo. usually go to banner but thought we give abrazo a chance. staff is friendly but do not communicate with patients or family. checked in room by 8pm after hour and a half wait which understandable they are busy. later daughter was left  unhooked from fluids to give a urine sample and no one rehooked fluids back which she needed. no one came back to check on her for 2 hours and hard to flag someone down to come check her. only time was able to get someone was when they came back to take her for an ultra sound at 11pm and let someone know. finally after 15 minutes of ultra sound tech notifying them someone finally came over. they make you feel uncomfortable and not want to stay. it is worth to drive a little further to a different hospital.

my adult son works in marysville. he was in extreme pain and come to this hospital. i was worried because of their 2 star review but the staff, nurses and doctors were very friendly, helpful and quick to figure out what was wrong and treat him.

the va is worthless, they won't see me because of my bcd (caught my then wife in bed with a soldier and beat the shit out of him), even though i have 4 of the 8 gulf war syndrome symptoms. 3 years and 9 months of stellar service (2 aam's, an arcom, c.i.b., jump wings and all the other medals and ribbons). now that they should be helping me, nope, f u mr. jason s.

i am sick from the b.s. i did and went through "for my country", now they just blow me off.

my husband was her for 1 week after having a stroke. they told us he would be discharged on a friday and would start in home therapy. his case manager gave us the name of the agency and said they would contact us over the weekend. no call. i called the agency monday morning and was told they didn't have anything for him. they were waiting on the insurance authorization. i reached back to our case manager and explained what was happening. she said she couldn't help with the authorization. that's part of her job to make sure the patient is set to be discharged and his next step is in place.  how do you discharge someone and not have the therapy set up. when we left the case manager was in the room and said you're free to go.  we are walking out and the security guard stops us and says "are you a patient"  we reply yes.  he said there should be a nurse escorting you out!  this facility doesn't follow protocol.    my husband is at a standstill. all this shows is encompass doesn't care!
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Miami

review: wonderful nurses and staffs here! they are all every professional and caring about their patient !
fac_name: The Silvercrest Center for Nursing and Rehabilitation

review:
memorial hospital........when you say that name in our city people shudder and look ill. 
this hospital needs to be closed and the staff sent to prison. they are evil incarnate. 
i am writing this for my wife who was victimized by the staff at this hellhole.

my wife was first seen at grandview hospital, but they were far and away to understaffed and lacking facilities. so, despite her medical mandate, the staff sent her to memorial hospital anyway. she was then robbed(actually robbed) by a nurse whom stole her engagement ring. after being victimized for the 1st time in regards to her ring. she then had a colonic resection for a perforated bowel. this part was the only event of a positive nature at this garbage dump. the anesthesiologist called me to authorize an epidural for pain management. this is when i informed him that my wife has a problem with opioid drugs, and will become instantly addicted if given to her. i asked him to note that in her records and he said he did. he then proceeded to badly botch the epidural installation. it immediately came out. 3 hours after surgery she was finally given a room. when i finally found her she was in agonizing pain at having just been disemboweled and then incredibly crudely sewn back together. the nurse said she would check with the surgeon and the anesthesiologist about what to do. the nurse practitioner came in and informed the city nurse to request a bolus dose of pain meds. another hour later it was approved. by this time it was around 9 p.m. and i had been driving around town trying to find my wife and then waiting for her to get a room and went home to sleep. the following morning i went back at 8 a.m.  she was still in agonizing pain and had been complaining to the duty nurse all sleepless night long. the new np and duty nurse had again called the anesthesiologist whom could not be reached period. so, a new anesthesiologist came in to advise. his discovery was that the epidural was very poorly done and had come completley out of the incision and had been pumping the pain meds down her back all night long. he authorized it's removal and installation of an iv instead. an hour and a half later someone finally showed up to put in the iv.  at this point my wife had gone through almost 15 hours of abuse and manhandling neglect by the incompetent staff. all of these people at this hospital should be charged with criminal neglect and abuse. medical malpractice is the mainstay of this facility. the pieces of human garbage here tortured and abused my wife and then pumped her full of highly addictive opioid drugs despite the warnings issued to them. they also illegally performed surgery on her due to her medical mandate to never be seen at this location. we are currently interviewing out of state attorneys because u.c. health apparently goes out of it's way to threaten and intimidate local law firms.  

if it were up to me, i would send this entire staff to prison with a tattoo on their foreheads that says.......hi i'm a pedophile.
 the management staff are 100% equally complicit in this as the internet is full of nightmare stories equally terrifying or even worse as this and they still do nothing to rectify this ghoulish behavior. may you all burn in hell for eternity.

multiple errors the past few months at memorial north and memorial central. memorial north: i had a hand xray as an outpatient...when i viewed the results posted in "my health connection"...there was a shoulder xray that was not mine in my chart. the shoulder had a replacement part (metal)...and i don't have that. it took them 2 weeks and 10 people to fix that mistake. my brother was an inpatient at memorial north with the flu. the very young, inexperienced rn gave him 35 units of short acting insulin at bedtime. this is a huge error, which i later found out was a error written by the doctor (resident). but the nurse should have been smart enough to know not to give that much insulin, without food at bedtime! i just had my gallbladder removed 2 weeks ago at memorial central. i waited 3 months to have dr. willard do my surgery. i literally saw her for 30 seconds in the pre-op holding area; she didn't even make eye contact with me; didn't introduce herself to my husband; didn't ask if we had any questions. never saw her again. i asked my rn if i could speak with dr. willard either in person or by phone after surgery... she said "no we don't do that".  the rn forgot to send my paper rx for pain medication with me upon discharge...because narcotics "cannot be sent electronically or called in"...i found out later when i called her from home. she said "oh yeah...our printer was broken...". so it took me two hours to get the pain medication straightened out...then the pharmacy didn't have it ready til the following day. i decided not to pick it up...by that time i just decided to use tylenol. i also asked for follow up lab work requisition from the surgical resident at the hospital because my liver enzymes were very elevated due to the gallbladder issue. she said "oh, you need to contact your primary doctor for that". so i did...it took that doctor 4 days to get back to me. so taking tylenol with elevated liver enzymes concerned me...but i guess the physicians at uchealth are ok with it! today... was the cherry on top of this disaster of a cake! went to memorial central for an arthrogram of my wrist with an mri. i was told a doctor would be doing an injection of dye into my wrist before the mri...but no. a very shaky, nervous rpa shows up and fumbles around just long enough for me to tell her to stop the procedure. first she didn't use enough lidocaine to numb the area; second, she put the injection needle in...it fell over when she let go of it...so the needle moved! then before rechecking the needle placement with fluoroscopy...she decided to try to go ahead and inject the dye until i asked her "are you going to recheck the needle placement?"....so she did. it was completely in the wrong spot! so she decided to start pushing the needle in (without using the fluoroscopy viewing) and when she hit a nerve in my wrist and i jumped, she yanked the needle out! then she said i guess i will give you more lidocaine... i said nope we are done. ( i am a rn...vascular access rn...so i knew for sure, even tho anyone could have picked up on this...does not know what she is doing.). i am done with this hospital. going to mayo clinic in az for my wrist surgery and testing. i will either go to penrose...or drive clear to denver from now on for health care.

my review is strictly for the radiology dept #1..... that whisked me over to the other radiology dept #2 that was at the other end of the hospital where i originally parked- because who knew there are two "2" radiology dept's in one humongous hospital- but there it is--- and it's right there on the hospital map in all it's color chart glory that i couldn't read due to a serious eye issue (which is why i am here) and - my pic who had just had 1-eye cataract surgery a week ago - can't see for shizzle- (so we were doomed) and basically we only had 1 good eye between the two of us- and my small chubby legs, t-rex arms and doggy heart were not-going-to -make-the walk- back to 10 plum st- where i parked and was supposed to be! in the first place.

- but anyway- the other radiology dept was waiting for me, i had a massive migraine and the admit desk called a wheel chair for me, thank goodness- and off i went to the to the other radiology -anyway---the team here---  awesome amazing and helpful with that wheelchair on what had to be the freaking coldest day ever!!  yes, i left my jacket on the 10th floor of the parking garage! okay! 

i had to keep this review light and quirky -considering my situation is not but hey - gotta find the smile in life!!

ah. healthcare in the us. your  fear of getting bad  treatment only rivals your fear of going  bankrupt after. 

it's the system  they say, and yes to a certain extent that's right. in what  other system  can a piece of medical software promote addictive drugs to doctors  disguised as real advice but is actually just a kickback from a drug maker?  that doctors went along with it isn't exactly reassuring, but a system with profit motive and dealing in life and death can't promise  a good outcome. 

however you do find medical people rising to the challenge to make the system better. and not just in television shows. 

is robert wood johnson such a place? no, not at all. want to  know when your surgery will be? tough you aren't going to  know. want to park to visit  your loved one? twenty dollars please!  want receptionists who are kind and aware that  people looking for room  numbers may be under stress and offer kindness? well, move your ass into the right line and shut your mouth. 

you are treated like you are visiting a prisoner   your loved one will be treated like  one too. i can't imagine in an actual emergency what it would be like. 

the argument in the us against nationalized healthcare is that one will lose the quality of care in the us. it's no accident the argument has now been people in insurance will not have  jobs; places like this make the quality argument weak. nowhere is the emphasis on care  on display here. if you have a choice don't come here. it's dismal indeed.

my wife waited for three days to get transferred here. was told the surgery would happen monday. now it's going to be thursday. maybe. or maybe not. maybe they will just keep her there forever.

i was skeptical about coming here. i have a 5 month old. my child couldn't breathe because my child was coughing and turned blue. they did not even stick me in a triage room. it was awful. you put unvaccinated babies in an adult waiting room  with the general population? i hope osha or whatever nj has to regulate hospitals wakes up. someone will die due to the advanced negligence of this hospital. if i ever get shot in nj, drive me to kings county brooklyn. you have a better shot of surviving than to go here. 

once my child was in the pediatric er, the nurse was good. they send in a resident. it took forever to see the doctor. she was ehhh. no bedside manner. i felt like i was wasting her time being there. like mom shamed. my doctor was sick. she doesn't have a backup. she said take baby to er. so i complied. next time i'll drive to nyc. i understand there are tons of respiratory infections but they wouldn't even swab my under 6 month old baby for rsv. can't wait for the bill. i am absolutely calling the patient advocate team to complain. they claimed it was crowded. come to ny and you'll see crowded. healthcare in nj is subpar. hackensack meridan is so much better. no sense of urgency at this hospital. i'm glad the nurse came out and got me and brought us in. she was empathetic. no one else gave 2 shits. i should have called 911.

having had previous, unavoidable experiences with robert wood's emergency room, it was with a mixture of trepidation and dread that i found myself once more walking through the emergency room entrance. previously, my father had often been a patient there due to a long battle with cancer which necessitated several trips to this particular emergency room.  at that time i had never before experienced such a complete disregard for basic patient care in an emergency room setting.
so when my elderly mother was transported there after a very serious fall this past week i was shocked as to how little has changed. this was a monday afternoon however you would have thought it was new year's eve - the waiting room was a war zone. at least forty people were cramped inside - patients were sitting on the floor - vomit was on the floors, in the bathrooms and even in front of the entrance! several heavily armed policeman stood looking menacingly at every person checking in. my mother was already in the er so i was waiting in line to check in. not knowing what her status was i was understandably anxious to get back to see her. however, i had to wait in line with patients that were checking in. as hipaa does not appear to be something that this hospital is familiar with, i was privy to most of these patients entire medical history. this was unavoidable as the receptionist loudly repeated it back to the patient, in front of all of us standing there. i became even more outraged when it became evident that most of the patients there were using the emergency room for their primary care - issues included stomach aches, slight fevers, colds, headaches, etc. - which were non emergencies and could have been dealt with at a pcp appointment. 
upon finally getting my "clearance" to go back to the emergency room (i had to have my id scanned - was told that weapons and/or drugs are not allowed - i felt like saying that the brooks brothers topcoat i was wearing does not have inner pockets large enough to hold a glock and meth just to be snarky however with two police officers glaring at me i felt it more prudent to just hold my tongue and press on).
once back in the emergency room i was disappointed to see that although the interior had been updated their view on quality of care remained the same. when my father was there he and several other patients were lined up on guerneys in the hallway for hours - one visit my father was in the hallway for 7 hours!
i arrived to find the same scene - row after row of patients lined up on stretchers against the walls. i found my elderly mother next to the nurses station covered in blood from severe facial lacerations. and then the wait began ..... one hour no nurse/no doctor; two hours the same; three hours the same. i was given a wash basin so i could wash the blood off my mom's face and hands. 
as this hospital once again has no conception of hipaa i found out from the team of doctors and nurses hovering over the patient in front of us that he came in with what he thought was chest pains - however he said it could have been indigestion from the two double cheeseburgers he ate. the young woman behind use was going through chemotherapy and was severally ill - once again staff went through her medical history for all to hear. 
i am generally a very patient person. i cannot begin to understand the stress that the staff in these settings are put under. however after 4 hours without a nurse or doctor even having the courtesy to stop and just apologize for the delay my patience was at an end. i stopped the nearest nurse and demanded that my mother be seen.
well amazingly enough a neurology intern and two nurses appeared out of thin air. they said it was busy but they would follow up and try to get my mother out of the hallway and into one of the er bays.
after 2 more hours she was finally moved to a semi private bay.
my niece who is a nurse practitioner arrived and thankfully took charge. the remainder of my mom's stay went relatively smoothly due to my niece's non stop advocacy.
however my niece was appalled by the condition of the facility. the bathrooms were filled with feces and urine, she found hypodermic needles in the elevator, the puddles of vomit in front of the entrance to the er remained there all day. 
in closing, avoid this emergency room at all costs! my mother will now be going to princeton medical center - a new facility that is clean with top flight staff where patients are treated as human beings and not objects of inconvenience.
also as an aside, during our "stay" in the er we kept noticing police and detectives running up and down the hallways - evidently there had been a "drive by shooting" in which 3 people were shot. individuals associated with the event were attempting to gain access to the er which had security on hyper alert. not the type of environment that i would want to expose any of my family members to again.

i love this emergency room. so huge and so busy. everyone works so hard. i came in one busy day and a team of doctors seen me and diagnosed me. they said i only had 6 months to live. after 6 months i couldn't afford the bills anymore so they gave me another 6 months to pay. how nice. 

thank you kaiser er.

had to come here this last week with a family member who got hurt at work.  occupational medicine staff was extremely nice and helpful. they sent us to the er to help get member fixed (great service in er, but could've been a lot cleaner) and then off to another building for a prescription.  as the weather was nice, going back and forth to different buildings was doable, but would be a nightmare when the weather is bad. we got a bit tired in the end. plus, the maps to find your way are few and far between and hard to find, so its hit or miss to figure out where the heck you are. we ended up resorting to the 'map view' on our cell phone and that made trekking back and forth easier.

the worst thing i can say about here--and its well known--is parking. the lot is full to the brim and good luck finding a spot. kaiser could have the place covered in 10 story garages, and parking would still be hit or miss.  security roams constantly to make you move your car and i basically ended up dropping my family member at the building he needed, then circling the lot constantly until he called me to come pick him up. that's pretty much the only downfall here.

parking sucks!!! it literally took me 30 minutes to find a parking spot. i'm so glad i actually got there early enough to waste all of that time. we made it to our appointment with 3 minutes to spare. get there early. expect to spend a good amount of time trying to find a parking spot. we were there on a wednesday at 2:00. (just an fyi). other than that, the hospital was great, staff was great.

by far the most degrading emergency room visit i've had. they literally leave you lying in a chair on the side of a hallway. there's no care for patient dignity. when asked if i was waiting for a room to open up, they said "no. sorry. we've just been really busy. and we're just waiting for your test results"
the lack of diversity amongst the e.r. staff was discouraging.
when you remind them that you've been there for hours they tell you they've seen people there for days.
"atleast you have a recliner to sit on" -kaiser staff
they had such an amazing staff. unfortunately i had to stay at the hospital for five days , but each and every nurse/doctor that helped me was very informative and helped me with all my needs .

juliet is the amazing nurse that was taking care of my husband in icu a26 west. rm 19. she kept us entertained. super nice and took a realllly good care. if you or family member ever get admitted there in icu ask for her. also mike who helped him walk, he truly cares for his patients. just great staff and shout out to amy she was awesome. these are rockstars of kaiser.

the doctor blake montana legit sucks. it's like he doesn't even know what he's talking about. he just comes up with some random solution about what he thinks might be the problem. just sucks to wait here for hours on end and for a doctor to talk to you for two seconds and not know for sure if it's one thing or the other and to follow up with your primary care doctor. like come on people if you don't like your job then quit. he doesn't know anything about customer privacy, he's screaming at my sister about what she thinks might be wrong with her and he says how "he and his coworkers all had a laugh" about her symptoms. what the hell is that? horrible er. wow, i'm amazed.

my wife just delivered at the roseville eureka location.  holy smokes it was a crazy experience. this was our first child.  we are and we're complete rookies.  

my wife was in labor for four days.  the doctor broke her water to help hurry the process along.  after 20 hours they brought her in for a c-section.  i was freaked out.  being a rookie in this area i also didn't realize how serious this procedure is/was. anyways, my wife had some minor complications and our baby landed in nicu.  needless to say i was a hot mess.  i've never felt more helpless in my life.  

if your in the same situation i recommend this location.  the nurses are literally solders.  they each have there own stories, and in almost all cases have been through something similar or more substantial.  i learned so much from all these amazing people.  i really appreciate them.

the ladies in nicu were also the best.  i feel like i owe them more than a co-pay.  they were upfront about our situation, but also reassuring.  i learned how to clean diapers, feed, hold the baby properly, and burp from tera and janelle.  i love them both.  words cannot illustrate how grateful i am to both of you.  

i'n the end everyone made it out healthy:)

i'm sending the post from my iphone, so please excuse any misspellings or grammatical mistakes.

cheers!!

they take good care of me! they are good about preventative medicine, promote diet, exercise and healthy lifestyle. my doctor is good listener and very knowledgeable. good parking and convenient location.

very disappointed with the services here. my husband was seen here friday and sunday for severe stomach pains. both visits the doctor did not provide any testing on his stomach. next time, we will go to sutter roseville.

beware of christopher romberg!!!!! wow i have never been so disgusted by the lack of "bed side manner" or attitude from a doctor. i'm severely concerned for anyone who has to been seen by him. he walked into the appointment for my mother and immediately stated - "i have 20 minutes so let's do this" in the rudest way possible. from that point on the appointment was extremely uncomfortable. he seemed as though he didn't want anything to do with the appointment he was very rude asking the questions and acted as though the answers to the questions were not adequate enough for him. he then gave a bs response to the pain in my mother's stomach advising that he will just give her numbing shots instead of getting down to the root of the problem. it feels as though he didn't care about fixing the actual problem just scratching the surface enough to say he did his job.... not. i then said to him that i understand he may be over worked from a large caseload or something along those lines but this is 10 years of pain hes trying to brush off like it was nothing. he then became extremely hostile and stood up towering over my mother and i with his voice raised and said that i was attacking him and that he's done with this appointment and he'll just assign us another doctor. i am blown away. we paid a $55 copay for 15 minutes of a half ass dr being rude and making us feel extremely uncomfortable. i am disgusted.
the doctors have been great here. the parking is not great but you'll usally find a spot but further out. overall the staff have been great and i'm happy with the service here.

if i could give one stars i would. this is the third bad review i have had to leave because of freaking kaiser. i was at the discharge pharmacy the early morning of dec 17, 19 at 12:00 in the morning. i was waiting on a script for my very sick husband to get his cough stuff. his name came up on the board and i got in line behind the customer they were already helping. as i was standing there a man sitting down behind mes name came up on the board. he said "oh my name just popped up" to nobody in particular. then he gets up and stands next to me but he kind of kept inching his way toward the window. i figured he was maybe trying to make sure that other people knew he was in line. nope. as soon as the people being helped were done he jumps in front of me and strolls on up to the window. i said very politely that i was indeed next. he ignored me. then the pharmacist looked at me and asked what i had said. i repeated that i had been next in in line. the rude pharmacist said to me "his name is in the board and you need to check in. whoever's name is on the list has medication ready. youre not next." and i said "my name showed up on the board first as i was there before he was in general". and the pharmacist just ignored me too. wth. normally i wouldn't care but my husband was super sick and i dont like for him to have to sit there longer because the rude pharmacist wants to play favorites when my hubs was miserable and just wanted his cold meds so he could go home and go to bed. toatally rude and unacceptable. as the line jumper got his meds as he turned to leave he said to me "im sorry i jumped in front of you. i didnt mean to". first of all, yes you 100% meant to but whatever. at least he apologized and acknowledged what he did. but i was so mad at the jerk pharmacist and the fact my hubs was having to wait longer i just shrugged. not my finest moment when someone was trying to correct a wrong (even if he did lie about not doing it on purpose) and normally i would have been more understanding but the fact that the pharmacist had decided that one patient was more important than another despite me being 100% ahead of this other man and dismissed me like im not a paying customer and called me a liar pretty much i was a little less unaccepting than usual. that is definitely not a way anyone should be treating patients. we pay far too much money a month on our insurance to be treated that way by anyone working there. the guy checking people out wasnt the problem, so i have nothing against him except he missed a medication i had asked for and then had to rewait. but thats a simple mistake. he was nice and doing the best he can. but the actual pharmacist, he has no business treating anyone like they are nothing, especially when the cutter himself admitted what he did. so thanks discharge guy. thanks for making my husband even more miserable because you want to treat people like dirt. another grievance to fill out. imagine that. we pay enough for our over expensive care that there is no excuse for what he did. none.

the er is in need of a overhaul the system in place is awful.  they need better staff and need to let at least one family member back in the er.  the nurses do not keep you informed or have any information on the patient.  this hospital should look at others to see where they can improve    they also need a larger er waiting room.  i was attacked by a patient waiting to be seen that needed help. this hospital needs to know who needs care

this place can be quite busy some days and hard to get an appointment. despite that this place can be very welcoming once you get used to it. the office staff are very hard workers. they are very patient with us on the phone  and during office visits. they are very helpful and are willing to most of our  questions. 
we love our nurses very much.  they are very sweet and show wonderful bedside manner. we appreciate that  especially when we are not feeling our best . all that is missing is the hot soup. just kidding!
 most of all we love our doctor ! we highly recommend dr libre! he puts the needs of the patients first. he listens to them. and he takes very good care of us.
i like that if he makes a referral that it is right in the network. and he can communicate with provider ! technology has changed so much.

my goto person here is miss lana simmons, who is a np.  she is exceptional, always listens, and, what's to help and do the right things for you.   she's very responsive and thorough.  i'm was fortunate to find her and to get the exceptional care.

this is the worst er ever took a loved one in the middle with a possible allergic reaction the people checking and taking vitals out front tell us oh it's just allergies huh are you a doctor???nope so we sit here waiting and waiting for a room mean while a baby is taken back before anyone because his parents can't get him to go to sleep for the night are we for real here maybe you should review your process of emergency patients before a baby not going down for the night tell me how that's an emergency a baby not going to sleep. after sitting for nearly two hours we left without medical treatment since the staff was to busy shopping on ebay and amazon to tend to patients horrible horrible stay away from this ed at all cost

arrived in er 5 minutes before my husband's heart stopped. as soon as they had the monitors on him, they moved him to a room with the correct equipment, so they had the defibrillator at the moment they needed it. the techs were right on top of it. dr. mejia, the cardiologist on staff was there immediately and they got him stabilized before checking him into icu, where he stayed for two days before being discharged to get some rest ahead of surgery for an internal defibrillator/pacemaker. the doctor was present and available multiple times a day during the er and surgery visits. the nurses were wonderfully attentive, and the department manager checked in at least once a day to be sure we were getting everything we needed, especially appreciated since it was a holiday weekend. hope i don't forget anyone, but special thanks to nurses chris, emily, tracy, summer, jana, and another great gentleman whose name i can't spell. they were all rock stars! it is really nice to have such a fine hospital close to home in lakeway.
fac_name: Baylor Scott and White Medical Center - Lakeway

please avoid this hospital at all costs if you're able to!

if i got sick, this is definitely where i would want to go. 
the team approach to care here is wonderful when it's working well (although at the beginning of the visit there can be done bumps in the road as everyone gets up to speed). there's a few glitches in the matrix for sure -- a volunteer knocked on my friend's closed door while she was sleeping, barged in without being invited, and very loudly asked if she wanted a magazine -- jolting her from her sleep. to say i was nonplussed seriously doesn't cover it! 
the rooms are generally nicely appointed (although there are some counterintuitive issues with the furniture -- it would be nice if the recliners actually reclined or the "couch" had a table on the side instead of the middle so loved ones spending long hours at a patient's bedside could be a more comfortable).
the facility itself has some lovely features (the bright area atrium and the garden cafe area is a welcome oasis, with stories-tall trees and lots of light.
they serve local water street coffee and victorian bakery products in the cafe, and have a large cafeteria with lots of options (today's burrito bowl was extremely ample and healthful).
parking is definitely a pickle (this afternoon there was seriously not a spot in the entire 4-story ramp) and there are never enough handicap spots at the garden entrance to meet the needs of their patients (many of whom double park in the turn-around area). 
i've always felt my loved ones were in the best care the area has to offer when i've visited them here.

review:
i am currently staying at the east tower fountain valley. i want to start off by thanking the nursing staff, and east tower staff, as they have been great. 

as far as my experience with my current situation, it has been less than ideal. 

i was transferred here last wednesday @ 6am from hoag. i didn't start my care until 30 hours later, thursday. i brought with me multiple mri copies from the previous 24 hours at hoag/ private mri facility. not only were these discs lost, (2 separate times), but i was told they were uploaded to my patient portal. unfortunately this wasn't true because my doctor told me they were never uploaded. the discs were eventually recovered. this caused the 30 hour delay, as confirmation of mri results were needed to help expedite my care.

this minor frustration was easily overlooked, until i received a biopsy on my l4 spine, on thursday afternoon, the following day. the next 4 days have included doctors telling me the results aren't ready, or the doctors not coming by at all. until today, monday, my doctor finally informed me the hospital lost my biopsy cultures. 

my doctor was very upset as well because the last 4 days i was told we are waiting for the biopsy results to start my specific antibiotic care plan. well now they lost the biopsy cultures and since the biopsy was on my spine my doctor doesn't feel comfortable ordering another. instead, he says we will just treat the problem with pathology results.

so my bone cultures are lost. i've been recovering in the east tower. my mri discs were lost. (since recovered) and i still don't have an update from my case manager, regarding my outpatient care plan. 

again, the nursing staff have been extremely kind. (5 star for the nurses in east tower)

but, i am beyond disappointed with this current experience. a week in the hospital, with minimal progress. 

i will update accordingly.
