review:
i had 2 procedures done via the cath lab within two months.  the first was outpatient and the second inpatient.  
the intake at fvh was fast and efficient. 
the nurses and my primary cardiologist, dr. donohue, were wonderful during the first procedure.  two of the nurses hugged me goodbye when i left.
fast forward two months and i'm back in the cath lab and the same nurses gave me a warm welcome, hugged me hello and remembered my name.  :-)  they were professional and made me feel at ease.
this procedure was held in an awesome o.r. with huge screens and beautiful equipment.  all of the staff preparing me were kind and reassured me that i was in good hands and not to worry.  dr. warrier performed my procedure and then i was taken to "the tower", a 3 story building behind the actual hospital, for recovery.  
my roommate was an elderly woman (who must've been deaf) as she had the tv at the loudest volume up to midnight.  i should have complained, but i didn't.
i had to lay flat for 6 hours beginning at 4:00pm. my lower back was on fire within two hours because of no support.  i finally requested some pain meds @ 8:30pm, the nurse called the doctor and was given the okay.  
the two nurses who took care of me in the tower were fine.  

one thing, though.  i asked the second nurse for directions for my neighbor who was picking me up.  she didn't know the address, the street or how to tell him to get to us.  i found that a bit odd.

all in all, it was good for what it was.

while i hope that my son won't have to be a repeat customer (or at least a frequent one), our experience at oishei was as positive as it could be given the circumstances.

review:

i was told "we are not going to let you"
i guess they told someone because some doctors i saw in icu volunteered the same reassurance.

thank you englewood for keeping your promise

that goes to all doctors, nurses,  pca, staff, care coordinators, transport, maintenance, etc.

my grandmother collapsed on christmas eve and we came here.  while we believed the collapse was due to a change in her blood pressure medicine, the doctor whom came in, said that she didn't think so, and that they should keep her overnight.  she was going to find a bed. fine.

some 3 hours later in the er, with repeated attempts for staff to locate the doctor to find out what's going on, she only makes herself reappear when i make it clear we are going to leave against doctor's orders - my grandmother is a stubborn sicilian.

the doctor comes in going on and on about how we shouldn't leave and she must be monitored.  so i asked her, what did the monitoring for the past 3 hours show her or the nurses.  cue the confusion when they realize, they'd never hooked her up to anything.  understand.... that's three hours then, that not one nurse, looked at the wall of monitors and noticed my grandmother had no vitals showing.   yeaaaa we're done.

kept an eye on my grandmother vitals myself all night, and took her to the doctor a day later.  guess what, it was her blood pressure medicine.

no expected minimal patient care here.

my first time here was  a year something ago at er ( work accident) and i had a routine colonoscopy on december 2019. the customer service was great; the profesional team, the same; facilities, clean and great! almost all the bill was charged to my health insurance. i give them 4 stars and a half. congrats and god bless you all

find a different doctor! i waited 3 months for an appointment with one of the doctors and one week before the appointment they canceled! when i tried to reschedule they wanted me to wait an additional 3 months! 6 whole months to see a doctor. that is absolutely insane!! they made me waste 3 months without the medical care i need because i was waiting to see this specific doctor. if i knew this would be the outcome i would have tried to find a different specialist. the receptionist could careless about this fact. and they were very "oh well" and totally thought this was acceptable! run!!! find a different doctor/specialist. not worth the headache.

englewood hospital's quality of care has gone so downhill that i don't think they can get any worse.my mother came here in august for a hernia repair and the doctor completely botched the surgery. she developed a condition called gastroparesis and her stomach stopped functioning. from that operation, she was  in and out of the hospital for 5 months. during that time, she became bedridden due to lack of movement. she was labeled a fall risk.. but somehow she "fell" while she was in the hospital. the nurse said she got out of bed looking for her glasses. how does that make sense? she had no upper or lower body strength. she contracted an infection while there, she was sent home with medication in her clothing, she was sent home dirty. we complained to patient relations and they couldnt give us a reasonable explanation so they made excuses as to why that happened. the last surgery she had was the icing on the cake.. she started to show signs of shock in recovery but the nurses kept saying she was fine. i knew something was wrong but they continued to tell me she's fine and they would be transferring her to a room. 20 minutes later she went into cardiac arrest and had to be resuscitated. she was without oxygen for at least 5 minutes and became vegetative in the icu. she had no brain function. it was torture. she stayed in icu for 2weeks before they put her on hospice to let her pass away. on the morning she died i found her unresponsive.. there were no nurses to be found. seemed pretty typical of englewood's staff. 
this place is a nightmare. if my experience there doesn't convince you, nothing  else will.

pain. they should give the fathers free parking while staying in the mother baby unit. would i give birth there again? no, i rather go to manhasset. was it a terrible experience ? no, but i know it deanna was great in helping me get an appointment scheduled quickly for my son!! the doctors & staff here are great with children! especially andrea in ot.

i think really the only thing i can gripe about here is the parking situation. parking lots can be a nightmare at times. plenty of spaces that are too small, a-holes that double/triple park, and overall cost when validated seems like a rip off. easily had spent a couple of hundred here in parking within the last year from the monthly check ups to the few days we needed to stay after delivery. other than that, great hospital and staff.

i've only experienced professional, courteous & friendly attention from all the staff when having procedures done at pmh. the entire visits from signing in to the actual tests have been professional & quickly done.

this was a really bad and scary experience for our family.  my family member was transferred to kindred on monday and we were told they would have 24 hr care, a dr. would see him daily and that he would have intensive therapy for rehabilitation after a massive stroke. first of all, the staff could not communicate with each other or our family because of a multicultural language barrier. we weren't told this was a training facility for rehab and home health. second, neither call button worked and had to go out and ask for assistance.  it took two requests for a respiratory therapist to come and help our family member who has a new trechionomy and was experiencing difficulty. this was not what we were anticipating in such a stressful situation.  needless to say, this is thursday and our family member has been transferred to a new facility. i want to thank kaiser permanente for hearing and helping us through this desperate and frightening situation.

truly, almost everyone provided the sharp experience and you could tell the employees who really enjoyed their job versus the employees that view their job as just a paycheck. perception is everything. i actually took down names of those i found were the epitome of the "sharp experience" and those who need a little sprinkle of the "sharp experience" back into their lives.

i will start with the good. check in process was good. the er staff were quick with triaging and with getting labs/xrays/ekgs done before you even go to the room to be seen by the dr. we waited a long time , more than a couple of hours to be seen-but it was ok because we had heard the code being called overhead so i knew someone needed all the help they could get. cambria was my moms er nurse. she was awesome and always kept my mom and i up to date. she was personable and i really appreciated it. another shout out needs to go out to luv who is another er rn that was helping with my mom's iv. i thank you for your hospitality. 

there are 2 individuals that rubbed me the wrong way in how they approached my mother-they are the ones to why this review is 4 stars versus 5. i really wanted to mark this review as 2 stars but i didn't want to downplay the services of the employees that were really awesome.  one was a healthcare partner by the name of april and the other is kandra or kendra from the pharmacy. everyone but these 2 employees were friendly, others came and introduced themselves to my mother and i. april came in, no introduction. she just stated matter of factly that she was there to do an ekg. no smile, nothing. not sure if she worked a long day, however, that's not an excuse to be the way she was. kandra or kendra (her badge was flipped and could not see her name)from pharmacy...she was just plain rude and condescending. she came to ask my mother what meds she was on...mind you my mom had a list and by the time kandra showed up-my mom had shown 3 other people including dr.shipley the list of the 4 meds she is on. kandra came off as being annoyed or irritated that my mom didn't know her meds by heart. my mom told kandra that she had given the list to dr. shipley and kandra retorted "the problem is the dr.'s don't always document it. so you don't know the names? the doses?" and just kept asking the same questions using the same tone while staring up at the ceiling. hmmm...ok. how is this our monkey? that's not our problem that they don't always document it. what a way to throw another staff member under the bus. she was short when talking to my mom and honestly my mom and i were happy to see this employee leave the room. for my mom to sit there and say "what's wrong with her?" speaks volumes. some people need empathy training and she is one of them. they need to put themselves in the patients' shoes. guaranteed if kandra/kendra had brought her mother into this er and was approached by a employee who acted just like her-she would be upset too. she acted like she hated her job. that was my perception. so cold in her responses, no smile, just not sympathetic and makes me question why she is in healthcare to begin with. she was rude and cold, plain and simple. maybe it was a long day? maybe she had seen a million patients that day? should that matter? no, it shouldn't.

back to the good. my mom was admitted onto 6 south. theresa (her pm rn), luz (pm aide) and joe p.(am rn)-i have nothing but the greatest things to say about these employees. hardworking, personable, helpful, always smiling, always keeping us updated, you guys have no idea how much i appreciated you and i know my mom appreciated you all just as much. i could tell all 3 of these employees love their job and love helping their patients. please make sure these 3 individuals get the recognition that they so deserve. sharp is lucky to have them on their team and we were really fortunate to have them taking care of my mom. 

also jay r. and christine f. in interventional radiology deserve recognition. they were phenomenal in their explanations. i loved how christine was practicing her mandarin with my mom. it's personal touches like this that makes me love sharp. 

she stayed one night. i finally convinced her to switch to sharp and tomorrow i'll be calling to find her a primary care physician with sharp rees stealy.

i hate this place with a passion!!! 
even with insurance, they continue to bill me for little stuff without even double checking if what they're doing is covered by my insurance. 

i went in to the er for chest pain and even with insurance, i've paid over $1000 already on little b.s. things they didn't even need to do. left the er with no meds or anything... just a "take it easy"

how can you truly rate a hospital? based off of skill of drs/surgeons/np/nurses/cnas? of quality of care? quality of food(which we all know who have been in a hospital for any extended time can be atrocious)? how about all of the above!

i was admitted on 11/7 for a major surgery. not simple by any means and i am glad and blessed that this was the hospital i went to. aortic valve replacement which entails open heart surgery is scary enough to hear, but the team here at sharp memorial along with my surgeon dr. adamson put my fears to rest. from the initial consultation with him and going over what was to occur i felt at ease along with my girlfriend. even making jokes with me to relax me and calm my nerves just showed the bedside manner was well above par.

the complex is large and if you have multiple appointments in different buildings as i did. just ask the nurse assisting you to request a shuttle and they will get you to were you need to go. instead of moving your car over and over and dealing with the parking.

depending on what you're in for will dictate what floor/building you will be placed in. post op recovery icu is 2nd floor of main building and god bless if that's what you're in for.

nursing staff along with the np(nurse practitioner, don't call them a dr even if they're right there) have some of the most gentle care i've experienced from any hospital. i've bee. to other sharps and i can wholeheartedly say this hospital takes the prize. from providing you with as much information as possible to assist you in your recovery to ensuring you help is merely a call away by providing you with their direct number(they're given a cell phone at work so they can be reached by you or the nurses station if needed urgently) these ladies and gentleman embody care. my hats off to floor 6 (cardiac recover) for all the outstanding service and care they provided me. i honestly don't think i would have been recovering as well as i am without their support and care.

food is still none the less hospital food but i was able to speak with the chef in charge and here their plans for the coming year. adopting a comprehensive plan to ensure that the food quality and nutritional value are in keeping with the care provided at the hospital. a one of a kind program that already has made staples in improving the quality of the food and nutritional value(small steps so far such as switching from iceberg lettuce to green leaf lettuce and such). my hats off to them for improving this overlooked aspect in hospitals. the ordering system is fantastic how they take your meal order ahead of time to not interfere with your recovery and to ensure that you designated meal with restrictions if any get to you on time. i lived how each .real came with a nutritional overview letting you k ow nutrients, calories, etc in your meal. loved that!

radiology/radiologist as i had to deal with frequently were friendly and helpful. whether they had to assist me in my room or take me down to get mris(be aware, its always the coldest part of the building because they do have to keep those machines cool or they can burnout so ask for bra blanket if you need it). the transport team who assisted you getting from location to location or helping you leave in the end were always kind, helpful and made sure you knew you were always welcomed back.... hopefully not soon though.

all in all if i could rate this hospital a 11 or higher i would! excellent is the only word i can come up with to describe the care provided by the staff at sharp memorial. my hats off to all the staff that help in the recovery of the many patients who walk through their doors and the supporting staff behind the scenes.

cannot say enough nice things about this hospital!! youngest daughter ended up visiting the er when she became very ill. for the severs hours before i was able yo get to her she said everyone was very nice, caring and warm. when i gig to the er i saw it firsthand from the nurses to the doctor to the technicians. she was admitted to outpatient observation and received excellent card and attention. even during shift changes it was not chaotic as had been my experience at other hospitals. also like the concept of this unit. you're not technically admitted to the hospital so the rates are s big lower. when dud was discharged the process was smooth and efficient...no waiting an hour for a transport to the pick up area! also like they treat family members gently and provide in and out privileges in the parking as well as discounts in the cafeteria.

i'm not sure if it's because i'm a black woman or if sharps is just like this in general but every single time i've went here they've dismissed my claim, told me it's not that serious, and treated me like i was lying. last week i went in for asthma, the nurse told me i seem fine..... the following day i had an asthma attack and ucsd la jolla treated me. i am now on the road to recovery. on numerous occasions this hospital has said i was fine when i wasn't, as if i just like to come to the hospital for fun. like it's a nice little vacation for me or something. don't go here if your a black woman, they automatically assume your trying to just get meds and play games.
ucsd is awesome!
professional, kind, understanding. the best experience in an er ever! was in and out in just over an hour, including xrays. everyone spoke english and were easy to understand!

last week my husband spiked a fever of 105.  i called 911 and we were taken to sharp hospital.  he was treated in the er by fantastic caring people.  then he was sent to the icu.  i can not say enough about the staff in the icu. wonderful people. monica - you were awesome. tom - you made this crisis seem bearable. thank you for your kindness. becky,  you are wonderful and made this horrible time not so bad. he was then moved to the 7th floor where we met kevin ,hannah and last but not least the magnificent laura. the worst time in my life left us with hope knowing that people like that are there when you are in need. i am sure i have missed a few names because there were so many kind folks we encountered.

i would like to highly recommend sharp hospital to everyone. two nurses especially made our hospital stay amazingly comforting and healthy. tim and jasmine are rns on the seventh floor and they deserve a gold medal. not only are their clinical skills top notch, they both had the most compassionate heard and conversations that i have ever seen. our whole experience was salubrious.

we are living a nightmare at sharp memorial. my son was admitted at 10:30pm with appendicitis requiring surgery. we were told by the er doctor that he would be operated on in the early morning. we expressed concern that his appendix might burst in that long a period and he offered to see what he could do. after paying for the er and being admitted, the staff told us my son would not be operated on for 14 more hours. if we had any other option at this point we would use it. this is the most negligent, callous care imaginable. don't entrust your loved ones to this place. they will ignore them to death.

hospital clean . but the nurses on the 4th floor are lazy. yael & jesse . let me sit in a hospital bed all night not checking on me once while i was having panic attacks. i had to go to there desk to even communicate with them. when i explained how i was feeling and told them i was nauseous they ignored me and got on their computers. then i just walk back to my room because clearly they're no help what so ever. and you can here them giggling about it. come on this is a hospital you guys are supposed to help. i sat up all night waiting for a doctor that never came from 12 midnight till 530 am the time it is right now . these guys definitely need more training and more care for patients. don't just try and skim through your shift. if someone isn't comfortable do something about. terrible!

nurses, doctors were extremely professional and helpful. i'm someone that suffers from a few chronic ailments and they've always been there to help me. only issue i had is with two of the entry level staff members in the er department that were not well trained and most likely new. due to myself having focal seizures and other issues in the past i've been required to have a medical alert dog with me at all times. the rules are that you are not to separate this dog from the handler (myself) and this dog is also protected by federal law for access. in addition, this dog can hold its bladder/etc for over 15 hours if necessary. so a clerk telling me "we can't take your dog out for you" is a bit disrespectful and ignorant. so everything else rates a+ i'd start with educating your plebotomists and medical assistants for check in in regards to the laws in regards to service dogs. i understand it cost more money to train a service dog then to onboard a staff member at your hospital but we're not trying to compare anything here now are we.

we live in las vegas but it was necessary for us to have a surgical procedure performed in san diego at sharp memorial. from the time we walked in the door, our experience exceeded all expectations.  the staff was helpful, friendly, and professional.  the hospital was beautiful with a clean, uplifting, inviting atmosphere.  everyone from the cafe employee to the rn was so kind and very professional.  we especially appreciate chris, michelle, carol, bethel, albert, and brandon (rns, recovery, transport), and of course, our anesthesiologist and dr. dente.  the care we received was excellent.  everything was according to schedule, and throughout the whole experience, the staff took great care of us; extremely attentive, positive, reassuring, available, and happy to assist.  everyone seemed very happy to work there; no one seemed stressed, overwhelmed, or grumpy (we know hospitals can be very  high-stress environments with heavy workloads).  the procedure went quickly, smoothly, and was successful.  we are grateful for the excellent care we received at sharp memorial, and we will never forget your kindness.

when we were getting ready to have our second child we learned that the hospital we delivered our first at was not in our insurance network. i was anxious and upset since i already knew what to expect at mckay-dee. when i read the reviews online about ogden regional i was even more upset. i read some negative things about the labor and delivery unit but decided to keep a positive outlook and go tour the facility. the nurses at the front desk were incredibly friendly and gave us a wonderful tour. i had a lot of questions and they took the time to answer all of them. i left feeling a bit more positive and less anxious. eventually, i had to be induced here and i cannot say enough good things about the labor and delivery unit here. when i showed up for my time the nurse (ashley) took me to my room and got me situated. she was awesome and was with me through my delivery. 

i do want to mention that mckay-dee is a beautiful hospital and a bit more updated with larger rooms but my experience at ogden regional was far superior. my room might have been smaller but all of the nurses, doctors and staff i encountered were kind and professional. my room was clean at all times and everyone was constantly checking on me and baby. i had an awful experience with my epidural at the other hospital so that was my main concern here. ashley assured me that the guy administering the epidural that day was fantastic and everything would be ok. she was right i couldn't believe how smoothly everything went. the entire staff treated me like i was important and not another number to them and that really made a difference for me. i feel very vulnerable during the recovery time and to be treated with care and respect is huge. i actually teared up multiple times because i was so happy to have such a better experience here and vowed to leave a positive review. i'm a bit late leaving that review but i remembered! if given the choice now i'd select ogden regional to deliver at!

i arrived at ogden regional hospital with kidney stones and in septic shock. the care i received was immediate and efficient. not only did they save my life but the kindness and attention to details made my stay there very pleasant. everyone on the staff, the doctors, nurses, pt, ot, cleaning personnel etc were all so courteous and helpful. i felt well cared for in every way. thank you ogden regional employee's for your 5 star service!

the staff here is great! my grandma was here for a brain injury and everyone that checked in on her was phenomenal. emory's neurologists are simply the best.

also, the facilities are beautiful, super clean, and there was a small room attached to my grandma's suite for visitors. just fantastic.

the negatives? my grandma said the food was super nasty which is part of the reason she lost weight fast while she was in there. also, their parking rates are rather expensive.

a couple of years ago the nyu langone er, cobble hill (also fabulous) sent me to nyu langone, brooklyn by ambulance for pneumonia.  i was hospitalized for seven days.  when i was dismissed i felt like i was leaving a large community of old friends. 

the cobble hill er gave me a choice of nyu langone brooklyn or manhattan, where my grandson was born.  i knew nothing about the brooklyn hospital except the fact that it would be an easier subway trip from my son's office in lower manhattan & closer to their home in brooklyn. and i certainly wanted visitors.

the hospital, formerly lutheran, is a large older hospital with shared rooms.  but that wasn't a problem.  in fact it made me happy to nurture my last roommate through some of her health care fears.

the staff was awesome!! i can't say enough good things about the entirety, from the doctors all the way to the attendants who took me to radiology.

nyu langone is a teaching hospital.  so i had 3 specialty teams treating me and trying to discover the root cause of my months long bout with pneumonia.  from the specialists, to their residents, to their interns to their med students, i received excellent care.  the specialty teams coordinated, getting together to discuss my case.

they performed an enormous amount of testing in addition to treatments.  when the specialty teams would visit, they would discuss their findings and answer all my questions.  i really felt i was in excellent hands.

but the good and friendly care also came from the nurses, nursing technicians, food service workers, lab technicians, breathing specialists, swallow specialists, orderlies and housekeeping staff.  have i forgotten anyone. many would hang out in my room.  it doesn't have to be miserable being in the hospital, even if you're really sick.  it can be fun.

it was fun pretending my hospital bed was traveling the bqe as we rushed down the halls to radiology.  (i have to admit it was my idea.) it was fun when the pulmonary specialist took a picture of my iphone because i had over 60,000 unread emails.  it was fun making someone smile who seemed to not have smiled in a long time.  

the meals were very good for hospital fare, although i didn't enjoy having to be on a heart healthy diet.  each morning food services would come around for the daily menu choices.  they were very good about bringing extra coffee and goodies.  i didn't starve as i've felt in other hospitals.

and they were attentive.  i've been in a hampton roads hospital in terrible pain in the middle of the night while the nursing staff ignored my continual buzzing for help.  not so at nyu langone, brooklyn.

even though i was close to the nursing desk i could sleep.  as much as they will let you sleep in a hospital..... :)

when i was dismissed many staff came to give me a goodbye hug.  it felt like leaving a group of friends.

the hospital scheduled the follow up appointments with nyu doctors.  they checked on me afterwards.  i was also given a followup nurse number that i could call.

the nyu langone app is fabulous.  i can still see all the results of my testing, both at the hospital and the cobble hill er.  the catscan reports are extremely detailed.  i wish the hampton roads hospitals provided radiology readings with such detail.

i would not hesitate to go back to nyu langone, brooklyn.  my care was wonderful.

emergency medical treatment & labor act (emtala)

in 1986, congress enacted the emergency medical treatment & labor act (emtala) to ensure public access to emergency services regardless of ability to pay. section 1867 of the social security act imposes specific obligations on medicare-participating hospitals that offer emergency services to provide a medical screening examination (mse) when a request is made for examination or treatment for an emergency medical condition (emc), including active labor, regardless of an individual's ability to pay. hospitals are then required to provide stabilizing treatment for patients with emcs. if a hospital is unable to stabilize a patient within its capability, or if the patient requests, an appropriate transfer should be implemented.

review:
choose your hospital wisely:

i went to holy cross for a knee replacement.  the doctor was great and replacement doing good. however, when i came home i was on pain meds with tylenol.  doctors told me i most likely acquired a gram negative ecoli infection from the urinary catheter. the infection then grew into my blood and i became sepsis. after a week in another hospital and sent home with a mid line iv for antibiotics. i recovered after three weeks. i called holy cross hospital infectious department to let them know.  well i received no concern, no caring, and an excuse that i only had the catheter for one day. they also said, in order to pick up this infection in the hospital i would have had to have the catheter two days.  so not a very educated answer.  infections are acquired through direct contact and time exposure plays no role. 

copied from the internet:

causes
bacteria are normally found throughout the body including on the skin and in the intestines. when kept in balance, bacteria can help the body work normally. however, an imbalance of the bacteria or passing of bacteria to areas where there are no bacteria, can lead to an infection. an infection will develop if large amounts of bacteria are present, the bacteria are aggressive, or the immune system is weakened.

common ways for bacteria to pass to vulnerable parts of the body include:

use of medical devices that pass into the body, such as iv or urinary catheters
open wounds
contact with someone who has or has been exposed to gram-negative bacteria
risk factors
hospitalization is the most common risk factor for gram-negative bacterial infections. the longer the stay in the hospital, the higher the risk of infection.

other factors that increase the risk of a bacterial infection include:

recent surgery
use of urinary catheter
war wounds
dialysis for kidney disease , which includes regular use of iv lines or catheters
mechanical ventilator use
weakened immune system

with my experience it doesn't matter how good the doctor is.  if the hospital is a sick hospital, even the most mild surgery could cause sickness or even death. do your research.

by far without a doubt one of the worst emergency room situations i've even been in.  there with my partner who was in excruciating abdominal pain...  hour and half and still sat in a chair.  there were people sleeping on the floor!!!  no help whatsoever!!!  people were in agony!  completely disgusted and will never again use holy cross!  i would rate it a zero if i could!  stay away from this place if you have an emergency!!!

we ended up at holy cross hospital after midnight on a saturday after my husband fell and cut his head. (due to being lightheaded because he's on blood thinner)  we were very apprehensive going to an unknown hospital on a saturday night - we're from pa and in our 60's.  the service we received was superb, from the security guy to the nurse to the pa to the doc to the paramedic. the pa sutured a bad gash expertly, and the hospital was very thorough in its treatment, including an ekg and a cat scan.  the continuity of conscientious, quality, compassionate service was unexpected and very much appreciated.

i have nothing but praise for the professional staff. doctors, nurses, techs, etc.  the clerical and ancillary staff needs improvement. calling patients by wrong name, not explaining why things are or aren't being done, etc.

went to holy cross for a standard outpatient procedure. from the front desk to post-op everyone was very nice and helpful. it was very busy and packed but i did not wait long and i was frequently asked if i needed anything. the nurses are incredibly friendly and the doctors made sure to answer all my questions. had a great experience and was very comfortable.

horrible experience in emergency room.  nurses have a lack of bedside manner. felt like a number rather than a human being. was there for hours and not seen by a doctor. finally left to go to other hospital.

the absolute worst experience i've ever gone through. took my mother to the er  after her doctor said it would be easier and faster to get blood work, ct scan, mri and urine work done. my mom was in severe pain, so much she could barely walk. she had vertigo, tinnitus and was shaking. she had "flu" symptoms earlier that week but that was not the point of the visit, her pain and unbalance was. we waited around an hour to get a room, then we had to wait even more for a nurse to come and take a urine sample. we got into the room at almost 3, she was finally given tylenol at 4:30 for her severe pain. we didn't see the doctor until 5:30, after waiting hours. the doctor said my mom was okay to go home, without any blood work or exams. someone who is crying in bed, unable to handle the pain is okay to go home??? the doctor lacked any sort of humanity or empathy. i obviously felt insulted that nothing was done to help my mom apart from 1000mg of tylenol (which can be bought at any store) so i asked why she was in so much pain, why she was so dizzy she couldn't walk alone and why they didn't do any blood work. the doctor looked me in the face and said she didn't need it, that she needed to go home and rest. we were just another bed that needed to be empty for the next number to come in. i had to hunt down a nurse to get discharged, she said they were going to give mom a dose of vertigo medicine before she left. they weren't even going to send her medicine to go home. i was told that ct scans and mri were not done there, and that my mom would have to have an actual reason to them. urine culture was not sent to lab to find out if there was an infection, because that would take 48 hours and that wasn't needed. belittled and abused are not enough to describe this disgusting experience. all they're good for is over charging people for terrible service. if you go to a hospital you expect to be getting the best service possible, but instead here you leave just as bad as you came in and mentally drained. go anywhere else. the er doctors are inhuman.

nuvance health network formerly known as wchn / danbury hospital / new milford hospital /praxair center/ in my opinion has major compliance and regulatory concerns to address. the billing department and staff lies to you as the patient & consumer. i was treated at the praxair center last year in 2019 and received 2 statements in excess of $20,000 for an iron iv transfusion the praxair center sent the claim through my med insurance provider rightfully so however as a patient i was never once informed that 1 treatment of iron therapy would equate to $10,000 each time for a total of 2 per the dr. when i called my insurance to review this matter i asked them if anyone called to review what my co-payment was going to be or if the office submitted a treatment plan with codes that could be reviewed of coverage. my insurance company said no - no body called to review your benefits or obtain a precertification for your treatment. the praxair center denied and said they did but what they failed to realize is that my insurance company tapes every incoming or outbound call and they were not in fact called. when i went w my concerns to the nuvance billing department they gave me a very big run around and made me feel it's my error because i have low iron. i have since filed an appeal with my insurance provider and will be pursuing this at a vigorous rate. it is completely unacceptable and alarming that a medical network / facility does not value patients vs a way for them to make money. i would recommend to fact check everything the doctor and group or hospital is doing  and to be diligent regarding their billing practices.  this network earns 0 stars but to inform patients i have to place 1. good luck

review: here's the good: the main pharmacy in the med center is awesome. the techs & pharmacists i've encountered are smart, efficient, and thank god have a great sense of humor. pretty much the same with northside. the lab: i've had great techs and really fast, efficient service. this is the organizational best here. my husband has not fared as well. he's allergic to plastic tape and every time that's what's been used to adhere his bandage. he's an adult, can walk, talk, see. obviously he can't think because he never  says anything!! oh well! the not good: follow up for problems, assessment of problems, primary care at the lowest possible level for the masses. it does not matter if the lowest possible action or treatment is not effective. it does not matter if you are willing to pay cash for legacy medicine that has proven to be effective and with which you've been stable for over 50 years. it does not matter if an inhaler for asthma is not effective despite correct use. there will not be any evaluation or consideration of alternative evaluations or intervention. you will not be evaluated for the possibility of eosinophilic generated asthma or asthma triggered by leukotrienes. apparently in the land of kp, albuterol is the only existing rescue inhaler in the universe. does not matter if it doesn't work. use the steroid inhaler & if the rescue doesn't work, well if you die, it's cheaper. family member with adult onset t2 diabetes? well if your glucose has been stable at 90-100 and your a1c at 5, they'll stop your effective meds, watch your glucose climb to 400+ then put you on 80-100 units of nph insulin and continue to enable out of control t2dm. no return to effective treatment-that's not how we do it now. my colleague is a nationally recognized advanced practice cde rn. she is appalled by the lack of current accepted practice management. so in these areas, kp fails. we will return to ucla & cedars-sinai during next open enrollment. my family member's life depends on it. but for well-person routine care & immunizations kp is great & convenient. perhaps a more forward-thinking pcp would also be better.

from sign in to the finish, we couldn't have been treated any better, it was the best.
special thanks to nurse janice and angela.
also thanks to pa and doctor....
everyone showed so much care..

he is a decent person who takes time to listen to what you have to say, but then he dismisses any concerns. i've been his patient for several years and i keep riding it out with him but i'm just not satisfied with his care or lack of it. i had pain and stiffness in my right foot. i gave him all my symptoms. i went to remove my shoe to show the exact area and dr. lamie said, "i don't need to see your foot, it's gout." he prescribed pills for gout and i finished the prescription but still no change and the pain was worse. the doc refilled the same script and after taking that extra dosage. no change. i asked him to refer me to a foot specialist. that doctor took an x-ray and said it was osteo arthritis and eventually i would need surgery. that doctor laughed when i told him my gout diagnosis from lamie saying, "it's definitely not gout." that just one story. i don't have room to type other issues.

i am not sure how to put this into words representative of the lasting emotional trauma they caused me, my girlfriend, and anyone else who received the same treatment; but i will do my best in articulating a proper review for this soulless place. 

stormont vail is yet another culprit in the ongoing "cesarean section epidemic" attempting to push them on anyone they can, regardless of a clean bill of health each time they run tests. if your tests do not meet the average with pinpoint accuracy, they will shame you into receiving a c-section.  

i am sad to say that shaming is the perfect descriptor for what they do to someone who questions why they are demanding you get a c-section. if the shaming does not work, well then they turn to directly strong arming you. they will berate you, and put you in such an uncomfortable position that you will suffer emotional distress. some of the doctors will even overstep their bounds and directly threaten you if you bring facts contrary to their beliefs. do not let them fool you.

i say my son suffered for a week, and the key point here is that was when his natural birth was meant to be, a week after the scheduled c-section. pure coincidence he left the nicu on his scheduled natural birth date? i'll leave that to the scientists who know better than shyster doctors. i can only present the data i have at hand. 

prospective families, do not under any circumstance let them sway you. unless they say specifically that your case is imminently life threatening (they may do that anyways, hence why i say overstepping their bounds), do not give in to the duress.  

in closing: the nursing staff is overworked and undervalued. their ability to be cordial is limited by this. nonetheless most of them were absolutely terrible at their jobs, and had atrocious bedside manner; often they would forget about you and become irate at even the slightest reminder. communication between the multiple wards is also nearly nonexistent, leaving you to run middleman for them.

during my stay here i got to eat many yummy foods. there was a good variety no matter how i was feeling. internet connection was also good enough i could watch shows to stay up. the nurses, cleaning individuals, aides, and techs were all very welcoming and kind. they were very helpful when i needed it and where very patient with me. 

overall i would definately recommend the epilepsy monitoring unit here for those looking  for more information or those needing it.

i went for inpatient electric shock therapy so i had to stay on the behavior award... called ahead of time to see if i could bring a blanket and book, was told that would be fine, nothing about it having to be a soft bound book and then they wouldn't let me take my blanket... i had a horrible first night, i was sat in a room by a tech who was not very nice to anyone, and as fake as could be. i don't remember her name but she has a piercing on her cheek. she said she'd give me a tour of the floor but instead left me in that room for 35 minutes then came and got me and just took me to my room. it was very cold in there and all i had was the regular top blanket and a sheet and since they have to do bed checks every 15 minutes when someone come in at ask for a blanket and they would always say that they would come back with one i didn't get one until the next day!i felt like in a place where i needed comfort, there wasn't anywhere to look for it... after i have been crying all morning finally a nurse had approached me, penny. and she said that i could have my blanket if they washed it which was fine with me i didn't care so i had my husband bring it at visiting hours. and i asked if they could put it with the next load of laundry but instead i didn't get it till 530am the next day! i thought this whole process could have been a lot easier on me if things were told up front to me over the phone. there's some really great workers there though i have to say and some really nice people that do work there! i did get a voice my complaints to the guy running the floor. it seems like you have to figure out by yourself though how to get your hygiene products and your clothes because nobody will tell you, you have to ask. but i guess that is such as life with every place you go there's some good employees and some bad!

great place to work. mountainview has great benefits as well as competitive pay. i've been at mv for 4 years now and look forward to many more.

i arrived at mclaren hospital in an ambulance from war memorial hospital and admitted to a double room in the cardiac unit.  i was scared, talking a mile a minute, while gasping for breath.  the hospitalists, the nurses and nurse practitioners, the ultrasound tech, the cardiologists - all were professional, caring, willing to listen.  one fellow who delivered food, made me laugh and relax.  the hospital also had color-coded uniforms so that you could tell whether it was a phlebotomist or a nursing assistant or a medical doctor coming in to your room. even my roommates (4, over the course of 7 nights) were interesting and non-intrusive.  i was very pleasantly surprised that this relatively small community hospital gave me such good care.

the nurses were very nice and gave some wonderful tlc but the hospital as a whole is terrible. just entering the hospital is a death trap (construction everywhere). when released, i was told to go to admissions on the first floor. another nightmare with a woman who has definitely been doing her job far too long. rude and dismissive. barked orders at me, never looked up from her computer. of course there aren't many options in the area but if you can avoid this house of horrors, do so.

mclaren's billing:

my husband had a stroke december 2019. he was rushed to mclaren northern michigan hospital in petoskey. frankly, i felt my head was in a fog most of the time and i was just so glad he came out of it alive. he had rehab done locally in january and had to have a follow-up with the neurologist february 3rd. doctor said that they cannot find a reason for my husband having a stroke and he needed to have a loop recorder placed inside his chest to see if he has a-fib.  february 7th he has that put in.  today (february 26) i am sitting at my desk paying $1,300 in co-pays for the things he had done - i admit it is a bit steep for us but praising god my husband is still alive. however, as i was paying by phone with mclaren, they let me know that there was a bill for $11,000.00 coming down the pike that wasn't covered by bcbs. it was the loop recorder. they called and asked for a pre-authorization for the loop to be placed in and was told by bcbs that they didn't one - no mention that it wasn't a covered benefit; the doctor's office didn't ask and bcbs didn't offer them the information. how does two retired people on social security suppose to pay for their mistake because each one blames the other for not getting the information and we are stuck with the bill? 

paying on these bills are equally as hard because all you get from mclaren's is the dollar amount - you really have no idea what you are paying on (it isn't itemized). also, when paying online through your bank, you have to input each bill into your system as each bill has its own unique account number. so you may have a dozen bills (like we have) and each one has its own account number - very time-consuming having to pay online.

i would like to describe my dissatisfaction with the services at the entrance tonight. i am extremely upset at the way i was treated by the security that expressed his name: brian diaz.

review:
check the demographics of this place before you seek treatment. like many va hospitals, this one is broken. 

i received a phone call from a dr. stephanie curry at dorn. i've never been seen by this doctor in my life. this lady sounded aggressive, and was quick to anger when i asked her a question. i thought i had just got a call from one of the homies. sounds familiar? needless to say, i wrote the hospital director, dr. omura about her behavior. i would not recommend dr curry. she did not treat me like a customer. i don't think the type of attitude she displayed would be tolerated in private practice. people don't want to spend their money to be treated rudely. 

the va does not profit from their patients like a private hospital, but i can assure you that the va expects a return on investment (roi). veterans do carry "vote dollars." i suggest veterans utilize the choice program and see just how well you are treated at a private facility. as well as the effectiveness of your medical care. 

just ask yourself this one question about the va. "why does the housekeeping officer make more money than a doctor at the va? still want to go there for treatment? oh, and the housekeeping officer only needs a high school diploma. shocking!

this is why trump gave the va his immediate attention once elected. he initiated the "mission act of 2018." that means that veterans now have the extended choice program and can get their care with a private doctor within the va pay network. 

veterans, if you do chose this hospital, always please be sure to take a family member with you; it keeps staff honest. and don't lower your standards just because the standards are low at this hospital.

review:
my google review of albemarle hospital was shadowbanned, ie., censored, so here i go on yelp to alert the public. these events are old, but they give insight to albemarle hospital's problems which go back to old style politics within the physicians themselves and the hospital board.
in 6 years before i arrived, albemarle had cycled through 5 orthopedic surgeons and while i was there at least 6 more came and left.  i was suspended three times as a physician at albemarle hosp. first for chewing out a  registration worker who had refused to register a patient in the waiting room who was in tears. this  registration worker was female, black and addressed her grievance with the title of "minister." with god on her side, she could do no wrong. the 2nd suspension was because i did not come in to see an "emergency" patient, even though i had gone on courtesy staff a few months earlier! when i returned 4 days later from my trip, this patient was sitting in the wheelchair in the parking lot smoking. some emergency. nothing had been done for his dislocated total hip by my competitor dr watson, except to report me! my third suspension was a summary suspension for my complaining to kathy fairfax, surgical head rn, about how the administrator sharon tanner was running the hospital financially into the ground. (reportedly $40 million in the green when she started, $100 million in the red when she was escorted out under police guard.) i was labeled a "disruptive physician" despite three negative evaluations by a harassing nc medical board. nevertheless, i was exiled for 3 months to hattiesburg ms pine grove "treatment center" for "anger management" where i was suddenly diagnosed and treated as a drug addict/alcoholic! there had never been any issue of either drugs or alcohol in my entire life! no "anger management" was offered. quite hypocritically, edward eadie, md chief of surgery, and ralph battles md, chief of staff,  who were both signing my suspensions, had histories of having physically assaulted nurses! when i returned from my 3 months exile, it was learned that my "replacement," dr kona, was the alcoholic.  kathy fairfax then left shortly thereafter for florida.  then i discovered neurosurgeon  dr sonnino had refused to come in to see a post-op spine case with an epidural abscess. his patient ultimately died after being shipped to virginia. this was all  kept quiet and he was suddenly "rescued" with creation of the position of "chief medical officer and vice president of quality" with a  $275,000 salary by tanner now that he was no longer insurable for such an egregious patient abandonment. but my hip patient was supposed "to have set the precedent for future acts like this" according to eadie. i guess not! these are the games that go on in hospitals. nothing has changed.   eadie, battles may you burn in hell for what you did to me!  meanwhile, the nc medical board is not protecting the public either. it is public relations management and they served me up as a poster child to  launch their new crusade against the so called "disruptive physician."  and you wonder why i was so angry?
don't take my word for it. check out my story. you wouldn't believe it.  karl w hubbard md

management/professionalism:

felt like there was very little physician or rn oversight or presence in the er. no sense of leadership presence. this erodes patient/family confidence in staff ability to provide appropriate care, competently and timely.  this is heightened by fact that a lot of staff only a few years out of school.  

staff were observed discussing personal issues, staff-staff issues/gossip, other patients, vacation plans, "crazy people", etc.  discussing patients in areas where others (everyone) could hear.

staff need coaching: e.g., christopher d., rn - did not treat patients with respect and dignity (despite patients being challenging); i observed his demeanor with one challenging patient in particular; it is never ok for any staff member to be rude, argumentative, dismissive, and poke fun at a patient - or anyone for that matter; terrible. this rn threatened to withhold meds "next time i won't give it to you." laughing, rn said, "it's almost entertaining...you have to laugh at it" referring to the patient.  another rn had to take over caring for the patient.

lack of attention to patients - hours would go by w/out staff attending to a patient.  what is rounding protocol?

noisy - staff loud and boisterous in late evening and early morning hours - disruptive and not at all conducive to healing 

upon arrival to er check in - rn kelly wore mask but later had it pulled down below chin.  rn in nearby room celebrated he had just seen his "last patient" before his shift ends, but noted unfortunately he had to fill out some sort of paperwork; he held up a folder with a pink sheet of paper

masks - lackadaisical approach by many staff with respect to wearing flu mask - either pulled fully off face or wore half on - below nose.

musical chairs - patients left in chairs (not enough beds); moved several times within the same ancillary/accessory side area: why?

cramped spaces - er berths only as wide as a bed, with flimsy partitions that would not always stay in position.  very little (no) privacy.

providers (resident? and student) - using patient spouse for medical (clinical) translation to get medical history, document symptoms.  staff knew little or no spanish.

while the hospital was extremely busy (flu season), there is never any excuse for staff to act in the ways described.  this behavior is unsafe, provides a poor patient experience, and undercuts the work of team overall.  i encountered many (named above) excellent, caring team members.

i hope this feedback improves care and environment at nyu winthrop.  i want this hospital to thrive in our community.  we have much need for healthcare access.
fac_name: Emergency Department at NYU Winthrop Hospital

review:
i have never written a hospital review before today. this saddens me that i am leaving this type of review for winthrop hospital. i have been to their e.r. on many occassions. unfortunately,i have very serious health issues,that warrant me going to a hospital.

my father had cancer several years ago and he was treated @ winthrop. he often spoke about how he enjoyed the care he got there. i felt no issues going there... based on what he told me of his experience. the majority of my experiences,i was satisfied. (save for a few)

on march 3,2020 i went to their emergency room in the midst of a lupus flare. i was placed in fast track,the area w/the big blue chairs. it was busy and my nurse pedro couldn't/wasn't more attentive to me based on that. i literally had to call out for him. he was zipping by me constantly w/out asking if i were ok etc. did i need anything etc. when he did answer me,he was pleasant enough.

a pa by the name of kim(kyu-ree) approached me. examined me quickly,asked several questions and began speaking about pain medicine. she just fixated on that line of questioning. her tone : accusatory. she even told me" i was lucky to be able to get one of the meds they gave me."she said " we weren't even supposed to give it to you." she also told me that some system called i stop tells dr's not to give lupus patients medicine for pain."

there are so many levels where improvement could happen for this department. kim went back to her area,ate chocolates,sitting,laughing talking w/ colleagues. (which included dr. bernot)

dr. randye bernot treated me absolutely horribly. never asked me how i was feeling. rapid fire questions about why i came to this hospital,what pain meds did i take,why did i take them,how many do i have,and on and on. her tone :accusatory. this lady harassed me. she badgered me. over and over with pain medicine questions.

no one ever came back to discuss my blood results etc. no one ever came back to ask me how i felt etc. 

i wound up crying like a baby to the tech who did the doppler on my legs. he is the one who suggested i see patient relations after i asked him for a manager. i couldn't believe the lack of care ran through these people on this day.

i'll end it here for time constraints. i placed a complaint to patient relations. my heart is broken. people/patients seeking care,shouldn't be treated in this manner.

god bless you all.

review: absolutely horrible. in the middle of a procedure they had to change the course of action and couldn't move forward without a billing  change. due to an it glitch it wouldn't process and the patient was waiting in limbo on the table for over an hour. no one could fix it. horrible patient care

review: discharge and sends clinicals with incorrect information to nursing homes for patients' assessment for potential home residents.

i had two outpatient eye surgeries in 2014 and everything was fine.  i recently had a two-day in-patient knee replacement and i was seriously disappointed.   everything was fine with the surgery as before but the in-patient stay was horrific.   it was like staying in a stripped-down cheap motel 6.  the staffing was limited.  they encouraged you to have someone spend the night with you post surgery.  there were strangers roaming the hallways and patients were in single rooms.  it was scary.  the only persons i saw the first night were male attendants who helped me to the bathroom.  there is no in-house food service.  it is all brought in on trays like airplane service.  meals were microwaved and you are given flimsy plastic silverware that broke when you used it.  the day following surgery, no one came to check on me until 10 a.m.  the nurse?came in and i asked when breakfast was coming and she informed me that breakfast was over and there was no food.  eventually, a man came in in a white coat and pulled two small cereal boxes from his pocket and announced "breakfast is here!"  no bowl, milk or silverware.  they don't keep any juice, crackers, yogurt or jello for post-surgical patients who might come out of anesthesia with a queasy stomach.   there were no
amenities nor creature comforts like a carafe of ice water in your room, a towel or facecloth to wash up.   there was a bed, tray table and chair in the room and lousy tv service.  it was a cold, spare, soul less place.

the physical therapists were two older teens who helped me walk across the hall once and then showed me how to push a walmart bag back and forth while i sat in a chair.  i was never given a discharge meeting and was told ten minutes before i was picked up that an ambulance was coming to transfer me.  it was friday and they do not want to staff over the weekends so everyone was supposed to leave by noon.  i believe the kids might have been summer employees as it was summertime.

this is a doctor-owned facility and it is truly bare bones and they are pinching every last penny there.  the only good thing was the nurse who started my iv got it on the first try and it was painless.  kudos to her!  i would never go there again as an inpatient.  it was too barebones for me and scary at night if you were alone.  i think the out-patient surgery staff is good but the inpatient staff needs a lot of training and employees.

i started going to bsw because my insurance changed. i was trying to pick a doctor. i had to make a quick visit for a illness and i was paired with sarah yeakley demuth, pa. she is now my pcp. she has the best bedside manner. she takes the time to listen to any concerns and explains everything in detail. she searches for solutions to my problems with me. she is the best health care provider i have ever visited.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Emergency Medical Center - Cedar Park

review: came here for an er visit. they gave me fluids and i waited for about an hour before they said they couldn't serve me because the computers and thus equipment was down. i was transferred to an actual hospital for the duration of my care. i just received a bill for both hospitals despite the fact that it was their fault their equipment was down. a decent doctor would not have charged $400 for fluids when they knew i'd have to be transferred. safe to say i will not be recommending anyone to go here.
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Emergency Medical Center - Cedar Park

review: my mother came in for a couple of procedures and i must say the treatment she received from the staff was wonderful.  her doctors, nurses and other staff members were friendly and wonderful.  we even had the housekeeping staff ask us on two occasions if they could get us anything.  very good people.  the reason for the lower ratings is the physical environment of my mom's room.  a patient's room is used for recuperation and it's important that this living space provides a physically, as well as mentally positive experience.  the furnishings needed updating and their were certainly signs cleaning was needed.  the vent in the bathroom was filthy, as well as the air conditioner vent.  the ac unit looked like the find you would find in a cheap, older hotel.  it did not cool very well, even though it was reading 72 degrees.  the vent here was also filthy.  not what you want after having surgery.  the bedside table looked like it had come from someone's home after 20 years of use.  window corners also had a great deal of accumulated dust, dirt and who knows what else.  funds should definitely be provided to upgrade the patient rooms and basic cleanliness everywhere should be a top priority.  make the surroundings as welcoming as the staff.

i think all of these "amazing" reviews are bs and fake. i'm watch my husband slowly die because he needs a kidney and liver transplant. he had just under 2 inches of his liver removed in may and also his gall bladder because that organ doesn't "do much". then his kidneys failed after the surgery. he went from 185 pounds in may to now, 113. i'm transferring him out of there. in my experience with them, all methodist facilities have been a death trap. stay away from them. they don't care. at all.

unlike aurora doctors their er  are doctors are a subcontractor not theirs! lately the the er doctors do not like listening to you! had a dizzy spell where i could not stand up and the er doctor refused to call my heart doctor kreager! if they tell you they are going to admit you for observation watch out medicare does not pay for that! my heart doctor kreager is now at aurora hospital and i am now at aurora for heart problems! best suggestion get rid of er subcontractor doctor's, get your own doctors in the er!

my daughter was sick in 2014 and we received a bill from tx med clinic. we waited a few months to make sure all insurance had been filed then paid the remaining amount. tx med clinic filed three separate collections for paid and closed amounts to my credit and have continued to submit. i have had to dispute several times because they keep resubmitting. when i spoke with experian and transunion, they both told me tx med clinic was responsible but tx med clinic "claims" they are not the ones who are re-submitting. the entire process has been frustrating and completely avoidable if tx med clinic followed ethical business protocol. i do not recommend tx med clinic. go somewhere else and save yourself a huge hassle as well as your credit.

great affordable care can be found here this flu season. by checking in and filling out symptoms and other background info online prior to arriving, i was able to be seen immediately. the doctor made sure to give the proper attention to my concerns, told me when to come back and see her, and sent me on my way within 30 minutes. yes, i said within 30 minutes!

i shouldve gave an update since my last visit. the staff was way better this time. yes i was passed up by a few people but the clinic was fast this time and i felt they did their best to get me out of there. i hope it goes that fast next time.

worst clinic ever. falsely diagnosed me and made me pay them & get medication when i really needed to go to the hospital for surgery. there was nothing that could have helped me but surgery. the wait time said 15 to 20 mins. more like 40 to 50.

i went through a minor surgery and asked the billing department for a copy of my records and bills for reimbursement purposes and they sent me someone else's records (copies). i sent it back and asked them for it again, and they sent me a different patients records with all his information and medical conditions, notes, etc. i got tired of the wait and the errors, i went in person and the billing manager says 'its not new news but im sorry!!!!!' seriously????? if i could give you a no star i'd give you a bird instead. these are confidential information with social security numbers, addresses, phone numbers, exam results and so forth. its your main priority to maintain its confidentiality. dont tell us its not new news that someone is reading my medical information.

went there in the afternoon on december 26. you fill out a piece of paper with basic information and then sit down. after a while you get called to a desk to be checked in. then you wait. there were people coughing all around the waiting area. there's a sign saying that people coughing should wear a mask, and where to get one, but nobody was. many of these people were morbidly obese. after i'd been there perhaps an hour, i realized that only two people had been called into the treatment area in that time and there were quite a few people who were there before me, so it would probably be many hours before i would be seen. at that point, i decided to leave and not wait any longer. i hope to never go back.

perhaps it's less busy at other times, but since the waiting area is large and there are three desks for checking people in, and dmh has closed several other expresscare locations, i think it's probably often as busy as when i was there.

the doc i was seeing left the practice. he was great! when i went in for my follow-up the doctor was horrible! the people answering the phone are rude. i called in for a follow-up and she asked me why. i guess i was supposed to leave when my doc did! he could not pull up my file, so he took me to another computer where he still could not pull my file, so he went to another computer and left me with another patient's info on the screen. it was clear he had not read my file and didn't care too! i left without any new info, had to find someone new.

please be careful! i'm a healthy woman who went through a very scary illness this past year. it took me months to realize how sick i was and took even longer to get in with the appropriate doctors. capitol gastro was my first gi in austin. after unfortunately spending christmas in the er, i finally received a clinical diagnostic via ct scan. consulting gi specialists and surgeons provided a list of follow up steps for my condition with a recommended list of expedited testing and vascular surgery referral. i called capitol gastro immediately to let them know so testing could be expedited. they did nothing. with er notes, recommendation letters from other gi specialists and the ct images on a disc, they did nothing. i fought with the office, drove there in person to plead with the staff/medical assistants and, after 3 weeks, finally got a clinician on the phone. their response is that they would not order me a ct scan because it wasn't clinically indicated. i was distraught, disheartened and terrible upset. i had a ct scan that was abnormal and, for whatever reason, that message and all my records were never actually reviewed by a provider. i found another gi in austin who is wonderful and she had every test/surgery referral completed within one week. she was dumbfounded as to how capitol gastro could have dropped the ball so egregiously. i had been sick for over 6 months and suffered for weeks unnecessarily because of their negligence. there are more responsible gis in the austin community!

in the past week i have found myself in this emergency room 3 times. this place during basic admission seems to have no idea how to get the process moving along. as a result, every trip is a minimum of a 2 hour wait. on top of that, once you get to the back to be seen, they're just trying to get rid of you asap....after making you wait an hour after each person pokes their head in the room. i have a 92 year old grandma that couldn't be seen in over 5 hours while her muscle spasms were causing shortness of breath. if you have to go to an emergency source for healthcare i strongly recommend that you find one of the many local outside sources instead of this sad excuse for a hospital or you may not even live to regret coming here.

***it is not the service or care of hospital but the northwestern medicine"s financial assistance office***  went in for a ct scan and pre approved and was estimated $800 out of pocket..  that turned into $4345 and additional bills keep coming..  my insurance covered $2,474 which leaves $1,872...  applied for assistance and was told no and offered 24 month payment plan...  i suggested maybe the hospital focus on keeping costs down by not having baby grand piano or floor to ceiling art work.. pointed out that this is why people don't get checked...  i pay $1,344/month for my family health care and i get the shaft... i want to personally mention the rudeness and lack of empathy from the financial aid department!!!  anais and richard are horrible representations of the fine staff of nurses and doctors in the system....  i have spent well over $120,000 in your system between the care and birth of my 3 children and to be so rudely dismissed and treated is a statement of the lack of care this corporate system has for general public...  profits and bonuses is all this system is about!  shame on you

i've been to several hospitals in the area and will never come here again, 5hrs plus in emergency waiting room, then the dr comes in for two seconds and leaves and again the waiting begins once more....they will only do x-rays and won't do any ct or mri scans in  the emergency room! horrible service, horrible experience all around!
sherman is probably the worst , but this place is right next to it in line, it's a beautiful looking hospital, but service just sucks!!!!!!! no emergency room should have a 5 hour waiting!!! none!!!!!! st joseph sucks too 
 alexian in hoffman is the best, long wait but never nearly as long as delnor and difference in service is that alexian  thoroughly checks and make sure to take care of everything  and run all sort of scans and xrays and mri if needed- they actually care, unlike other places!!!

went to the er after falling off ladder and hitting my head and back. took over four hours to get a ct. could have internal bleeding but that was the wait. writhing only pain, no attention. finally pumped up with fentanyl and morphine and other pain relievers to no avail. put out in vestibule by myself after seven hours with fall risk bracelet on after they knew it would take her half hour to arrive. no regard for pain or inability to walk in my own. got bill for over 26,000. appealed to no avail. they stand by their service and cost for same. recently got similar ct elsewhere. $390 out of pocket. these people are absolute criminals. this is the same hospital system that told my daughter to abort her baby. now we have a beautiful, happy, and healthy 3-year old grand daughter! stay away from northwestern medice system!

i went to the er a few years ago one snowy sunday night/monday morning around 2 am when an infected index finger began throbbing so intolerably i couldn't stand it any longer. stony brook medical center would have been a tiny bit closer, but lancing and draining an infection seemed simple enough, i opted for mather assuming this would bring about relief faster and quicker. 

parking at 2 am in a snowstorm on monday night was simple enough and the waiting room was empty...score! first problem, i was parched and the soda machine in the waiting room stole my money. 

the triage clerk would win no awards, but with nobody else around, it was unremarkable positive or negative. 

once inside the er, the nurses were fantastic and remained so throughout. then the problems. i was treated by a physician's assistant who had the personality of a phone book and the skill of a kid still developing motor control playing operation.  i received a local anesthetic and the pa told me the finger must be good and numb. i insisted, no, there is zero loss of sensitivity in the finger for the simple reason because there was zero loss of sensitivity in the finger. somehow i was convinced to allow the pa to start draining the infection. each poke by his scalpel or needle-mind you well after the anesthesia should have kicked in-resulted in searing bolts of pain. the genius pa shouted "sir.  you're in an er, you must be quiet!"  i replied "there is only a single patient here besides me, a super fat pregnant woman demanding benzos. you need to remove your incompetent hands from me and gtf away from me. i'm leaving." 

then, unbelievably, it got comically worse as i did consent to the pa's attending physician to have a look. like the amazing way donald trump has actually made george w. bush seem competent in comparison, the attending arrived ungroomed, in a stained shirt and with distinct bo, and managed to improve my perception of the pa (only in comparison). 

i dismissed the attending. the fantastic nurses bandaged up my finger and i proceeded to get dressed for winter weather, which took some time since i was one handed then. knowing the nurses couldn't say anything, but equally well knowing they had to know the incompetence of those two losers who "treated" me, i trash talked the pa and the odoriferous attending during this lengthy process to give them a voice they were surely denied in public. 

in closing, i note that nancy w writes in response to these reviews the same insincere boilerplate so often that i am sure she has a macro since it is called upon all too often. i hope that nancy u or whomever reviews these matters does not cherrypick my kind words for the nurses as praise, because my encounter with mather was a breathtaking failure. all of the negative reviews posted here look credible to me. the positive reviews are written by people too unsophisticated to know they had shitty care (a good outcome does not necessarily  mean you received good care) or who happened to be lucky or not seriously sick or injured 

tl;dr - avoid this shithole at all costs.

my daughter was having stomach issues while at college. we live 3 hours away, so she went to their walk in clinic. what a waste. they ran tests, and told her to go home to her doctor to get a referral for a gi doctor. don't waste your time.

i was kept informed abt my treatment every step of the way. everyone was so very kind. i had the best nurses nite & day.

nite staff
