the hospital is new the people are friendly but no real doctors in the emergency room.  i ask  for some food because  i have diabetes and they said ok but nothing was done.

eileen was very rude to my boyfriend .. he came in with some kind of a stomach virus and she tried to insinuate not once but twice that he was faking ... she said "oh you were fine before i came in the room" question for you eileen  ... we both work full time jobs just like u so  wtf would make u think we wanna be here at 7 a.m  on a saturday morning ... unprofessional ... your job is to make the patient feel better and comfortable but all u did was piss us off ... learn your place you work in service so act like it

i am a registered nurse and was transferred to this hospital from our birthing center because i failed to go into natural labor on my own. i have been a nurse for ten years on an impatient level so i knew what types of interventions i may have to have and was assured my wishes would be respected. that is exactly opposite of what happened. this hospital on their website claims to support low intervention births and that is not the case. 
for example, i wanted to walk in the hallway. it took hours and a really persistent saint nurse jac to let me do so, and then their signal was so poor i only could walk a short distance. this is not a huge request, walking has shown to help labor progress and they should have equipment to be able to accommodate. 

our doula was not respected by the staff and management and wasn't allowed to do any of the things all the other area hospitals allow her to do as a birth professional. she has been allowed in the room for epidurals and c-sections at all the other area hospitals, this is not a new or unusual request. 
the charge nurse sarah insisted on throwing a paper in my face that i had signed about their policies and being extremely rude. part of their rules were on the back of a paper and i hadn't even seen that section because the place for me to sign was on the front.
we unfortunately had to argue to get them to allow our midwife in for a short visit. she was not doing any patient care, just wanted to be supportive. we did have a couple standout nurses (jac, alanna, stephanie) that did their best but it's obvious their hospital policies are not supportive of natural birth.

the manager told us that we should have gone to another hospital if that's the type of care and birth we wanted to receive. she also told our midwife our family was disruptive in the waiting room but never told my family or us that they were disruptive at all. she should have come out to the waiting room to handle the disruption (if it even existed) as a manager, but that was never done. due to their strict visitor policy before birth my father had to wait for 48 hours in that waiting room and wasn't able to see me even for five minutes, so maybe he was a little frustrated. it is obvious to me as a nurse that leadership will round to see if you have any problems but make it clear they have no desire to change or consider policy changes.

i was promised i would get to do skin to skin right after the birth, yet they wouldn't let me hold or see my perfectly healthy son until i was out of the operating room. our birth center no longer recommends this hospital unless it's an emergency. if you are wanting a low intervention birth go to another hospital. you have the right to be respected and you have choices in your birth. don't make the same mistake and let yourself be bullied like i was

i recently had surgery here and could not have been more satisfied with my care.  my pre op nurse, ricki, was amazing.  i am very difficult to start an iv on and she used her tricks to make the process easy and painless.  she was very thorough and kind and i can not say enough wonderful things about her.  my surgery went smooth and the whole surgical team was great.  i would not hesitate to have surgery here again.  

leading up to surgery i had different staff call to collect payment, update health history, remind me of my surgery and pre op instructions.  everyone i spoke to was thorough and kind.

er staff is amazing. so respectful.

labor and delivery nurses are one in a million. nicu nurses and doctors were  so delightful. if i ever move back to vancouver i 100% be using legacy for my medical needs

had to come back for a more serious procedure. i was very impressed with all of the staff. i was treated very well.

i've been in some very good hospitals. this is the best so far.

this hospital is the most uncaring hospital i've ever been in the staff is rude i bought my 86 year old mother in .. sick with problems breathing i ask for a blanket they said they were out i was the only one sitting in the waiting room for over 2 hours when we got to the back there were 2 rooms with people in them all there were doing was talking to each other and laughing about yesterday super bowl game i have ever in my life been this poorly treated any where at any hospital in my life .... this place needs some new management and the woman behind the counter  need to work at a bar because that's how they were acting so rude unbelievable rude never will i ever come back to this hospital i would rather drive out to kaiser sunny side where this hospital could learn some much needed manners from this is just unbelievable i have never  ever been treated  awful ever

no reason why i should rate this any lower, service was prompt and my physician was nice and informative. very pleased with my experience. however, parking can be confusing but that is par the course.

well took my four kids and i to the emergency room because we weren't feeling good for about 2 months now. we all have had runny nose bad cough hacking up stuff throwing up running fevers. so decided it was time to go to the emergency room and see what was wrong. one thing i could say is we found out that we have flu b. there's nothing that they can really do about it have to let it play its course and run out crazy hoping to get an antibiotic and they can't give me one. but i will say that is the best hospital i've ever been to each time i've gone with getting x-rays and blood work the most i've been there is 2 hours i highly recommend this hospital and the staff was great to my kids and i.

i went to legacy salmon creek  for an eeg. first of all, i'm used to epic imaging in portland, where the tech, eeg, and dr who reads the test are in one place and on one bill. my insurance was billed separately for the tech and separately for the procedure. then i received a bill from radia, based in seattle, whose physician read my eeg.  that dr was out of network, although i had requested an in network doctor. stay away from here!  i'm returning to epic-- it's worth the drive

sorry i can't give this place 0 stars.  i was sent to the er by my then-physician without any acute symptoms - she was mad (the office staff used the word "angry") because i didn't have a $4000 test she wanted me to have ("to cover myself," she said).  er doc found nothing after a ton of tests i'd had a few months prior and wanted to know why i was there.  

i got a pretty sizable bill, which i couldn't afford to pay, so i set up a payment plan.  they billed me more than we agreed on and now, with still $600 left to pay, i am unable to buy medicine i need to control my seizures. 

i sent in the financial aid application - 2 people in customer support suggested it - and just got a denial because i have insurance and don't need help. 

my monthly bills are greater than my income.  

if you are not wealthy and have a $5-10,000 deductible, don't go here.  the "care" is bad and the customer service is worse. on the other hand, if you suffer because you are unable to pay for life-saving medicine because of their (inflated) charges and unwillingness to work with you, you can sue them and probably make a bundle.  if you are alive to enjoy it.

i went here after developing an allergic reaction to something. upon entering we were greeted and i was seen immediately. the entire staff, dr. moore, my nurse peg, registration amanda, were all fabulous and attentive to my needs. my nurse peg called the next day to check on me and make sure we made it home safely. i was beyond satisfied with my experience. the doctor gave clear instructions on what i needed to do when we arrived home. peg made sure i was comfortable, just recognizing i needed some water to a warm blanket. i am thankful for the staff.

if i could give this place zero stars, i would.

my son's annual physical appointment at at 1pm and it took them 40 mins to bring us back.

my father who is 93 was transferred to park bridge after a stay in a local hospital since he needed more therapy and medical attention after suffering a brain bleed. he was still unable to stand without help . sandra who was my initial contact made the transition smooth. she is so thorough with paperwork and his transport to from hospital to room went well.  we met the next day with a team who oversee his care with a plan in place.  all i can say is his nurse elmer, occupational therapist worked intensively giving him the attention he needed to rehabilitate him somewhat to his prior baselines in order to return home. he was clean, his clothes laundered, fed wonderful but most of all the care team really helped. teresa was so engaged as well.  my father said the social director michael came many times to see if he'd like to join & engage in activities however my dads focus was mainly rest & therapy . this is a skilled nursing facility!!

review: suburban pulled me out of a very dark and depressed state in their inpatient facility. the staff was stellar, the groups were helpful and i never felt unsafe or inhuman. they let me wear my own clothes and have visitors daily, and there is plenty of time to use the phones. the majority of other clients were wonderful people. i cannot say enough about suburbans inpatient program.

well if you are a senior, or have a senior that you care about- do not go to this ageist hospital. young patients will come, receive care and treatment- all the while i witnessed my father- 94 years old- languishing in excruciating pain for over 9 hours. i had to beg for pain management. i had to plead for water- even after it was approved. i had to plead for a urinal so my father could relieve himself. while approved, no food was offered to my father for breakfast, lunch, or dinner! we pleaded, and finally my father was offered nourishment from suburban hospital after 9 hours in the er and begging on behalf of his children at 6:15 pm. please understand he was cleared to receive hydration and nutrition in the am hours. i wonder what happens to vulnerable  seniors without an advocate???? does this hospital think that excruciating pain is something for seniors to endure? are younger people more important because they can advocate for themselves? shame on you, suburban hospital,  and johns hopkins for  supporting ageism. i will be raising awareness for your policies as much as possible. we will never use your services in my father's life your mine. #seniorbullies #suburbanhospitaldoesntcareaboutseniors

review: if i could give this er zero stars i would. i want everyone to go to a different hospital because they are no help here. my father had internal bleeding, to the point where he was grey almost passing out . he walked in to the er with my mom and they were going to make him wait an hour to see a doctor, wouldn't even evaluate him to see if he was higher priority. there was no one in the er waiting room. they left and went to advocate. my father happened to be high priority, he was seen at sherman and was admitted to the icu for internal bleeding. i know other people who have had to wait 6 hours and they were presenting serious signs of something wrong, high bp, headache sweating nausea. they just left him sit in the waiting room 6 hours and wouldn't even let him talk to a doctor. i really hope that they fire and hire new staff. i have never met so many unwilling to help nurses and doctors in my life. i will never go here and i've told everyone i know never to go here. i'll drive the 20 mins to get actual help at sherman.

review: i wish i could give this place negative stars... my young son and i were two of only three people in the entire waiting area, and yet as he laid on the floor writhing in pain, i had to go to the counter not once, but twice to see if someone could come help him. once they finally ushered him back, the er doc spent all of 20 seconds in our room only to come to an incorrect and baseless conclusion (misdiagnosis), and then give him a medicine that actually made his symptoms worse. but the even more frustrating part has been everything after that - i spent over 10 months trying to speak with the hospital in regards to the bill, and repeatedly they forgot to return my calls. i finally get thru to someone about adjusting our er bill based on the misdiagnosis, and she said that the almighty board decided - without ever having talked to me - that they did no wrong (surprise surprise!).  during this time, i was also told our bill was on hold while they "assessed it" (ie, forgot to call me back) only to get a collections notice because they also forgot to actually put the bill on hold. terrible service, terrible billing practices, this er clearly only cares about the money coming in and has no interest in the actual quality of care they provide.

review:
my father in law has been in this is hospital for the past 4 months and there have been numerous issues. blood thinners given before surgery which is a bbq no no down to simply not answering his calls when he asks for a nurse or help. we do not recommend this facility and never want a loved one in this situation again. we often hear the staff in the  hallway laughing and carrying on like it's a party but they dont have time to take care of their patients. he has been on floors 5 and 11 aardvark don't really see a difference in care until a doctor walks in and then it's all business. 
also, there are no couches or places for my mother in law to stay the night and be with him. every other hospital i've ever visited has had a couch that can be slept on or at least several visitors can sit on. we sit on the floor when visiting, which is ridiculous. 
when your family has medical issues look for another hospital this one could cost time, money, health and possibly a life.

can i give no stars? over 11 hrs sitting in the er waiting room with an iv line in but not attached to anything. then told me i wasn't allowed to leave because of it.  only took close to 12 hours for them to offer the basic standard of care - iv fluids.

i can't say enough about how life-changing my delivery experience was with the entire labor and delivery team at saddleback. i made the decision to leave my former ob and hospital (hoag) when i was 37 weeks along in my pregnancy because i was feeling bullied into a particular birth plan. luckily, my perinatologist was located at saddleback memorial, so i made the switch because they made me feel like i could - and should - be an active participant in my birthing experience (crazy, i know!).

to dr. huete, dr. may, and dr. bush - thank you for all that you did to help realize my dreams of a successful vbac.  delivering my beautiful baby boy with your team last week was truly the most empowering and validating experiences of my life. to the entire team of ldrp nurses - ellen, christine, sally, emma, christy, all the charge nurses and nicu nurses, thank you for the truly outstanding level of care and genuine emotional support you provided. you ladies made labor as fun as it can be!  to all the expectant mommies out there researching hospitals, i have delivered three babies at three different hospitals, and, for me, saddleback was, by far and away, the best experience of them all. 

also, just to add on to some of the other reviews - it's true, the food is pretty good! the ice chips are even better .

around 7pm that night kathy left and two nurses catherine and jane took over. they coached my wife through it all to say the least. we are so grateful for their hard work and dedication 10/10!

review:
my other half and i delivered our beautiful baby girl at this wonderful hospital. i am so grateful for our amazing and dedicated nurses- sue, meagan, cassie, jane, catherine, and christina +
the doctor who helped bring our precious baby girl into the world, doctor dejbakhsh. everyone we met were all very kind and compassionate. they truly went above and beyond when it came to care for mom and the baby. they also made sure that dad was comfortable, too. the entire staff was responsive, professional, kind, and overall exceptional in every way. i also love that they allow dads to eat meals here, too. the meals for two comes with your stay here, and the food isn't too bad. breakfast burritos in the morning were quite good, the sandwiches for lunch + the quesadillas and burgers weren't too shabby either. they served pretty decent hospital food! i was surprised. this hospital also makes sure you're set up with all of the extras that you will need- definitely not stingy here! &the staff is always on top of everything when you need it! they're all truly wonderful. overall, this hospital is truly a hidden gem- my experience here was absolutely amazing, and i am so glad i chose this hospital for such a special and memorable life event! i would recommend this hospital to anyone looking to find a great place to have their baby!!!

review:

nicu nurses cut a piece of my baby's hair without asking me first.  
rather than deal with this shock i was pressured and grilled about this issue and that issue.  i had just come out of general anesthesia... there was so much trauma caused by the nicu doctor and his staff and social worker that i should have sued.  seriously.   
if you child has any reason that may call for a nicu stay, do not go here.

i have a thing for unusual dining experiences, including hospital cafeterias when i have no reason to go to the hospital. today was an exception, as my father was getting chemo.

like most cafeterias these days, the cost of food is dependent on the weight. my omelet and sweet potato chips came out to less than $5. not too bad for basic sustenance.

allegedly, my first review violated yelp's guidelines (this means someone who really cared must have flagged it) although my angered verbosity was very much provoked by a horrible experience i had with my mother getting checked into the er.

apparently it's passé for a 64 year old woman to mysteriously collapse. i'm sorry you see the same thing over and over to the point you forget that you're dealing with other people's constant concerns over life and death. i'm usually a nice patron who realizes the soul sucking and overwhelming dread of customer service but how someone treads around my mom's life isn't innocently shrugged off like a bad cheeseburger. the 24/7 on-call nurse who determined my mom's collapse as an emergency made it seem like we were dealing with a seizure or a mini stroke so when we regurgitated her words to the guy at the er desk, he chuckled and condescendingly disregarded that information. people faint--yes. but fainting for a 64 year old with a family history of brain diseases can mask itself in a lot of alarming red herrings. just because you see "real emergencies" it doesn't warrant you to lose compassion and sensitivity. 

so kaiser, i hope i didn't violate anything this time by expressing that your er desk staff over on zion ave. really needs to have a pep talk about how to process patients with integrity and without making comments that are better left for a doctor to determine.

my wife fell and because they thought she may have head trauma the ambulance people thought university hospital was the best place to take her. boy were they wrong. my wife got to the er around 2:15 friday afternoon. the first people to see my wife was a financial counselor followed by a resident physician, an attending physician and a student. they couldn't have been there more than a couple of minutes because i arrived about 15 minutes later and they were already gone. i told the nurse that there was a possibility of a brain bleed and that my wife needed a ct scan. about an hour later they came to take my wife to x-ray. i asked about the ct scan and they said there wasn't one ordered. seriously! she's got a goose egg on her temple with obvious bruising and no ct scan? it was after 8:00pm when she was finally taken to have the scan. we got the results around 9:45- 10:00pm. luckily the scan was negative for bleeding on the brain. during all of this there was a vile of blood laying on the table next to the sharps disposal box. i don't know if it was my wife's or someone else's but it didn't belong there. next came the discharge nurse who put a sling on my wife and tried to send her on her way with the iv needles still in my wife's wrist. i pointed that out to him and he removed them but my wife was now bleeding profusely where he had removed the iv. i had to point that out to him too. when we finally arrived home i had to not only remove the electrodes used for her ekg but the wire leads were still attached to them. my wife was there for over 8 hours with nothing more than a few ice chips for thirst, nothing to eat and she was dehydrated when she got home. as of this writing we still have not seen the results of the blood draw and i don't think we will. you'll be better off going anywhere else other than here for an emergency. and if it is suggested that you come here like it was us, ask for another suggestion.

this is beyond me. so i finish all the three tests they ordered and waited and waited and waited and waited. during waiting i did get impatient maybe once and went up to the desk where the nurses do the triage, and i broke down crying because the wait was a lot and she told me that i could go and come back to the clinic tmw or i can stay to see my results and maybe the doctor will give me medication.  ladies and gentleman i received my results @2:40am and the pa , not the dr says that it's nothing all the labs (3 tests) came out fine. but did i not tell them it's my thyroid ? no scans of my neck were done, no touching of my neck, no repititi of my disease was mentioned. i asked the pa what if this happens again? what if i faint or am feeling fatigued again? he says well everything looks normal so we don't know why. seriously.. i really wanted to cry at this point literally waiting 12 hours just for him to tell me i'm okay. if i am okay why was i not able to see for 30 seconds, why did i feel dizzy and felt like i was going to pass out? he says he doesn't know and next time i should just go to their clinic ! how is passing out not an emergency i don't understand. then i said okay thank you i would like to leave and for someone to take my iv out he said ok and leaves the curtain room. then 10 minutes pass and no one comes to take my iv out. seriously i'm still in this er that is causing me mental stress, and i walked out of the room to ask a nurse to take this iv out and he says they need to check if i've been discharged. i haven't been discharged. even though pa morris told me i am okay. i'm stuck here, and i want to cry my eyes out this was the worst experience in my whole entire life. i even got up to ask the nurses at the desk where the pa is so i can get discharged and they were chitchatting it up about something funny, and one of the nurses told me after i asked if she can tell the pa morris to discharge me and she said first of all ma'am i don't even know your name and she rolled her eyes at me .. i'm pissed i don't recommended going here ever for the e.r. please save your time, your feelings, your mental state, your mental health, and your money and spend them on places that actually care about your wellbeing and mental state. let's see how long they take to take out my iv. will update, what time i am discharged.

i do not recommend this clinic.  i saw drs. pemberton and gopal, and would not recommend either.  

i first went  to this clinic because of excruciating menstrual pain.  after waiting quite a while, i was seen by a woman who only later identified herself as a student and not an actual gynecologist.  i had made an appointment to see a doctor, not a student.  i understand that students need to learn, but i should've been notified of this when i made the appointment, and asked if this was an acceptable substitution (it was not).  what should've been a 20 minute appointment became 1 1/2 hours because the student kept having to excuse herself to go talk to the actual doctors, recount to them what i'd just said, get their feedback, and then come tell me what they'd said.  it was like a terrible game of telephone, and not at all professional.  please note that they billed my insurance as though i'd seen an actual doctor.

i had to come back for a biopsy.  dr. pemberton offered no pain control options for the procedure and just told me to "relax".  ultimately, it was unsuccessful because she said my cervix was "being shy", so i had to make another appointment, take a cervical relaxer, and come back.  i did this, and the biopsy happened...but it was the most painful thing i've ever experienced (and i've passed kidney stones!!)!  at one point, i screamed for her to stop, and she did not.  that's not okay, and i felt violated, but also felt like i had no other options, given the physical position i was in.  

i was diagnosed, medicated, and while this helped, it didn't completely fix the issue.  i then had to go back and negotiate treatment options with dr. gopal, because dr. pemberton was on temporary leave.  he refused to even consider a hysterectomy, because he said "i might want to carry a child someday"...even though i explained to him that that wasn't going to happen for a number of reasons.  what is this, the 1950's, where keeping my lady-parts so i can reproduce is more important than treating the very real medical issue i have???  dr. gopal offered other options that included a lot of disruptive medications and unnecessary medical procedures, none of which will actually address the issue directly, and instead made it clear that he doesn't really have any real solutions, but doesn't want to admit that he doesn't know what else to do.

i'm not including all the medical details, because frankly it's private, but let's just say i'm beyond frustrated.  i am medically-savvy enough about my own body and the medical issues i have to know that i'm getting sub-par care.  i understand that medical science has limitations, especially for women's bodies, and especially when it comes to gynecological issues.  but i'm also not going to let myself be experimented on like a guinea pig by someone who clearly isn't taking me seriously and who wants to subject me to unnecessary medical interference that isn't actually a solution, more like an expensive, exhausting, painful, time-consuming distraction.

this practice clearly focuses on pregnancy and childbirth, rather than complex gynecological problems that have nothing to do with actual reproduction, something i wasn't aware of when i was referred to it by a different, well-meaning doctor.

this office isn't fully wheelchair-accessible (turn radii are too tight, furniture is placed poorly, doors are hard to operate, none of the staff has ever offered to assist me).

review:
as far as care goes, this place is amazing.   if you are lucky enough to be eligible for a clinical trail and willing to be a guinea pig, they do an excellent job at patient care.  all of the docs and nurses were friendly and caring.  not sure whether the care is working at all, but i do feel good about the experience so far.  

knocked off a star for two reasons.  the travel reimbursement is awesome as a benefit, but the process of getting it is a total cluster.  tons of inconsistencies in what does and does not get reimbursed and a terrible process at the voucher office.   don't try and do this on your way out the door, because there are a lot of steps and it takes forever.  first, your coordinator has to put it in the computer.   then, you fill out a form (paper) and provide all your receipts (on paper) again.  then you stand in line to submit your form.  the voucher employee doesn't get out of her chair, so there is a sign telling you that if you don't stand, you won't be served.   then, they take the form and receipts for processing.  then, you wait 2 hours.  then, you come back and stand in line again.   then, they give you a pile of paper back.  then, you stand in line for the cashier 5 feet away.  then, you sit and wait for the cashier to prepare a check.  i didn't have any patience at this point, so i don't know how long the check takes.  instead, i stuffed $1300 in cash in my purse since that was faster.

hi, i am 30 weeks pregnant and came to the emergent care on the advice of my ob. i was having braxton hicks contractions but this was not the main reason for my visit. i was unsure as to whether my water had broken. when i arrived the nurse that brought me to the room was very nice, laura, i believe. she asked me to put on a gown and give a urine sample. while in the process of doing this, the rn came in and was extremely rude to my husband and i. she would ask me questions but would not wait for my answer and at one point put her hand up to me to stop me from talking so she could interrupt my answer. she was very condescending, telling me that if i think my water had broken that i should not wait more than 12 hours to do something about it. also telling me let's hope that nothing is wrong because you should have gone to a hospital with a nicu. at this point, i made it pretty clear on my face that she was making me angry, so i told her that i was following the instructions of my doctor, and the nurse at my ob office instructed me to come to the hospital that i would be delivering at. she leveled out a little after that, however the doctor made me feel as if i had done something wrong as well by coming in. telling me that i cannot be analyzing every pain or i'm never going to make it through this pregnancy. this whole experience has me rethinking having my child in this hospital because of how i was treated when i followed every instruction of my doctor, as well as all of the labor and delivery classes that i have taken at st. joes south. i should never have been made to feel as if i did something wrong, or that i was stupid for even showing up there. the emergency room is the last place i want to be ever, and if i am advised by my doctor to go again for any reason during this pregnancy i don't know that i would be coming to this hospital because of the treatment i received.

waited over 2 hours. my medical condition was serious and i almost died.  they refused to update my correct name. they had "no beds" but could have moved me to ob or taken blood while waiting.  they don't care and aren't professional.

with  the deepest appreciation  i wanna thank each and everyone one of you for coming to a busy doctors rescue. dr singh your sharpness and diagnostic skills and delivery deserve an emmy. the traveling nurse, lisa i believe you made me laugh the entire time while not being able to breath that well. the  triage nurse, damn you work fast but very caring! and last the  the security guard for recognizing my urgency at 3 am. man you deserve a metal. ok....i believe my point is taken...i picked up my meds, returned and finished seeing my patients  and successfully heading home. to my family. my appreciation to you all! dr. j

salinas valley memorial hospital is an old hospital that has become much to small for a city the size of salinas.
the waiting area in the emergency department is a very small area cramped with chairs and numerous people waiting to be seen. as i sat there waiting i felt as if i was in a third world facility. i was surrounded by non english speakers many of which had numerous children with them. the waiting area is also dirty and not very comfortable.
after having my vitals taken i was then brought back into the hallways near the emergency department. i was triaged in the hallway and told to wait on a shitty cheap folding chair until a room became available.
the first emergency department room i was placed in already had another patient with her family in the room. the only thing seperating us was the flimsy curtain.
this patient and her family were obnoxious and loud laughing and making alot of noise. i finally blew up and told them to shut the fuck up. after me yelling i was then removed and placed in a private room.
the staff at this hospital are terrific some of the finest i have experienced. however my reasons for this 2 star rating has to do with the dirty waiting area and then being placed in a hallway on a cheap folding chair while waiting for an available room.
it is pretty pathetic.
what's more disturbing is the fact that this old hospital is to small as well as being outdated to handle the large city population of the salinas valley.

people are kinda rude

but the place is pretty nice though compared to other hospitals

i went to check in the er. there were a few people there and the clerk didn't ask why i needed to be seen.   he was security. he took my name and told me to sit down. i am two days past surgery and my in call doc thinks it might be blood clot. it appeared everyone else was here for cold /flu but you wouldn't know because security was doing the check in. unbelievable

my ophthalmologist told me to stop by an er asap while i was traveling home due to some eye issues i was having. i'm two hours from home and have been in the er for nearly three hours. doctor said that ophthalmologist left for the day and to come back the next day. i would have been much better off driving home to my local hospital. im not sure how much longer i will sit here before they release me. they say i might have a tear in my retina. nothing conclusive. i'm sitting in a room with six other patients who are waiting to be released. one man said that he has sat in this room for three hours before. they have checked my vitals twice. technician said he has no idea when i will be released. this was a waste of time as well as a waste of my er copay. it seems that this hospital al can't handle the patient load.

facility was definitely outdated, but all will change for the better as the new hospital is nearly complete.

fast, thorough and clean er. medical professionals were kind and caring. a  student doctor who spoke to me, asked great questions and although i hadn't mentioned a genetic issue i should have considered, he keyed into a potential issue that my dad has had for 30 years and likely i may have. i will need further testing to confirm, but am relieved to have an avenue to pursue. the physician also felt what i was experiencing was what the student had concluded. greatly relieved after my er visit.

i arrived at the emergency room on saturday january 11 for neck, shoulder, and chest pain. i agree with the reviewer who didn't understand why this hospital get such a bad wrap.  i had a good experience from the staff in the er, to the doctors, nurses and techs on the floor. my stay lasted 4 days and after several test they were able to properly diagnose me by process of elimination.  i would also like to thank the staff in the various labs i visited.  for anyone reading this post don't take your frustrations out on the staff, rather reach out to the administration.  these people work hard and you're not their only patient.  we often thank the military for their service but during my stay i thanked the hospital staff i came in contact with for their service. these people work hard and don't deserve any unnecessary grief. if you experience any mistreatment then take it to their leadership.  thank god for doctors, nurses, technicians, and all other hospital staff.  i appreciate all that you do to get us well.

excellent hospital experience super attentive staff they all seem authentically care about patients my mom was very confused she is 87 years old the doctor took time out to call me in florida and discuss the entire case and the situation where my dad with me so i can explain it to my mom excellent service real professionals here from the people who clean the room to the doctors they all have a smile on their face and know what they're doing all the equipment and machinery is top-notch very clean hospital would recommend to anyone

just recently found out apparently our daughter was not covered even though we we told she was. we paid copayments as expected and never thought about anything else. until we just got a bill saying the first visit was $40+ plus a $300+ for a new patient! $2,000 for a mri and multiple $200+ fees for reading the results!

we still don't know what is wrong with our daughter but cannot afford to come back here! we trusted all was covered since our dr referred us and the ladies at check in advised our insurance was accepted. 

the people are super great but unfortunately we are one of the patients that are just "business" for them.  so while i applaud them for being a childrens hospital i advise you to watch your billing nothing is what you are told. we had given 5 stars here and referred friends here now i have to follow up and make sure they are not in the same situation.
sick babies shouldn't have to wait 5 hours in the er before being seen. inexcusable!

we had only been to the er once three years ago, and being the only ones there, we were happy with everything. now, i rushed there with a patient having stroke symptoms. we were taken right in. the professionalism was astounding. not having  much medical knowledge, i couldn't have been happier with the triage, questions asked of us, and the communication between the doctors and nurses to us. up on the floors the staff again were great. they were busy with us and educated us. nighttime was noisy and the patient was checked often. the meals were quite good. hillcrest has two buildings. in the older one the rooms are very small. there is barely space for a chair. the bathroom is large. in the newer building the rooms are large with room for a visitor or two. elevators have letters and signs to help visitors get around, but it is confusing for newcomers. there is a lot of walking to get to offices and patient rooms. be patient. wear walking shoes. take reading material.

i spent several days here with my grandfather in the icu. the rns here are entitled and seem completely unapologetic to their patients problems. 
our cna was very sweet and took the utmost care of us. the doctors did well at explaining the issues and updating us when possible. the reason i can only muster of a 2 star review is by just how terrible my family was treated by the rns. the hospital itself is beautiful and modern and parking is a breeze. these rns need to come back down to earth though.

doctors in the emergency department are horrible - constant misdiagnoses, as has been my experience on multiple visits over the years. if you have to go there, good luck. the nurses and technicians however, are lovely.

i was taken to er and then admitted for surgery. i was there for 4 days. i was very pleased with all of the staff, nurses and doctors. they were all very courteous and well trained to attend to all my needs...not just medical. 
omg!! the food was fantastic! i would definitely recommend them.
this is the worst hospital i've been been too!!! lack or urgency and poor communication. don't come here unless your on your death bed. because you will be before your see.

this place is crooked as heck. double charged me. double charged. got 7 different bills for one stay. all charging me for the same thing advent charged me for.  took advantage of someone that was on pain medication. took me from an out patient without telling me . did test without consent.

i was making payments for 5 months what i could pay. seeing i live on 850 a month. the lady told me to pay what i could. they demanded i pay 280 a month. which i could not do. when i went to pay this month it wouldn't let me pay so i called to make payments and was told they turned it over to collections. which wrecked my credit.  they did this without any notice or anything. they lied. 
have called 14 times asking for them to take us off there mailing list and still getting them 41 mailing have been sent back. bunch of crooks. they should run for office.

new to this insurance. saw a family practioner and had blood work done.  saw an orthopedic and had x- rays done. they also scheduled an mri and made sure it was authorized under my plan which is advent health. as a matter of fact, all these services were done under advent health. you would think that billing would fall under an advent health central location. after all they want your copay, deductible or coinsurance before you have any services. not so. they call it precheck when they call you to get you to pay for your service instead of pre pay. i had a deductible to meet and paid it. the payment took care of my deductible except for 92 cents. well the radiology department has not sent the bill to be processed. so in the mean time all the other bills have been sent and processed under the deductible. will now have a credit and who knows how much because they haven't sent the bill to process. they would not see me unless i paid and they don't even know how much i owe. now all the billing will be going to the deductible until the radiology bill processes. it's hard enough to keep track of everything especially when you are sick. very wrong and messed up billing system. the patient gets taken advantage of financially here. so messed up and wrong!

needed physical therapy for pinched nerve in neck. treated by dr. shandrea boyd for 3 sessions. she was the most hospitable, professional and down to earth doctor that has ever cared for my well being...very much recommended!

review:
re: dr. ken thompson  

november the 26th, my family decided it was over due that i see a doctor.  after breaking my shoulder last year, i never wanted to go to an emergency room again. 

i was not at home in ovilla, texas, but at my lake home in oklahoma. i do not have a physician here. after being sick with a horrific stomach virus for 7 straight days, i was miserable. 

upon arrival at the emergency room, i ran inside like a wrecking ball to continue my illness. thank you jesus, for er nurse rebecca and dr. thompson. i was so sick the whole time they patiently attended to me. they never stopped being attentive to me as i profusely apologized for my sick stomach. 

i had dehydrated with a virus that last from 9 to 10 days. i was finally on the down side, but could not keep nothing on my stomach. 

after an iv and meds, i finally felt better. i should of gone to a doctor sooner. i just kept thinking it was a 24 hour bug that kept on lingering. 

kudos to dr. thompson, you made me feel comfortable during my illness. i am so grateful to him and nurse rebecca. 

i was good as new on thanksgiving!  thank you both, including the warm staff at registration. 

i definitely would return!
fac_name: Baylor Scott & White Surgical Hospital at Sherman

review: i wish i could rate this place less than one star. i brought my girlfriend into the er tonight for being violently sick with a flu on top of stomach issues she's been having for over a year. from the second we walked in, we were treated as if we were a problem rather than my gf being cared for as a very sick patient.  she was told to wait to throw up until she received a pee sample cup!! all of the staff was extremely rude except for our doctor. however, the nurse seemed miserable working her job and made us feel it too. after expressing my concerns and frustrations with the staff, my gfs nurse smiled at us (the first time since we got there) as if it was amusing to her that we were unhappy. i'm not sure if the entire staff is homophobic or just hates their lives, but the mistreatment was so bad we got up and left to go to a different er before the nurse could even put an iv in. do not come here unless you want to leave feeling. oh and i should add that we still received a bill for hundreds of dollars when we received zero treatment...

review: this place is a joke! do not go here even in an emergency. a girl on my daughters hockey team broke her back during a game last night. they were off-putting, acted as if we were a disturbance to their busy day, we were the only ones in the place! they were useless and very uncaring! this 17 year old girl broke her back, and they did x-rays after 15 minutes of her sitting in her wet cold hockey gear, then they wanted her to stay in a hotel overnight so she could be fitted the next day for a back brace, no kidding! then for the pain they gave her tylenol!! stay away!!!! make the ambulance take you to madison!

review: i have a relative who is an inpatient in the emergency department of augusta university health medical center. she's just completed 24 hours in the emergency room she's in a room that does not allow her phone to communicate outside the room she is hooked up to equipment that does not allow her to get up out of the bed to use her phone. i have called 706-721-4951 and asked that someone take a phone to her so she can call me in augusta. they say they don't have a phone. she's in a room with the tv that doesn't have a remote add is on one channel and no one will change the channel for her. this is mental cruelty and it's not right their patients are stuck there i am in a wheelchair and can't go down there because my driver has to work.

emergency room as jam-packed on a tuesday night. wait was long but staff were friendly and courteous even with difficult patients. my mother included. 
security came out and help me roll her in.

one nurse or receptionist, not sure of her position, ran out to help a very young, crying boy wheel his mother who had a broken foot into the er.

i came here for a common day procedure and was very happy with the care i received.  my nurses were compassionate, friendly, and reassuring. my doctor was also friendly and took the time to answer all my questions. the hospital itself is clean and they are organized, the wait times aren't bad. i recommend this hospital just based on staff interactions alone. good doctors and nurses are hard to find and this place was full of them.

my husband has come here once a year for a physical.
the girls at the front desk are always nice so i'm not sure about the other yelpers and their problem with customer service we don't have that.
my issue is the weight it's ridiculous to have an appointment at 8 o'clock in the morning and not get seen till 1030 and then take another few hours just to have a physical.

unfortunately i cannot rate this place less than 1 star. this was the absolute worst experience i've ever had at a hospital. i had done something to my jaw last night and couldn't really move it because it felt so loose... my face swole up and my lips were numb. i was freaking terrified because a. i hate hospitals... and b. i'm a hypochondriac. 
so i walked in, wasn't greeted. explained my situation to a nurse who was genuinely nice... then the biggest piece of human waste walked in. i wish i remembered her name. she basically interrogated me for 30 mins about information that didn't effing matter considering i was almost passing out every 2 minutes. it was obvious i was out of it and i got 0 concern from her.

for example: 111 county road 1111 houston, tx 
we got in a disagreement about the fact... i try to explain to this dumb woman that my road in fact is not called county road? that it's literally a county road... that my street is "1111". because i lived in a small town. finally i go into the dang room to see the doctor and i was told i had tmj, then ended up being tmd. i asked the nurse and she said she didn't know the difference and didn't know about it. wtf?!?
and when i was leaving i followed her because i assumed she would show me out and she turned around and was like "do you need something?" 
moral of the story: screw this place

clinical staff were fine.  front office staff were rude, arrogant, and demeaning.  they attempted to force me to sign for documents i never received.  after i wouldn't capitulate, they relented and gave me the documents.  after a lengthy verification that i had already satisfied my insurance deductible, they were set to charge the deductible anyway, but we caught it, so they corrected it.  then after a long wait, i discovered that they had put me back two patients in procedure order.  i was finally moved up one patient when i said i was leaving.  i will never use this facility again.

can't get anyone to pick up the phone to reply my pharmacy for refill. i tried calling three times, each time goes straight to a waiting queue for 20min (60min total ) and have no inclination when # in queue i am. maybe the office is shut down. don't know

the hospital only had water available for the patient (really)  imagine if this was your family member or friend.
this is a hospital that you never want to go to ever!

i wouldn't bring stuffed animals to this hospital to have their plastic eyes glued on.  nearly 7 years after my initial review and they still don't have their $hit together. my father recently visited the er due to elevated bp.  personnel bickered about availability of equipment to perform an ekg and he observed someone actually hide a machine. he became disgusted and left without being evaluated.

respect the medical profession enought to consider that human beings are coming here for compassionate care, and they represent more than an invoice!!

please do not go to this hospital,  my loved one went there with extreme back pain and was waiting for 6 hours before he had his mri and just to be sent home and told nothing was wrong, he went back 3 times in pain and the lady at the front desk said you are back again, how rude, its not like somebody wants to come back three times for the same issues that wasn't addressed the first time, he ended up having a herniated disk and had to have an operation, i felt so bad for him and i begged him to go to another hospital but unfortunately he didn't want to start the procedure over because of the pain and time, the surgeon did a great job on his back but he ended up going back again for the same issue a year later with excruciating pain with the same run around before getting the help he needed.  you would think a repeat patient would at least get decent treatment.  without patients the hospital wouldn't make money so please treat your patients with respect and dignity.

my dad went and was given the run a round and i told him to go to a better hospital and he did and they were able to help him and found out he had congestive heart failure and the other hospital treated him respectfully and there was no going back and forth, here it is 3 years later and he is doing great.

something needs to be done with this hospital either fire the front desk workers, retrain them on how to give excellent customer service, send the doctors back to college or just close the whole damn hospital down!!!.   i mean this from the heart.

review:
so i went to the er around 8:30pm and stood in line. i was the only one in line and the intake nurse just sat there typing on her computer. she was obviously busy but didn't even acknowledge me. then when she did call me to her, i told her that i was sent by a kaiser doctor to the er and it was prearranged. the er doctor (dr. ly) and my primary care doctor had already spoken to each over the phone. i told her my diagnosis was on my chart with my medical record number. she ignored what i said and just said you have to get on the scale. i told her that there are other patients standing here and their family members. there is no privacy. i don't want to talk in front of other patients nor do i want them see my weight and listen to my medical diagnosis. she began yelling at me saying i don't know what is your problem is. i can't give you medicine unless i weigh you in front of all these people. then she proceeded to get up and move the scale by another nurse which was still by other patients and said to me it's in kilograms so i don't know why you are so worried that other people hear or see your number. by then i was utterly embarrassed and taken aback that kaiser had such an unprofessional woman/ nurse talking to patients this way. i would complain to the head of er but i have a feeling it will fall on deaf ears. my purpose in writing this review is to inform you of the quality of care given at this facility especially at the er. avoid this place. kaiser customer service has fallen! it's like a run of the mill county hospital.

"not for profits" are actually worse than "for profit".  their agenda is still to make revenue, that they can in turn invest into their staff and hospitals and especially line their executives pockets with.

***surgical biopsies are done in a hospital or surgical center, and they can cost thousands of dollars.  but a core-needle biopsy costs as little as $500.  it is done in a radiology or breast imaging center, or in the doctor's office.***

so, it is more cost effective not to have this procedure done at the hospital.

i can't say enough wonderful things about this facility being there, when i needed them.  and god forbid i find myself having to spend extended amounts of time at ucla in the future, just knowing they are there makes the word of difference!  

the last thing a family member needs to worry about when they have an ill loved one, is logistics.  tiverton house takes all of those worries, concerns away from you and simply allows you to focus on the important matter at hand.  they provide you a place to lay your head after those rough days.  thank you tiverton.

beware of frisbie and their practices. i had the same primary care for years. this last visit the doctor informed me she was moving to another practice and also that family care of somersworth was closing their doors. (not sure if they're open now). i went for my regular yearly physical which is covered by my insurance for free. i was also seen in a different office building over by skyhaven airport because of the practice closing their doors. i got a bill for services that the doctor didn't tell me was covered at my visit. also for services i never had...a sleep test? i tried talking to the hospital billing department which they informed me to write a letter to risk management. i went ahead and did that. i was still stuck with the $60+ bill and a hand written scribbled letter back from frisbie hospital saying it was a different service they were charging me for. so what is it? they said one thing then turned around and said another thing ( very unprofessional) and then my bill was sent to collections. watch what they charge you for!!!

don't go there if you want rehab after surgery.  they will take advantage of your insurance and do every test they can think of.  
my husband needed physical therapy to get strong after surgery.   he sat for 5 days not allowed to get up and move.  therapy amounted to a group in morning with arm peddling exercises.   the beautiful gym and equipment is a facade.   no one is every doing therapy there.   i have to keep complaining and threatening to get attention.  we are leaving in 4 days.  they best be ready by then.  called my insurance to request home therapy.  if you need therapy......research and be sure that's a facility for that.   i saw people there kept alive for no reason except money.   terrible.  just don't go.

i have seen multiple oncology physicians in the sutter network, and i have had wonderful experiences with them all. i was diagnosed with stage 3c triple negative breast cancer 2 years ago, and decided on a very aggressive treatment plan. dr nitin rohatgi is my primary oncologist, dr lisa guirgis is my surgical oncologist, and dr lynn hackert is my plastic surgeon for breast reconstruction. they all are wonderful and have given me so much in terms of care, comfort, reassurance, and tools to get through a shocking diagnosis at a young age. i highly recommend the sutter oncology group. they saved my life and are truly a wonderful team.

review:
i am extremely upset! 
i can understand the need to remove all clothing due to potential metallic particles but - i have a laundry list of allergies that was refused because no dye was being employed. 

i am allergic to perfumes and laundry detergents! 

i employed the greatest level of self-control to not itch during the procedure. by tomorrow, i expect an itchy rash. 

the nasal air supply spews perfume! 
i had a raging headache when i departed that i endured driving home in traffic. 
my skin and hair reeked of that fragrance!  
and i showered as soon as i arrived home and still itch! 

the laundry you use has a perfumed ingredient. 

the technician shared with me that another patient complained of having hives - that should tell you that you have a problem with your laundry service that you need to address. 

i worked out an arrangement with morton hospital wherein if i ever had a procedure, they would wash the linens in just water! 

you need to screen patients for this allergy because my concern is that at some point it will escalate to anaphylactic shock due to excessive exposure.  

you also need to enter any allergies into patient records - yes! it matters! 
that's why i bring my lists with me. 
while my pcp teases me that i am allergic to air, i track not only medication allergies, but chemical allergies.

i'm torn on this one. my experiences here have ranged from a minus one to a near four. there is a certain inconsistency that needs to be looked at here. the last time i was there the doctor did me a solid...but i was not impressed with the nursing staff...and i have not been impressed with any of them in any of my personal contacts with them. maybe they are over-worked? maybe they suffer from an empathy deficit? maybe some of them need to find another profession? something needs to change about the attitude of i know what's best for you so you better follow our/my procedures and protocols. doesn't work for me, sorry. back to the doctor. she was kind, empathetic, patient...and she listened...after my partner of 20 years insisted that she listened and give us a diagnosis and a solution to the chronic debilitating pain i was experiencing. (i cannot take opiods...i am allergic to them.) my partner confronted her and said to the doc...what would you do if this was your daughter, your mother,  and she finally stepped up and found a partial answer as to what was going on with me.  i give her credit for finally listening and being willing to do something for me...but isn't that what she is paid a salary to do? it took over five years to find an answer to the chronic pain issues i was having..because this one doctor finally listened.

the theme of this review is "not my problem." this is the attitude i got from day one to when i informed their staff i would no longer be attending any of their facilities due to the seriously lack of internal communication. 

when it came time to receive certain procedures , i was told i had to contact my insurance company to see what is covered - fine - i am happy to take the reigns. but, when you are playing middle man between two organizations and a language you do not speak it becomes disastrous. i won't bore you with the small details, but i communicated back and forth and couldn't get a straight clarification on the coding of the procedure or anything to describe to my insurance what would even be happening. i told them this is the first time i have had to be the one to deal with this type of communication, and they didn't have much to say. 

 i went ahead with things and when i received my bill and had an issue, i called to ask blanchard valley. the billing department said i would have to talk to the nurse. the nurse said she "doesn't handle situations like that." and that i would have to call someone else. that someone else said they would look into it and two weeks later they had not contacted the person they needed to speak with. 

an utter disaster and lack of professionalism at this place. 

i am now with a new health provider and at my appointment, they clarified - "we looked into your insurance and since this is that, it will be coded this way and you will only have to pay a copay." i overheard another conversation - "yeah we coded that wrong and that was our mistake, so we talked to your insurance and got it cleared up. you actually owe this." 

they do not care about their patients. their nurses may, and the individuals you see may be polite, but the organization as a whole couldn't care less about how things go along the way. they're not walking through this with you, they're not invested. you're a transaction and they're blindly going through the motions. 

don't waste your time. 

p.s. this is the first time i have ever been driven to the point of writing a negative review. it's disappointing and careless and people should know.

i really think they need to consider multiple options of seating. in pain management off they offer higher seating or ones with lumbar support. while waiting for my mri appointment the lower seating or narrow arm rests in registering area just isn't comfortable... but i guess i'm the only one there for back issues.

the admin needs to tell pharmaceuticals reps to not park in the back institute parking -- literally limited spots.... i mean can't they get validated since the $4.00 parking fee is so strenuous on their income....

if i can give 0 stars i would for the two times i've been here with both of my sisters having babies i've never dealt with rude customer service then this!!!! waiting in the waiting room for hours and no one telling me nothing wondering what's going on this is not right at all i'm glad i don't live near here you need to hire people who can deal with people and are not rude!!!!!

worst hospital ever i went there with my daughter at 6:00 pm cause she had a pain in her chest they took blood from her ultrasound x-ray etc they put us back in the waiting room to keep us there till midnight waiting on results and no doctor . so i ask the nurse that was there when was the doctor thinking to come in the room to give me the results she says to me she didn't know and that i had to wait longer cause they were taking care of people on critical conditions first. so then i tell her that if by 1:00 am he doesn't come in the room i was gonna take my daughter and she said well u won't get ur results if u leave ur choice and i said can they atleast call me for the results she said no sorry in a rude way. never again i will go into this hospital.

over four years have passed since i was treated like a piece of trash at this hospital when i visited their er.  i didn't think it would affect me this long.  i live near foster and ashland and every time i pass swedish covenant it brings back those memories and then i can't sleep for a few days.  

i am terrified if i have an emergency the ambulance might bring me to swedish.  i tell my kids to make sure i go to weiss, thorek or illinois masonic, or even that little methodist hospital off of ashland.  i think the statue of limitations probably passed but i wish i had sued this hospital.  or at least stood in front of the doorway with some leaflets and a poster with information of what happened to me.  maybe i'll do that this summer. perhaps that will ease some of my emotional pain.

i was in severe pain and had security called on me for being too loud.  i was told not to fall because they weren't going to pick me up.  i was touched and pushed on without my consent.  i was told i had no gall bladder when i never had it removed.  i was treated like a piece of garbage by the male "night nurse" at the counter and the other nurses said they had problems with him before with other patients.  so i am sure the hospital administrators also knew.

they discharged me with a diagnosis of gastritis and told me to take maalox.  a week later i wound up getting my gall bladder removed at illinois masonic, the gall bladder swedish covenant says i didn't have.  and judging by the countless 1 star ratings i doubt things have improved very much.  i used to always doubt how people could claim emotional distress, but after all of this anguish i have been feeling, i completely understand now.

im in cafeteria eating my pretzels and some man rolled in a  large cart. it looked official so i asked what it was; he said just surgery stuff. i said  surgery stuff in (dirty)cafeteria?  and he said "oh yeah". he and a woman in a hospital uniform preceded to organize this stuff onto a cafeteria table. yechhhh!!

my friend is in the hospital and has a serious bacterial infection after the surgery, not surprising after i saw this  place. 

i wouldn't want to be admitted here.  clean your act up, swedish!!

so i get a call from my sister around midnight that she was admitted to swedish covenant er for an allergic reaction. 
this is nothing new in her life as she grew up with severe allergies and asthma and was a regular patient at children's memorial growing up and then northwestern in adulthood. on this occasion she was rushed by ambulance to swedish covenant. this time was also different as she needed an epi pen. 
she came in with my mother who also insisted that her daughter needed an epi pen.
the staff treated my mother and my sister like animals. after my sister was admitted, our mother was denied access to see my sister as the front desk said she was unruly.
then i arrive. i arrived because my sister called me and said she wanted to see me. upon arrival, i am told that i cannot see her because of the way our mother acted. i insisted i had nothing to do with that. that the patient requested my presence. after questioning the rights of the patient, the nurse rolled her eyes at me and threatened to have me removed if i didn't sit down. 
at this point i know my sister requested to be transferred to northwestern. the nurse said this would happen but not one of us would be allowed in the ambulance. which is total hogwash. when i asked if we can be informed when the ambulance would be taking my sister to northwestern, i got another huff and puff and an eyeroll. 
meanwhile my sister is calling and texting me that she wants to see me. 
i ask again what her status is. the nurse says she is undergoing a 'procedure' and again get threatened to get thrown out if i don't sit down. 
apparently this 'procedure' is sedating my sister. which has never been protocol any of the hundreds of times she has been admitted for allergies or asthma. 
when they finally say she can go home, they show me to her room. she was lying in a bed with blood and vomit.

this hospital sucks. the staff treats humans like animals. i will forever hate this place and still believe they ignored the patients right to a visitor.

make sure to bring your bank account number because that is the first thing they ask for, even before registering you.  i went for a test and could not pay for the test in full as i do not have insurance.  sure, they will give you a payment plan and triple the price.  the lady at the financial office was very rude and refuses to work with you.  is either take it or leave it.  zero stars. one only because i have to in order to write the review.

since there are only two long term acute care facilitates in san diego, you don't have many options for your loved one.  once i found out my father would need to go to one, i immediately came to yelp to check the reviews.

i'm of the opinion that a lot more people come to yelp to complain about something versus coming here to praise something so the reviews tend to trend to the negative.  therefore, so people can get my honest opinion, i will do my review on a day-by-day basis.  i'm going to start my rating at 3 stars just so that it doesn't skew the overall scores on here.

admissions - i spoke with april on the phone.  she made me feel very comfortable with this facility.  she gave me all her contact information.  my dad's transition here went very smoothly.  

day 1 - when my dad got to his room on the 4th floor, he was greeted by david and tami.  they did a very thorough check of him and changed all his bandages.
they were great at explaining everything which made me feel like he was in good hands.  

day 2 - i arrived at the room just after 10 a.m.  my father was alone and eating breakfast.  the orders that came over here from ucsd state that he needs to be supervised while eating due to the possibility of choking.  i spoke with the dietician sherry about this and she promised that she would get those orders onto his plan over here.  apparently, that information didn't get transferred to this facility but i'm not sure who's fault that was.

he did get his best nights sleep in about 2 weeks.  he has a private room here and isn't constantly being woken up by the two other patients bells and whistles going off every 10 minutes like at ucsd.

day 3 - the orders for supervised eating are now on his orders here.  his nurses name today is eileen.  she is giving him great care.  she checked an infected wound dressing that wasn't scheduled to be checked until tuesday.  she changed it and is now adding to his chart for it to be checked daily instead every three days.  nurses like her make it so much easier on the family when they leave for the night.

days 4 to 15-  mostly very good nurses here.  there was only one that he didn't seem too happy with one morning when i got there.  but since he's been unable to speak since his stroke, i'm not sure why.

laura the speech therapist was good.  so were the physical therapists.

it's never an easy time having a loved in a care facility.  you're always worried if they are being taken care of well when you're not there.  looking back on the past two weeks here, i'm very satisfied with the overall care of this hospital.

my mom was admitted to this long term care hospital on jan 30th.  she stayed for 3 weeks.  she was on high flow o2 & not doing that well when admitted.  the care here was 5 star from top to bottom!  she loved it here & she kept commenting that everyone was so kind & quick to meet her needs.  the staff here was able to get her from high flow o2 to standard o2 flow - with an even lower setting than she has at home!  she made such amazing progress here & i would highly recommend promise for your aging parents as they recover.

sadly, my one star review will remain. now st. luke did apologize for all their screw ups (such as leaving a pegtube in my mother's stomach way past its removal date), and we negoiated that st. luke should pay for the shuttle to get my mother to and from the hospital to get the pegtube out. granted...st. luke did provide the ride.

however...upon arriving, the shuttle driver wasn't informed on where to bring mom. the admissions team had no idea about the situation, and admitted that 'they' (the nurses and doctors) do not communicate much to admissions! the surgeon apologised at least, but i'm not sure if he is to blame at all.

also, mom became car sick and had an accident on herself. the nurses did not clean mom well as my father soon found out.

the outpatient surgery was successful, but it would appear that nothing has changed at st. luke as far as having absolutely poor communication amongst their staff. there is still no team work at this facility, and this is bad because your communication can either save your patients' lives or end their lives. it still appears as if st. luke does not take their patients' seriously; therefore, i can't recommend this facility to no one.

sadly i have another review to write. however, it is a review that is as full of praise as my previous one. new injury, new need for surgery, and once again taken care of wonderfully. read my old review. i really can't praise northwest hills surgical hospital staff too highly.
