i have been hospitalized many times and without a doubt temecula valley hospital is the best; from the time i arrived at the emergency room until the time that i was discharged everyone show that they really care for you. i will give them a five stars. because to me they are uniqual.

i wish i could give 10 stars! went there last night for an emergency situation and from start to finish they were awesome. check in staff ( jillean) ran thru some tests and we were in a room very fast. everyone was concerned, kept us informed and we couldn't have had better care. by the time we left i felt like we had made about 10 new friends! thank you to all the er staff and x-ray folks working last night. all went well and super happy i live close to this facility.

drove 120 miles to visit with my 95 year old father. he is sick and his condition is up and down. well there is a new policy about visitations. only 2 visitors per day. that's not 2 at a time but 2 a day. my family is flying in from across the country to see him because we don't know if he will ever get to go home. because of the policy we will have to choose one of his six children to visit for the day. the other visitor will be his wife, our mother, of course. this policy is too restrictive and is unfair for families in the situation we are in. the management at temecula valley hospital needs to get a more caring attitude.

this place is not a good hospital.  go anywhere else!  avoid their emergency if you can!  i am not a good patient but their service is horrible and if you call, you will never get through to the billing department.  you must leave several messages before a call back.  to call and ask questions afterwards, they will not take those questions.  you must go to  your own doctor.  what if you do not have one???  just go to inland valley or the other hospitals around this area.  avoid them.

change of heart about this hospital. once again my mother went to visit my baby brother who live there one temecula a couple of weeks before thanksgiving.. she ended up in the  emergency in temecula hosp. she needed an emergency surgery to place a pace maker for her heart..my sis and i flew  from san jose california to be there for her through surgery. i was blown away how the change around of professionalism in this hospital. i'm giving y'all a 5 star!  the nurses and doctors are amazing!! my mother surgery went well and  we were very happy on the out come. shes now back him with us fully recovered!! thank you soo much for everything!!! my mother's name is maria escobar shes send her love and big thank you!!! god work is amazing!! merry christmas & happy new year!!

this hospital is very unprofessional. they put you in the hallway with a iv on your arm and asking you kind of personal questions while other patients and staff are hearing you talk very clearly. they are violating your privacy so there is no patient doctor privacy in temecula valley hospital...... and they are more worried about to get you insurance information sending you through 4 different registration then paying attention that you are really sick to help you. but for me the most uncomfortable thing was that they placed me in the hallway and asked me personal questions just like 3rd world countries which i have seen when i was deployed. everyone was rude didn't give the attention the way they suppose to. and no respect whatsoever for your privacy very disappointing

terrible experience on 02/24/2020 night. went in at around 9:30. i let the staff know my daughter was experiencing flu symptoms because they have a sign asking patients to let staff know immediately which was still pointless. she had a 102 fever and after speaking with the doctor she stated they would run a chest x-ray, test for the flu and get her started on an iv shortly. she mentioned there were no beds but hallway space. we sat back down in the waiting area. while waiting sandra from registration called us and i was about to get up and approach her when all of the sudden she saw someone she knew in the waiting area and completely left me just standing there like an idiot! she began chatting with her friend and her friend was waiting to see someone in bed 10. well sandra gladly walked her back there and just literally left me there without a word! she returned shortly and apologized but i still found what she did was unprofessional and rude. almost 2 1/2 hours went by and as i sat there i listened to the employees sitting at the entrance laugh and chit chat about their personal lives including sandra. i felt that was also unprofessional given there are people in that area sick, and waiting hours to be helped. so i finally decided to get up and go. i let the two girls at check in desk know how upset i was with the wait even to start the iv and get my daughters fever down. allison v very rudely replied with "i'm sorry you feel that way but okay" she gave me a form to sign stating i was leaving against medical advice and death can occur etc. after i had told her i was going to take my daughter to another hospital upon leaving. their staff except for the doctor was unprofessional and rude. hospitals are supposed to be about patient care and this hospital definitely lacks that! i came to rancho springs as soon as i left temecula valley hospital and my daughter was given a bed not even 5 minutes after checking in and their staff showed they actually cared about her well-being. i'll never again go back to temecula valley hospital. also, it's dirty! there were tissues on the ground and the floor was so dirty. i'm so disappointed and will definitely look into filing a complaint.

i don't even want to give this hospital a bad review. i've never ever had any problems here. but tonight...tonight is the night. this review is literally based off of one staff member.  celine from x-ray. rude! rude! rude! 
i'm here tonight (1/25/2020). it's 9:55 pm. we arrived at 8pm. my 4 yr old daughter was roughhousing with her cousins who are the same age as her. end result, her toe looks like its broken. we get to the hospital...triage checks her out, says she's going to order x-rays & then we wait for the results. at 9:30 pm my daughter is called by one of the male x-ray techs. as he's walking us to x-ray, here comes this other x-ray tech, (celine) ...saying, "i don't have the xrays ready! why are you bringing them back?? they're not even on my list!!" just on & on...he responds, "uhhh you should...a 4 yr old" she says, "no. they're not." then they ask the name of my daughter. i tell them & celine says, "well she's at the bottom of the list!!! i have people ahead of her!!!" she's saying this all the way to the x-ray. once at x-ray, he turns to me & says, "now i have to ask this before you enter...is there any possibility you could be pregnant?" before i could even answer, celine turns around looks at me & says, "you can wait out here! dad only!!!" & shuts the door. my gosh. 
i mean, i get it. if the other x-ray tech made a mistake, then i think that's something she needs to address away from the patient, that was completely unprofessional of her to discuss her frustrations in front of us. she made us feel like we did something wrong. 
if you ever have to get x-rays at this hospital, i sincerely hope you do not have to deal with celine. the hospital was very packed tonight...i understand if this is overwhelming to staff members. but you don't have to show it to the patients. in my opinion, celine is a very  unhappy person or unhappy with her career choice.

i had the unfortunate experience of needing to be hospitalized.  the staff and treatment i received was world class.  every doctor, nurse and administrator was incredibly attentive.  i feel incredibly privileged to have a care facility of this caliber in our community.

i would like to thank john e , the volunteer at temecula valley hospital . he was super sweet , patient , and kind  . i really liked his hospitality and you can tell he  enjoys volunteering  he should be able to aaccept tips
my mom and i were here over the christmas holiday and i just wanted to give jinia in admitting and registration a shoutout - she was so friendly, even at 7am on the day after christmas!

my review is of the er only. i specifically went to this hospital because of the good things i had heard but as long as i'm still standing and breathing i will never go here again. both visits at this hospital one in the morning and one at night and i had the same experience. both visits with potential life threatening situations and yet every single person i came in to contact with from the front desk to triage to the nurses to the x-ray techs were all complete assholes. not one single person was capable of smiling, showing compassion, or caring about my wants or needs as a patient. bunch of money collecting robots with attitudes. it was so bad i finally walked out the second visit. and i walked out with my veins in my arms destroyed and bruised because nobody seems to know how to draw blood or administer an iv properly and instead of listening to the patient let their egos get in the way. there is only one positive thing i can say about this hospital and that is that they are definitely thorough leaving no stone unturned. however, if you are self pay or have horrible insurance this is not a good thing. instead of just running necessary tests they do everything!! there is no need to get another urine sample when that person was just there 15 hours earlier and you took one. they don't care. never in my life have i met an entire hospital or office where everybody was an ass until now. it must be an office culture. i also have never met a hospital who questions your legitimacy of a heart attack with utter sarcasm when you complain of chest pains and a numb left arm! isn't the rule of thumb to go to the er in these instances?? am i interrupting your coffee break??! a hospital where people are sick, scared and in life threatening situations is the one place you would expect people who care.

after my visit to mortan plantt hospital i realized how much of a joke our health care system is. apparently morton plant is a nicer facility compared to others like state facility but still. after talking to multiple patients and nurses!!! i learned the only way to get out is to lie to them or serve a jail like sentence. you could be actually suicidal and depressed butt that doesn't matter the dr only meets with you for 5 mins in the mornings to see how u feel and then dope you on more drugs and have you a sit in  ah. empty room all day. they don't actually care here. go somewhere else for help

valet was wearing perfume so they couldn't get in my car- i have severe allergies to it. so i staggered 3 blocks from the parking garage while having an adverse drug reaction to a prescription medication. after 20 min i had to inquire if a registrar was going to check me in, no one was waiting besides me and the registrar was not around. once i complained my vitals were done and then i was put in a different waiting area for 5 hours. i seen a pa- not even a physician, for 4 minutes and then sent back to the waiting area like cattle. then the nurse brought me discharge papers and i hadn"t  even spoke to the physician or the pa yet. when i had asked the nurse if they were going to at least review my test results with me, she mumbled and walked away. a different nurse came after another 30 minutes, put me behind a curtain and the pa came in for less than 2 minutes and just said that they're changing antibiotics. no conversation of test results. 
i sat upright in a wheelchair for 6 hours total while having an adverse reaction to a drug. i couldn't walk and could barely pick up my head. 
to be left on a waiting room with no care for hours on end is neglect. i needed to lie down. i begged but was still told no. 
this is the worst experience i have ever had at a hospital and will never be back. they treat you live live stock here, not human beings. shame.

ok... i was transferred via ambulance from bardmoor to morton plant clearwater because of chest pains, and pains between shoulder blades. i am 60 years old, fairly athletic, but i knew something was terribly wrong. dr. lin made the decision to prep me for stent surgery. the wait was not going to be that long, but i was laying in a bed, bells going off on the machines, four nurses came in and asked me how i was feeling. i said ok. they knew something was going on. a couple of seconds later i flatlined, actually died for over one minute. the next thing i know it felt like a grenade had gone off in the room, they had brought me back to life with a defibrillator. i was in the hospital for eight days, as a matter fact i just got out of the hospital three nights ago. these guys are incredible, every doctor in there was very supportive, every nurse, nurse practitioner, tech, you name it. i hesitate naming names, because three or four of those nights were a little fuzzy and i do not remember anything, and i apologize for those of you i forgot your name. but i would like to thank from the bottom of my heart, every cardiologist doctor there, as well as: joe, henry, planco, brusem, brian, usuf, kayla, krysta, erin, jamie and dallas. one of the cardiologist told me and my sister that he did not understand how i survived, again i apologize for not remembering  some of your names. dr. lin is now my cardiologist, as i just got back from from my follow-up appointment with her. she is absolutely outstanding. if i could ever humanly do anything for any of you people, , i will do it.

this is not a rehab center people, this is a nursing home. lots of senior citizens who are there to make their legs and arms stronger that is all.
some of the patients have alzheimer's, some have dementia and the staff is overwhelmed and indifferent.
the meds are not monitored, they are not given to the patient in a timely manner. you basically need to hire someone to be on top of the nurses and the workers. you press the nurse bottom and it takes for ever to get help. someone goes on the microphone and asks the nurses to  help the patient, but for ten minutes no one shows up. 
physical therapy is a joke, there are not enough of them for all the patients.

i recently gave birth to a healthy baby boy at kaiser vv. due to some unforeseen issues (my iron levels) i ended up staying a week in the labor & delivery / postpartum ward. the staff was exceptional and took fantastic care of us. they truly made us feel like family. 
shoutout to mama deb, audrey, raj, terri, dr le, and all the other exceptional doctors and nurses (i could go on and on listing everyone) that took care of my growing family. we truly appreciate every single one of you that helped us go from a family of two to a family of three.
i absolutely love my healthcare setup with kaiser, from joanna, elizabeth to dr zolinger,i seriously couldn't be happier.

so upset with their medical directory. called 4 times to try and get in touch with their emergency room. first two times i was hung up on, ...ok maybe it was an accident. third time they never answered, and fourth time i was hung up on as soon as she heard my voice. i have to keep calling because i'm looking for a family member so i'm hoping to get another answer. so beyond upset with the service abby provided. she answered every time.

i had an upper endoscopy yesterday and the experience was really the best that it could be, given what an unpleasant procedure it is. i went without the sedation and was a little scared about being able to breathe when the nurse put in the mouthguard and then the scope. but the nurses and doctor talked me through it and said i was doing great. it was over in just a couple of minutes! i thought everyone was very kind and i felt i was in good hands the whole time.

kaiser is the worst medical system.  they don't care about their patients. they don't care about their employees.  every employee is overworked. it's almost impossible to get an appointment when you need help. especially bad is there a behavioral health. especially dr. fudge. they don't listen to you. and they don't give you appointments when you are having serious problems. they should be ashamed of themselves.

my elderly mother has been rushed to this hospital's er and subsequently admitted for congestive heart failure flare-ups and other health issues numerous times since 2017. i've been very involved in her care as her patient advocate and dpoa (durable power of attorney). as a concerned son, i always aim to collaborate with the care staff. each time my mom and i have engaged this hospital's healthcare services, we have enjoyed a deeper understanding of just how difficult it is to provide 100% care, 24/7. the er is a fascinating and unpredictable mix of chaos and coordination. yet with the challenges of providing care for the never-ending flow of patients, this hospital's er has been extraordinary in my view. thank you to trisha (charge nurse) and her team for keeping my mom safe and stable until her admit to the hospital was possible. beds were limited due to the swell of flu cases in sd county, i assume. mom and i had to wait a long time, but we got in and once admitted, my mom continued to receive excellent care from the team on the 5th floor - north. 

during my mother's 5 day recovery, we continued to receive the best care from vangie & norma (charge nurses), kyah (rn) and oliver (cna). my mother's team of doctors also delivered the most excellent care. dr niguidula (you're a rock star!), dr maa chip (a+++), dr fernandez and dr lim, thank you all for your stellar attention and expertise. my mom can breathe again. much appreciation to you all! thank you paradise valley hospital! 

for those family members who read this review and have had different experiences, please remember that these facilities have protocols that must be followed and limitations on what can be provided. our health care industry in the usa is always evolving, and insurance is like navigating a never-ending sea of red tape and bureaucracy. you must advocate for yourself or for the loved ones who can't advocate for themselves. be patient and polite, when possible. your nurses and doctors care... and they're only human. team work makes the dream work!

i was very impressed the first day when i visited this hospital to be with my son during his wife's labor.  however, i never felt so humiliated when i was basically pushed out the room by the charge nurse sharon.  we were told by the doctor that i could be there during the entire labor  and we told the nurse who was taking care of my daughter-in-law but she went and told the charge nurse that i was in the room.  two minutes before the baby arrived, this charge nurse came and literally pushed me out while i was tryng to explained that the doctor authorized for me to be there.  she was not friendly from day one, i work in the health industry and i don't let my employees or myself disrespect families the way she did to me.  she needs to find another job where she doesn't have to deal with clients or perhaps her boss needs to send her to a customer service training .  horrible experience!!!  no wonder this hospital has so poor reviews.

i do have to say that the nurse in training was wonderful, caring and very sweet.  i will come back later to edit this review and make sure to add her name maybe she can take the place of this "charge nurse" who did nothing then come in the room twice, one to check the iv machine and the other to push me out the room. i hope this review gets read so they can talk to her and teach her how to treat clients with respect.  

sharon if you are the "charge nurse" then set an example to your team, because your helper who took care of my daughter-in-law is very knowledgeable but she is following your lead.  like i said i will definitely call your boss to share my

the worst service ever the front desk nurse anthony is the worst came in with my nephew he had a bad fever and he had us wait 5 hours with my nephew running a high fever when i asked him if we were going to be seen he was a total jerk laughed in my face a patient asked him for water and he refused to give it to her this hospital should be called death valley instead of paradise valley there was a patient laying down on the seats crying in pin and she went and told him to get up that he could not be laying down. they need to fire anthony immediately he is in emergency as soon as you walk in. worst damn service ever this happend on december 30, 2019 and i was waiting from 7:30 to about 12 pm in the emergency waiting room

this hospital is the worst. i went in yesterday to the er around 5pm because my sister was experiencing bleeding (she's pregnant)  and they didnt get her in a room until 10pm. this doesn't seem like an er, more like urgent care where you're expected to wait longer. after being there for 7 hours+ all they told my sister was she was bleeding and that she has a threatened miscarriage but they don't know why. what the hell??? and while she was there they inserted an iv which was connected to absolutely nothing. the nurse that took in discharge papers was rude and didn't even explain the process of what to expect. the other nurses in the area were laughing in the hallway and the doctor even joked around about a very sick patient. the patient was yelling from his pain and as the doctor exited our room he giggled and said "let me go save that guys life". this hospital is filthy, unprofessional and seriously don't give a damn about their patients. if you're seriously ill expect to die here.

i'm sitting in the emergency room currently brought in my boyfriend who is having chest pain , dizziness, headache, cough and fever. we have been in the waiting room for more than 2 hours has not been triaged. i understand wait times may be horrible but not when you come in with symptoms that should have been cared for right away. still triage nurse (male)has passed in other patients before whom have arrived after , it may not be on first come first serve , but the symptoms are something that he should have been atleast triaged for already. it's very upsetting to see how the staff is here as well, not just to us, but i have seen how they have been very rude and disrespectful to many other patients that have came in, it's very sad to see how horrible customer service and patient care is given here. i work in healthcare myself , i would never treat someone as disrespectful and rude to patients. especially if they are coming into my facility for care. the triage nurse male in here as ignored patients who have asked him questions, he has talked back in way that a profesional healthcare personnel shouldn't be taking towards his patients! i saw how a supervisor male came out to speak to a patient he was very rude himself, they are the healthcare professionals they should be explaining things to their patients not just telling them to leave go elsewhere , because the person is sick they are frustrated and having to deal with a nurse who is very rude  and is not explaining any of your concerns makes it more frustrating,sending a supervisor out because he couldn't "handle " a situation or answer some patient questions because all he has been doing is chatting in the back, i saw him playing with a ball. it's sad it's upsetting to see horrible care ! and this was not done to myself it was me watching how they treat their patients that are coming in. and asking for their care.

i needed to write this to help the next person reading all these reviews with their eyes wide open. let's get this out of the way--it's a surgical center. not a hospital. don't expect a long drawn out time there. expect efficient expert care. they do a lot of surgeries and it is an in and out process. yes, it's $7 to pay for parking, my doctor's office forewarned me though. i don't care about $7, some people will. second, i was called with my cost, so this also wasn't a surprise. next, the front desk was great, and again efficient. i was called back minutes later and everyone was amazing! my waiting area had all of my paperwork, bags with my name on it. everything was neatly prepared. i felt cared for, they looked out for my needs and every person came to introduce themselves (nurse, anesthesiologists, pre-op nurse, iv guy), ask questions, and assure me that i was in the best care. i mean really, each person really listened to me, was patient, and attentive. they explained every single thing down to what they were giving me. my doctor came and he was great, gave me some instructions and assured me again, that all was well. i didn't wait long, in fact, we went in before i was scheduled. my pre paperwork actually said that the schedule can change per the centers discretion, so i was prepared if something changed. everyone in the or was comforting and kind--and funny. i went to sleep imagining i was in miami getting a cocktail--it was a cocktail all right--i was out cold. anyhow, i had some pain in recovery when i woke up, but my post op nurse covered that right away. no, slow moving, let me check this or that. she checked the papers, got me something and helped me get to a place to leave. i was out of there a bit later and i say i was there for about four hours total. yes, i understand surgery is an anxiety filled situation that you want to linger and cry about, but they don't give you a chance to worry, they get you feeling better, and home in your own bed to recover at your own pace! advocate for yourself, ask questions, pray and feel better!

the hospital where i gave birth to 2 babies and recently had an outpatient surgery. great hospital. the nurses and staff here are all so friendly. when i had 2 c-section surgeries, the nurses and my doc was always checking on us to see if we needed anything and everyone i came into contact with was very friendly. great bedside manners and always put me at ease. 

i was here recently for an outpatient surgery and hate being in hospitals and was not looking forward to my surgery. the nurse brenda took me to the back to start prepping me. she was so friendly and made jokes to help me feel at ease and not scared. wonderful bedside manners. she explained everything with what she's doing and the whole flow of what is going to happen. great hospital!!

this review is based solely on my experience with labor and delivery.  i've been to l&d a few times during my pregnancy but this time was different.  i was five weeks early and didn't think my water had broken but it had. from the time they told me i would be having my baby five weeks early and delivering that day.......i received the best support, attention, care and professionalism ever. i'm not sure how they could have possibly hired the most talented staff around but they were the absolute best. from the dr who delivered my baby, the nurses that took care of me, the baby nurses who took care of my baby, the staff who brought my meals, the janitorial staff and everyone in between...  they made me feel comfortable and cared for.  i left the hospital with a happy,  healthy baby and i am grateful for that.

the hospital staff doctors and nurses in medical are the best.  the emergency room is a totally different issue and i wold recommend going somewhere else like sentara bell harbour and then transport to obici if heeded.  er is unorganized and painfully slow.  expect 5-7 hours if they get busy.   once admitted the best hospital staff and nurses treat you with respect and kindness.  they go out of their way to make sure patients are comfortable.

my review is specifically for my labor and delivery experience. i was having my first child, so needless to say i was nervous and had no idea what to expect. my labor and delivery nurses were marina and madison and they were phenomenal!!!! they made my labor and delivery experience so positive and memorable for myself, my husband and our families. they were so attentive and on the ball with everything! they were both so friendly and made me feel comfortable immediately. marina was very encouraging and she made sure i was constantly being preoccupied and not concentrating on contractions, which was awesome and very needed! i am so happy that i had these 2 to bring my son into the world and i couldn't have asked for a better experience! all thanks to marina and madison

i was directed by my child's pediatrician to head directly to onslow memorial hospital's er because they suspected a ruptured appendix and they even called ahead to warn them we were heading in and get the surgeon on call ready. we sat 7 and a half hours in the er before we saw a doctor and even longer before we saw a surgical team who wanted to get my child in the or within 20 min and we would be "delaying care" if we didn't get my child to the or immediately, plus my child was not stable enough to have been transferred. we subsequently agreed to have the or team take him into emergency surgery and spent many days in that horrid place with sub par care before i had my child transferred out to continue care and get stable and home. i wouldn't even have given them one star if not for the surgical team nurses and the anesthesiologist. do not go to onslow memorial hospital if you can make the drive to wilmington or greenville for your care.

i brought my daughter and myself in because we thought we may have caught the flu. we were out of town during christmas. so we got in and immediately experienced one of the most awful experiences from rude female nurses. i was asked if i took drugs several times and responded no each time. i am sick so i do look rough but no need to ask me 5 times if i am a drug addict!. my 4 year old daughter the whole time hearing this and the rude nurse saying we "should have" gotten the flu shot. they kept pushing the flu shot on us and we just don't do the flu shot for our own reasons. my family does not do flu shots but we do vaccinate other shots. so then the test was said to be 50% accurate. do you know how much money we spent to come to the er!? the nurse said i waited to long to come in treating me like a crap mom not knowing we were traveling out of town. then she demanded i take my daughter today to her her pediatrician to get her flu shot which if she had any sense she would know they dont give you the flu shot if you are already sick. so we met some of the most arrogant and prideful staff who obviously are more concerned with being right or thinking they are right than patient care and empathy! we will drive to the base hospital next time and will not come back here to the er.
this place dont be fooled by the name of it being in the heart of buckhead this place needs to be closed down and remodeled.

i went in for test results for a mass on my pancreas but by the time i got to the doctors office i was in severe pain. they sent me down to the er where all my troubles started. 1st off i told them the pain was my back not my abdominal area and that i had a mri scheduled across the street in 3 hours. well they ignored that and ordered a cat scan and when i couldn't lay flat on the table they (x-ray techs) were looking at each other laughing like i was faking it. well after they finally got the pics with my legs bent up they said oh we got what we needed as if they found nothing. well 1hr later they come back & get me for a mri on my spine. mmm?? well what do you know they find a severe herniated disc & when the tech is taking me back to my room she is jerking the wheel chair hard as she can as if trying to hurt me. after i ask if she could not be so rough she said sorry & started even harder. when i tried to complain to my nurse she said oh she's having a bad day. well ill finish this on another day of what happened after they got me to a room upstairs 12hrs later.

this is more for my doctors office than the  hospital.  i will include the hospital. my doctor is dr. amy buchanan and she is the bomb!!!!!!   atomic!  bomb. com. have been seeing her for over ten years and no matter what my issue is she is there  to make it a non issue. she makes sure that i am  a part of the process. she teaches me as she diagnoses me. love that about her. 

the hospital i is blah.  needs better signage bit overall it's there for the community. i wish they would add pediatric dentistry.

my 76 year old father was admitted here for gallbladder surgery suddenly and we were worried because we weren't familiar with the hospital as my family had just moved nearby. naturally i was worried reading some of the negative reviews but we had a pleasant experience. the or room might be different than er but staff and nurses were very friendly and accommodating! the surgeon himself came out to let us know of a successful surgery and he was very vibrant and nice as well. clean facility, could use more light and maybe some decor in lobby waiting areas but all in all a good experience!!

do not have any surgical procedures performed at this hospital! my husband underwent wrong site surgery at this hospital. i gained copies of all his records - proving that the surgeon admitted he did not perform the correct procedure. i filed a grievance with the medical board and was basically told "too bad - pay all the bills anyway." terrible hospital. incompetent staff. stay away.

* my grievance was filed through patient relations, which is the only way to file a grievance. i am unsure why the hospital responded to my review by asking me to contact patient relations again. further proof of their ineptitude. just trying to show the public that they are "helping" but it is no help at all.

horrible service! er nurse ivette was really rude! i do not like going to hospitals unless necessary. i have been sick for two weeks now. my primary doctor called me today and per cdc regulations she was told i should go to the er and get tests done. i followed her instructions and headed to gotlieb. i didn't expect them to test me for coronavirus. because obviously they need to rule everything else out first..... the nurse insisted that she didn't understand why my doctor would sent me there and said they couldn't do much for me. not just was she not careful when doing my swaps but she has a nasty attitude the whole time, acting like i was a bother. after waiting a while a provider came in to my room and i explained how rude her nurse had been and that i did not appreciate how harsh she did my swabs and the things she said. she apologized for the nurses attitude and insisted it was good that i went and that they would do the tests necessary. she left and the next person that visited me was the same nurse with her smirk face on to discharge me. they couldn't do anything for me and i should follow up with my primary health provider. she is a rude person and obviously in the wrong profession. also i understand that there is a lot going on with the whole virus thing but all i want is to go back to work!!!! and i need to do everything i'm asked to go back to work... our health system is failing and we need better service not this crappy hospital . next time i'll just go elsewhere never again

my dear wife has just completed a 2 month stay.  she went in on a guerney for rehab to regain her strength, and walked out on her own power. during her stay, she had several problems to address - the most acute of all her throwing up everything she ate or drank. while, she had outpatient appointments at a urologist, and oncologist. a blood transfusion was required at another facility 7:00am in the morning. the transportation to and from these places was always on time, and immediate response. the staff, nurses, and admin were pleasant and caring. my wife used the "help needed" red button quite often and received quick attention. the facility is always kept spotless, there is a beehive of work going on. activity rooms, physical exercise - monthly calendars of events. it is an older facility, but top notch service and care. in my 2 months there (i visited my wife everyday, sometimes 2 times a day) - i got to know and observe the staff - they conducted themselves as professionals with a mission to provide the best care for their patients. so, my highest recommendation and thanks to the folks at apache junction health center.

we took our 10mo daughter here three days after visiting polyclinic madison.  not only was the facility very clean, well designed and staffed with friendly people,  but the quality of care provided was light years beyond what we've received since she was born. this place is great -- i wish we could use it for general pediatrics.

review:

the small little hallway of waiting rooms are awful though. these box size rooms are the most unpleasant places to wait. no windows, no tv, just a small couch & a table with chairs.

review:
was hit above the eye. had a deep gash about 3 inches long that was bleeding very badly and needed stitches. it was sun late afternoon so ended up going to this er with a bloody face. wait time was listed as approx 30min. well i was there for over 4hrs and was only triaged initially where they take your blood pressure and temp and send you back to the waiting room to be seen by a doctor. 

went to the check in desk to inquire several times and was always told, they will see me shortly. i understand there are emergencies that take priority but 4hrs with a bleeding, deep open wound seemed ridiculous. also at the time, i didn't know if it was just the gash or if i also had a fracture. i ended up leaving this er untreated.

close it down!!, poor front desk skills,security ,and the way  the patient is being handled. malpractice must be common in there.management never gets back to you for complaints .so its just a matter of time till it's close down -5 review for not caring for the patient!

janice hamilton is not a medical professional, and tempe st. luke is a terrifying medical facility, i am so concerned that such a dishonest hospital exists. on 2/8 i had a ski accident that resulted in extreme left knee pain, and the inability to walk with my left leg. i'm a 30-year-old active person, that has never had a major injury, so i was very scared, to say the least. i made an appointment with my pcp on 2/10, and got a x-ray. i wasn't able to get an appointment for an mri until 2/14. i was so afraid that i was making my injury worse because the pain was so extreme, it was making me physically ill, so i decided to go to the er to get answers on 2/13. i was met with condescension, lies, and no treatment, however, i received a bill for not getting treated. when i went to tempe st. luke, my intake nurse, rachel collins, checked with a doctor in the er  to ensure i could get an mri. when i met with janice hamilton, the first thing she said to me was that i couldn't get an mri for a swollen knee, that i had to wait 4 - 6 weeks before doing anything. which is interesting because she never offered to provide me with an exam to verify anything she was saying to me. i told janice that  i was told that i could, and she rudely responded with that tempe st. luke does not have mris, so i said i would leave, and do i need to pay? she rudely shared, of course, you are at the er. this exchange probably lasted 2 minutes. i left and shared my experience with the risk director cindy price. janice and cindy, falsified the situation that took place. my medical records state that i had minimal pain, with no knee swelling, and that i refused an exam. i was never offered an exam. why should i pay for something i did not receive?  how can medical professionals get away with falsifying paperwork? i attended my 2/14 mri, and found out i had a torn acl and fractured tibial plateau. how could my left knee not be swollen, with such major injuries? now, cindy price is saying because i saw my pcp and had an mri appointment, my lack of care at tempe st. luke was warranted. i am so disappointed and scared that people like janice and cindy have power over people's health. please do not see janice if you have an injury or medical situation, she is unprofessional, and will lie to save face, and tempe st. luke will back her up, with more lies. really, i would advise to not go to tempe st. luke to anyone. i have lived in tempe for 10 years, no one i know has had a good experience here. i should have never gone, but i was desperate for answers, and my desperation led me to a horrible experience. please don't be like me, even if you are in immense pain, please go to another hospital. i really don't want this type of emotional and physically draining experience to happen to anyone else. if anyone would like to talk more or see the paperwork i have from the hospital, i am happy to share. i am in absolute shock about how i was treated, and how a hospital can get away with completely lying on official medical forms. also, if anyone else has gone through this, please let me know what steps you took. i am taking action now, but i am curious, and i just hope this doesn't happen again to someone seriously hurt, and scared.

next day discharge, the nurse takes the iv, drain and all that good stuff out and throws it in the regular trash. blood and bodily fluids in the regular trash. they  are supposed to go in a red bin and disposed of properly. infection control nightmare. no red bins, needle holders in her room. they opened this wing  because they had nowhere to put these patients and they didn't have the proper set up and put us in a dangerous situation. violated policy's and procedures, rules and guidelines   staff was scrambling everywhere was ridiculous and no phones. so when they pulled the drain the nurse that threw the medical waste i in regular trash rips a stitch out. didn't stop the bleeding nor bandage it. my parents didn't find this out until they were home because when she woke her mattress was covered in blood. it was so much blood they couldn't have it professionally cleaned they had to throw away and buy another mattress. elderly couple on fixed income. our experience was a complete nightmare. i do not advice to go here. they are an embarrassment to the medical community.

" he's a coward for making such a very ignorant comment. there is a bunch of thing i'd never do so to me they crossed the line.

i'd suggest this hospital it's a really good hospital i went here for an emergency  and they got me in right away and was able to go home the next hour they are fast with doing things and the correct way i've always been going to this hospital they are good

review: both my husband and i have been patients of dr. feder for about 30 years. dr. feder is wonderful. he is kind, caring, highly perceptive and communicates quite clearly. one may have to wait a bit, much less so than in the past, but it was because other patients were having medical emergencies. we know this because each of us has needed to been seen very quickly a few times in the past, and dr. feder and his staff have always been accommodating. he is indispensable and a treasure. we always recommend him heartily to friends.

we brought my son here to check on a sprained ankle. the staff was so helpful in assisting us with choosing whether to be self pay or file through insurance (because i needed what was cheapest!) she gave me a number to call and explained to file it through insurance if it was too much money. we were seen within 10 minutes of arriving (which i know is luck). we got x-rays done and got a verdict within the hour! the doctor was so sweet. also, my child's name was still "boy" from whenever he was born. i asked for a number so i could change it (because another urgent care told me i had to call). the front desk informed me to just fill out some paperwork and she could change it! it was a great experience and i'll be driving to vintage park texas children... even though we are a little closer to a different location. they even offered my son play-doh to play with while he waited!
fac_name: Texas Children's Urgent Care - The Vintage

review: if i could leave a zero i would. this place is poorly ran and incredibly insufficient. more people standing around than actually working. it took more than 3 hours to be seen. they select who they want doesn't matter when you arrived. this place is terrible it's better to drive an hour than go here. stay away! i will never be back!
fac_name: Texas Children's Urgent Care - The Vintage

review:

weekend appt. given to us - limited security, no valet, no help at main desk

i was a patient in the er thursday  3/5/20. i had been sick for almost 4 weeks. i went to urgent care  x2,  my family physician 1. meds didn't work. from the moment i arrived the staff were professional and helpful. from the registration rep, to the triage nurse the ed nurse. lab tech , radiology tech all were very caring and helpful. dr benevides was excellent.  my diagnosis was confirmed and i am feeling so much better. thank you !

i had to go to er at chapman for a obstruction in my stomach and the nurse was rude and when i was grimacing in pain, she stated " settle down!"

             this is by far the worst organization i have ever dealt with. i had received a bill for $3100.00 6 months after discharge, they hit me up for $2000 while i was in my hospital bed already! i called the billing department to get my bill audited because the codes were excessively over charged. code 74176 avg cost $488, chapman billed me $4878 and code 74250 avg cost $123, chapman charged me $1132. i had some legitimate concerns and just wanted to make sure this was correct. i talked to george employee #je6 and ask him to look into the charges to make sure they are correct. he told me they will have the bill audited and get back to me and not to do anything until they do, i specifically ask him if this will go to collections and he responded:" no we will contact you when the audit is done".

called the number that responded to my post. i explained my story and gave details the representative said he would look into it and call me back for sure. no response or explanation 6 months later!! pathetic customer service and this place is a joke!!

thank you all so much! along with the paraamedics and firefighters. knowing your are there is a blessing  and comforting. amanda you were amazing! i'm sorry she's the only name i remember but dr. b too! and everyone else there last night! thank you for keeping me alive. i wish everyone could appreciate the work you do, you're all the best and the world needs to know!

they don't keep you very long but last time i was there with flu symptoms the doctor came in told me they will perfo tests and i never saw him again the nurse came in with the results and send me to the pharmacy if it wasn't for me to ask what was that i had i will never knew i had bronchitis...  that was very disappointing  we as patients need to know what we have hog long we will be under medication, if is contagious etc. i felt they treat me like an other number.

avoid this for profit disaster of a hospital at all costs! it has been rates as one of the top 100 hospitals in the us with the most negative patient ratings (center of medicare and medicaid). the routinely get cited for inappropriate readmissions. i went to the emergency for severe back and hip pain. they did x-rays and an mri and 'found nothing'. a few days later i passed out at the mall and was taken by ambulance to hoag hospital in newport beach. horrified when they told me the pain i was experiencing was from kidney cancer. i was admitted to hoag that evening and had my kidney removed two days later. finished treatment and am doing well. global should be shut down.

my dad was in for a procedure and had extensive bleeding afterward.  the bleeding started in recovery after the surgeon had left.  nurses called and we had dad kept over night for observation.    i needed to have a cbc because dad is anemic as was still losing blood.   they agreed to the cbc but it was scheduled for morning.  when i said i needed it done stat because of his anemia he might have needed a transfusion before morning.  side note:  dad is 89, rebuilding strength in anyone is hard but more difficult with his age.  the cbc was ordered and they checked it every 4 hours!  by 8 pm the bleeding subsided and i was comfortable leaving my dad in the competent hands of the nursing staff.  dr. malhortra and nursing staff patricia, mark and lori were amazing.    i love hoag hospitals and was really not expecting much being "stuck" at chapman.  this is a staff that was amazing.  totally exceeded my expectations.
thank you.

i don't want to get into specifics, but basically, think on all the horror stories and complaints people have about kaiser and then realize that this hospital run by scripps this is the complete opposite.

this misrepresentation has caused billing delays and confusion as their billing is not done through the scripps medical hospital encinitas.  these 3rd party providers tag the patient's credit record with collection accounts for payments and circumvent the scripps memorial hospital billing process.  

both the 3rd party providers and scripps memorial hospital billing representatives state that they are "sorry" that this happens, but are unable to resolve the billing gap crisis.  the patient is left to "figure it out" on their own.

as for the patient experience, the staff ranges from expert to novice.  they saved my life, but forgot to put the bed rails up...

i'm new to san diego county and i went to another scripps facility in oceanside but this was my first time in encinitas. it is much larger than oceanside and a little difficult to navigate at first. there are several different buildings so make sure to have your building number and suite number available. there is limited parking outside of the building so i would recommend saving yourself the trouble and heading right to the parking garage. it's free to park and fairly close to everything. i was able to check in, easily. they told me to be there 15 minutes ahead of time but i'm not sure why they said that because it took me two seconds to sign in. i was there, now much earlier than i needed to be. i figured i would get some work done while i was waiting. except, the wi-fi barely works and there's no service so i stood outside for a while and did my work until i was called in. i met with dr. langley who's absolutely amazing! he was a great listener and gave me great insight while answering all of my questions. great doctor and staff. i will definitely come back here again and recommend it to my fellow yelpers.

this place sucks! stupid nurses and overworked doctors. i hate this generation medical field professionals. went in to get fixed and sat for hours. the democrats of california can suck me balls. they have completely screwed everything up for the everyday tax payer!  #recallnewsome

manish champaneria, md and the staff at this hospital were great! the nurses were very caring and made sure that i was taken care of and were very helpful. my 1 night stay was great. my surgery went well. if you're ever looking for or need a great plastic surgeon this is your guy.
scripps is best to go to if you need to be seen by a qualified doctor.

last week i suffered a heart attack and was taken by ambulance to scripps. from the moment i arrived in the emergency room, and then later to the icu, the care i received was truly exceptional. the empathy and professionalism on display by everyone was heartwarming and put my wife and i at ease. i have some special accolades for a few of the many who treated me. in the emergency room james was our first contact and kept us thoroughly informed and was reassuring of my upcoming procedures. in the icu the nurses in charge of my care over the next few days were angels. lora, emily and irene provided excellent care while keeping my spirits up and had me laughing in what would normally be a very dire time. last, but certainly not least is the care i received from dr. bulibek and his cardiac team before and after my stent procedure. they enabled me to go home sooner than anticipated and to share what would be a very meaningful thanksgiving with my family.

the nurses here are extremely rude(particularly karol) . i came to visit my wife after work and was told that i need to leave after 15 minutes. my wife non stop complained about all their services the short time we were allowed to see each otherand ended up checking herself out against dr advice. do yourself or your loved one the favor of brining them to st. cloud or maple grove.

ucsf lab and blood draw location. this is one of 3 in san francisco. the building is non descriptive and it's not clear where you enter. after you find your way in your inundated with signs. find the sign that says pick a number as that is step 1. from there you will be called. step 2 is interacting with the intake representative who has no people skills. from there you wait for step 3. after about 15 minutes i was called into a room. the phlebotomist was the highlight. she was funny, friendly, and personable. 

ucsf has free wifi. i would also highly recommend making a mychart account online so you can monitor your test results. i received my results within 1 hour for some a few days for others.

awful er department. i was taken by ambulance for feeling dizzy and confused. while i was on the ambulance they established that my blood sugar was incredibly low. when we got to the hospital, one of the emts said i needed some orange juice or something to raise my blood sugar. they told him to put me in the lobby and they'll get to me. i was taken back and asked the basic questions but was asked multiple times if i used drugs. i told them no repeatedly and explained that my blood sugar is low and if they could please get me some juice. to which they replied are you sure you don't use drugs? i was so angry. i was asked 3 times if i was a drug user when i was obviously showing signs of hypoglycemia. my husband arrived at the hospital shortly after i did and they would not let him back to give me some orange juice. they would have let me go into a diabetic coma because they were just assuming i was a drug addict. there people need better education and to listen to their patients better!
