zero stars!
i never leave bad reviews but this one is worth the read. this was the worst experience i've ever had with any hospital. especially finding out what i just did. we went in about 12:15 for my 4 month old. the waiting room wasn't completely filled, but it was a lot of people. they seen us in triage, took babies temperature, swabbed nose for influenza and all those things. first red flag, that i honestly didn't trip off of at the time because my baby was screaming her head off, was he didn't even tell me what her temperature was. we went and sat down like they told us to. we were there for a little over 2 hours, and not even exaggerating, my baby cried the whole time, minus the 10 minute nap she was able to get. around 2:20am i went and asked for an update, and possibly a time for my child to be seen. i had my 4 year old and 4 month old in this place for hours now, and if we aren't going to be seen i may as well take them home and deal with it there. the check in person, who i thought was a nurse, told me she wasn't and called the nurse . the nurse came out and i asked him was he the nurse that i was supposed to talk to, and he replied "no, i'm the triage nurse". then the lady called his name and told him he is the nurse that i needed to talk to. i expressed my concerns & he told me that it's up to me, they are completely full. at that point i got irritated because it makes no sense. i understand that everyone in there needs to be seen, but i had the youngest baby in the waiting room, no nurses or any one for that matter was coming out checking on any of us or giving us updates. literally just letting us all sit. when i went to even ask for an update  i had to look through windows to even see the woman sitting there. here we are now sitting at stanford urgent care (great service by the way) and come to find out, my baby has rsv and the flu! this is where my review kicks in. it was a bad experience but i wasn't even going to say anything, just not go back. they swabbed her nose for the flu and said the results come back in 1 hour. we didn't hear anything! although we left, they had all of our contact info! when those results came back positive, i would think they would reach out being that she 4 fuckin months old. i wouldn't recommend this place at all. i work at a hospital! i understand we get busy, but they honestly did not care & it showed!
i been going here for almost 15 years and they have the best stuff. everyone is super friendly and the doctors are great and caring. i appreciate everyone here and salute them for the great work.

what a rip off . went in for 2 hr not feeling good . charged me over 7000 . hospitals should not have blank check . to charge what ever they want . not i am worried to go to er again because off the amount they charge .

i brought my 16 year old son here today after 6 days of fever (flu diagnosis at urgent care and upper respiratory infection diagnosis at his doctors office just yesterday). unfortunately, he was a lot worse this morning and his doctor doesn't see patients on friday. we signed in and they immediately ordered a chest x-ray and blood work and had us go back to the waiting room. after being called back for the blood work, they sent us back to wait for the x-ray. about 10 minutes later, my son said everything was "going black" and he felt so sick, and he became gray in color, shaking, and clammy. i wanted to run for help but i couldn't leave him sitting there because he felt like he was passing out. i asked a woman sitting nearby to please ask the security guard to get help. he immediately went for help while another patient yelled for a doctor. the nurse came right out and brought him back to a room, he was shaking, so out of it, and so gray in color...he was going into shock, and needed to lie down. thankfully the charge nurse (i found our later her name is gerri) rushed in and had him in a gown and on the bed so quickly, all the while telling him what she was doing, telling him she knows he doesn't feel well, and reassuring both of us that she was going to start an iv and get him feeling better. she was amazing! kind, compassionate, and incredibly efficient. i honestly felt that he would be ok as soon as she took over. it was a bit of a blur after that, but gerri and his other nurse who took care of him for the majority of the time we were there (joyce) brought warm blankets, reassured him, was made us feel like our son was getting the care he needed. joyce  was very kind and caring also, and checked in with us often, even calling multiple times to find out the status of the chest x-ray. we found out later that this was their busiest day in years, and gerri and joyce both took the time to make sure our son felt safe and well cared for, and made me as a mom feel so much better. i can't thank these 2 nurses enough for taking such good care of my son. they both deserve 5 stars, the only reason i put 4 is because the first nurse didn't handle the situation well and showed no compassion, and very little competence. maybe she was having a bad day...maybe she's seem this too many times...but for my son and myself, this was a terrifying experience. i feel so grateful that gerri stepped in and took control of the situation, and handled it with such empathy, professionalism, and efficiency. thank you, gerri and joyce!

i broke my ankle in 3 places when i was downtown and i feel very lucky that i was taken to mercy in the ambulance. 

i got fast treatment in the er, which enabled me to only have one surgery for my ankle instead of two, which was a definite possibility. they set my ankle quickly and took very good care of me.

the 5th and 11th floor nursing staff also took good care of me on the nights before and after my surgery. everyone was very nice and made sure i had the best care possible.

the anesthesia team did an amazing job! i have always been very sick any time i've been under anesthesia (throwing up for 3 days typically) and thanks to the team at mercy, i threw up a little bit once the first time i was able to walk to the bathroom after surgery. that is an amazing improvement.

surgery seemed to go well, though i'm still not at the point where i'm able to put any pressure on my ankle.

i wish i had been told more clearly how long i'd need to be on crutches with absolutely no weight on my bad ankle. since it was in a boot immediately, i didn't realize it would be over 6 weeks before i could even put pressure on it with crutches. due to the pain i have just when i drive on bumpy roads, i understand this, but i had no idea how massive the surgery was, so having it explained to me in the hospital (rather than being told 2 weeks and then told 4 weeks at my first follow-up appointment) would have been very nice. i'd never broken a bone before. i didn't know how much the boot protected the ankle, but it seemed similar to the immobilizer situation i'd had with knee surgeries. it would have been nice to know right away and be able to rearrange more of my life, but generally everyone took very good care of me.

my 85 year old mom was transported to this hospital after taking a serious fall.  the treatment in the emergency department was horrible, the nurses were cold spirited, nonchalant and slow to respond.  we waited for 10 -15 minutes for a bed pan.  can you imagine an 85 year old being forced to almost urinate in the bed. we waited 3 hours for a room, not because there wasn't one available; because the departments were not communicating to get it done.   after being admitted to the 7th floor, the nurses were friendlier and more eager to help.  my intent was to leave an up to par review.  but, there are too many small details that are overlooked. the therapist is running late, the meal plan is limited, the nurse leaves the unclean bed pans in the bathroom on top of the toilet or near the sink, very unsanitary.  not the worst hospital in the world, but they are lacking the feeling of "going the extra mile." the hospital needs a new administrator or a new form of leadership that is willing to implement systems that will eliminate bad review.

back at the hospital with my mom. this time the 12th floor.  the emergency room visit was way better than 8 months ago.  the service was fast and the support staff was friendly.  we are now on the 12th floor and it's on to a bad experience.  my mom hasn't been bathed in 2 days. thank goodness my mom is not as sick as she was 8 months ago.

i like this building. they have free park, a beautiful chapel inside, staffs are nice and helpful. i just don't like the fact sometimes i have to wait longer than expected but in general this hospital is pretty good for out patient.

well i have been in three different hospitals this last week visiting patients. mercy has been the most impressive of the three. from the parking lot worker, explaining how to get into the hospital to the medical staff who offered to show us where the starbucks was (in addition to telling us) -hands down very customer/patient/visitor oriented. not sure if it was because it was christmas eve or what but their genuine kindness and helpfulness sure got my attention.  the gift shop was by far the superior of the three hospitals as well, with such a lovely selection and a great christmas discount!  well done mercy, well done !  ps. this is my first time reviewing a hospital too.

they don't seem to care about patients. during a recent visit one of my family members was left out in the hallway for an extended period of time.  he also overheard the nurses basically admitting that they do not offer sufficient care due to the fact he comes in often. he suffers from seizures. it is absolutely ridiculous.
fac_name: Atrium Health's Carolinas Medical Center - Mercy

review: do not go to this "hospital"!! it's completely understaffed and should not even be considered a emergency room. my daughter went there for stomach issues and had a iv and ultrasound. we received the bill for that 1 hour visit and it totaled over $6,000. they like to charge $500 for a iv needle, $500 for the tube, and pretty much anything else they can think of to rip you off. if your business model isn't working you just can't start ripping people off to account for it!!!! i will be contacting the better business bureau about this!! if you go to this place beware they will do everything they can to make the charges unbelievably extreme.

i cannot day enough amazing things about my experience as a first time mother delivering at this hospital. every single nurse and staff member we had the pleasure of helping us was extremely helpful, patient and so professional. 

a few names stand out, for starters amanda was the nurse that help deliver our baby boy she is just so amazing at what she does and definitely made my labor so much easier than i thought it was going to be in every way. we cannot thank her enough. 

yamila was one of the nurses we had in our recovery room. we unfortunately had to stay a few nights extra due to some tests the baby and i needed done so we had quite a few different nurses but yamila stood out because she really took the time to explain so much to me about my pain and how to ease it. i know she got the end part of our stay so she needed a little extra patiences with me and she was amazing with that. 

kristen is the director of the maternity and labor dept and she went in everyday into our room to make sure our stay was going great and anything we needed she made she to get for us. her energy was just so happy and positive and it's exactly what we needed during our stay.

debbie was the lactation consultant during our stay. she made the impossible happen and helped me latch my baby for breastfeeding. i was so tired and overwhelmed during this stay and didn't think this breastfeeding thing was going to happen for me but she helped so much with that and all the questions i had. 

and last but not least, our baby boy tested high for jaundice so we had to stay yet another night because he needed treatment at nicu and samatha was definitely a nurse i will never forget. she was so helpful and made everything possible to inform us of what was going on, let us interact with him as much as possible while he was getting treated, gave us so much advise, walked us out, help us first timers sit him properly in his car seat, just completely went above and beyond and was simply amazing! she definitely made that experience less painful. 

since the baby has to stay an extra night and i got released from my doctor, the hospital worked with our pediatrician to make sure we could still have a room during that night our baby was in the nicu. the rooms were so nicely renovated and super clean. we cannot thank the staff that night enough for being just so accommodating. just a great experience overall and would recommend this hospital to anyone and if and when we decided to have another baby, southern hills will be our hospital of choice! thank you again!

i have given birth at this hospital twice so far. and both times have been really comfortable. 

the hospital is definitely maintained and clean. 

staff is nice. and the lead nurse would check in every day to make sure my stay was going nice and smooth. 

as i was contracting in the middle of the night, i decided to head to the er. i had already checked in and done all my admitting, so i went straight to the labor and delivery floor. 

they checked me in right away and got me comfortable. i was already dilated enough to get an epidural but the anesthesiologist was in surgery so they kept me up to date. 

they welcomed family members with no issues. 
nurses were extremely supportive during my labor and i can't thank them enough. 

after delivery they moved me to my room. the baby was always with us or if they were to take him for the bath, one of us were able to watch. 

nurses always communicated with us. 
they served us a celebratory dinner on our last night. it was super cute with sparkling cider and a nothing bundt cake. 

nurses always kept us stocked on diapers formula, whatever we really needed. 

on our way out, 
they gave me goodies and made sure i was ok to leave. 

i even forgot my medicine in my room and as soon as they called they put it on the side for my boyfriend to go pick up. 


overall a great experience. and i would definitely recommend giving birth here.

my mom recently was ill and was admitted to the hospital for 12 days.  she was in the icu for the first week and then moved to a regular floor then moved again to another floor (the 2nd move without letting us know).  

in the icu, the nurses were great.  some of them were awesome and very helpful.  the icu doctors seem to rotate in and out.  the one that was there at the beginning was only in town for a week then moving onto another hospital.  she was very nice but i felt her and her staff were more concerned about just letting my mom pass away instead of getting her well.  the 2nd ice doctor was much better and was willing to do what it takes to get her well.  

once in the regular floors, care is more limited though all of the nurses were very good. they then decided to transfer my mom to rehab facility without telling me.  i happened to ask and they said that it was happening later that day.  the case manager who arranged it was so scattered, it a miracle it happened.  and don't get me started on the rehab center.

also, why don't hospital cafeterias actually have healthy foods?  it was all deep fried and grill foods.  and a crappy salad bar with two veggies and they rest all being various cream based salads like potato salad.    

my mom also was at this same hospital the day before getting a colonoscopy and endoscopy and i think she picked up a bug that started all of her issues.

great nursing staff but the food is awful!!! you may think the nursing staff is the most important, but when you have been in the hospital a few days and can't regain your strength because the food is sooo bad, you will feel differently. 


my nurse told me some patients order door dash or another food delivery service. that's what i ended up doing, but that is so sad! 

this hospital is so close to my house but i will not be coming here again. i'd rather drive to sunmerland and go to the hospital out there.

wow... i have never been to such a friendly and fast emergency room! dee at intake was amazing so bright and peppy and really made us feel at ease. the rest of the rn's that treated us were just as exceptional. 

keep doing what you guys do :)

southern hills is my favorite hospital before. i would have given it a five star if it wasn't for some rude lying doctors. some of the nurses are awesome including the billing staff they are sweet and funny. but not the nurse on the fifth floor they are liars. the charge nurse said she would help me but all lies. what i dislike the most when the doctors treat you like you are a drug addict. seriously ? a drug addict ? when i am an esrd patient, neuropathy, diabetic, i have ghost pain due to toe amputation on left and right foot. i constantly have pain all over my body and including severe itchiness. so when i stayed at the hospital i had this physician dr. zdrnja. he was the worst md i ever had in southern hills hospital. he refused to give me iv benadryl, when my nephrologist in my davita clinic prescribe it to me at every visit. which is monday, wednesday, friday at 2:45-6:45. even when i stay at southern hills hospital by another physician they always give me iv benadryl. so i do not understand what is his problem or what is the big deal. not only that he refused to give me my other meds like antibiotics, my insulin or provide me wound care when i had a major operation.  

doctor tahir? the kidney doctor ? omg if it was up to him he would say you need dialysis everyday. if you needed dialysis ? that's what he would say. oh and if you needed anything else like other medication ? forget it don't bother asking because he will not give it to you. some of the doctors at southern hills hospital do not listen to you. i would never go back there again. oh iv benadryl i needed it because i am a dialysis patient and with diabetic disease, we do not have the best skin. we have very dry skin and it's very itchy. i will never go back there.

i went in for lung cancer surgery 2/19/20. the checkin process was organized w efficient & friendly staff. the pre-op staff was also very efficient. however, i am not sure if the icu floor is short staffed or what but it was very lacking in care. was in a lot of pain & at times had to wait an hour or so for a nurse to come in after i called them. once there the gals were great but the wait time was not. also a few times had to wait to be helped to the restroom & almost wet the bed, had to call a few times in an hour before someone came in.
i do understand i was not the only patient, but i would think the icu would be more on top of things. nurses work hard, yet the icu floor should never be lacking. one of my nurses, carrie rocked when she did come around.
not sure i would go back. mountain view is a better place.

the hospital staff are actually quite great in the er but the security at the front desk really acted out of line. my mother came in with numbness and tingling on the left side of her body. the kiosk addressed her to go directly to the front desk. she was having trouble walking and numbness/tingling and security told her to take a seat and wait her turn as patients are taken in the order they are received even though we informed him that the machine instructed us to go to the front desk right away.this happened around 4 pm on sunday, the day that i'm writing this review. his response not only of announce but was "fine do it your way whatever". i don't typically write bad reviews as shown on my yelp account. something had to happen for this to take place and guess what. something happened. members of the security team should not be making medical assumptions or decisions let alone statements. they are not qualified medical professionals. the real talent is in the actual emergency room and that was reflected today by the staff members of the hospital themselves. beyond security, everything else has gone fine. i am greatly appreciative of southern hills hospitals emergency room team.

had to take my mother there because she dislocated her jaw while yawning. the er front desk was friendly and quick. she was in a room within 7 min. the doctor pops her jaw in quickly and explained everything he was going to do. glad to know we have a great hospital to go to that is just down the street!  thank you southern hills!

i had to come for a slight case of pneumonia. here fo 5 days. while the staff is very good , getting any decent food to eat here is impossible. under seasoned and extremely overcooked. out of 10 meals, i could only eat 2. sure i complained but it never got any better. dry chicken, fish and turkey. mushy cauliflower. horrible.
very clean. nice staff that is always willing to help. very professional and knowledgeable.

i'm here because of my lungs,and today was a scary day,had to get my lung drained. beyond scared and  crying, john s the tech there was amazing he calmed me held my hand and was there every step of the way. thank you john s you made it so much easier for me. thank you. also kelina she was so kind and amazing it was unreal.  she had a way to make u feel special and relaxed . one of the best nurses i e met

southern hill hospital er, they was very welcoming and they on top of everything. once we check in they took my daughter right away and had her register on the system. the nurses are very friendly and supportive. we was there for 2 hours and i understand that they was busy. thank u!

i went into southern hills last tuesday night for an er visit. they had to admit me and i stayed a week. i had surgery. this was the most amazing hospital stay i've ever had. it's hard to be sick but the entire staff was sooo amazing. they took excellent care of me! the food was good! i saw another review that said it was horrible. yes you only get a few choices and some meals it's hard to pick something you feel like eating. everything i received was great! my hubs and kids met the head chef down in the cafeteria and he is the absolute sweetest! i will definitely be using this hospital in the future for our medical needs!

went in for a surgical procedure. was treated like a vip from the first minute until i was discharged. highly recommend this hospital. the lady at admitting on the left side with the long hair.  great service. i'm sure the others are just as good, but she was the one who helped me. even house keeping seem to go out of there way to help. great hospital.  i hope i never have to go back as a patient, but if i do. i want to go there

i had surgery here a couple of weeks ago and decided my experience was too good not to be included on this page. in scheduling my appointment, both amanda and sharon have to be mentioned. they are 2 of the most professional schedulers i've encountered. they were able to calm my anxiety and made me comfortable. though the hospital is undergoing a major upgrade in decor and equipment, it is spotlessly clean, from the floors to the ceiling... and i saw a lot of the ceiling during my day of surgery there. the staff was all very kind, understanding and attentive. i was constantly asked if i was warm enough if i needed a warm blanket or anything else. my urologist, dr. lesani, is a consummate professional and i can understand why he performs surgeries here. i cannot recommend this hospital and it's wonderful staff enough. well done!

i am so glad i choose this hospital to have my baby at. the entire staff here is amazing excellent patient care and service. the registered nurses here are caring, knowledgeable and do their jobs very well. my room and the entire hospital is clean and organized which makes the stay there so much better. i want to send a special thank you to registered nurses christy and robyn thank you for making my entire delivery and stay there unforgettable.
clean, efficient, friendly...my hospital of choice when it becomes necessary to choose. only area i would improve on is better communication from the dr's who back up various areas there.

great assistance upon arrival and the staff at the check in counter were professional and friendly. triage nurse was swift and thorough. the wait wasn't as long as i thought it would be. the wait was fairly clean given the amount of people in the waiting room. the lighting was bright and the television sound was nice and at reasonable volume. the care was great. i want to thank the gentleman at the security desk ms. bettye and sonny (we entered on the wrong side) for getting us to the er side of the hospital.  thank you so much for you all help.
the most treasured of the doctors, i have the privilege to have dr boucree.  excellent bedside matters, most knowledgeable in all areas. i trust him because he trust god!

mountain view healthcare center treats their patients with respect and dignity. mvhc is a good-size facility, but the facility has a small facility feel.  administration, as well as, medical staff know each patient by name.  in addition, all mvhc employees and  physical / occupational therapist are responsive and attentive to all patient's needs.

my mom just finished a 4 week stay at mvhc.  the staff was fantastic!  all of the cnas were kind, caring and attentive (special shout outs to erick & azucena).  everyone was helpful and very focused on my mom's care and the therapy staff made great progress with her in her rehabilitation.  when it was time to leave, the social worker (rose) was very attentive and helpful in recommending resources to help us care for mom at home.  we have had other experiences at snfs on the peninsula and this one was by far the best.

once again, a parent in the er and dealing with a rude nurse named melissa. after, a day in a half in the er this nurse has the audacity to be rude and chastise my dad for having more than two visitors in a private room. front desk receptionist in er allowed us in because it's a private room that we will pay for. i spoke to charge nurse robert and house supervisor araselia about this unprofessional and rude nurse melissa. i honestly hope she was dealt with and has been informed that we are customers and not only patients.

i was admitted to antelope valley hospital as a trauma patient early last month after a terrible head on collision. initially the trauma nurses were great until the ct scan. a woman who was in the ct scan room asked the man who was wheeling me in if he asked if i may be pregnant. "that's not my question to ask" is what he said. then she asked me directly if there was a chance that i could be pregnant and i said yes. after that the entire staff seemed extremely annoyed, and didn't end up even administering a pregnancy test before the ct scan. although this was very upsetting i wasn't in the state of mind to bring any more concern on the matter.

they then put me in the emergency room and eventually came in to tell me i had a fractured l5 vertebrae, and fractured fibula on my left leg. i knew something was wrong with my right foot but they insisted that nothing showed up in the ct scan. they ordered a cam boot for my left leg then tried to put it on the right instead. a common theme in my 5 days here was that i had to inform almost every staff member of my own injuries and i wasn't even confident that they had diagnosed everything properly.

i had two mris done because i kept complaining about my foot. it wasn't until the 4th day that they found 2 fractures in my right foot. this was extremely upsetting after a ct scan and x-rays on my feet, and the doctors kept promising that i would go home the next day after day 2.

i spent the first night and second day in the critical care unit, which most of the nurses there were extremely attentive, i believe angela was the name of the rn i had during the day and she was great. once they moved me out of critical care the second night, it all went extremely downhill.

the remaining 3 days consisted of an average wait of 30-45 minutes for any nurse to assist after i pushed the button (especially during the night time) and a lot of rough handling when transporting me anywhere. keep in mind i have a fractured spine vertebrae and (soon to realize) three total leg/foot fractures between my two legs so i could not do more than roll on to my side, let alone sit up/stand/walk. this is incredibly disappointing beings how i am only in my 20s and someone who would seriously need help could possibly not have their call answered in a timely manner.

the two other nurses that stood out to me were stephenie (rn) and sherri (nt). sherri, who was very nice and talkative, unfortunately spent entirely too long speaking with patients about her personal life. she was the one i had the biggest problem with answering my calls. after 45 minutes, i sent my husband to find her, then 30 minutes later she came back in a rush and told me i just needed to be patient. i'm sorry but waiting over an hour for a bed pan because i can't walk myself to the restroom is ridiculous. this seemed like a common theme before shift change that the wait times would get longer and longer.

stephenie on the other hand, was the best nurse i had. she answered my calls promptly (usually within 5 minutes),was very informative, gave me a lot of supplies and products to maintain my hygiene, and helped clean my tables often. she was very nice and offered a lot of emotional support as well as she was my nurse on day 4 and i was ready to get the f out of that place.

all in all, if you are not a trauma patient, please go elsewhere. that is the only reason i had to go here and although i am grateful for the staff members that truly helped, i wish that my experience was different.

i had to take my daughter to the emergency room for a sprained ankle a few nights ago. i was there 7 hours and the treatment there was just not a good experience. most of the staff were nice but the procedures and protocol need help. first, in the midst of flu season i arrive to a room mostly full of people coughing and wearing masks. but when i asked for a mask they told me they were out of them. so i had to sit exposed for 7 hours trying to keep myself away from the coughs.

then no one helped with the wheel chair throughout the entire stay.  additionally i have never seen a hospital run in this fashion where patients are treated in front of everyone in a seperate waiting room. it felt to me like an invasion of their privacy and fight almost broke out in that room as well.

went to the heart and vascular center at avh yesterday.the service and professionalism was outstanding. the entire process from registration to being released was efficient and enjoyable. getting prepped for the procedure was excellent. jan and her team of nurses knew what they were doing. letty the nurse from the cath lab explained the procedure to my wife and i  so we knew what to expect. the doctor was outstanding and experienced. the recovery area was well managed by cody and her team. i would definitely recommend this facility.

terrible nursing staff, can't even tell who is a nurse because everyone wears all different color scrubs with all different patterns.

there's no way of knowing if the person you're trying to find is a nurse or a respiratory therapist etc.

er is a disaster, overcrowded to the point that i think it is a fire hazard.

i think everyone who works there is overwhelmed as most of the people we've encountered have a lot of attitude and don't seem to put patient care/customer service as a priority. 

there certainly is not a lot of compassion or empathy.

thank you to the antelope valley hospital 2nd floor nurses and staff, especially sam r.n.  she was so caring, as was the rest of the staff, the day my dad passed in the early morning of 11/22, and his hospital room was filled with over 30+ loud latinos. she provided refreshments for all and cold water as we bid my father farewell .  a true kind human that went beyond her duties, i'm so grateful for people like her.  letting my dad go was the hardest thing ever but thanks to dr musoud, nurse kieren(sp?) and beautiful nurse sam, his transition was easier on his family.

horrible experience yesterday. my 4 month old was running a high fever of 103.3f that wasn't letting go. from 2pm to 7pm i gave him a few doses of tylenol as recommended per weight, but it wouldn't drop, so i decided to rush him to the emergency at av hospital er section. when i got there they made my distressed baby wait a while until i brought to their attention that they were being medically unethical for making a ill baby wait, once i said something, triage took his temperature, and confirmed he had a high temperature and showing signs of discomfort, so they will put in an order for medicine and had made he continue to wait. after being accepted in the back, they made us wait more while my baby was burning fire until they gave him another dose of tylenol. a nurse came into check my baby after 45 mins after receiving a dose and the he was still @ 102.2f, and that nurse had the nerve to say it isn't really a fever, like it's no big deal. after 3 hours there, we finally saw a nurse practitioner, who ordered an x-ray and immediately did a flu swab once seeing the condition he was in. then waited again, finally after nearly 4 hours there, they take us to get x-rays, when we finished and came back to were my baby for resting in a bed, i quickly noticed they removed the linens, so i asked why? they said that we now have to wait in the green zone, which is a basically a hallway with a bunch of other sick people sitting in close proximity, so i calmly told the nurse this isn't right and that my baby's immune system is shot right now and being in with other sick people isn't safe, may i remind you he's distressed crying with a fever. he said he doesn't care where i wait, that i had two options, either in the hallway where there's sitting or stand in the hallway away from others, but that it's protocol and i couldn't return to the room my baby was comfortable in. i am furious at the lack of sympathy and i felt my baby was so neglected . as a mom, it's an indescribable pain in my heart. so at this point, i felt there's no reason to stay, because this nurse wasn't being helpful, and i didn't want to expose my child to any other possible disease and stress, mind you, he is sensitive to noise. i told the same nurse i was going to leave, if not placed back, because why make my baby stress more, so he then replied without listening to me all the way through and said do what you want, also keep in mind we don't give results over the phone. i asked that they call me if there's something that needs to be treated and left. he was a a**hat, who clearly didn't care. my baby was suffering a fever that following night and once morning came, i called his doctor who accepted us and retrieved results from av hospital, that reports show he's influenza positive and still at this point with a high fever. never received a call from av hospital to come back for treatment or prescription, or even review results. i feel like they are extremely neglectful and need way better training and customer service. try to avoid this place if possible. i mean it.

my most recent visit at av hospital was less than desirable.  i was transported through paramedics entering in through the emergency room.  after waiting in the hallway for several hours, i finally was seen by a doctor.  he ran test and then sent his nurse back stating that i was being discharged.  after having me sign for billing.
i went off.  i complained that i have not heard from the doctor since his initial introduction.  i continued by saying no one has talked to me about my test results and why i was feeling ill.  i had no more knowledge than i did after now 7 hours of waiting.  i was furious and requested the doctor come and speak to me.  av is very good at billing you for a job undone.  i would never recommend av.  they were also very negligent with my mother who is no longer with us.  i had to make a malpractice complaint against the hospital.  i tried to take away the 1 star that it placed there automatically but couldn't remove it.  stay away!!!  if at all possible go down the hill.

expect to wait longer if you have medical and be treated like u don't matter. i don't mind waiting but expect less unprofessional care, misconduct, harassment, and i had a nurse practitioner tell me that the reason they took the person before me that arrived after me is because our insurance policies are different, either way they get paid this was discrimination and misconduct to make something like up

once again my mother is in av hospital with symptoms resulting from an ongoing back problem. tonight, the staff deliberately waited until family had left her for the night, before coming in, grabbing her stuff, and moving her to a new room. the orderly wanted to put her into a wheelchair. well wtf? she just had back surgery two days ago, and you're asking her if she can get up on her own power and get herself into a wheelchair??? no one contacted us about this move to a new room.  selfish, sneaky bastards. how can you justify doing this to older people?? also ran into a nurse with a bad attitude yesterday. mom's call light had been on for a full hour when this b came in, shut the call light off, didn't even bother to find out what we wanted, and began to walk out - until i said something. she copped an attitude just because i asked for help, and raised her voice to me in a nasty way. wtf kind of sht is this? why do families of patients have to put up with this kind of treatment?? the hospital has to do better than this!! we only have two, and from i have read, palmdale is much worse. god only knows what other crap lies in store for our family. i will update this review as other things occur.
i cant believe how horribleeee they treat their patients !! this doesnt even deserve 1 star

i love this kaiser hospital. it's clean and gorgeous outside and inside. the doctors and staff are friendly and they genuinely care about their patients. 

i was hospitalized a few years ago and i was amazed and extremely grateful that each patient has their own rooms. being hospitalized is bad enough but sharing a room with someone else as sick or sicker than you is not ideal. 

thanks kaiser for making my hospital stay something nice to remember.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Modesto Medical Center and Medical Offices

franciscan health wound care institute is precisely what you'd expect. it's an outpatient clinic located within st. francis hospital that provides care for wounds including hyperbaric oxygen therapy, diabetes foot and ankle care, limb salvation, and general services related to a wide variety of wounds including pressure ulcers. 

during my recent hospitalization, much to my dismay, i was found to have multiple pressure ulcers secondary to my recent health decline and also due to my status as a wheelchair-using paraplegic and amputee. these wounds healed dramatically during my 10-day hospital stay, but following my discharge i was also seen by a wound care nurse through home health and, as such, was provided an appointment with the wound care institute to ensure that healing was maintained. 

my appointment was about three weeks post-discharge. the stitches were still in my recent amputation, while i continued to be receiving home health care. 

the clinic is located inside the hospital at the outpatient center entrance - entrance 12, a fact that should probably be advertised somewhere but isn't and partly contributed to my being a few minutes late for my appointment. as this is a healthcare setting, accessible parking is plentiful and st. francis actually offers free valet services. 

the clinic is located on the first floor - it's a bit winding, but the signage is actually pretty solid and i had no problem finding it. 

while i had some experience with iu wound care previously, i'd never been to this wound care and it's run quite differently. with iu wound care, you're essentially seen by physical therapists who specialize in wound care and are nationally certified. at franciscan, it's a more traditional clinic overseen by two physicians. i was seen by a tech who did my vitals, a nurse who examined my wounds and took measurements/photos, and a physician - dr. monica joyner. as my frame of reference had been iu, i expected a different set-up and had specifically requested my clinician be a female due to my background as a survivor. 

due to issues with my transportation and getting lost a bit within the campus, i arrived about ten minutes past my appointment time and past the 15 minutes early they had requested. i thought the response to this was a tad snarkier than it needed to be, but by appointment's end i had certainly apologized and they seemed fine. instead of a "we told you to be here at 10:45," a simple "we were getting worried as we expected you at 10:45," a gentler way of inquiring about someone's tardiness. since i'm post-op and reliant on others for transportation, i just really didn't need or deserve the snark. the nurse had even made a point of saying that she was getting ready to go upstairs and see a patient (implying that i'd almost missed her), an odd fact to me since my appointment was scheduled for an hour and i was there well within that hour. 

okay, i'm done venting. 

fortunately, once the snark was done st. francis got me to providing the usual quality care i've come to expect. i was pleasantly surprised by how accessible the table/bed in the room was and i was easily able to transfer independently even as a new above-knee amputee. the nurse in question had actually seen me while i was inpatient and was well informed about my case and quite wonderful to work with. she was professional and compassionate and explained everything she was doing. she was pleasantly surprised with the amount of healing and actually showed me a photo taken of the first day she had seen me - my first thought was "wow, gross!" and my second thought was definitely a little pride at the work i'd put in to get healing going on. 

dr. joyner saw me quickly and agreed with the nurse that both wounds of concern were obviously in good shape and improved. she didn't change the course of treatment and only sought to schedule one more follow-up with possible cancellation if everything continues going so positively. 

my appointment actually did finish within the hour, though i was very pleasantly surprised that they didn't have any intention of seeing me on an ongoing basis. i always felt like at iu like they were determined to squeeze in as many appointments as possible. franciscan, on the other hand, focused on healing and didn't seem to be trying to extend treatment. they simply did what was necessary. 

while the wound care institute is a decent drive for me, i was impressed with the warm atmosphere and it felt less clinical. it felt like a doctor's office and this was even with one elderly patient nearby who was obviously suffering. it was a very peaceful setting and very healing. 

i didn't appreciate the initial sense of snark, but everything else that followed was top notch and i would definitely return should the need arise.

well, a few weeks before giving birth, my husband and i went on a tour of the hospital (sloane) where i was going to give birth bc that's where my doctor delivered (ironic that at this time i didn't realize that my doctor's practice has about 12 doctors and whoever is on call at the time, even if that doctor is a complete stranger to you, they will deliver your baby = i could have just rolled up to any hospitals and would have had the same level of personal care).  anyway, we were highly unimpressed with the aesthetics of the hospital:  it's located within a children's hospital, there is no waiting area for family, the only food is a small, dirty "cafe" with limited hours and a lot of the rooms and areas we saw just looked dingy and dirty.  we sucked it up because we had no choice unless we wanted to change doctors and that seemed like a hassle.  

flash forward to being in labor.  i must say, all of that one star is for the nurses - awesome, kind and phenomenal labor and delivery nurses!  and then came in the anesthesiologist at 2:30am.  little did i know that she was on the 23rd hour of her 24 hour shift (and this is the head of ob anesthesiology!).  she started my epidural and i immediately felt an electric shock run down my leg and an intense splitting headache and neck pain wash over me.  she had me lay down and confusingly offered to let me know what was going on after birth.  what??  no, tell me now.  she rambled on about giving me a wet tap instead of an epidural but how this is actually better than having a regular epidural.  the back labor excruciating pain allowed me to not really care about what she was saying in the moment and carry on with labor.  as i had said to my doctor for months, i started asking nurses and doctors about the baby's position so he was presenting posterior on the prenatal exams and i knew that this would cause back labor.  everyone continued to brush me off and as the wet tap wore off, i began to feel the most intense pains of my life in my back, head and neck.  after 15 more hours of this pain and questioning what was happening, i finally started calling for a c-section because i didn't know how this was going to happen (why is the patient bringing this up when they know the baby is in an unfavorable position and very large! and they know the mother is a small framed person!) - i didn't want a c-section but i had no other option at this point.  

as they moved my body to the operating table, i screamed in pain for my head and my neck - as they prepped for the c-section, i had two anesthesiologists standing behind me trying different drugs in my botched epidural and asking me if i could feel what they were doing.  as they started the surgery, i would scream out as i could feel (yes feel!) parts of the procedure and they would quickly inject more drugs into my iv.  when all was said and done, my 9lb 6oz baby was not breathing well when born and sent to the nicu and i laid on the operating table and cried - cried bc i didn't have my baby, cried bc i was in so much pain, cried bc this was so far from what i could imagine a nightmare would look like.  

i am now 4 weeks post partum and i was hospitalized for 12 days of that time due to the spinal headache i developed from the botched epidural.  on monday i go to a vascular neurologist to see why my mris have been abnormal and see if the botched epidural has now caused issues with my brain.  i missed out on so many moments with my baby due to this nightmare - i know this is a long post but i feel like it doesn't even scratch the surface of the reasons to stay away from
this hospital.  especially the head of anesthesiology.  

i never published this review and now i am almost 9 months out.  i am still dealing with the neurological effects of their huge mishap and i have thousands of dollars of bills rolling in for my baby's room and board.  they have their patient services lying in writing saying their care was extraordinary and helped (all lies!) - this place is an epic nightmare- please stay away.  no one deserves to have the first months of their new family life completely destroyed.

so easy to get in and out of the cancer building behind the hospital. cherry, natural light in the infusion rooms. friendly nurses, staff and volunteers. i work during chemo treatments and wifi is great.

my only complaint is the rest of the hospital. need some type of general store for necessities for guests of hospital patients. while the facility is beautiful which is so important if you're going to be in a hospital, it's also helpful if it's a practical place to be spending a lot of time.

not to be confused with the downstate medical university, which is in maine, and isn't really the maine focus of this review.

it's a modern building and plenty of friendly people work here, but there are some severe downsides. they charge patients for the tiniest little things like you wouldn't believe.

do you know you have to pay an activation fee and a daily premium to watch tv if you are a patient here? this is despite the tvs already being hooked up and in the rooms.

this is not one of my favorite hospitals because it is so much a money-making institution like so many other hospitals, but at least some of the others are more subtle about it. this is kind of like the easyjet or ryanair of hospitals in that they will openly charge you for everything which most other hospitals do not.

review: we had the best experience at choc hospital! my son had a developed bronchiolitis and needed to stay over night for a few days until he could breathe easier on his own. our morning nurse jenn made our stay the most enjoyable and pain free stay. she went above and beyond basic nursing and i can't thank her enough. what felt like the worst night of our life became much easier when she stepped through the doors . she treated my baby like her own. she never just went by 'orders' but went by a plan of care that truly was for the comfort and wellbeing of my child. the charge nurses were also all amazing. thank you jenn and choc!
choc hospital is amazing. is good to see health professionals who are truly dedicated to the children.

had to come in this past weekend and go to the er! actually went twice to get my follow up bloodwork done. i had dr. smith and he was absolutely wonderful with my case. my nurse erica made me feel so much better since the er wouldn't let my husband come back due to not knowing anyone to watch our kids. she got my iv i'm on her first try because my veins are stubborn and blow easily. theo was my tech and he got my iv on the first time, but as soon as they went to get my blood it blew as always. erica was so gentle and through with my care and explaining everything to me. 

when i went the second time to get my follow up bloodwork i have nurse kevin who did my blood and got it the first time and luckily he got my blood before it blew. (my left arm clearly doesn't like needles) i have a couple of different nurses and people who took care of me and checked on me brian, kaitlyn and i think kelsi. they were all so nice and helpful through this experience. 

overall doctor smith and nurse erica were my favorite and everyone was so nice and helpful. my experience due to what was happening wasn't easy so i thank you to the nurse and dr. smith who had to talk to me before i was discharged saturday and monday.

the er doctor i saw was extremely aggressive and literally yelled at me for both my anxiety and my physiological orthostatic issues. he badgered me almost like a cross examination in a courtroom about the possibility of pregnancy and my sex life. just run a test lol, why are you screaming at me? i told him i couldn't be pregnant because i was celibate (my husband is away), and he ridiculed me for my 'sad life' and gave me creepy looks. it was beyond insensitive. another doctor made insulting remarks about my face, strongly implying i was less homely with my glasses on, and looked like 'two different people'. again, super weird and gross and inappropriate to say the least. it actually really upset me and any kind of stress is really bad for my condition. 

some of the nurses here are really nice, and a med student spent a lot of time with me, giving advice about my condition, even though he didn't have to. i wish he had been my doctor!!! he was so caring and attentive. the younger people here seemed much less jaded i guess and treated me like a human being. 

the room i had was great, very private, pretty decent food, and a lot of television options.

i had a scary finding on my echocardiogram that has even to this day not been explained to me, no matter who i contact.

had a test done here outside the er and the doctor was on his phone the entire time and he too was not very nice overall.

i did appreciate the discretion when chest tests were done. not once was i exposed, so that was nice. but some of the doctors here really need to take some sensitivity training, especially when dealing with nervous female patients. the way three of them spoke to me (but especially the gruff er doc) was quite shocking. it should go without saying that remarking on a patient's personal life and appearance is wildly inappropriate and unacceptable.

my review is based on being a friend bringing a patient.  

you can park in either two garages at this location.  i recommend driving into the first garage and turning right.  on the first level during the morning, there is plenty of 2-hour parking spaces.  

as a friend/family member, you're required to stay in the clean and quiet waiting room as you enter the center, but the patient first has to check-in at suite 110 next door.  my friend was out in two minutes.

the very happy and calming staff at tsc greeted us and made us feel relaxed.  one came around with a bowl of snacks for those who are waiting, but normally snacks are upon request.

amenities include water, tea, coffee with plenty of different flavored creamers, padded seating, umbrellas, tv, magazines and tissues.  they have wheelchairs for patients that need it.

after surgery, you have to get your car from the garage and drive down the right of the building and meet your patient.

overall, i was happy with my experience and how they treated my friend.   everybody, i mean everybody, was so accommodating and friendly.

most medical facilities get a bad rap, because unlike a coffee shop or hot new bar, you're going there because you have to deal with some potentially serious medical procedure and not a latte or a beer. along with that is the complications of our healthcare system and the medical-industrial complex and a host of other issues. 

va in specific maybe even has more red tape given that it's a government-run facility. 

all issues considered, they still should hold themselves to some sort of higher standard than the complacency which runs rampant. they are still providing a service, a very important one that everyone will at some point need, and their employees are still getting paid and should be at the very least be able to provide a level of care and human decency--that doesn't change regardless of the budget. 

most of the staff i've had to deal with here, just doesn't seem to care at all about anyone. and i definitely understand it's just a job for them, that they aren't saints, but they are still providing a sort of costumer service, even if they aren't working for tips. 

while it is great that veterans have a place for free and reduced cost medical services, it's still sad that the men & women who served our country have to settle for such treatment. 

the medical system as a whole has issues that won't be taken care of with a simple fix, but if the right people are in charge and holding people accountable; i think they can all take steps toward improvement.

my experience with tosh is through the physical therapy and pool therapy programs due to shoulder issues and previous spinal surgeries.

i have had nothing but positive experiences at tosh.  all of the pts i have seen have been very professional and knowledgeable, and relatively  easy to book with.  i am currently waiting to see a knee surgeon who is booking a month out, but he is apparently amazing and in high demand, so i'm ok with waiting.  front desk staff are always friendly.

something that tosh has that other clinics typically don't have is an olympic-sized pool. this has been excellent for my spinal surgery recovery. there are options to see a therapist in the pool, and after "graduating" from the therapist sessions, there is an option for an independent program.  lance is the exercise specialist (he rocks!!), and he is able to provide additional exercises to complement the routine from the therapists. you pay a monthly fee for the independent program, and it has been a lifesaver for me!  there are both morning and evening hours available, which works well for my work schedule.

my only complaint is how much the pt services cost.  a pool session with a therapist cost me $300 for an hour (with insurance), which is completely unaffordable.  a few years back, someone in the office told me that i should look into other offices because tosh charges so much more.  (the exception is the independent pool program, which is very affordable).  just something to keep in mind if you have a high deductible plan.

the hospital is currently undergoing some renovations at this time. hopefully they also improve their postpartum rooms where you spend the next 2 nights. they could use some improvements in lighting, blinds & accessibility for new mothers from the bed to the baby or side items. our room had blinds that didn't work. for lighting, once you were in the bed you could not turn on or off lights without getting up again, which was frustrating when managing a newborn when no one in the room. they could also improve the bedding for fathers as they are important too & the single chair/bed is very uncomfortable.
the nurses in the postpartum area were also great, but it varied per rn, as some were more knowledgeable & helpful than others. but, they always provided the care you were asking for.
another improvement that could be made is not having procedures during the night shift. this is very disruptive to a new mother & baby trying to set up their schedules & obtaining maximum rest. my experience was that once the baby was sleeping the scheduled procedure was about to begin which would wake up & upset the baby. for example, circumcision was schedule for 10pm & labs were early morning based on the baby's delivery time. it would be nice to have these items done during the day hours.
overall, i would recommend this hospital for future mothers, however i hope they can make some changes to make their stay more enjoyable.

review:
it's weird to write a review about kaiser, but, here i go. 

i gave birth to our daughter at kaiser and really glad that i did! kaiser has an extremely low c-section rate and the kaiser in san jose has a bunch more midwives than the one in santa clara, which means that more of the deliveries are actually done by midwives, rather than obgyns. obgyns take care of the births that may have some complications. 

i ended up having a c-section (breech positioned baby!) and dr. sheila loanzon was awesome. it felt like my daughter was born, being surrounded by strong and kind women, and i wouldn't have asked for a better experience. i was part of their centering pregnancy group, which was led by sandy pineda, and while i didn't feel like i learned new information, it was a great way to build community. one of the other people who assisted the group, lex, made sure to be part of the c-section/delivery, and it was so relieving to have a familiar face from that group. 

the postpartum care nurses were pretty good, but i did have to call them rather than them check on me a ton. my recovery was great, and even though i wasn't keen on having a c-section, kaiser made the whole experience easy. 

i've had interactions with their phlebotomists, and they are so friendly -- definitely a big fan. docked one star since some of the facilities could do with an upgrade/better cleaning.

( we live several states away). from the initial telephone communication to the final honor walk to the or for organ donation, the staff was beyond excellent. professionalism isn't always easy to balance in situations with emotionally raw family members that are grieving in their own ways and time but the employees here are examples of how it should be taught.

i thank you all for the care of my mother and how you handled her family after her passing.
from my first experience i've heard this a very nice hospital. cousin is in critical condition but with best of care 'prayers' needed. it's going to be a long night!

absolutely the worse care i've ever encountered 
please people stay away from this place! all about the dollar sign  believe me on this! if you wish contact me directly i will share.. in extremely well traveled and have had my patient experiences but never have i seen this type of hospital  very very sad!!

i will do everything in my power never to return to this place. patient registration is unprofessional and er physicians, although helpful, take forever to discharge. 7 hours later and i'm dressed and still waiting to go.

the worst!  the nurses pay zero attention to the patients and rather than check in on patients they over medicate patients. incompetent and their lack of attentiveness is a danger especially for elderly patients.

i am a veteran and normally seek health care an medical attention at the va hospital. historically, this has been at martinez va and palo alto va, both in california. both excellent facilities. 

however, we recently relocated to nw tennessee and my current health care and emergency(ish) needs are taken care of by the dyersburg va clinic and memphis va hospital respectively. both treat me well, though not quite to the standards i have been accustomed to back in california.  but i'm not complaining

then, having suffered a dog bite injury that had become painfully infected, i was introduced to this hospital by way of an emergency room visit where i was treated by the support staff, nurses and dr. g. 

from the moment i stepped through the er lobby door, till the moment i stepped back through that door after treatment, i was treated with the highest level of attention, compassion, respect and medical professionalism. 

i wish to extend my gratitude to all that assisted me that day. i wish to further extend a much larger shout of kudos specifically to dr. g., who went above and beyond to insure my healing needs were met, as if i were his only and most important patient to ever see him. 

in closing, in a world where people only comment to complain, it seemed imperative that anyone that reads this review know just how good this hospital patient care system is and how much it is appreciated that the staff took such great care of me during my emergency room visit.
i've been a patient a few times there. love the food in the cafeteria!!!  will visit again!!

this hospital is a nightmare, give your symptoms and you are immediately diagnosed without any additional testing.

my past experience for the past 2 years with palisades hospital has been horrible, in the past i've had wait until my daughter was discharged from the er to run from palisades to hackensack hops. to only find out my daughter needed to be admitted, how did they find the issue? they preformed additional testing! had i not followed my instincts to take my daughter to a better hospital, she would had been in a worse and very painful situation. 

had to bring my mom in being her "union" claims this is the only hospital she can be seen in with her insurance along with jersey city medical center (2 of the worst). brought her in for a pain in which has caused her to not be able to walk, lift her her, stand etc. basically paralyzed with-out an explication, she has to use a cane and even with that she is unable to move an inch on her very own. 

victor (pa) took advantage of a previous diagnose many years ago which i am sure he found on the hospital system (epic) we confirmed her previous diagnosis as well. 

mom was previously diagnosed with a (herniated disk) 7 years ago, her symptoms related to her back and upper thigh clearly come from her previous medical issues (which i can understand) but victor (pa) would not look into the problem deeper as far as to her main complaint which was the pain also coming from the groin area. 

i had to request the actual doctor to come in because the (pa) victor showed 0 care 0 compassion 0 empathy, he rushed the entire process along with his assistant at the moment, when the nurse told him we requested a doctor, his attitude was uncalled for. i laughed it off because as a medical precessional, i understand that you can become lazy through out the day and lets also put some blame on me, because my attitude switched the moment he opened his mouth and responded to her symptoms.  

dr. andres baquero came in and examined my mom "further" stated mris are not done at the hospital, mmmmmm jajaja, i book mris, nucs, ctas, sleep studies etc. every day! at palisades, i am close with other pas and drs whom have confirmed that information is complete bull**** he really wanted to get away with that one, he completely ignored me and continue to ask my mom the same question to prevent responding to my comment in regards to the mri.. 

the kid next to us had insomnia, his parents were concerned, very worried, he showed 0 compassion! told them they could not do much for him (0 testing) this kid looked as though he hasn't slept in years. 

i could not help but over hear the ridiculous way he would respond to the patients, his dismissive reactions etc. it's disappointing, if i could get a hold of his license # and npi i would file a complaint against him. 

they gave my mom a steroid shot (awesome) that's exactly what i knew she needed, the prescribed her with muscle relaxer (ok) and a pain killer (i could have prescribed her that my self) but her comes a hefty bill for absolutely nothing!

i found myself in the emergency room early monday morning, turns out my appendix ruptured.  i must say, from the very beginning, i found the nurses and er doctor caring, compassionate, and knowledgeable.  i was immediately assessed, put on an iv (with morphine to diminish my pain), taken for a cat scan(great tech up there), put in a room, surgery by 4 pm.  the nurses continually checked on me, i never felt alone (even though i was).  when i was recovering on my floor, nurses came immediately if i called.  i was constantly being monitored, and ended staying an extra 4 days because of an infection.  everyone was helpful and i cannot thank them enough for my great care!  ps i feel so much better!!!

if you come here for emergency , you will regret it.  the most discriminated hospital i ever ever seem. the worst thing is that it wasn't only me and it wasn't one day type of thing.  
  
  i spent 4 days in this fucking hospital, 3 days without eating. my surgery was never set and so they never set a fucking plate of food down for me. 

the emergency team in my opinion needs more coordination.

went here this week for an infected finger in the early am. we parked at one of the many spots near the er entrance. they checked us in right away, there was nobody else waiting. they put us in a room and the nurse came in right away, but his english wasn't that great. though, he immediately tended to me, checking my blood pressure, etc.

the resident doctor came in within an hour to ask questions and diagnose.  he ordered an x-ray and other items. i told him i wanted to make sure my insurance company will approve to pay for everything he was suggesting. he sent in a hospital overnight admin and he was pretty casual. when i told him i want to make sure the insurance company will pay for all that was being ordered, as we had a terrible over billing expense of $5000 at doral er over just a sore throat swab, he said, "i don't do that, that's for the day shift people". well, that wasn't much help, was it?!

the main er doctor came in and she was also pretty casual. she cancelled the x-ray and said i just needed antibiotics. she said she would give me a prescription, and one dose of antibiotics for now. after waiting over 90 minutes for the paperwork, there was no antibiotic dose for the day, just prescriptions. when i asked the resident doctor why the change of plan, he just said after a consultation with the other main doctor, they will not be giving me a dose for the day. how confusing! the last thing i wanted to be doing is going to the pharmacy at 4:00am, but they obviously didn't care. 

in summary, i was there 3 hours and experienced staff that were far too casual and not interested in checking if anything ordered from the doctor was covered by the insurance company. not nice.
why did all the permits for the elevators expire in 2017? this is weird... it's been over two years...

i know many people write terrible things about this hospital but as for me, i give it a 5 and more. i was treated back in 2018 by the trauma unit for a terrible motorcycle accident (i don't ride no more) and the whole experience from admission to discharge was excellent. even the surgeon who operated on my many broken bones was exceptional. all the doctors, nurses and staff treated me with warmth and care.
