i don't think i've ever witness gross mismanagement of patient care and miscommunication how i have in the past week. my grandfather was admitted to the er with a heart attack this past sunday. that's when this all started, the only person out of all this experience who was caring and helpful was the er staff and our first icu nurse. it's been a slew of lies, he said she said and no one really knows what's going on. he's been waiting to be discharged and all we are waiting for is someone to "fax" an order for his discharge yet the person is nowhere to be found nor has he been discharged ... it's now been 8 days in this hospital and i have yet to have someone take care of him without a serious attitude problem and no one has their stories straight. we even had a representative of the hospital tell us without a pace maker he will die in both english and in spanish just incase he didn't hear.... also be prepared to find plenty of folks on facetime or texting rather than attending you or the patient. everyone from the valet to the cafeteria and the patient care staff. stay away from this place if u want proper professional care you're better off going anywhere else but here. still waiting for a discharge fax.....

don't share your opinions they will baker act you. stay clear from this hospital. i took in my brother on tuesday at 8:00pm he was having trouble breathing. the er dr. said it was best to have him admitted. he was only admitted to the hospital the next day at noon. they ran a bunch of exams and every doctor says he has something different, finally by by saturday they agreed he had pneumonia but by that time he was done and annoyed with the staff (especially since the nurse didnt show up for an hour twice, once during lunch and another during thr middle of the night when he was complaining about chest pains) he asked to be transfer to treat his pneumonia and the staff was making it impossible to transfer after getting into an argument with the resident physician they asked for a psychological eval. i was there with my dad with him for 4 hours and no psychologist showed up. we went home qnd about 1.5 hour later the baker acted him because he used foul language at the doctor. apparently showing your frustration is not acceptable. makes me wonder how they are still functioning as a hospital. no wonder they have 2 stars. management is the worst. i saw the number for the marketing people i called them and of course there is nothing they can do. i would give negative reviews but unfortunately it is impossible.

the hospital has bad rep., and i thought ok lets put that aside but after being there with my relative almost a month, and every medical staff had a different opinion or communicate lost in my relatives condition, because no one was on same page, it was to me a total disaster and irresponsibility on the entire team. they still need training in communication skills and priority of the care of the patient's . mind you i was walking out of the floor and i heard a patient scream calling nurse "alluda", and the nurse was sitting there in her chair without reacting at all, i walked to the end of hallway looked back and the nurse was still ignoring patient in her chair.
the doctors and nurses helped to save my son's life. they truly care about their patients. many thanks.

if i would give this hospital 0 stars i would. so i walk in and the girl in the reception is currently with another patient so i wait patiently. she finishes with the patient and still doesnt acknowledge me so i keep looking at her until she finally says "do you need help" like are you serious. anyways i go in 13 weeks pregnant because i am leaking something and i had some cramps. the lady, instead of taking me to emergency or to the maternity part of the hospital (as my doctor said they would) took me to these little non-emergencies tiny rooms. the nurse comes to the room and i asked "why am i here?" to which she responds i dont know you tell me. i explained my doctor said they would take me to the pregnancy part of the hospital to which she tells me we dont take patients there until 16 weeks pregnant. i go back to the room and another 5 minutes pass and one of the nurses came and asked me to walk with her to go take out blood, remember i have cramps. so the lady directs me and a group of people to a hall full of more sick people and hands me a face mask because guess what? everyone around me is coughing. at that point i got soo annoyed, i was freaked out because i didnt know what was happening  with my baby and on top of that to put me at risk of all these infections?! i turned around, looked for the lady that walked me even though i was having cramps to that place and told her i was leaving to which she said okay. i went to baptist and had a much better experience

i checked into the hospital and the people at the front desk were kinda friendly. then i wait on the guy to take my blood and get a urine sample. everything was going per protocol. when they finally call me for the doctor to see me it turns out that he is not prepared. the doctor did not prep himself on what happened in other parts of the hospital. he had no clue on blood work, medications i was taking, he accused me of using drugs when i have never done so in my life. he was extremely unpleasant and rude. he spoke to me as if i was a horrible person. in all it was lol due to an allergic reaction to my medication which prompted my visit. i will tell everyone not to come to this place. i will not be back either.
i got my wallet back...but i did get kidnapped into their psyche ward and told the ama and fingered the shrink that dressed up in a g4 security outfit w a gun!!!

i was a patient for 5 days on the cardiology floor and had excellent care. the physician coordination was excellent.  i did not need to use my call bell a single time! the nurses, therapists,  and pct's were wonderful!

i've been here two times and both times were great experiences (considering the circumstances).  the first time it was very crowded and while the wait time was a little long (to be expected as there were many people waiting on care), but, the staff was friendly, caring, and very apologetic.  the second time (this morning), ai was the only ooze in the waiting area and was in and out of the hospital within an hour and a half and his nurse, jan, was perfect. both times, my children were treated wonderfully and professionally. the nursing supervisor even got me some coffee. while i don't hope to come here often, i'm sure that if i do have to come, we'll be ok. thanks for your hard work!

i requested restrictions on the uses and disclosures of my personal and medical records:  "all of my personal and medical records.  all people and companies except myself, son and daughter.  i will never seek treatment at any ascension facility again."  having rational communications is virtually impossible with ascensions' employees.

ascension denied my request to restrict use of my protected health information (phi) "in order to provide our patients the best care possible" ... allow your providers to securely search your healthcare records" ... "to guide your care" ...  "have access to all of your healthcare information" ... "clearer picture of your overall health" ... "better to provide you care" ... "treatment of you" ... "if we restrict your medical records".  

if i am never going to have ascension provide treatment again, why did ascension justify denying my requested restriction based on providing my care?  maybe they assumed i have no control over who provides my care.  i have numerous non-ascension in-network doctors and my primary-care doctor has no control over where i go.

i appealed ascensions' denial stating, " it is obvious your rejection was based on your absolutely false assumption that i will ever have any relationship with any ascension provider under any circumstance.  no ascension provider will ever have any need to access my five visits.  if any non-ascension provider needs to access my seton medical records, i will provide them.  i have all 425 pages." 

guess what?  ascension denied my appeal.  ascension denied my original request for restricting use and disclosure of my phi so ascension could provide better care for me, even though i also stated i would never go to an ascension provider again.  in denying my appeal, ascension never once mentioned the argument they used in denying my original request.  instead, they threw out an argument that has absolutely nothing to do with my original request or my appeal ... an issue i never mentioned.  ascension stated, "due to state and federal record retention laws and other legal considerations, ascension is mandated to maintain medical records.  therefore, we are unable to restrict your medical records ..."  ascension either does not know the difference between maintaining and accessing or it is playing games.  i have 3 books in my desk that i have never opened and never will because the subjects are irrelevant to my life ... analogous to maintaining, but not accessing my phi.  why does ascension not understand?  since i will never be treated by ascension again, why does it need to access my phi?  maybe ascension just cannot find its butt, even if it uses both hands.

this happened a while ago but it has stuck with me as completely worth putting out there. first time i saw the doctor. i found the nurse practitioner was better than the doctor, initially. i went about 3 times to np with o.k. results, probably because i was asking for referrals. she often questioned my medical history. initially, i gave her the benefit of the doubt because my history is rather lengthy for someone my age. i thought that maybe she was wanting to check something. now i know it wasn't any of that and she was falsely judging my issues. on the 4th visit when she denied me help with lower back pain which was causing a lot of fatigue and said she didn't know where to refer me and so gave me a blood test. feeling a little in shock i just went along with her ordering a blood test for vitamin deficiency, when i knew it was because the pain was serious. when they were taking my blood in the lab in the back, i could hear the nurse practitioner talking about me negatively to the staff around the desk. you're lucky i wasn't feeling well or i would've confronted you and reported you to the nursing board for confidentiality violation. it turned out i needed physical therapy for several things she totally missed. the doctor and nurse practitioner were incompetent. the nurse practitioner was also unprofessional.

i was referred to dr. hamer for carpal tunnel by the scripps primary care doctor on february 4, 2020.  today, february 19, 2020, i have yet to receive a call from his office.  do these doctors operate by a quota or out of concern for ill patients?  do they care about the pain or do i have to constantly fight for an appointment?    i called the scripps patient liaison, the call wasn't returned, instead i received an e-mail that she would connect with me in 4 to 6 weeks!!!!  what hmo did i get myself into?  i thought i would get better service then sharp rea-stealy and scripps has definitely failed. 

a few months ago, i dealt with the mission valley scripps clinic because my resting heart rate was in the 150's.  did they care?  absolutely not.  i had to fight my way in to see a physician.  the p.a.'s they had sent me to did not know how to handle the problem.  the third time, after losing a pound a day, i had to put a stop to their attempt to send me to a nurse practitioner.  and, when you review the insurance bills, they charge for a physician's appointment (i need to check with my insurance about it).  i was so sick and the lead nurse at the mission valley scripps clinic did not seem to care.  months ago i sent a complaint and have not heard back from the patient liaison.  do not recommend scripps.  the breast cancer center is great but that's about it.  

i consider this a breach of contract with patients, considering i signed up for this particular hmo and it denies the service i am paying for.

this hospital declined to investigate my injuries and conduct any appropriate testing for my condition. coming on board with acute head and neck pain and pressure after a severe martial arts injury,they neglected to take a single mri or cat scan of my head or neck simply dismissed me with a diagnosis of depression.  

had i been properly assessed, i could have averted 7 surgeries ahead.  the singularly talented and educated physicians, thomas milhorat and paolo bolognese at the chiari institute ultimately saved my life after years of suffering encouraged by scripps hospital.  

who comes into a hospital with severe head pain and has no associated studies conducted?  they were completely idiotic and useless costing my uncle thousands of dollars in the midst. truly mind-blowing. it was long ago but i recall sitting on the floor of the follow up doctor's office watching my uncle praise them for their incredible work. 

(he was a bio-tech dude and only cared about sustaining his financial relationships with such facilities with no interest in finding the truthful answer for my incapacitating pain.) 

meanwhile there i sat, guinea pig in drag, listening to these two men congratulate one another on such mutually profound accomplishments.  meanwhile, my pain went undiagnosed and untreated for years, largely because of scripps inability and unwillingness to look for the answers.  they essentially put me through hell.  total dope heads ! 

just don't get injured or sick and if so, stay far far away from scripps hospital.frankly, you're better off dead.  they are thieves in hospital drag; absolutely the worst care ever anywhere.  

but heck, if you're looking to be called "crazy" and prescribed dangerous anti-depressant drugs in place of real research and it's application to your condition, that's the spot to go to. and all for a mere $28,000.

great experience coming here. i had an injury i needed to be seen for and i didn't even wait a minute. extremely clean facility. friendly nurses and doctors, technologically advanced equipment, and extremely quick wait time. i couldn't believe how nice everyone was, even down to the billing guy.

i had an emergency earlier this year and was taken to scripps memorial hospital, la jolla.

first of all, the ride to the hospital took forever. once i was admitted, i was made to wait for about 2 hours by which time my symptoms subsided. the physician came and saw me for about 1 minute and a half. i was first charged $999.60 as a claim from my insurance which i paid. and then i received this random billing statement from la jolla emergency specialists. they're now charging me $1,355.00 for the physician. i would think it should be the hospital's responsibility to find an in-network physician to treat me for my situation instead of having an out of network physician see me for one and half minutes and charge me an exorbitant $1355.00 fee in addition to the $999.60 that i've already paid. 

this is an unethical and illegal way of taking advantage of a patient who is coming in with an emergency situation. it is an outright scam that people need to be aware of. as if they anticipate me refuting this amount, they are also offering me a 40% discount and the ability to pay by installment if need be. i highly recommend families of individuals to be cautious about this hospital and their appalling manner of billing before they treat a relative or a friend. if you have the time, and can make a decision before being treated here, please avoid this hospital.

i am also seriously looking into pursuing a legal action against them. this has to be stopped.

this hospital is a scam. it is in my insurance network, but the doctors are not, so the copay will not be covered, so the total charge is huge. but this this not the full story. they first sent me a statement from la jolla emergency specialists with a charged of 454 dollars. i argued with they, and they gave me 40% discount, so i paid for it. however, after a month, they sent me another statement from myscripps, which asked for another 482.8 dollars. scam hospital.

following up on my previous review, we just received a collection letter from la jolla hospital services and, after being told that our co-pay for our emergency room visit covered everything. now we have to deal with this and risk potential damage to our credit report and score.

sure the hospital provides handicap parking. but...to have it validated you have to somehow get down to the parking valet to have it validated or go to another building!  i know this seems menial to those people who are ambulatory but it is very difficult for those of us who aren't.   
also, paid parking has become very inconvenient.  going to another floor just to pay is ridiculous!  on various occasions i've witnessed weak, sick people (one man was actually being held up by a woman) standing in a long line to pay. 
no, i don't want to talk to any patient advocates, etc. 
just fix the problem. this is a medical complex. you'd think they'd be a bit more sensitive to their patients.

i am going to make this company sign my own terms and conditions.  they can't seem to send a bill for services within 30-60 days.  almost every bill is 180+ days and more after services? i just got a bill for more 9 months after service?  what gives?

i can not say enough good things about this hospital. when i was pregnant the dr. silver took such good care of me. and when we found out i had a high risk pregnancy everyone on the perinatal floor of the woman's center building were amazing to me. when i went into labor they kept me and my baby comfortable and safe. the postpartum room i was in was kind of small but the labor room was huge. and when i was uncomfortable with one of the nurses and i spoke up about it they made sure she didn't come near my room again. 
i have also been back to the er a few times with my son and each time they got us back right away and took care of us as fast as they could. one time we were about to be discharged and the computers went down we were there for a while but they kept checking on us and as soon as they came back up we were out of there in no time. all the doctors and nurses i've come across seem to really care about their patients and not waisting their time.

i had gastric bypass at your hospital because i had heard good things.  dr. bhoyrul did my surgery and i had several and still have complications.  the first couple er visits were great but after that dr bhoyrul and the er staff became less compassionate and more irritated with me.  i could hear the er drs talking to dr. bhoyrul and his staff and the way i was treated completely changed.  it was embarrassing.  i won't ever go back to this hospital.  i got a new bariatric dr i wish i would have gone with in the first place and i am getting treated for my complications with compassion.

i cannot say enough about scripps memorial and the care i received after my thyroid surgery.  from the moment i checked in until i was released the next day the care i received was superior.  my surgery was supposed to be a day surgery but due to complications i had to be admitted overnight and was parked on the 5th floor of the prebys building while i recovered.  the nursing staff was impeccable.  i would definitely give a shout out to the nurses aid that attended to me the most in the morning, victoria you are amazing.  while i do not remember anything about the surgery itself i know it was a challenging procedure for the surgical staff and i appreciate the long hours they put in taking care of me.  i would not hesitate to put my care in the hands of scripps memorial if needed in the future.
i had a very successful experience at this emergency room on wednesday 1/29. much better than ucsd which is a mess. they were competent, kind, efficient, and timely. very good.

having taken and stayed with multiple family members in emergency rooms on both coasts i can attest to the efficiency and quality of care in an er. a recent er experience at this location was excellent. speed and quality of triage, nursing care and er docs were amazing.  to say an er experience was pleasant sounds weird but this er visit was as good if not even better than kaiser zion and far superior to ucsd thornton. thank you and kudos to the er staff from intake to exit.

review:
nothing in life is more irritating than when a billing dept. contacts you with a price that is significantly lower than the price presented to you from your healthcare insurance provider.  

prior to being rendering services at this location, i was contacted by billing and was presented with the amount of $738.72 as well as a request for payment.  mind you, this is before being rendered services; hence my insurance had not yet been billed.  aggravating, i know.

then, when i go check in, the same amount was listed in their system; and then after being rendered services, an estimate w/ that same amount was sent to me via usps; with a request for payment.  

meanwhile, i decided to go and check my claim through my healthcare insurance provider and i see an amount of $1,684 for the same services; as the amount of my deductible.  i call my insurance and inform them that i was presented with an amount that was less than 50% than the amount displayed on their portal; only to be told that that is the accurate amount that i will be responsible for.  so what happens next, you ask...

i file a grievance through my healthcare insurance and then contact the attorney general's office; even though i know deep down inside that not a damn thing is going to change what has happened.  i wait to hear back from either or; and below and behold i hear back from my healthcare insurance provider with the lame explanation of:  " in review of your grievance, i brought your case to the attention of a svh patient access operations director, who appreciated being made aware of your concern. the director stated that you were provided an estimate based off the cpt code that was going to be used during the procedure. the director stated that the estimate is subject to change if the provider in question uses a different service code (cpt code) or adds any services..."  

ok...let me start off by saying... that in the world of business, i have witnessed estimates being different by either 10-20%... and the differential is usually written on the estimate to let the customer know.  
in this case, the amount was over a 50% difference and nowhere was it listed that the amount could be significantly higher... also too, where it was an "estimate" then they truly had no flippin' business requesting payment in the first place.

seriously... the poor business displayed by the billing department is unbelievable and the fact that they can get away with, what other companies cannot, is repulsive.  i mean,  would you allow a company to bill you a price that is significantly higher than the price you were originally presented with?  would they not have to honor that lower price?

i thought so... 

so with all due respect, what makes this situation any different?  it may be the medical field, but it's still a business...and well the same rules should still have to apply... 

needless to say... i am not in the least bit impressed and if i have my way, i will be taking my medical needs elsewhere in the future.

maternity ward is amazing but the rest of the hospital is horrible. so hard to book and appointment and wait times are awful. just takes up your whole day

this is probably the worst hospital i have ever been to, with a 7 hr wait at the e r. suprisingly someone hasn't died in the e r. seems the staff don't give a crap about the public that supports them. one star is to much

after a eleven hour wait , my husband was taken back to a er room... lack of communication was very evident... during our eleven hour visit... my husband had a ekg and blood work... in the er room nurse ( jarred... nice man ) discussed doing some test... some that had been done during our wait... he said a doppler had been canceled and  my husbands symptoms deserved it... and didn't know how it got canceled... he got the test and when the er dr came in she was unaware of his tests and any results... total breakdown of communications... it got  scary that medical errors can and will be made in this environment... the improvement of processing needs  overhauling at the entrance of the er and better communication and making sure the doctor's has all the information they need to treat patients properly... and this will prevent medical errors, list  of life and law suits...
went to visit a friend today and everything and everyone was nice! clean, nice outdoor area. staff is friendly.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Tustin

review: my parents are elderly and in poor health.  i have had extensive experience with the big dallas hospitals.  my mother spent a week here over the christmas holiday with pneumonia.  i have to admit when the nursing home sent my mother here i was concerned about a small, old hospital not being good enough.  i couldn't have been more wrong.  the er staff was fabulous.  not only were they efficient but they were very kind to my mother.  she was in the hospital for a week and we did not have one complaint.  everyone did their job professionally.  they treated her with kindness and respect and we got all of the information we needed.  the food was even good.

avoid all all cost slc larkridge !!!  dr. lisa mullin was the best physician one could ask for. no one can blame her for wanting to leave this horrible place. i decided to go to her replacement dr. clair shimke just to have 3 medications i have been on for years. 

today after having to wait 1 month dr. shimke informed me 

" it was against her morals to prescribe my medications"

not that i was asking for pain medication mind you !  why is she there in the 1st place ? what kind of physician would say that ? 

i can say the say the same. it is against my morals to pay the bill for services not rendered. 

this physician should have her medical license taken away. i was told by the office manager that apparently when you call you need to ask if the physician is licensed to prescribe medication . that is a new one. 

i am 60 years old and on disability. this is absolutely the worst physician i have ever seen in my life.

scl firestone

kendra at the front desk is rude and disrespectful, she clearly is unhappy in her job.  came in early, she could not find me for appointment.  then she copped an attitude and argued i had just had blood work two weeks ago so it was too early. i guess they have a doctor manning the front since she is an expert on my chart. she told me i would just have to wait, so i walked outside. when i came back in she said "oh you are too late now for your appointment since you left". i  sincerely look forward to speaking with the office manager on this...hope she will return my calls

tried to visit the er today as i slipped and twisted my knee very badly in the yard. i previously had a partial replacement surgery in 2011 on this knee and am almost certain i tore or broke something once more. my boyfriend went to grab me a wheelchair after we parked and the staff wasn't liking the fact of giving one out. once he was able to snag one, he wheeled me in to find a buzzer that you press to be helped-- except there was no way of tracking when you'd be seen and nobody there to help you or take any info. so we press the button as we await in their condensed er area. ten minutes goes by-- 10 people are in there hacking all over me and others. the sickness was apparent in there-- the nurse comes out and tells us to be patient and for my boyfriend to sit down and stop standing. we packed our things and took off to st joseph's after that and now i'm happily in a real waiting room with actual staff who can do their jobs. never again

spent four hours just to get one minute with a terrible doctor. wrong diagnosis, no information, had to go to saint josephs a few days later to get diagnosed with acute bronchitis. when the nurse came in after the doctor left he asked "what did the doctor say", i paused and thought about it, he said nothing. no explanation for any of my symptoms, nothing. avoid this place at all costs. if i'm taken there by an ambulance i will refuse to enter. go anywhere else.

horrible. only one md for patient care and hes a surgeon...dr barker...does not give adequate attention to admitted patients cause hes too busy with surgery. high wbc count so infection, get on abt only one dose in then nothing for over 12 hours. how is that suppose to work? wbc still elevated but nothing else ordered and he is in surgery? no internist to follow up when hes not available? no consistancy in care.  what a joke. but hey i'll bet billing wont lack.   no star

the staff are helpful and comforting for the most part. the wait times are long so expect to wait. if you are being admitted, bring your own food and snacks. the standard for cleanliness is great. i see a lot of areas that are cleaned throughly. my room and the bathroom area was very clean. the staff are responsive and make you feel at home.

this was my 2 second outpatient experience. the staff as before where very comforting and polite. i highly recommend this hospital for your medical needs. the nurses and doctors where very supportive and through. the staff made sure you knew where and when to arrive,have someone to pickup and ,have  wheelchair service to your car. if you need a persciptions the have a pharmacy on the premises . the nurses have great bedside minors. if you looking to have service speak with you doctor about this location.

i had to come to the hospital to reverse a procedure that i had to have emergency surgery for.  here is my experience with this hospital: check in for my 2nd  surgery was extremely easy and i was in the prep area in for about 10 minutes.   everyone from basic technicians to the surgeons took the time to explain my procedure to me and to answer any questions.

the facilities are admittedly older, however everything seemed to be well maintained with no signs of aging.  the hospital can be state of the art and brand new and still get a one star rating for me because of the quality of the people that work there. at virginia beach general hospital, the people all the way up the chain are wonderful and i could not of been treated better.  my procedure was a success and the experience overall was superb.  i had a life threatening injury and the care made a difficult situation better.   an overall very good experience.  get your colon scoped after 50.

am here for a procedure for my mother.  the procedure went well the nurses were truly helpful and explained everything as they went they procedure.  her area is very clean and sanitized.  she was comfortable as she can be thru the entire procedure.  which is a big relief.

i've been to medvet on a few occasions with my beloved furbaby 'abby'. 
i've been to the worthington location, as well as the hilliard location, and the hilliard location by far shines the brightest. 

i think it's really important to know that med vet is an emergency vet service. just as you would expect a large bill from a regular er for your own medical issues - such would be my expectations for med vet. if you feel you have an issue where your pet could wait until a check up with your vet, then you really should wait. it's $100 fee just for entering their doors. 

it was an early sunday morning - i knew my vet's office would not be open, so my only option knowing the inevitable was here was to take my abby to medvet. i won't post the entire story of my day, but just know that the staff there was caring and compassionate from start to end, which is all i would have expected even from my own vet's office. 

the staff gave us plenty of time to be with abby before euthanasia and were compassionate and sympathetic knowing that this process was both overwhelming for myself and my husband. up until the end and abby's last breath they made her comfortable and calm. 

they offered a few different options for handling the body. we went with their cremation option, and they also include keepsakes such as an ink paw print, clipping of fur & clay paw-print with their name printed in it. they outsource the cremation process, but the company that did handle it did a great job and got her ashes processed within a business day. 
 
there were so many tears that day, but the process was made easier knowing how compassionate the doctors and assistants were when handling pets. she was always treated well - even with minor injuries, or ailments when we had to visit the 1-3 times over her 11 year span. 

rip abby and thank-you medvet for caring and taking gingerly care of our old dog!

i went to the hospital on february 18th 2020 and honestly my visit should be free. i had the most unprofessional nurse. she was rude and condescending and yelled at me the whole time. she made a comment about my age and told me to grow up. my bone had just broken and i was crying. i've never been so appalled  in all my life at how disrespectfully i was treated. she told me there were women and children in the hospital as if i was a patient who didn't matter at all.... i am a 25 year old women by the way so that comment was offensive. i can't tell you how genuinely livid and upset i am at her behavior. it made my stay and my pain so much worse. why does it matter what age, race, or sex i am? it's 2020 everyone should be treated with kindness. i think you are the one who needs to grow up red headed nurse. also their refusing to give me a discount when their staff did a piss poor job... so i'm paying full price for bad service. that doesn't seem right.

suffered a stroke in switzerland in june.  in august of this year, i had the same symptoms.  an initial scan was done and immediately i was told i was suffering from migraines.  this was before i even saw a neurologist.  i was admitted and tests were scheduled but not completed. i was seen by a neurologist who told me i had not suffered a stroke in august or june.  he told me my symptoms were not stroke symptoms and that he doubted i had suffered a stroke in june.  when asked if he had reviewed my records and scans from switzerland he admitted he hadn't.   when the scans were shown to him, he hurried off, discharged me without completing the tests that had been ordered.  i reported this and six months later the only response i got was that they were busy.  when i consulted with my current neurologist, he informed me the symptoms i had suffered, especially with my history were stroke symptoms.  the staff was overworked, and the doctors were rushed and not prepared to treat the patients.

eighty-six year old  mom was vomiting for 24 hours.  hospital got her in immediately.  had to call in a specialist for a picc line, and mom had to be admitted for rehydration, anti-nausea meds.  from arrival to getting settled in her overnight room was less than two hours.  the emergency room looked like a hotel room.  private, quiet, peaceful, unlike bigger hospitals that are noisy, stressful, and always have the loudest alarms on monitoring equipment.  her room was just as nice with modern equipment and comfortable accommodations.  during my mom's stay, she was treated like queen for a day.  we have never been treated so wonderfully respectful at any hospital as we were at this micro hospital.  these medical personnel actually listen to you and spend time serving your needs with compassion and professionalism.  i have found the best place in vegas for medical care.
fac_name: Dignity Health - St. Rose Dominican - West Flamingo Campus

review:
i hear a lot of complaints about st john's, but really i think complaints can be made of all medical facilities: and they are usually based on the experience you have with your independent doctor and medical staff.
st. john is always very clean.  the check-in staff, always friendly and pretty quick. plenty of parking options and clearly marked signs to tell you where to go.
as stated, doctors and ma's can be hit or miss. i have had both of my children here: the first doctor, (who has been there for years i couldn't stand, it was a horrible delivery, yadayada); the second doctor was a midwife and she was amazing-perfect experience, not a single complaint.
my kids primary doctor as well as mine and my husbands are all located here and i have had all of my medical work done here for about 10 years without a real issue.  my primary doctor is excellent and i have had three er experiences-two were really great, one was not so much. but this past saturday my husband had to go to the er for an open hand wound. he was stitched up and out within about an hour! unheard of. the nurse and doctor were professional and on-top of it. don't necessarily believe all of the reviews-yep, people have bad experiences but the hospital/facility itself is not bad in my experience.

absolutely amazing er staff, i brought my daughter in at 3:00 in the morning shortness of breath and her hands curled up into fists. they took her immediately and the er rns and doctor was there before i could get her jacket off. after 4 hours of constant attention they got her breathing under control and she was admitted.  fast track to the 7th floor. absolutely amazing the nurses were so calming and caring towards my daughter and even me. the reassuring words and care they did convince me to go home and they'd keep me updated on any news. come to find out she was severely depleted of vitamins and minerals after a few bags of magnesium,  saline,  and a few other bags they were confident to release her to our home. (less than 10 minutes away) they called my daughter a few hours later to see how she was doing and to remember her of a follow up dr. friday.
wow absolutely amazing to he treated with kindness care understanding and like a true human being.  
thank you so much for your well trained staff.

if i could give this place 0 stars i would.
this place is a fuckin joke.

i went in with a concern that i was pregnant with an iud i have in place because i have grown sensitive to smells, my back and hips hurt super bad, bloated, and nauseous. i have never missed a period with my iud i've had it for over a year and this is my first missed period. 

not only did a male doctor talk to me, he also would not listen to me, talked down to me about my symptoms and issues and concerns that are going on.

like what the hell is wrong with you?!
if you can't find my iud by opening my pelvis you better start trying to find the fuckin thing and do your fuckin job as a hospital and treat the medical emergancy you are refusing to treat assholes!

i am here today to see my sleep specialist dr.loffer. if you have sleep troubles i highly recommend him. i have narcolepsy which is a sleep disorder. it's a terrible thing to have. i can fall asleep at any moment. it might be while you are talking to me and you will think i'm bored if you don't know about my narcolepsy or i might fall asleep in the middle of a sentence while i'm talking to you. i have no control over it and i hate it. i take special medicine at night to make me sleep and medicine in the morning to keep me awake. right now it isn't working at all. i fall asleep over and over during the day. i even fall asleep when i'm chewing my food. it's dangerous because i could easily choke. it's not just about me, but all people who have narcolepsy. the staff here is very nice. dr. loffer is nice and he is very smart. sometimes he talks very far over my head, but then he brings it down to earth. he cares about the patient. that's the important thing. the only bad thing i have to say is that he is always behind. not just a little bit, but a lot.

if i could give this hospital negative stars i would.  if you are in need of medical attention go to durango or farmington, or have your loved ones make sure they fly you out. the staff is uncaring and assume that everyone is a drug addict. the only clean surface in the whole building is the sinks that are supposed to be being used to wash their hands in. sent me home with a cantaloupe size hernia and said they "thought" it was a fatty cyst. no test done, just a guess of what was wrong.  they have let my loved one run out of insulin 4 times because melissa churchill wouldn't refill the prescription. and then watch the billing,  then love to double dip. they get payment from your insurance company and then also bill you.

my mom has been here a lot. the staff is caring. the food is good. the professionalism is top notch. 

who likes hospitals? but it's also clean and a comfortable place to sleep overnight in the room with your loved one.

the worst experience. hannah b from management ask that i email their public relations department. after two emails to the pr department i finally received a response from hannah b stating that she gave my information to their patient advocate. you must be kidding. forwarding my information to the patient advocate is a joke -- this "resolution" is nothing but delegating the issue to somebody else. i previously forwarding my information to the patient advocate before hannah ever responded to me and and it took all of 2 minutes. if you are reading this review, i highly encourage you to look at all of the yelp reviews below with a low rating attached. they all have something in common, which is a business owners response stating "that they will review this information internally and email the business owners at publicrelations@healthonecares.com". this business owners reply to yelp comments is nothing but an effort to protect their brand, which is undoubtably failing. there is truly no resolution from this request to email the pr department. i contacted the patient advocate nearly 2 weeks ago without any response since. to make matters worse, sky-ridge billing billed my claim as an accident when in actuality i went in for the flu. how does such nonsense happen? i have no idea but i am in the middle of this debacle now. 

please note that sky-ridge did absolutely nothing for me when i went into the er. yes they gave me a flu test, which isn't used by many hospitals due to the inaccuracy of the results. littleton adventist hospital er physician refused to give me flu test because of the many false positives that result from the test. yet, as a result from visiting skyridge, who discharged me with nothing more then a an advil prescription; i acquired a bill that was sent to insurance for over $10k, with a patient responsibility of $3k+. i went to littleton adventist er the following day due to the poor treatment at sky-ridge and my bill for much better treatment a blood panel and prescriptions was $4k with a patient respisnbilty of $1,888.00. 

all in all, if you have the ability to go to any er please go to any other place other than sky-ridge. i highly recommend other hospitals not from a quality standpoint but from a billing and claims standpoint.

wow. i cannot say enough about the level of compassionate care i received here. i had to have a surgery that i was really nervous about. at my pre-op  appointment, i totally broke down and the  nurse was so sweet. she even made note of my surgery date and said she'd try to come see me after i got out of surgery. the day of, my surgeon,  dr. jeffrey james, reassured me (again) and answered all of my questions. my anesthesiologist kept me laughing up until i  knocked out and my post-op team was so kind and attentive. the food looked amazing, but i wasn't able to eat much and the room was comfortable. the nursing staff throughout the night and and the following day was also great. they were great at helping me manage my pain and checking in often.

ridiculous! 20 year old goes in with pain when she moves her eyes... i'm thinking sinus infection but sent her to er to be sure and get meds. never gets taken out of waiting! they tell her, unsure, need ct scan very concerning. so she waits with an iv in the waiting room for five hours. scan is done.... pain meds previously offered never given. results...nothing abnormal so we don't know.  no follow up, no nothing. after 45 minutes they finally took out the iv gave her an advil and sent her home with zero information.  your hospital disgusts me.  she came to you for help and because stomach flu was taking over the er she didn't matter enough for you to pay attention to. shame on you!

i provided my insurance card when i came in and once again when i got the full bull in the mail. a few months goes by and now i have a bill in collections that has reported to my credit. their best response was " we've put it on hold and once insurance kicks in it will be removed". 

thanks for nothing sky ridge. now i have a hit on my credit for no reason.

it was scary being transported in an ambulance but i was glad to be there. definitely has great staff. er nurse was kind of rude but, nurses are nurses. 
i'm sure she was having a tough day too.

came to pick up someone who was supposed to discharge, they said it would be ten minutes, then they said we had to wait for respiratory to come see us. when they eventually did show up, they literally handed us a business card to call a number and have oxygen dropped off.. that was it. waited 3+ hours in the room for that, leaving after noon when we were ready to walk out the door at 9:00am. the care was fine but the wait time is ridiculous. day wasted sitting around waiting.

i am quite disappointed that in light of the coronavirus outbreak and extra measures- the hospital has ignorantly placed a sign at the entrance asking people if they have any symptoms or have been to wuhan, china. the virus is global and we have a reported 1200 cases in the us with thousands around the world. i could easily come from italy or germany and have contracted the virus. let's not feed the xenophobia anymore. this is no longer a "chinese" concern but a world concern. they also ask that if you have a cough to wear a mask. but right after i walked through i stood in line with a visitor at starbucks that was coughing! get smarter people- this is not the first global health crisis and definitely not the last!

my brother was transferred here from ucheath highlands ranch, where his care was so fast, and felt like the doctors and nurses really cared and were concerned about his health! as soon as we got to sky ridge care was so slow, and he wasn't even hooked up to any type of machine to check his oxygen levels or blood pressure. when someone needs blood transfusions you would think he would be automatically hooked up to machines! fast forward to tonight 12/10, he hasn't had an appetite all day and as soon as dinner comes he's starving, and finally agrees to have some soup, we ordered at about 4:50, food arrived at nurses stationary 5:20. we are wondering where the food is and call to check, they tell us it was delivered at 5:20 it was then 6. i have them re order his food because it was obviously cold. i ask them if i should go back to pick up the food or if they will deliver it. they say they will deliver it and of course again they do not! i have to go out there and grab it so my brother can have his dinner! if my brother was alone here i can guarantee he wouldn't have gotten his food! way to go 3rd floor at sky ridge hospital!!! you are all great nurses who cares if your patients get food and fast care!

i was transferred to rch from corona regional medical center for a neurosurgery need due to an infected lumbar surgery from another hospital & medical provider. stayed at the hospital for 8 days. my overall experience is very good except a particular "dr simone singh". 
she spoke to me before discharge & reassured me to prescribe adequate pain medication. i was discharged 3 days after spinal surgery with no pain prescription. i called dr simone singh's office next morning to get pain meds. she never called back. walking 10-15 feet w/ a walker, dragging my left leg is painfully miserable. i have been in tremendous pain from left hip down the long bones of my left leg each time i bear weight or even move. 

stay away from dr simone singh. she is incompassionate  & neglectful. dr singh is zero star!

i've came here to deliver all my three kids and i had one bad experience in 2014 for my first born when the nurses shifted shifts. the second nurse was unprofessional but when we complained the nurse in charge handled it, i continued to have my two other kids here and had the best experience ever , the nurses and my dr were the absolute best and attended to mine and my families every needs.

if i could give zero stars i would for this visit. my father in law was admitted to the hospital for stroke symptoms. this is the room they put him in! there was blood all over the walls and cabinets and it was not from him. the room was clearly not cleaned after the last patient. when we my father in law told his nurse about it she just laughed and did absolutely nothing about it. this is completely unacceptable! so many violations made here. hospitals have evs for this reason to have infection control.

very disappointed with experience at emory er last night - which has been our go-to hospital for years!  my husband had a head trauma and was bleeding from a severe wound so we drove to the er at midnight. 

there were two hospital administrators checking in patients and one yelled over to us "are you here to see a patient" or "checking in" and when i replied back "checking in" she yelled right back "well it's a 4 to 5 hour wait". yikes!  

there were 6 other folks in the waiting room so when it was our turn to check in i asked why the long wait and she said they were slammed with flu season (which is totally understandable as to why she was so stressed). 

i'm looking at my own stressed husband with blood dripping down his face and decided to leave. 

we arrived at north forsyth hospital in cumming at 12:30am - what a totally different experience.  waiting room was empty!  greeted by a super friendly staff.  they have a triage room right in the waiting area and took care of the bleeding gash immediately. 

we were there for 5 hours running extensive tests and found the doctors and nurses to be friendly and attentive. 9 stitches later we were sent home with recommendations for more tests. 

while emory is closer, north forsyth hospital is an excellent option and will be our new go-to er. having the triage room at the entrance in the waiting room is a big differentiator as you get immediate attention - which is comforting after a horrible accident.  

i understand how stress can impact customer service and quality of care - and while i'm thankful emory is in our backyard, i expect more from a hospital er. 

the triage room at north forsyth is exceptional (and comforting) for treating immediate wounds and the quality of customer service and genuine customer care my husband received from the staff was outstanding. kudos north forsyth.

went to er. was seen quickly. and thought i was being taken care of. but once they drew labs and shot an xray. that's when i felt forgotten. i got to the er around 2130 finally checked out around 0100. they refused to give me any result to take with me. stating is was hospital policy and that i could come back tomorrow to records to get them. the charge nurse was rude and pushy.  i do not recommend this location

mercy's getting 5 stars cause of awesome  doctors & nurses that have helped me & my friend every time we go & the blood  draw station staff that say hello & ask how's things are and now & then tell a joke. my illness keeps me from doing a lot i get tired quick if i do to much at one time. but thanks to everyone at mercy hospital  the staff the coffee shop there & yes the cafeteria staff & the food they put out thank you for making our day brighter. godspeed god bless  merry christmas

so we when to the er because my dad had a heartattack  and they got everything done really fast and then when they took a x-ray it was correct but it took a little longer then they expected but they got everything tooken care of and the way to make it fast is calling the hospital before going then you'll be out of there in no time!!

a few years ago, a friend tried to harm herself by overdosing on tylenol. this was a serious and critical moment for her and her family. she was in icu on a vent. as the family and i are waiting in the waiting room, shift change happens and i hear a group of nurses walking down the hall talking about my friend, stating " well , maybe she had a headache" while laughing and the other laughingly said "well this will be her last" 
i'm also a nurse. i understand that our jobs are hard and people do stupid things. but you have to think about when and where you say things. if her family would have heard that......thankfully it was just me. i will never go to this hospital if i have a choice. she didn't.

my hospital stay was in december 2017, two years ago. finally leaving a review. i'd like to think most of the one star reviews are from people who were recently discharged and are still pissed and going through their recovery. i was sent to college hospital cerritos from
hoag newport beach after being placed on a hold. kaiser only had a bed for me at this hospital, none in orange county. this is solely on 3north and my experience. 

pros:
-social worker was amazing 
-the guy who ran the groups was super sweet and very passionate about what he did 
-the groups were all day so it kept you out of your head 
-did not extend my 72 hr hold (psychiatrist hospital brownie points are real... take your meds, go to groups, eat, and be nice and leave with a treatment plan. fight them and they will hold you longer) 

cons:

-since no one showers it's hard for a nurse to take you serious when you request showers and get told not right now 
-only get to see the psychiatrist twice once during first day and once before being discharged 
-diagnosis is bullshit a so just follow up with your regular psychiatrist 
-everything was calm until my last day there when two homeless people came into the unit and decided to flip food trays and chairs/tables. don't worry everything is plastic so it doesn't hurt tooo bad when you get accidentally hit with a flying chair. 


if in orange county id recommend st. joseph's in orange psychiatric unit for adults and uci's in orange for adolescents. my stay in 2018's st.joseph's in orange was much more therapeutic and have successfully remained outside the hospital since then. i'd like to think college hospital is was the start of mental health wellness road. now i go to a support group once a week and have a great psychiatrist and therapist.l

i spent 18 awful days at college hospital cerritos.
juden valdez, md was my doctor. he completely over medicated me with horrendous side effects. he doesn't listen to his patients. he has an authoritarian approach to medicine, and he is inept and dangerous. he violated the hippocratic oath and because he harmed me physically, emotionally and mentally.

under the care of college hospital, our daughter was a 100 lbs and started having seizures on day 5.  they contacted us and asked to come pick her up as they did not have the means to treat her epilepsy.  we told them that our daughter does not have epilepsy.  when we arrived to pick her up, she started having a seizure and my wife and i screamed for a medical dr.  a nurse came out and told us this was normal and that we should take her to the er.  dr. valdez over medicated our daughter and would never discuss treatment.  she has since tested positive for anti-nmda encephalitis-which is not a mental illness.   neurological history of disorders must be considered when approaching psychiatric patients.  if you're only tool is a hammer, you'll try to solve all problems with a nail. 
dr. valdez needs to retool his care because he is clearly harming people.

if you want to get a good idea of the broken healthcare system, this is the place.  understandably the doctors have the ultimate say in patient care here yet the doctors are all but invisible.  the docs make decisions (to push pills) on feedback from the case workers who are clearly overwhelmed.  you are guaranteed to be forced to stay longer than expected.  they don't have the time to address your case in a prompt manner hence you're in for a long stay and at risk of bodily harm from your unpredictable fellow patients.  the longer stay also covers the hospital from potential liability assuming something goes wrong shortly after your release.  your longer stay is financially beneficial for the hospital as well.  the nurses hands are tied so don't bother.

it's been now one year since i stepped foot outside this hospital when i was placed on a hold for attempting suicide last year. it's bad enough living with what i tried to do and even worse remembering what happened to me while in the care of this hospital. i'd like to start off saying that i'm still not fully okay or better but i have been getting professional help (not what this place at all provides) each day gets better but some days are a struggle. i feel like it is extremely important to speak out about this so that no women, or man ever goes through what i did and can possibly save themselves from going here if you're needing help. on arrival i was terrified and in an extreme fragile state. i had no clothes and was given only a hospital gown that was open in the back. when i said i didn't feel comfortable being exposed like this in front of male patients, a male staff said to me "only the privileged are allowed clothing" after that i sat in a chair terrified and lost for a couple of hours until another staff noticed me and found a place to put me. the first room they put me in i was attacked by a female patient. i was moved to another room with other women but across the hall was a room full of men. once again i politely pleaded for clothing so i didnt feel exposed. i told another staff member i didn't feel safe sleeping or resting in any open room near grown men with nothing but a sheet covering me. the staff member said no and that nothing was going to happen to me and if so to just scream and they'd come running. i kept to myself the rest of the night, i pretty much stayed in the bed they gave me the whole time because i didn't feel comfortable walking around in a gown with nothing on underneath. while keeping to myself, sitting in bed, reading a self help book for guidance someone had entered the room. i didnt look up to see who it was because i was reading and was scared and to nervous to be social with anyone there. the person who my six week postpartum appointment was five minutes.  

someone is going to comment and tell me to speak with patient relations. i did all of that, and again, my concerns were brushed off. i received a follow up call from a physician at the hospital. while i received an apology for not being offered the procedure while in recovery, he pretty much blamed me  because i had asked questions about epidural stuff early on in my pregnancy. apparently, if you do this, you have a hunch that something could go wrong. the words "should be fine" and "reassured that epidural is possible" should have made me realize that everything was going to go wrong and would be my fault. he also said he spoke to the doctor who was in the room with me, and she had told him she thought she was helpful and reassuring. i'm not sure why he even bothered to call me if he was going to just invalidate the feelings i have about my birth experience. so thank you for that follow up call! 

this was me at my most vulnerable emotionally and physically, and everyone forgot that behind all this "medical talk" was a person enduring a traumatic event. these were supposed to be some of the happiest moments of my life, and this hospital took those from me.  

it would have been nice to have had someone acknowledge that what i went through was terrible. instead, i feel that they either ignore or attempt to blame me. go elsewhere for medical care. no one should be treated this way.

ah. healthcare in the us. your  fear of getting bad  treatment only rivals your fear of going  bankrupt after. 

it's the system  they say, and yes to a certain extent that's right. in what  other system  can a piece of medical software promote addictive drugs to doctors  disguised as real advice but is actually just a kickback from a drug maker?  that doctors went along with it isn't exactly reassuring, but a system with profit motive and dealing in life and death can't promise  a good outcome. 

however you do find medical people rising to the challenge to make the system better. and not just in television shows. 

is robert wood johnson such a place? no, not at all. want to  know when your surgery will be? tough you aren't going to  know. want to park to visit  your loved one? twenty dollars please!  want receptionists who are kind and aware that  people looking for room  numbers may be under stress and offer kindness? well, move your ass into the right line and shut your mouth. 

you are treated like you are visiting a prisoner   your loved one will be treated like  one too. i can't imagine in an actual emergency what it would be like. 

the argument in the us against nationalized healthcare is that one will lose the quality of care in the us. it's no accident the argument has now been people in insurance will not have  jobs; places like this make the quality argument weak. nowhere is the emphasis on care  on display here. if you have a choice don't come here. it's dismal indeed.

i wish i had the time to really explain my experience at henry mayo.  in july, i had a bad kidney infection and went against my gut instinct to go to cedars, and opted to go to henry mayo because it is closer.  i should have followed my gut instinct.  

their website said that the er had a five-minute wait.  

i was in the er for eight hours without a room, just stuck on a gurney in the hallway with no pain medicine (i was in excruciating pain), no care whatsoever, and had to be moved to another hallway at one point due to some loud and crazy criminal who was threatening patients (cops were everywhere).  it was a nightmare.

finally i was put into a room, and received pain medicine.  the nurses felt really bad for me, and that was appreciated.  the room was shared (unnecessary as they had many empty rooms) and my roommate wanted the room so hot i was dripping sweat.  the nurses called the room "the sauna" because it was so hot in there.  i begged them to turn down the temperature and every time they tried, she'd cry and beg them to turn it up because she was so cold (even with many blankets).  i am not a complainer, and not demanding in the slightest. she was very loud and very demanding.  so she won out.  they could have moved me into another room--that would have been great.  but no.  it was days of this...it was awful.  finally, i was ready to go home and because they didn't have the proper staff to release me (it was a friday and they are understaffed on the weekends), they wanted me to stay an extra 2.5 days because they would be back on monday.  

i could not deal with this for that long--besides, i did not want to overcharge my insurance company (that seemed like fraud to me), so i checked myself out ama.  they threatened that my insurance would not pay (this is blatantly not true).  they tried everything to scare me into staying.  my doctor even told me to go home.  they refused to talk to me once i signed on the dotted line, and would not even give me outprocessing papers.  i had to walk myself to my car.  fine with me.  the nurses were really pissed.  i found out later that they are audited based on number of amas, and they get dinged for each one.  i'm sorry for that, but maybe they should run a better business.

top all of that off with receiving a $1500 bill from the er doc--the doc i never saw.  turns out that, though the hospital is in my network, they hire out of network doctors for their er.  now i'm fighting with my insurance company, the doctor, and the hospital.  this is ridiculous.  this has happened to me before--getting an out of network doc in an er--and now i always ask if the doc is in my network.  if not, i won't see them and/or i'll go to another er.  i did this on this trip, and was told that he was in my network.  they lied.  he is not.  this is quite a racket, henry mayo--taking the people who need the care the most, who put their trust in you, and give them the bait-and-switch with out-of-network doctors who will bill as much as they want for their "care" (even if there is no care).

between the misleading information on their website for er wait times, the lack of care in the er, the hospital experience, ama experience, and final billing--this was a nightmare that i hope i can save you from.  skip it.  it's just not worth the convenience of "local".  

providence holy cross is not far from here--and it's a great hospital.  next time in the need of an er, i'll either go there or to cedars.  never again, henry mayo.
