do not go to sutter lakeside hospital er!

one of the worst hospitals i have been too in about 20 states. unbelievably dysfunctional staff that consistently violates patients rights and neglects the standard of care in the er department. i even brought this up over the phone and in writing to the patient relations staff. typically this department spanning most hospitals is the one that holds the many other departments accountable for their conduct and behavior in hopes for training. that's the scary part of the last line of defense doesn't value feedback or act on the many issues that run over this hospital then i'm afraid it is too far gone. beware many assistants with zero accredited training will often walk in and attempt to act as licensed medical providers but are nothing more than admin support. make sure you get a copy of your rights and hold them to not violating your rights. make them introduce themselves, state their names and positions. do not assume anything. please don't be like me if you have transportation  go anywhere else!! and please, if your going to respond with a generic response that is generated automatically, save your time . i expressed my concerns in writing and over the phone with no interest in bettering your hospital. how can you operate so egregiously?? how does the rogue staff that works there live with themselves?

on monday evening, december 30, 2019, i sustained a broken ankle injury and was taken to the er room of memorial community hospital in blair, ne.  i received fast, excellent care in the er from dr. jeremy lee and the nursing and x-ray staff.  my dislocated foot/ankle was realigned in the proper position, x-rays were taken, and i was put in a cast to transport me back to my home in kansas city.  
i appreciate the professional care and kind attitude of dr. lee and hospital staff.
fac_name: Memorial Community Hospital and Health System

review:
i'm new to the area and my past hospitals experiences have been at stanford or ucsf. my expectations are high on quality of care. i came to the er on a sunday evening and was pleasantly surprised by the fast admission and triage process.  during my initial tests another issue was found.  it was impressive how thorough they were and how they were able to bring in specialists on short notice.  i spend one night on the second floor  next night on the first floor.

the thing that stood out to me was that every single person i met from the guard at the gate, admissions, er doctors, hospitalist dr omogrosso, nursing team, to the janitor were personable, collaborative, helpful, and generally liked their job and people in general.  whatever the management team is doing to motivate their staff to work together and  show patients they are important is working. i spent one night on the top floor and the second night on the first floor. 

my experience was the hospital is clean and the facility while older is well  kept.  the staff is pleasant, knowledgeable and works well together.  doctor are approachable and take the time  to be sure you understand. if you look at the review this hospital has online it's terrifying but that was certainly not my experience.  maybe things have changed for the better.  i would go back if necessary.

after i left the update, they connected me with someone who told me a) bills are not negotiable and b) the second bill which was just for the doctor (not the hospital) would need to be dealt with with the doctor billing service directly. i called them and the only way to contest a bill is to fax a written statement describing the billing code and how the service i received is not accurate. im going to report these folks to the medical board. truly outrageous. more like dealing with a credit card company or a phone company than organization of people who literally took an oath to help. disgusting.

as a point of reference, i had to go the er again for a very similar issue. this time i went to auburn. my total bill was $74.11 instead of over $2000.

my family member went to the er. he was pretty sick. he was diagnosed and treated well. his nurse scott his nurse kept us updated. dr alsop was great to him as well. thank you sierra nevada for providing such great service.

doctor gave me an allergy med, apparently she doesn't believe in clarifying questions like did you throw up, itch, break out in hives and pull you hair out. it's ok send your patients on trips to pharmacies for drugs their charts say they are allergic too! i didn't catch it till pharmacy, too much shock and doctor wouldn't change it after i bought it back.  don't use the er at providence milwaukie,or! they asked me what to next 5 times just to discharge and get a splint. charting is a thing and it was dead in there, how many times should you have to tell them what you're waiting for. teaching is very important but it really does matter how you teach.l

quick service with no one there, but poor medical skills. spent a total of 15 minutes in er and less than 2 minutes with doctor.  did get a prescription to help, but only enough for 3 days, knowing my follow up appt was 7 days out.  then the after visit summary suggested follow up with a pediatric doctor in wentzville ( for a 70 year old)??   waste of my time, but at least it was quick. 
note - other friends have had better outcomes here, but mine was of little value.  dr sutterer was no help and provided no diagnostic services or even attempted to do so.

my daughter is getting an mri today! the nurses and doctors are amazing here. they have everything children need and want to be comfortable.  the staff goes there extra distance to ensure my daughter was happy.  they knew she loved music and came by with an ipad for her to listen to her favorite songs.  the whole team talked and went over every detail about her mri with me since she needed to be under general anesthesia. the outside play area is really great, it's like a little adventure for small people....

arrived 10 min before my scheduled appointment... then waited 1.5+ hours before seeing the doctor.  traffic to and from stanford can be notorious....so a simple doctor check up took over 4 hours.  yes, they don't want you to be late for your appointment  but it's ok for patient to wait hours.

i don't know if the hospital changed a few procedures because this time it was a whole other experience. first off the room this time was brand new and very comfortable, one nurse though stood out so much to us. in all our experiences with nurses elvina choi stood out! she was so caring and helpful, best nurse that we have ever had. she made this experience as best as possible for us. we will not forget her. this time around the hospital did well and the nurses were great.

good staff nice hospital parking fees take full advantage of you anything over two hours is $10 and it doesn't matter you pay every time you go in or out considering the situations of some people having surgeries that require multiple visits from family and the weekly pass being $50 it's a bit excessive

i delivered my first and only baby here in july. i can tell you that this was the absolute worst hospital experience of my life. the hospital is under construction. i had a c-section and was stuck here for 4 days. while recovering from a c-section and having to care for a new baby (baby stays in the room with you 24/7), i had to endure the noise of the construction. jack hammers and pounding all day long. i couldn't sleep. the nurses were always late with my meds. i only had one nurse that i will say was great and i can't remember her name. 
our room was dated and every time we flushed the toilet, the pipes would rattle loudly and wake whomever was sleeping- including the baby. on my 2nd night, my call button did not work. i complained to my nurse and she insisted that it worked. i called again to get help to the bathroom, my baby was crying, and my husband was out. no one came for over 30 min. finally, after i really got mad, the nurse realized that the call button in fact did not work and the head nurse had to call engineering to replace it. 
the food was so unhealthy and just awful for a new mother that is healing. my husband had to go to gelsons to get us food. 
i'm sad to say that i regret having my baby here. it ruined my experience. if i didn't have a wonderful ob that delivered here and knew about the construction noise, i would have gone to cedars or thousand oaks. what a horrible experience.
they get two stars for being close to my home and for the one wonderful nurse i had. she was so kind and thoughtful. she added a bow to my daughter's little cap.

as a new patient as u of a cancer center, abd i could not be happier. my former oncologist never took the time to do basic testing for side effects of my treatment which is done regularly at u if a. 
the staff is incredibly helpful and friendly. i can even got my meds filled on site which is very convenient. in addition to excellent care, the new building is beautiful. each infusion space is separated so you have a feeling of privacy in your interactions with nurses & doctors. they also offer social workers that helped me to find a decent therapist for the depression that can come with living with cancer. if i could give 10 stars i would!

i recently had orthopedic surgery at this hospital. the first thing i noticed was that all staff, from the front security guards, maintenance staff, administration/ clerical staff, nursing/ health care staff, were all helpful and went out of their way. and they all seemed happy to be there. this is a "patients first" hospital. the facility was very clean and well maintained. no peeling tiles, no curling carpets, no dirty bathrooms. by the way, the food was truly superb, restaurant quality - not something one would expect from a hospital. the medical care provided to me pre and post surgery could not have been better. i spent 3 days there and the medical care was spot on. ultimately, i'd prefer to avoid hospitals. but if i had to choose, syosset hospital would be at the top of the list. yes, i highly recommend this hospital for orthopedics.

i don't even know where to start.   my daughter was referred for depression.   the info during the 3 hours of getting checked in was extremely vague.  and after seeing a lot of the reviews i now realize this place is a joke.   my daughter got ahold of me on the 2nd day of being there and asked to be picked up.  which i did.  being told that with her volunteering to go to intermountain rather than involuntary.  she was free to go at anytime. not advising that insurance may not pay.   i am pissed.  they withhold info until if u do discharge early., they don't tell u that til u are about to walk out the door at the end.  i asked my daughter what she thought about the place.  in her words, mom they did nothing.  we sat in a group setting for about 20 minutes, and then ate and hung out with kids.  claiming an adult daycare.  poorly ran and disorganized and no help at all.  staff comes acrossed rude.  they r quick to throw out your current medication and medicate on their own.  which they seem to be big on.   i am not impressed and advise others to carefully know what u r getting yourself into before enrolling your kids here.  i waited another 3 plus hours to get her discharged , nothing ever being said about the insurance not being paid and it may be out of pocket  for the early release until she was ready to walk out the door. so extremely unprofessional and no concern for the parent and what this could do financially...waiting now on insurance to see if it is covered or i see a court case if they try to slap me with a bill.  sick at how they purposely leave out pertinent details when it comes to the billing.   and being a single mom i can not afford this if they come knocking at my door.

"out of network" doctors for an "in network" hospital, enjoy the surprise bills every time you go to this place. absolute worst hospital network i've ever had to use. i'd rather drive hours away to literally anything else.
oh, and don't forget how many times they code things wrong and leave it up to the patient to figure it out.. hopefully you'll get reimbursed within a year, i'm still waiting for a $900 screw up to be resolved.
after almost 7 months, their billing error was finally corrected. some of the senior staff was helpful.

the receptionist was so rude and was talking sarcastically. i called twice to take an appointment, the first receptionist hung up on me after leaving me on hold for 5 whole minutes. the second receptionist (alicia) was talking sarcastically the whole time and kept repeating every single thing i told her. and this experience was expected since this place has a 2.6 total rating on google maps.
fac_name: The Children's Hospital at St. Peter's University Hospital

review: great hospital and er! fastest emergency facility i've ever been to. super nice and knowledgeable staff.

i had outpatient surgery yesterday and was so pleased with the quality of care i received from being admitted to being discharged. i don't remember all the names but everyone was fantastic! i had surgery done at backus years ago which was horrible!!!! which made me nervous but this totally made me at ease.
fac_name: Yale-New Haven Hospital Saint Raphael Campus

review:
ten hours plus!
over five hours in the filthy waiting room. the ladies room was a horror show of filth and unflushed toilets. 
five hours in the back with a pa and a nurse, visiting off and on. 
someone gave an eye exam-overkill, as it was done a week prior. told them that!
md breezed by to perform a visual. 
no info, no updates, no communication. 
finally, rn stops in and removes my iv and tells me that i am being released. infectious disease deemed me okay! really?
my insurance was billed over $2200.00. 
really?
all because my primary md 'thought' the er would treat me?
all of this is upside down. hoping to not need these services again. 
still sick and seeing other parties outside of the yale network.
fac_name: Yale-New Haven Hospital Saint Raphael Campus

review: i went to the er and it was a horrible place!! the first nurse i encountered was cold and uncaring. she took an oral temp when i couldn't breathe or keep my mouth closed so that wasn't accurate and was told i didn't have a fever. the pa listened to my lungs and said i would get a breathing treatment which i never received! i was told that i was going to get prednisone and i told them that i couldn't take that but they gave it to me anyway. i was in and out of there in two hours. it was a case of treat and street but i was never treated. i would suggest going elsewhere if you want to be treated like a human being.

went in to check up on my newborns belly button since it hasn't fully healed and was nervous that it was getting infected. the check in person blanca was very sweet made the process easy and fast. she was very cordial and made sure my baby was out of harms way since he is only about 3 weeks old and there were many sick kids around. the nurse that checked his vitals nayeli was very gentle with the baby and interacted with him as he was getting his vitals. once dr akilah jackson walked in and checked the baby she talked through the whole check up and made sure all our questions were answered. over all the staff is very polite and made me feel more at ease.
i get it , jamaica hospital is not a nice place in terms of the location and facility itself.  however the quality of care is excellent and i have been treated very well.  they have great doctors.

my wife delivered our first child at mercy hospital in chicago on feb 28th, 2020.  we had such a great experience on the labor and delivery floor (3rd) that it makes me want to have another kid.
the staff in the delivery room was welcoming and the room was cozy.  my wife had a great experience - felt comfortable, safe, and informed throughout the entire labor.  she loved her ob, dr. barry - she was encouraging, honest, compassionate, and patient with us. she took care of my life and i really appreciated her for that.
after delivery, you're taken to the mother baby rooms with what have to be the best nurses in the city of chicago. they're honest, quick responding, funny, and obviously love their jobs.  thanks rose for the newborn bath that put him to sleep for 4 hours! chris and lauren, thank you for answering our questions and making us feel confident in becoming parents. martha, the on-site lactation consultant, is professional and was eager to teach my wife all about how to breastfeed.
overall, we felt welcomed and supported while on the 3rd floor at mercy. really, we just want others to know about this hidden gem because we hadn't seen any reviews about it online. thanks to the entire staff on the 3rd floor.

the doctors are good but the parking facilities are awful!! i went to see my orthopedist following knee replacement surgery. i had to park and walk about a quarter of a mile from his office because every lot was overflowing. the valet service was backed up by about 30 cars and was almost back to ballas road. this is not acceptable!

warning: long and ridiculous, but true story.

the wait time was outrageous and the staffs were unbelievably rude, also they lied to us trying to scare us into staying the night at the hospital.

i went to the er with my grandma this past sunday (12/15/19) because she was feeling really sick. we arrived at the hospital at 2:30p.m. and i was surprised there was only one other person in the waiting room. we were immediately called by the triage nurse after checking in. my encounter with that triage nurse was very unpleasant, and looking back i still can't believe how they could have someone this rude to work a position that requires so much communication with patients - when i met the nurse we immediately greeted her. she didn't greet us back and she asked us what languages we speak and i told her we speak english. while we were walking to her office she asked and i quote, "does anyone speak english? fluent english." i was like, "miss, didn't i already tell you i speak english. is my english not fluent enough?" and she somehow was offended and literally started yelling. ridiculous. i mean, why did she even have to ask? was she going to ask if i can speak fluent english with perfect grammar and american accent next? i decided to let it go and asked if we could just move on, but she refused to quite her yapping and babbling until after i have requested her to shut up and give my grandma the treatment three times.

after the triage nurse took my grandma's blood sample, we were sent to the emergency room at around 3:00 to wait for the doctor. a doctor soon came and told us they would check back one the blood test result came back. that was the last time i saw her. we didn't get any update until we were seen by a nurse at 6:30 who said my grandma was admitted to the hospital. i told her we were not staying, then she said my grandma's troponin was high which might lead to a heart attack, and that we should talk to the doctor if we refused the admission. a moment later the doctor came and i was on the phone with my cousin who is also a doctor. i let them talk and the doctor told my cousin a different story. she said the blood test result had not come back so they didn't know what happened, but she wanted to order another blood test to compare the results before we decided if we wanted to stay the night. my cousin told me later troponin doesn't cause heart attack, it should be the other way around and without the blood test result it would be impossible to tell my grandma's troponin was high. was the nurse just misinformed or was just downright lying to our faces? i'll let you be the judge. 

anyway we waited and waited but no one came to take my grandma's blood. it almost felt as if everyone's shift all ended at the same time and they all went home. at 8:30 a nurse who just started her shift finally came to draw the blood and i was told normally it would take 30 minutes for the test result to return. i couldn't help but wonder what happened with the first blood test that took forever to be processed. eventually my grandma was discharged at around 10. i guess i can understand why there were almost no one in the waiting room when we arrived.

while we were there, i was asked if i spoke english by almost everyone i met. i found it rather insulting that they even had to ask. i don't know if that is a question they were instructed to ask all asian patients or if my face is just screaming "i no speak chinglish". i hope that's not the first impression i give my clients at work. this emotionally taxing trip really made me start to doubt myself.
they didnt listen to what i was saying told her i had been taking ibuprofen and that it didnt help and they prescribed me more ibuprofen

if i could rate this hospital a negative, i would. my father came in struggling to breathe and already battling severe heart disease and heart failure. i got to my dads room at 11:30am. he was struggling to breathe and not doing well at all. a nurse never came in to check in. i finally had to hunt down a nurse by 5pm. not a single person checked on him for hours! also, they decided to discharge him at 7pm at night before they even checked his vitals. once they checked his vitals it became clear he was running 104 temp, his oxygen level was 84 and his blood pressure was dangerously low and close to a stroke low. they were about to kick him out of his bed when he was in dangerous conditions. we had to tell them we refused to leave. 95% of the nurses were rude, too busy on their phones and talking openly about other patients in front of everyone. what a joke of a hospital.

i was there for a foot problem last month that i had no clue what it was. the waiting room people and the nurses were friendly, and the doctor didn't take long to figure out what's wrong. they worked with my primary care physician and got a plan going to take care of it. there was a guy in some trauma a few rooms away, and they were very prompt in stabilizing him. if you're sick, they'll take good care of you.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare White Oak Medical Center

review:
1.  took a relative there that complained of excruciating abdominal pain. they kept them for six days--but left them as 'observation' and not inpatient.
2.  observation adventist cheat method so they can bills you at a much higher outpatient rate. they don't tell you that even with ivs, testing, and antibiotics--you still don't matter to them!
3.  physicians would promise to see you and then become a no call no show.
4.  communication is very poor.
5.  staffing is terrible.
6.  adventist is practicing a financial shell game with your hard earned money.
7.  if i had an enemy--i wouldn't even bring them here.
shame on you adventist health white oak.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare White Oak Medical Center

review:
if you have a child, don't even bother coming to this hospital. no pediatric unit (which no one mentioned after 8 hours in the er). the nurses were very good but the rest of the staff was horrible. er receptionist didn't care at all when i told her our 2 year old was having trouble breathing. she just asked if i had insurance and told me to sit down. after 8 hours of getting our little one stabilized the p.a. (we never saw a dr) told me they were going to admit her. again she never mentioned there was no pediatric unit so when ambulance drivers arrived, i was in shock. the nurse said, "well you know we are taking her to children's hospital right?"  ummm what???? we get to children's, a doctor checks her and says, "im so sorry they sent you here, your little girl is stable and should've been sent home to rest. 

btw - i emailed the address in the response and someone replied that they'd pass my email on and i've never heard from anyone.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare White Oak Medical Center

review: wow could not get my mom in the er last night, 85 year old american, had to wait for hours and hours to even be seen while coming in by ambulance, because and  i quote from the nurses, (every illegal in the area knows the hospitals are not allowed to turn them down for service, so they treat he er like the cvs minute clinic, where they belong for their minor sicknesses) so sad what we have done to america. every hospital in the area was under some sort of code red on a tuesday night! no beds  available at holy cross, washington hospital center, etc... we need to build more clinics and keep emergency rooms for emergencies not sore throats and sniffles. hope i never have to go in the er myself, staff was great, doctors, nurses, security all fantastic. nothing they can do about the politics of it all, shame, shame, shame on us for not taking care of americans first.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare White Oak Medical Center

review: very nice employees . great doctors ! came in and got good care by all the team members and doctor was very understanding  and went out of his way to find out what we can do .
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare White Oak Medical Center

review: this used to be my  go to hospital for er visits. but within the recent years, it's been busier then what i'm used to. it's a clean hospital and they provide parking at an affordable rate. most or my interactions with staff  had been extremely pleasant aside from one time with a very rude doctor.

tl;dr if you feel as though you are getting unnecessary diagnostic tests, please refuse them and state that you would like to be seen by an md before getting any tests done. while you may have to wait a bit longer, you won't have unnecessary testing/billing done. also, speak up!


this is regarding the er. i was incredibly disappointed with the care received. my little sister fainted while in the shower during her period. she had a small gash on her head-- because it was on her face we wanted to make sure there was no scarring and thus took her to the er. when we got there, they checked us in... and called us to the back for an ekg and blood work (excessive, yes, but it is the er). they took us back to the front, and called us back again for a chest x-ray. the np was walking by so we inquired as to why a chest x-ray was needed for someone who fainted (with known cause) after an ekg was already done.  the np proceeded to tell us that football players have fainted and died (completely irrelevant). i asked her if the ekg was normal, and her response was that there was syncope and we needed to find the cause of the syncope. then she asked my 18 yr old sister if she felt a vagal response. i looked up what syncope was on my phone- "fainting"? why is a medical professional using these terms when talking to patients? terrible bedside manner. my sister had to ask what she meant, and she still was unable to explain properly. i asked if my sister needed all these tests as she has been acting completely normal- she just has a cut on her forehead and i wasn't sure if it'd scar. np asked when the fall occured and i told her it was 10 am (this was about 11 hours later), and she responded she didn't realize. i asked if they would give my sister treatment without all these diagnostics tests and the np said that they would not! we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor. 
the poor doctor came in a while later and was very sweet. i was ready to just have my sister receive treatment and leave, but my mother said it was important to tell/ask about what happened because other patients need protection to. i then went into detail of everything happened, and said i felt the chest x-ray was completely unnecessary, i was appalled that the blood pressure of a patient who came in because she fainted was taken after having a chest x ray, and the bedside manner and advanced terminology of the np (kim tarver) was unacceptable. very surprisingly, the doctor agreed. she professionally stated she agreed that the chest xray was unnecessary and my sister did not need a cat scan. she said the blood pressure thing was an outlier, but still needed to be noted...and she stated the terminology used was a personnel issue. after all this, she used liquid stitches (liquid skin) on my sister. she's good to go now, but it was an incredibly painful, unnecessary process.

this hospital is a joke. the nursing staff is generally pleasant, but their doctors for the emergency room must've all barely graduated at the bottom of their classes.. they talk down to their patients, i've been there multiple times for multiple injuries and they refuse to run proper diagnostics. they have patient advocate signage in every emergency room, but i've still yet to ever speak with one and the doctors even refuse to allow the patient advocate to be summoned to the rooms.

the nurses in the icu department are amazing. i would like to shine a light on nurse eli. he keeps us in the loop and updated with a family member's condition. he throughly explains everything that we need to know in terms that we understand. he is a great example of a nurse who has a passion of caring for others. thank you to the staff at this hospital that continue to care for our family member. you all are greatly appreciated!

wow! i had a big l3-l5 360 surgery at age 39 here! from the moment i walked in, eddie greeted me with a big smile. sarah in pre-op made me so comfortable. dr. park was a rockstar surgeon. the hospital team worked together and went above and beyond. some of the memorable faces were hin, lovey, joseph, sherry, princess and kent. total rockstar team. i felt like this was my best medical experience yet. amazing job to this team!
absolutely awful awful how they don't answer the phone in dental. i've been trying for days now..

unfortunately i found myself needing to come here quite a few times for my two year old daughter. 

for my daughter i wanted the best of the best so we went with the head of the department. dr. alexandra elliot of ophthalmology is amazing. she is so kind and actually listens to you as her patient. if you need to get in contact with her, i suggest via email as she replies fast. i would recommend her in a heartbeat to any other parent who may need a surgical eye procedure done on their child. 

the waiting area keeps my daughter entertained, with coloring materials, a tv that plays disney jr shows, and they even have a wii for kids to mess with. 

staff has always been very nice the times we've gone, only once did we ever wait longer than anticipated.

my dad didn't end up going to mirada hills due to insurance but when my family and i called to get some info we were lucky to speak to johnny in social work. 
he provided me and my family so much info on available resources we will be eternally grateful. 
my sister visited and said the facility was clean and staff was very nice and
professional.
i recommend this establishment. staff was really helpful and attentive to our needs. facility was clean. the head of social services johnny was very resourceful.

the staff at this facility really helped out my family through a rough time and they were really friendly when my loved one wasn't the nicest person to be around due to their situation. i would highly recommend this facility. i have to give a huge thanks to our social worker johnny, who answered all my family's questions.

as a former employee of mirada hills i have nothing but good things to say about the staff and facility. not only is staff caring and attentive but also ensure the residents are as comfortable as possible. great rehab team and not to mention the social services director johnny valera is helpful and caring  to both residents and family

this is from the heart a very special thank you to all the staff at mirada hills. my mother was admitted to mirada hills september 2019 and is currently her home after being discharged from another facility. upon arrival, rose noticed the discoloration on my mother's leg had x rays    and was determined she had a fractured ankle that went unnoticed by emergency room doctors or previous nursing home. it has been a long process of recovery for my 90 yr old mom but with a great support system mirada hills staff. i would like to thank everybody in every position. my experience mirada hills is a very clean facility, the staff doors are always open and willing to answer questions most important they care about our loved ones, guide the family through the process.  there is family participation activities that i so much cherish. we all say our love ones at one time or another will recover better at home, not the case. mirada hills has my mom and other resident's well-being first, i have seen this first hand. yes there will be issues that come up, but there is always someone to talk to and take the appropriate action. we could not do what the staff members do at mirada hills at home in reality.  1 year 5 months i'm still enjoying my mom because of mirada hills care, my mom is happy and safe most of all because of caring staff members.

i recently had to visit the er last week for an unusually bad flu! i somehow got insanely lucky because when i walked in around 5am, there wasn't anyone else waiting in the er, so i walked right on back. the nurse completed some tests right away and about an hour later i got to see the doctor. during the 6 hours i was there, the place got a lot busier, including a traumatic head injury which came into the bed next to me. obviously my face to face time with the doctor declined, but a nurse was checking in on me every 20 minutes or so. every single staff member i interacted with was kind and sincere. though i can tell they don't put up with nonsense complaints. props to them! it's an emergency room people... as long as you don't expect them to walk on egg shells around you, you'll be pleasantly surprised with the quality of the job done. thank you, st. joseph's.

i have been extremely sick for 2 days and knew i had the flu, so i called my doctor's office to see if they could call in a prescription for tamaflu for me. they said they dont do that, i would have to come in, and my regular doctor didnt have any openings so i had to see doctor dolan. fine. i will have my husband drive me and my 2 toddlers, who are all also sick but not as bad as me, to the appointment (because i am too sick to drive and we dont have a sitter).  so now we have 4 people sick with the flu in their waiting room. sounds great so far, right? way smarter than just calling in a prescription durning the middle of flu season, right? 

so the nurse calls me back, takes my vitals and swabs my nose for the flu virus. fine, whatever. then the doctor comes in and wants to know what i "want?". kind of weird thing to ask, but i tell her i think i have the flu and i would like tamaflu. she tells me i don't have a fever and i let her know i am taking dayquil religiously every 4 hours because i am very sick and it helps a little with the fevers. then she asks me how long i've had symptoms. i tell her and she says that's longer than 48 hours and they dont prescribe tamaflu after 48 hours. mind you, we are now at about 50 hours. i asked her why not, since i have read many times that tamaflu helps even if you start taking it after 48 hours. her answer was "it makes people nauseous". ok, i think that if that's your only concern you should let the patient make that decision. 

so after that conversation, dr. dolan says "your flu results will be done in a couple minutes". i told her i didnt see the point in waiting on the flu results because they wouldn't prescribe me medication anyway. all of the sudden she says that i might be a special case because i take steroids for an autoimmune disease that makes me more susceptible to pneumonia. 

at this point i'm wondering what's wrong with this woman. she goes on and on about how she wont give me tamaflu because it's been close 50 hours and it makes people nauseous, then literally her next sentence is telling me i'm a special case and i need to be on tamaflu.

anyway, she leaves for the lab results and guess what, i have flu type a. she gets my local pharmacy phone number to send over a prescription for tamaflu and i ask her for a prescription for cough medicine. she says they dont give prescriptions for that. fine. can you reccomend an over the counter cough medicine? "we reccomend a teaspoon of honey". i asked her to repeat herself because i was in disbelief. she repeated "a teaspoon of honey". listen lady, i already know you are a nut, but if you think i am getting up every 3 minutes in the night with coughing fits to eat a teaspoon of honey, not only will i not get any sleep but i will have diabetes by morning.

anyway, we head over to the pharmacy to pick up the tamaflu i had to suffer mind games at the hands of a doctor to get, and guess what. they didnt send my prescription to the pharmacy i specifically asked them too and gave them the number for. nope. they submitted it to my mail order pharmacy. so the kind people at the pharmacy called my doctor and told them to send over the prescription and cancel the order with the mail order pharmacy because my insurance wouldn't cover both. cool. except now i have to wait another half hour for my prescription. we wait a half hour, go back up, and they tell us my doctor cant seem to cancel my mail order prescription and they wont be able to do anything for me until the mail order is canceled. at this point i'm exhausted so we just leave.

as we get in the car to drive home my doctor's office calls to tell me what the pharmacy people already told me, that they sent the prescription to the wrong place and they were not able to fix it and i about lost my mind. they made a huge deal about how many hours i had been sick and didnt want to give me the medication, but then realized they should, but instead of sending it where they were supposed to, they sent it to mail order where it would take literally days to fill. i told them to cancel all the orders since "hours" seem to make a huge difference in efficacy. they had already wasted at least 2 additional hours at this point and i didnt even have the medicine yet. i just needed to rest and the stress was making me feel even worse.

done, right? nope, 2 hours later i get an email from the mail order pharmacy saying that my order will be delivered in 4 to 7 days. thanks dr. dolan and thanks to her super incompetent staff, i guess i will just wait and see if i get pneumonia.

oh, also, the staff at the doctor's office was apparently supposed to have me put on a mask so i wouldn't spread the flu virus to others in the waiting room with my horrible cough, and they didnt. doctor dolan told me that after she came into the examination room.

bye bye saint mary's! if this flu doesnt kill me i will be seeking care at another practice.

i'm usually not the one to write negative reviews, but i'm writing this on behalf of future patients to forewarn them on what to expect. i'm saddened to say i was very disappointed in the lack of bedside manner and professionalism by the front desk receptionist in the imaging department. she was visibly overwhelmed and projected her frantic nature onto the patients checking in. not only did i observe her rude mannerisms to other patients including myself, but she gossiped with other coworkers about how annoyed and frustrated she was due to the amount of people checking in "all at once". it isn't fair to the patients who already have nerves about getting medical imaging to then deal with an employee of hoag who is dismissive, insensitive, unprofessional  and clearly unfit for handling a position at the hospital. upon checking in (without a greeting), she said name and insurance. i told her my insurance was in the system and she had responded immediately(without looking) that it was not. it was, because i was a rehabilitation patient for 2 and a half weeks at hoag, recovering from a near-death car accident that put me in a wheelchair. understand that you are working in a health care environment and you need to be trained as such. you are working with people who have suffered to some degree and you should be sympathetic and accommodating in making their experience as stress free as possible, not adding stress and anxiety to an already tense situation. i do not recommend going here.

i had a sleep deprived eeg scheduled for today at 9:30am. i'm new to the area and live in irvine. i show up to the hoag hospital in irvine only to find out i'm at the wrong hospital. who would have thought! they never told me the address when they confirmed the appointment and my doctor is in irvine. it was a complete nightmare. i have a 5 month old baby and a 3 year old plus we are all alone here in the us from canada for my  husbands work and i don't know all the hospitals in oc. i quickly call to let the newport hospital eeg department know i will be 1... not 5... but 1 minute late and she told me too bad! and empathy, no sympathy that i had zero sleep all night, a huge migraine, epilepsy, torn hip among many other issues hence the eeg and most cold heartedly tells me too bad! i am so angry! what horrible customer service. cedars sinai would never ever treat me this way and this is why i will continue to take the 1.5 hour drive in and the 3 hour trek home because they treat me with respect as a paying customer and understand their own mistakes. you guys never gave me the address! i had never been to your hospital before! thanks for ruining my day and for making my epilepsy journey so much harder.
great service, got registered and taken to my room quickly with no wait time upon my arrival.
great hospital but don't be late on any bill as this non profit send you to collections after 5 months from the first bill!?

december 27th 2019 was the happiest day of my life. my dear daughter was born. hoag is an amazing hospital i was dignosed with gd and their diabetes center gave me great support! the last weeks of my pregnancy i was refered to to nst (non stress testing) for my baby and the staff at fetal diagnostics was so welcoming and helpful. finally labor and delivery assisted me on 2 false alarms when i thought i was going into labor. they never made me feel incompetent even though  i clearly was not in labor. i am a first time mom and when finally the day came, they made my birthing experience wonderful. every step of the way i felt like i was treated like family. nurses and doctors were so warm and welcoming. my daughter was treated with so much care and attention. thank you so much hoag! i remember looking up reviews and would have loved for more people to truly express how this hospital is amazing! i truly appreciate all of the staff i wish i had names but forgot them. my ob was dr richard agnew i was one of the last deliveries for him he retired dec 31st he will be missed he was also so much help:) thank you.

hoag hospital has mis-diagnosed multiple times so far. they need to step up again and hire true doctors. it is really sad a hospital with this fame is so poor at proper diagnosis. me and family and colleague all tried this facility multiple times and they completely diagnosed wrong. all they did was trying to run tests and say things that wad not correct. very nice personnel though. i hope one day they be great again.

could your organization get any greedier or money hungry??? i had an ultrasound 8 days ago, i'm fully insured with ppo insurance. i have received two calls over the past 2 days asking me to call hoag's finance department. finally called back today to find out the billing department is calling me to tell me to expect the bill for the ultrasound in the mail and that it is hoag's policy to have all bills paid in full. when i asked when the bill was due i was told 30 days after i received the bill which would be, by my estimate, around 1/20/2020. i can't think of a more bizarre interaction with a healthcare system. how can hoag possibly be considered a nonprofit? no wonder you are losing business and out there begging for patients. since hoag is going to act like a for profit then it is time for this organization to start paying taxes!!!

this hospital is absolutely horrible and the nurses are so uncaring it's palpable and affects the quality of care. my daughter came here to deliver her first baby. they kept telling her she was only 2cm dilated. they told her she didn't need an epidural at the time and that it would only get worse. finally they agreed to the epidural because she  was screaming in excruciating pain. it ended up the entire time she was 10cm and ready to deliver. don't have your baby here as the nurses treated her like crap too. then while we were sitting in the waiting  room speaking to each other we talked about how ridiculous it was that someone went from 2cm to 10cm without them knowing and my son in law came out and said that they were informed of we said one more thing that we wouldn't be allowed to see my daughter or grandchild. this place is pathetic!

my husband was sent directly to the hospital after an appointment at colliers urgent care. we were extremely pleased with the check in process . we were sent to the emergency room and were fortunate to get a room. the hospital was extremely busy. the care that a nurse named jackie gave my husband was extraordinary. she kept us posted on exactly the care that they were providing to my husband. that evening we were relocated into a beautiful room on the 5th floor in the main hospital. i think we just got lucky on the room! unfortunately we couldn't take jackie with us!! again, the care was absolutely extraordinary. our nurses jason, stephanie, arik and stephanie ( another stephanie) were efficient and explained everything thoroughly. we were also told that we were very fortunate to have dr ranta care for my husband. everyone was kind coupled with being extremely knowledgeable. i would have no hesitation to recommend this hospital. 
thank you staff!

three times in the last 3 years:
 
a spider bite to the face, i was prescribed two antibiotics for a bad drug reaction it almost stopped my heart.  bad doctors.

during my wife's last pregnancy, a doctor misdiagnosed her and she was in major pain for hours they did not do anything but charge us for unneeded tests.  my wife's real diagnosis was stated as obvious by her pcp when she automatically recieved the ultrasound three days later.  doctor didn't care.

my one year old daughter from the aforementioned pregnancy had her finger caught in the door and we took her in for a precautionary xray.  it doesn't take two hours to read an xray to a waiting mother when they were not busy and the baby is crying.  to top it off the place is so filthy my wife and kid got the flu and gave it to the whole family.  

during all three instances this hospital is filthy.  the service is terrible.  the nurses are uncaring and the doctors are dangerously incompetent.  we will no longer be using them obviously.  anyone who lives in naples knows nch is terrible.  this branch is especially dangerous, it's staff cold and corporate.  anyone who says they had a good experience here is either lying because they are biased or they are stupid.  i would give them zero stars.  if you value your life stay away.

-parking is horrible
-staff lost 2 of my father (who is a physician) urine samples. not sure how you lose them, let alone twice.
-meals were ehhh. breakfest worst than lunch. for lunch it was just all diced fruits and cottage cheese..
-staff not as educated as ive seen in other hospitals.
-long line for check in, almost every time

-rooms were clean
-the lobby on floor 6 was nice and had seating for a waiting area

they starve you at this hospital! the attitude of my nurse cindy this morning was so poor it made my husband and i cringe. it was obvious that she hadn't called the doctor for permission to order breakfast after a routine stress test. nor was she in any hurry to do so. in the span of an hour, i asked for breakfast three times and all i got was attitude. i hadn't eaten a meal since breakfast the day before and they knew it. i couldn't eat their pot roast dinner last night because it was soaked in gravy made with flour. i have celiac disease and can't eat gluten as my chart noted. they had no dinner alternative to offer me. i have never been so hungry in my life! i ended up walking out with iv in my arm so i could finally get something to eat. i've heard people say "nch" stands for "never come home." it's true - they want to starve you to death!

i came to this hospital because i was vomiting and one of my body parts were gone which caused infection they say if i need something to eat or a dessert they say if i need pain medicine they are good service

i can not say enough about the emergency  room services in this hospital. it is just terrible. a few months ago my husband came in with all the symptoms of a heart attack, they made him wait outside and filled out some paper work. for about 5 to 10  minutes. in turns  out that in fact he had a heart attack!!! we all know that every minute counts when you are having one. 
today my mother, who does not speak english , came  in an ambulance due to possible stroke. she is in her 80's. i had to fight my way into her room, for about 30 minutes. she was by herself, unable to understand what was being asked, extremely nervous and none of the nurses seem to care,  they gave instructions of not letting any family member get in the room!!! as soon as i got in the room, they were able to clearly understand what happened to her, how she was feeling at the moment,  she needed the calmness and interpretation of her daughter. 
now i see why this emergency room seems to be always empty. 
ps. my husband had to be transferred to another hospital because they didn't have a cardiologist that could handle his case. my mother will probably have to be transferred too, no neurologist department here!!!!

hospital stays are not what we look forward to, but the staff at thph does their best to make you comfortable when you are the most uncomfortable. i spent three days there last week and really appreciate the nurses, pas, and doctors. i was admitted through the er and have high praise for their team as well. no matter the job, from admin to cleaning staff, everyone greeted me with a friendly smile, listened to me, and always asked if there was anything else they could do for me.

be very cautious about using this facility.  the care if fine, however, the billing will leave you extremely frustrated.  i visited the er and provided my license and insurance.  the hospital neglected to enter my address, and therefore never sent me a bill.  i finally was alerted that i had an outstanding charge when a collection agency contacted me.  after the hospital investigated and confirmed their error, they apologized and we arranged for a payment plan.  after finally being on a payment plan and making successful payments, i received another collection notice - the hospital was ignoring my payment plan - even after process a nov and dec payment from me in full.  basically they collected my in full payment and turned my account over anyway.  beware as this is unethical and i believe illegal when someone is making arranged payments in good faith.

this an utterly horrifying facility. 
an untrained and inexperienced social worker who clearly was newly "licensed" lied about what i said in an intake assessment. i had my lawyer attempt to get my paperwork under a hippa authorization release request and they admitted to shredding it. this is a complete violation of hippa.
i am in the process of attempting a lawsuit with my attorney.
do not go to this facility! i seriously urge you not to. it's dirty, unsafe, and filled with staff who lie to save their own behinds. seriously, if you or a loved one need mental health treatment, please go elsewhere. i urge you.
this place should be brought to light and shut down immediately.

i fell off a ladder doing a home improvement project barefoot and thought i broke my heel (#wearshoesonaladder). i didn't have time to shower and change clothes like i would have preferred-my wife loaded me up in the car as-is and drove me to medical city north hills. 

i found the entire experience to be exactly what i needed and hoped for- i got in quickly, had my pain controlled, was diagnosed accurately with a stone bruise (and thankfully not a fracture), and was discharged.  everyone was courteous and kind, the facility was clean, i got in and out quickly, and my care was very good.

this was not what i expected when seeing the yelp reviews being a "2 out of 5 star rating". i am grateful for the care i received and for having this hospital in my community right down the street.

i don't recommend falling off a ladder to experience  the er, but...they made a painful situation so much better for me and i appreciate they took great care of me when i needed them!!!!!!

i have been coming to this hospital since i was a teenager and every single visit i have ever had with them has always been horrible. their staff are not professional at all the doctors are not caring or almost not knowledgeable. the wait time is ridiculous i live right down the street from this hospital and i will go all the way to alliance harris methodist if we need to go to the er. my husband had a stomach virus and when we went there all they said was that he was dehydrated and just made it seem like he was just ridiculous for being there. when we went to alliance they kept my husband overnight and come to find out from a stool sample he had a bacteria growing in his stomach from food poisoning so therefore we now have a hospital bill that was unnecessary and a waste of time being there. you're better off going to urgent care and getting the same treatment because i don't think those doctors care enough to be in a emergency room setting. the weight and the rooms are so small cramped outdated and so uncomfortable for as long as they have everyone waiting there especially for labs it's ridiculous that they don't have it at least more comfortable. i hate literally hate this hospital it's the most horrible hospital ever.

i had a kidney stone today, the second worse pain i have ever had. what was the first? my first kidney stone. i have also had several broken bones, face reconstructed with titanium, and i have been shot. i know pain... i had to walk out of harris methodist downtown fort worth (literal assholes) twice before going to nrh er today... hm treated me like i had no insurance and no money. neither can be further from the truth. after still being in the triage area for almost 3 hours, i couldn't take it any longer, so i can to nrh er. they had me in a bed in 10 minutes, treated me with medicine within 30 minutes, and on my way in approximately an hour... all this while being attentive, compassionate, knowledgeable, and efficient. get this, they literally said to me that they didn't want to run up a needless bill... i will admit that i had a bad experience at this location once before but since it didn't have anything to do with compassion, i gave it another try and i was so glad i did today.

the infusion clinic here is the best!  my mom has a chronic illness where she can eat and drink very little.  she has infusion here every few days.  the  nurses are so caring and good to her!  she has been well taken care of and i'm grateful that we found this service for her.

this is sad at the quality provided by most of the staff here. 

  there are few shining lights of care and hope here but overall the support staff really need to consider their roles here.
  examples: dietary restrictions provided by doctors and yet food is still delivered late and the wrong meal. then the replacement meal is later than the first. (incorrect lunch is corrected and almost arrives at dinner? really?)

  medical staff does not make the scheduled rounds. services staff does not seem to care or pay attention to details.

 the cafeteria should be a nice area yet all i tend to see are dirty tables wiped with dirty towels while security and cafe staff just lounge.

  the cafe is always cluttered it seems and the food prep stations should be better managed and controlled; you would think that a hospital would respect safety and quality standards to prevent germ contamination.
  are these sticking points detailed? yes. for many reasons.
fac_name: The Medical Center of Southeast Texas

review:
one sorry hospital in my opinion. i have insurance and they demanded a very large cash payment before they would perform a procedure. i asked about a payment plan and they basically told me i could apply for their credit card and wait to see if i would get approved before allowing payments. i am sure there are people that dont have money getting write offs but the person with insurance that wants to make payments is screwed. i am seriously considering changing from a great doctor just so i am not forced to use this facility as its the only one he practices in.
i might also add that i got a rude phone call reminder to be at my appt at such and such time. lady acted like she was put out to call.
my recommendation---- go to beaumont unless you have no other choice-
fac_name: The Medical Center of Southeast Texas

review: went to the er for severe abdominal pain and was not treated until 6 hours later... no one checked up on us or offered us food or water, were promised a doctor and never received one. terrible service and will be seeking a different er.

this is going to personally be the hardest review i've ever written. it is with a sad yet grateful heart, that i commend the doctors, nurses, and technicians of inova childrens hospital. the people who work here have the kindest and most loving of demeanors, absolutely care about kids and their parents who worry so much, and i can't think of many places that truly are as loving as this place right here. i absolutely with five stars recommend this facility, and want to give the staff here the biggest possible shout out of support that i can. all of us human beings suffer the mammalian struggle, it's what we do that matters, and my hope is that you'll embrace each day and others on the journey. yes my oldest son was pronounced dead here. he had already died of a massive angelman syndrome related seizure, that triggered cardiac arrest at age five. it is the worst experience a parent can go through, and i don't want your sorrow, but if you could donate blood to your fellow humans that will help. the staff here that night kept me, from literally destroying everything as this is a living nightmare that took years to get through. never over. through.

before that my oldest went here for everything from the nasty rotavirus to seizures. multiple visits and my youngest has been here for respiratory issues. he's a bigger boy now, but guess where i'd go if he had a medical emergency. here. with love to all paramedics, i'm going to insist here. the doctors and nurses do everything they can, and honestly i have no idea how they work here everyday, as it definitely takes a special breed. it's a very clean facility, and getting in and out of here is relatively easy. also they don't forget who you are. it is a sad but wonderful circle of life, that on the night all was crushed, the same nurse who helped my oldest multiple times held on to his brother and loved on him. that as tear inducing as it is, that is a love of the highest i've ever seen. definitely you're in great hands here! while no parent wants their kid in the hospital, i recommend inova children's for everything.

such a wonderful experience here and extra nice to have a ronald mcdonald family room here! amazing staff including the best nurses and doctors around. we couldn't have asked for a better experience! thank you.

good doctors and nurses but a terrible billing experience. this "nonprofit" healthcare provider will not negotiate on the bill and charges interest on a payment plan. they charged $1,500 just for an overnight iv.

this place is really bad.  this is a great example of what is wrong with america's healthcare service.  it's set up for failure.  i'm sure everyone is trying their best, but it's horribly staffed and operated.  i don't blame the doctors, as much as the administrators running the place.  it costs an arm and a leg and it took over three hours to get in and out.  we only saw the doctor for 20 minutes in total.     the one doctor is seeing like 40 patients in the middle i'd the night with no support, there is no way anyone should be diagnosis under these condution.  even worse, there is no way anyone seeing that many patients has the capacity to care at all about anyone being seen.   and, i understand you all are "very busy". but, guess what, so is every other american that has a mouth to feed.  being busy doesn't justify leaving me and my  13 month year-old, who just threw up on the floor, in a room for 2+ hours to find someoneto explain how to use an inhaler.  it doesn't make sense, we can do better.
we had a fantastic experience while going through a difficult time when our 3-year-old had a phenomenon. very thorough care and compassionate staff. thank you for taking care of us
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado South Campus, Highlands Ranch

review: my pediatrician sent me to the urgent care at children's to use their industrial suction machine since my 1 year old son had been struggling to clear his nose while having the flu. after we were given an x-ray to check his lungs, we were moved to emergency and told that we would have to drive (in a blizzard) to aurora because our sons heart was so enlarged he might not make it through the night. after hours of waiting and being told nothing, my son getting an iv but hanging no bloodwork done, and absolutely zero medical care for why we came in, we were sent home without getting the suction or getting his lungs checked but told we had to get an ultrasound of his heart the next day. when i asked about my sons lungs, the doctor checked him in hallway and was concerned enough to give him cortisone. guess it's a good thing i checked since apparently we would have gone home after paying without even being seen for why we came in. at the same hospital, we followed up with cardiologist the next day and were told after a thirty heaving physical exam that he didn't need an ultrasound because nothing was even wrong with him and the second long x-ray appeared totally normal. so since er made it clear i had to do this ultrasound or my son could have a life threatening illness i decided with the cardiologist what we could do the x-ray to rule it out. now i am being billed for an x-ray as an elective procedure. believe me, i would not be getting a heart ultrasound just on a whim. i went through the appeals process at the hospital which is borderline criminal. you aren't allowed to talk to anyone about what happened or wrote a letter or see any correspondence from the hospital. the just let me know that they did everything right and the next day i got a call from collections. i've had a number of terrible experiences with care too. from the ent who told me not to waste his time with a sleep study, just do surgery or go ahead and leave to the patient advocate teams who pretend to care. i live less than a mile from this hospital and sadly can't even use them anymore. i am praying that kevin v has time to reply to me since apparently yelp is the only way to actually talk to someone in this hospital.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado South Campus, Highlands Ranch

review: horrible.  flat out horrible two years in a row.  last year i took my 2 month old daughter to this childrens to be assessed for rsv at 9pm at night.  the doctor at the time looked her over for a few mins and monitored her oxygen for about 30 and said very condescendingly "she has a cold".  we left and 4 hours later my daughter started to more seriously struggle to breathe.  i took her to her normal pediatrians in the morning which promptly sent her to children's main where she resided for 5 days with rsv. (they were amazing) thinking that experience was a one off, i just left there with my four year old daughter who i fear has the flu and the doctor did an adequate job observing her but refused to test her for anything.  we went in the middle of the night bc i was worried about her breathing.  on the way out, please sign your bill and oh by the way please sign this document saying you know this is a er visit and not urgent care.  i replied, no one told me that.  and she said "oh sorry mom". here's another form saying their may be surprise charges from this er visit.  please sign this as well.  if i wasn't so tired i would have not signed them.  i'm actually livid.  i'll never go back and you shouldn't either.   i will be filing a complaint about their office staff on monday when their offices open.
fac_name: Children's Hospital Colorado South Campus, Highlands Ranch

review:
if you can find someone there who speaks english as a first language, good luck.  they are stupid and rude on the phone. some random guy gets on the phone because the girl couldn't understand english, he said "who's this?" without telling me who he is. i asked "who's this" and he became defensive and said "well you were the one who called". really? when you are a professional at a business, you always tell the caller who they are speaking with. then he said "well you have the wrong number, how about that".  wow. i found out the a-hole's name is jose.... how about that.
this happened 7:00 p.m. march 12, 2020

emergency room at 1515 sw archer rd is horrible.  the staff is rude and so uncaring.  hung up on me twice on purpose and then when i was in lobby was disrespectful.  they appear bothered when you ask for an update. they are too busy standing around talking to each other.  waited 7 hours after all testing and everything was done for the discharge 'order'.  doctor said we could be discharged 7 hours ago but the order was never put in.  7 hour wait just for discharge paperwork. ridiculous
fac_name: Shands Hospital At the University of Florida

review: they need to do something about the damn parking. if ppl have to park on the street of residential roads, there's a problem.

mostly wonderful!
doctors are very knowledgeable and nurses are some of the best i've experienced. 
had problems with lack of communication within the hospital. i feel that the doctors, nurses, and other staff should improve by communicating more with each other. 
other than that small "hiccup", i would say this is the best choice for health care in wilkes, surry and somewhat yadkin county. 
overall a great experience!
fac_name: Wake Forest Baptist Health - Wilkes Medical Center

review: i think everyone in the er at this location needs a class in human compassion.  was there on saturday evening & was treated like garbage. had a broken foot and had to not only ask for an ace bandage, but actually had to wrap it myself. closest hospital or not, i won't be going back.

las encinas made a difficult psychiatric evaluation easier.
the food is good and the accommodations are okay for what they are. 3 beds per room but i had two nights by myself.
the nursing staff seems to really care.

please read:

i have been to las encinas few times...so i know how it was back then compared to how it was last year. never too late for a review though.

first: the nice pictures, the nice pictures , very clean, nice interior is from brier residential. not inpatient units either (detox or mental health unit)).  

few years ago,  both units were full., very clean, quite a few nurses, organized meetings for both units. we could go outside..get fresh air..there were puzzles, books. not to mention the cafeteria was open, and sunny (not 
half as it was last year). food, was great,

last year, it was a ghost town. downstairs unit was maybe one or 2 patients so they moved those patients from downstairs to detox unit. they closed the downstairs unit and it's nurses station. 

las encinas, the nurses and all the staff , all combined , was support 
system for what ever the reason for patients were there.

wish they would make some changes, if they haven't yet.
residential is great because they get money from insurance who people can afford to have expensive insurance plans.

bottom line: 

a)  the pictures are deceiving. it's residential brier. people with top notch insurance stay there and have money stay there.

 b)  maybe one group a day, if any...jeff gammy has a great meeting.  
back then we had morning check in group. also had aa panels that came entire day we were kept busy.

c)  having staff do your laundry? last year i was there for few days but that what i heard for this year.
so someone with ocd, like myself, have to let others handle my clothes..

d)  no activity what so ever, basically you spend time watching tv and day dream. if just around, looking like zombies.

e)  what happened to las encinas. i learned quite a bit with encouragement all day groups. 

f)  forgot this one:  back then( not my stay a year ago. few years ago, they would check our bags and suitcases inside the room. (right after in take) inside assigned rooms, so you wouldn't feel uncomfortable and more private.  las year they open your suitcase or bag inside the nurses station, and everyone on there (male workers) also watch. i felt so uncomfortable and with ocd i packed whole bunch. i'm sure all stuff looked at me thinking nut case!

all my recovery, med adjustment, i owe to las encinas.  i can't deal with change. i'd go back because it's familiar to me. 

jeff gammy knows recovery. some of the nurses were great

last years was not good. i hope they can make changes

worst staff ever! no one in this facility really gives a shit about the patients seeking care. you are treated worse than an inmate and forced to inhale feces that is never cleaned up. the nurses just lock themselves in their station and have no compassion for the patients having a hard time adjusting. the only good thing that came out of this place is knowing that this place is honestly worse than any image or thought of hell and i never want to end up in my dark thoughts again in hopes of never returning there again. las encinas is inhumane! shame on the staff for being so cruel. $1,500 to be tortured. dr. alikhan and all the social workers do not care about their patients.

i was in the day program due to mental illness. i was put in johnath group.  i was the only one that had a mental illness.  he didn't help me with my problems at all.  i left coming back worse then i started.

not a phone in sight.... just patients living in the moment....

in all seriousness though the nurses at this hospital took a few things from me. when i was checked in i was asked to sign a paper that was suppose to list all my possessions i came in with. the paper was blank and i was off an ambien so i didn't think much of it. when i was discharged i was missing my cigarette case that was full of gift cards (a few of them were unused with values of $100) , but since it wasn't listed with my items there was no way i could get it back. called them a few times and would get transferred back and forth between the wards for a few hours until i was told whoever handles the lost items had left for the day/ was on lunch. nurses also made me sign a release stating they would not return any of the ( legal and medical ) marijuana i had with me when i came in. hundreds of dollars worth of flower and cbd products gone just like that. i saw on the paper that it was optional, but was told i had to sign it or i wouldn't be able to get discharged. 

cassandra was my favorite nurse. only one who was gentle when waking us up for vitals and made sure she got all the smokers to come downstairs for cigarette breaks when they were happening.

i have now had two horrible experiences with this facility. the first was with a family member several years ago when i did not think their psychologists were professional with follow up. the second experience was just recently with a client, who was not told the psychiatrist who saw her in an emergency situation was not covered by her insurance. the admissions staff was not particularly friendly or helpful either.

our experience at the schneck er was awful.  we had an uncooperative, arrogant doctor by the name of dr. griffith.  he wanted to do a cat scan of my husband's throat to determine if the blockage was still present.  i asked him about the cost of a cat scan and he said around $2,000.00.  i asked about the price of a regular x-ray and he told me about $200.00.   i asked why a more expensive procedure was necessary and he told me that an x-ray would probably not show the obstruction (which we believed to be a chicken bone and he knew this). i asked how a cat scan worked and he told me it was a 3-d x-ray. he'd already told us that my husband would have to have his throat scoped to remove the blockage, so we wanted to know why either test was necessary.  he explained nothing.  he left my husband's room and ordered the cat scan,  proceeding with the expensive test which showed, wait for it.... nothing!    the man spent a total of 5 minutes with us and his bill was $1,300.00, more than the surgeon charged to scope my husband's throat.  we are under a self-pay insurance plan and part of our contract with them is that we get the best price possible for each service provided.  dr. griffith's office will not give us the cpt codes we must have for reimbursement.   we called the hospital administrator and complained about the unnecessary use and expense of the cat scan.  our complaint fell on deaf ears.  they did not care that we were fiscally exploited as self-pay patients. so, it looks like we'll have to eat the entire $1,300.00   once my husband was admitted, which was also unnecessary, the nurses were wonderful.  he also really liked his surgeon, dr. iwema.  she was compassionate and caring.  she even called the day after his procedure to check on his progress.  her bill was very reasonable and her office was wonderful to work with regarding the cpt codes necessary for reimbursement.  both she and the hospital did give us a self-pay discount.  the appropriate cooperation from the hospital and dr. iwema's office is the only reason this review received a three star rating.  the emergency room itself, would have received a zero.  always be your own advocate and never assume the hospital is working toward your best interest.  i know when you go to the er things are scary and you often aren't at your best, but these people will take advantage of your vulnerabilities.  we will never go back to the schneck er, but we will wind up at an er somewhere eventually, and when it happens, there will be a better result.
