oh god, she's so fat

ok lets be straight- i'm a big girl. i've struggled with my weight my whole life. 
i'm also narcoleptic, and have fought a battle with depression and anxiety since i was 10. are these things an issue? yep. do they define me and explain every issue without an obvious answer? no, they do not. 

unless, of course, i am an in-patient at abrazo central campus.

the first doctor i met was called "dr. d." the first thing to roll out of his mouth upon meeting me was "have you considered gastric bypass surgery?" no hello? the second thing was "are you diabetic?" diabetes was a natural first question, as i was there because neuropathy in my feet was spreading alarmingly fast up both my legs.

something to rule out for sure, but folks, i am not diabetic. 

not if abrazo staff pokes me every 6 hrs for 2 days, not if the dr orders 2 different blood tests, not if he adds insulin to my prn list while neglecting my actual prescriptions, not by the hair of my chinny chin chin! 
so whats next?

oh awesome, here comes the neurologist. a gallon or two of my blood was taken for testing, a spinal tap and mri were ordered. 

the spinal tap was, of course, terrifying. one of my symptoms was spontaneous involuntary muscle spasms and they wanted to put a giant needle in my spine that could paralyze me if i moved! 
i had a panic attack. i have already admitted that i have anxiety. but wouldn't you call that a reasonable fear? 

now, looking over the paperwork, i see references to my anxiety all over the place as a poor explanation for their failure to find the reason for the neuropathy

but back to the fat prejudice, as that is my theme.
 
when i was admitted, i was starving. i had spent hours in the er before being transferred to the hospital. i had only expected to spend a few hours at the er and for them to do whatever they do and send me home.
so i asked for a sandwich. 3 hours and multiple ignored requests passed between me and that sandwich. it was one of those little elementary school sized ones with one slice of mystery meat, a slice of cheese, and two pieces of bread cut in a diagonal. 

i ate it thankfully. an hour later, i was still hungry and asked if there was somewhere i could get some food. perhaps a vending machine? they put me off a couple more hours and served me fat shame with my second sandwich. 

then, when i was sitting up in bed in the middle of the night (as i do multiple times a night, part of the narcolepsy) the nurse walking by stopped and asked, "your not eating again, are you?" with a horrified expression on his face. 

time for the mri came, and the tech walked in, looked at me, and walked back out into the hall. he announced that i was too fat for the machine several times using different descriptors. he was ordered to try anyways. yep, i heard all of it. i'm sure the neighboring rooms did too. 

he left, and came back with the biggest wheelchair i have ever seen. 
i told him i had heard him in the hall, and he did look genuinely embarrassed and apologetic, so i dropped it.  it turns out that i did fit, but it was so snug that we decided it would be better to wait for a machine that was 70 inches rather than the one there that was 60. 

so yeah, he was pretty much right. 

but my complaint is about a complete and widespread attitude of prejudice and lack of tact because of my weight. 

i am also concerned about the fact that we, the patients, could hear everything the staff was saying to each other in the hallway. i can tell you exactly what was wrong with the people on either side of me and not because i was trying to listen. i think its unprofessional. 

i have a lot of other complaints too.... but i'll just leave it at that.

well, that and that my symptoms have not resolved, an explanation has not been found, and now i have a giant bill for labs that nobody bothered to interpret, and that i can only pray the insurance company will cover most of. 
the list is a few pages long. i may have been tested for bubonic plague, i haven't made it through the whole list yet.

if you are planning a visit to an abrazo er, do a quick check first. can you see your feet while standing up? 

if not, you might want to chose a different er.

i will update this listing with names once i remember where the heck i wrote them down but i felt the need to leave a positive review among all the bad ones. 

i had fai hip surgery there today via scoi next door. contrary to reviews and the zombie apocalypse look from the outside, i was absolutely impressed. check in was a piece of cake (but it was 5:30 am), where i got whisked away into preop and had the most amazing male nurses. my "main" nurse was so kind, thoughtful, and shockingly perky for that early. i emphasized my chlorhexidine allergy because i usually go to ucla where it's all over my chart. he made sure to tell everyone and added a red allergy bracelet on my iv arm. i asked if he chugged coffee and he certainly! he was also able to get an iv started in my forearm, which has left no bruise and just a teeny tiny scab. i met my or team and they were all lovely even though you don't get much time with them since they're buzzing about like bees. 

everyone i met in the or was great. my pacu and possibly one more step down unit also had great care. it's obviously fuzzy but they got me ice chips and some apple juice and made sure my pain was fine. even my transport was amazing! at ucla and cedars i'm used to waiting 30-60 minutes for transport and she was actually there before i was ready and her outfit didn't scream transport so i was confused. she helped me get in the car and was all around just awesome. her name is zoe. 

i will say i ended up itchy with hives head to toe (not from pain killers) and had hives on my face and i was really angry someone must have used chlorhexidine on me but once i thought about it i think it was the hospital's detergent. the or was so cold i pulled it up to my chin and i had a similar all over itchy reaction from the stuff cedars uses. 

anyway, can't speak to an overnight stay or the er, but outpatient surgery here was a total breeze!

avoid avoid avoid this "hospital"! i can't believe this place hasn't shut down! i will tell you about one of many awful experiences here! my father was bought in by ambulance last month as a code stroke and discharged within 5 hours! the er doctor stated that the ct scan was clear and nothing was wrong and discharged him back home via ambulance because he could not walk. they pretty much dumped my father at home as he urinated on himself and couldn't move. i called 911 again but only this time to take him to sherman oaks hospital where they were able to diagnose him with a stroke by doing an mri. i don't understand how this so called hospital can discharge a patient who is pretty much paralyzed on his left side! he couldn't move his left arm or leg and yet you discharge him?  shame on you! especially dr. david zohrabian! my father is currently in rehab fighting to walk again!

i had my son here on 11/02/2019 and let me tell you it has been an amazing experience! came in with some contractions to the er the nurse called for obygn and got admitted right away! everything went smooth ended up with a c-section and it honestly was the best experience i've ever had at a hospital! my room was always kept clean the nurses were friendly and on top of my care and needs ! love this hospital

my brother was taken here by ambulance and i wouldn't recommend it to anyone. as he came in they were fighting with the paramedics saying they were bringing too many people in. my brother kept apologizing and felt like a burden when he was the one in writhing pain. the whole experience sucked they didn't let the morphine die down before discharging and saying go to your primary care. if he could wait he wouldn't have called 911. but his ct scan guy was nice

this review is for jason greenspan md. stay away from this doctor.horrible!!! how could you send patient home with bp over 190!! about 3 minute examination is not ethical and still charge my insurance!! waste of my time!!i would give you zero stars!!!!

stay away from this hospital. they give the words care and compassion a bad name. i saw a guy sit there for 2hrs when he started having a seizure. then and only then was he taken in. me? oh i had surgery 3 days ago felt funny so they made me wait 6 hrs in er for a ct. i left when to a different hospital where i was admitted for checking in 30min. maybe a bad day for me but it is what it is. good luck.

had a revision spinal fusion a week ago here..let me tell u!! they have some of the best nurses/cna's/ ever!! they are attentive and actually listen to what u have to say and  address your concerns!! special shout out to the following people who made my recovery so much easier!! 4 west: michaela!! slava!! chika!! 4 south: tiffany is exceptional..she is very easy to talk to and addresses your concerns...and you can tell she actually loves her job...(day nurse) carmel (she was covering for someone but was  outstanding) and simon is simply the best!! he came up with a solution to my 'light switch' problem (overnight) and made me laugh when i was feeling down (after all laugher is the best medicine) ^_^ u guys rock!! thank u for everything!! also special thank u to dr. yates for going above and beyond to fight for me and get me the care i need/meds/home care/extensions...also for listening to me and making me feel like i what i said/how i felt actually mattered and i was not just a number or a dollar sign...

i would give -10 stars if i could my granddaughter wis taken in the hospital in ambulance from her doctor office.she is 11 1/2 months old instead of seeing her they put her in waiting room to wait. she had fever severe wheezing and was very cranky and crying. after a hour of waiting i asked where she was on list they said she was number 5. after another hour she turned in to number nine on the list. the people where rude and needless to say we left and went to northridge hospital and within 40 minutes we where helped.

when i go to the hospital i expect to be treated fairly with respect. i walk into the hospital and have the hardest time finding the er. i am following your signs and they keep directing me to surgery check in. i use the phone at the service desk press 0 and talk to an operator. i keep repeating myself several times to the operator. i found a nurse hung up the phone she directed me toward er. should never be that hard to find the er. during my check in i explain i dont go to the doctors that often and have not been to the hospital in a long time. during my visit the doctor comes in i explain that i went to urgent care beforehand. they gave me meds. i explained the reactions i have been having (shaking, confused). doctor said that its typical for that medication. he then asks me why i went to the er. after i explained my self several times and he reiterated. i will not be treated like a piece of trash. i pay for my healthcare. i was treated very poorly by this doctor and more complaints and reviews to come.

my mom was diagnosed with guillain barre and was hospitalized for 3 weeks then was discharged to encompass for another 3 weeks. as a nurse myself, this was one of the hardest things to endure. i worried about her overall care, hygiene, feedings and mostly therapy to get back to a sense of normal for herself. rest assured, she felt well taken care of. the physical and occupational therapists were wonderful and the nurses and assistants took care of her needs, a few nightshift ones left a lot to be desired, but the good outweighed the bad. the facility was clean and comfortable for her. the case manager, ketsia, was so friendly and helpful with her discharge process. thank you for taking care of my mom with minimal complications that come along with being immobile.

review:
i recently had to have surgery done at stl. 
it was a hernia/abs reconstruction.

the pca done just about everything else.

stl is an old hospital and the restrooms are to  small for you and your iv pole to both go in the there together. 
the hospital is well maintained for being over 50 yrs old.  i know they are building stl a new hospital and this building was bought by texas children's hospital. only makes since they are attached already. 
i was surprised to see that they only have 2 stars. 
i am giving 4. i hardly ever give 5 stars to any business.

i refused one. eventually he came back as apart of the transplant team and removed the bed pan and sat it on the floor. then a second doctor came in to say she was apart of the same team and explained no food or drink because of an upcoming procedure. we explained we needed a nurse, she replied ok and departed the room seeing the feces laying on the floor, with the common spread of germs you would think some one would have come to our aid. it took some 45 minutes for some one to come to our assistance. it was only after breaking up horse play at the door which i thought was a knock. i find the nurse and her assistant in a jovial horse play back and forth and after a mild scold i asked "is this how the hospital treats there patients? i immediately asked to speak to the charge nurse and after waiting another fifteen minutes i did. this was so hard to see after a major transplant to see this type of care. i hope that no one will ever have to experience this type of treatment. i think this team at worse should be removed from patient care. i have the video to prove my point. you don't deserve the one star let alone 5.

review:
a close friend of mine had a stroke on december 23rd. he collapsed and was taken to the hospital where they performed surgery immediately. he is now in the rehab hospital, where they are working diligently to help him. 

he is doing quite well, although his speech is not that great and his right side is affected by the effects of the stroke. he is such a great guy. i feel awful for him. i am confident that pinecrest will help him get back to normal.

the layout of the rooms at pinecrest is very confusing. it took me a half hour to find my friend's room. my prayers are with him in this awful time. he is very lucky that he was brought in to the hospital very quickly or he wouldn't have made it. i believe he'll get back to where he was before this unfortunate event. pinecrest is doing everything they can to rehabilitate him. their expertise is amazing.

my partner has been getting care here for sleep apnea.  for the most part, it has been pretty good.  he has however had a tough time with apria communicating with the sleep clinic.  they always seem to need paperwork for medicare.  
the staff is all friendly and professional.

i broke my ankle and went there on a recommendation. full disclosure, it was a friday morning (not a saturday night), but we were in and out in three hours, which went very quickly. staff was great, place is immaculate and now they have private rooms with televisions (a huge upgrade over the old er). 

one tiny complaint: i had to use the ladies room and the attendant didn't know how to transfer me from the wheel chair. i ended up hopping over the footrest. come on, i can't be the only one whose ever shown up immobile and had to pee.

one bigger complaint: my husband had to go back in to get my xrays on a disc after the orthopedist they recommended (and said they were on pascack's system) told me that they aren't, and wouldn't be able to read them unless we brought them. could i have been the first patient to go to the recommended orthopod after breaking a bone and showing up at the er?

mister's dad needed emergency back surgery on christmas eve and our experience at this hospital could not have been better. 

the surgery itself took about an hour and then they monitored him for 3 hours. after that he was ready to go home! not only was it quick, i feel like there was always a nurse coming in to check in on him or offer us something. 

i loved when our nurse said it was a super busy christmas eve night in the hospital. i barely saw anyone in the halls! any other hospital i've been to most of the time i'm in the hallway on a stretch because they don't have enough rooms. this place definitely took care of him and made every minute he was there as pleasant as possible. 

even though we were only there for a few hours, they offered us plenty of chairs and their nourishing room which had snacks and drinks. i mean really, it doesn't get better. it's way out of the way for me but if you're in this area this is the hospital to go to.

i am not a fan of emergency rooms however the nurses and doctors are so nice and accommodating the rooms are clean you get your own room with a tv.  the doctors explain everything and provide advice this  er is a hidden quiet gem.

fit me in right away for a mammogram  and the tech was super nice and explained procedure well . the front desk sign inn girls were "eh" they need to smile more . seemed like they don't like patients andd get along and are happy talking to coworkers . the volenteer guy was super bossy teeming me wheeze to sign in when i already new . otherwise i waac super happy with them doing it for me on a whim

my mom was about to leave the hospital and needed to go somewhere for a while longer until she could start breathing on her own without the machines. they gave me some recommendations for places closer to where i live so i did my due diligence and researched them. i narrowed it down to new england sinai and curahealth. my friend recommended new england sinai so i tried to set up a tour but it was like pulling teeth to get it arranged. i couldn't get calls returned and then when i finally set it up and showed up and no one knew i was coming so i sat there for 30 min so they could find someone to show me around. finally got my tour and i have to say it's really a nice facility but it was more of the same with the staff. they seemed overworked and rude and didn't want to be bothered. i'm from the south where being respectful and courteous to others is extremely important and these people really rubbed me the wrong way. so then i drove on over to curahealth without any appointment and walked in and asked the lady at the front desk for a tour. she thanked me for coming in and made a call and a minute later bridget came out and shook my hand with a smile (big points in my book) and took me on a tour. the facility is a little older and smaller than new englanf sinai but the staff was very friendly. eveyone was nice and answered my questions. so i made my decision and my mom was sent to curahealth a few days later. i have to say that i believe my mom got the best care there. i visited almost every day and was never turned away. i met all her nurses and respiratory people and everyone was always happy to answer my questions. i met the ceo greg who was a quiet guy and would never laugh at my jokes :( but he was always there for me. i even saw him on the floor helping his staff with patients a bunch of times. mom got better after a few weeks and we were a little sad when we had to leave but i still visit sometimes to say hi to everyone.

do not waste your time going to see him. i was 39w pregnant when i was able to get an appointment in the urology dept.( he was the only doctor available before my due date). when we walked in the room, he already seemed rush. he ask what we know about our unborn daughter condition, we explained. he just said "right now there's nothing i can tell you until she's born" and if we had any questions for him. whatever questions we had, either asking about similar cases, or options available for cases like this, etc. he would reply "we won't know until she's born" and kept rushing us. we understand he ca not give an exact plan based on ultrasound and test results. however i find it absurd he could not give a comparison to other cases he might had and what those cases looked like based on the information we provided. bottom line, we drove 2hrs to see him so he could just say over and over again "we won't know until she's born" and rush us through the appointment.

somewhat hard to find but very efficient and clean once you get there. something of a drive from marietta, but professional service with little waiting.

the hampton va medical center employs the best geriatrics & extended care and hospice unit staff. my husband was taken to hospice due to a terminal illness. ms. shelia griffin, home based primary care manager is the best there is. she is extremely knowledgeable and her experience is matched by none and had ms. griffin and ms. bailey not been there in my husband's time of need, i would have lost him a lot sooner.  they single-handedly expedited his transfer and his care began.  along with ms. griffin, yvonne bailey, mary wells, dr. rosanne newman, dr. terry guyton-smith and the entire hospice unit rendered compassion and care to my husband until his departure. i cannot express how much it meant to have had these individuals there for me when i was in need. i already knew that geriatrics had the best employees and i have been the recipient of the type of care they provide to their veterans. va care is very underrated and for those who are veterans, if/when the time comes to need medical attention, think first, to go to hampton vamc.

this review is for the walk-in/urgent care clinic. i was told at the ward clinic the wait would be 45 minutes there so i called here and the receptionist said that she couldn't promise anything but at the moment there was only one patient and two doctors. i was in a bit of pain so decided to come here instead. 

i wasn't aware the main hospital had a walk-in clinic, but the receptionist at ward was very helpful in explaining where to find it, and that we should park in the main hospital garage.

so fyi, the walk-in clinic is in the strode building to the right as you're looking at the entrance from king street. my husband dropped me off at the patient dropoff area so that i could go to the clinic while he parked, and there were plentiful signs for the strode building. it's located just past the pharmacy, and you go through a walkway to get to it. 

the super helpful receptionist quickly took my info and immediately provided me with a cup for a urine sample. i provided it, and it took about 10-15 minutes before they called me back to see the doctor.

based on previous experience, i thought it was a kidney infection or kidney stone - but i wanted to rule out appendicitis because two of my sisters had to have surgery for it, one of them just a month ago.

after hearing my symptoms, dr. susie chun didn't think it was appendicitis and ordered an ultrasound to check my right kidney, where the pain was. we then went to radiology, which is in the main building, second floor. the receptionist and techs were also friendly and helpful there; btw it's super freezing in there, so they provide warm blankets in a metal heater at the back, against the wall. note: you open the heater by pulling on the right side of the door, not the left. watched a couple of people struggle to open it before realizing what side to open. also, for an ultrasound, you must have a full bladder. because i emptied mine to provide a sample at intake, i had to drink several cups and wait about 20 minutes before they could do the procedure.

after the ultrasound, we went back to the clinic, where dr. chun said it showed slight inflammation to my kidney. she didn't want to have me go straight to a ct scan since it involves radiation, but with the ultrasound results she thought it best to confirm with a ct scan. so i went back to radiology, where they were just as nice the second time, and did the procedure quickly.

back at the clinic again, and dr. chun confirmed the kidney stone, showing me the imaging of one in my kidney (wasn't causing the pain) and one in my ureter (that was the culprit). it wasn't large enough to require surgery so she prescribed a medication to help me pass that sucker and i could go home. all in all it took about three hours, but the pain had eased and i was so relieved,  i could be patient with all the tests. 

everyone at both clinics were so helpful and friendly, from the receptionists to the nurses to dr. chun. it was a fairly slow saturday so maybe that made for a better experience since no one was rushed dealing with a ton of patients, but i appreciated the warmth and care i received today. it made a very uncomfortable experience much easier to bear.

careful of this place. they cancel appointments without telling you. when you ask the supervisor why said she's not familiar with mychart. really?! my appointment was on mychart a couple of weeks ago. where did it go? someone cancelled it and it wasn't me. 

it's weird when you leave your last appointment with an appointment card of an appointment and somehow you find out that the appointment was cancelled by me before my last visit when i requested an earlier appointment. well why did the receptionist and the md himself say i already had a follow-up appointment scheduled in four months (the original appt).

even despite that it's the  staff's incompetence, they blame the patient instead and say the md (who's double-booked and covering for another provider on medical leave) who is doing me a favor by offering me appointments at times that don't work in my schedule. i purposely schedule my md appointments on the same day so i don't need to keep on taking vacation leave. so i had scheduled other md appointments purposely on the same day. i can't reschedule these appointment either as it is still with a specialist too. 

then i get the guilt trip that i should make the appointment time they gave me because they are accommodating me on the day i was supposed to have my original appointment...their mistake. if i don't take the appointment there is no such thing as a wait-list because i am already being accommodated so my next appointment which was supposed to be next week is now pushed back another six weeks. apparently my other doctors don't matter because they are doing me a favor by giving me an appointment. 

some people need to learn proper etiquette and customer service skills, especially the so-called supervisor tracy. never do you blame the patient for a mistake made by your staff...

the operator nikki was so helpful in helping me schedule an appt. for the soonest available pcp. i first called to originally schedule with dr. zachariah but due to his new patient appt being on a day i couldn't do she helped me by looking through a lot of the int med doctors schedules to see what she could get us sooner and low and behold she found an appt for dr. picket (don't know if i pronounced that correctly). for next week monday the 23rd. so thanks soo so much nikki (strath pbx operator)

just had a left hip replacement performed by dr maeda and his team. it went very well, was on time, and the post-op team were incredible. nurse dandy made sure i was comfortable while i was waiting for my overnight room, which was available almost immediately. tasha, jp and aileen, the nurses helping me recover after surgery were awesome. they made me feel at home and comfortable while staying overnight. mahalo straub, your service is outstanding!

lazy and uncaring staff. my friend obviously had something wrong with him. he lost partial vision all of a sudden. the er checked him out briefly, no tests, said make an appointment with a neurologist. well, he had a massive stroke (in addition to the one he must have had earlier that caused the partial vision loss) 4 weeks later, 3 days before his neurologist appointment, and he died. i hate straub. i will never go there or bring anyone there again.

this review is for the emergency room physician assistant.  she made rude unprofessional comments to me.  i refused a test and she forced me to take it and claimed that if she does it, i wont feel a thing...she lied.  if you can't feel empathy for patients that come in or listen to how they feel or respect their decisions on health care, why are you working in this field??  even the nurse made a comment to me about the physician assistant after she left the room.  the doctor and the nurse was very gentle and friendly.  i wouldn't recommend coming here.  i would recommend queens.

straub nurses can't get things done. i went to see a doctor. i told her that i need to change my address. i tried to update my address using mychart weeks ago and it didn't get changed. the nurse said "ok". then i went to get imaging. i called to have my imaging record. the lady tried to verify my address. it's wrong. we figured they still have my old address on file. she said i need to call admitting office to have my address changed. she tried to verify my pcp name, is wrong. so i called admitting office, the customer service representative, a lady who picked up the phone sounded irritated and was trying to rush me off the phone. she said "you just had an appointment today, the department nurse should have changed it." ok, i asked her can you change it for me? she said "ok". after i told her my new address, i then asked her to update my pcp name to this doctors name. she said "ok". weeks later i still didn't see my information get updated on mychart. now i have to sign up to paperless billing to make sure my bill don't get send to the old address. why it is so hard to get our record up to date?

if you want your loved one that cannot walk to lay on a pee soaked pad around 10:30 a.m., then this is the place for your loved one. shift changes should have already happened and morning checks for water, freshening up, breakfast and meds. better care at a veterinary clinic. i gave 1 star only because i had to give a rating to comment.

an amazing place to give birth if you're able to do it. it's pretty advanced in the sense that as a general rule they won't admit you until you're in active labor, and then they'll hustle to discharge you as soon as 6 hours after birth -- which is great if all goes perfectly and you're ready for that level of independence. with my first child i needed a little more support both before and after the birth so i ended up across the street at the hospital, but i had my second child at the birth center, and i can honestly say it was one of the most beautiful and empowering experiences of my life. i felt so well taken care of and totally free to be myself at every moment. the midwives here are exceptional in that they truly make every effort to give you the birth experience you want. i also want to give special acknowledgement to nurse bronwyn mastrangelo who clearly has a deep passion for this work and was like a guardian angel to me throughout my delivery. if you're looking for a home-birth-like experience and you're prepared to do the early stages of laboring at home, but you still want the security of hospital resources nearby, this is the place for you.

terrible place.  i went in with so much anxiety and couldn't fully control my body or emotions and all i hear in the background is them talking shit about me saying i'm a dumbass and other rude things. i was told i could put my clothes back on by one doctor after the ekg due to my anxiety getting worse with it off and another guy immediately said he didn't care how it made me feel i had to stay undressed. they seriously don't care about how your feeling. they get annoyed when patients come in and they openly talk and laugh at patients problems thinking no one is listening. if you don't like people. then don't work at a hospital where you have to help people get better.

great staff from receptionist to nurses to the drs.   beautiful facility and supper friendly and professional.  nurses crystal and ruby was amazing and dr. jablonski and his team are the best if the best.  and lovely jessica (from puerto rico) was so cheerful and helpful (at 6:30 am).   great job everyone.   and thank you.  mike and doug (herman)

my wife has had two surgical procedures here; and, the facility is nice!  it is modern, clean; and, the staff is super - from reception to the nurses, to the doctors.  everyone is super professional, kind, and caring.

the facility has very ample parking, with a space to load and unload patients with mobility concerns or who may be recovering from surgery.

it is easily accessed from i-4 via the par street exit.

the staff there made me feel comfortable from the moment i arrived! angel explained that she had the exact surgery i was getting ready too have. made me feel at ease! the nurse ruby was excellent also and i dare not leave out the anesthesiologist who had such a wonderful sense of humor! i can't remember every one's name but the experience was fantastic! you guys rock thanks a million and god bless you!

don't get sick on the coast.  incompetence and you spend hours waiting and  the bedside manner of the doctors, nurses and support staff are severely lacking.  went to er with my wife.  they took an hour to see her and it wasn't a doctor then they put us back in waiting room,  and no communication from nurses or doctors on what's going on.....the medical community is getting paid far too much

the worst... nurses there are condescending and think they're better than others. not all nurses are bad but i don't recommend having a baby there. their moms program is ok but the nurses at the birthing center are so rude and just awful. the head nurse will ignore your concerns and will call dhs on you if you're a minority.  the worst nurses! exception of two or three... they made my first child experience incredibly difficult and made me cry.  i mean, i cry often but they made me depressed.

the thing about the little clinic is it's fast and convenient. if one comes here expecting great customer service by the front staff, then don't come. the last two times i've been here i have arrive at their opening time of 8:30. it takes about 15 mins to get greeted or even acknowledged as set up seems to be the focal point. don't get me wrong, set up is important but would it hurt to look up, smile, and make your sick guest feel welcomed? just a thought....

now the nurse practitioner/doctor is pretty sweet and caring so definitely sit out the cold welcome for inside the office as it does warm up. guess the cold never bothered me anyway?? ‍
address: 19711 E Smoky Hill Rd Unit C

review: $12,047.26 bill for my husband's stress test!  they do not take cigna insurance and said nothing about that when my husband checked in with a cigna insurance card!  i think they should be obliged to disclose that to patients checking in with insurance that they do not accept!      cigna paid nothing, and it was not applied to my deductible or out-of-pocket.  since we had the procedure approved in advance, if we had gone elsewhere, it would have been a $40 co-pay.

i actually do not allow anyone to call an ambulance for me because i always get brought to landmark hospital. ok so needless to say i was dying and an ambulance was called and for the fifth time this year i was brought and admitted to landmark hospital. i was told i had inclusions blocking the circulation to foot and yes they focused on that and secondary my toe that turned black and gangrene. they discharged me and referred me back to my podiatrist that had initially referred to the hospital. i went home only top bre brought back with the usual double pnemonia i seem to catch from there 4 times already this year. this time the doctors decided to play with my pacemaker...at the time i haff no idea they w0llere doing it without the bio company that controls and tests it. it's called comprising the integrity of my pacemaker. thanks again landmark. nurses were wonderful. especially jenn and all the icu nurses.

i cannot say enough good things about this rehab hospital, they were just amazing. 

i was admitted here from the hospital to undergo physical therapy after a stroke left my right leg very weak and i had difficulty standing. jean the nurse who was there when i was admitted was so kind and understanding it truly made me feel better about being there. that said all of the nurses were amazing, very kind and knowledgeable; it was because of them my stay was so smooth. 

the program includes three hours of physical therapy per day which was intense but welcomed. the gym they have was huge and had everything from a car to all stations one would encounter outside the hospital. the therapists were all great, they would push you as far as you are willing but we're very sensitive to over exerting. 

probably less important the food was pretty good all things considered and the rooms were very nice. this is a top notch facility and one i wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone in need.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of Desert Canyon

review: i guess it's okay. i don't much like the doctors here because they refuse to treat me because i have a condition that might cause their work problems. anyway, everyone seemed to be pretty nice and place is clean. i gave a ride to one of their patients and he seems to be happy with their service.

my husband passed away here 3 1/2 years ago. the staff could not have more kind and considerate of his care. and, the 18 month follow up by the social worker was fantastic! they not only care about the patient but their loved ones!
fac_name: Franciscan Hospice House and Palliative Care

review: had my hernia repair surgery done at mercy hospital and i was impressed. professional and caring nurses, great surgeon and quick recovery. valet parking made it easy. everything seemed clean and organized.

i got really sick and had to be taken to mercy to get a couple blood transfusions the nurses are super nice the doctors were very understanding and everyone was very helpful in explaining things that i had questions about - the only big complaint i have is that the last time i was a there they lost my moms car keys the valet lost her keys he showed us a key ring with no car key and he said it was like that when he got them - needless to say my mom was pissed we hardly got any sleep so we both had boho for over 24 hours so all we wanted to do is go home and get some rest but we couldn't because he lots the keys so instead we had to sit and wait for my uncle to get home from work (he works in fredonia) so he could grab my moms extra key from my grandmas house (we live in north collins) and bring it all the way to mercy - it was honestly the worst 48 hours of my life - i haven't been back to mercy lately because i get iron infusions at a different place now - just watch out for the valet parking

this is long overdue, like several years, but just have to review this hospital.  i was visiting my sister locally when i started to notice some chest pains. i was kinda worried as i had already experienced four heart attacks.  let my baby sister know and in the car we go to the er. only one patient registering in front of me but my sister goes right up and tells them i was having the chest pains.  
doors opened and two rn's come out, one on each arm and into the er i go. both started the usual triage, cardiac workup and iv's (know this stuff as i am/was an er nurse). then the respiratory therapist comes in to do the ekg, labs are taken, x-ray tech. comes in for for the chest x-ray and a very personable doctor shows up quite fast to start her exam. 
getting crowded in there but i am in one of the major treatment rooms so plenty of space.  there was a lot going on but all organized. sis is with me the whole time.
they admitted me for observation but first the hospital pharmacist comes to the er to verify my medications. all this for me but i know this is what they do for each patient that comes in for treatment but at the moment i felt as if i was their number one patient.
spent the night in a nice quiet room looking at the beautiful woods out the window.  all tests came back negative so didn't have to make the trip down the hill.  food was ok as much as you can get on a cardiac diet anyway.  only downside was an uncomfortable bed.  could feel the metal.

let me start by saying this is the day after i was released from south bay hospital. i read all the positive and negative reviews so here goes my review; first er staff were great (go chad!!), as a female i had 2 male nurses who were highly professional. i was having chest pain and was admitted for observation. my room was ready rather quickly, i was totally impressed with the cleanliness of this hospital (kudos housekeeping!). everyone was pleasant and they responded quickly to my concerns/needs. i follow a keto diet and although the dietary didn't know what foods i could eat, they allowed me to pick off the menu (what hospital does that?!!). now to the actual medical care-dr. wise was thorough and she kept me informed as did the nursing staff on the floor (2nd floor). david my first day nurse (best!) and the nurse lead chonda (can't get over her attentiveness for running a whole floor!!!), trish (sorry if i mistake spelling) and amy both afternoon and night nurses were great as well! keira and michele (big shout out!!) available and responsible as med techs! the phlebotomy staff, ultrasound technician for my echogram (bettina i believe), xray staff (made me comfortable through providing that extra support), the personable transport staff, and thank you all for your care. although i may not have shown it, i was nervous and worried! i didn't know the hospital and am really happy and satisfied knowing that you exist! so, thank you all again for the exceptional care i was given!!

this place is really bad, as everyone else has stated.  they kept me so drugged up that i have little recollection of being there.  they claimed i was an alcoholic and gave me detox drugs even though my bac was .00 and i hadn't touched a drink in over a month.  i told them not to give me detox drugs because i don't drink that much.  they did, and i hallucinated.

i have severe hypertension.  they gave me no bp meds.  my bp skyrocketed to the point that the pharmacist ran into my room in a panic, meds in hand.

my room was bad, but i felt horrible for the patients sleeping on the floor with only a blanket.

the attitude here is that patients are inmates and are the enemy.  jails are run like this, not a place that's supposed  to help people who need it.

geraldo rivera would have a field day here.  the state needs to check this place out and shut it down.

two days after i was finally unbaker acted, i flew out of florida to another state.  i would truly rather die than go back there.

horrible feel here. just came to visit my father who has dimentia. looks like he hasn't been given a bath or a shave in weeks. fruit flies all over room and visiting room temperature kept unreasonably cold for patients as well around food and coffee machines is disgusting. lobby dirty and staff not very warm at all. i'll be making formal complaint to state hotline and thank gos were transferring him monday to a wonderful facility in ny to live out his time with respect.  pathetic this place not held to minimum human standards.

i went for an ultrasound. i was told i could pay $40 if i paid cash, but then i was informed that because i have insurance my copay would actually be over $400. when i asked if i could pay cash and not charge my insurance, they said that was not an option. whatever payment scheme they have set up here incentivizes patients to not have insurance, and punishes the responsible people who pay their premiums and contribute to healthcare.

horrible doctors, old and stuck in their ways. don't treat the patient just a diagnosis. i had a bad infection and dr was so conceited and rude, didn't hear my concerns. the hospital is nasty, old building and dirty. there is no cafeteria. your visitors have to leave hospital parking garage to get food, then just decide it's too much a hassle to re park.  i'll never come back to this hospital. do not recommend if you have infections

the one star is for the coffee/food service staff, and one security guard in the morning. 

after being "transferred" from another hospital to pch i check my daughter in having a fractured tibia. she had x-rays done at the first hospital and the doctor there rushed us out saying how my daughter needed to be seen by a child specialist and pch is the best, they stated they contacted them and they had a bed for her. i declined the ambulance transfer since i would be covering this cost out of pocket. once at pch it was apparent every sick child in the valley was there. i put a mask on my daughter and we took a seat. 
once called up for triage about 45min later i informed the nurse that my daughter had a does of morphine at the other hospital and i was concerned that she was not being monitored closely. he stated her vitals we normal, she was fine. i then told him we were sent from another hospital, they told us there was a room for us and my daughter was really uncomfortable since she has a broken leg. he told me they always tell people this we had to wait. 
okay i understand couple 3 hours in the er naturally, 6 i repeat 6 hours later! mind you, my baby was freezing, she broke her leg at cheer i was not prepared for a cold all night stay in the er, i asked repeatedly for a blanket, we slept snuggled on a couch thing they have, and i watched her breathing all night because i was afraid of shock. 
once called back the nurse was sweet, i was completely out of it, no sleep, stress, worry, the list goes on... doctor came in to say her leg was broke, um duh, he was going to get her more medicine, and ct scan, 4 more hours later a new doctor comes in all i want to do at this point is leave but we came here for a damn ct scan so thats what i asked for, 2 more hours later i made an appointment banner children's specialist. 
i informed them i was going somewhere else for her surgery since it obviously was not nearly as emergent as the other hospital made it. at that point nurses became indignant when i asked for the records i provided when i got their. they literally lost my x-rays. in fact the nurse told me "i can call back and make a complaint if i don't like the way i am being treated". those people were just starting their 12 hr shift and were getting paid to be rude to a worried mother. good job. unfortunately, this was my first experience with pch and i will not be returning. i will pay my bill and pretend they don't exist. if your child has an emergency please call the ambulance because walking into this place is a joke.

another appointment for a daughter
moved around schedule multiple times
told to be here at a certain time
have to wait well past scheduled time
all the money they take in you would think....
but
not happening they waste your time and give you a broad statement of what something might be.

this place needs to be better

unfortunately we had to bring our daughter to pch. the nurses and doctors are very thorough and keep you up-to-date with what's going on. filling out paperwork is a breeze. the only two negative things i would say about the hospital. my daughter was given a e-signature for medication. the medication e-signed was placed on 3/7 /2020 at 1440 am. when i called the next day the e-signature was never sent over to the walgreens that we had on the paperwork.
the two negative thing i would state about the hospital is the discharge process was extremely long. we had to press the red button to notify the nurse that she was eating and drinking ok. the second negative thing i would say by the hospital is i had to call the hospital to have them send over the e-signature and i never received a phone call back. i end up going to my pediatrician and they ordered the proper medication that was needed.
my son came for an appendix removal. the staff are very nice and always keep you up to date on whats going on. we are very thankful to have such a wonderful hospital in my area.

watch out for some serious overbilling!! we took our son in to see how much a circumcision would cost. we received a quote for $7000 a $9000!! we checked around and found that this should be a relatively inexpensive procedure between $500 - $1500. guess we aren't going with phoenix children's price gouging option.... oh wait....they got me anyway, charging me $657 for 2x 10 minute consultations. i call to ask where in the world they are coming up with these rates but they felt they were perfectly fair. i don't.... shame on you.

now i hear back from them offering for me to call them. you have my number, call me if you want to fairly give me a reasonable rate for a consultation. also, i don't needd any financial counseling. my finances are doing just fine. what i need is a fair price for a 100 minute consultation... perhaps $50 or $100 would make a lot of sense.... not $375
what a disappointment!!!!!!! er is ridiculous!!!!! going on a 3hr wait in the er waiting room for a kids broken arm!!!!!!!!     this is fxxxxxxx crazy!!!!!

this rating is specific to valley anesthesiology consultants. this company has been very difficult to work with. we have been paying monthly for anesthesiology our son received during a procedure at phoenix children's. they sent us to collections without warning. we paid the bill off at collections but they don't have record of that. valley anesthesiology states they pulled it back from collections. what? why? why weren't we told that was going to happen!?! it has been four months and they are still not honoring our payment and we are still receiving bills. maybe phoenix children's doesn't deserve this rating but valley anesthesiology has a bad reputation per reviews i'm reading. maybe the hospital should consider discontinuing their partnership with them.

shame on you phoenix children's hospital. my daughter went for treatment a couple of months ago. i called to make a payment agreement to close the bill for 2019 and a supervisor by the name of luis c. was completely rude and disrespectful. i've always been a supporter of pch until today. so disappointed!

im originally from israel and i brought my 15 month old son to the er room. my son was hysterically crying with pain as we waited for 30+ minutes with zero care in the world. i ask the front desk nurse how long should we expect to wait and the response was "there are other people and we have 2 helicopters bringing people too so wait" as the other nurse is is smiling... my wife and i give it another 15 minutes and nothing. i left the hospital and went to st joseph's which took my son's condition way more seriously and let us in right away. my son has serious infections and he had a fever! i don't understand how you operate but this is the worst medical service i have ever encountered in any country i have visited or lived in! i would never trust your hospital with my son ever again! zero stars and shame on you.

dreadfully incompetent billing department. please allow me to provide some healthy advice pch: if there is an outstanding bill that is due go ahead and send it out so that it can be paid. go ahead and call me and that is perfectly fine as well. 

instead, i received a letter from a collection company because apparently phoenix children's hospital billing staff is so inept that they are unable to communicate in the simplest terms that there is a balance due.

my credit is exemplary. never late.  i went on the collection company site and paid immediately.  this was so unnecessary you bunch of dithering dolts.

my daughter had a simple cyst she was born with that needed to be removed. she had surgery at phoenix children's hospital. the surgeon did not remove the hair follicle (that was causing chronic infection) as he said he would. surgery left a permanent wound that would not heal (the size of a quarter). at follow up surgeon responded that he did not know what to do with wound he created (worse than the cyst) and referred me to wound care specialist. wound care determined that another surgery was necessary due to not healing. i was told by finance not to pay for any of the next surgery but at time of surgery nothing was noted about me not being responsible for payment. i complained to help department and was told that the case would be reviewed. i was just contacted by help department that phoenix children's did everything right and were not responsible. i was to pay for both surgeries ($12,000) after insurance. they were adamant that the hair follicle was removed, despite 2nd surgeon making sure that he removed it in the second surgery. i am so unimpressed with the poor care and irresponsibility of the hospital. two surgeries on a young child is too many.

sadly i have a granddaughter that's been in and out of pch for over two years now! she's currently in the icu and will be for a while longer. as everyone knows, a chronically ill or suddenly ill child puts a huge strain on all family members. the staff at pch, are all the real deal! from anthony the security/love spreading big guy you first encounter at the main entrance, the check in staff, dr's nurses ( nurses rule) the environmental staff, cafeteria staff, volunteers and all medical support staff  handle your child with kindness, understanding and honesty! they take so much of the fear and worry out of a very painful situation! i wish i could wrap them all in my arms and give them a big hug! thank you everyone at pch, love & hugs, cara's papa!

picu is a wonderful place full of angels. once we were moved to the regular floor, it was a nightmare. inadequate care, insufficient staffing and couldn't get the help we needed for my 4 month old son with rsv and reactive airway disease. instead of empathy or apologies, we got defense and excuses. my son suffered needlessly because of their nonchalant, blow-mom-off attitudes. i had to strongly advicate for my 4 month old son because they seemed largely disinterested in partnering with me. add to that the unprofessionalism of me walking out of the room to hear them bitching about me. i was terrified and frustrated and heart broken, yet still kind and patient throughout the ordeal. i just wanted partnership in helping my son. instead they treated us like an annoying inconvenience. my experience was absolutely not aligned to the values pch espouses.

terrible, terrible place !!  looks like a good stamp office !!!!  doctors are slow and this place altogether is horrible !!! i see now why all the negative reviews on this place! i had my 14-year-old son in there today and nobody told me to check in on these little red computers, how are we supposed to know to do that? so after 45 minutes of waiting i went upfront and asked how much longer and they said oh you didn't sign in! i said nobody told me to sign in on those computers that you're supposed to and she said oh well there's going to be two more people ahead of you and i had already waited  45 minutes,  the place was packed and  not a chair to sit in !! dirty disgusting and i will never go back to that place even if i'm dying !

please be advised - this facility is the worst, most unethical,  non-transparent rip off in phoenix. this place claims to be a non-profit, but uses this status to cover a corporate scam that takes advantage by charging exorbitant facility fees to families without prior disclosure. if you have any way of avoiding this place, please do so.  our son had three clinic visits for a pre-existing condition, a series of approximately 5 x-rays, and one mri (we paid over $1,000 in cash up front for the mri). over a year later we were hit with a surprise $3,000 more in facility fees for the x-rays after already paying hundreds of dollars in fees for the physicians, radiologists, and visits. we contested the non-disclosed exorbitant facility fees without any transparent process for how our concerns were handled. they refused to do anything aside from a 20% fee reduction, but these fees should have never occurred in the first place. we then had to take our son to another specialist in florida where the clinic visits, x-rays, travel and accommodations came to less than what we paid phoenix children's. the clinic in florida also addressed the issues our son had, whereas phoenix children's never even helped. if they had disclosed these costs up front, we would have seen their physicians in an outpatient clinic to avoid the several thousand dollar hospital facility fee. please do not ever donate money or resources to this hospital, because it takes advantage of its status as a children's hospital. we will never return to this evil place.

very, very, very disappointed with the er department. this is the 3rd time in a month  i come to the er because my daughter has an ng tube to help her feed and all of those 3 times we have waited for more than 5 hours to go home. today just did it, i can't believe how slow that department was. we go because my daughter's  ng tube will come out when she vomits so she needs a new one when that happens, but  we have to wait for that long and on top of that my daughter has to be without a feeding for 6+ hours. how is that even fair? she depends on that ng tube to eat. not only that, but because of us having to wait in the waiting area my daughter caught something two weeks ago so i had to go back to the er the next day. i had never had a problem, the staff has always helped my daughter out and i was so happy with pch, but this is the 3rd time this has happened and i just think it's very unfair to have a 10 month old go without eating for that long.

my son has received medical care at banner children's hospital and cincinnati childrens hospital. both are fantastic! providing a wonderful level of care. we had the horrid misfortune of spending 5 days in phoenix children's hospital. i would not allow my cat to receive treatment there unless it was the single last place for medical treatment on earth! even then, i would think twice about it. they gave my son medication that every record & document i signed clearly stated not to give to him! that my son had a medical condition that clearly, any 1st year medical student would understand the reasoning why not to give him that medication. phoenix childrens pain management doctors gave it to him three times! we had to go back to cincinnati children's hospital even though we live in scottsdale az for his extended medical care. there is a reason that phoenix children's hospital ranks among the lowest of children's hospitals nationwide!
they are very kind with a patient they treat it you with respect and fast thank you to the staff my husband are doing better this people here are amazing

i had my surgery here but i wouldn't go back if i had too , i had a very horrible experience, i don't want to talk about , bathroom was never cleaned , room and hospital is so outdated , the nurses are kind and understanding that's why i gave a extra star but i would never recommend this hospital , ever!!!!

plainview hospital er - go elsewhere

horrible. charge nurse "colette" was disgusting, rude, & horrible to my mother who was there advocating for me. i was seen on 3/11/20 for severe abdominal pain, fever, and vomiting which had progressively worsened for 5 days, 2 weeks after iud paragard  placement. i was seen this past sunday 3/8/20 at citymd who determined infection & started me on antibiotics. upon arrival to plainview hospital er they ran some tests which indicated fluid accumulation outside of the uterine tissue & again, infection. they also identified very high levels of eosinophils, indicative of allergic reaction, likely to the copper in the iud poisoning me from the inside. they hap-hazardly switched my antibiotic after about 10 hours of waiting. i was sent home with fever, severe abdominal pain, and throwing up. i repeat; discharged with a fever and throwing up on the way out the door.  i was there through lunch & dinner, but was only offered a mini can of ginger-ale despite all testing being completed before the dinner cart came around. 

that evening, the vomiting and pain became worse. i felt as though i was going to die of sepsis. i returned to plainview hospital er on 3/12/20 for severe pain, continued vomiting, fever, and now dizziness & confusion. i was provided a room with fresh blood on the fitted sheet after about 2 hours of waiting in triage. the nurses response "do you want me to change the bed linen?". after i insisted that it be changed, the nurse drew my blood, which again showed infection. after about another 2 hours of waiting to be seen by the doctor, he told to go home & follow up with gyn which was a pre-scheduled appointment with the wrong information on it. the doctor's name had been switched with another doctor, and the address was inaccurate. while we waited in limbo, my mother called to confirm this appointment scheduled for tomorrow, 3/13/20. the office had no record of me scheduled to come in, and denied speaking with plainview hospital er in coordination of services. the most pathetic of all was plainview hospital er's reasoning to send me home; they have no ob-gyn able to come to the hospital, nor competent enough doctors in-house to perform an iud removal at plainview hospital er (which was actually placed by a nurse at time of insertion). in the charge nurse colette's words, an iud causing such severe symptoms & infection was "not an emergency". i could not walk out to the pickup area due to such severe pain, vomiting, and dizziness. i passed out during removal of the saline iv drip, then began again vomiting. the nurses response "someone get a wheelchair to wheel her out".  i was given a vomit bag & wheeled out to the pickup area, shaking in pain. i am 25, excellent health, no prior medical issues. i live an active lifestyle, i am an avid skier & scuba diver. i was not seen for an injured leg, or as an elderly adult. i was seen for severe abdominal pain. to be in such severe pain warranting full body shaking, low bp, dizziness, & inability to walk; there is clearly an issue. i walked into this hospital. for a nurse to send someone who cannot walk out, worse than on arrival, is disgusting & negligent.  their excuse; "this is a community hospital, we can't help you". i work in a community hospital also owned by northwell health. the staff that i work with would never treat a patient or a patient family member like that. it was absolute negligence. 2 days wasted & infection worsening, but they "could not help" as "it is not an emergency".

and to make matters worse, the staff have zero concern for hippa or patient privacy. they sent an elderly woman with a broken eye socket having zero memory recollection in the bed next to me home too, after asking her about her iud removal. when she appeared confused & her family denied her having an iud, the nurse stated "oh right that is the patient in bed a". are you kidding me. not only did they clearly confuse myself with her, but they humiliated me in front of several of her family members present & violated my hippa rights. 

moral of the story; i guess the staff's operational definition of "emergency" only caters to certain populations. women's health & elderly health is neglected. stay away.

from pre-surgical to the operation, my visit with this hospital has been outstanding!!! five stars all the way! everybody made my visit comfortable, painless and accommodating. i had knee arthroscopic knee surgery and it was painless throughout. thank you to the entire staff that made my visit actually enjoyable!!!! dr. mallen who performed the surgery was outstanding! thank you!

it is extremely distressing that fremont hospital is one of the few inpatient psychiatric facilities in the bat area. it is, based on my experience, a terrible place to be.
specifically, the psychiatrist on staff seem to openly flout the law and restrict liberties of their patients. we experienced this first hand.

basically, "for profit" system. 

in retrospect,

years ago.  

the intake lady i wish i had her name was very good and promised real help. however, once our loved ones get up to the unit it's a whole "other story!"   they failed to follow up on service that was promised. 

sadly, the majority of social workers were "not" the humble, good, person-centered type, filipino. 

cuz, i know and have "real filipino friends".  to know the difference. 

these were the  "other" type. 

that get the degrees for the money potential. disregard people and real duties. real service. get paychecks, eat well sleep good at night. no worries. 

shame on them!!!

i painfully took issues up the chain of command, very time consuming, arduous, got run around with filipino social workers. with chatty ignorant non direct adhd like behavior. the first social worker that had answered phone sounded worse than a patient. i hoped it didn't set the tone of the event. unfortunately it pretty much did. turned out to be a bit of a joke experience. we didn't get the service the intake worker had promised. social workers who didn't care. dr rushed in all the time.and there only few minutes. disregard main concerns. not trauma informed obviously. 

on top of the already challenging circumstances in which we live in this world, being a caregiving support person to someone who is suffering in pain.  especially a kind wonderful, good, gifted human being who deserves the very best, who is truly suffering. to be let down like this is really painful and horrible. 

research shows family support is a must this should be valued. when it's not it majorly raises red flags. 

sadly, the response by ceo and his secretary was not much better. it's when i realized it's all about the money. my loved one was released and re injured despite my begging them. i later found out these filipino social workers wrote that i hindered the discharge duties. ugh, i'm pretty sure my loved one still has the scars to prove what happened. what "i" was trying to prevent!  the lack of accountability in this system is very damaging!!
