allow me to say first and foremost this hospital runs like a well oiled machine. unlike your local doctor mayo is seeing patients who have traveled several hours in order to be seen. i got referred by my ent after he was unable to help correct my severe sinus issue. the doctor and her assistant were both friendly and engaging and the doctor seemed to genuinely want to help. not only was i able to see the doctor but i was also able to get labs done without having to return. the only thing that i was unaware of was they charge $5.00 cash for parking and for someone like me who never carries cash that could have been a problem. i don't know if they have free parking available or an atm somewhere close. again not a big thing just something to be aware just in case you ever have to travel here.

very clean and organized just like the rest of the mayo clinic. connected to the main hospital through a tunnel. the volunteer desk was very helpful and kind. signs every where to direct you to where you  need to go. bathrooms very clean. staff here are helpful. doctors are great. very professional.

great experience, especially given the horrible back pain i was experiencing. arrived without appointment, checked in with very courteous, caring front desk staff, offered ice or heat pad, seen by arnp within about 30-40 min, prescription filled at franciscan pharmacy. didn't feel like a number in line like some urgent care facilities. thank you for the wonderful care and treatment you all provided.
fac_name: Franciscan Prompt Care at St. Joseph

review:
had four visits to the ed.  the staff and process were great.  no complaints.  i was in the icu on two of those visits for two weeks.  a few minor problems but they corrected them all, or promised to anyway.  so no complaints there.

so why i'm putting a one star?  this hospital touts itself as a community hospital.  however, it is not.  the uc hospital doctors prescribed some heavy duty medications that need (as per the fda and the drug manufacturers) close follow up including office visits and testing.  yet, the earliest i could get an appointment was eight months after the hospital visit.  the specialists tell me that they are outpatient and not connect to the hospital and so nothing they can do.  so why does this "community" hospital not associate with other doctors in the community who can treat in follow up?  and why start aggressive treatment and not follow fda and best practice guidelines?  their suggestion:  just keep coming back to the ed and get treated there.  

i spent over 20 years working in hospitals and suggest you avoid this one.

i'm writing specifically about the cancer center here and more specifically about the infusion center.  seriously, this place could double as a day spa if you weren't, ya know, going through cancer.  the nurses and everyone working there make the experience amazing.  they are so kind and attentive.  the views of the mountains out the large windows removes the need for further entertainment, and it feels new and clean.  if you are sick or need privacy, private rooms are available to combat the more open feel (vs the more hospital curtain separation at the main aurora campus).  it's truly a beautiful and new hospital with wonderful staff.  i adore it.  they need to hire more fulltime nurses so we can get on the schedule more!

a family member had a scheduled surgery at uc health in highlands ranch. the care she received from the surgeons and medical staff was great. no complaints there. my complaint is that the waiting areas and restrooms on both floors that we spent time on were very dirty, trash cans were overflowing full and there was popcorn and trash on the floors in the waiting rooms. we were there till past midnight and back again first thing in the morning and the areas were untouched, still very dirty and we never once saw a janitor.  it's disturbing to think that the hospital waiting areas and restrooms are not being disinfected daily.  i don't think it's a coincidence that we all came down with a virus after being at that hospital for a couple of days, despite being very diligent about washing our hands and using hand sanitizer.
quality care, caring staff.  i have had more than one outpatient procedure here and have always had great results.  thanks for your wonderful care.

if i could i would rate this hospital a negative 15. if you want to die come to this hospital its dirty , the staff is rude ,lazy & there system goes down ever minute. i came here numerous times and ended up leaving to go to a different hospital. this literally was the last straw for me. i brought my 4 month old daughter here so they can figure out why she can't stop throwing up , in that process  i signed in went to the back weighted her and  came back down to wait . it took them forty-five minutes to put us in a room. oh ps it's 2am so its barely anyone there , but any-who we got to the room i let her sit on the bed & we waited & waited & waited till about 25 minutes later , i seen a nurse walk towards our took a peek then turned around fast & walked back to the desk. after that we still  were waiting after another 20 minutes more i was already pissed off but i started to put our things together so we could leave, as i'm walking out there sitting there fat assess down talking about there relationship issues & what amazon has on sale. they need to have state come in here because this type of behavior is unacceptable nor professional. i know a few things on health and this is crap. plus on top of all this bullshit this lovely young lady  whom i met in the waiting room was still sitting there waiting to been seen which her daughter had a high fever of 102. smh something has to be done. this is the worst hospital i ever been to. the new name should of been advent death....

my brother got injured from playing turkey bowl football so i had to take him to the nearest hospital. since it was on thanksgiving, i figured it was good timing that it would not be crowded. 

when we arrived, there was no line so they saw my brother right away. the x-ray confirmed he had a broken collarbone so he had to wear a sleeve for a few months. luckily, he did not need to have surgery. all he needed was to take some meds. 

the whole staff were amazing and provided all the help we needed.

i came after a car accident. the care i got in er was magnificent. i had help  both from the night and day shift on early morning of  march 1 2020. 
i should have taken all the names of the nurses and er staff who attended me and thank each of them  within this review. 
i have received not only medical help but also warmth and  advice. doctor amburgey  was my doctor and he was excellent, compassionate, understanding and very helpful. 

  i saw some negative reviews . the problem is, writing a review takes additional energy
 - which is in most cases provided by anger. satisfied people do not write - they expect the best and when they get it- they are silent. 
within scope of my experience which includes also europe- this is one of the best hospitals i have been to and the best er i was a patient of.
mjhc
terrible staff interaction. i would never recommend coming to this hospital as a person of color.

i had a emergency visit at the labor and delivery section today and olga and anita (rn) and the hospice doctor there were so kind and accommodating. i've been to almost all the other hospital in the bay area for relatives and friends and i can say their service here was over and beyond. i'll be delivering my first child here and can't wait and feel confident i chose the right hospital. this is how health care should be ran with integrity and true compassion

excellent emergency room. i've only been to an er a few times in my life, and this was by far the best and speediest experience. despite the fact that the er was very busy, i was in and out in 3.5 hours, including getting an ecg, ct, bloodwork, iv saline, iv antibiotics, rxs, and a cd of my ct. previously, i've sat in ers in which nothing happened in 3.5 hours.

the doctor took time to answer all my questions, and the nurses and ct tech were very thorough and nice (i don't know their names, but they were all men). the ecg tech (a russian woman) was also very good and caring. all this despite the er being very busy in the middle of the night. 

most important 24 hours after being diagnosed with pneumonia, i'm already feeling better on the antibiotics they prescribed. 

if you ever need to go to the er, go to this hospital!

***another review*** so here i am back at pl again this time my daughter jumped on her bed and hit her head on the desk. we were seen by kristen rodriquez do and she did an amazing job, ordered a ct scan just to be sure all was good. then she and two nurses came in to suture my daughter up. the male nurse brought his phone and put on you tube and the female nurse held her head as i held her body. dr rodriguez did an amazing job suturing my daughter, and calming her so good that my daughter told the nurse that she didn't have to hold her head as she wasn't going to move! i really appreciate the staff that was working the er on 12/28/19 @ 8:00 p.m. . another rough experience made easier by er staff and a great er dr. 

leilani says thank you! 









i have been coming to placentia-linda for years from the west covina area! i even brought my dad here and he eventually passed here. i have always received compassionate care, sometimes better than others.. but never any negative care. and friday when my daughters (kindergarten) school called me my daughter broke her arm i immediately came here. the er wait has always been very shot. as we drove over to pl every bump we hit, move we made my daughter cried in pain. we arrived at the er and checked in when we were immediately called back. (during flu season)! the nurse took us to our room and within 3 minutes we were greeted by dr hoynak. he was very nice and genuinely concerned. he then ordered and x-ray that they did bedside. he was even there to read them while they did them.  she had a bad break in her elbow. the whole time we were their the nurse never left our side from check in - during sedation, putting in place and splinting! 

once it was determined that she needed surgery they made a transfer to choc and we parted ways!! 

i won't go on with my story more because the rest would take place at choc. but i will say the i heard the surgeon dr aminian and dr mueller talking about what a great job they did when they put her arm in place, (dr hoynak) and i'm sure that helped the surgery because they didn't even have to open her up!

i want to thank dr hoynak and all off the er staff at placentia linda for making this nightmare a little bit easier.

this is the most unethical form of billing i've ever seen.... i went to the er and was seen by an attending physician for 5 minutes max. i did not receive any medications or services besides a doctor touching my cheek to tell me he thought i had an infected salivary gland.... 

my insurance was billed over three grand for this and i'm left now with a 552.92 medical bill for a er visit that took less than an hour total from time of entry to time of discharge.

the bill has no itemized services whatsoever and does not explain where this figure came from!?!! 

do not go to this er. this is highway robbery and patient exploitation!!!

staffed 2 doctors on a holiday weekend at peak coronavirus outbreak. i had heart palpitations. i waited 5 hours. didn't even see a doctor except for when they ordered an ekg and a chest x-ray. didn't talk to them either. guy across from me had a broken nose and bloody face. didn't see anybody for over 5 hours either. we were not given any water so we were dehydrating the whole time too. i was discharged with zero communication with aftercare instructions for something i didn't even come in with. they didn't listen to me. i had a preliminary ekg from urgent care that they took from me and never gave back. still don't have my chest x-ray and was never consulted on it.

do not come here if your life depended on it. seriously, just don't. i can't believe i had to pay for this er visit.

had surgery here last friday. was very dark and hard to find at 5 am. 
upon entering they have a seamless check in process, very efficient. all the nurses were amazing especially the surgical nurses who were able to get an iv in with one poke after carefully studying my veins and using a special gauge. this is much appreciated! thank you placentia- linda team!

placentia-linda hospital not only took excellent care of me from the er to the room and icu. i came in with pneumonia and apparently it was advanced and the care i received, along with their experience, saved my life literally! i'm so thankful. i'm 41 years old, male and couldn't believe i caught pneumonia and hospitalized. i was so sick i don't remember the first 4 days of the 6 days i was there. what i do remember, when i was rushed to icu, i was in and out and the respiratory therapist which i found out later that's who is was, her name is emily, she saved me and looked after me throughout the night, along with the rest of the icu team. thank all of you and god bless all of you not just for saving my life but i pray they save many more.

i have been a patient at this hospital alot. i have a  number of issues that i battle with daily. i moved to be able to be brought here by the paramedics when i need help. i would not want to go anywhere else. it is a small hospital and i have never seen a hospital treat everyone with so much respect for each other and for their patients. i trust every nurse, cnas, and social workers, physical therapist,  and the doctors. i would recommend pl hospital to anyone who asks. they have become family to me. i don't think i would be here today if i was sent anywhere elae.

boutique hospital doesn't not mean boutique care., it doesnt even mean great care. i checked in on tuesday for an extreme lateral intraboday bone fusion, which was not only confusing but misleading. he created a 1.5 incision on my right side and did that work. then from what my family was told he rolled me into a prone position and spent another 6 hours there. i am in  such an extreme amount of pain. i cannot sleep, cough, sneeze, or even eat without some type of pain interfering. i was told .5 of dilodid every 4 hours and 10mg of percocet the opposite 4 hours should be enought to manage my pain. the nurse doesnt even want to call the doctor and when i said i would instead, she said that's no how things are done here....  i cant believe i'm saying this, but i think i miss kaiser.

i was seen in the er last year and was treated by dr. paulina mendoza-mancini.  she really took the time to listen to me during a time when i needed it the most.  i'm not going to get into the details here on the world wide web, but i am truly indebted to her and very appreciative of what she did for me.  thank you paulina mendoza-mancini.

top notch care from top notch professionals! many many thanks to the er nurses and dr. who quickly, efficiently and lovingly took care of my 80 year old mom who fell and dislocated her shoulder! high praise to this er room and all the nurses, drs, technicians, and staff! we had initially gone to another closer to them er but left right after checking in due to extreme crowd and rude staff... i called ahead and we rushed over to placentia-linda er , where the staff was caring and the attention immediate! the nurse never left us! i know it's not easy to be a health care professional, the hours are long the patients can be demanding, the work is labor and emotionally exhausting, but placentia linda staff have not lost sight of why they are in the profession of helping others! kudos to you all! especially anthony, caroline and leanne god bless you all!

i had to have surgery and it was done here at placentia-linda hospital.  it all went as planned.  the surgeon was awesome ( dr. kachikwu) and the hospital is beautiful!  the staff here is top notch. they really have been taking care of me while i'm here recovering.  the nurses really are exceeded my expectations every day.  they must love working here because they are all so happy to do there jobs. everyone keeps checking on me and making sure that i'm comfortable. i'm currently in the med-surgery wing.  i can't say enough nice things about this place. if i was closer to another hospital, i'd come here instead. thank you so much to everyone!

we brought my mom carol  here to the er when she became extremely sick with a uti/sepsis, and i cannot say enough good things about our experience at this hospital.  from the er to the dou to the med/surg floor, her care was top notch the entire time!  the hospital is clean, all the staff was so friendly and helpful and i knew my mom was in good hands!  many thanks to her nurses in the er, especially megan, and also simone who wasn't even her nurse but still so helpful!  on the dou unit, thanks to the nurses romarie and alishia, they truly went above and beyond taking care of her, and also to the nurses aides gilbert, and cigi!!  on the med/surg unit, special thanks to some truly spectacular nurses, ryan, virginia, and lauro and all the nurse aides there (eugene, lauren, emily, pedro, kelsie, summer) and i am sure there are some i forgot, but everyone was so nice and caring and patient with my mom, again, i cannot thank you enough!  if you are looking for great care for a loved one, look no further!

excellent doctors, poor nurses. what's the point of having excellent doctors if the nurses are terrible. the nurses are not the nicest. from 5 nurses i'm sure 1 is ok. but the others are not of service. it seems like they don't want to help. asking for things is like pulling teeth. i highly recommend having a loved one care for you 24 hours rather than depending on a nurse to care for your loved one.

the staff leaves a lot to be desired.  2 cna's in my wife's stepmom's room and just not very friendly at all.  and the cleaning after a patient was released in the same room was very shoddy.  i'm hoping i will never have to be placed here.

after going to first aid urgent care at 8.15am today, dr dautey looked at my husband and told us he needed to go to the er. i knew my husband would listen to the doctor. (i said he needed er last night, beside the point.)
off to verdugo hills er we go. parked right outside. we were in triage in 7 minutes of checking in, by 9.30am we were in a room. excellent care, lots of great drugs, plenty of attention given us, of course it's never fast enough when one is in pain. this er was busy. we appreciated the level of care given. 

thank you.

i was in the hospital in january with an emergency hip
replacement. i had an excellent experience on the 8 th floor during my 5 day stay . the staff was completely attentive at all times. i could not have been more impressed with this hospital staff. i highly recommend usc verdugo hospital. along with dr. stephan owens orthopedic physician. very best bedside manners as well as excellent doctor.

excellent service all the way around.  wife went for arthroscopic surgery on knee and it went smoothly.  nurse was attentive which is my #1 criterja.  prior to check out, they made sure she understood how to use crutches.  pleasant experience for an unpleasant experience.

i went to the er for severe pain. when i arrived i waited for 3 hours to see a doctor. when i left i got hit with a $6000 bill. when i look up fair market value for these services, they are around $1000. if you want to wait a long time, be overcharged. this is the hospital to go to. highly suggest avoiding it.

i'm providing an updated version of this review after my complaint was handled very well by the usc verdugo hills patient relations department.

after posting my initial review (which i wrote after several voice mails and calls to that department went unanswered), i received a call back from two different people, one person i'd been in touch with before and also the head of the department, who i'd left a message for. her name is angela. she was extremely kind, responsive and truly listened in a way that would have been great during my actual er visit. it sounded like angela really cares about the hospital and the people who work there, and felt bad that i didn't have a good experience at usc verdugo hills. she assured me that my complaints have been logged and shown to the new head of the er, and was able to amend a portion of my bill so i wasn't responsible for the full amount, both of which are very much appreciated.

even though my visit was bad and i'm still not sure if i would return to this hospital, i would encourage people who have a concern to contact the patient relations department. based on my experience, which is all i can speak to, they do listen and try to make things right. it's unfortunate that i had to deal with them in the first place, but as patients with complaints it's important that we advocate for ourselves so the hospital can hopefully learn from their mistakes. thanks angela!

my father in law had hip surgeryy  because he  broke his hip . he was transferred here  for recovery! worst ever! he git here sunday & today is  wednesday. he had to beg his nurses and drs for a shower. and he finally got one today! unfortunatkey the nurse at the time had a huge attitude.  his breakfast got cold because he had to shower! the air!!! ridiculous! he also  just now got an extra blanket..  he told the nurse he was cold . and the nurse replied "its not cold" like how u know??? these people need to be retrained on how to treat and talk to patients! especially the elderly!

i don't know of any other feeling that could match that which i felt when my doctor looked me in the eyes and said "you have cancer." my life quickly changed direction, to say the least - fortunately i was under the care of dr. rene sotelo, usc urology clinic, who was amazingly empathetic and calming as he explained the surgery procedure using robotics and reassuring me that i would be under his expert care - and i'm here to tell you, i was, he is amazing - i had what was referred to as "major surgery." my recovery has been very fast and little to no pain at all - i feel that dr sotelo saved my life. 

i also want to mention how professional, caring and very attentive everyone at the hospital was, in the entire process of my surgery, pre-surgery, day of the surgery and aftercare. 

in the hospital, recovering from the surgery - in walked catherine pradt and introduced herself as my "care coordinator." now i'm not a religious man, but i like to think of her as a gift from heaven. i was really taken care of - she completely took charge of my needs - presently in the hospital and my home health care needs. i didn't even know she had done that until i got home and received a call stating that a nurse will be arriving shortly to assess and assist me in my home and to make sure my medical needs were met. trust me, my family was very happy.

a few times some concerns came up regarding my recovery, and i would call or text catherine and she would respond straight away putting my fears to rest - she completely understood my recovery process and with clarity explaining and walking me through what my concerns were, establishing the appropriate next step in my "window of recovery." she was very calming and reassuring, so was the nurse, but it was catherine i relied on.  

i would recommend usc verdugo hills hospital, dr. sotelo and catherine to my family, friends and anyone who finds themselves in need of a hospital, expert doctor and a care coordinator.

my husband was scheduled for surgery at 12:30 pm and was told to arrive at 10:30 am.  after 5+ hours he was finally taken to surgery.  excuse for the delay was that one surgery went longer than anticipated and then instruments weren't ready for my husband's surgery.  omg doesn't this hospital have enough instruments?  can this be typical of a keck usc hospital?  i would never recommend this hospital to anyone.

we had an unfortunate incident that necessitated a visit just before  10 pm yesterday.  i was very surprised at how quickly they got us in - 10-15 minutes.  they triaged my husband and had him in a room in no time, receiving treatment.  they gave us medication to take home and we were on our way about an hour, hour and a half after arriving.  the doctor, nurse, insurance lady, er admitting lady, etc., were all super nice, helpful, and totally on their game.   the only thing that was really strange, that neither of  us has ever seen, is they made us pay our er copay right then and there.  i've never seen a hospital, with a well insured  patient, not just mail us a bill.  i mean, what would happen if i didn't have cash, credit cards or whatever, on me at that moment.   overall, it was a very positive experience.

this is without a doubt the best hospital i have ever been to. anytime i've come here the nurses and physicians have gone above and beyond in order to make sure that i'm okay and well taken care of. the compassion and empathy that they portray really shows no matter which provider it is. they even go out of their way to do things that aren't in their job descriptions such as offering snacks or drinks to make the patient more comfortable along with many other things. thank you for everything you guys do here when a person is feeling their lowest.

i fell when i tried to change the battery of my smoke detector. i'm 4'11". i landed on my left hip. i had hip surgery the next morning at huntington hospital. i was coming down with the flu at the same time so i was placed at verdugo hills hospital for rehabilitation post surgery because i needed to be in isolation to protect other patients. i am writing this to commend the dedication, the support, hard work and the love of the staff on the  8th floor. whenever i needed anything they were there for me. dr barry and dr ghandi answered my questions. the pts worked with me. and the nurses and cnas were so devoted to helping me feel  comfortable. and i needed help every couple hours. no one complained. and the place has the best fish tacos! i wish i had chosen to be a nurse. thank you verdugo hills. god bless you.

the emergency room seems very understaffed with doctors. it took over 4 hours for the doctor to finally come see us in our room and we were told there was only one doctor on staff in the er. i only gave this 3 stars because the staff are friendly.

on christmas afternoon my mother suddenly could not see out of one eye. after going to urgent care we were told to go to the er at usc verdugo hills hospital. the staff at verdugo was amazing especially dr tashman. urgent care scared my mother and told she might lose an eye which increased her blood pressure. after some examinations dr tashman assured us it did not appear as such but did suggest she see a specialist the next day for a follow-up. he called her insurance and gave the authorization for an emergency referral (she has hmo) and gave us his number in case there were any issues. due to the holidays she wasn't able to get seen until 2 days later but i as able to follow-up with dr tashman and make sure it was ok. he saved us a trip to usc county on xmas day and i was able to communicate with him until she was seen. even a couple days after he texted to see how she was doing. i was truly amazed on the level of service we received from dr tashman during the holidays. him and his staff work during holidays and the level of service was truly unexpected but truly appreciated. thank you dr. tashman and er staff!

this hospital is wonderful. i was worried with some of the comments but there is no need to be concerned.  the staff's number one goal is to make patients feel cared for and kept comfortable.  the nurses are top of the line and i have had several surgeries in several locations.  catherine, rowena, hazel and nazeli are the best.  they know their field and have great attitudes even when i was in pain and had discomfort from my surgery.  dr. nguyen and dr. eric are very skilled surgeons and excellent care givers.  the parking is free!  the food in the cafe is tasty.  if you have a choice of hospitals for urology surgery, go to verdugo hills usc hospital!

i just had my 5th surgery (3rd stay as inpatient) in four years at usc-vhh, and i can state unequivocally that this is an awesome facility.  it is well run from the moment my doctors' offices or i call to set up a procedure.  i am always treated with dignity, respect, caring and a sense that my well-being truly matters to them.  the facilities are impeccably clean, well staffed and my paperwork is always correct and timely done.  all staff, from intake clerk to surgical intake nurses to or nursing to recovery to floor nurses, therapists, cleaning crew, nutrition employees are unfailingly polite, competent and attentive. post-hospitalization care arranged by julie in ortho nursing is so well done - all i have to do is answer the phone!  billing is a breeze and handled well - my 6-day hospital stay ending 12/22/19 has already been billed and paid in full according to the contract between vhh and my insurance company.  i only have one criticism - which is that the onsite lab required for use by the patient 72 hours prior to surgery for cross-match does not have a contract with my insurer (2nd largest health insurer in usa), and although my deductible and out of pocket maximums have been met, i end up getting billed at a non-negotiated rate because i am required to use this lab.  this needs to be addressed by admin, please - completely unreasonable policy, in my opinion.  other than that one hiccup - everything was absolutely stellar.  michele m.

went to this clinic since it's sunday and i was not feeling good from my ears... i have insurance but since it's a weekend i just thought they charge $35 for the consultation plus what ever they prescribe i will go there instead of waiting for my doctor to have an appointment....they asked me all kinds of medical questions i told her i have gotten all my blood work done already, mammogram within the past 6 months and everything was going just fine.. i knew all i had was an ear infection i thought they would do like all the other clinics i have gone to give me drops and something for an infection... these people are in the business of making money... the young girl there called a doctor by webcam he was on the line for less than a minute he told her what i needed...she explained she was going to give me a couple of shots and a prescription plus they wanted to get blood to see what bacteria i had results would be back in 4 to 5 days( ok in 4-5 days i don't think i would still be ill) when i asked how much was it going to be my $35 went up to $270 dollars... i told her i didn't want the blood work that i have never in any clinic seen them want blood for an ear infection so i asked her just to charge me the consultation i didn't want anything else done to me...she was already upset and said $170 for seeing the doctor.. so i asked he was on the computer for less than a minute why so much? so i told her just charge me the consultation price you said i am not getting anything else from you not even the prescription she said don't pay anything just get out of the clinic she threw me out... no manners what so ever...i have been to dr. wong office he never overcharges me and never runs unnecessary bloodwork or tests...never going back to this place i don't recommend it at all unless you really have no other options... took my friend there for a broken rip she was charged the same as me i understand that she had a broken rib...

who likes going to the hospital? me neither. thankfully, i haven't had to do it much but recently i had appointments with specialists who are located on this campus. it isn't a very large hospital, but i find getting around confusing. there appears to be only one road in, and the signs aren't laid out very well. once you find parking (likely on the highest roof level), you then need to navigate the place. asking for help is a 50/50 proposition... sometimes i just get blank stares or unhelpful responses. but, i now know where i have to go even though it isn't located near the parking. and, usually my visits are so short that parking is only $1 (but they don't take cash early in the morning, so beware).

i was admitted to the er in october of this year. i received the worst care i have ever received at this hospital. i was never assessed by a physician and my main concern of pain in my chest, back and abdomen was never treated or diagnosed. the care i received was minimal  and i was sent home with no diagnosis for my pain and no pain relief. the physician and nurse treated me without compassion or care in regards to my concerns. i was sent home with abnormal labs and a referral to a gi doctor. 

upon seeing the gi physician he explained to me that my labs were abnormal and asked if any tests were run such as an ultrasound or ct scan. i said no nothing had been run. he was also concerned at the lack of attention to detail of my care. 

do not go to this emergency room. head to iu north where you will get proper care and compassion from the staff.

great hospital because they really care and have excellent people working at this hospital.
when joelie went to the er we found out it was a broken hip. the er doctors and nursing staff were on point as to what was happening. from the er we were schedule for hip surgery the following day.
surgery went well, doctor jeffery worth explained everything well and followed up the next day. dr judgar eliacin the internal medicine doctor was really caring and approachable explained everything.  physical therapy came next day and got joelie up and sitting . tomorrow i don't know what else but what i can say thus far the attention to care is outstanding . thank you so much.parking can be an issue at times.

i really expected better from penn medicine, which has given me exceptional care and service in every other specialty.  take my review with a grain of salt:  i came here for six weeks immediately following surgery on my acl and medial meniscus.  i would wager that even the pts themselves would not consider this to be the best facility for this kind of injury; the focus seems to be patients with parkinson's or huntington's.  

i found the equipment and overall space to be antiquated.  no elliptical, no stairmaster, and a single treadmill with insufficient shock absorption.  the staff is constantly juggling multiple patients, precluding one-on-one attention.  i would be given an exercise, and then my pt or her assistant would tend to another patient or go back to her laptop.  my form was rarely corrected, and there seemed to be a disconnect between my pt's approach compared to her assistant's.  appointments lasted about 30 to 45 minutes, and no manual work such as stretching or massage was offered.  this was not unlike my experience at rothman four years ago, when i went for bilateral gluteal tendinitis from running.  unfortunately, this business model has become the norm for physical therapy, but not all places have to be this way. 

if you're young, active, and want to be challenged, i cannot stress how much better zarett rehab and fitness is.  they provide a personalized experience that feels not only like a medical appointment, but like getting personal training in a state-of-the-art facility followed by an expert massage and stretch.  after my first appointment at zarett, i felt refreshed and was more flexible and able to walk with less pain.

then i was wheeled off to recovery where i was offered water and crackers. my ride was able to join me there for the 20 minutes i waited. then i was wheeled out to the car and assisted inside. 

personally, i like effective time management and that's exactly what this place does. i'd much rather be in and out so that i can rest at home than be cooped up n a hospital or similar setting.

review:
this review is only for kaiser's mental health department, specifically dr. jessica bergstrom.

i have ptsd and was assigned to bergstrom because she is apparently a ptsd specialist. at my first appointment with her, she arrived 15 minutes late. therapy is only 50 minutes long, so i ended up having a very short 35 minute appointment due to her lack of professionalism and inability to arrive on time for scheduled appointments. any other doctor would understand that it was their fault that they were late and extend the appointment accordingly, but not bergstrom. she apparently doesn't understand accountability and responsibility.

the appointment itself wasn't great. she's a pretty cold and unfriendly person. she spent quite a bit of time complaining about how she doesn't like kaiser and she wanted to go on strike. i figured i would give her one more chance though, so i scheduled another appointment with her. again, she arrived late, only this time it was by 20 minutes. this time, she was completely offensive, texting someone on her phone and getting angry at me when i asked her to stop. she also seemed to have completely forgotten who i was and what my problems were; she gave me advice to "fix" my ptsd symptoms, even though the particular symptoms she was discussing weren't symptoms i had. when i tried to tell her that, she snapped at me, "do you even want to get better?!" then she ended the appointment. 10 minutes early. so this time, i ended up getting seen for 20 minutes.

i later called and requested a different therapist. i got told that my request would be sent to a manager and someone would call me back within 3 days. no one called. i called again and sent in a change of therapist request once more. again, same spiel but no call. i called again. no call back from the managers. instead, i get a call from bergstrom, asking me why i didn't want to see her anymore and what had she done wrong and can she schedule another appointment with me to find out why i'm switching? i was just completely horrified by how she was acting and also by kaiser, for letting her call me when the manager was supposed to. i can't believe how unprofessionally and immaturely this woman acts! and i can't believe that kaiser doesn't have the sense to let the managing therapist handle therapist switches so that patients can honestly explain what went wrong. the whole thing was a nightmare for me and ended up taking over a month to sort out, when it really only should have taken a few days. i really would not recommend jessica bergstrom to anyone who is looking for therapy at kaiser walnut creek. there are better options out there.

review: i went into the pharmacy this afternoon to pick up a couple of prescriptions that were called in earlier today. while there, i thought i might as well pick up two other prescriptions, which needed to be refilled. i asked the pharmacy tech to share with me my very small list of medications, as i couldn't remember the name of one of the prescriptions; yet he would not. instead, he asked me a series of questions: "who's the doctor? what's it for? is it (name of medicine)?," and i was forced to name my symptoms in public at the cashier ("it's for menopause.") after his failed attempts at determining the name of the medicine, he then referred me to the pharmacist who put me through the exact same routine. i asked the pharmacist for a list of my medications, and he wouldn't provide one either--written or orally. i was quite irritated at this point and told the pharmacist that the pharmacy tech asked me the very same questions. i said, "i feel like i'm being quizzed; i don't like that...i have a right to my healthcare information." however, he maintained the same stance as the tech, explaining that he couldn't give me a print out of my prescriptions because of hipaa (yet somehow it was okay to for me to share aloud my symptoms and diagnosis at the cashier?). i told him i am well aware of hipaa rules, as i'm a psychotherapist and deal with phi in my own job. after he finally called out the name of the medicine i couldn't remember, and i confirmed it, he agreed to fill the medication along with the others. by the way, i have gotten a list of meds before from cvs when i was not a kaiser member; it is not a hipaa violation. it's these kinds of experiences that make me consider changing my health insurance during my next enrollment period at work. kaiser continues to be a disappointment.

review: literally the worst possible mental health coverage you could possibly get. all the therapists are experienced and professional, but are way way way too overworked because kaiser refuses to hire enough therapists. a normal therapist should have like 10-20 clients and according to the therapists at kaiser, they had like 900+ clients which meant there was no way they could possibly devote enough time to make a difference in the life of someone with a legitimate mental illness. i was only able to meet with my therapist once every two weeks even when i was suicidal and severely mentally ill and was needing care at least 1-2 times a week. they refused to provide residential treatment when i was struggling with a rampant mental illness and eating disorder, even though that was undoubtedly what was best for me at the time. overall, if you or your loved one is struggling with a serious mental health issue and not just some situational life issues or mild anxiety, kaiser will not provide you with literally anything helpful. there is no access to intensive care for moracute issuesthe psychiatrists are just barely adequate. they are not pill pushing doctors so that's good, but that's pretty much all they're good at. they do not explain the purpose of the medications they are prescribing beyond a surface level explanation. they also do not listen when a patient says they are not having results with a medication unless the patient is very assertive about it. the teen therapy groups do not teach coping mechanisms or how to change ones thinking process, it's basically just a group session where everyone goes around and says what is hard for them in life at that moment or why they are sad and they are incredibly unproductive

my daughter was a patient on 6 south (surgical)  at oakwood/ beaumont hospital dearborn and i have never run into such a bunch of lazy, could care less nursing staff to the point of endangerment. as an rn myself i know my way around a hospital so i have a very good idea when something is very wrong  when i worked at oakwood back in the day we had double the amount of patients to take care of and we did this with efficiency, being well organized  helping each other, and taking great care of our patients. what i recently witnessed in the nursing care  at oakwood, dearborn, shocked me to my core ie; my daughter put the call light on because her iv bag ran dry and ²the ivac machine was  beeping, we waited and waited for someone to come but no one came, call light on again, no one showed up and 20 minutes pass, i glanced out in the hallway and their were 5 nursing personnel chit chatting and ignoring the call lights. i went up to a nurse aide and she blew me off. for instance with an iv going dry you only have so many minutes to get to the iv before a clot forms in the cannula and renders the iv site useless causing the patient more pain getting poked again for an iv site, there was blood backing up in the iv but no one came to check the beeping iv which is designed to be heard at the other end of the hall. these nurses have only 4  patients to take care of and they refuse to work as a team to help each other out with the attitude " it's not my patient"... this is dangerous, irresponsible, selfish thinking and will inevitably end up hurting a patient. on my way out i complained to the charge nurse mary who blew me off, there were 2 people sitting at the desk who could easily have answered the call light but chose to ignore it, which begs the question; if a patient is in imminent danger either from falling on the floor or develops an emergency of not feeling well and no one shows up to help!
this is a very scary place for a patient to be in and it shows the lack of commitment these nurses and aides have toward their patients which should be, "do no harm" by keeping them safe at all times instead of  an attitude "so what". i would give the level of care a big 0. horrible place!

we agreed to stay at hmc. 
it was the best decision. his care was stellar from the front door and back out the front door. the medical staff was remarkable and everyone we encountered were helpful, friendly and made our stay comfortable. each person went beyond their job description to be welcoming. the emergency room staff was great prompt and kept us informed on time frames. the admitting girl was funny and polite. she was so sweet. when we arrived on the floor our room was spotless. the cleaning team took their time and attention to detail which was so appreciated. the food service team was delightful. they went above to make suggestions for his selections and the quality of food was amazing. the nursing staff out shined any of the staff i worked with in my 32 year practice. our doctors were prompt, through, insightful, intelligent, non rushed and informative. they kept us included and up to speed on every detail of his care.

if i could give this a zero i would. i went in 12/31/19 around 11:30 pm. i had a c section 5 days prior and went on due to severe pain and possible infection. i was on pain meds that were not working. parker has 0 wait time listed on website. got in and waited 30-45 mins to get a "room." the nurse who took us back brought us to the behavior health area due to overflow. but did not tell us until after. our room has writing on the walls! a camera! the bathroom was a stall in the hallway. so the security could hear everything. we had a guy dr and his nurse (whom i will not name) they were awful! 1. the guy doctor should of had an obgyn exam me since i just had surgery. he hurt me soooooo bad i almost jumped off the table and started hysterically crying! they gave me

this hospital is a piece of shit including all the people that work there, they don't give a dam about you when i was being treated there the nurses were all really rude i had even asked for water and the nurse told me that she didn't give a dam if i died this place is the worse if i could give it a negative stars i would ,

it's a mixed bag here. i would generally say the service is either fine, or good -it's significantly better than the boston bi. you will generally get served somewhat quickly, usually without a long wait. if you show up early, it can actually speed up the service. so, if you are busy and just want to leave asap it's on  the quicker end of service. i wouldn't say it was fast tho'. it's just more timely, and the pace has less waiting, boredom , and time wasting. 

i wouldn't say anyone working there was rude or impolite. they check all the boxes as far as being polite to your face, speaking all of the expected choice phrases in order to not be considered rude. but, it feels very mechanical, coached, plastic, fake, hallow, superficial, and empty. they're not rude per se, and they  do and say all of the "correct" or "pc" things, so you can't accuse them of doing a bad  job. but, so much of it lacks warmth, bedside manner, and you don't actually feel cared about. it just isn't there. you can see the smiles, and hear the "customer service" tone of voice. but, it feels more like a drive through service at jiffy lube, and you are the car. you don't feel like a human person, but a thing that needs a checklist of things to be performed and spoken to you, then get out, but "have a nice day". 

i wouldn't say any of the personnel working there were bad or negligent people. but, they definitely do not have any wish to connect with anyone on an actual personal level. they only want it to seem this way on the surface. i noticed that if they were speaking in a manner that was meant to simulate trust building or relationship relatability, if you actually became candid and treated them as a person, and not submissive to dominant power dynamic of professional above the patient, they would often change the subject, give you a very extra big smile, and try to leave and send you on your way immediately, rather than actually forming a bond of personable trust. 

if you are having surgery, like i did here,  remember to address your fears if u have a special circumstance like if most people have a pair of 2 organs but you only have 1, and they removing giant growths from it, but they've already told you that if it bleeds, they must remove it. because they can totally forget. in my case i could've become castrated if they removed my ovary, because i only had 1 left. then i would've been thrust into menopause and my life would've shortened abruptly and thrust into rapid aging. 

this was very concerning  to me. i was having anxiety over this  for months. i also had other complications due to this issue, and the causes were unknown until  after the surgery. 

everything was a success. i'm fine now. 

but, it bothers me a lot that they felt very cold about this. i felt like just another machine on the assembly line, and not a person. the personal discussions i had with the professionals felt more like a puppet show of telling me things i was supposed to hear, to dupe me to believe everything was fine at the push of a button, or just speak  some specific words and everything was good,, then send me on my way like a drive through. 

but, since my circumstances were unique and complex, it shattered the customer service illusion that they cared, and it wasn't real trust or care. it was people going through the hum drum daily life of a career, and the semblance of a number of things on a resumé. 

it's bothered me a number of times. and i assumed i was  just picky, or overly sensitive, or worried i did something wrong. but, after having spoken with a recent recent professional that spoke too me as a person on the phone, actually cared about me, didn't rush me to hang up or leave, and didn't speak to me with cookie-cutter phrases from a scripted coached list of things to say, or boxes to check  off, i realized that the person i was talking to was a real person whom actually cared about the entire process, the care, the person. and they didn't just put all the burden on me, or pass the buck while "have a nice day"-ing me. 
so, i felt it validated my feelings of how i felt about this place. 

it has just been a long time since i'd experienced people being authentic, natural, and caring. i can feel what people feel. it's called empathy, and it's something the brain does. but when people are saying all the right things on a checklist customer service style and fakely smiling at me, it puts me off.  because i can't feel anything.... but i can feel the: 
oh no! she's trying to get to know me, bond with me, and relate! get out! send her on her way! smile and nod, and get out! 

it's not me being overly sensitive or picky, it's that my sensitivity of my empathy in my brain is functioning fine, and i'm actually picking up the mixed messages. hence my mixed feelings. 

i hope this information is at least useful and constructive.

my first time at ecmc i was transferred for severe anxiety symptoms and self harm. the holding unit is terrible enough on its own, i'll get to the longer term ward area soon. staff tries their best to not acknowledge the patients in distress. even when they're screaming and crying and in pain. it was extremely traumatic being left bawling on the floor having the worst panic attack of my life and staff just looked the other way as if i was nothing. i really didn't matter. they told me they would keep me here longer if i didn't calm down, needless to say that made it much much worse and quite literally drove me mad. 

patients regularly fight one another and staff once again do nothing about it. they're completely useless for the field they signed up for. 

a woman around her mid twenties fell into a seizure right in front of me and the staff didn't realize it until the other patients alerted them. patients aren't told anything for hours upon hours and are left there without being properly updated on the process of getting them discharged or into a room. there's only a limited number of beds, which are usually all taken up, and you have no choice but to lay or sit on a cold hard surface. patients regularly piss on the floors in front of others, it's ignored. 
there's a clear pattern here of things being ignored they simply shouldn't be. 

there's no cushions or anything to give you some semblance of comfort except for the limited number of beds. 
they do not care. they really don't seem to have any empathy whatsoever. 

let's get to the ward part..

there was never enough water to drink. i was severely dehydrated to a point they couldn't draw blood from me for days. 

they make you bathe like an animal in showers that only stay on for, no joke, 5 seconds at a time. you have to keep pressing the button every 5 seconds to keep the water going. no counters or toilet in the shower area, so everything you brought in with you got soaked. even your clean clothes and towels. it was just one single small room you got to bathe in. 

one night they completely "forgot" to feed me and i was physically sick from not eating/drinking enough for so long.

you also never saw the same doctor more than once, they sporadically just disappear mid conversation, these "professionals" are never on the same page with each other. one doctor said they were thinking about holding me longer, then she just leaves without saying anything else. literally never saw her again. she left the unit. she caused a huge, unnecessary meltdown for me that night i'll never forget. (don't worry, all that was ignored too!)

there's no group activities, no counselors to talk to, not enough snacks left out at any given time, i had to hoard food in my room to make sure i had enough to make my meds work. 

suffice to say i'm still really traumatized by the whole experience. i still get nightmares and terrible anxiety to this day thinking about it. i've never been treated like such trash in a psych unit in my life. i had been in 8 different psych hospitals back in massachusetts/vermont and even a fraction of what i saw would be enough to shut the whole damn place down. this is not okay. this is immoral and should be illegal to continue to operate. 

if you don't have enough staff or funding to operate this place and give those who are at the lowest point of their lives any sort of compassion or empathy, do buffalo a favor and cease to operate. 

you're doing much more harm than good and should be investigated. 

this is my final warning, do not go here. seek alternative mental health help. anything is better than buffalo ecmc.

i appreciate very much for their saving my mom's life.

currently on our 2nd hour of waiting in the er, my partner with severe upper abdominal pain. i was told they can't give him any pain medication because he isn't in room. he is almost in fetal position because of the pain. many staff members including one doctor just passing us by. no one staff stop to check on him to see if he was ok. i work in the er myself i understand we get busy but to not check on a patient in distress for almost 2 hours. some patients stopped themselves to ask if he was ok. when i tried to ask for help from a female nurse another older male nurse with messy hair interrupted my conversation and said you need to go to the registration window ask for the nurse. still waiting for this nurse that i am supposed to have talk to 38 mins later. my partner is still in the wheelchair l slumped over the arm of the wheelchair in pain and no nurse checking on him. no meds given yet for the pain. i know your supposed to get another set of vitals at least once every hour to make sure nothing changed or worsen. this is unacceptable and i work in a er that has twice the patient flow then this hospital with almost a third of the staff and we never ignore patients in distress.

do not bring family here. my aunt who was dying with stage 4 cancer was in the emergency for 3+ hours without any help because they "couldn't find the bloodwork results" and it was because of the staff's negligence. they took the blood and left the vials on the counter in my aunt's er room for over 3 hours! once i brought this to their attention they profusely apologized and tried to gaslight us into understanding there's a lot of patients in the emergency-- that does not excuse your negligent behavior. we moved her to another hospital.

unfortunately my grandfather was taken to this hospital by ambulance when he had pneumonia. he was under the care of palliative dr. cortez during his recovery with pneumonia. and dr. cortez lacked complete emotional awareness, professionalism, and had terrible bed-side manner.

he gave my grandfather a death sentence which turned out to be a false alarm and caused my family to experience unnecessary emotional turmoil and trauma. this all could have been avoided if he had taken the time to first get the full results of my grandfather's condition instead of making assumptions and condescendingly demanding we hold a conference to have my family decide between hospice and a feeding tube causing my family extreme emotional distress before my grandfather even took the swallow test recommended by the speech therapist.

we spent days grieving and mourning and had to plan a really difficult family dinner to make a decision between hospice and a feeding tube because dr. cortez made it clear that my grandfather wouldn't be swallowing food and his body was preparing for death by his weight even without conclusive results yet from the speech therapist. dr. cortez assumed because of my grandfather's bmi he was dying, although i explained he had swallowed fine prior to coming in for pneumonia and has always been a small petite guy his entire life. dr. cortez did not hear me at all.

my grandfather passed the swallow test and did great. and when dr. cortez came into my grandfather's room the next morning to tell us that my grandfather passed, he said, "he did great, but let's see if he actually eats!" which i felt was extremely cynical and negative. dr. cortez's attitude and lack of empathy causes families to have to endure even more emotional distress and negativity when they are already facing a really traumatic time having a loved one in the hospital.

this was after my grandfather had already eaten two meals at the hospital which dr. cortez could have checked on prior to making his assumption about if my grandfather eats. he then proceeded to say that if my grandfather continues to eat, he does not need hospice care, which he is eating and is doing well at his new nursing home.

this entire ordeal was rather infuriating to have gone through and we felt it could have been completely avoided had dr. cortez taken the time to wait for the results and gotten the proper information or at least had better emotional awareness because these are actual people's lives, family members, not just numbers or diagnosis-- actual people. and especially considering he works in a very sensitive field. just because most cases of palliative care turn out to be end-of-life, doesn't mean each individual patient shouldn't be looked at on a case-by-case basis as a person but with assumptions.

his bed-side manner was also horrible. i was sitting in my grandfather's hospital room while dr. cortez was at the nurses station ranting about another family to the staff. he literally said, "it's unfortunate that family just can't come to terms with reality." it's not appropriate at all to judge how a family or anyone handles a traumatic experience especially one so emotionally sensitive as end-of-life, and i feel it's even less appropriate to be ranting about other patients and families in a space where others can hear you. it's extremely unprofessional and something should be done about this type of unprofessional behavior.

again, please please please don't bring your loved ones here.

 i told her she didnt even bother checking on me and didnt really talk to me at all ( i was crying when i was telling her that..cause i felt neglected). she asked me to go with her in the bathroom and explain everything to me. she was one of the best nurse in that department. i asked her if she can ask her supervisor to check on the schedule the next day to make sure that i will not have that same nurse. they were very kind to change their schedule for me. 

the whole experience was good, but that one nurse reslly ruined everything for me. i hope nobody gets treated again the way that nurse (rowena) treated me.

if ever i get pregnant again. i will never go back here since it was really nightmare especially during my postpartum recovery.

review:
outstandingly great hospital. my wife, my youngest son, and i have been here many times for various services. we have never had a problem in numerous visits for sleep studies, outpatient surgery, emergency room visits, lab work, and so much more. every medical provider we've met with has been compassionate, great listening skills, and quick to handle each reason we've been here. and to make this even better, this hospital is less than 15 minutes from my house in the mountains above woodland park.
i won't go into all the reasons we've been here, but each and every time has been an excellent experience. even in the emergency room. fast, efficient, great service, including from the doctors on call. i will relate that my wife has had two different types of overnight sleep studies here, and both times, the sleep room was comfortable (i stayed in the room with her on a fully reclining recliner the first time!) and the sleep study technician was very personable and enjoyable to talk to. even though she did not have to, she even made sure i was comfortable the first night i stayed overnight with my wife during her study.
for anyone who wants to question my experience here, just look on yelp as to how many times we've checked in here... i've lost count! and i only check in on yelp about half of the times i'm here!

we have been struggling with our son getting sick multiple times a month for the last three years! we have been to numerous doctors, urgent cares and hospitals during that time. we have seen dr. muhm twice now and i'm convinced that he is the best doctor out there. he actually listens to what you are saying and tries to get to the bottom of the issue. most just give you an antibiotic and send you on your way but with dr. muhm i actually received a specialists phone call the same day as our appointment with him. he is extremely knowledgeable and has a conversation with you about all of your options. i highly recommend him and he will be our primary care doctor for both of my children without a doubt.

i have been to the hospital on several occasions and i cannot say enough about this hospital! 

the first time we went to the er, my child had swallowed a button cell battery. i immediately called poison control, and they patched me through to the battery ingestion center (yes, it's real.) after giving them my sons information, battery type, and the closest hospital. they instructed me to get there asap. i was literally 8 minutes away at this time. when i arrived, the doctors already had a plan in place for my child, x-ray technicians waiting, and the had alerted the helicopter that we might need them. this all within the 8 minute drive! luckily, my son had a good prognosis, and none of that was needed, but i am impressed by their urgency.

f i could give zero stars i would. last monday, 2/15/20 my brother was admitted to the hospital after suffering a stroke. he was admitted to the neuro icu sunday and was cared for by nurse albert during the day & another nurse at night. they were amazing & they went above and beyond to make sure my brother was comfortable & treated him with compassion & were very supportive of the family. monday morning, it was decided that there was nothing else medically that could be done to get my brother well. the family decided to place him in hospice. we were told while making this decision that all of my family could visit my brother anytime of the day & night. we selected a hospice company, who the hospital staff recommended. they told us they had a contract with cima hospice. a person by the name of mary castelan from cima came to do the intake paper work. i met her in the hallway & i specifically asked of her that when she was ready to come look for me so we could begin the paperwork. whats the first thing she does, she goes into the waiting room and begins asking my family members medical questions about my brother in front of other people and other family members of other patients. very unprofessional. my family told her that that was not the place and time and needed to leave. while doing the paper work, she was nothing that i expected from a person who works for hospice. very chatty, seemed like she was not very knowledgeable on some things and simply the process with her seemed like it took forever. finally, paperwork was done and they assigned my brother a room on the 4th floor. my family is a very large family and very united. so my family went upstairs and i rode the elevator with my brother. when we got to the 4th floor, they put my brother in his room and right away a nurse with glasses came out of the room right away and asked where the son was. she didn't even greet anyone and came off as very rude and seemed she had a big ego because she was a nurse. while we were waiting for them to finish with my brother, a large and tall security guard walks up and tells us that we needed to get out of the hallway because "the nurses didn't want us upstairs." he asked us to go to the waiting rooms. again, he said the "nurses didn't want us there." we were up there because we knew the end for my brother was near and we were trying to be with my brother. 10 to 15 minutes after my brother was transferred upstairs, he passed away. there was no nurse in the room or anyone from the hospital. one of my family members asked if a nurse could check to see if my brother had a pulse. it took like 10 minutes before the nurse came in to the room. she came in and didn't say much and walked out. by this time we know my brother was gone. this nurse showed no compassion. all she asked my nephew was if my brother was an organ donor, which he wasn't. while waiting to see what would happen next, there was a patient in the same area where my brother was at yelling for a nurse. there were several nurses walking by and they would laugh and comment to each other "she's call you" and the other nurse would laugh and answer "no, she is calling you." very unprofessional. they didn't even bother to check on the patient who was yelling for a nurse. they held my brothers body for 15 hours after passing & they didn't release him until after i called administration. they never contacted the funeral home either. i spoke to parker mcdonald and waiting for a reply as to why the funeral home wasn't contacted and all the other issues. no autopsy was needed. the most horrible experience & the laughing of a patient calling a nurse was very disrespectful & not treating them with dignity & respect. these nurses have families & i hope their love ones don't go thru the same thing my family was made to go thru or treated & laughed at their love one like they did with someone else's love one. please don't ask me to contact you all, i already contacted administration. disappointed & disgusted with the behavior and quality of service from the 4th floor nurses in 1440's room

i went in for a tv (transvaginal) ultrasound and was very nervous about the procedure, as i did not know what to expect. 

the preparation for the exam included me drinking 32 oz of water and holding it. the technician,  karrie, was sooo empathetic. she quickly scanned my pelvis and allowed me to void.  (whew!) she went on to explain the tv procedure. she was very professional and engaging and made the entire procedure non-stessful and informative.

kudos to this ultrasound technician with an excellent bedside manner! she's absolutely phenomenal and should be cloned!

i had a procedure in ambulatory surgery yesterday. let me say that  i would definitely go back to south suburban again. the facility was very clean! they checked my name, birthdate and procedure information with every health care person i encountered. sheba and the other nurses were very professional and reassuring. the anesthesiologist and doctor were awesome. they explained everything thoroughly. i was very pleased with my care!

i recently had to come here to the er.  patrick and marnee were the nurses that assisted us, they were both very nice and professional.  they made sure to provide their names.  two different doctors came in and don't remember their names were nice too, but doctor name on the board and ones that came in were different.  no biggie, very professional, explaining everything, and helpful.  

this is the place to come if you need to visit er.  

my only compliant.  came on a sunday morning was in er for 4 hours and had to pay to park.   the er parking spots are never open.  i come here regularly and never see open er spots.

diabetes patient went to the hospital and was treated fairly poorly; wasn't given diabetics snacks and then almost given insulin while having low blood sugar; given medical gear that didn't fit at all. grace and a few other staff members were great; but overall i'd pick st david's south, even though it's farther from work.  parking is about $3 a visit.

i spent about 20 hours here. got my appendix out on monday. i adored almost everyone i came into contact with. i had alicia as my nurse almost the whole time. she was great; attentive, quick, responsive. loved having her.
as far as i can tell, everyone involved in my surgery was wonderful. i met them all briefly before being put to sleep, and then never saw them again. but i woke up alive and couldn't remember a thing, so apparently my surgeon and anesthesiologists did their jobs. 
i did wish the surgeon had talked to me after my surgery. he talked to my husband, but i didn't get to see him or ask any questions once it was over.
the nurse i had at check out was...a bit incompetent. i loved literally everyone else i interacted with, at least a dozen people in the two hospitals and the 20 hours i spent there. 
but, my evening nurse was a mess. she didn't know how to use the equipment that gave me my medication. she was tapping all over the machine and eventually called in another nurse for help. together they still couldn't figure out how to get both bags going at once, so i only got the antibiotics, not the saline as well before checking out. she let a ton of air into the line, and told my husband it didn't matter, even though alicia had made sure to clear the line of any bubbles. she didn't know how to turn off the beeping, she didn't seem to know how to do anything. as we were checking out she didn't have any of the discharge care instructions printed. we asked for them, she couldn't figure out how to print them out, so eventually she just wrote a bunch of notes. it was all important stuff, like how much i am allowed to lift and how long before i can get into water! she would have just sent us home without it if we hadn't noticed it was missing and insisted on getting it. it was just sad. the rest of the visit was great, but she was the last person we interacted with and it was just frustrating.

took my mom here a month ahí because she had chest pain. she was left overnight in observation. waiting times for everything was excessive. her dinner never arrived so i had to buy it from the cafeteria. there were only 2 nurses to look after 5+ patients, these women are stretched too thin.

i went in for pre-op, was seen by initial associate and she said some someone would be with me shortly. i waited 45 minutes more, i peeped out the window heard assistance laughing, i walked over to the break room, and asked if i was done? the young gentleman came and said let me check yes you're done. i said did you forget me? he didn't say anything, but it was obvious he did. no apology nothing. i had to ask which way was the exit. 
disappointed.

leaving 1 star because i can't leave 0. 

i've been incorrectly billed 5 times in amounts 3-times higher than my payment arrangement. they say they cannot issue a refund as long as i have a balance on the account even though i've continued to make manual payments as well. 

this is the worst customer service i've ever experienced and it's just shady business practices.

i suggest looking into other healthcare providers in the austin area.

i visited the maternal fetal medicine clinic and was disturbed by the uncleanliness and overcrowding in the waiting room. chairs needed to be wiped down, there was a sick patient wearing a mask but was accompanied by three children and another adult. the waiting room is very small. the sick patient was not taken to another area. people were giving up seats to other arriving patients or waiting outside the clinic in the hall. also, several patients were taken  ahead of me even though they arrived very late for their appointments. we waited for nearly an hour to be called to the back. very unorganized and poorly managed. i was happy with the demeanor of the ultrasound tech who took care of us and the two minutes we spent with the doctor, she seemed nice.  the room we were taken to have the ultrasound was crammed with three chairs between the wall and patient bed. a third person definitely wouldn't be able to actually sit in the chair provided.
what's worse i woke up the following morning to a sore throat which progressed over the next couple of days into nasal congestion and a nasty cough that keeps me up at night.

if i could give the er at seton medical center a minus 1,000 review, i would.  i am celebrating 5 years of life after they almost killed me with a misdiagnosis of a ruptured appendix and sent me back to my hotel telling me that i had food poisoning.  after being in agony for 3 more days at my hotel, i went to the er at st. davids, was properly diagnosed, and was told that i could have died.  as a result of seton's gross incompetence, i developed massive infections, required major surgery, and spent an agonizing 3 weeks as an in-patient at st. davids. thank you seton medical er for costing me tens of thousands of dollars in medical bills after insurance, causing me a year of agonizing recovery which prevented me from working (losing a year of income), and leaving me with a life-changing chronic bowel condition that will never go away.  your incompetent staff almost killed me. your er should be shut down.

had surgery here because they were in network with my health insurance. it was the worst experience from start to finish. i was sedated for an hour and a half of additional time because some of their equipment broke during surgery/ they didn't have the proper tools the dr needed. due to the late finish i was admitted overnight ( was suppose to be out patient) where the bad experience continued. the staff didn't seem to know what they were doing and weren't helpful. they didn't give me food with meds that indicated "must be taken with food" so i became sick to my stomach. this was only some of what went on while i was there, but i will spare you all the details. it was a battle to get out of there even after my surgeon released me. this process took it took several more hours for no reason and resulted with me insisting to leave immediately. my recovery would have been much better if i simply just went home. i will never return to any seton facility again

wonderful hospital. came alone for surgery to treat my appendicitis which was a little nerve wracking since this was my first major operation ever. however, all the nurses and doctors were extremely friendly and welcoming. they quickly put my mind at ease, patiently answering all of my questions. my surgery was scheduled for noon but they were able to squeeze me in an hour early which meant i got to leave the hospital earlier than expected later that afternoon. overall, excellent quality of care.
fac_name: The Hospital At Westlake Medical Center

review: best hospital i have been in. everyone in this facility is efficient and friendly. they are so caring.  i will tell all my friends about this great hospital.
fac_name: The Hospital At Westlake Medical Center

review: today i attended a neurology apmnt. with my great nephew. it's been a long while since i've stepped foot in the hospital let alone experience all the up dates! magnificent job on the remodeling! as far as services and patient care. this is my first time n a while i hope it's a positive experience.

i came this hospital for er on thus night!
all er stuff are so nice and very friendly ,unfortunately i had to have surgery and stayed 6 days

at hospital room, all nurses are so nice and very knowledgeable,

i'm so happy i choose o'conners hospital,
