thank you for great service

oh my god, out of all the staff we've come across during my dying grandpa's stay here, there were only like 3 that were compassionate and actually doing their job right. one the worst doctors was dr. saha who was very cold hearted and rude. and there were 2 nurses whose names i didn't get but they would push her way through between my family members, not even acknowledging our presence as we just witnessed my grandpa die! the nerve of those b's! this low review is for the 3 of them. the rest of the staff provided 5 star care.

i had given birth to my daughter here via c-section in april of last year. i had the best staff/nurses care for me. many of them were traveling nurses though. they were attentive and made sure i was comfortable during my labor despite being in pain from contractions. also, at the time, they were transitioning into santa clara valley medical system. so, timing worked out perfectly for me because i had medi-cal at the time and i did not want to give birth to my daughter at valley medical hospital. yes, everything seemed out of date, but the hospitality my bf and i received in labor & delivery was amazing. i enjoyed my 5 day stay because it wasn't crowded or busy in comparison to kaiser's labor & delivery. idk how things will be here in the future due to their transition, but i would deliver my next baby here again.

i gave birth to my son here in 2013. all my needs were taken care of and i always felt like i was in good hands. my son was a healthy 22in 8lb baby and i couldn't be more grateful to this hospital for delivering him

even a star is a waste for this facility called hospital. 
they do what they do for themselves as a job. doctors, rns, therapists, and clinical staffs are all useless and helpless. please be a hospital for the patients not for yourselves or the bill. we are not the figures that you tests or source of your financial aids.

don't waste on your time and budget for posting those replies. 

do one round of visiting current patients will do a lot of those discussions that you want to do. if you really want to hear. don't pretend this facility is care for the people.

i had great experience delivering my baby here.  all the staff were nice and friendly.  most importantly they were helpful and attentive.  i wanted to thank hawa and huong for an outstanding job in taking care of me during my 5 days stay.  i have nothing bad to say about the staff other than receiving excellent service.

place is horrible. only guy actually helped me with advice that i was seeking for. i don't have any insurance or medical but simply for advise and no one helped me but one guy at the desk. i was ask for personal information & no treatment of any sort was occurred whatsoever for my situation, but kudos to him. this hospital is just sad, even bascom does a better job.

if i could give zero stars i would yesterday i took my daughter to the nearest hospital which was o'conner for an open head wound and when i got there the emergency room was empty no people what so ever they check her vitals weight they send us back out to wait again to get called while my daughters head is bleeding my 2 year old she was falling asleep they said it was fine will after an hour waiting the room was already full of patients they were getting seen before us another hour passed my daughter kept bleeding so we kept asking what's taking so long and they told " we take in people in fashionable order" what does that even well we ended up just leaving because they didnt seem to care we went regional medical hospital where the room was beyond packed no seats to sit but we got seen within 20 min i advise you not to take your child to o'conner hospital please if its urgent go somewhere else there staff was betond rude and careless

20 year-old student with asthma, severe chest pain and difficulty breathing made to wait in waiting room for three hours and told the earliest she would be seen would be three more hours. forced to seek treatment elsewhere at 4am. sad state of affairs when this is the medical care in this country. good luck if you have to go to this hospital.

i got admitted after been in the er for like two hours. in the time i spend in the er i got x-rays from my lungs an electrocardiogram to check my heart they took several samples of my blood also i was send to have an ultrasound done for both of my legs to check for blood clot. i really want to thank every single person in the er because they were all real nice patient and caring with me. once i got a room upstairs my whole experience during the two days i stayed was awesome no complaints all the nurses i saw were super nice and helpful. the food they provided me was unbelievable good the people from the kitchen also very nice everyone i talked to. overall the only complain i have has nothing to do with the hospital but with the roommate i got. omg i mean she was 93 years old and basically all she wanted and all she was there for was pain killers lol and she wasnt shy about it i had to put up with several tantrums she had screams whining arguments etc. at the same time it kept me entertained so there's that. back to the main reason i'm here all i can say it's that  o'connor hospital rocks and my whole experience there was awesome. i want to say thank you every single one there. next time i'm sick hopefully not soon i won't hesitate going back there again. i also have recommended to my whole family and friends to give it a try. thanks again you guys are all super stars. ‍‍
i came here to visit a friend in hospice.  i was so impressed with this hospital i moved from southern california to work here.

my grandmother spent 11/28-11/29 at o'connor hospital and what a disappointment it was. besides the obvious of the hospital being old and dirty the care she received from the nursing staff was not a positive experience. the nurses that admitted her to the 4th floor were good that night, as she was being wheeled into her room from the er the smell of marijuana smacked me across the face from before the time she even entered her room. (it smelled like her roommates were wiz khalifa and snoop dogg) the roommate had so many visitors they were sitting on the floor, took the chairs from our side, and were using the restrooms constantly that is intended for the patients use only. those evening nurses did eventually move my grandmother to another room after we expressed our concerns. the rest of the nurses seemed to be disinterested in patient care and more robotic focused on the computer more than the patient. thankfully my grandmother was discharged the following day and when she asked the nurse for her discharge paperwork the nurse responded coldly, "i will get to it later. there are sicker patients that i am taking care of." unfortunately, this is the hospital that my grandmother comes to as all her doctors are from och, but i pray that she will not have to have another hospital stay here again. there were many other issues that came up in her overnight stay, i would hope that even though o'connor is now a county hospital it would retain some of the compassion and patient-centered care that it had in the past.

had a really scary experience with an inattentive nurse named dominique on the med surg floor. on tuesday february 11th around shift change at 7pm, i was in room 641 recovering from an appendectomy procedure. i was in the restroom when my incision site began bleeding in excess. i hit the call light and sat for ten minutes waiting for my night nurse to come into the room, as my day nurse bryan had been dealing with a critical situation in another room. i was bleeding all over my gown and onto the floor, and my mother in law went into the hall to find my nurse, dominique. dominique told my mother in law that she hadn't read my chart yet and that i would have to wait. my mother in law was able to track down bryan, my day nurse, and he went into action right away. two surgical residents were in my room and they began working to stop the bleeding. they bandaged me up, and the residents said they would be back to check on me within two hours. during no time did dominique check on me or take my vitals signs. my husband happens to be a nurse, and because he was so worried for my well being he took my vitals every 15 minutes to make sure i was stable. around 9:15pm, i was 2 hours past due for pain medication and dominique was nowhere to be found. i hit the call light and the patient care technician came in to assist me with my bedpan and i asked if i could please have some tylenol as i hadn't received anything for pain for over 2 hours. while waiting for dominique to finally do her job, my mother (also a nurse) caught wind of what was happening and phoned the nursing desk. she was placed on hold for 7 minutes and never spoke with the charge nurse as she had requested. dominique finally appeared in my room with tylenol and berated my husband for "calling the front desk." her exact words were "sir, i understand that she's bleeding but there is no need to call the desk on me!" luckily my bleeding stopped on it's own, because i would have hated to become a critical situation in the care of this disinterested and negligent nurse. 

ascension, you have a very dangerous employee working for you. i am shocked and appalled by how horrible i was treated by this nurse. nothing about her is caring or safe; she does not deserve to be employed by such a reputable health institution. i hope you will do the right thing and end her employment with ascension. my mother, mother-in-law, my husband, and myself plan to take this up with the higher ups at the hospital. i hope you will do the right thing and reprimand this employee. 


if dominique is your nurse, request another one! she is dangerous!

i should have looked at the ratings here for this hospital before i chose to have my surgery there. the ratings are low and for good reason. uncaring staff and lazy for the most part. patient care was terrible, ignoring calls; be prepared to take care of yourself or bring a caregiver with you. patients can be heard down the halls screaming in pain and yelling for help, it was horrifying. some doctors are aware of the conditions and get on the staff and their patients get better treatment hence the few good reviews. some doctors even recommend you hire a nurse to stay with your loved one if you can afford it. 
staff lied to my insurance company about my care and services that never happened. i will be contacting my insurance company.

the instructor, tim, was awesome. i really regret not taking him for other courses because his class was very informative and he is really knowledgeable about all the aha's protocols and algorithms (and he hilarious to boot). i am a nursing student that is about to graduate and i wanted to get as much certifications out of my way prior to applying for jobs. i took the pals course with tim, and, honestly, i learned so much more in the couple of hours with him than i did with my other certification classes. he was able to explain the pals information in a quick, efficient, and understandable way. tim is a working paramedic so he has a lot of stories to tell to related to the algorithms in pals which, for me, makes it more easier to understand. tim really cares about the success of his students so he'll recommend free online certification that will further make you appealing when you apply to hospitals such as nihss or fema. i loved the way tim so much that i also took his ecg/pharmacology course and, now, i feel so much more comfortable with ecg strips. thank you very much, tim!! i will definitely be coming back for more certs!
highly recommedagntqzqnded, easy quick and fast! spread the word! awsome place to go to!
as a doctor or chiropractic, i'm pretty bored with cpr training. these guys were very funny, and so knowledgeable. i will definitely be back. they have to keep it a little more cleaner though.

this was the worst ever experience that i've had in a cpr class, or any class at that. first off, i want to start by saying that the the two young ladies working here are amazing and put up with a lot, the real problem was the main male instructor tim. when you go to a class you are there to learn and be corrected in a professional and positive manner, but not here!!! tim decided to combine both the als and bls classes, which at first i didn't mind because they needed the extra help for there scenario and more knowledge is great. however, he began to treat all of us in bls as if we were in the als class and when we didn't do as he said, due to confusion of lack of knowledge, in a matter of seconds, then he would stop to ridicule us. his exact words were that we were "mediocre and careless." i understood his perspective, since he says that he deals with real life situations in which deficient knowledge can be harmful, like in a health care setting, but there is a manner in which correcting someone is done that doesn't lower their self-esteem and confidence. the entire emergency scenario he was insulting either people individually or the entire group, he even went as far as to insult his own staff while all of us were in the same room. oh and he continuously preached about having confidence and how it was critical in a health care setting, which i agree with, but how are we supposed to build confidence with instructors like him that focus there class around what we were doing wrong and insult every chance they get, rather than on how we could improve ourselves. now, what was even more disturbing was his sexist remark that he made when were practicing cpr. he said that men should be doing the compressions because "they are built differently" and that women should be comforting the scared parents because they are more sensitive/compassionate. like i am not making this up!! he literally said that to me and my friend!!!!! i honestly can go on and on....but i can't waste more of my time on this guy. all i am going to say is please, just avoid this guy and his class if you want to avoid his negativity and ridicule, believe me, saving no amount of money could convince me to ever return here. i would rather pay the $65 dollars at the other cpr classes available and enjoy my experience. by the way, i literally made a yelp today just so that i could share my experience, reason being that i've never felt the need to before, so i did this merely as a friendly warning!!!

2 hour long wait. extremely rude and unhelpful front desk staff. woman with medium length brunette hair, bangs, and glasses is the prominent reason for this one star review. drive the extra few minutes if you can and see any other  urgent care in the area.

after taking antibiotics for what i thought was a uti, my symptoms just weren't going away. i couldn't sleep through the night, so i took myself the er in the middle of the night. my husband is deployed, so this was the first time i had to go to the er alone. let me tell you, that's scary. i brought a blanket, and a phone charger and i walked in, tears in my eyes. i had read the reviews before coming, since i'm brand new to the area and i was nervous. but i'm glad i came anyway, everyone was sooooo nice i felt so taken care of. the nurse at the front desk got me checked in quickly and brought me to my room. the nurses checked in on me frequently until the doctor came in. it was around midnight on a wednesday night, and it wasn't too busy. turns out i had a kidney stone! worst pain of my life, but the staff did a great job of making me comfortable. every single person i talked to that night made me feel less alone, and for that i am so so grateful.

if you care about the wellness of yourself and your loved ones, i'd advise that you stay clear of this hospital. i've had two relatives who needed to be transferred out of this hospital because we saw that they were not being given proper care. one of the many instances of neglect was not giving my father in law (who is both a diabetic and transplant patient) his antibiotics on three different occasions. when questioning the staff, i'm forced to hear a run around of answers.

after a week, he looked worse in the care of those at alameda hospital than he did prior to being taken there.

i, myself, had to be transferred to alta bates because of the amount of neglect i experienced after a gallbladder surgery (which included significant internal bleeding caused by mistakes made by the surgeon). because of their mistakes, i had to spend an additional week and a half in the hospital.

i plead with you.

if you care for your loved ones, do not bring them here.

boy has this place gone downhill. i'm sitting in the parking lot waiting for a family member to be seen in the er. it's been hours and no action. there were only two people in the waiting room when this started.  there has only been another few coming and going since.

there is now a security guard just inside the entry door who won't allow anyone to sit on one side of the room away from those who are coughing, etc.  he said it's because it is for check in. there was no one checking in! 

in the meantime, the receptionist was advising my family member what treatment would be needed, despite the fact no actual medical provider had seen or spoken with her yet.  

when she finally got into a freezing room, she had to don the gown and wait for an hour and counting.  she finally had to get dressed again to get warm.  

she has a previously diagnosed kidney stone-a huge one, and brought the imaging documents along to prevent the need for more costly tests or god forbid, another round of unnecessary x-rays.  this thing has kicked up with pain and bleeding. she just needs some symptom relief.  instead of processing her quickly, she's been put on ice (almost literally, due to the cold room and flimsy gown).

what has happened to caring in the medical field, and specifically, in this emergency room? 

shame on those front-line folks and administrators who have forgotten about people in favor of process.

i went to the er over the summer. the care was adequate. however, i am still dealing with the billing. i tried to get them to send the bill to my insurance. the hospital bill went in ok. when i got the doctor's bill, i sent it back with my insurance information. they never billed my insurance, and a couple of months later sent a "final notice". i took the notice to my insurance, but they couldn't pay from that, as it wasn't the actual bill. when my insurance called the medical group's payment processor, the medical group had my birthdate wrong, and would not release information to my insurance. today i got a call from a collection agency.

i will never go back because of their fraudulent billing practices.

my then 4 year old son was being treated for scoliosis by dr. michael glotzbecker at boston children's hospital - orthopedics.   due to my sons age and nature of his curve the md ordered a mri to rule out certain neurological conditions (chiari 1 malformation, tethered spine, etc) and said the procedure was i would be contacted if an abnormality was detected.  one full year later (after glotzbecker left for cleveland oh) my son's new physician reviewed his file and found that nobody had ever reviewed the mri and my son in fact did have a chiari 1 malformation causing a syrinx in his spine.   this should have been communicated immediately a year before and addressed surgically.  dr. glotzbecker's negligence and the failure of boston children's hospital to have proper procedures to ensure proper review and action was taken endangered my son's health and will have an unknown impact on the future outcome of his scoliosis.  i can not recommend dr. michael glotzbecker in any way as he was responsible and his failure is in my opinion negligent, and boston children's hospital also failed because they had an "unknown open loop" in their system... aka failure to ensure the mri was reviewed.   we went to boston children's hospital because they promote themselves as the top juvenile orthopedics hospital in america.  unfortunately in my experience they are simply living off their own self promotion not providing world class care.   they have also failed to take actual accountability for the issue and are treating it like an "oops" and imply that i should be thankful it wasn't worse.  tremendously disappointing.

do not go to this hospital unless you're unconscious and can't make the decision on your own.  they are completely incompetent.  they didn't even ask my daughter if she was allergic to any medication, and wrote on her chart that she has no known allergies.  she is deathly allergic to a particular medication.  she waited for 4 hours and never saw a doctor.  if you care about you or your loved one's well-being, stay away from tmh.

review: if i could rate the mental health facility less than one star, i would. i attended ediop there twice and the only positive part of the experience was the friends i made, even though we were banned from outside contact with other patients. before starting the program, you have to prove you can complete a meal in 30 minutes. when i failed at this twice, i was sent back to outpatient and told to come back when i could do it. i'm still not sure how that was supposed to help, since obviously this actually meant i needed more support, not kaiser's one appointment a month outpatient philosophy. once i entered ediop, i found out that the entire system is devoid of any compassion. if you are a minute or two late, you're kicked out for the day. if you leave any food on your plate, you're kicked out for the day, if you finish after the meal timer goes off, you're kicked out for the day. i once finished 30 seconds after the timer and was still forced to leave. my anxiety over finishing meals became so bad that i began involuntarily gagging while eating multiple times. each time, i was told to step out of the room, stop panicking, and just eat. when i got it under control, i wouldn't have enough time to finish and i'd be kicked out for the day. i was driving 2 hours to get to this program, if i had been physically capable of finishing that meal, i would have. i drove that 2 hours home sobbing every day after being told i just wasn't trying hard enough and that i was being difficult. after nearly 2 months of this, i was told i needed to leave for residential treatment because they couldn't help me. my only other option was just going back to outpatient again. i went to residential at an out-of-network facility, and i'm so glad i did. the gagging never came back after i left ediop. i later found out that the residential program nearly sent me to the hospital the first week i was there since i was in such bad shape after leaving ediop. ediop told me residential was only necessary because they couldn't deal with the gagging issue and i would have been fine otherwise. i hadn't even had bloodwork done the entire time i was there, despite my weight rapidly declining. i was forced to return several months later after i relapsed due to lack of aftercare, and i could go on and on about my terrible experiences there. the staff is rude, the program flawed, and kaiser has no clue what it's doing when it comes to mental health. i am so thankful i no longer have to deal with them, and i firmly believe my new insurance has played a huge part in the fact that i am now firmly in recovery from anorexia. i still have friends with eating disorders dealing with kaiser, and it makes me so mad that they refuse to change despite proof that their outdated model doesn't work. seriously, if you are able, pay out of pocket for one of the other iops in the bay area. many offer scholarships or financial aid and all are very much aware of the kaiser horror stories. their incompetence is very well known.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Walnut Creek Medical Center

this review is part of my cousin needing to heal from the emotional and mental abuse she suffered at the hands of staff at riveredge hospital in forest park in the late 80's.  i am speaking on her behalf.

my cousin had some teenage depression.  she was admitted to riveredge as a teen.  no drugs, no drinking issues.  depression. 

my cousin told my aunt and uncle some things that were going on at this facility.  when the staff found out from my aunt and uncle whom were upset with what they found out was going on in that unit,  they said to my cousin "who do you think people are going to believe?  us or you.  look where you are."  the staff in a group session  then allowed another teen to berate my cousin in retaliation for my cousin complaining to her parents about some transgressions that transpired with this other teen on that unit/floor. 

when the staff could not find any diagnosis other than mild depression for my cousin that was a teenager at the time, they told her she suffered from, "narcistic personality disorder."  years later my cousin was told by a psychologist that as a  teenager any teen can be, " narcistic," in nature.  riveredge needed something to hold my cousin with for insurance purposes longer term.  something to diagnose her with for insurance purposes. 

it was common knowledge amongst the teenage patients that the only way anyone was, "cured,"  and released was either to lie and agree with what the staff members told them they were feeling or if the parent's insurance ran out.  the kids called it, "playing the therapy game." agree with the therapists on staff at riveredge or you will not be deemed to be making progress and released.   many kids knew they were stuck at this private hospital for great lengths of time due to mom or dad having great health coverage.

today,  despite being at riveredge hospital for a month, my cousin is a thriving individual.  she is a productive member of society that is happy and healthy in mind, body and spirit.  that is despite her stay at riveredge hospital as a teen for mild depression. 

 occasionally she still has  nightmares about her experience at riveredge hospital in forest park.  

i told my cousin i would write a review even though this  transpired in the mid-late 80's.   i did this for her as part of her healing process.  i am happy as her cousin and as her friend to do so.

please seek therapy elsewhere for your teen, child or for yourself.

i can see from more recent reviews of riveredge in forest park that it is still a pretty lousy place to experience therapy.

my mother was admitted from desert springs hospital after having suffered a stroke, a broken hip, pneumonia, a uti and a gi bleed that required 21 units of blood and a 13 day stay in the icu. she lives in vegas with her husband while i live in boston. i have been trying to help my step father navigate her care from boston and it's been trying to say the least! after roughly, 2-3 wks at kindred- she developed rectal pain... (she suffered a rectal ulceration/bleed in the icu) and required 21 units of blood over a 5 day period. so- yes- when she develops 9/10 pain, she should be "evaluated" by a doctor. instead, the doctor took her history, and prescribed percocet. well- he never examined my mother. instead- prescribed a narcotic that would likely constipate her more, and perhaps cause another rectal bleed! when i asked the nurse why it was prescribed? she replied "for her rectal pain?" when i asked her what the diagnosis of her rectal pain was? she replied with "idk". i demanded someone actually evaluate her that same day- her response? "this is a snf you know?!" (it's actually not a snf) but my thoughts were "and that means what exactly....???"   
when i asked the rn (charge rn) how i could get my mother evaluated by a doctor same day? she advised us to call 911!!! ok?! well? i think that's a horrible way to practice medicine but i don't make the rules!!! so? we called 911- and she was transferred back to desert springs hospital. while there- she was evaluated and diagnosed with referred pain from her broken hip and another uti. when it was time to discharge her from the hospital and send her back to kindred- tried to send her back to kindred, kindred refused!!! they lied!! said she signed out ama! what?!?!?! i've been a nurse for 22 years and i am well aware of what's required to "sign out ama"... i have to spend 10 minutes explaining what that means to you as a patient, you have to agree, then sign a document. this never happened with my mother. instead, bc i was a pesky daughter with medical knowledge- the nursing staff "hospital dumped" my mom on to desert springs. i was enraged and filed a report with the complaint department at kindred- i was reassured that this type of behavior is not tolerated and that i would be called by corporate within 24 hours. that never happened. i've since reached out to the ceo and still no reply. apparently, abusing, neglecting, and abandoning the elderly is what kindred stands for!!  when we were discharged from the first hospital- we had a list of rehabs to choose from. they all look the same on paper- having said that? stay away from this neglectful institution. the nursing staff could care less and administration cares less than them!! i will be filing a report with the bbb about the treatment from this facility! 

and please see the owners response to me in private bf he didn't want to reply for the public to see. deplorable!

my father went to kindred after a week in desert springs for treatment of a foot infection. he died there on tuesday morning, january 28. the issue with kindred that i will discuss here has to do with what happened after his death.

or does it?

the afternoon he died, i received a call from someone at kindred, a woman whose name i didn't get, who told me that they had found a shaver in cleaning his room. i said i'd come by to get it the next day if that was all right. she said yes, it would be left on the cart the nurses used (it has everything from a computer to gloves and the like) in the hallway where his room had been.

the next day i went by and went up to the nurse, who i did not recognize (the nurses do not always work only the same hallway, which is not the point here anyway) and explained that my father had been in that hallway and they had left a razor (i should have said shaver) on her cart. she checked a couple of places on it and said it wasn't there, and said i should check at the nurses' station. i went there and said what had happened. they asked who had called. i said i didn't know. they looked around and couldn't find it.

the nurse practitioner walked by. i thought i'd ask her, and did. she asked who had called. i said i didn't know. she asked if it was a man or a woman. i said a woman. she said that narrowed it down. she sent someone to check in a nearby room, where, i guess, they put laundry and that sort of thing. the person came back to say they hadn't found anything. she then thought maybe the social worker could help and i headed for her office.

she came out and offered condolences on my father's death. i thanked her and told her someone had called me the day before that they had found a shaver, it would be on the nurse's cart, it wasn't there, and we were looking for it. she said, "who called you?" i said, "i don't know." she said, "was it a man or a woman?" i said a woman. she said that narrowed it down and then said, "i need to look into this for a few minutes, so can you wait?"

i'd had it. i said, no, i could not wait, i had funeral arrangements to attend to, that they had the address, they could send it if they found it,  that i found this whole thing offensive, and i left.

over the next few days, i called back the number that had called me a couple of times and got no answer. on saturday, someone answered that number. i told her what had happened and she said the number probably belonged to a social worker, though she wasn't sure she was in her office at that moment, and she would transfer me. she did so. i got a voicemail and left a message. ten days later, i have not heard back.

the shaver was not important (it had no sentimental value, although it was my backup, and i'd brought it in for my father to use--but did they know that? of course not). nor is it the issue here. the issue is how kindred handled this situation and dealt with me, including not even having the courtesy to call me back after i left a message, or to apologize.

does this mean i question kindred's medical care for my father? well, what would you do? would you have faith in kindred as a hospital when its staff, many of whom i found to be quite nice when my father was there, cannot even do something like this right? all i can suggest is that if someone suggests kindred hospital to you, run the other way. your life may depend on it.

by chance this year the doctor's ekg had an "blip", nothing crazy, but his primary doc decided to let a cardiologist look at the doctor. the cardiologist scheduled a nuclear stress test on valentine's day and immediately checked him into the hospital based on his stress test.  so instead of eating chocolate cake and drinking champagne we were in the hospital.

on feb. 25, 2020, the doctor went in for a triple bypass at evanston hospital. there was 100% blockage in two areas and 90% in another area. there was absolutely no indication that there was anything wrong as he didn't exhibit any of the common symptoms (fatigue, shortness of breath, chest/jaw/arm pain, water retention, etc.).

the procedure went smoothly with no complications. he had an amazing surgeon who rocked that procedure. his surgeon was very pleased with the process and said he could see an immediate improvement in brian's heart function. he was in icu for 24 hours, then in a private room and they had him up and moving right away once the tubes came out.

fast forward to today. he is home and doing well. to look at him, you would never know that he had major surgery this past tuesday. he still has a long way to go in healing, but he looks great. i was concerned about a possible personality change as i have read papers about that...hell look at bill clinton. but the doctor is still the guy that went in before getting cut :-) 

i am giving major props to this hospital.  from the time we checked into the emergency room to the day of the surgical procedure, the staff was amazing!  customer service skills were off the chart!  the nurses, pas, housekeeping, food service, transporters, the staff where the angiogram was done, the people working in the cafeteria, etc. were all so nice.  i am saying for the record this was not a fluke,  the doctor was initally in the hospital from 2/14 to 2/20 as they were trying to figure out the best course of action for him, then 2/25 to 2/29 for the surgery.  i was at the hospital every day from early morning to late at night to be with the doctor.  everyone was friendly and seemed to genuinely care...great bedside manners, even the intern chaplin.  i had no idea that hospital chaplins did internships!  during the surgery, a nurse called me every two hours to update me on the doctor's progress.  at one point i was on a conference call on my work phone and missed a call from the nurse on my personal phone.  she called the receptionist at the desk in the waiting area and had them look for me so i could get the update from the desk phone,

i wanted to be there with the doctor every day and had no problem getting him ice water when needed it, but the nurses were constantly telling me to call them for that as they would take care of it, even if i needed water.  i just felt like i was capable of getting that for my lil man to free them up for more medical stuff.

i hope none of you ever need heart surgery, but if you do, ask for hyde russell for your surgeon.  he was amazing, but most important, he was very personable.  when he talked to us prior to the procedure, he was reassuring and comforting.  after the procedure, he came out to tell me how it went and it honestly felt like he was happy the doctor did so well.  his delivery of the news felt like he was happy how things went, not that he was this great surgeon who played god and save my husband.  he stopped by every day that we were there to check on the doctor's progress and to give us time to ask questions.  he didn't look at his watch, he didn't rush us because we loooove to talk things through (that is the engineer in him and chemist in me).

and i hope none of my yelp folks in the chicago-land area never need to go to the hospital, but if you do, this is the place to go.

i brought my husband to this care station on december 26, 2019 because he was having flu like symptoms. we arrived at the care station at 1:30pm and was called in at 2:30pm. we were finally seen by a doctor around 3:15pm-3:30pm and he then proceeded to swab my husbands nose to get it tested for the flu. the dr. stated that we would have the results the following day because they needed to send the tube over to labcorp. i thought it was weird that they couldn't give the results right away being it's an urgent care but i left it alone and waited for the results. the very next day my husband wasn't feeling better so i called the care station at 10:14am to see if the results came in early and the 1st person that i spoke to stated that the dr. that saw my husband was in another location for the day and she would send him a message asking him to call us with the results. so we wait for 3 hours and i decided to call back again at 1:23pm and i speak to a 2nd person and she states the very same thing but what she did that the 1st person didn't do was state that she would have another dr. that's working in that office today call us with the results. she places the notice in his chart and apologizes. now we wait 3 more hours and 50 minutes, which makes it 5:13pm and i speak to a 3rd person and then she states his results are not in yet so you have to wait until the dr. calls. now i'm pissed because the last 2 people i spoke to stated that they couldn't give me the results and it has to come from the dr. which indicates to me that the test results are in not that they aren't in and a dr. has to give the results out and not them! she then process to tell me that this care station isn't an urgent care but a primary care provider and that the dr. would call us again. now lets remember what their website states "at care station medical group, our linden, nj walk in clinic is available to 7 days a week to treat your urgent care needs. we offer onsite labs, x-ray and ultrasound to quickly diagnose and treat you quickly so that you can get back to your busy life." regardless if this care station is a primary care provider or an urgent care the inconsistency that i got from 3 of the different people that i spoke too was not expectable! oh and to make matters worse today is december 28, 2019 and we still haven't received a phone call from any person at this care station giving us any results or at least calling us to state "i'm sorry the lab is probably backed up today which is why we haven't gotten the results yet or i'm sorry i know you called a few times today but i'll see what i can do for you on my end" etc. my husband is feeling worse by the minute and now i have to take him to a real facility that will actually provide him with the proper care and results that this facility stated that it would. since i was a teenage i've gone to this care station for several different reasons and the care has always been okay up until now! the flu is a serious virus that can kill people and i thought bringing my husband here would have benefited him but instead it did the complete opposite! i'm sad to say but if your looking for fast results and the proper care and treatment do not go to this facility!! you'll be wasting your time, money and effort! i truly hope someone here at this care station will read this review and never allow this to happen to another patient that is ill and in need of the proper care that you advertise. 

god bless

going to the er here resulted in a bill of $1,500 and a misdiagnosis. i went to the er here with a painful toe injury. after a wait of nearly 3 hours, they did an x-ray and a nurse practitioner told me the bone was not broken. i was given instructions about caring for a "contussion." two hours after i was discharged and was back in my room icing my black-and-blue toe, i got a call from the np saying that the radiologist had finally gotten around to looking at the x-ray and  my toe was broken! incompetent and very slow care!

i had a horrible experience giving birth here. it was my third child and i pretty much had no choice; i had to be induced in this hospital. everything was perfectly fine  until i got out in a room. it was so hot and i guess the ac was out because there was only a room fan in the room. strange but it wasn't a big deal. then i look over and i'm sharing a room with another woman; i still did not make it a big deal. after i give birth, i got put into my room. i didn't feel anything at the beginning, but later on i guess my bladder was really full and i was in so much pain, literally crying. i asked the nurse if she can  please get me a bed pan because i was in severe pain i couldn't even get  up and she rudely said "i can't be doing that you need to get up and go use the bathroom yourself" i was in utter shock and disbelief. i was literally begging this woman to help me, my insurance was paying and that's the response i get? later on this really nice nurse came in and she was godsend. incredibly nice and  patient and understanding. i don't remember her name but i think she worked at pacific alliance hospital. she is an example  of how all nurses should be! i will never ever come back here.

one star is generous.  i've been to this emergency room more times than i'd like.  when it first opened up it was great.  the quality of care, speed in which they got you out and it was well staffed.  now i feel like it's the adult version of going to the nurses office.  they give you a juice box and some crackers and send you back to class.  my most recent experience was with my mother.  she got there with my father around 11:30am.  they took her in, did the limited number of tests they  can do there.  then she sat  in a room for hours after that.  no one offered her even a cracker.  she's diabetic and they didn't even have the medicine she needed and i had to bring  her medication from home to her because she was there so long she needed to take her night time doses.  my parents were  told she was being as admitted but that there were no beds so she had to wait.  my father had been there all day and had a chair with a wooden bottom and back to sit in, in six hours you would think someone might offer him a better place to sit.  they had one md on and my parents saw that person for 5-10 mins.  the prices they charge and you can't even get the care you need.  what frustrates me the most  is when i got there i could hear them discussing my parents, what they looked like and my mom's medical information out in the open.  i also could hear what was going on in other rooms and hear them discussing other people's medical information.  what happened to privacy laws?!  it's funny how after i made a call to patient relations that a bed suddenly came available.  i'm very disappointed with this facility and with yale in general.  i think that they have grown too big and their standards of care have fallen significantly.  sadly around here you don't have any other options in an emergency but yale because they own everything.  do better!

review:
i would never expect five-star service from a government agency! (dmv anyone?)  so, i was blown away by the service i received from this clinic.  remember they're closed from 1130 am to 1 pm. i showed up precisely at 1 pm, and the doors opened promptly.   

you pay 50$ upfront for the consultation (insurance does not cover that).  within 15-20 minutes of arrival, my consultation began, and that included the time to fill out the paperwork. khanh gave me an excellent consultation; she broke down every city i was visiting in the philippines and told me every virus or outbreak that was currently happening in the region.

we went over the preventative measures i should take in each area.  khanh answered all of my questions. i ended up getting a polio booster shot and an oral medicine for malaria. they recently got insurance to start covering the vaccines themselves, although it does depend on your insurance what is included.  luckily they were able to pull up my vaccine record, and i had a lot more than i expected.

overall it was a quick, efficient experience, and i will be back when i go on my next adventure!

review: great clinic! i wasn't sure what to expect, and thought it was great. almost no wait time (got there on a weekday, 10 am). people were very friendly and very helpful. the pharmacist spent a long time going over all the possible info about the country i am traveling to, explaining everything, from recommended vaccines to eating street food and avoiding bug bites. got all my shots and much more!

review: i have been here many a times. it is a small hospital, and i feel well taken care of when i come. i have been to the er for myself and family members at least 10 times in the past  5 years and the staff is always friendly and always right there to help, even in the middle of the night. i had my appendix removed here and the doctors were great. i had my son here 2 years ago and we were the only ones there having a baby those few days. 4/5 nurses that were there for us were awesome. i give it 4 stars because i am not a big fan of how close the sick patients are to the new babies. the only thing separating the two wards is a nurses station.

you may ask, why one star rating?  

the good:  

1.  the staff is very friendly and attentive with great attitudes.  they really try to provide good customer and family service.  

2.  small facility-73 beds

3.  the facility is clean with no gross  or "old people"  smells of urine or feces.  

4.  aesthetically, the facility looks well maintained.

5.  issues brought to the attention of staff are immediately addressed; except for the middle of the night, unauthorized room charge (read below).  

the bad:

1.   this is a kaiser-contracted facility and as such it appears to have very little oversight once the patient is transferred.  

2.  this is a for-profit facility and it is clear by the available equipment and amenities that making money is the bottom line.

3. below standard rating in health inspection (2 out of 5 stars) is accurate.  this primarily has to do with quality of care.  specifically, shoreline has a lower percentage of short-stay residents who improved their ability to move around on their own compared (59.5%) to averages for california (67.5%) and nationally (67.5%).  the higher the % the better.

another rating that his bothersome is the percentage of short-stay residents who were re-hospitalized after a nursing home admission (30.1%) versus california (21.1%) and national average (21.1%).  lower percentages are better.

4.  it's been 24 hours since admission and we (the family) has not been contacted to schedule a meeting to develop an appropriate treatment plan.

5.  the discharge and treatments plans have not been followed.  

6.  it's very noisy because most rooms have 3 patients in a very small room.

7. my loved one was moved from a 2 patient per room to a 3 patient per room without our knowledge or consent in the middle of the night.  clearly, a medicare violation.  issue still not resolved.

if you or a loved one is admitted to a nursing home or rehabilitation facility, make sure you familiarize yourself with the following information about your rights:

https://www.medicare.gov/pubs/pdf/02174-nursing-home-other-long-term-services.pdf#page32

and

https://downloads.cms.gov/medicare/your_resident_rights_and_protections_section.pdf

also, make sure you look up the rating and violations report for the facility you are considering.  at www.medicare.gov.

shoreline's report is located at:

https://www.medicare.gov/pubs/pdf/02174-nursing-home-other-long-term-services.pdf#page32

also, if you have complaints find the ombudsman for nursing facilities at:  

https://www.medicare.gov/pubs/pdf/02174-nursing-home-other-long-term-services.pdf#page32

lastly, if you are like me and are a part of the "sandwich generation" (caregiver for both your parents and your children at the same time) it will be important to file for family leave to protect your right to care for a loved one without fear of losing your job.  
here's more information about fmla:

https://www.dol.gov/whd/fmla/

knowledge is power!!

given what we have experienced in just 24hours i really believe this facility is a mismatch for thetype of facility and the level of care needed for my loved one.  i will be strongly advocating (demanding) for her immediate transfer.  


update:  i was notified by the licensing agency the kaiser physician and his case manager were terminated!  that's the best thing that can happen to shoreline!

i've been going to mayo clinic since 2008.  i've had 6 surgeries and numerous tests for several different health issues.  i am rating this for my most recent surgery and after surgery care. i went in for a very lengthy and very serious surgery in september of 2019.  let's just say that i was released within 2 days which i was pretty surprised about but happy as i have spent 3 weeks after a previous surgery there a few years ago due to complications that they created.  i could go on and on about the different hospital stays and the bad experiences that i have had but i'll get to my most recent experience.  while in the hospital, a student nurse (from an outside school) was left alone with me, she took my temperature and forgot to put the safety plastic over the thermometer.. yep!  it was too late once she placed it in my mouth, i asked her and she freaked out!  my main complaint is the fact that i was discharged with little to no instruction on how to handle/care for my surgical wound.  i am now 5 months post-surgery and still the wound which has not healed!  i am now going to another facility to handle my wound care as i have to get my life back!  i cannot afford to keep traveling back and forth and keep paying them my copay for them to say "it's healing, be patient".... definitely not worth all of the hype!

my 92-year old grandfather was admitted directly from st.jude er due to insurance reasons on 12/30/19. it is definitely not one of the nicer hospitals. but i do think the staff here does an amazing job, the nurses in particular. he initially got admitted to dou in the middle of the night, during which grace (almost positive that was her name) was the admitting nurse. i was not present but i was on the phone with her during the entire intake process since my parents speak minimal english. i could clearly tell she was incredibly patient and caring, thoroughly explaining every level of dnr and expressing her concern for blood in his urine seen in the foley bag. she ensured that his pain was controlled from the foley insertion (which was immense), not treating him like a drug seeking patient. 

the next day he was transferred to med-surg 3rd floor, stella (daytime) as his nurse for the next 2 days. she likewise provided exceptional service, tending to all his/our needs in a very prompt manner. she consistently went above and beyond, not hesitating to call physicians and inpatient pharmacy to obtain orders, inquire about starting his new chemo meds, verifying home meds, etc. 

the last nurse i encountered was chona up until his discharge (1/4). i did not have too much interaction with her but according to my sister, she was also very kind to make sure that he was able to be discharged home with enough supplies before home health nurse can visit. 

shift manager (unfortunately don't remember her name) was also diligent in consulting case management when we expressed our concern for discharging without having a follow-up with a urologist and oncologist, given he newly had a foley catheter and a nephrostomy tube, although the doctors were basically telling him to just follow up with the primary doctor to get referred to a urologist. i knew for a fact that it often takes months to  see a specialist through primary md referral. case management did an amazing job of securing an appointment with an oncologist, urologist, and even home health within a day. thanks to them we were able to take him home, knowing he will have adequate follow up with the doctors and professional care for his foley and nephrostomy tube dressing changes at home. 

we were less impressed by the physicians but everyone else sort of made up for it. maybe it's because i'm an inpatient pharmacist and knew to demand the right things to the right people, but they really did deliver. and even though i deal with nurses everyday, being on the other side as  patient's family, i realized so much respect and gratitude for all the nurses who genuinely care for their patients.

i don't think i would have recovered or had this miraculous conclusion without the dedicated staff at this hospital. at every step of the way, they were professional, caring and extremely kind. every staff member i came in contact with made me feel like they really cared,  they were concerned, and went out of their way to reassure me and be extremely kind. all were of course incredibly professional. if i could give 15 stars i would. this was a terrifying event, i was made so much more comfortable by the true concerned  and caring staff. i will be forever grateful for everyone involved, and that i had the great good fortune to be at this facility.

i got hit by a car in december 2018. i have spent the last year and a half going to doctors and hospitals and health care centers and physical therapists and sports medicine clinics and dentists and oral surgeons and orthopedic surgeons, a recuperative care center, a church and even a crisis house. and right now, i am at grossmont hospital in la mesa, california, where on march 2nd, 2020 i underwent total knee replacement surgery. now don't get me wrong, i trust and appreciate my surgeon, dr. michael sirota. i trusted him enough to let him cut me open and put in a fake knee while i was unconscious and helpless. i trust and respect his staff, especially rose martin, who went above and beyond to make sure i kept my surgery date. but from the moment of my joint replacement class through intake and waking up in recovery, i have received the best care i've ever gotten, physical, mental and spiritual. and i mean by everybody i've come into contact with, phlebotomists, nursing assistants, the social worker, intake folks, my surgeon's assistant, the meal hostess, the nursing students, the chaplain, the physical therapists... every single one has been as though they were snapped up out of the best, funniest, most soulful, helpful and charming medical comedy/drama film ever made. now, i have to be brutally honest, i have been on some strong pain medicine, but nothing that has significantly altered my cognitive ability. unfortunately, it has caused me to forget some of the names of a few of the remarkably compassionate, funny, kind, competent medical professionals i have ever had the privilege to be cared for by. but it has truly been the nurses and nursing assistants who have saved me here. over the last nearly 4 years, i have lost the love of my life, two close friends, a cousin i grew up with and my dear little dog. i came here angry and tearful and hopeless. i actually expected to wake up from surgery missing a leg. so, here goes. the nurses...lizzy, young, funny, immensely caring. she stayed over after shift change when she'd been up for the whole night shift taking care of me, because i was scared and in pain. she stayed past her work day (night) until she was sure i was ok. mikell who was so compassionate and thoughtful that he made my bed into a cozy cocoon so i could sleep comfortably even though my leg was excruciatingly painful. loretta, who liked to pretend she was just a no nonsense health care worker, but helped me bathe and go to the bathroom and learn to safely get in and out of bed when i could barely move without pain and never once made me feel embarrassed or desperately dependent. martha, whose quiet, peaceful competence made me feel safe and as cared for as when i was a child...and my childhood through my adolescence and adulthood was plagued by illness and injury. and dina, a straight forward, no nonsense nurse who ended up not only caring for my physical well-being, but gave me the straight forward life advice i have needed to hear since i lost my husband and my relationship with my daughter and my  mind and my life on an extremely heartbreaking mother's day. and my last night nurse, mark, who anticipated my pain and my fear and my boredom and my anxiety and put me at such ease that i actually want to adopt him, except that he already has a great mom in the phillipines. there was virginia, who i barely remember because of the heavy pain meds and anxiety, but who i know took excellent care of me. and finally elizabeth, the nurse's assistant who didn't laugh at me when i asked who all my other caregivers had been while i was crying with sheer gratitude over the  incredible staff at grossmont hospital in la mesa, california. if i have missed someone, i am sincerely sorry, it is only because of the pain medication. so, there it is then. nuff said. kate  okay, it's been just 22 hours since i first posted this review. there are five more grossmont care givers i need to mention. 3 from the very beginning of my stay that i've only now remembered and two from the very end of my stay, whom i had not yet met when i first reviewed grossmont hospital. first, the lovely and extremely informative astrid, who hosted the total joint replacement class before the surgery. she answered all of my many questions regarding my knee replacement surgery and post-op care. she actually came to my hospital room before i was discharged to answer even more concerns i had post-op about how best to heal and get the healthy diet i need to heal quickly and properly. technically, her job was already completed even before i was admitted. thank you, astrid, for coming in to check on me when you simply heard through the grapevine that i had some questions about discharge and my post-op journey.

i've been seen by three mds and two nurse practitioners.the three mds frustrated me. the reason i wanted a single primary-care provider (with others at the practice filling in when necessary, such as on short notice) was that i take medication prescribed by several doctors for various conditions. specialists are not necessarily familiar with medications outside their expertise and don't usually even inquire or jnform about probable drug/drug interactions. primary-care providers do.

or they should anyway. otherwise i would have gone to a walk-in clinic.

the three mds i saw were uninterested in medication management. not even lab results from blood drawn at honorhealth moved them, despite ongoing elevated blood glucose while fasting and the well-known hyperglycemic and glucose-intolerance effects of one of my prescriptions, for example.

an absolute horror show, travesty of medical care, and a lawsuit waiting to happen. 

my mom fell this week (fragile, dementia, history of stroke, and a hip replacement). i called 911 and on scene the paramedics asked which hospital we preferred- i chose mercy general as her pcp and records are all at dignity health. 

worst decision ever. 
how the hospital is run: 
a doctor saw my mom for a total of 1 minute at arrival and 30 seconds at exit. no supervision or accountability. lots of people here seemed "checked out" working in an untenable environment. 

medical assistants and one rn is on duty, one pa or doctor for what seemed to be 50 or more patients. there are lots of guys in green outfits doing, apparently, nothing that i noticed for the five hours we were there. my mom was parked on a gurney for the whole time in a busy hallway. people, patients, staff, gurneys, paramedics, security guards, and random people coming and going nonstop. 

she had imaging of her hip, elbow, and arm. there were good people doing the imaging. i repeated that her head hurt- mom chimed in- and then that was related to the doctor and a ct was ordered. too bad the doctor refused to talk to the patient and just felt  her bones for minute and didn't ask one question to her "patient" aka just a number.  props to the imaging team for maintaining a system and compassion for patients in a totally chaotic situation. 

she was offered a tylenol and glass of water. no updates on what was happening...i assumed a room would be provided eventually.  other patients parked in hallway, including a man and his wife- he begged to have someone help her use the restroom- for an hour. 

at about 8:30 pm the medical assistant popped by and said no broken bones, mom had to get up and prove she could walk before being released. i stepped in when mom got upright on the gurney and said she felt dizzy. 

medical assistant said she would have a chair behind mom as she walks. my dad was helping. honest to god, this was the plan. my mom fell, said she's dizzy, and they want her to walk in a busy hallway with people crashing around pell-mell. 

i spoke up loudly, said you need to get an orderly and she said, this is how we do it do you have a better suggestion? 

this could have been solved by having my mom move to a room- (literally across the hall an empty room with three hospital beds) for a safe environment for a trial run. 

we worked with situation at hand with me guarding the hall like a pit bull behind mom and blocking people and gurneys from coming through....and dad ready to catch mom. and then medical assistant tells mom to get back to 
the gurney after a successful trial run. mom has lymphedema and her swollen legs would be hitting metal. i said no get a wheelchair. then a guy in green shows up. apparently ready to catch mom if she falls. thanks, perfect timing. 

so, end of story- doctor comes by for 30 seconds to tell us no broken bones and runs off, totally masked  to protect herself from coronavirus. brava. medical assistant turned out to be a nice person and she stood by us while my dad got car. she was smart and empathetic once she was freed from caring for 50 people simultaneously with no tangible support. 

literally the worst er i have ever been in. train wreck, third world care. danger. no info. a few decent people trying to do their best in a disaster scene. never again. they should close their doors if they can't serve patients and provide a baseline of medical care. our east sac family has been born cared for. and died at mercy for three generations. sadly, switching care to sutter asap. 

every person who walks out of these doors should get a t-shirt that says, "i survived mercy er."

suggestion: hire some nuns to get this place shipshape. someone needs to be slapping a ruler.

review: horrible emergency room help! took a friend in need into this hospital pre approved by his insurance. got absolutely no help! never again! i left getting the flu and already had a flu shot! they had no masks in emergency room at all had to ask for one. was like well people steal the masks so you have to ask? really? where's the security that all hospitals should have in a emergency room anyways! horrible about there hipa laws as well no lines painted no signs! i'd like to see this facility closed just due to non compliance with such laws!

i had my daughter a month ago at this facility and loved it, minus a few not so nice nurses. the hospital is overall gorgeous and the inside is very nice. i was in labor a total of 36 hours and over that time had a couple complications which resulted in a c-section. the anesthesiologist doing my epidural poked me four different times and then during my contractions i kept feeling them and i felt like no one was believing me. they kept having to come in to give me a bolus about four times because i could feel everything in my right side. before my c-section another anesthesiologist came in to talk to me about the spinal block  and he told me that the epidural wasn't working correctly because he did a test and i could feel my whole right side. the doctor who did my c-section was very nice but the main person who i cannot thank enough was my nurse albert( i think that was his name). i was extremely nervous about having a c-section and he did everything he could to make me feel comfortable. after my husband and family had to leave the room to get me ready he came over and gave me this little thing that stuck to my robe with lavender essential oil. during my c-section he had my husbands phone snapping pictures and i love looking back at them. he made all of my worries go away and made the birth of my daughter very special. when i got to the postpartum room he also came and visited us before he left his shift. 

also if you have a night nurse named lauren i am sorry she is very sarcastic and not very comforting during a very vulnerable time.

review:
the architecture is striking relative to the drab office buildings surrounding it.
even from afar while driving in the freeway when i glance at this hospital building, it is impressive.

the interior is open and still quite new.
i have only been there a couple of times for urgent care.
the urgent care area can be dark but the outpatient pharmacy next door is bright in contrast.

the staff is helpful.

the cafeteria is all windows so it is an open feel as well.
much better than the "basement" feel of kaiser zion hospital.
the food still is subpar though.

nevertheless there is plenty of seating outside to distract oneself from the boring hospital food. alternatively there are walking paths around the campus.

if you do not want to try out the cafeteria while waiting for your loved on in the hospital, the surrounding area has eateries.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Diego Medical Center

review:
it makes all the difference if you have a good nurse. 

joanne - er nurse today 1/1 /2020 5 stars

my husband has been to er's 3 times in the last 6 weeks. 1 surgery, 3 ultrasounds, 1 mri, 1 endoscopy, 1 ct scan, two hospital stays 3 days or more. believe me when i tell you, we know a good nurse from a nurse who's phoning it in. joanne is a great nurse.

what makes for a good nurse? actually caring for a patient as a person. being gentle when putting in an iv. thinking about what will make the patient comfortable and alleviate anxiety. cleanliness. good communication. asking good questions and listening to the answer. following through as promised. 

it doesn't matter how many years you've been a nurse because we've had some who are very seasoned and some in training. it comes from something within, a genuine empathy and kindness. i don't think you can teach it, you either have it or you don't. joanne has it. 

also a very special shout out to our er doctor today, dr elizabeth owen. she is one of those rare gems who tries to figure out what is actually wrong with you. not just mask the pain with painkillers. she is genuinely trying to solve the mystery of my husband's pain and help him heal. she spent more time with us today taking about possible causes and remedies than the surgeon who had done the procedure and any of the rounds doctors on our hospital stays. i truly appreciate a doctor who is hell bent on figuring out a puzzle.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Diego Medical Center

review:
i'm a medical profession and this was one of the worst er and bedside manner experiences i've ever had. 
i just switched my insurance to kaiser and came to the er with severe food poisoning at about 1 am. there was no one in the er waiting room yet it took an hour and a half to get me into a room.
every time i've come to the er at a uc facility i dont wait more than 20 minutes to get into a room with other people in the waiting room as well.

 after i get into the room it was again over an hour later before a nurse came in to take my vitals and put me on fluids and anti nausea, mind you the nurse shoved the needle into my arm while i was vomiting because she couldn't wait an extra 20 seconds for me to finish heaving.

 after that it was another hour before a doctor finally came in (about 4 am now). the doctor didnt want to give me pain meds before the blood work came back on the off chance i was pregnant (even though i explained to her there was no chance i was pregnant). after she asked me some questions and left the room, no one came in to check on me/give pain meds or follow up until 7 am when a nurse rolled me out because they wanted to take an ultrasound. 
the doctor came in an hour and a half after the ultrasound was done and proceeds to repeatedly accusatorily say, "well you still haven't given us a urine sample so we're not sure exactly what it could be." 
literally no one ever asked me to give one (no one even came back to check on me once during the night) and i asked her if there were urine sample jars in the bathroom i missed, she checked and said "oh there's none in here," then proceeds to find one for me. 
i told her its probably just food poisoning anyways, she tried to push for a cat scan and other tests which i refused because i was feeling better.
get the bill, (and i have kaiser insurance). $2000 dollars to be given fluids and sit in a room with no one to check up on me all night. 

thanks kaiser, this is the reason why people avoid coming to the doctor's.
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente San Diego Medical Center

review:
hard to overstate the level of bullshit you have to put up with at kaiser. without extreme self advocacy you will get nowhere. there was no better metaphor for my experience here than when one of the nurses checking people in was counting money in the cash register for five minutes instead of checking in people in the line for urgent care. 

situation a
i injure my achilles in winter 2017 and via my employer, i change insurance to kaiser to start 2018. i set an appointment for my achilles and am told i will have to see a general doctor who can write a recommendation to see another doc for an ultrasound/mri/etc. doc 1 sends me to doc 2. doc 2 misdiagnoses the achilles injury via ultrasound and recommends physical therapy. two doctor visits and one month have passed and i have received no treatment, now on my way to doc 3. i do physical therapy for three months (would later find out this was all done on a partially torn achilles) not surprisingly, ankle makes no progress. probably tore it worse in pt. five months down, i've made no progress and finally doc 4 prescribes an mri. now i have a correctly diagnosed interstitial tear and can begin actually recovering in a walking boot. over one year after the initial injury and i am nowhere near returning to running.

situation b
i have an ear infection. doc at urgent care correctly prescribes flouroquinolone drops, but does not insert a wick to get the antibiotic past the swelling down to the ear drum. two days later the ear drum is more painful and nearly completely swollen shut. i come back into urgent care and the check in nurse tries to shove a thermometer in the ear i just told her was infected. finally sit down with the doc, and without warning he shoves the wick straw into my swollen shut ear--worst pain i've felt since getting stung by a stingray. 

situation c
i get back from travelling abroad and go to urgent care for bad flu symptoms. doc gives me a flu swab (much more painful than it sounds). i sit in the waiting room for one hour waiting for the results. tired of waiting and feeling like hell i go knock on the door, nurse says the lab has not sent results back. they contact the lab, lab has forgotten to send results. 20 minutes later doc says results are negative and recommends sleep and fluids. meanwhile, my friend on the trip has the same symptoms, and random local doctor in the san juan islands correctly diagnoses travelers diarrhea and azithromycin. friend is fine in 24 hours. two days of feeling like hell later, i return to urgent care to request azithromycin.

to all those insured with kaiser, good luck and godspeed.
