well , 9 mos after the incident with my mother at santa cruz hospital , a very good friend was brought to the emergency dept. . his experience was much  like the june event. the staff and md's in the ed are a disgrace. little to no communication between staff and patient no warm blankets for my friend who had the chills, long wait time to see the md even though only 3 other rooms were occupied, the ct tech was having trouble with the machine while talking on her personal phone about her dogs and what shouldd be cooked for dinner that  night. it was rude, unprofessional and gave the patient high anxiety.  he was admitted after not seeing a hospitalist, or a gastroenterologist. needless to say, after many hours there , he walked out , after signing his ama release form.  this hospital gets a negative 3 stars  again . never ever will i , or members of my family and friends , pass through those hospital doors.

brought my 5 year old son here last week not because he was experiencing cold symptoms but because he had also started wheezing when breathing and also vomiting. he had no fever but the wheezing concerned me because he has never had any issues with breathing or any asthma related issues. 
all the staff that helped were wonderful and friendly. 
they gave him some breathing treatments which really helped with the wheezing. they also did chest x-rays and tested for flu and strep. tests came back negative and x-rays looked fine. doctor said his lungs were reacting to something, possible allergy or asthma related, so he prescribed an asthma pump and a couple medications for nausea and his chest. 
came in at 3am, left around 7:30am. 

now almost a week later, my son woke up at 3:30am with a 104 fever that wouldn't go down. brought him in at 7:30am, was brought in immediately which was surprising to me because usually they make us wait a bit. doctor originally was going to just test again for flu because my boyfriend recently tested positive for it, and give him a bunch of fluids because his heart rate was out the roof. they also did some blood work. while we were waiting for results, he started screaming, crying, and clutching his stomach. this went on for 30 minutes before they were able to give him motrin which helped with the pain and fever. at this point i believe his temp was 102, heart rate still above 150. he also started vomiting a lot. now this concerned the doctor more also because his blood work showed his white blood cell count was 24 and normally should be 8-10. she said that was showing that his body is trying to fight something off so something was wrong. because he was clutching the  right side of his stomach, they thought it was possibly his appendix so he went off for an ultrasound. they couldn't see his appendix because his bladder was full and he did not want to pee so the result was that the doctor thought he might've had appendicitis and we were transferred to hartford hospital because it's a dedicated children's hospital and if it was appendicitis, he would have to have surgery to remove his appendix. waterbury hospital does not have a pediatric department. 
we were transferred about noon and got to hartford hospital about 12:30. 
once there we were seen immediately by a bunch of staff. he got an ultrasound done and appendix looked normal. they did more x-rays on him and turns out he had pneumonia (they could see it in the x-rays and doctor says it explains his fever, and abdominal pain). they diagnosed him in about an hour and a half, and we were out by 3. 
so....he had pneumonia since the first er trip we took but instead he was diagnosed with asthma and this second trip was diagnosed with possible appendicitis scaring me to death! why couldn't they see the pneumonia when they did the x-rays the first time from the very beginning?! extremely frustrating!!

still, the staff that helped me during this time were all great, friendly, and treated my son very well. 
i took 1 star off because of the wait time that always seems to be a problem and another star because of the improper diagnoses, not once but twice. 
i should've known though because when i came here for myself awhile back, they tested me for strep and although it came back negative, i was still prescribed strep medication for whatever reason. unbelievable! 
anyways, if you're coming here for your children, know they do not have a pediatric department so either go to saint mary's or i highly recommend hartford's children emergency department, worth the longer drive trust me!!!!

it was my first biopsy (and hopefully my last) so i had no idea what to expect.  dr, belcher explained to me exactly what the procedure was and why they were doing it.  marlene was empathetic and helpful in every way.  i couldn't ask for a better experience.

we had a great experience with the emergency department. we rushed there with our 8 month old son who was having an allergic reaction for the first time. they ushered us back to a room within 2 minutes upon our arrival and started to treat him. the doctors and nurses were kind and knowledgeable. they helped us go from a panic to calm knowing he was getting the care he needed. overall, we were really happy with our experience and are surprised to see so many negative reviews.

i'm disgusted with how my type 1 diabetic daughter was treated in the er on 12/30/19!!!!! when we arrived my daughter could barely breathe because she was going into ketoacidosis (dka) which is life threatening. your body breaks down fat to fast and causes your liver to turn the fat into fuel which is ketones and your blood becomes acidic. so pretty much your body is filled with acid blood. her sugar levels were 563 when we arrived and all i was told was she'll have to wait because there were no beds available. there was only one nurse who showed her concern and kept trying to get someone to help my daughter. my daughter was in pain, could barely talk because she had a dry mouth, that feels like cotton in your mouth and she couldn't breathe. i kept asking for help and telling them she couldn't sit in the waiting room like that and her condition is life threatening. she could go into a coma. my plea went on deaf ears, my daughter cried saying she wasn't going to make it and she thought she was going to die. when my daughter was about to pass out and my younger daughter started crying and i started yelling for someone to help is when helped arrived. the one nurse who cared from the beginning came out and took my daughter to the back and immediately hooked her up to iv fluids and got my daughter a doctor and nurse to help. no type 1 diabetic in dka should ever have to wait like my daughter did. they waited so long to treat my daughter that it took hours before they could get her stabilized! if i could give this hospital a negative zero or no stars i would.

the hospital has a very stupid entrance for an out patient use. no sidewalk, a very long  uphill walk if not being dropped off   however the culture inside is so genuine and caring as to mitigate the experience.  the technicians are caring beyond any expectations. they realized that i was hurting and took every care to help me and keep me informed as to what i would undergo. i had 3 tests and had ample time to meet several ladies and a man. this was not expected  to be a good experience. ii am naturally a curmudgeon with far too much experience with medical staff. this very same hospital actually dropped me on the floor in transferring me to a room from the icu in 1985! but these techs in the outpatient department were in fact exemplary.

wow, just left the er after what could have been a painful experience and was instead easy, efficient and painless.

everyone was wonderful, we were seen within 15 minutes of arriving (it didn't look busy in the waiting room, but the er itself was busy). the er techs, nurses and doctor were amazing.

in less than 3 hours, we had a full set of labs, x-rays and ct scans with results.

broke my ribs.  for those of  you who have had broken ribs there is nothing a doctor can do.   you just need four or five days  of rest to let them heal.  but in the wisdom of the american medical community - the most expensive in the world, double than other developed countries,  and least effective - the inova  hospital system pumps me so full of drugs that i couldn't go to the bathhroom so i am cut off from drinking water and a catheter is inserted.   how in the world does that make any sense?????   at each point i ask for a price, nobody knew anything.  they tried to send me home with some ridiculous thing stuck to my back for pain.  i was able to find out that the stupid thing was going to cost me $1400.  i told them to forget it.  but they send me a bill, four months later, for $28,000 for four days of rest.  stay away from these greedy pigs!

what garbage emergency room they first kept me in that hospital for 20 hours and then the latter part of it with the worst nurse i've ever seen or heard! was barely around and could not communicate effectively didn't understand half the things she said! this was in july and maybe if their doctors were doing their job i wouldn't have this cast on my foot and having to miss more time from work but the hospital probably doesn't care about that which is fine i'll make sure i'll never go in there lol i drove into their to begin with what's the difference! then my second issue i had was when i did a delivery for a 3rd party company i go to emergency room to ask where i should take this delivery they make me walk all around the hospital which probably or most likely contributed to me having an air cast on right now and still didn't take me to right place even though they could've just pointed to where cause i then find out that i could have drove to the complex i was supposed to deliver too!! this er is some hot garbage and a waste of tax payer money and a disgrace this what we get for hard earned money!! well i'm gonna drill this hospital whenever i get the chance and either go to medstar or dc for healthcare!!

should be in the negatives if i could! the er and icu staff at this hospital is quite simply put: rude! even my husband who never says a bad word about anyone was disgusted with their behavior. nurse assistants who don't have time to make an 86-year old patient feel comfortable or assist in having him use a urinal over the side of the bed; nurses talking about visitors behind their back but in a very obvious manner; staff that doesn't introduce themselves or care to use/learn the patients name. disgusting, disgusting! there was only one rn in the er dept that actually got into nursing to help people, and she was an on-charge nurse who was covering for the main nurse while she took lunch; went above and beyond. icu should also work on their people skills when dealing with family members of individuals with serious health issues. upon arriving in the icu, i was basically kicked out while dropping my dad's bags of clothes off escorting him from the er. not hi! i'm your father's nurse, would you mind stepping out while we get him settled? that would be too much for them to utter. totally rude! oh and the kicker! when i call back to check on him, the nurse states: "are you the young lady who i kicked out earlier this evening?" awkwardly, "yes, that's me." "let me give you a code for when you call back because if i didn't know you were the woman i kicked out earlier, i would ask for it, too." like who talks like that? i had every right to curse him out, but let it go since my dad is under his care; insensitive jerk! for context, my dad is an 86-year old who has stage 4 kidney cancer in his lung, has one kidney, has had prostate cancer, eyelid/skin cancer, has diabetes, etc. and was admitted for a potential heart attack/inflamed heart. like i'm his daughter! have a little compassion. if not for me, certainly for him. at his age, the worst thing is being admitted to a hospital; you don't think you are going to come out. some people should really just not be nurses, etc. - in it for the wrong reasons. the majority at dover certainly didn't get involved in healthcare to help people, and if they did they lost their humanity along the way. if coronavirus hits this hospital, they will be ill-prepared to handle patient care - and certainly not prepared to do it in a respectful manner. get it together!

my 73 year old gentleman friend from the east coast decided to trim my tree.  no good!

one day later:

back to the emergency room at pvh.  now they diagnose 6 broken ribs,  a punctured and partially collapsed  lung, and broken arm.  ambulance to santa rosa.  surgery on collapsed lung. one week later informed that his arm was crushed.  the cast from pvh was removed and two plates were placed in his arm.

i don't understand all the bad reviews... i feel bad for anyone that has had a bad stay here, but truly i have seen mostly the opposite. i don't know many of the nurses names but mallory in the er is the sweetest person ever and you can tell she cares a lot. i don't doubt that there are some nurses who might be burnt out after a long time in such a demanding profession, but generally it seems that the nurses do care. why else would they be there tbh? this is a trauma hospital, and from what i've seen, they deal with a lot of stuff. i couldn't imagine doing what they do. 
the hospital takes tons of insurances and patient services will try very hard to get financial assistance if you do not have insurance. 
food is pretty good for a hospital, especially during the week when jason is cooking at the grill. he makes really good quesadillas lol
all in all, i wouldn't disregard this place based in other bad reviews. if it's close by and you need er services, just come here. of course, if you could go to an urgent care instead, please do that. part of the reason er wait times go up so much is because people come in when they could probably do with an urgent care visit instead. i do know that if you're in a real emergency and not just coming in with a stomach ache, the make sure they see you swiftly. 
anyways, that's just my opinion.
i am commenting about the emergency room, these health care professionals . consistentlyrise to the occasion and exceed expectations. i can't be thankful enough for having them serve our. community
waited four hours in the er. and nobody here what a joke.  poor communication.   nobody around to help

its almost midnight and still nothing. hopefully she doesnt have another episode. they might as well as left us in the waiting room up front. never coming back to this unprofessional hospital.
nice people and super easy to get it. the urgent care is one of the better ones in the area

one of the worst hospitals i've encountered. their nurses have no clue whether drinking water is acceptable for a person who will have to have an mri. i understand you don't want me to have food but if i arrived at 2:00 pm and it's 7 and no one is helping, than what am i suppose to do? yes, i arrived at 2:00 pm and did not leave until 9:30 pm. i ask people why it's taking so long and crickets. there was a time when the front desks were empty. this is suppose to be the emergency section in the hospital? no communication, felt they did not care for the well being of their patients, extremely slow, old school, inattentive, etc. if you want to go to a hospital to find out what's wrong with you, be prepared to stay long and people not give you answers. you only received about 5 prescriptions to take per day until you get your results. by the way, their testing is not done in the hospital but somewhere else. if you want answers, expect to call them in 5 business days. i guess this hospital must not know the meaning of "life is short".

i would give zero stars if i could. my cousin was taken by ambulance to bsw-wax. she requested to be taken to big baylor in dallas, but because it was a "busy night in town" she was taken to waxahachie, (this is really just a side-note and will be addressed with the city of waxahachie). she was writhing in pain...wailing from the intense migraine that she had been battling all afternoon. a migraine so intense that she had not experienced one that debilitating since she had a stroke ten years prior. the attending doctor came in to her room and began yelling at her asking her questions. her husband asked him to please lower his voice. the doctor responded with, "well, i've got to be louder than her so she can hear me." upon my arrival she was being attended by a nurse who got her some pain relief. it finally took the pain away enough that she fell asleep. it was about 30-45 minutes later that the doctor came back. he was so loud it was obnoxious. he asked if the meds were working. i turned and in a low voice replied, "yes. she is sleeping." it was then he lowered his voice and told us he would check back in 15 minutes. before his return the registration nurse came in with her computer. she was told that my cousin did not have insurance. assuming she was indigent, she told her partner that there was sometimes financial assistance available. now, before she was registered the attending nurse said she would be getting a ct scan to rule out stroke, etc. that was before they learned of her not having insurance. guess what? i have been here for hours and there is one doctor in the entire hospital. my friend is sleeping in the hospital and the doctor will not eek lease him. the service here is slow. they will not answer my questions and it is annoying annoy. i'm not impressed.

feels like the monopoly it is. not quite the three stooges but very close. some very good people there, some very bad software and protocols. i felt like i was a barcode. i got better, but i can't correlate that with the care i received.

came in for a good laceration on the index finger. required x-ray as the knife went down the the bone. came in at 3pm on a sunday. 

upon walking in, we were greeted and assigned a wristband. the triage nurse gave an initial assessment and recommends an x-ray. by about 3:45p, we went back for the x-ray. the x-ray technician was knowledgeable and took time to deep clean the room, which made me feel comfortable about the procedure. i then travelled back to the room in the er and the nurse came in by 4:15p, cleaned the wound, and the pa made an assessment. 

first, we are in an er with a lot of sick people. the process is going to take some time, so it's important to manage your expectations. the staff made sure to keep us informed of wait times, which was appreciated. the rn jillian and the pa kristin were great providers. 

with that said, there are a ton of impatient people in the er (patients) who were being disruptive and inappropriate. everyone wants to be the top priority, but that's not going to be possible. give these er employees a break, they're doing the best they can.

 i went to a different er two days later and tested positive for influenza b. i can't believe i paid melrose wakefield and had to visit another hospital to receive the care i needed!

was seen saturday around 4am. saw the dr once. he was rude ignoring me while he had a 10 minute chat with the person that brought me about my friend being a vet. then insults me. he asked me a question about my nose ring and then proceeds to tell me how much he hates tattoos and piercings and finds them ugly. i also have tattoos. then he tried to give me a med that i'm allergic to despite the red band on my wrist that said allergies and the fact that he was holding the report of my allergies in his hands not 4" from his face. and that was the last time he came to me room. i was there for 3 hours and saw him that one time. he let the nurses and triage guy that took my vitals attend to me. he was supposed to have an iv set up with meds and never bothered to write it up so that never happened. so let's get this straight, first he ignores he, then insults me, then tries to kill me with meds i'm allergic to.... great dr you have "helping" people there, not. i'll not be coming back there again, i'm apparently safer at home!!!!!

our daughter had to have a dental procedure here. it was scary for us to hand our 4 year old daughter over, but they did their best to make it not so bad. the staff is very friendly, and made sure my daughter was never worried or scared of what was happening. they talked her through the entire process and came out once she was asleep to tell us that she did fine. the recovery nurse was a little cold, and it seemed like she was trying to rush us out the door before our daughter was fully awake and pain free. i had to keep asking if it was ok to stay a few more minutes, she seemed annoyed but allowed us to stay. overall it was fine. as a parent you just have to advocate for your child, in all scenarios.

they still need to put a sign about their weekly parking pass by the pay parking machines to make people aware of it and reduce the amount.  

the nurses and aids  here are wonderful, a very special thanks to nurse gloria, 6th floor, room 6203, who was amazing, so caring and compassionate.

i'm back again!!! this time the wait was the extremely long. the sanitation was a little better. everything was fine until i needed blood work. i entered the er at 3. just got my blood drawn at 8:30. i'm still waiting for them to determine if i need to stay over night. they also informed me that the bed wait is 5 hours long!!!!! i wish i didn't have to come to this er because the wait is ten times worst then washington hospital center. it is getting to the point where i think will be in this er for two days. i will update once i get a room. wish me luck!! thank god i'm not dying. but if i do just look for me dead by the vendor machine. waiting for my results and bed space!!

the worst! the pediatric er is severely understaffed. the admission staff/front desk is wonderful, responsive and helpful. once you get into the back - forget about it! we were there for 3 hours or more before they even took my daughter's blood pressure. she was just lying there in pain with no monitoring, and no one checked on us except the person responsible for billing - never too busy to make sure the billing is done. apparently they had an emergency and all resources had to be used for that one patient leaving all the other children just waiting for unreasonably long periods of time with zero communication from the staff. 
when i inquired about the staff i was told that they had just one pediatrician and 2 nurses working. they were unapologetic and seemed unbothered. i would not recommend taking your child here.

this hospital is a nightmare! it's dirty, staff members betty and ana in the er were both rude, aggressive and lazy! if i could i'd give it negative stars!!!!i am very easy to please, but those two just plain didn't like me, it's probably that they just don't like white people! that's kinda how it seemed! when i walked thru the door, betty looked me in the eyes and walked away from the desk! seemed like she was more interested in sitting with ana watching tv and gossiping! i asked her for more supplies for my medical problem she didn't even acknowledge me! so...negative stars for betty and ana!

why is this place still operating??!!! ughhhhhh!!!! 
walked in on a tuesday, and was shocked by the amount of patients just waiting.. as i walked to the initial intake/registration, i over heard her tell an elderly gentleman the people there had been waiting nearly 5 hours!!! wth? icing on the cake, is that not only did the "nurse" seemingly ignore me several times while others pranced around giggling with their co workers and talking about the damn  weather! what a joke! mad i didn't snap a picture.. but why would a hospital ever post a sign saying "if you have the flu or flu like symptoms, please don't enter the hospital"! excuse me what? this place is a disgrace! i wouldn't take my gold fish here for water..

well, despite the doctor calling in ahead of time for a re-admission to this hospital, we have been sitting in the er waiting room for almost 2.5 hours.  as the er empties out, i have to wonder whether people are actually being taken back or if they are just leaving because they are tired of waiting.  they are understaffed, as they were the last time we were here and the intake process is freaking ridiculous.  we literally had a guy come in while getting vitals taken with his teenage kid complaining of chest pain and he wasn't immediately screened to go in.  i honestly hate this place, i wish my spouses doctors had not sent them here in the first place because the follow up has been anything other than pleasant.  do yourself a favor and go to less of a shit hole hospital.

as an update... the nurse in the er was nice, but the only positive thing i can say about the experience here.  the doctor (dr. evans) refused to see the patient and instead wanted to do a transfer to another hospital.  my spouse just went into a bathroom in the observation unit and the entire thing was covered in blood... not sure who or where it came from but talk about a health hazard.  when leaving, because they decided to not treat and wait for a transfer (just like last time) we decided to check out ama to speed up the process and go to another hospital ourselves instead of waiting multiple days for a transfer, which everyone told us would be faster.  well when we went to go leave they refused to provide any records and told us we needed to go request them specifically because we decided to make the best choice for my spouse medically instead of waiting days to be transferred.  this place is a nightmare and seems to keep getting worse.  at least last time we were there it was somewhat clean, this time it was absolutely disgusting.  when i left there last night they had an older person in a wheelchair in the waiting room hallway near the er who appeared to have possibly had an issue and instead of cleaning it up, someone threw chucks on the floor and just left them there.  i wonder if housekeeping is on strike because it was nasty!!

my 85 year old uncle arrived with my 83 year old aunt to the er he was complaining of difficulty breathing, severe head, neck and back pain. they waited over 3 hours in the er unattended. when his name was finally called, my poor aunt could not rouse him. although she thought he'd fallen asleep he'd actually died. they whisked my aunt away as they tried unsuccessfully to revive him.  do not buy in to the model senior emergency care facility. this is a dangerous, inconsistent, overcrowded er that cannot safely care for the volume of patients in the er

the only reason i'm giving this place one star is because zero stars are not allowed. words cannot describe my disappointment with this horrible establishment. it was exactly 9:33pm when i walked in. i came to the e.r. because i was experiencing flu-like symptoms, i had a severe pain in my chest, and my vision was very blurry. when i checked in, i noticed that the man at the front desk typed, "patient is complaining of flu." first of all, rude. second of all, what about the chest pain and the blurred vision? those are serious symptoms. i ended up waiting quite literally six hours before i saw a doctor. i was taken into the back at 3:12am. six hours. during that time, i asked so many times, "can someone please take a look at my chest? it really hurts!" and they just kept dismissing me. turns out, i was in stage 2 hypertension. i could have had a heart attack and died. how did the person who took my vitals not have alerted someone that my blood pressure was so high? how could all of the staff just dismiss me and tell me that people had "bigger issues"? this was the most unprofessional hospital that i have ever been to. i would quite literally rather die than ever return to holy cross hospital in silver spring.

very bad experience - my husband has parkinsons.  he fell and could not get up so had to call emt's to get him up and they took him to holy cross, his first time there (and believe me, last time). they would not give him his medications and then diagnosed him as confused.  yes, parkinson's sufferers get confused when they haven't had their meds in a timely fashion.  they didn't clean him.  they didn't let him clean himself up.  they messed up the iv, tore up the top of his hand and it came out and the fluid went under his skin.  the neurologist was not understandable (accent like martin short in the movie "father of the bride") and did not make sense.  i told him to call my husband's neurologist, i hope he did.  many people asking the same questions over and over and over again. i asked four different people how to register with my insurance information - all gave me the wrong information. very confused, disorganized, no communication.  and to top this off, i have had three different people call about nurses to inspect my home and trying to sell me nursing aid even after i told them my husband was moved to a group home specializing in neuromuscular disorders.  yes, why is this place still operating?

the first time ever at hamot was the result of a heart attack on 12/23/19.  i was mercy flighted from wca hospital in jamestown ny directly to hamot.  once we touched down was immediately taken to surgery to open the closed artery that cuased the inital heart attack,  it was good to see the staff were ready for me and quickly took me directly from the helipad directly into surgery to repair the closed artery, they  found i had two closed arteries and explained that they would need to have me back to stent to other one.. they quickly and professionally installed the first stent into the artery.  all time time the staff and professional explained everything they were doing.  i spent 23rd to the 25th of december there and the staff went above and beyond to get me fitted with a life vest so that i could return home for christmas.  at all times when in 5 south -  room 545, from the doctors, the  nurses, the aides, housekeeping and the kitchen i was treated with respect and kindness and concern for my well being.  they went above and beyond in my opinion to insure my comfort while i was there.  they all explained everything that they were doing and why.  i returned for my second stent on january 9th, again in 5 south room 544.  i was treated exactly the same as i had been the first time there.  so many times people are quick to criticize and complain about there care but i for one was treated exceptionally well,  they truly did show compassion and caring and were willing to accommodate where ever they could to make my stay the best it could be considering the reason i was there.  i would highly recommend hamot to anyone going through what i did and humbly and sincerely thank the doctors, the nurse , the aides for the caring and considerate care they provided during both my stays.

i am being treated very poorly by the system. patient interaction is very poor.

i blacked out about a week ago so called my dr. at lowry campus for an appt soon. the soonest was 2 days later with someone else. i went in and saw the other doctor and lo and behold, my doctor showed up to consult! well, they ordered a ct scan of my neck which i had last sat. yesterday i received a phone msg from someone i don't know telling me a surgeon's office was going to call me and i had a narrowing ... i couldn't actually tell what he said bz the sound was garbled at times. i called and left a message yesterday morning asking my dr. to call me. i called again just before 5 pm yesterday asking if he had received the message and asking him to call and tell me what was going on. he did not call me. also yesterday i got a phone call from a neurosurgeon's office saying i needed to make an appt. so far though, i had not talked to anyone but a receptionist. at home i logged on to my health record and saw a letter from the second (substitute) doctor saying what was seen on the ct scan. i didn't know what some of it meant so i looked it up online. i can tell you it was very scary - ischemic stroke, rare condition, c1 or c2, surgical intervention might be possible. 

today, my doctor still has not called. i called again asking him to call me and tell me what is going on. i also said that they now have me terrified and i need to talk with him. the gal said i just have to wait until he calls me at his earliest convenience or have someone else talk to me. 

what on earth!  i have never heard of such poor patient care. they hand me a very scary diagnosis then refuse to talk to me. they just pass me around, one person to another person, none of them so-called "my own doctor", none of the others know me. they just look at pictures and read words. that inspires zero confidence or compliance with recommendations. studies have shown and we medical folks have known for 40 years or more that good patient interaction is the best way to get the best outcomes.

so now i feel like i could die at any moment or have a stroke that will leave me a vegetable. i have no one here to advocate for me and i don't know just what to do. where else could i go?

i was an rn for many years (cardiology icu) and took excellent care or many, many people. now when i need to be cared for i'm not getting it. 

i give 2 stars bz i have seen good care given but i'm sure not getting it now!!

update: 
at last my doctor called me just a few minutes ago. he said he had not received either of the 2 messages i left for him yesterday. he saw them this morning only. he now explained everything such that i am not terrified now. i'm still pretty scared but it is manageable (i think). so, i'll add a star.

review:
i was taken here back in july due to a horrible mental health episode i had at work. i gave them my health insurance info when i checked out so i thought it would all be ok in the end.

5+ months later and i still haven't gotten a bill from them or a change to my account balance. every time i call they give me another excuse. one time it was because they ended up sending my claim to the wrong address for my insurance, who by the way doesn't cover emergency care anyway. another time i guess they did it again and yet another time they said to wait for my insurance to say anything back. well they didn't so two and a half weeks ago i finally said "look, i keep telling you they're not going to cover this. what am i waiting for?" they still couldn't give me a good answer so i decided to take the self-pay option, which would take a few thousand dollars off the bill.

i'm still waiting for that bill or a change in my account balance. yesterday they told me it could take anywhere from 3 to 45 days to process the self-pay. didn't know that would take that long. so after that call was done i did the post-call survey and requested a follow-up call.

"oh no, it shouldn't take that long! if you still don't have anything after that 45 days call us back and we'll escalate it."

i have no confidence that anything will change between now and then or that escalating will do anything. at this point they should just write it off so i can move on with my life instead of being dicked around by this hospital's awful billing department.
fac_name: UCHealth At University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

review:
hmmm... if i leave a negative yelp review, will they connect me to a human who will find my referral that is probably floating around their system somewhere?  then can i finally make an appointment??

i can only assume that cu anschutz has a centralized great paper shredder where they send all referrals, medical records, and requests to insurance companies.

my husband had a fantastic doctor in the neurology department who helped him finally get the treatment he needed... after months of struggling through lost paperwork, unreturned calls, etc.  then the doctor submitted a request to the insurance company, but that must have gone to the great paper shredder too, because the insurance company never received it.  required several more phone calls and waiting, resulting in a couple months delay in treatment.  the whole time, the doctor never got any of the messages he was leaving for him.  not great when you have a neurodegenerative disease.

then we moved out of state, and after two months of weekly phone calls to try to get his records sent to the new hospital with no luck, the new hospital finally gave up and went in and pulled his records electronically.

two years later, we are moving back, and i try to make an appointment with the pelvic pain clinic.  different department... maybe it was just neurology that couldn't handle paperwork.  nope.  sent a referral, and just got a "we don't have anything."  still can't make an appointment.  i'm in a lot of pain, have been for years, nobody's figured it out yet, and just as i'm moving/switching doctors, i'm having a really bad reaction to the latest birth control they've tried to put me on as treatment.  i'd like to at least have an appointment lined up, because i know it can sometimes take months to see a specialist.  meanwhile the meds are making the pain worse as well as causing my head to feel like it's floating off into space like a balloon.

i asked, is there a number that my doctor could call to make sure that my referral is received this time?  answer:  "no, it goes somewhere else."  yeah, it must go to the great paper shredder to join all of my husband's medical records, phone messages, and insurance requests.

their suggestion is for me to hand-deliver the referral, thus circumventing the great paper shredder that relentlessly guards the fax machine exit.  sure, let me just get in my car and drive 18 hours to hand-deliver a fax.

their next best suggestion is to have my doctor's office staff write "second attempt" at the top of the referral.  perhaps the great paper shredder does not have a taste for the words "second attempt."  i'm not optimistic.

too bad, because the doctors and researchers there seem quite good, and it seems to be the best or only place in the state to go for some health issues.
fac_name: UCHealth At University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

review: the eye center didn't help me with my eyes, the first doctor didn't care if i went to my appointment. they were not nice as doctors at all.
fac_name: UCHealth At University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

review:
uchealth center is the worst place that i have ever dealt with.  patients are not their priority.  communication is horrid.  if you have to contact someone, you can't call the office directly.  you have to work your way through a network of individuals to only be told the staff will call you back, which many, many times they never do.  i am serious!  i have also had doctors change appointments on me and three doctors have actually cancelled appointments that were scheduled.  no human being actually calls you; the system just sends a message via your patient portal.  if you don't check your portal, you wouldn't even know the appointment got cancelled.  you then have to call to reschedule and to find out why the appointment was cancelled without consulting you.  so what are you supposed to do?  guess what, you jump through the hoops again to try and talk to someone, but are told the staff will call you back.  of course, they don't!  if they do, you find out the doctor is no longer there.  hmmm, i wonder why!?  is it because of a screwed up system??  so, again how am suppose to develop a rapport with a doctor when i have to start all over again.  it's maddening.  
another terrible experience was when i had a doctor leave me in the exam room, telling me he would be right back.  he had to clear things with the supervising doctor.  i waited an extremely long time and finally went to the desk to ask where my doctor was.  unbelievably, he had gone home!!  what!?  at that point i realized that i have to get out of this unbelievably crazy system (they only refer you to other uchealth doctors) and find some responsible doctors/facilities that are more professional and care more about their patients than themselves.
fac_name: UCHealth At University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

review: oh my goodness if you need to be sick and served medically this hospital is the place. it has so many  friendly employees. from the transportation workers to the nurses to the radiologists to the doctors even the security they are so professional and so nice.  it is a huge complex and so i thought how could they make it seem homey and caring but they do once admitted. there are many long term employees there not just 5 years or 10 but many longer than that retiring from there. what does that mean? they know a lot about the place and how it runs. every person i asked ,if they like their job or not, surprisingly did. that hasn't happened in other hospitals i have been to. now it is a busy place so you will have a wait for things and things will get forgotten sometimes but the people have heart. the er gets crazy and the amount of people waiting there is so insane you feel bad for them. downside of the hospital  is it is not exactly easy to get a room and you share that room and bathroom once there. you hear everyone's business  in the room you share. the nurses and aides are helpful albeit running around constantly. i wish i could clone some of these workers. if you find yourself there  and your experience is like mine, you are in good hands
fac_name: UCHealth At University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

review: i just went in for a dislocated shoulder. they gave me an ekg? didnt look at my shoulder! told me i had a strained shoulder. they did take an xray but the don't view them there. dont go to this location. they don't read the charts. please help me to understand.

i almost don't want to leave this review because i'm afraid the secret will get out and this magical place will be ruined forever.  however, i feel drawn to share my amazing experience at this facility (mostly in hopes that the staff sees it) so here it goes.  

i came in today after acquiring a hiking injury.  it was not really a major injury but it was definitely one of those injuries that you think you miiiigght need to have checked / your mom magically takes you to get looked at after your lunch date. (lol thanks mom )

from the moment i walked in every single person on staff was friendly and welcoming.  even the security guard was friendly.  when does that happen??  not only were they super nice, but they were hilarious!  i haven't laughed at an er visit ever in my life, so to laugh multiple times on one visit was a pleasant surprise.  

long story short, it turns out i am a first aide professional so the doctor offered me 2 options and let me choose which way i wanted to go based on the educated information he gave me.   i opted out of the stitches, so he offered me the best advice on how to care for my wound and advised me to stay away from bears next time. lol. oh and bonus.... i got a tetanus shot, just for stopping by!   lol.  (jk. i actually needed it for this injury.)

i should also note, i didn't wait a single minute!  walked in, registered, was taken back immediately, doctor came in as the nurse walked out, another nurse came in with my shot before the doctor was even done telling me how to care for my wound, discharge nurse was in before the tetanus shot was even done being administered.  boom! just like that, i was outta there!   maybe 20 minutes tops. 
thank you to everyone at er at the lakes!  you are the real mvp's. 

i hope they read this and laugh all over again.  

merry christmas!

eric anderson is one of the er doctors!
i have something stuck in my sinuses it's been in there about a month now. i have been dealing with it hoping it would pass on its own. it had gotten to the point i was unable to sleep and was starting to cause pain and irritation. i went in to seek treatment and was basically told that i am there for drugs is the impression i got.when i specifically told him i don't want any medications or any types of drugs. i just need this looked at to see if anything can be done. he told me again that i was full of shit and there was no way i could have this issue unless i was genetically different from everyone else. there's absolutely no way nothing could be lodged in my sinuses. it was impossible to have this issue and there was absolutely nothing that he could do or would do for me. i asked again and disbelief absolutely nothing you can do? couldn't even refer me to an ent! !?!? after i said that he got pissed and left the room his own nurse was stunned at the way he was talking to me. the man wouldn't even examine me or look to see if there was a fucking issue. i am extremely upset over this i have never been treated this way by any medical professional. i am not the type of person to go to the doctor for anything!! i have done everything in my power to this point to not go to the doctor and this is what i had to deal with... worst person to have to see in las vegas. go anywhere else but to this guy. i don't even know what to say still in disbelief with the way i was treated.

you will be charged emergency room prices! our bill stated a total charge of $7,606.00 for a single ct scan (cat scan) which is normally about $200 at a radiology center. when we called to complain that we were not warned the person answering the phone said the people at the front desk have no idea what the bills will be and no way of finding out. they are technically (legally) an emergency room of southern hills hospital and they will charge you exorbitant prices, and you will get the runaround when you try to get some relief. southern hills hospital, when you finally get a real person there, will tell you that hometown health negotiates all the prices, but you can't talk to them, only doctors can.

after reading the reviews i was nervous, i don't know what everybody's talking about this place was literally amazing it's owned by southern hills hospital but you don't have to wait for hours to get in i walked right in they saw me within five minutes doctor was amazing in and out after x-rays and all within an hour i'm telling you this place is unbelievable!! i had walking pneumonia and they totally got me fixed up

we just had a great experience here. we are visiting from out of state and my son needed stitches. we got referred from urgent care because they couldn't help him. everyone was nice from start to finish. the facility is clean and well lit. i hope to never need to go to the er in vegas again but if i do we know where to go.

i wish i could give this place a -5 star rating. as you can see based on the other negative reviews, this place does not treat their patients as people but more as numbers and dollar signs. this place is considered an urgent care and not so much of an er, it is not a hospital so they should be prepared to explain what they are to people walking in. i was on the phone with my husband today when he walked into this place. listening in, he told the negligent lady at the front desk that he has a simple throat ache and stated (many times) that this was not an emergency and he kept on repeating himself. he told her that there was a long line at the cvs walk-in across the street and asked the incompetent woman at the front desk, jana white, if she can verify with his insurance because he doesn't want to be charged a large sum. if she cannot do this, that is fine but as i am sure that this is not the first case, she could have told him that "we will accept you by law but because it is not an emergency, you're better off waiting there because this place will charge you a lot more - but if you decide to continue, then yes, of course by law we have to take you." since she is either incompetent or just doesn't care about people, she did not explain this to him and assured him that everything would be fine. she walked him into a room without explaining the terms but it still didn't sit well with my husband. as he was sitting and waiting for a doctor, he decided to call the insurance company to ask about how much he would be charged and the insurance company said that he would be charged 400$ for this visit. as the dr walked in, he said that he did not want to get treatment because he didn't want to pay $400!! a few nurses walked in and started yelling and bashing him that its the law for him to stay in the room. he kept on repeating himself - "i asked before checking in, and nobody explained the terms to me." "i specifically said that i have a simple throat ache and this is not an emergency" - they continued to yell at him although it was their mistake! as he continued to walk out, the lady at the front desk rudely said that he would be billed (although he had no treatment from the doctor). it hurt my soul listening to them talk to him the way they did, i wish i was there to help him. when he came home and we were talking about it, he even told me that the dr understood what he was saying and actually apologized to him (but obviously he has no control). it was such an awful experience. so there you go - we are getting billed $400 for a common cold...and during the holiday season! - this place should be embarrassed and admit to their mistakes instead of throwing their faults on a patient who was so polite! ..and they should fix their processes.

excellent hospital and staff.  already says ready with anything you request. i have been to other hospitals in nc. they do not even come to the quality of this hospital.  if i need anymore care i will come to duke-raleigh.

had surgery in aug, 2019.  when asked my surgeon afterwards why they use this hospital was told because i have medicare and not allowed to use others. i waited 3 and half hours after my surgery for a room in a noisy crazy post opt environment. the anesthesiology was dangerous and left me with some brain damage. i never saw or talked to an anesthesiologist. it all was done on the fly. their excuse was there were issues with everything because they had a lot of emergencies that day and that all hospitals are overcrowded in raleigh and that  i was just lucky that i did not have to spent the night in the post opt. this was a weekday surgery scheduled a month in advance. it seemed my health and safety was on the bottom of the list to anyone who walked in that day. i felt as if i was in a dangerous third world country receiving care. would never go there for anything!

i was unexpectedly admitted earlier this month to upmc shadyside, after first going to the upmc urgent care facility across the street. the staff at the urgent care determined i should have testing that they didn't have the capability for.

i got there at 3 p.m. and left 26 hours later.

the service was prompt in the er, the nursing staff was attentive.  after they decided to have me observed overnight, i was sent to a room, and the nurses there were very nice as well.

food was fine.  i got the tests they had prescribed, ct, echo, eeg promptly and the staff was nice.   they didn't dally in getting me out at the end of the stay.  when i complained about the temperature in the room as too warm, the nurses turned it down right away.

no one wants to be in the hospital, and i only ended up at upmc shady due to the accident of choosing to go to the upmc urgent care.  if i knew i was going to the er , i would have probably chose to go somewhere else.    but it was really fine, really convenient, the staff was nice and attentive, i have no complaints about any of them.

my care was great in icu after surgery. nurses and staff were very nice all around. my complaint is with the head of this hospital and whoever is in charge. once i was moved to a regular floor i didn't have one hospital employee the whole time i was there. they were all temporary fill. they were nice, competent i think, but only saw a living being if it was time for a medication round or shift change. what incentive do any of them have to go above and beyond when it's just a temporary day here and there? none! the goal is to be like a nursing home where nurses aids care for you and a rn passes pills. it's ridiculous! this is a hospital not a nursing home! i was in here for a major surgery. lost a lot of blood. filled up with fluids and the day they discharged me i ended up in our local hospital that night for two more nights here with small clots in my lungs and 15 lbs of fluid taken off. you want to talk about a dirty  and gross cafeteria?!? check it out! i don't know how in the world they get away with it. whoever is in charge of this hospital needs to take a trip to cleveland clinic and have lunch there. maybe take some tips from them. maybe the head honchos at shadyside should be paid on merit and not just position title. i don't know how you go about affecting change here but i hope and pray someone cares enough to step up to the plate and actually speak up and do something. we spoke to our dr but that was going no where fast.

i work as a mortician so this review comes from a different spectrum than regular customers or patients. never before have i been disgraced with such lack of care and unprofessionalism from the nursing staff than i have in this hospital. it would appear the people here aren't capable of doing their jobs and rather than admit it with sooner rather blame you for your work ethic, and just be standoffish as opposed to a caring and understanding individuals that you would expect from doctors or nurses. 

when addressing the issue with the management, it would appear that they had no inclination of addressing this issue as they choose to listen to me silently and as i was done wordlessly let me leave with nothing else to add. a sign that this has happened in the past and they're used to dealing with these kind of complaints.

all in all i'm not sure how patients fair from this hospital but from a professional and business side i would not recommend doing business with these people. the way they handled decedent affairs is disrespectful to both families and the workers involved.

pros:nice staff(except for the child center experiential therapist because she constantly made kids cry and feel anxious)however the child center staff is good nice rcs and treatment team

cons:terrible food

this place is amazing! working in er's for years-i never wanted to be on the other side of the equation but i quickly realized i need to find somewhere to go asap. i was able to check in online. arrived- filled out the necessary paperwork and was taken directly to a room- dr ely and triage rn came in immediately. i was triaged, iv placed, labs, ct and meds within an hour!! results, diagnosed and discharged 2 hours! everyone was super nice and professional. i appreciated everyone i encountered. i am happy to say- 2 days later i am feeling much better!!! i cannot praise this er enough.

no one ever wants to go to the er, but when they do, you at least want a good experience. from what i remember check in was easy. i was somewhat disoriented with what was exactly happening so i don't really remember. the lobby was clean and the person up from during triage was very nice. i signed a few forms and was quickly taken back to a room to be assessed. the staff was very nice and patient with me. luckily i had my better half to answer most questions and help me when i needed him most. it was overall a great experience. the rooms were quite small, but everything seemed very clean and the staff was great. the doc was able to assess and do what he needed rather than spend hours at an urgent care only to be directed to go to an er. 

if i need to come back, which hopefully i don't, i will be going here.

these folks are pros! great service and wonderful facilities! they have the ability to do a cat scan and have it read within one hour. this is exactly why i went there and they helped me get to the er for emergency surgery. they took my condition seriously!! thank you!! i'd choose them again but hope i don't have to!!
everyone here was very sweet after i was in a hit and run. dr. gill was kind and thorough and the nurses were awesome.

the medical staff were great, very helpful, caring and patient. i was helped quickly. parking is easy. the facility is clean.

the billing department is hellish and dysfunctional:

i had a visit more than five months ago and gave them my insurance information (cigna). i asked cigna many times and cigna told me every time that there was no claim from the facility. i called the billing department many times and every time, they told me there is a bill $95xx.xx and it's "pending" or "in process", but cigna still told me there's no claim received at all. finally a month ago in december, i decided to push them about this. after being on hold for many hours and waiting for their call back many times (multiple csr said they'd call me back but they never did, not even once), i finally got to speak with debbie who was working on my account. 

debbie said the claim was not submitted because their company had a merger recently and it's all confusing. she finally sent it out in mid-december. cigna said they received it but it's invalid because there is no provider name. so it's immediately rejected. whenever i talked to debbie, she was being extremely rude and condescending. apparently the actual billing department is incompetent too.

as of yesterday, more than five months after my visit, cigna does not have the claim from this er facility. it's supposed to be $95xx.xx. without their timely filing (six months), cigna wouldn't pay them and i might be on the hook for the entire amount. how can i ask aec to submit the claims correctly? i'm so frustrated after dealing with them for the past five months.

do not go here!!! this is a free standing er, not an urgent care clinic, so they can charge absurd surprise "facilities fees". i was here for less than 30 minutes for a broken toe and received a $1860 facilities fee. after arbitrary "adjustments" were made and hours talking with the billing department, i paid $400 (and yes, i have health insurance). that facility fee was in addition to the doctor's bill. watch out!!!!

my wife went here for a broken toe. received no treatment and a surprise $400 facilities bill. they refused to negotiate and threatened to send it to collections, so we finally paid it to avoid damaging our credit. this is not an urgent care facility. do not go here if you don't like surprise medical bills.

first, we should start with the good:

the facility was very clean, they were very prompt to serve me, and the staff was very friendly.

the bad:

this establishment is an actual scam.  first, the receptionist was trying to obfuscate whether the site would be considered (and thus bill) like a hospital or an urgent care facility.  most people, and anyone in healthcare, would understand the ramifications of that distinction from a payment standpoint and any legitimate hospital would be forthcoming about what to expect.  second, i entered the facility for a broken rib, for which they gave me a pain killer and took an x-ray.  when the x-ray came back that i had a minor lung collapse, they instructed me that i needed to go to a real hospital because they could not treat serious injuries.  yet they're still trying to bill as though they are a hospital.  third, when i finally did get the bills my less than 2 hour visit cost me more than an overnight stay in an actual hospital.  a hospital stay that itself had charges such as a $10 bandaid.  and lastly, once i had decided to just pay them off in installments so as to get rid of them and personally vow to never return, i received an additional bill not crediting all of my payments with a threat to send me to collections despite the fact that i've paid in full.

and i've seen the responses in here where they try to act like they're willing to work with people on billing and apologetic, but i've had numerous interactions with them on the phone and have not received any of the sort of understanding or compassion that they try to display publicly.

please don't go here.  please don't continue giving money to this predatory establishment.

staff was friendly and professional. i was in and out in a timely manner, unlike other er's were you'd have to wait in the lobby for about 3 hours. austin emergency center was very clean. i highly recommend this emergency room for after hour care.

this place has the best service. we came in after a bad experience at saint david's urgent care. they helped my father in law without any issues he fell an hit his head leaving a big gash. they spoke spanish an helped him without judgement and the whole process was as easy as a er visit could be i greatly appreciate everything they did to get him stitched up an checked out.

(i didn't mention how clean this place is) thank you everyone!

after 6.5 hours and in isolation i have been told they do not have the ability to test for corona virus. they lost my swab test which added on another two hours.

female security "officers" at the front of the hospital were over the top. questioning people like criminals waiving her water bottle around like they had some sort of real authority   just be nice. it's really easy. we know extra precautions need to be taken because of coronavirus but there's no need to be a bitch. just saying.

downey emergency is full of people with the flu or colds. came in with emergency and still waiting after close to 3 hour wait. why don't they keep urgent care open for flu and colds so when an emergency occurs the er isn't full of flu . you could die sitting in here waiting. other services have been good but this is horrible.

emergency waiting could improve by:

my grandma had to get an emergency surgery. they transferred her from the icu to the 5th floor. some of the nurses were kind, but for the past two days my grandma has been getting rude nurses. my family and i left to go eat real fast and when we came back my grandma was ringing the nurses. so we asked my grandma how long ago did she ring them. she said over 40 minutes  & no one came. that's ridiculous when we leave we expect them to see what she needs not wait over a half hour!! she had needed to be changed and was in her own feces for over 30 mins that's ridiculous! my grandmas nurse was rude! horrible hospitality and caregiving on there part! and to top it off when we first walked in my grandmas nurse was just talking to her coworker!

i birthed my son here at kaiser downey in the month of january  had a awesome labor & delivery doctors listened to my needs on what i wanted and didn't want. my son was transferred to the nicu due to being born prematurely nurses and doctors were very informative & very comforting while going thru that hard process than 1 week later my son was ready to come home and i just was so thankful for the nurses and doctors that helped my son get on track with his growth the care they give there  is outstanding and i totally recommend kaiser labor and delivery & the nicu department to everyone..
came in with crono virus and they waited 3 hours to helped me. by the time i got in i got the whole waiting room infected. up your fucking game kaiser.

went into the downey kaiser er department by ambulance because of extreme pain and couldn't stand or walk because the pain was that bad. i had a ureteral stent removed earlier that day and wasn't informed of this pain was coming and it hit harder than the 23 hours of hard labor i had 32 years ago. i was strapped to the gurney and couldn't breathe deeply because of the pain. i sat in the walk way of the er department for 3 hours in pain and also unable to move my legs. there were people being brought in by ambulance for cold and blood pressure issues and soon they were taken to a room where soon their families (more than 4 people) arrived and started eating and talking as their sick family member was laughing on the hospital bed) i was in tears in pain and they were just taking up space. when i finally got to a bed my back and legs cramped badly, but my pain i was experiencing was gone. the nurse katie came in and hooked me up to bp and oxmeter and left. another hour went by. i got up and went to the nurses counter and told them i wanted to leave asap and informed the nurse i waited on an ambulance gurney for 3 hours and hospi8tal bed for another hour and no doctor. she asked me what room i was in and i told her, she got the nurse and she asked me what was wrong. i told her that i was no longer in pain that i came into the er dept. for, but was experiencing leg and back pain from being strapped down for 3 hours and i want to go because i dont need help. she then left me to get the doctor. i told him what i went through. he said he needed to call urology to see if any other treatment was needed. ugh! i got no pain medication, just labs and urine and i have an infection, duh! im on antibiotics! my husband asked the doctor why i wasnt seen when i got to the er room. why??? when my fever hit 104, i decided it was time to go to the er. i had an overall positive experience in the gw emergency room. the wait was not too long, and i left within a few hours, feeling much better. 

pros: 

short wait times--it was not too busy when i was there, and the folks there seemed to have a good process for moving patients through the registration and care processes 

patient care: i received care which left me feeling much better, quickly. i felt that the nurses and doctors knew what they were doing, and effectively executed. there was a student shadowing the doctor as well, and he was very respectful and kind. 

clean: the facility looked clean and organized. i felt comfortable in the curtained-off area i was placed in.

cost: not overwhelming. for a diagnosis of flu, strep and dehydration -- (flu and strep test and 2 hour iv treatment), i paid close to $400- with comprehensive insurance, and having met my deductible 

cons: 

patient in-take: folks were overall extremely nice, and made jokes and though one lady repeatedly questioned whether i had gotten a temperature reading of 104, in a way that put me off a little-her tone and demeanor was seemingly implying i was exaggerating or fabricating this. by the time i was seen, my temperature was much lower, so i understand her skepticism to a degree, but it didn't feel great to be doubted when i already felt so bad.


additional: i thought that the nurses/docs could have been a bit more interactive with me. though i'm aware my case was not serious comparatively, the er was pretty empty, so i thought that the doctor/nurse could have checked on me a couple more times than they did. overall not bad here, but could do with a little improvement

of course, no one ever wants to need a psych hospital for their child, but it's good to know that safe places are available, if needed. we adopted a young teen who's been in the foster care system since he was 6, after sustaining significant trauma. he works really hard but needs extra help sometimes. 
the nurses and direct care staff at austin oaks are very caring and compassionate. they were kind to him, no matter how disregulated he became. they crafted a very unique program to address his special needs, even arranging for extra staff to insure safety.
the clinical director,  molly wang, was amazing. she really went out of her way to insure that our son would have the ongoing support he needed after his hospitalization.... meeting with us,  calling other providers, advocating for him to be able to stay long enough to stabilize. she was very approachable and supportive, and we truly felt like she was part of our team. our only concern was with the psychiatrist,  who made drastic changes to our son's medication regimen without talking to us (or his longterm psychiatrist, even though we'd signed a release). the med changes really exacerbated the problems that had brought him to the hospital in the first place. fortunately,  that psychiatrist is no longer with the inpatient division, and our son's doctors are working to get his medications back into the therapeutic range.
if you must seek out acute psychiatric care for your child, know that they will be well cared for at austin oaks.

the blake medical center has an in-house hospital rehab center located on the 2nd floor of blake hospital, a dedicated wing for rehab patients. my dad went there after an eleven-day hospitalization stay for a punctured lung and broken ribs. at age 96, he wanted to be at home rather than rehab, but as he began his rehab stay of 8 days, he realized this rigorous program was doing him a world of good! he came away from the experience more knowledgeable and stronger than ever!

if patients get approval from the nursing staff, they can ride the elevator to the courtyard with family! a little fresh air and green space is healthy for healing! the staff on the rehab floor is kind to the whole family and involves them in the healing process, whenever possible. 

nurses and doctors quickly attend to patients' needs and, importantly, are sympathetic and understanding to their well-being. my dad's rehab was a four-piece collaboration between nursing and doctor care, physical therapy, occupational therapy, and patient's desire to get better. dad's therapy was rigorous - 4 times a day. we could observe his therapy sessions, which we did a couple of times. the ot and pt gave us helpful hints to use at home. he gained great confidence and strength during his rehab stay!

menu choices are very appealing and arrive to the patient on time - fresh and hot! he enjoyed his meals very much, especially the chocolate cake and the carrot cake. 

this rehab hospital is outstanding in every way! the rehab program couldn't be any better!!!

review:
well, i don't like leaving negative reviews but this experience was really just inappropriate. i went in to the er with kind of a slew of symptoms as i've been sick for about 6 months. i try not to be difficult as i understand that being a triage doctor is no easy task. but the doc that i saw in triage kept laughing at me whenever i answered his questions. i came in with severe chest pain and was having trouble taking a deep breathe and was quite scared. he made fun of me because i told him i didn't want a chest x-ray and then pushed it on me. after that, he insisted that i was probably pregnant. now i know that a pregnancy test in the er is pretty standard, but he really kept insinuating that my chest pain could be related to pregnancy. and made fun of me when i told him that i wasn't. he could have just said that it was a test they do before an x-ray or literally anything other than respond by laughing and condescending to me. the test was negative. 
once i got to a bed my new doc was so nice and really explained everything well. told me i needed an mri of my neck, as i hadn't been able to eat for two days and that i could do that outside of the er. i was really relieved that i was okay and could leave. but when the woman came with my discharge papers, she got upset that i had a passport instead of drivers license and then said that i didn't meet my deductible so i needed to pay up front. i asked if my insurance could bill me and she laughed and said, "obviously, and it's going to be a lot because you didn't meet your deductible." my boyfriend was in the room and asked out of curiosity what the deductible was and the woman yelled, "she's not even sick!" and just left. 
if it had just been the first doc that kept laughing at me i wouldn't have written this. but there's just really no need to treat people this way. i understand how hard and taxing those jobs are. my whole family works in the medical field and my sis is a nurse. but i was quiet, respectful, and never complained. but no matter what i did i got quite awful treatment that honestly had me leave in tears.
working at an er is stressful. but people are at their most vulnerable when they come into one and should be treated with at least some decency.

piedmont has some practices that are the exception and not the rule when it comes to childbirth, and it cost me thousands out of pocket. 

i just received another $2,600 bill for myself and $1,800 bill for charlie for delivering my child. this brings my total 2019 oop expenses to over $23k ($750/mo in premiums--with the other $750 paid by my employer, fyi, and $7,900 max oop costs each for me and my child, in network).

expectant mothers:

*piedmont is the only local hospital that considers your child an independent person on insurance the moment they are born. this means a new deductible, co-pays, and coinsurance for that child the moment they leave your body. we are now at over $5k in oop expenses for the baby alone for standard care over 2 days (she had no problems). all other local hospitals bill the child as part of "you" for the first 30 days of life.

*ask to be told every single time--in advance of being provided non-emergency care--if the following people providing your care are in-network under your hospital or are being pulled in from an outside vendor, then check with your insurance on whether they are in your network before you see this person. this includes nurses, your doctors, anesthesiologists, pediatricians, nursery staff, specialists, and pediatricians.

*i'd suggest you request your vitals only be checked once a day, not every time a nurse changes shift. every entry into the room is a charge of multiple hundreds of dollars. change your own linens and have family bring you food, don't eat the hospital's food. request to take your own medicines and bring them. e.g. your own prescriptions, motrin (they will try to give you a drip and then will charge you $30 each time), etc. be extremely clear and demand that you give yourself those medications you brought as long as the nurse witnesses it - do not let them put them in a cup for you. basically - avoid any care that feels superfluous. they (meaning piedmont, not the medical professionals) are doing it to add to your bill.

*for any non-vital services, refuse them. e.g. some random person comes in to ask how your experience is.

*make notes or have your family make notes of every single name of every single person who walks into your room in a medical capacity, or if the baby is wheeled out, who touches them in the nursery. take notes of how many times and for how many hours, on what days, your child is in the nursery. note all services provided.

*do the same for yourself. every time your vitals are checked, bedding is changed, food is delivered, etc. (if applicable). ask for an itemized list when you leave. they only keep these records in l&d for 30 days, and your bills will come after that. 

*demand to be consulted in advance of any paperwork being filed on your behalf beyond nursing notes and notes from only doctors you have personally seen. yes, i'm serious. i got charged $351 for a doctor i had not seen "putting a nurse's notes" in another document i've never seen.

*ask before you go into labor for a list or detail of services typically provided for women giving vaginal or standard c-section birth and what the self-pay rates are so you can decide if you want to not send specific pieces through insurance or not. if you can afford it, consider self-pay regardless and submit a claim to insurance if expenses end up adding up to more than you predicted. do this with your ob as well. call your insurance company to compare. be prepared to pay your max oop costs for you and your child - unless you work with someone out of network, which will be extra.

i'd suggest you mail these logged notes to yourself in a sealed envelope the day you are discharged from the hospital, and also file copies with the billing dpt of the hospital and your insurance immediately upon release.

when you argue about this, you are told you "should have checked" whether someone was in network before you saw them. this process is all 100% legal.

let's face it. hospitals in america are no longer about patients. they are about $$ and keeping shareholders happy. we don't have the best medical system in the world. we have a greedy, for-profit corporate industry that fleeces americans with high-costs and third-world patient care. glenbrook hospital is just another one. 

you won't have any doctor-patient/family interaction here. the doctors are god  - invisible to the lowly, sick and suffering. they speak only through their angels (nurses) to patients and their family.  there are no smiles or happiness by the staff - only the typical condescending arrogance of those who work in the medical profession. 

there is no method of communication here - only madness and frustration because, again, the glenbrook north doctor gods cannot be bothered. 

you will end up shouting in frustration at nurses who are not responsible for why the corporate method of caring for sick human beings simply does not work. then you will feel bad and apologize, even though you did nothing wrong. the people who are wrong are simply invisible. they sit in boardrooms, accounting firms, and doctor heaven. 

i always laugh when people condemn countries with national healthcare because it's "bad and has long waits." visit any us hospital like glenbrook north and there listerally no way anything can be worse. it's just more expensive. 

i have lived in other states and i've lived overseas. american hospitals are declining in every area of patient care while the costs are skyrocketing. 

glenbrook hospital is just a rubber stamp of other corporate-owned us hospitals. i have had better care in europe and it's cost me so little. the people who argue that it's not have never been anywhere but a us hospital.
