this place has the most efficient admissions system i have ever seen.  when you feel bad or are going to the hospital, you don't need extra aggravation!  both times it took 5 minutes to be on the way to a room or radiology.  the care was good and people nice.  the facility is up to date, for the most part.  the equipment t is up to date, for the most orr

this hospital caters to military active duty, family members and retirees and their dependents. it's a very big facility. the staff is really friendly. they have ambassadors that help guide you in case you're not sure where you're going or if you don't have the time to figure out where you are to get to your appointment on time. although, they're only there during regular hours. i think if you come after 6pm. it's basically just the specialty clinics and er that's open. it's essentially a ghost town so make sure you know exactly where you're going. i had to walk around the whole building trying to find the radiology/mri clinic. there's a self-serve check-in process in this specific clinic (sort of) and you have to call to make sure they know you're there. otherwise, you'll be waiting around and they're not going to come out unless you call them. 

i also came in here to get some blood drawn. the staff at the front desk weren't so helpful- kind of rude to be honest. they know people are waiting to get checked in but they're just sitting around lounging and chatting up with each other. 

they have a nice open area in the main entrance with a large staircase that takes you to the second floor. there's a grand piano by the lobby that sometimes gets played by one of the staff members. their pharmacy is huge but the wait is just as bad anywhere so be prepared if you're going to pick up your medications here. they also have a chapel and offer services to the staff and patients alike.

they have a dining area in the top floor where you can get decent lunch at a very low cost. there's also a starbucks and a small convenient store where you can get drinks and snacks and maybe pick up some last minute card, flowers or gifts. 

all in all - i think the staff could be better. maybe their supervisors/administrators can walk around more and see how their staff are treating the patients. have a better feedback system. i want to give them more stars because they cater to the military, but honestly, they could do better.

i had a mri done there and was billed $8,556.70.  there is no reason for a procedure to cost this much and there are other places in the surrounding area where you can get it done cheaper.  i think it's awful that the cancer patients already paying unreasonable amounts for health care are being charged obscene amounts for mri's.  so my suggestion is to shop around for the best price.  i'm sure you will be able to locate one a lot cheaper than here.
you are your only advocate. this place is really hit or miss. we h by abe had both good and really bad experiences.

not the best place to spend a friday night but i will say the staff was great and if i had to be in a er i was glad to be in east stroudsburg and not in nyc. thank you for taking care of us with zero wait. zero drama.

we waited for 3 hours to talk to the doctor, or resident, taking care of my mother in law.  we know the (excellent) nurse called the doctor twice to let him know we were there and waiting.  he/she never came.  not impressed. uw should do better if it wants to keep any sort of good reputation, and find doctors willing to talk to family members.  i would give the nurses 5 stars.

requested medical records from 5 clinics or hospitals to be transferred to another medical facility.  only 1 charged for 8 pages of records.  uw.  $5.37 including tax.  amount is not the question some of the others were transferring 100 pages and cds no charge, they don't use their own name but send bill under ciox.

i was sent to uw hospital from urgent care on nov 19th to get an ultrasound for what turned out to be a calf strain that they thought might be an achilles issue. i was told by the triage nurse at about 9:15pm that she was going to go tell the ultrasound folks to get ready. i was finally brought back at 11:45pm. at 12:15am, the resident doctor told me they don't do ultrasounds overnight. i cried. i asked for discharge papers. that was the only reason i had come and i was very clear with the front desk and the triage nurse. they convinced me they could clinically diagnose the issue. i talked to the resident doctor who said it was a calf strain, the attending doctor who said it was an achilles problem, and finally at around 1:30am i was seen by the orthotech who said it was probably a calf strain. i was discharged at 2am. more confused than ever. since then, i've tried to  work with patient relations two times to get the charges reversed. if they'd have been honest when i checked in that the ultrasounds aren't done overnight, i would have gone home and gotten a good night's sleep. i'm a single mom and had to get a friend to stay with my kids overnight. i had to get up early in the morning to get my kids to school and missed half a day of work trying to catch up on sleep. for what? for more confusion and a huge hospital bill. i would recommend never going to this hospital, unless you are truly dying and, in that case, good luck. they didn't seem to talk to each other or know what the other was doing at all. at one point, i was wheeled to the bathroom and abandoned, even when i used the intercom system, it took 5 minutes for someone to answer. pretty bad situation for an emergency room.

i would like to start by saying thank you for saving me and loving what you do. my review is for the labor and delivery. i gave birth to my son here back in august 2019 and it was the best care i ever received!! from the moment i got in and settled my nurse was helpful and so caring even playing with my 5 year old daughter!! made my husband super comfortable! 

night time came and i got a new nurse, i believe her name was katherine or something along that line, super short hair and amazing!! she made me and my family so comfortable! she was simply amazing, caring and loving. she did a great job helping me with labor, pushing, etc. i felt like my mother was in the room that's how amazing she was! gave birth to my beautiful son all good. 

now here comes the scary part, i had postpartum hemorrhage and honestly i was thinking the worst and was so scared i was gonna die and not be able to be with my family... it was the worst and most scary thing i've  ever been through. the moment they rushed me back to labor and delivery i remember just being in the elevator asking the nurses if i was gonna be okay and she responded ""you're in the #1 hospital for trauma i promise we will take care of you" we get to the same room i delivered in and i was asked to get on the smaller bed because they needed to sweep the clots out my uterus. i stood up and the biggest clot came out and the man who did the sweep told me "we can't waste anymore time let's get started" the girls were each on one side of me and the man did the sweep using the ultrasound machine to make sure they got em all. it was so scary. then my nurse susie came omg love her!!! she was so amazing and the whole time i was  crying an emotional wreck, asking if i'd be okay to go home with my family she kept assuring me i will be okay. with my daughter husband and newborn in the room all i did was pray  so hard. susie was beyond amazing. i learned that she lived about an  hour away and still came to work everyday. she gave me proper medicine, kept measuring my clots and assuu ring me i will be okay. i couldn't have been more at ease with her. 

katherine came up to see me that same night she came in before she started work to chat with me and check on me. lord i believe  was her name took care of me in mom and baby unit. she was amazing and made me feel so great  and at home! she went above and beyond for me!! 

my son had shoulder dystocia and jaundice he had to stay there you believe the  hospital let me stay in my room until he was discharged? 

thank you to your caring, loving, well trained staff for making me feel comfortable, having a  send of assurance and everything they did for me!! 

not only did they save my life, they were family as well. thank you for saving me to allow me to be here with my family. god bless
thank you dr. daniel hammond! my ha1c has never been better! now i can live forever!

terrible service. front desk nurses & staff at er we're so unbelievably snarky/ rude. they were making jokes to me as i stood there vomiting. waited for 2 hours as my appendix was bursting. ended up leaving & going to rose hospital instead (who got me into a room immediately). i will never come back here again. if you have a legitimate emergency, go to another hospital. gross

bewarbrought my son and daughter to urgent care.  diagnosed with strep.  my kids shared a room and were out of there in 30mins.  i now owe $600 for each child...$300 for the room and $300 for the doctor.  wtf!  go to carenow for urgent care visits.  
*update* denver health reached out to me but there was no resolution and no one was willing to assist me.  i still owed $1,200.

i was a recent patient on the fourth floor adult psych. almost all of the staff--drs. to techs--were very kind and caring. i felt they truly cared and wanted me to get better. dr. medlin was particularly helpful and gave me specific techniques to help rather than just "use your coping skills".  i think if we could have worked together for even just a few more days i'd be feeling even closer to stable/baseline. the groups were mostly well prepared. the nursing groups were a bit scattered. the best group was maria's music group. the biggest draw back was therapy dogs. i very much do not care for dogs. i'd return to them again if necessary.

been there twice and both times was the worst hospital time ever. rude front desk, mean nurses and everyone else running around with their heads cuts off. was given the wrong meds thru iv once and thought my arm was gonna fall off. very slow at helping and even if you're screaming in pain they will snap at you but they are the ones taking so long and socializing in the hall.
they never helped my conditions and made my life worse. its a drag to go to the doctors and i avoid as much as i can. and the nurse line is a piece of shit. i hate what you did to me.

i wish we had another option! the staff is rude and also will bump you if yoo-hoo knew them. no ethics or courtesy for families with sick children!
apparently a two year old it's possible flu and 102.4 fever is not serious enough and will make you wait longer is you ask or complain!
they need to check their front desk and triage staff for ethical practice

i had an accident last year where i lost my fingertip, it got caught in a door that the wind blew shut which removed the tip from the base of the fingernail. i went to this hospital, it was around midnight, and i had to wait 3 hours to see the doctor although no one appeared to be there. it was extremely painful and psychologically traumatic, yet the staff didn't seem very caring, and it took around 2 hours to get a shot for the excruciating pain. the shot was something called hydromorphone, formulated to not get people "high".
if ever there was a time a person needs to be a little bit high, it's when you have had a fingertip torn off. i have no history of drug abuse, though i understand we are all suspects due to the drug problem.
3 hours after i got there, i was given a shot in my hand which finally relieved the pain, if briefly, so the doctor could look at it and clean it up. after that a wonderful nurse wrapped it, and showed me how to do so which turned out to be a real blessing, as it had turned out my insurance had been cancelled shortly before though i didn't know, and i was not able to see a doctor afterwards because of that.
the doctor came in again, and gave me 2 percocet pills to take home with me (that helped much more than the worthless shot) so i could have something to take before seeing a doctor the next day, though as i soon found out, due to a glitch in my insurance took 3 weeks for one to see me. thank god a friend had some kratom which she gave me, and between that and tylenol pills i was able to somewhat manage the pain.
we should not be punished because of the drug issue, especially with a chopped off fingertip, the pain issue should have been addressed better. 
the 2 stars i do give was for the very nice nurse who bandaged my finger and showed me how to do it and what materials i needed.
i don't understand why i had to wait hours though when no one was there.
if i have an emergency again, i will try to have it taken care of in olympia instead if possible.

i spent 9 days recovering at the main st. joseph hospital. recently after my mother passed away from metastatic stage 4 colon cancer, i became ill  at work, taken by ambulance to the nearest hospital. grant you, i will say it took a couple of days to determine the root cause of my painful problem which was a little too long. they thought it  was gall  bladder related which also is a problem i have but where the pain was stemming from a pelvic scan should've also taken place because one night with the severe agony of pain and being that no form of morphine orr without pain meds  their higher doses of pain meds was not stopping  it should have red flagged the er and hospital doctors.  the doctors i feel could improve on connecting with their patients more. with the epidemic of burnout within the staff especially the doctors, it's easy to find themselves disconnected,  quick to categorize and set you aside. the need to visit their patients more in the evening as that's when the worse begins. if it wasn't for my empathetic and smart nurse, diane, to help me with the pain, encouragement through the night and strongly advocating for me to the doctors while unable to  talk and delirious from the pain.... i'm not sure if i would've made it.  she deserves a daisy award for going above and beyond, pushing the envelope so the doctor would listen. finally, a hida scan later, they ordered a pelvic scan and found a huge mass and cyst  on my ovaries  plus one terribly contorted ovary. after the emergency surgery- -what should have resolved everything- i was still in pain especially after i ate which was liquids and that same day i was already on solids which maybe had a little spoonful of mashed potatoes. i would just take a sip of water then this terrible pain that doubled me over would wave through me. the pcp thought it was normal at first and maybe thought i just was a light weight to the normal pain. the nurse(s) knee something was off and again advocated for further review. finally after about a day of this type of gut wrenching pain, constant push from my husband and nurse, and finally witnessing my extreme pain  in action (mind you i was super pale and my temp low) the dr ordered stomach scan to find an obstruction intestinal ileus which in nutshell my intestines were in shock and not working so the food is not moving. needless to say, they tried 4 times to put this gastric nasal tube through my nose but ended downstairs where they had to put a bigger tube up my nose while experiencing gastric spasms in the x-ray (hope i got the dept right)department which i to say was super friendly and staff is super supportive.  i had over 20 nurses total caring for me including the technicians which would make sure to wash me and push me to get moving when i finally could which sometimes get on my nerves but that's because i became so depressed too. thank you for doing that- encouragement and keeping me clean, keeping the room super clean and letting me have my hubs and dad with me. putting up with my dad. taking me for those walks to fight it and get these tubes out of my nose. to get better.  thank you for all your care and time. thank you  for the meditation exercises at first was a little negative but it really helped. i loved that i got visited by the dog and for some reason that visit  made me cry, releasing my sadness over losing my mom and fear of my situation. my recommendation is for better follow up pcp visits to be made available through the hospital especially with this type of surgery and intestinal issues after discharge because regular pcps or gastro doctors will not touch you. i'm not sure if it's a fear of medical liability but no one would do a follow up  and they refer me back to have the hospital doctors or gi surgeon that was caring over me during that time. thankfully my ob/gyn, dr. sheldon from woman's care, did not do that instead made sure to have me come in and check that there was no water or whatever residual. she has kept a good follow up in place with me. i've found  the gi medical doctors or surgeon teams are not the same way. other factors outweigh patient care first, sadly.  however thank you again to the 7east nurses!!

review: i have never posted on yelp before and this my first review. this hospital is amazing!! went to loma linda  urgent care for my 6 month old son  having trouble breathing. after examination, started turning a little blue and doctor called an ambulance to take him to loma linda pediatric er. (note: if your child is sick, call 911 and get an ambulance. ambulance er visits get them to the front of the line immediately.) after in pediatric er having breathing treatments, he was diagnostic with rst, bronculitis, and one other virus i can't remember. the pediatric er is small, crowded , loud and will make you very irritated. hang in there. the staff know what they are doing and make quick decisions. once my son was diagnosed, they wanted to admit him to pediatric icu for his condition. i thought it was ridiculous that he would need that level of care because he was alert and giggling with his toys. i was wrong. after admission, he was on oxygen. then he got dehydrated from not eating and had to go on baby cpap machine. almost went to tube breathing on a ventilator but he improved slightly. he got a lot worse before he started to improve. the staff at the pediatric icu were amazing. very attentitive, very informative, and constantly checked in on him. children have died from these viruses and i believe that loma linda pediatric icu saved his life. please go to pediatric er and get admitted if your child is sick. remember to take an ambulance ride. worth the money to be at the front of the line.

this message is for the owner of the hospital, i'm an ex employee that use to work for loma linda security department. i've seen so much corruption, racism, and hippa violations from  all your security staff! i've seen the way that my security coworkers treat patients! excessive force & racism is what loma linda security department delivers and it makes me sick to my stomach! i've tried reaching out to hr and i haven't even received a call back! i promise my voice will be heard & people will know the truth!! my civil rights were violated here!!! that i'm aware of i have 365 days to find the right lawyer. and yes i will be reaching out to cbs news! ow & security staff makes fun of deceased children & children that are on 5150 holds! and also security staff makes fun of donated deceased bodies that are located at the centennial building! 

i quit this job that paid me 17.85 an hour!! not all people are crooked & have a heart! i'm not going to try to fit in and become one of them, a crooked employee that is!

honestly this has got too be the worst hospital to ever go to. if you are dying i still recommend going elsewhere. these assholes are making my life a living hell. i can't explain why. but they are making a bigg mistake in what they are doing. straight jump to conclusions. also went to emergency room and waited 8 hours too be seen. do not go here!!!!

the night peds floor on 4200'is beyond rude! the nurses do nothing you have to ask for pain peds for your children instead of them staying on top of it. they are loud all night long and the change of shift is ridiculous! this children are sick and need to try and get rest, and when you are being beyond inconsiderate, loud, rude, no empathy, how can anyone rest???? 

update: we have now been here several days and it's just gotten worse and worse! i am not happy with this hospital and i would never bring  another child here ever! we will go to choc or another hospital!!! this place is horrible! i have not one  good thing to say except we have had a few kind nurses!

pediatric er. kind of a joke. tbh go somewhere else. my niece went here a few months ago she was super sick. they barely cared for her said it was a upper respiratory infection and it would go away, well her mom took her somewhere else and she had bronchitis.  then i took my 2month to her dr. he said go to loma linda er. i asked if i could just do redlands er he said no. so i went here. such a joke waiting room is tiny. half is outside (it was cold and rainy) then the nurses don't even know correct medical information.... told me a high fever in infants is ok. (no it's not 102.8 is not ok and climbing) also her heartrate was at 180 (lowest it went to) to 220 (highest) it jumped in between these, they said it was fine. her labored breathing they said was also fine. and with no test except a uti check (so dumb and the nurse did it 3x and couldn't find it so we told her either another nurse try or they aren't doing this, fucking ridiculous so uncalled for if u ask me.) they sent us home with the diagnosis upper respiratory infection....then my lil sis asked if they swabbed her and tested it to be sure. no they didn't. i even told em i wanted her tested for flu and stuff just to be sure. they didn't want to. so today. her fever isn't as high, she still has labored breathing and congestion. and she has only eaten 2-3x (breastfeed) and all she is doing is sleeping. my poor princess. if she's not better i'm taking her to redlands er tomorrow. just ridiculous how they just shrug off such a lil baby who has an extremely high heart rate, labored breathing and congestion they couldn't even suck out. ‍ don't waste your time.

omg also wanna add the fact a child that was quarantined.....was using same bathroom as we were told to use. just doesn't seem like a great idea, he's quarantined for a reason he shouldn't be using the same bathroom, he should have his own. just uncomfortable!

a one star is put just because i have too in order for this to be process but let me tell you it's by far the worse hospital for a mother who was seeking help for her son....i took my son in with a fever of 103.7, vomiting blood, a super dry cough, body ache, and drowsy eyes along pink eyes, & after being there 12 hours just to see the doctor for twenty minutes top that off i get send with home tylenol and ibuprofen medicine that i can easily purchase over the counter like really...then they do a follow up call just to say oh sorry you can bring him in and we can double check him for what so i can be there again for 12 more hours. if any manager is reading this i hope your not a parent because i can't  stand my son being in pain and after 7 days he is only getting worse. but thanks to the help of another hospital and his pediatric  i'm hoping to see him better!

i've checked in my son at 1pm it is now 6pm and we still have not been seen. we are here for my sons arm .. i physically can see his arm is broken and we have yet to be seen. i've paid his $200 copayment for the er and all we have done is sat in the waiting room and freeze. they have both front er doors wide open and letting the cold air come through.. they have poor babies that have been coughing and crying because they are in pain. they have the elderly constantly getting out of wheel chairs to take vitals signs. this er needs a new system and this was my first and it will be my last time i come here.

this review is several experiences first with my best friend who had an eye infection and was going to be blind if not treated  went to miami 7 times they saved his eye sight ,he is on medacade and has no money  they treat everyone  weather you have the ability to pay or not . if its a true medical emergency .

review:
this review is mainly for the icu west tower

this place is huge and i think it's a new wing. so be careful when get the address. and, depending where you park will determine how far a walk you will have to take. makes all the difference if you're with elderly or handicap family members. 

as far as care. the icu has a friendly staff. very respectful and kind. and, know their stuff. i'm very happy that my brother is being well cared for there right now. 

never too fun whenever anyone is in the hospital. but, comforting knowing that the drs & nurses are professional & passionate.

again. this is based on our family personal experience. for others the experience might be total opposite.

i am really trying to like this hospital but it is horrible we are in the er room with my father and people are leaving there beds and going home beacuse no one is helping we have been here for 7 hours and we still don't know what is going on , no one says anything they keep looking for a doctor that did some test on my dad and they can't find him the nurse is asking me what is going on what a nightmare

i've had to go to their emergency room for 15 years and the staff has always been knowledgeable and considerate.  i live in shirley and it is the closest hospital.  the only complaint that i have about those visits (bladder infections, migraines, or asthma attack) is once by ambulance with no way to get home.  i've used them for x-rays to avoid going over to leominster hospital.  still, every time i've been to nashoba late at night there are a lot of drug overdose cases that come in.  i didn't know that we had that much of a drug crises around here, but we do.  with all that going on they do their job.  i have no complaints about any other procedures, such as pt, medical records.  everyone is courteous.

so i found out the day after christmas that the baby that i'm pregnant with had no heartbeat.  while i tried to naturally induce the miscarriage my body wasn't cooperating and the thought of going to bed with a corpse inside of me was tearing me apart. so i called nashoba valley to ask if they had misoprostal available. i couldn't remember the name so i asked for the "abortion pill.   the woman on the phone, directly after telling her that i just learned that my baby was dead, responded to me in the absolute most condescending tone as if she was annoyed by my stupid question. "uuuuuh no..... those pills are for after you have sex. that won't do anything."       

that level of beside manner alone was enough for me.    i don't see myself ever walking in their if they are that inconsiderate and rude. after i explained to her that i was not looking for plan b but something to induce contractions so i could actually complete miscarrying she  suggested planned parenthood.      fine. however, she didn't handle that call right -at all-.
this hospital should be closed  all about the money  medicaid should review it drs are not qualified

the experience here couldn't have went any better. we brought our little guy in for them to diagnose an issue with his wrist. security here is comprehensive, the pa and attending staff were great, and they got us in and out reasonably quickly. that said we came as early as we could and were one of the first families through the door at around 9 on a sunday morning. this place was world-class!
fac_name: Golisano Children's Hospital of Southwest Florida

review: i am incredibly disappointed in the "care" my husband is/isn't receiving. thank god i'm here through the night to take care of him and get him to the bathroom or he'd have been on his own, no vitals being taken, his fever spiked through the night to 104! i had to go find a nurse to tell them he was burning up. we've seen 3 different doctors, none of whom talked or communicated between them, i have to retell his heath history and current issues every time, to every person that comes in the room. his regular specialist still hasn't been contacted or consulted and i'm ready to just pack him up and walk out the front doors and drive to the university of utah. i earned a helluva paycheck here, and they'll want 6 months worth of my husbands paycheck for this unwelcome hospital stay. and just a side note i am not an asshole! i totally get nurses can be overworked and most of them are absolutely amazing, my point is, that has not been my experience at this hospital. one star  . and that star is only because i can make a badass pot of coffee or hot chocky due to the fact they provide a small galley kitchen for others like me taking care of their loved ones.. so.. ya. that's cool. but not cool enough to make up for poor care of my sick loved one. one star. do not recommend.

had a wonderful experience at this hospital. we brought our teenage daughter in for what we thought was an appendicitis and the nurses and staff were sweet and wonderful. her doctor was john hughes, so nice and best of all sympathetic with an awesome bedside manner. our daughter was well cared for and treated so nicely. we'll be coming here for all our emergency needs from now on. hopefully not too soon though hahaha.

high security at memorial south hospital . i had to answer a few questions on paper ,use hand sanitiser and then i could register for my mamogram appointment . 

at the imaging center i was given a gown and robe  and told to wait at the seating area which had refreshments . 

i only waited about five minutes before i had my image taken . i asked for the thyroid guard as my thyroid is on the blink . the exam was taken by a very gentile lady and  my breast were flatten in this devise . lucky for me this time i did not scream. 

all seems good as i was told i can go and will be given results by mail.

would i come back here again , the answer is a big yes . parking is easy , staff is great . i'm a happy lady.

i went to the imaging center this week for two screenings. it was not crowded like it can be in october and november. i was able to get in/out in an hour, and not enough time to get lost in a book. great job ladies from check in to getting results.

this is the 2nd time we have had to come here and both times have encountered great people. staff that are courteous and polite. these people are so nice, friendly and always at the ready to answer a question and meet a need. the doctors are experienced & knowledgeable with great bedside manners. the office is clean through and through. the pre surgery prep area is also very clean and detailed. it is so efficiently run, impressive. 
the waiting area is great, they even make fresh pots of coffee all day, along with a tea kettle running for tea drinkers. there is a cafeteria and also a subway café inside the hospital that are not bad.
there is a free parking lot across the street and they also offer valet parking. 
if needed, hope not, but if, this place will be great.

i would give zero stars if that were an option.  dr. agarwal is absolutely the most arrogant physician i've ever seen, and i have ulcerative colitis, and advanced stage primary sclerosing cholangitis, so i've seen a lot of doctors.  i've been told by my gastroenterologist that when i'm having a flare up, i need to go to the er to be checked out, as my disease can be fatal.  i've been made to feel like i'm a med seeker (addict), and i'm far from that!!!!  i received a letter from the higher ups in that hospital, and was basically told to pound sand.  i know i'm not the only person to give poor reviews to dr. agarwal, because i've seen another, and their story was like mine.  do not go to this hospital.  they don't care about their patients!!!

i had my baby at good sam. everyone was top notch-  nurses, drs, cafeteria workers... everyone! our stay was longer than expected but my suggest and i both left healthy.  this might not have been the case without the diligence of the staff. we are forever grateful to god sam. the hospital will be even better once the facilities are updated. this is the best place in cincinnati to have a baby

i just went to the er for migraine treatment. we pre registered online and when we arrived they brought me right in. they already had a quiet, dark room waiting for me. the nurse quietly put in my iv on the first stick, i barely felt it and he was so quick even though i am generally a hard stick for an iv and especially when i am dehydrated from throwing up. they got my fluids up and running before the doctor came in. i told him what actually works for my migraines and even though it's a new and fairly 
controversial treatment he immediately agreed to do it to get me help. 15 minutes later my infusion was running, the nurse and intake coordinator, and doctor were all very compassionate and cared about my well being. 
it was clean and quiet and a quick experience. in 25 years of horrible migraines and nightmare er visits this was by far the easiest most efficient hospital i've ever dealt with and i was in and out and very well treated in under 2.5 hours. i was impressed to say the very least. hopefully i won't have to go back again but if i do i know where i'd go,
fac_name: Ascension NE Wisconsin St. Elizabeth Hospital

review:
great stop for emergency or urgent care,  which is all they do here. you are generally processed quickly and wait very little, unless it is a busy time. 

doctors seem attentive and knowledgeable. i have had only one visit with a doctor when came in with a terrible migraine. had to explain my entire life history of migraine. i explained what i generally get when at the hospital. doctor said they do things different there. i wasn't sure what he meant by that. they said no narcotics for migraine and then they gave me morphine. apparently they don't know about that drug. morphine is a useless drug for migraine, whereby it's side effects are the worst and the medicine wears off fast, which it did for my visit. i came in one day with a terrible and was out in 90 minutes, loaded with migraine. the medicine wore out 30 minutes later. the migraine resumed.
terrible. long waits. rude doctors, many changes. just go anywhere else. i went here over ten years and it's just not what it was once.

i came to visit a family friend who had just been admitted and needed rehabilitation.  the place is beautiful.  it is very state of the art and the staff is welcoming, professional and attentive.  during my visit, the staff was always readily available to the patients and checked in every half hour or so.  

they provide a wide variety of activities for the patients which include music, trivia and arts and crafts which is a major plus because one can get board while recuperating without any capability of getting up and moving around by themselves.  also, the volunteers *huge shout to the volunteers* because not everyone is fortunate to have family, loved ones and friends to visit.  there were a group of them that went room to room to check on the patients.  

some actually came to collect the patients to get them out of their beds for a while.  a very crucial part of healing and rehabilitation is support from other caring individuals.  

this rehab facility is exemplary and the staff takes pride in providing care which is demonstrated in their bedside manner.  highly recommended facility.  i feel comfortable and confident that my family friend is getting the best care and that she will recover nicely.
an absolute and total nightmare. 0 stars, do everything you can to avoid this place if you value your health and that of your family.

this is specifically for the ct room. i've been to this location a couple of times and i can say that this is the worst location for nyp.
when i called to make an appointment last week, no one picked up. after repeated attempts throughout the day, some guy finally picked up and was extremely disorganized.  

it's a freaking maze here while the other locations are straight forward. had an appointment at 8am, after filling out the paperwork, they didn't provide the oral contrast until 9am, with the second serving at 10am. this whole time that i was waiting, they could've provided this. the ct scan took only a few minutes, yet i didn't leave until 12:30 pm. while the staff is friendly and in good spirits, this is an completely unacceptable wait time. i don't recommend this location at all.

while once trying to fly out of new york city to las vegas (don't ask), i cut my foot in a delta terminal at jfk. 

i was bleeding pretty bad. delta/jfk didn't have the proper emergency kit available (no offense to them -- this was ancient history -- way back in 2017). an american ambulance would of cost over $1000, so a cabbie kindly dropped me off here. 

aghast, i found myself lying on a stained mattress (think all body fluids) to simply be *prescribed* aleve and then charged bankrupting american emergency room fees with insurance. i would of been ok with brush-off service, because in all fairness, in true triage, i was not dying -- but wow someone obviously died on the mattress right before me that i was put on...it was horrifying to be placed on top of so many stains. it must of been more horrifying for the person before me. 

until it is 1863 again, i am not returning.

this review is for "advanced womens imaging" who could've resulted in me having a stillbirth! oh my god! 

i was referred to here by a list from a private ob who doesn't do sono's in office. i thought it made sense to come because i am delivering here. 85% of their patients are from the clinic across the street and yes expect to wait 3 hours at least from your appointment time, there werent even chairs they were so over booked and we had women who were over 30 something weeks pregnant standing. i had my first sonogram here at almost 13 weeks. both abdominal and transvaginal.

my ob doesn't order many sonograms, but i told him i'd feel comfortable having one once a month to be safe. he said sure and wrote a bunch of referrals at once. 3 weeks later i called to make an appointment. they tried telling me they'll make my 20 week anatomy.. no, i said- i have a referral for one before that. they were not understanding the clear  and thorough  referral and said they  can't help me. also they'll randomly ask in the middle of the phone call if you're pregnant right after asking your due date... wtf? 

well i trusted my gut. at 16 weeks i paid out of network for a high risk specialist instead. within minutes they detected multiple blood clots in the  placenta that have been forming since day 1,  beyond 5cm, almost 7! i am now on blood thinner shots everyday, and me- a 21yo, 135ib, healthy first time mom is high risk. they kept asking who did the first sonogram and how wasn't this seen? 

negligence. avoid. im now 18 weeks and so thankful i stopped coming here. im
so scared to deliver here now. the only person who's  "advanced" in this center is sydney the genetic counselor. she's an absolute peach, please see her if you're considering genetic testing. so kind and informative.

this hospital is amazing!!! the staff is friendly, attentive and available with advice and updates. it was really terrifying to have my mother hospitalized but they really did save her life and i'll always be grateful!!!

went because urgent care referred me due to abdominal pain.  i don't know why the fuck they didn't get around to asking my insurance for the money until november when i was there in august, but thanks for ruining my life, fuckers.  i was just starting to get on top of shit.  now there's this bill and you know what, i'm not just done with this shit, i'm done with this country.  next time i'll just die in the most inconvenient way possible (in public, loudly, making a scene) or go to a more civilized country and be a pain in the ass if i die from my appendix exploding on the way overseas.  get your fucking shit together.  also i had to bring my own blankets, and fuck those fluorescent lights.  people who are sick need sleep, not that shit.  also the wait time was stupid.

if you're hit by a car, be prepared to use bed pans and to receive zero help. but it gets better. 
if you're on medications, be prepared for medications that can cause serious interactions to be prescribed. out of concern for your liver, kidneys, and life, be prepared for no new medications to control the pain to be prescribed. 
prescription errors have occurred more than once during my visits to this hospital. 
on occasion, if your condition does not allow you to move, expect wait times up to 8 minutes to sit in your own urine and/or feces for someone to help you move the bedpan, after which, you have to figure out a way to clean yourself because an absorbent pad is placed under you without any concept of cleanliness. i asked the nurse if diaper rash was the goal. 
my primary care physician said at this point, at the rate their emergency room is declining, if i return here, he's expecting a call stating i passed away.

my son was spiking 105.7 temperature and of course i was freaking out we got in the car and drove to the closet er. on the way there and the cold got his temp down to 100... they were excellent with my little one talking to him and making him feel comfortable at 6 years old, we had doctor jay. he was a younger man and absolutely fantastic with my son, they did a strep and flu test ended up being the flu b.  they let him pick out a gift and gave him lots of sponge bob stickers. i was very happy with my experience. we got in right away.

this hospital  is getting worst and worst. i went to  er and my fever was so high that i felt i i was about yo pass out. even though i wasn't all there  they didn't allow my husband to go in with me. he was told i was an adult and i could take care of my self. guard was very rude. when i was dismissed at around 9 pm i tried calling my husband to come pick me up  the guard told me to step outside to use my cell so i did and since it was so cold and windy i walked back in and he told me i had to  wait outside. i told him i was really sick and it was cold outside and he said i had to wait outside. as i was waiting outside this lady went in and was on her cell and since he was on his cell too  he didn't tell her anything. when i had my son back in 2012, my son was born at 1pm and the next day by  10 am they wanted to  discharge me because i had no complications. then they realized i had to  wait at least  24 hrs so they were kicking me out by 1 pm at exactly 24 hrs. oh but they  want your ins info right away, before they do anything.

do not come here if you have asthma or breathing issues. they'll take hours to tend to you even tho you're gasping for air and nurses will stare at you because they can hear you wheezing but still won't do anything. i was given 2 breathing treatments and the respiratory nurse said i was still wheezing pretty bad but that i needed to leave there was nothing else they can do. i went home to struggle to breathe for 1 more day and decided to goto st joseph's they knew exactly what to do for me all were so nice and helpful tested me for everything and was confused on why holy cross didn't run tests. they started me on an iv with medications and the next day i was feeling 70% better. never going back to holy cross they need proper training on how to treat patients to have more compassion they're extremely rude. i would hate for them to send home a patient and something worse to happen.

the quality of care here is fine. they took good care of me post-surgery. 

but good luck getting your money back from them if you pay in full on the day of your surgery and your health insurance covers some of the cost a month later. if i hadn't noticed i'd overpaid by $1300 once i got my estimate of benefits back post opp, i have a feeling the hospital would have kept it because they made no effort to contact me about my refund and once i noticed it, it took 6 months and maybe 20 phone calls and at least 3 faxes for them to finally give me back the $1300 i overpaid. 

very stressful un-cool situation to be in.

cindy at the front desk, has the worst customer service, every time i check in, she gives me an attitude, i've been here three times to check in to see family members and she always has attitude. other than that the nurses are great and the device is great.

this is an embarrassment to the healthcare community. 5 hours in the emergency room before any treatment began is completely unacceptable. this is a non-profit and teaching hospital which is not a bad unless you get what we have here, inefficiency and ineffectiveness. it's sad that the az dept of health services doesn't have a standard for er patient care that involves time to begin treatment. 
as many other reviews state, unless you are bleeding externally, you will wait in the er for as long as it will take you to drive to another facility where you'll inevitably receive better care.
since this is the only er in yuma you may be stuck going to it and if that is the case, call an ambulance as that is the only way you won't be waiting more than 2 hours for treatment to begin.

if you have the flu go ahead and go there but for anything serious please do find someplace else. go to phoenix or san diego.

this place is the biggest joke. it is staffed by walk in clinic dr.s. and any dr worth his shit never stays. unfortunately for yuma residents. other hospitals have tried to come here and somehow magically they go away....hmmmm.

plenty of winter visitor's are leaving here because of the poor health care. don't just take it from me.....read the reviews.
..."2 family members lost with no explanation"
..."worst care in 60 years"
....incompetent, incompetent incompetent!

yrmc, medical staff that can't make it elsewhere and the costs, well like i said read the reviews.

dr thomas shields (npi: 1760400873) in the er had to staple a simple head laceration after  sustaining an injury at the dunes... sloppy, non-sterile, didn't even clean the area before or after the 12 staples he rammed in.  then they take ct scans, multiple other xrays and tell me "...sorry but we don't have a radiologist to read your films....". this is a level four "trauma center"; patients need to know that if yuma regional medical center is a level 4, than siri and alexa would likely be better surgeons or er docs than this place has. to be clear... this in my personal opinion is nothing more than a overpriced primary care  clinic commonly found in mexico.

absolutely the worst. i came in on a saturday morning following a fall the previous day. the doctor came in and his first question was if i had been drinking. i told him i had the night before, but nothing that morning. he replied he'd been doing this for 20 years and he could smell it. after ordering x-rays, he told me someone would be in to clean the wound on my hand. the x-rays came back negative, but i'm not convinced they were read properly. the nurse had me wash my wound with soap and water. i asked if i should wrap my writs and she told me whatever i wanted to do. the doctor never returned. i asked for something for the pain. she promised tylenol, but never brought it. shameful!

absolutely the worse service ive ever experienced!! my daughter was very ill, vomiting blood, abdominal pain level of an 8 and the sat us in the waiting from from close to 5 hours, in the meantime, she still vomiting blood & severe abdominal pain! all the took was a ua & a basic cbc/cmp and back to the wating room. i know it gets busy but c'mon...they treated her like she came in for toe pain !! its sad that this is all yuma has for a hospital!

we visit every year and i have been to this walk-in clinic 3 times, most recently a couple of weeks ago. this is the worst and i'm an rn who knows how it should work. they advertise "walk-ins welcome but don't have the staff to accommodate them. people sit in the waiting room for hours coughing and spreading whatever. on my second visit, i saw a sweet female pa or arnp named jennifer who was very good, but when i went back the next week to say the abo i was on was making me very short of breath - omg - two hours just to get in back where i waited again behind a curtain listening to the staff joke and laugh and blah blah blah.  the black male pa was flirting with a nurse, discussing whether or not she should put her car in an upcoming car show or not and on and on....and on! guess what all you people sitting around the desk - we in the cubbys behind the curtains can hear you in spite of the stupid out-of-sync "ocean wave" tapes in each one. when the nurse came in for vitals i commented that they were very loud, she agreed and looked disgusted. when the pa finally came in, all he said was to stop the antibiotic i was on and "see."  i'd already done that! i asked if i shouldn't start something else because i'd only been on it for 3 days...again ""wait and see." i ended up going over to the foothills clinic on fortuna where i saw john smock and got another prescription and also sent my husband the next week where he got excellent care. don't waste your time at the foothills yrmc walk-in clinic...go across the highway to the foothills clinic instead.

what a great place to bring someone with heart issues. i had to bring my husband to the emergency room. he was having trouble breathing. first, they had valet services. this was such a blessing . once we arrived at the emergency room. i felt such a sense of relief knowing he was being checked out completely. with the most qualified, professional staff.

our family would like to thank the incredible staff at mease countryside. the care we received for our family member was beyond what we could have ever asked for. we would specifically like to thank the staff at the ccu for ensuring we were comfortable and that our family was informed and supported.

i had ct scan or xrays that determined my ab pain was from appendicitis.  during the service, i asked if the bill is for everything and they said yes.  then i receive a separate bill for the reading of the xrays!  i called mease and they say sorry we didn't tell you that there would be another charge for the reading of the xrays offsite!  i said the xrays were read right there within 20 minutes, that  is why i went to the emergency room. they apologized again and wiped their hands clean of their lies. thanks again mease countryside.

was scheduled for colonoscopy.   received an estimate of 4700 from hospital saying i was in insured called them gave my  insurance info 3 times.   they assured me that it was taken care of.   did my prep (which is not fun) went to register again at hospital and waited an hour for them to tell me that they don't take my insurance.   that i could pay them 5500 before procedure.  beware stay away!!!!!

i did a review a couple of year's ago and clobbered them.in the beginning of january i was taken here by ambulance---what a difference.the er was busy but ok the staff were friendly and attentive.  my room was clean and nice  the staff was very friendly and knew their stuff. the food was good. it was noisy only 1nite because of a new patient.  my feelings about this hospital have changed drastically

did you realize that you could be charged $6000 for having a baby there even with insurance but if you don't have insurance they'll charge you $2000 less?  that is what mease countryside is trying to do to us right now.  that they would charge through our insurance company $2000+ more than they would charge a person without insurance seems like insurance fraud on their end.  we've already tried discussing this with cynde in their billing department and they were no help at all.

dr. jeremy daniel webb is a scam artist. every time i have an appointment, he's more concerned with referring me to specialists or ordering random lab tests. i assume there's some sort of commission or referral fee because he acts like a salesman more than a doctor. 

it's required that i come in every 3 months for a checkup. every time i reject his offer referral/bloodwork (that i don't need), he punishes me with monthly visits instead of the normal quarterly visits. i've even tested this theory by agreeing to bloodwork once. 

here's how my past 3 visits went:

me: thanks dr. webb, i'll see you in 3 months.
dr.: would you like to see a specialist? i can refer you.
me: no thank you.
dr. let's get some bloodwork then?
me: no thanks. 
dr.: ok, i'll need to see you next month for a check in.
me: why?
dr.: i'd like to make sure the medication is good for you.
me: i've been on it since the 1990's 
dr.: ok, see you next month.

i'm now on the line for $150/mo instead of every 3 months. 

stay away from dr. webb, and stay away from honor health. it's very clear that they want to refer you to as many in-house specialists as possible. it's a shame what the medical industry has turned into.
fac_name: HonorHealth Medical Group - Osborn - Primary Care

review:
totally bottom of the barrel medical providers. they spent multimillions on a beautiful east campus but should've spent the same amount retraining their staff. if your loved one needs urgent mental healthcare, don't send them to benefis. no wonder so many people are addicted and having breakdowns in great falls. their er and mental health team run a factory farm, get them in there and get them out of there as efficiently as possible. next. that is if they even allow an evaluation of an individual suffering from a crises. its symptomatic about the hypocritical hatred of people who have a psychological disorder. that subconscious bias equates to neglect. especially of the undiagnosed. 

other issues is nurses have left gravely ill patients alone in their hospital rooms for extended amounts of time, risking the lives of patients. some doctors here have been pompous. be careful, the er doctor might insinuate you are a hypochondriac even though you have a lifelong immune disorder, and that bad cold happens to be meningitis that you could've died from. 

inadequate care has been a longterm problem spanning decades, and even goes back to when the hospital used to be the deaconess. great falls just doesn't attract the best medical talent, except cancer care. 

the cancer center is top notch and deserves a star, because they will help a loved one stricken with cancer using the latest technologies. a second star goes out to their native american welcoming center, so they did their cultural sensitivity homework. both benefis east and west have nice views of the city and countryside. but if you need the best medical care, providence and even community hospital in missoula are my recommendations. good luck driving the three hours to zootown.

i also forgot to mention nurse gabby. how rude she was, how she ignored me. laughed in my faced. turned around and spoke badly and mocked me to her co workers to get a laugh out of them , refused to get me food when i was here from 6pm-4am. how i had to scream to get a sandwich. i was just attacked in the street... choked out until i was unconscious and beat up. this is how you treat me nurse gabby?!?? patient relations will hear about it all tomorrow. your supervisor already did. 

edit: i went in at around 6pm. i just got discharged. it's now 5:23am. that's fxcking sick


disgusting. staff is rude. you can hear the nurses / doctors fighting with each other . they stack up patients right on top of each other. now as i'm typing this 2 nurses are fighting over the schedule , one nurse is mine and she was supposed to bring me food about 1.5 hours ago. after making an extremely loud outburst i was brought food within seconds. funny how that worked. when you ask how much longer they tell you "no time frame were busy" or just don't answer you at all. i asked a short haired african american with glasses where the bathroom was and she just looked at me like i was crazy. i asked her if i was maybe invisible ?!? she laughed in my face and then joked with the other "nurses" i found the bathroom on my own. i will never ever ever come her again. i would never send my worst enemy here . who is the director . there is so much malpractice going on . i experienced it myself, already called my lawyer and he is looking into it.  you call this a hospital ?!? this should be called a funeral home!!! before they get to you you will be dead !!!

i'd give this place 0 stars if possible. the wait times are ridiculous. they range in time from 3 to 5 hrs. i was just there 2 weeks ago for 5 hrs. also, they keep messing up the appointments. the call center & the medical staff give you different info. i once waited for abt 3 hrs for the doctor to just fill out my med form but it was 4:30 by then & i was told that the doctor was leaving & i had to return the next day just to pick up my form again. 

last time i went, i had 2 appointments. i had 1 at 9am which i was told was actually at 11am for some reason i don't know. the 2nd 1 was at 10. so, i went to the 10am apt 1st & waited 3hrs to see the med assistant.

for the other apt, i just needed to get a vaccine & bloodwork done for more med forms. even though i waited for 2hrs to see a doctor, i was told i'd have to come in another day for bloodwork. in total, i waited 5 hrs. i was there before 9:30am & i left at 2:30pm.

don't even bother with this hospital. just go to a doctor's office instead. its a nightmare in there.

i called the hospital twice for a doctor's note. they transferred me to 6 different depts & an invalid #. the 2nd time, i got transferred 3 times until they transferred me to ambulatory care where it was just voicemail & i had to hang up. so, i went in after work again to tell them i need a note. i was told a day later i'd have to pick up the note. they cant fax or email it as i requested. i was told i can come in during the weekend to pick it up. i went in today, sunday, & adult primary care is closed. apparently, they're only open weekdays said the guy at the front desk of the main entrance.

just don't go here. nothing is good about this place! 
spent 9 hours in the emergency room just to see a nurse!  and on top of that they give you a dirty bloody bed, have drunks smelling like crap next to you peeing on themselves, throwing up and acting like dumbasses. been to many other er's never seen something like this place! first and last time!!!!

unresponsibility, unprofessional ... just push patients go around for weeks, no official paper document about medical record, no direction, no take care ... i don't receive what i need. i really don't want to come here again. it waste of my money if i have to pay for this stuff

this is the worst hospital i've ever been to. my cousin was admitted and was only seen by the doctor after many hours. been in the e.r for two days because there was no bed and finally got a bed and when we got up there, it wasn't even ready. he was told that he will be getting surgery the next morning and not to eat anything after 12 am. but guess what, they left him hanging about the surgery and told us in the evening that he'll be getting the surgery next day. my cousin did not eat for 18 hours and they didn't even mention about the surgery postpone. i had to ask them for meal otherwise they were not going to give him at all. 
the staffs are rude and doesn't care about the patients at all.

wait time is ridiculously long even if you have an appointment i've been trying my hardest to get my appointment locations switched it sucks i have to come all the way here for a sonagram and then have to wait almost two hours to even get called. i mean this is really ridiculous i would not recommend this hospital it's extremely big and very easy to get lost, not many people around to help you find your way then when your waiting to get seen the people at the front desk act like they don't know that you've been waiting forever or maybe they just don't care i'm so fed up with this place!

needed to be seen quickly and went to the expresscare at elmhurst. it was a great experience - fast care and a friendly doctor who made me feel at ease (i'm usually incredibly squeamish when it comes to anything clinical!). thank you dr. rabinovich! marisol at the front desk made the process easy and made sure my regular primary care doctor was informed of my visit. highly recommend if you need to be seen fast and are looking for an easy process with good care.

fuck this place and all the staff that abused me when i was younger. they treat people with anxiety disorders like utter shit and force you into a piss smelled room and call you a liar. fuck this place i though i was going to die in there.

father in law was treated here, nurses and doctors were all great! thank you dr. kira xie and the nurses in 4a for taking such good care of him.  also thanks so much to the trauma team day and night team... you made sure everything go smoothly!

i've had my double jaw surgery done here. dr. montazem, dr. avi, dr. akbari, and dr. schiff did an amazing job. they took care of me and monitored my healing progress consistently. the nurses at the icu were very patient and attentive during my stay, and i can't thank them enough for their hardwork.

my dad was transferred to this hospital for their acute rehab. i was told by their medical team that they're the stroke center for this area. what a joke! neurologist were never involved. we never had a family meeting or discussion of dad's care plan & his medication regimen, and when i asked, dr im says i'm putting alot if stress on my dad & i had to be very patient as its a slow recovery. there's one nurse that touches our heart, his name is n jean joseph, he's so caring, gentle & thoughtful, he makes sure dad is clean & comfortable, he always assist w/ dad's transfer from bed to wheelchair even when he's not dad's nurse! he deserves a 5
the physical therapist & occupational therapist were all awesome, specially ate bernie (ot) & maria b (pt tech). maria b is so caring & helpful, she made our stay tolerable. ate bernie explains to us what & why she's doing certain exercises & how she's trying to activate/retrain the brain/muscles. 10 days later, some regional director, i think its dr nori, she came & basically saying  its time for dad to transfer to sub-acute rehab since he's not improving & insurance wont be paying if he continues to stay. my whole family takes turn staying w/ dad everyday, we never saw any medical team doing an assessment on dad. they came  looking at their papers & say, "ok, no change" then walk away, i have to ask questions very quickly & most if their answers are "i have to look at the chart or computer, i will update you later" 60% of the time they dont come back!!
in short, the stroke center title should be removed, stay away from this hospital. the whole pt/ot team deserves to be relocated to a better hospital like nyu langone or ny presbyterian in manhattan.

north shore birth center gave me exceptional care throughout my pregnancy - they always listened, were on time, and really treat you like a whole person. i felt incredibly supported and educated, and like i was allowed to ask any 'dumb' question and take as much time as i needed with appointments. i had previously been getting care with the midwives at mgh who were fine, but i definitely felt more like a number on the conveyor belt there. each midwife i met with at nsbc was wonderful and i would have been thrilled to have any of them there for my birth. we wound up being lucky enough to get lisa t. for the day of my daughter's birth, and despite a couple surprises, lisa and the team truly supported me in having an incredibly empowering, powerful, safe, and healthy birth experience that i feel eternally grateful to them for. while some of this is always luck, i think that because i felt so comfortable and trusting of them, knowing they were my advocates, an unexpected birth 2.5 weeks early went smoothly and beautifully. i highly recommend them without reservation.
address: 85 Herrick St  On the Campus of Beverly Hospital

review:
my scheduled colonoscopy was friday. i was greated as soon as i entered the door and filled out the paperwork.  i was treated as an important client and made to feel welcome. 
when it was my turn to enter for my exam the nurse welcomed me and took my vitals and started my iv. a very gentle caring person. 
the anthologist came in and greated with good humor and asked basic health questions and described what was going to be used to knock my lights out for the procedure. 
a few minutes later the dr came in and greated me and asked if i had any questions to how the process went.
a few minutes later the anthologist wheeled me to the examination room and set me up for the exam. he asked if i was comfortable and then said goodnight,  bam i was out. 
the next thing i remember is coming out of the fog in the recovery room with my wife by my side.
a nurse came in removed my iv, took my vials. the good dr came in a few minutes later and discussed my procedure and asked if i had questions.  he gave me a computer print out what he discussed for my records and to discuss with my dr.
all in all it is a very good practice,  i was treated with care and respect. in 5 years i will have no reservations about scheduling another exam here.
fac_name: The Endoscopy Center of Santa Fe

review: had a great experience today!! i went in today with my 10 year old daughter that i was up with 3 times last night and they were amazing!!! so caring and fast. i truly appreciate all of them today. i will definitely  be back but hopefully i won't need them.

so i've read the reviews and was shocked about them.  upon arriving at emergency room the staff and pa were fantastic which ultimately took me to admission for 6 days. dr borrero, hospitalist fantastic and very good. i was she was in also private practice i'd be a patient. the cna's especially laurie was amazing and the care she did should be a teaching model for new students. the cleaning lady and great. probably never gets enough thanks. the respiratory people are fantastic and friendly. the nurses are good and like anywhere there are 1-2 that need people skills and need to be faster on the call button and remember patients. now dont get me wrong there were some awesome ones and. i can't remember all their names. wish i could . 5th floor was very good all in all and holmes does not deserve the kind of reviews previously posted. knew i needed medical attention and glad i took the chance and came here. great job to the majority of the care team. the nurse from maine is great. nurse maureen great. word of advise the staff communicators that they wear are a total distraction and hinder patient care. just in 5 min one nurse in my room was contacted 4 times with our conversation and one interruption was simply asking where she was. these communication devices are being abused and overused and not fair to patient care they loose focus

this hospital is far the worst. my husband has been here since 6:50am and we are still waiting on a room. he asked for pain medication and it took 4 hours before they requested it from the doctor   i had to call the doctors office to get them to page him. finally i thought we were going to a room but no they took us to a closet down the halll and not one nurse or doctor has come in here to check on us no one has asked if he wanted water or a pillow or something to eat. terrible i wouldn't recommend this hospital to my worst enemy. enter at your own risk.

my rating is directed at dr. ashton connor, whose a fellow-md at duke university hospital.
august 27, 2019, i was hospitalized at duke for a hip replacement. directly after, i developed an acute kidney injury and another bowel blockage, which was the second consecutive. they were considering possibly having to put me back on dialysis, which i was on for 4.5 years before my kidney, pancreas transplant on december 1, 2016. after weeks of intense treatments, my kidney began working again. eventually, i began to slowly recover from my blockage, which i expected, being at such a prestigious hospital like duke, but what i didn't expect was to encounter a doctor like ashton connor. although he was a fellow-md, i still expected nothing close to who he was, and i couldn't believe that duke would have a doctor like him working there. i'll explain now. a day after i began recovering i called for my nurse to help me use the bathroom. this should've been a good sign but dr. connor turned it into a bad one. because my nurse wasn't available, i got my bedpan but made a mess on myself and my bed. by trying to clean myself up my gown was no longer on properly. i remained in this predicament for about 30 - 40 minutes before my nurse, along with three other nurses and dr. connor arrives. i immediately asked my nurse to help me and dr. connor told her not to. i then asked the doctor if he thought it was appropriate for me to be in this predicament without needing help, and without hesitation, he replied yes. minutes later, he left me the same way he found me and took all the nurses with him. i realized how he blatantly violated my patient's rights by his unprofessional, incompassionate, and unscrupulous demeanor. he intentionally left me violated and humiliated and days later, he had the audacity to tell me that he was there to help me as if god hadn't given me a brain in order to differentiate helping from hindering. i'll update my experience by the outcome after i file a complaint with patience relations.

this review was initially posted on 11/23/19.

update: 01/09/20

after filing my complaint with patient's relations, it wasn't what most duke patient's would expect from their patients advocacy. it appeared to be more of a doctor's advocacy, instead. there was absolutely no transparency and what they did share wasn't, in my opinion, appropriate under these circumstances. they concluded that dr. connor didn't know my condition, although he was there to witness my surgery and was at my care team meetings. they concluded no wrongdoing, instead, they used my humiliation as a learning tool for their staff, and their staff is supposed to learn to make sure they know their patient's condition. yes, know their patient's condition, as if dr. connor didn't know my condition and the patient's bill of rights before he violated mine. my conclusion of the experience with dr. ashton connor is, he had no good intentions and a doctor with bad intentions is not there to help me, you, or anyone else. 
don't be oblivious, be careful and aware. make your own conclusion about our patients' advocates, protecting our "patients' bill of rights".

i take my hat off to the doctors, nurses, and staff at medstar washington hospital center because they are slammed with wall-to-wall patients, due to the recent shut-down of providence hospital and lack of hospitals in washington, dc, yet they still maintain a courteous and friendly demeanor. 

my family member just recently spent a week in this hospital and i can honestly say, it probably saved his limb. the doctors are so knowledgeable and aggressive with their diagnosis and willing to make rapid moves to save a life. we experienced nothing but patience and understanding towards the patient, as well as the family. the doctors/surgeons made time to discuss every option and outcome with the family and it was greatly appreciated. 

now i will say that the er triage is something like a third world country war zone. i've never been, but i can only imagine. since my family member was admitted to the hospital unexpectedly from a doctor's appointment, we were told that the er would be the easiest way to be admitted. whew! well, he was admitted easily, but the triage area was flooded with people!!! people stacked on top of people, no privacy, people in the hallways, cops guarding individuals that were under arrest...just a mass chaotic mess! people yelling out, hacking, sneezing, just a big germ fest. i wanted to go home and bathe in a bathtub filled with clorox and lysol. 

i truly didn't want to leave him there because he/everyone looked so miserable. it's no way on earth anyone could get any rest in this area because it's just a big ball of confusion. he spent two days in this confusion until he could get into a room. that's how crowded this hospital is, you have to wait until a room finally becomes available before you can leave the er. i don't know how they do it, but the nurses and doctors persevere on and act as if nothing is going on. i would lose my mind if i had to deal with this chaos everyday. 

oh how i wish dc would build a new hospital or 2 to take care of the citizens of the nation's capital!!! they need it asap!!!! 

after he was placed in a room, he was able to receive the care he so desperately needed.  if i was basing my review on the er alone, it would be a 1 star review, but since i had to factor in the staff, the rapid response of the doctors and my family member's care, i had to bring that star count up. this truly is a great hospital. it's just overcrowded. i truly hope another hospital can be built in the district to alleviate some of the crowds.

don't go to the medstar was hosp ctr emergency room for anything less than a life threatening condition.  or at least if you do, be prepared to wait after triage (initial intake interview) for 12 or more hours to see an actual doctor.  and then if you are admitted, you may wait on a supremely uncomfortable stretcher for a day or more. at least, that was my experience. next time, if at all possible, i'd go to an urgent care facility to initiate medical treatment. if you have to go to the er, be sure to bring something to do, ear buds, and a charger for your device

this hospital is trash i don't recommend it to no one, the nurses here are very very very unprofessional they have an ugly ass attitude one of the nurses in the emergency room which is in the front window is the worst nurse she is hispanic wears false eyelashes and has an ugly face really bitter nurses in here with the most ugly attitude as soon as you walk in the er you can feel the nasty vibes with all these unprofessional people they hire here as nurses, security and doctor, it was the worst experience last night. i literally walked out after waiting for two hours and no one cared for me while being in serious pain. no one offered a wheel chair, nurses were complaining of how annoying i was getting and they were saying they were annoyed just by hearing me complaining when i was in pain. i don't understand why they choose to be nurses when they can't deal with patients and have the worst humor of scense. i will definitely be filing a complaint with this hospital and the cheap nurses in the er. i'm gonna sue them for neglect and maltreatment.

review: my son called surgery center and canceled his 2 year old non- emergency procedure due to he could not be there on the day it was schedule due to work. he explained he was notified friday at 4:30 pm procedure was going to be monday morning at 7:30 am which was not enough notice for his work for him to be off. he also notified them that he had joint managing custody of his kids per court order so he had to be there to agree to the surgery and that he wasn't agreeing to it. my son called again on monday to make sure procedure was canceled and that even if his ex showed up to have the procedure done that they did not do it because they did not have his permission to touch his son. again explained that per court order both parents had to be there and agree to procedure. monday morning they put his 2 year old son to sleep with anesthesia and did the procedure without notifying my son. he received a text from his ex after they had left the hospital. my son has called to talk to risk management several times since last monday and they still have not returned his call. he has made a police report and has received a  civil case number.
