review: so ghetto here. i got into a car accident and was transported here, the first staff i met was extremely rude. she was uncaring and had no care for appropriate human interaction. i was placed in a room of multiple sick people, coughing up blood and others with flu like symptoms, being healthy but in pain this was not the appropriate placement. there were no doors but a cheap sheet no longer than a few feet.  i felt that i was there for insurance purposes and not for care. they did an irrelevant ct scan, expensive and cannot see the issue. overall, i would not return nor recommend due to hospital conditions and the lack of personable staff.

my wife got really ill  were from out of town visiting family were in our motorhome she must've threw up eight times violently went to er 3 am and  they all were great it's now 9:30 in the morning the daytime doctor walker and  eddie  nurse are great their going the extra mile to check for possible stroke  i'm very pleased with all their concerns   chuck.  aruta.

earlier this week, i had an unfortunate incident with my car door; i accidentally slammed my thumb in it. after almost a day of excruciating pain, swelling, and bruising, i went to a cvs minute clinic where they immediately suggested i go to the er to have it x-rayed, to make sure it wasn't broken. naturally, i came here and received exceptional care.

i came in at about 1pm. like always, there weren't very many people in the waiting room, but it was full house in the back; they weren't sure when they were going to be able to take me in. still, they took me into triage right away and performed the x-ray all while waiting for a bed to free up. after a little over an hour, they were ready to see me in the back. my thumb wasn't broken, but that car door gave it a hematoma. the doctor burned a hole in the nail, and drained it to relieve the swelling. before i knew it, they were ready to give me my discharge paperwork. all this in about two hours.

way to go oro valley hospital! they are the only place i've ever seen that manages a full er gracefully. i'm so glad to have them nearby.

i had a surgery procedure in outpatient surgery here today, first time to this clean n modern facility! from the intake woman to the nurse lynn, anesthesiologist dr. vetter, surgical nurse (forgot name) and my great ob/gyn dr. heather stephens all great women were so pleasant, thorough, upbeat, patient, thorough, respectful, efficient just amazing! thought i was dreaming since i've been in other facilities where the staff seemed overworked n not happy doing their job and you had to go look for staff n wait too long for everything! the team made me feel so comfortable and special was treated as a queen! highly recommend this facility

i received excellent care at st charles.    despite there being a few folks in the er waiting room at night it was rapidly realized i had a condition requiring attention.  i had a diagnosis rapidly and a plan right after.   after an uncomplicated bit of a stay i'm improved and on the mend.   a huge thank you to all the staff i happened to encounter.

dr ryan peterson has the absolute worse bed side manners out if anyone i have ever met. it surprises me he is able to be a doctor. he was extremely rude and short. it was disturbing to see they way he speaks to and treats its patient. i will not go back to bend hospital and risk being treated by him again. he basically kicked me out when i asked if there were any more tests to be done to figure out the issue. i just sat there shocked and then left. it's really sad that st charles can't find qualified doctors that can treat their patients without being cruel.

i would never recommend this facility. a huge cover up of abuse from a therapist to patients. this facility continues to allow this therapist to practice and abuse patients. this therapist lied in order to save her job. the therapist has abused her powers over innocent and powerless children.

wow, you know what would make a really great hospital? medical professionals and medical nurses or even operators that actually care and are nice to people. i understand y'all think y'all must know literally everything, but when someone comes in not knowing how to explain something or how they feel... please have some damn patience!!! the people that work here are so incredibly rude, i felt like i was being judged just for telling them what i need done. i know why people hesitate to come in this hospital now and voice what is wrong with them. because the people that work here will tell them their lying, they will use a sarcastic voice with them or they will judge them and others can clearly see you going back behind your little closed window to talk crap about that patient. y'all disgust me, this hospital needs to fire all the rude people and get nicer people that actually care for others and their health. if i'm dying, i'll take my ass to alabama, screw mississippi hospitals, especially this one.
i can only say good things about this hospital. i have only had minor illnesses but they beat my blue cross blue shield any day.

worst hospital in houston . got there at 7:00 pm and by 1:00 am they were barely doing my registration . they pass someone to a room every hour seems like . there was limited seats from how packed it was . i left and went to another hospital . if you go there expect to spend all day / night there

had an ms flare up and was admitted in the hospital. i was there for a week and my stay was surprisingly amazing. the only bad experience i had was that i felt discriminated by some of the black staff. other than that my experience was very good!

not worth the gas money. my girlfriend had to stay in the neuropsychiatric center for one night and a worker (african american, bald, around 30 years old) taking care of her decided to put her bed under a tv with loud volume and yell/laugh with coworkers throughout the night. the service was good, but the staff needs an attitude change.

i had to switch doctors recently and decided to switch medical groups as well. there's a hoag at the aliso viejo town center that is convenient to me so i decided to switch my pcp to dr. sweetser. here's the thing, dr. sweetser works limited hours on limited days. also, new patients are on a 3-month waiting list to see her if it's just an annual exam. she had high marks from her patients so i decided to give it a go. making an appointment with her was not easy. the staff explained her hours to me. they also would not book me unless i was officially switched over. i had called at the end of august knowing that making an appointment would be 3 months out but since she wouldn't become my pcp until september 1st, i had to call back on september 3rd because of the labor day holiday. that being said, i called and got an appointment in december. i arrived on time and had my paperwork ready. you can download the application from the hoag website in advance and fill it out. the reception person really loved that and i was checked-in quickly. i was called in within 5 minutes. i met with dr. sweetser and she's great. i really like her but she also informed me that she's switching to another office in foothill ranch in a few months. and the front office did not tell me that. womp womp. the search for another doctor continues. i may stay with hoag but i think i may go with the irvine office if there are more doctors there.

providence health system prides itself on their core values--compassion, dignity, justice, excellence, and integrity. the system began over 100 years ago when eight nuns decided to come up with a system of care that was based around the principles in the bible. my phs doctors have always been good, but the nurses, supervisors, and support staff have often been absolute nightmares. the more i work with employees of providence, the more it's confirmed to me that these staffers don't care about being in a noble profession nor following in the footsteps of christ. they only care about working for a company that pays well and has great benefits. i have no problem with people wanting financial stability. my problem is people hiding behind the disguise of "i love working with people" when they sincerely don't. none of the nurses and none of the frontline staff have treated me with compassion, dignity, justice, excellence, or integrity. to say the staff at newberg providence "suck" would give discredit to solid plumbing and piping. staff here are rude, overbearing, and mean-spirited. and it's hard to get in a word because they always talk over you and down to you. in fact, this one young nurse was uncomfortable with having a critical conversation with me (i wasn't putting up with her rudeness or ineptness), so instead of talking like two adults, she called security on me. when security asked what was going on, i told him the truth. "you have a young woman on staff who doesn't know how to have an intense yet honest and critical conversation. if she thinks i was attacking her, she has no concept of how the world works. perhaps she needs to find a better source of income. nursing is not her thing. nor is compassion." without mentioning any names, one of the staff workers did give me the mobile phone number to lori bergen, chief executive, providence medical center. it all begins with leadership. and based upon my experience with those who work beneath her, lori must seemingly find acceptance with a medical and support staff that's completely without compassion, dignity, justice, excellence, or integrity. ironically, each room has a brochure on providence, and specifically on why they care. it looks like mine has never been touched. one of the sentences in a paragraph about how much they care is this one: "please be honest and...tell us what you think." lori bergen, most of your staff at the hospital don't care, and they don't care that they don't care. you should be ashamed, which is why i insist you get better acquainted with the anti-core values outliers on your team. don't work in healthcare if you're not amazing with people. on a final note lori, i always hear you say, "you are the key member of your healthcare team." your staff has forgotten that. not once, not once when i had something to offer was i supported. the only positive thing i have to say about my experience was the night security guard was super respectful and helpful. he should be running this hospital, not you. and by the way, lori, your emergency room lost a $500 pair of glasses. i need those to see. please get on this immediately.

oh. my. goodness. my daughter had a fractured pinky toe - fractured, not displaced. because she dances, the walk-in-clinic referred her to wisconsin river orthopedics. she visited 3 times, each time talking to someone for 5 minutes or less and getting an x-ray. *each* appointment cost $272.75, with extra for the first one. in the end, we will have paid almost $900 to a place that simply read x-rays and provided advice, with no actual treatment of any kind. guess we know how they pay for that expansion and fish tank. i will not be taking referrals to this place again, not being independently wealthy.

my husband had surgery here and they did all they could to keep me from being with him before and after surgery. the only way i was allowed to go back with him while they prepped him for surgery, was to lie and say he needed me to communicate. then for an hour and a half after the doctor spoke to me, and after repeated requests to see my husband, i finally told them i want to see the supervisor, then they allowed me to see him. we will never use this surgical center again.

now i know the luxury of being a domestic medical tourist. i've never had such a pleasant and professional experience at any other az. hospital, ever...from check in to check out, everything was 5 star service. night time was quiet time and i had the room to myself. it was a room with a view of the desert landscape and super clean bathroom.the staff seem aware, focused, present on all levels for patient care, conscientious, courteous and patient. my pillows were fluffed and placed behind my back and bolstered under my knees for me. i was given great food. i was gently handed required meds, given cups of water with ice, no ice and refills with out asking. they have leg stimulation equipment that the nurses patiently unhooked, and hooked up after each walk, bathroom break, etc... i never got any attitude or push-back from any staff, at all. (i've literally had a night nurse leave the ice cup just a far enough distance that i couldn't reach it at a tucson hospital). no passive/aggressive disgruntled workers that i saw here. doctors and nurses work well together and discharge happens in a timely manner. the volunteer who wheeled me to the rotunda was even pleasant and patient despite my crabby, impatient, homesick attitude. thanks to the entire medical staff! this place is medical heaven...

i'm a long time caregiver to my father who had a left ventricle device implanted in 2013 when this was scripps memorial, i can't say enough good about this hospital and their staff. the new facility is even better (if possible) the only reason it is is because it's so new. the surgeon who implanted my dad dr. baradarian, there isn't any better surgeon on the planet! his cardeologist, dr. james heywood is one of the most caring and educated cardiologists i've ever had the pleasure to know.  this man is not only good at what he does he's patient! i've put him through so many trials! i'm sure i'm referred to over there as "the daughter"  ha ha

one of the best facilities if you are in need of emergency care. every other er in san diego can learn from scripps la jolla er as there staff are professional, kind, and understanding, especially with complex medical conditions. it is also extemely clean,modern, and well kept with a more private atmosphere compared to other ers in the county.

i travel a lot back and forth between anchorage, ak and montrose.  during a recent trip, i was in utah where i was diagnosed with pneumonia.  fast forward a couple of weeks, and i am still a bit under the weather, coughing and still without a voice.  i went in for a chest x-ray to see if i had at least beaten the pneumonia.  the medical team was outstanding, and they had me in and out within an hour or so.  the good news, no pneumonia present.

i took the bls class, my  instructor was friendly  
the course is super easy and the test  is based on common sense. you will pass if you really pay attention the instructor will give you hints about what's on the test ....bottom line overall best bls ever

this was my first time taking an acls course and i found exactly the right place to do it. angelo is not only a fantastic instructor but he is also highly accommodating! he was able to work with my schedule and was also very informative and explained each content very well. he also offers cpr and bls courses. i highly recommend this place to everyone that either needs to take a class for the first time or is going back for renewal. the location was also very convenient for me as i live around the area, but i find that no matter where his students are coming from, the drive will definitely be worth it!

brought my daughter in for what seems like the flu for the 3rd time in 40 days. barely touches food or drinks for last 3 days. came in at 11am, triaged immediately then waited 3+hours. then reassessed. clearly hot to the touch but was told machine says other wise. refused to check it again. then waited another 2 hours. finally brought to room to be told that she tested negative and they need to test her urine. since she's only peed once in 24 hrs it may be a while before she'll pee so i cann go home if i'd like and follow up with her doctor if fever stays for another two days. told them no. i don't want to leave without answers. they said of course that's completely ok. spoke to them about fever again. and same response. she said can do rectal if i'd like. told them yes please because she is clearly hot and needs to be medicated for fever since she tends to spike to 104/105. yeah nurse left and never came back to check. never heard of a hospital that desperate to kick out their patients. finally got her to pee. was told it was all negative with some dehydration. ask about iv that they were supposed to administer earlier but since she took 2 sips of juice it wasn't need anymore. along with the 2 pieces of chips she ate. that was good enough for a sick 3yo apparently. doctor comes backk and  says oh sorry we didn't get full rresulta earlier. her urine showed some abnormalities so they'll send in her urine again. asked about blood work but was told unnecessary. and when urine comes back they'll just send her home with antibiotics. without even confirming anything she said we'll be home in an hour. wtf

*update. left hospital with my daughter not eating or drinking. urine results came back normal. so wasn't prescribed antibiotics. when it was time to discharge they repeatedly took her temperature unsuccessfully by mouth because it wasn't giving them a clear reading. when they finally got it, it still reads 98°. got home not even an hour later and test with ear and shows 103.8! spent 8 hours at the hospital with a fever unmedicated because they refused to work a little more and get correct temperature with a rectal reading. unbelievable. left so disappointed and heartbroken. was told to come  back if fever lasts more than 5 days. i will definitely take her back to er but not to christ!

my husband had an aggressive brain tumor removed october 1st with dr veronis.   this was my husband's second tumor in over a year. 
the first tumor was removed at university of miami hospital and we had no complications and he was able to leave the hospital a few days later totally fine.   
dr. veronis was going to do an awake surgery, but due to my husband's declining speech and a recently diagnosed uti, we were told it would no longer being awake surgery.  
i was concerned about potential complications, and asked what the worst case scenario would be, and was told that my husband might lose his speech and possibly his writing ability. we went ahead with the surgery.
fast forward, my husband is partially paralyzed on his right side, is incontinent, and needs a diaper for  his bowel movements.  his speech has been impacted as well. after 6 weeks of rehab, things are not getting better and we will be bringing him home for hospice (according to the neurologist/oncologist, he has 2-6 months). 
i'm angry because i feel like i should have been told the worst possible scenario (paralysis) as we may have not gone ahead with the surgery.  at least my husband would  have dignity and mobility with whatever short time was left.  
i realize that  is a medical professions problem....to operate, but sometimes it is not in the best interest of the patient if it only prolong their life for a short while.  i hope that will change.
update:  my husband passed away 2 weeks after coming home.  i'm still angry and sad.  what was the point of the surgery if the doctors knew he wouldn't have much longer to live?

review:
my louisville kids just had there 1st child there. my 1st trip in any of the louisville hospitals.

inova surgery center is located inside the inova healthplex and is a good option when offered for your surgical needs instead of the traditional requirements of an actual hospital visit for outpatient surgery.

i accompanied my mom for her outpatient procedure and we were pleased with her visit from start to finish.  the check in process was seamless.  i appreciated that they use a color system to get patients registered so you just have to listen for your corresponding color card to be called.  this allowed each patient to maintain their privacy respectively.  the pre/post op nurses were gems with great bedside manner every step of the way. 

if you are waiting in the waiting area, make sure you dress accordingly because it is super chilly.  they do have a coffee machine and bottled water while you wait as well.   

need to charge your device?  there are a plethora of plugs both around the walls in within the middle of some of the tables.  just in case you forgot your cord, they have one of the free standing charging stations if you are lucky enough to the chair located directly to the left of the stand. 

facilities are clean which is always a plus considering the environment!

how people like that sleep at night.  one thing my family has to looko forward too, god sees everything and has the final word!!! don't take your loved ones to depaul hospital!!!

my friend stayed 2 nites. the staff professional and so polite. they all did a wonderful job. if you have to stay at this place you will be in safe hands

i am writing this review as my father began his treatment recently at kentfield after having a difficult time at a different ltac facility. i have nothing but good things to say about kentfield. we have seen a huge progress since bringing him here. the nurses, cna's are incredibly attentive to his needs and make sure he is comfortable, clean, and well taken care of.
the physician staff is caring and transparent. we had a great chance to talk to his attending and understand his plan of care. 
when it comes to the various therapies they offer, each member of therapy is very rigorous and focuses hard on getting a patient better. my father who is incredibly drowsy and incoherent is still attended to daily by his therapists who strive to keep him going. even if he is conked out the entire day they still spend the time with him trying to at least get him moving involuntarily so he does not develop sores or lose muscle mass. 

kentfield overall is an amazing place and very appropriate for someone with a brain injury. i am very confident as of now, they saved my father from negligence at his other ltac facility, and i hope over time we can see some recovery with their honest and sincere efforts.

this is a terrible rehab hospital,a doctor named doris purcell works there
she is awful and was responsible for me having a muscle in my right leg getting torn and having to have 4 blood transfusions and 3 iron transfusions. their lead physical therapist who name is kelsey is lazy and will not help you. the management is incompetent at best.

wow! i have nothing but amazing things to say about birthing here. the abc (alternative birth center) is for low-risk birthing mothers and has a home-like feel. the midwives through providence southfield work in the abc and they did my prenatal care. each abc room has a queen sized bed so that not only can the birthing mother sleep in it overnight but a partner can as well. each room also has a large tub for labor, mine had a tub with jets which was just what i needed during labor. the nurses that work in the abc are specially assigned to that area of the hospital and are experts on natural birth! they were all so encouraging, kind and empowering. my birth was everything i dreamed and prayed it would be, in part because of how amazing the abc was. i will most definitely go back there to birth and suggest it to any mothers who are low-risk!

review: the behavioral center is a nightmare, especially for someone with ptsd. it took everything i had to stay sane in there. men were hitting on women and trying to make sexual advances (and vice versa), there were sometimes multiple fights daily, it was very unclean (food messes everywhere, people would be soaked in urine or have deficated on themselves...and then sit down and the furniture not be cleaned til the following day. multiple people hadn't showered more than 1 time in the 14 days i was there...yet they stress hygiene). the doctor might spend 30 seconds a day with you, if you are even that lucky. he does a fantastic job of misdiagnosing people and prescribing the wrong medication. i have very bad anxiety, and he prescribed me with antidepressants. i'm not a depressed person at all. i felt like a complete zombie the whole time i was there. i felt like i was going to pass out half the time from not eating enough because the food portion sizes were so small. the only good thing about this place is that it felt like the techs were on our side most of the time. if you treat them with respect, they treat you with respect. it was a very stressful environment to be in, and i feel sorry for anyone that has to be in there. it's supposed to be a place to get better, but how can you do that with people of all different diagnoses in the same place? you cannot put a person with ptsd in this type of environment, with constant physical altercations, and expect them to be ok. there needs to be hospitals out there for specific/individualized mental health conditions.

upon my discharge, kaiser leadership noticed the "pattern" in dr. yamamoto's notes, and told to her make corrections. but the damage was already done. she did not have the decency to reach out and apologize for harming me either. but i suppose if she was decent, she wouldn't have falsified my records to begin with. what makes this matter worse is, as a result of filing a complaint against dr. yamamoto, kaiser oakland has blackballed me. i cannot get services there. when i spoke to the chief of psychiatry, mr. timothy barry lcsw, about my 5150 and dr. yamamoto's misconduct, he dismissed me by saying it was "water under the bridge". he went on to say that no one is willing to work with me because i reported dr. yamamoto. 

why am i being penalized for filing a complaint? it's retaliation. kaiser policy states that a patient has a right to "voice complaints freely and recommend changes regarding the quality of services throughout the established process, and without being subject to coercion, discrimination, reprisal or unreasonable interruption of care, treatment and services." it's strange how kaiser's mental health clinicians go on strike to advocate for patients getting better care, and here they are denying me care for speaking up about unprofessional, unethical, and negligent acts. they are hypocrites. dr. yamamoto's colleagues are simpleminded and prejudice. instead of finding ways to help me, they take dr. yamamoto's side. not only do i have a trauma of being put on 5150, but now kaiser staff is patient profiling me. if i call the facility and share my name and medical record number, reception hangs up on me. 

i cannot believe how someone so vindictive, malicious, and unethical like dr. yamamoto is still able to work at kaiser. people have been fired for doing less serious things. dr. yamamoto brings shame to this profession. she does not have a genuine desire to help patients or help them reach their goals and have a life worth living. i had 10 sessions with her at $166 per session, and all she told me was to watch tv, play with my dog, and go for walks. mediocre advice at premium prices. there was no treatment plan or structure in our sessions. i later found out from a manager that she was part of the dialectal behavior therapy, (dbt) team. the goal of dbt is to help patients find a life worth living. dbt is comprised of 4 pillars, distress tolerance, interpersonal effectiveness, mindfulness, and emotion regulation. dr. yamamoto never mentioned the existence of this group, nor did she use the concepts in our sessions. there is a big difference between incompetence and malicious intent. for her to worsen my symptoms to the point where i had to be hospitalized shows that she is not a good person and has chosen the wrong profession.

when you walk into the ambulatory care center you walk into a 3rd world country. 

i was referred to brooklyn hospital by my surgeon at my request just bc it was close to home and what i needed was "a super simple process". that should be the case.

my only need was a medical clearance for a minor surgery that would require local anesthesia (i.e. numbing my ear for a procedure. my ear!). the clearance equates to less than a common physical.

after waiting in a loud, chaotic, asylum-resembling lobby for 40 minutes beyond my appointment time, i was taken into a room where 2 techs/nurses took my vitals. over the next 15 mins they argued which vitals were needed, how the scale worked, how to enter the details into the computer...and what they wanted for lunch (it was 9:45a). 

they moved me to another room...waited 20 more minutes and an intern/resident showed up...nice guy...but had no idea why i was there or what was needed. said he'd grab the doctor and i'd be done shortly. 

thirty minutes pass. i walk down the hall to track down someone...anyone...that can help. (random non-patient civilians freely wandering around the exam areas.) "the doctor is on her way". 

twenty minutes pass...the doctor arrives! however, she's only there to inform me that unless i make her my primary care physician and commit to using her in the future she will not provide the clearance i need. 

it's been 2 hours. i'm not making her my pcp. 

they don't reimburse my co-payment bc the 2-min conversation where she denied me her assistance "counts as a consultation". she never actually entered the room. she told me from the hallway.

folks, don't. just...don't.

(btw my surgery is not taking place at this hospital)

i visited the orthopedic clinic today at the brooklyn hospital and had the pleasure of seeing dr. joseph fetto. i was most impressed with his professionalism. he spent quite a bit of time with me discussing the cause of my knee discomfort and provided recommendations for pain relief and a treatment plan. he truly understood what i was going through and i am grateful he could provide some pain relief. i highly recommend dr. fetto and the brooklyn hospital's clinics for all of your medical needs.

donna lindsey

awful experience.  a woman at the desk in the er room literally rolled her eyes in my face, when i was trying to let them know i was leaving the room for a second incase my son woke up and rudely said " oh god, he'll be fine" 
nobody wants to being the er,  but she gets paid to be there and i'm sure that ignorance is not in her job description. we were also in a room right next to the nurse's desk, i've never heard so many complants about coworkers. speaking loudly about staff that messed something up. it was worse than teenage girls. the dr and nurse that treated my son were very nice and professional. the bathroom was disgusting, i could go on and on. luckily, i live closer to milford hospital and probably won't ever have to go here again. however, other people will and whoever runs this hospital really needs to look into how things are being run in that er. if you have time,  go to a different hospital, avoid this place at all cost.

in june of 2016 my husband living in ponca city and was having chest pain.  he went to the er and had elevated troponin. the did not do anything because the md wanted to go home and eat supper. the room he was in had no ac and they gave him nitro and morphine overnight. his troponin levels climbed all night, they took him to the cath lab the next morning and he had several blockages and they decided that it was a big push to get him to okc to get emergency heart cath. the heart cath that they did was diagnostic only because they cannot place stents.   the care that he received did not seem to be up to par compared to the care that was given by the cardiac departments of mercy hospital.

ponca hospital is a joke. i went to ponca hospital on december 22nd because of pain breathing and high temp they told me it was a viral infection on december 24th i ended up going to a hospital 30/45 minutes a way and found out i had severe left lobe pneumonia and was admitted for 2 days. i had to return to ponca er today due to pain in my left ribs (which the doctor who admitted me 5 days ago said to go to the er if it happened). i have been sitting here in a room for over an hour and no boday has been in to hook me up or check on me or anything.

don't be fooled because it's related to partners healthcare system, definitely miles below that if spaulding rehab in boston. horrible patient care. the nursing staff was generally pleasant, however, knowledge of serious medical conditions was just non existent. they gave the wrong medications to my family member. my family member was also first sent to cape cod hospital and waited for hours because they refused to transport to where their brain surgery had taken place. if was not until after an argument that they "happened to find a solution". completely inappropriate.

been seeing dr. sundaram since november. in that period, he failed multiple times to do what he said he was going to do. referrals were either not sent or not accompanied with appropriate paperwork. prescriptions were not sent to pharmacies even with one or more "resend" requests by me. office staff dragged their feet forwarding biopsy tissue samples to ucla med and then never followed through with diagnosis without being prodded. 

despite numerous questions posed to dr. sundaram or his staff on the status, treat-ability and prognosis of my cancer, it took over 2 months of cajoling, coddling and pestering to get dr. sundaram to admit there is no fda-approved chemotherapy and the radiation i'm receiving is palliative.

his final suggestion? - try to get me into a clinical trial of chemotherapy targeted at my specific mutation (unlikely).

i had surgery there in january 2019. as i am very fearful of anesthesia which i had a very scary episode when i was younger i was reluctant to go forward with the procedure. dr. hodin took every precaution necessary to alleviate my fears and have me seen by cardiology, anesthesiology to verify that everything would be fine. the anesthesiology team were outstanding! cardiology was outstanding. the massachusetts general hospital in my opinion is the number one institution in the country. be honest with your doctor tell him what you think what your fears are and i am very confident that they will be honest with you about your care. the sad thing is it was very difficult for me having been in pathology for 25 years to totally alleviate my fears. but the nursing team and other members including my physician were top notch. i would recommend massachusetts general hospital to anyone especially if you're concerned about your care

i thought i will not write review, because so many people wrote about absolutely the same experience as my mother had there. but changed my mind, when today she complained on pain in her upper arm caused by blood pressure cuff. she is 92 years old with very sensitive skin (and flesh too). the nurse in acu was making crazy efforts to take bp automatically, my mom cried and begged not to do it. i wouldn't say the nurse on purpose was not securing a cuff properly, but last time it ballooned. she stopped torturing my mother. bp was not taken. after it in the room another nurse told that any patient can request taken blood pressure manually! 
p.s. maybe i must complain.

my dad got discharged yesterday afternoon 1/11/20 and we were told that he would have  the cipro and the naproxen to take after he got discharged. however, cipro was never sent to cvs and i called five to six times to white 8, the floor my dad was in,  and even paged dr. micheal forrester myself. no phone calls were returned. now is 1/12/20 3:30am. i just placed another called to white 8, the floor my dad was in. i got the same answer," i will let the doctor know, i will let the nurse supervisor know...". i thought mgh was the best hospital. now i definitely know it's not. my dad needs the cipro to fight his prostate infection. i am so disappointed. i am writing this to document what is going on.

my epidural was inserted 7 times over two hours while i had contractions. by residents without my consent, the dr. supervising them was passive aggressive to me and almost seemed mad that i was trying to stay as still as possible, despite all my pain, so it could be done correctly. my birth partner wasn't allowed in the room, and i didn't know how to stand up for myself. i don't know how that's abuse, to not step in after the residents failed more than a dozen times (pic was taken a couple weeks later one of the marks isn't showing up). if any lawyer wants to take my case contact me!

jason in medical records is the most unprofessional person i have ever encountered. he started raising his voice and yelling at me, saying hes the operations manager. if the actually is the operations manager, he certainly should not be. horrible and rude person.

feel sorry for patients who are treated at phillips house 21. that is where they kill your loved one quickly by injecting them with all sorts of lethal injections such as morphine and dilaudid and their doctors claim that they are keeping you loved one very comfortable!!! you have to agree with their doctors or else they call the security guard on you to throw you on the ground and send you for detention to mental emergency. they restrict you to see your loved one to 30 minutes a day with a body guard. sounds like a horror movie. well unfortunately it is the truth. very scary. you think you are coming for help from the doctors you don't  know what you are getting into. where is medical ethics autonomy,beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice for all in order to protect and defend the patients' rights? stop racism and discrimination. treat all cultures as human beings. do not hurt them but help them!!!!!!

tripped over a wire at home and chipped bone in foot. system was efficient, people smart, no one asked me for money until after i was treated, x-rayed, given crutches and a protective boot for my foot, and a prescription for pain killers. good feeling of genuine compassion from workers.

the communication between the intake workers-- the x-ray technician,  the er doctor who looked at the x-rays was good and i didn't have to repeat myself or deal with people who did not know why i was where i was in the building.  . good integration of personnel

i asked to be tested for corona virus.... was told that was not possible.... then they hung up on me.
my health insurance premium is over 2000 per month.... as a customer and a patient i don't think they are able to do anything but take your money.
i'm a person who tries not to be a complainer in my reviews.... but their services are inadequate and suspect.

there drs here at this facility you can't understand almost 100% of them! there dialect. no english! like talking to at&t service department or billing department! or i should say you can't understand a word they say! i'm looking for a better hmo this one is horrible! there pharmacy's are horrible lines sick people everywhere. if you want to get better really isn't the place! they have tried to make it better but they brought on welfare patients making this facility one not to even walk into! now like all community hospitals.

i would recommend anyone who has a choice to avoid kaiser. i have been dealing with severe eczema for 45 years. there are now meds available that will most likely finally provide me some relief. kaiser refuses to prescribe the meds because it's not profitable for them. my doctor is rude and mean. the dermatologist i'm dealing with ignores my emails and medication requests. very negative experience across the board.
the worst center. waited over an hour to be called into urgent care; another hour to see an np (not even a doctor). they prob forgot about me waiting in the office.

my dr today took away my handicap parking which i've had for 4 years, i had a knee replacement surgery over 2 years ago and it was not a good outcome by another dr at the same place fresno hospital so i switched doctors, well he said an unfortunate knee with an unfortunate outcome, i go in every three months to get a shot in the other knee and every three months for bursitis in both knees and he takes away my handicap parking because it makes me lazy, i'm 73 year's old i walk my dog i go to the gym, take care of my house and yard, so when i go shopping it's hard for me to walk very far, i'm really sorry i didn't change insurance, but i probably will because of the 2 orthopedic doctors at fresno, california.

i came in tonight due to chest pains.  there was one person in the lobby. i arrived at 11:30pm and they gave me an ekg test and took me right back. everyone was really nice, but the emergency area was very unclean! the floors were filthy and when the nurse brought me back to a room in emergency, the sheets were stained. i asked for clean sheets which i received. because i didn't want to go to royal oak beaumont, i came here. it will probably be my last time here. i've never seen an unclean hospital. it gave me the creeps.  all the nurses i met just graduated 8 months ago!  everyone has only been there a few months. where are the tenured folks?

do not under any circumstances go here. whatever your emergency, go somewhere else. i took my boyfriend here last year because he had an intermittently racing heart. i wanted to go to a real er connected to a hospital, but he wanted to go here because it was closer and there wouldn't be a bunch of people in the waiting room. the positives ended there.

the nurses and doctor convinced themselves we were drug addicts and kept insisting that we weren't telling them the truth. okay whatever, i get that drug addictions are a problem in florida but we don't do drugs and didn't ask for any medication at all. we figured after his urine test they'd realize they were mistaken. 

his urine test came back clean, so that should've been the end of it. but instead the nurse concluded that what he gave her wasn't urine! excuse me? she told him to provide another sample while she was in the room, so he complied and i held up a sheet to provide some privacy. when the second urine sample came back clean, she was forced to finally accept reality, but nobody apologized for bombarding us with demands for "the truth" nor for delaying medical care. 

they decided to give him a medication that made him extremely tired. i was just about to leave the room to go to the bathroom when a different nurse came in, an older white woman with glasses. she said they were discharging him, at which point i told her it might be difficult to wake him up. she said she'd wake him up. she approached his bed and to my horror, violently and rapidly shook him from side to side while loudly saying "that's enough!". enough of what!? surely she should understand that he's groggy from medication they provided? it seemed like she was still convinced we were drug addicts, reality be damned. my boyfriend has multiple preexisting spine injuries including herniation, which he told them about upon arrival and they noted on his medical chart. we'd been there all night, i was exhausted and now terrified, i just wanted to get him home and away from this violent nurse. when the medication wore off, he had whiplash!

thank god his whiplash healed. he tried to contact them about his mistreatment, but the emergency center couldn't have been less interested that their employees are so obsessed with phantom drug addicts that it interferes with their ability to provide medical care, and that a nurse brutalized a patient with spine injuries noted on his chart.
absolutely fantastic rehab center! i've never seen a nursing staff (and support staff) so attentive to the patients. definitely the place to go for geriatric inpatient rehabilitation.

i went in for a knee injury. the pa did a bad and cursory exam (i am a surgeon, so i know), ordered the wrong test, gave no crutches or pain meds and misdiagnosed me. i got a bill after blue cross for over $1600. avoid this facility if you want medical care.

the er doctor i saw was extremely aggressive and literally yelled at me for both my anxiety and my physiological orthostatic issues. he badgered me almost like a cross examination in a courtroom about the possibility of pregnancy and my sex life. just run a test lol, why are you screaming at me? i told him i couldn't be pregnant because i was celibate (my husband is away), and he ridiculed me for my 'sad life' and gave me creepy looks. it was beyond insensitive. another doctor made insulting remarks about my face, strongly implying i was less homely with my glasses on, and looked like 'two different people'. again, super weird and gross and inappropriate to say the least. it actually really upset me and any kind of stress is really bad for my condition. 

some of the nurses here are really nice, and a med student spent a lot of time with me, giving advice about my condition, even though he didn't have to. i wish he had been my doctor!!! he was so caring and attentive. the younger people here seemed much less jaded i guess and treated me like a human being. 

the room i had was great, very private, pretty decent food, and a lot of television options.

i had a scary finding on my echocardiogram that has even to this day not been explained to me, no matter who i contact.

had a test done here outside the er and the doctor was on his phone the entire time and he too was not very nice overall. 

i did appreciate the discretion when chest tests were done. not once was i exposed, so that was nice. but some of the doctors here really need to take some sensitivity training, especially when dealing with nervous female patients. the way three of them spoke to me (but especially the gruff er doc) was quite shocking. it should go without saying that remarking on a patient's personal life and appearance is wildly inappropriate and unacceptable.

the rescue squad took my husband here with copd and asthma acting up very bad. chest tight and  having trouble breathing and they are such a screw up and just don't care about the patients. they admitted him and yet will not use the iv for meds when they said they would treat this aggressively if he got admitted. they hardly give him anything but neb txs which he can take at  home. the nurses are awlful and you call them and they take their time coming. he keeps saying he feels  tight in his chest and he is being ignored. this hosp needs to be shut down as they are horrible. all they want is your money and will tell you anything to get it. they are not even truthful.

if i could give zero stars, i would. last october, i came down with intense flank pain, sweating, and nausea. it was a kidney stone. i knew because it was not my first kidney stone and those symptoms are hard to forget. my employer told me to leave work early and get medical care.

i tried an urgent care first, but they refused care because they didn't have imaging equipment to diagnose a kidney stone. i asked google for the closest hospital, because i was in too much pain to drive but had no one else to drive me so i needed to get there as soon as possible.

i checked in to ahmc emergency room at 12:30pm but was not attended to (other than a urine test) until 3:00pm despite being in so much pain that i was writhing and rocking, and had short/ragged breaths. and yes, i had taken pain relievers... 4 excedrin migraine, which did absolutely nothing for my pain.

once i got into a bed at 3:00pm, where i sat without treatment or fluids for another hour. finally, at 4:00pm, i was given toradol which relieved my pain for about 30 minutes, and 1 liter of saline. then, at 4:30pm, the doctor came to chat with me for about 30 seconds and tell me he thinks i'm an alcoholic because i have pancreatitis (a pathology which can also happen if you're in extreme duress, which i had been for 5 hours) and that he's holding me overnight.

i'm not in the habit of disobeying doctors' orders, so i allowed this and informed my employer immediately. no one on the hospital staff would tell me approximately how long i would be hospitalized, only that i would be going upstairs.

well, upstairs was even worse. i didn't get there until 6:15pm (nearly 2 hours after any pain relief had long-since disappeared), and an hour passed before i was even 'checked in'. around 10pm i was finally given pain medication, but they didn't bother to ask me what medications i respond to, just asked if i had any 'tolerance issues' (code for, "are you a drug addict"). well no, i'm not, but i am an advocate for myself when it comes to pain management and morphine, which they gave me, only causes chest pain and severe anxiety.

i immediately expressed this after the nurse gave me the morphine, because i felt the familiar symptoms, and he said, "oh, well give it some time."

i suffered for 6 more hours without seeing another person's face, although i could hear them talking just outside my room and ignoring my moaning/crying from the pain. the next time someone checked on me, it was 4am. i begged for something different, even the toradol that i was given downstairs because it worked. the nurse said he'd have to check with the doctor on call. i didn't see him again for hours and when he did come back he said the doctor refused the toradol because it's "bad for the kidney," all the while i've been given just 2l of fluid for the past 18 hours. hey, idiots, kidney stones don't spontaneously pass. you have to flush them with fluid.

i finally did get a norco at 10:30am, which meant that about 18 hours passed while i was in 11/10 levels of pain and completely unable to sleep or focus on anything else to take my mind off of the pain... and, once again, listening to nurses talk about other patients while they were right outside my door and had to have heard my cries. furthermore, they would not allow me to take any of my regular medications, which meant 1) no anxiety medication, 2) no sleep medication, and 3) no depression medication when i was still there the next morning.

i begged to be discharged, because they were doing nothing to treat my pain or the cause of my pain. and it still took until 5:30pm (seven hours after the norco) for me to actually be discharged so that i could drink water and pass the stone, which i did in a walgreens bathroom while waiting for the azo and diuretics they had prescribed.

a couple of months later, i got a bill that stated my insurance (which was a 10% coinsurance, mind you) covered all but $900. the original bill was over $18,000. there were fees on the list that looked completely fraudulent, like a $700 charge to assess pulmonary function. unless that was how much my pulse-ox cost, there is no reason i should have a charge for pulmonary assessment. and my 2 liters of saline? $298.

so there you have it -- 30 hours of my life wasted on lack of treatment, only to receive a $900 bill.

since this incident led to me losing my job because my boss felt like i had taken a "vacation" without warning, i didn't have the energy to fight the bill. i just paid it. but you should do anything you can to avoid this hospital like it's the actual plague. walk, take the bus or a taxi, or pay a random stranger to take you to another hospital because all you'll get here is people ignoring you and then asking for ungodly amounts of money for it.

just had my gi procedure yesterday at this facility and my experience was superb. the place was so clean. everybody from admitting, to gi nurses (cheryl and rolan), gi tech (george) and dr b riff were all commendable. they explained their plans and treated me with respect. everything went smoothly.

don't go here. longest wait time ever with staff that seems it's their first day. go to any hospital besides here. this place shouldn't be called a hospital. with a ridiculous small er waiting room, sick patients were sitting on the floor while a sad amount of staff walked past them until one finally asked to bring out chairs. no one should be on the freaking floor of a hospital.

i swear by valley. i delivered both my children here, and have had surgery here. the facility itself is kept nicely, always clean, spacious and smells nice. the most important thing about valley is the people. all of my experiences here for myself or visiting the staff is always very friendly and willing to help. they made some of the best, scary, and life changing times comfortable for me and my family. 
the signs direct you where you want to be, there is valet for visitors, and a full cafe and gift shop for your convenience.
if valley is an option take it, and ask for extra heated blankets !

i went to valley hospital back in august with extreme pain in my abdomen where it felt like very tender lumps. the waiting room was very busy and i waiting over 3 hours knowing i had to get to work in the morning, if nothing was wrong. after waiting 3 hours the dr. didn't think it was anything serious but wanted to do a few more tests. i have add and severe celiac desease and i couldn't sit there any longer. i said i wanted to leave and come back within the next day or so. they said fine, i asked if the can just start where they left off and not have to register all over again and they said we can do that. my insurance co pay is $200 and that why i asked because i could not afford to pay another $200 upon returning. they said i would not have to. i came back 2 days later and guess what? i was charged twice for my copay because they put it as another visit to the hospital instead of using my registry from 2 days prior. now i've called multiple times and no one seems to care and i cannot pay that. i hope someone that can help me is reading this review. very disappointed with the valley hospital in ridgewood!

this is a horrible hospital.  first, they failed to read my mammogram until i called to follow up because i hadn't received my results which they promise to communicate within a week. i was told they they hadn't yet read the mammogram over a week later. i am now battling breast cancer. my treatment was delayed because of valley hospital and their negligence in my medical care. i am now dealing with their incompetent billing department because they keep sending me a bill with no explanation of what the bill is for.  i have asked for a detailed bill of the services they are charging me for which i have not yet received after multiple conversations with them.  i did, however, get a letter from a bill collector for this bill.  i always had the intention of paying the bill - i just wanted to know what it was for which i don't think is too much to ask for. this is causing high stress during a time that i am not supposed to have any stress! i do not recommend valley hospital!

came here to visit a friend. when you pull up toward the front, they have valet service, courtesy of lincoln varsity in novi. the front desk service was very friendly. during the christmas season, a full manger with all the fixings, it was so beautiful in the front lobby area. the concierge directed to the correct hallway and set of elevators to the direction we needed to be. seems like most of the staff was friendly and ready to assist and serve you. i'm not one for staying in hospitals but this really didn't seem or feel like a hospital, more like corporate offices and everyone was tucked away in their cubicles.

it is a great hospital, my father stayed in this hospital several times, and received very professional and caring medical services. 

highly recommend!

worst hospital experience ever! not inly do we have to go to another hospital because the doctors here did not do a full check of my wifes problem but the nurse was very unprofessional too with drawing blood it went everywhere. this er will kill you!!!!!!!!!!
the emergency staff suck! first off the people checking us in took their sweet time laughing to even call us up for like 10 minutes. it's called emergency for a reason but they don't get that. and once we finally were checked in the people that were calling names didn't even say it loud at all. it's 3 am some people have the flu and can't help but doze off. i'm one minute away from here but unless it's a true emergency i'd probably just go to another hospital next time.

horrible emergency room.  we went there when my 13 year old son had abdominal  pain (it turned out to be a kidney stone- after  i took him elsewhere).  providence left him  writhing in the waiting room while they saw other patients who were less acute first.  beyond having poor judgment they seemed to be completely understaffed. still, they manage to get our complete financial information before they even took his pulse!

so far, in general, i found the care and treatment at ascension  a+++
the doctors and nurses especially the specialist are wonderful. 
i did have a problem once with an emergency when i went in for a kidney stone and was in horrific pain. the staff that night was slow at helping me out. especially when they weren't busy.

this hospital is first class in every way, the best of the best top to bottom. it's been a tough few years with hospitals for my family and we were all amazed by the hospital itself as well as the staff.

pity the patients that have dr.michael kirsch as anesthesiologist for he sure won't make you feel less anxious or comfortable.  maybe he chose his profession because he does not like to engage with anyone awake.  did he ever have a course in how to deal with patients?  how to be kind? make them less fearful? speak humanely to them?  then there's the nursing assistant whose nose kept dripping mucus.  and she's working in a hospital!!  a hospital employee who does not stay home when sick?  incredible.

worst hospital in the county. rude and disrespectful doctors. useless staff. i wouldn't recommend anyone go here. i'll never give this place my business again. in fact they should just shut the place down. i've never been treated so rudely by doctors in my entire life. what a terrible and humiliating experience. do yourself a favor and drive an extra 20 minutes to huron valley. hell i'd drive a couple hours to avoid this place.

frustrating hospital. it's closest to where my dad lives so we will spend a lot of time there, no doubt. the parking lot is like a corn maze. and the nursing station in the emergency department is a loud flurry of social activity. my dad was in the er overnight and the nurses at the station seemed oblivious to the fact that they were caring for tired, sick patients. i could hear them talking about their holidays, their weekends, what they are for thanksgiving, while watching my dad try to sleep. they were sooooo loud. two words for them: "indoor voices". if i talked that much on the job at their age, i wouldn't have had a job.

i had my mammogram performed at the facility on medical center drive. was greeted immediately, asked to fill out certain forms and taken back fairly quickly. i had tracy performing my mammogram and felt totally at ease with her calm and informative demeanor. she performed a 3-d mammogram, as it does not cost the patient extra. she wanted to take an extra film due to her personality of going the extra mile, rather than put me through another trip back.  i was so very happy with this well-run facility.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare Shady Grove Medical Center

review: my father is  kaiser patient he was finally transported to holy cross silver spring for further care for a sepsis infection.  i have attached 2 photos, his room at shady grove and at holy cross  both taken at same place, at the door entering the rooms.  take at look at both and ask yourself which one you would prefer for your 88 year old father suffering with an extremely serious infection.   i hope this post is shown to the president of shady grove but i'm sure it won't be.  how they keep such great nurses in that kind of work environment is beyond me.  pictures do not lie.

was told that my folder would include some info on how to find the results of my bloodwork after i was discharged from the er...no paperworks on that...called a couple phone numbers but received scam answers strangely...kept on calling but got passed around as a ball for 30 min...no one seems to know what's going on...

unprofessional and disorganized

review:
2 stars only because the awesome, underpaid staff is so stellar.  i want this hospital to be great....really i do.  have never stayed at sg but have had er visits for stitches for self and child. 

recently, i had a scary incident at home and called 911.  the wonderful paramedics were able to address it at home but were very forceful about my going to hosp to get checked out.  i told one of them i wanted to go to to suburban because that's my doc's hospital, but since i live so close to sg, they said that would be impossible.  i was told in the past by a much more assertive woman i know that if you push it, they will comply.  but i didn't.

the er nurses were incredible - angels. the docs were very nice and seemed knowledgeable.  they could have let me go home, but decided that i should stay overnight to be on the safe side.  i refused some meds-a shot to the gut. whaaaaaaaat?  no.  it was about 2 am at the time.  i could have walked out, but my husband and the docs, i decided, were right.  that's when things went downhill. 

the room i was assigned to was right next to nursing station.  so very noisy.  it was literally freezing in there.  not enough blankets to be comfortable.  the nurses were lovely but they kept coming in and out instead of doing what they intended to do the first time.  then they'd burst in, throw on that damned stark white overhead light and ask 25 questions that required cogent responses.  problem with this and probably most all hospitals is that cya and $ hold precedence over patients' health.  this is the *hospital policy*, not the employees' faults, but they lose good people because of it.  

finally a doc came in, said he would have let me go last night and kind of muttered about the fact that 2 short procedures would/could be done before i left.  but no one came to do them.  i waited for hours.  finally i found my nurse and said, "i'm leaving and will take responsibility for not having the procedures.  made an appt w/my doc and he'd take care of it. true, i did make the appt and he said he could do one of the procedures. he felt the other was not necessary.  

she summoned the the way overworked "hospitalist," who said i couldn't leave w/out the procedures.  she didn't mention the magic exit, which is to sign a release stating i didn't comply w/medical directives or whatever.  i said i "need to get out of here."  patients were ill all around me, coughing like they had the worst pneumonias, whooping coughs, etc.  i thought hospitals were very concerned with people catching infections while there and wanted them outta there asap, also $$$. i was going crazy.  finally had the 2 procedures.  then the waiting till i was told of the results and hopefully, released.  i tried to find my nurse, over and over and over.  finally found her and she said i'd have to sign the release. i said, "hey that's fine but *i* complied, i did the 2 tests. you guys haven't held up your side of the bargain...i should have had the results hours ago!"

she said the hospitalist had to sign the release! omg. she finally got ahold of her.  the woman looked like someone had dragged her behind their car.  she's young, very smart and competent, but they are killing her! i actually felt sorry for her, everyone was calling, approaching her, pulling at her.  that is *just* inhumane.  these cheap arse hospitals lining ceo's pockets with money and understaffing to keep it that way should be thrown in jail.....for life.  she was very nice, pulled up my results, signed my forms and i was so outta there!!!!!!  i could have cried, i was so frustrated and needed to get out of that place. 

this was disorganization at its worst.  the nurses were, overall, incredible.  but no matter how good you are, you can't do this job alone or be pressed this hard and retain your quality and/or your attitude!  i totally get that. 

at the *very* most, in the am, i should have had the two tests (15 min at most), gotten my results immediately and been sent on my way.  if they had needed the bed, magically, i prob wouldn't have *needed* the tests anymore. 

this place needs to get their act together and treat their employees right.  hire more people and get your procedures in place.  i realize there are  priorities among patient care, but a hospital or any health care facility, had to have have enough committed, serious people so that you can keep the process moving efficiently.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare Shady Grove Medical Center

review:
honestly, this place is a mess. i've been admitted there via the emergency room and to do out-patient procedures. i've had the nurses release me from out-patient procedures and forget to remove my iv port (which i luckily noticed before i got to my car). i've had them make a data entry mistake on my address and received threatening phone calls months later about bills i didn't receive because they put it in the system wrong. if your insurance doesn't cover the full bill, they will call and harass you at least every two weeks and give you a count down a deadline to sending you to a debt collector on as little as a $200 bill, even if you're making payments (but they don't deem them enough). i had two bills and they gave me 3 months to pay off one of the two when they were collectively about $1000. they legitimately call my cell phone all the time during work hours regardless of my making payments. 

i will say, the overnight nursing staff when being admitted are absolute saints. also, the er wait is not so bad. so, not all is lost. but, never again.
fac_name: Adventist HealthCare Shady Grove Medical Center

review: dr. brent cardwell is nothing short of amazing. from checkups to getting our five month old through flu a (so scary!), we are incredibly pleased. dr. cardwell is professional, kind, knowledgeable, and all around wonderful. we're grateful to have found him for our most precious little one. the checkin and checkout process is also super easy and the receptionists are personable and kind.
fac_name: Cedar Park Pediatric and Family Medicine

review:
we've been taking our now three year old to this practice since we moved to cp about two years ago, and now take our newborn.  we primarily see dr. moore, who is absolutely lovely--but we've seen a variety of other doctors when she's not available, and have never had a bad experience. some of my favorite things about this practice include:

-after hours and same day appointments are available. a few months ago, we had to pick up our daughter from preschool because she was ill. strep was going around her school. we got her into the doctor that evening, the test came back positive, and she was on antibiotics in time to miss only one day of school.

-the doctors are incredibly supportive of breastfeeding. despite my son's jaundice, i never felt pressured to switch to formula. rather, dr. givner worked with us to create a feeding schedule that minimized supplementing with formula while we waited for my milk to come in.

-the doctors ask about, and care about, the health of the whole family. when i came in for my daughter's three-year-old check up in the middle of a rough pregnancy, dr. moore took time to discuss how i was doing. the postpartum depression screening at my son's two week check up was more than pro forma. 

i could go on and on.  we highly recommend this practice.
fac_name: Cedar Park Pediatric and Family Medicine

review: asylum hill was my obstetrician, and is now also our pediatrician. when our child needed a specialist, asylum hill assembled a list of the most qualified experts, filtered by our insurance, recommended three of them, and provided a referral to the one we chose. the. same. day. the pediatric care is beyond excellent. the doctors explain everything they're about to do so my child is at ease during the exam. the doctors ask questions directly to my child, treating them as a whole individual, with a mind and voice of their own. nearly 10 years as patients at asylum hill, and the staff still remembers "when your child was born, we all thought they'd be a redhead, but the platinum blonde was amazing, and the sandy blonde now is very charming." and we normally only go for our annual well-child visit! why i gave only 4 stars: parking is often a bit of a squeeze, and, because most of the physicians are residents, they only stay three years.

i came to the er after experiencing some back pain and vomiting. there was concern for meningitis as i had been exposed to it earlier in the week. i went to the er early afternoon. it took a while to be called back after checking in. but, once i was placed in a room i was greeted and examined promptly. the medical staff made me feel calm and comfortable, they were very professional and reassuring. overall a good experience.

i take vocal lessons.   in late december i was referred to this place by an ent specialist for muscle tension dysphonia therapy.   i heard nothing from this place for weeks (i usually get phone calls from places that receive referrals from my doctors.)   i called them and they had my referral, and told me that they get "hundreds" of referrals a day and don't call people.   so, i made an appointment a month or so in the future, and an hour before the appointment (thankfully) i did get a phone call from someone telling me that my appointment was for a physical therapist when what i needed was a speech therapist.   (this person noticed "dysphonia" in the referral.)  then i was told they had no speech therapists, and i was given two numbers of hospitals i could call to, well, start over again.    the carelessness i encountered here was almost breathtaking.

i was referred here by my primary physician, a sharp doctor, who suggested i explore outpatient services.  i called and answered a few questions, then was called by an admittance administrator who said they would only admit me as an inpatient.  despite both my own and physician's feelings that felt i would be fine with outpatient services, this facility denied me access based on a single phone call... no offer to meet in person, explore my situation, etc.  clearly they were more interested in the revenue from a mutli-week stay.  thankfully i didn't enroll and with the help of my physician, no longer find the need to explore any options.  before wasting many thousands of dollars at this facility, be sure to explore others who actually care more about people than profit.

i have successfully received the majority of my care from physicians affiliated with nmh.  therefore, when i had a problem with my foot and did some research about the different treatments available, i chose dr. sisson's practice.  since his partner did not have an appointments available for six weeks, i saw dr. sisson. what a mistake!  he refused to discuss the treatment about which i inquired and instead described an invasive procedure in brutal terms.  he commented rudely and intentionally about my age, which visibly embarrassed his resident.  i was appalled by his insulting manner, his refusal to adequately respond to my questions, and his lack of interest in my physical ability, which would have informed a better course of treatment.

i love this doctor!  i was hospitalized at st. davids with a bowel blockage and dr. vineet choudhry was called in to follow my case in the event i would need surgery.  he was excellent and i truly believe that his expert directions were the reason i did not need the surgery.  (he canceled a medication that had been ordered by a gi doctor that should not have been.) he even spent time explaining to me my entire ct scan and all that it revealed--not just the bowel issue.  he went above and beyond the expected service.  i hate to admit it but he was the only doctor assigned to me during that visit that i had faith in. 

due to the way this form was set up i was forced to put in info on my office visit which i did not have but i have spoken with his office assistants and they were quite friendly and helpful.

overall, general practitioners are ok.  specialist services are better.  our girls' pediatrician was a wonderful doctor who truly looked after each of them until he retired---kind, patient, and relationship-oriented.  

based on our family's collective health experiences, the quality of services vary by department.  
podiatry department is consistently helpful and supportive.  
dermatology department can learn basic care from podiatry.  
auditory services were special.  
cardiology care was excellent. 
pharmacy wait could be better.

empathy is key.  even if it's evident healthcare workers cannot fix a problem, a patient in need simply needs to see that he or she is heard and understood.

tip of kaiser: it's better for kaiser workers to err on the side of overflowing kindness than curt reprimand.  you will get better cooperation when you are kind to patients in need.

my doctor at kaiser vallejo is awesome. i've seen her for 15 years. she referred me to bariatrics back in 2005 because i was very challenged losing weight and was at 320 pounds. i went to the kaiser bariatric program in richmond ca, and yes, they make the patient go through all kinds of psychological tests and all kinds of classes so we can make an informed decision about whether or not to have weight-loss surgery. here's my warning for anyone thinking about having radical weight loss surgery. they'll teach you about not being able to take nsaids, drink alcohol, eat more than 5g of sugar, no time-release or extended-release medications, etc. the problem: you don't know what is yet to come. i developed osteoarthritis years later. what is the treatment for osteoarthritis? nsaids. unless you have ever had osteoarthritis, you don't have any clue how painful your life is going to be. the only pain-relieving alternative (legal and permitted by kaiser) is narcotic. percocet works really well on osteoarthritis pain. but it wears off after 3.5-4 hours. that means on really bad days you take 6 of them. a 30-day supply is 180 pills. 

kaiser used to provide 200, so there was always extra and refills were about every 4.5-5 weeks. then the government's war on opioids kicked in, and that overshadows patient needs. if someone is in pain, and has no other options for pain control, too bad so sad. sucks to be you. now kaiser limits to 90 tablets for 30 days. they wear off after 3 1/2 hours so that means more than half of the day is spent in pain. and there is no other option. i've complained all the way up the chain at kaiser to no avail. there is not another option and no fix. my recommendation to anyone considering bariatric surgery is fine out before you proceed what your options are if, 15-20 years down the road you've got arthritis that has you in pain most of the time.

all of that said this kaiser is awesome. i just wish they recognize that some patients are in real pain and are falling through the cracks and they need to find a way to address it.

review: can not say enough about choc. if i could give 100 stars, i most definitely would! i will forever be grateful to each nurse, doctor, volunteer, cafeteria, child life, specialists, and any person associated with this hospital. my son had severe asthma attacks for almost 4 years. every single visit that ended up at er, icu or just admitted to regular floor was exceptional. everyone's focus was my son and his well being. there will never be enough words to express my gratitude to everyone at choc!
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital of Orange County

review: my 9 year old sister was transferred to choc from a local emergency room with signs of pericardial effusion that resulted in a 2 night stay. the nursing staff is amazing, the doctors on the other hand were not. besides guaranteeing the flu shot wouldn't cause any side effects- which is did, he also released my sister although she was having breathing issues still. 2 days later, her follow-up appointment at another facility, new x-rays were ordered and they found pneumonia. maybe take some time actually evaluating patients instead of being in such a rush. what a shame. also said she was good to go back to school the next day of her release. imagine sending a sick child with pneumonia around other kids?! thank goodness we kept her home.
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital of Orange County

review: after taking my daughter to the pedestrian, she recommended i bring my daughter to choc children hospital. i was hesitant since i had previously taken her to saint joseph urgent care and had a horrible experience ,i didn't want to go thru that again and be told she just had seasonal flu. however i knew i had to take her because she was spiking a high fever , when i got there they had plenty of parking, i arrive on a wednesday and the waiting time was just an hour .. after the check up they told me they were concern with her breathing and were going to put her on oxygen.i was worried sick but the nurses were so kind and explained in detail what was going to happen, we stayed over night from wed-sunday morning. i can honestly say the staff was very sensitive and kind to my child, offering her toys and answering any question or concern i had. i can thank you enough for making my baby feel well! cleaning crew is amazing they stop by every morning making sure everything was sanitized and clean..
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital of Orange County

review:

fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital of Orange County

review: this is one of the worst service provider i've had - trying to make an appointment was bad - rude, unhelpful stuff on the other end; but cancelling the appointment was even worse - 20 minutes waiting on the phone listening to the useless info, again, the person on the other end could not care less. just such an unpleasant experience, i am thankful that it was not an emergency and i had an option of going elsewhere.
