review: i took my son in this morning due to a fever and a cough. the front desk ladies were so sweet and greeted me the minute i walked in. the doctors and nurses showed nothing but care for my son. i honestly will never take nun to a regular hospital or urgent care anymore. the service was so different here. thank you choc
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital of Orange County

review: attention all parents!! do not use valet parking .. i understand that it's convenient but i want to let u know that on 1/10/20 i took my daughter to the er and since it was an emergency i decided to use the valet ... i was there for over 6 i arrived early and left by night time.. the following morning as i was leaving to go buy coffee i noticed one of my car's rims was badly scratched.. i immediately knew that one of the driver's at choc had to of hit the curb while driving my vehicle.... since i'm the only one who drives my vehicle i know i didn't hit any curves and my car is brand new i've had it for 3weeks i bought it off the lot with zero miles and it inspected with no damages.. i called choc and spoke with chris the supervisor in charge and his answer was we are not responsible for any damages cause at choc and i told him so if one of the valet drivers crashes someone's car he isn't liable and he said nope!! smh this is bullshit and he said i will review the video recording to see if i see the crash .. after 2hrs he calls me to say that unfortunately the are he parked my car has no camera's lmao so convenient huh! so he tells me that all he can do is provide me with customer service phone number so i can file a complaint, however the damages to my car would not be paid for.. i already had a rough night considering i spent so many hours in a hospital with a sick child and the aftermath just made my stress even worse ! this is such a awful experience and i wish i had just parked my car myself.. i guess i will have to pay the $150 for the rim repair
fac_name: CHOC Children's - Children's Hospital of Orange County

review:
my grandfather was a great guy who alway's allowed to do thing's on his own.. very independent man who never let anyone help him...he got sick and got water in his lung's when we found out we immediately started searching for places to where he can be in short term.. we started searching and found arcadia which had a few bad review's but the place looked beautiful... once we called to go check the place out we spoke to ana which was very brief, very specific, very nice, sounded friendly, and most importantly was very patient with us while explaining our situation... we then started the process of getting all the paperwork ready and we also went to check out the place and we loved it staff seemed very nice and helpful and also the cna's were very friendly and sweet. i also met a don or dsd who's name was melissa? she was a true sweetheart very funny, hugs smile when i walked in and very friendly....once visiting my grandfather his usual cna's were katty and marleen i want to thank them  very much for all their hard work and dedication and having so much patience for him while he was going through a tough time i just hope i can one day pay you back for all you did for him..!!! thank you guys for always asking him if he needed something and being very attentive with him and his needs i will soon be back to visit.. thank you all staff for being good at what you do 
 sincerely amanda.

this hospital has terrible service. my mother has been up there for a week now and the room went 3 days without being cleaned. still we have to make the nurse call every day for a cleaning. they just changed the gown she has been wearing the entire week. only because she asked. there is zero pro activeness in this hospital. she falls so she needs the nurses to come help her to the restroom. many-many times (diff shifts) there has been times she calls for the nurse and gets 0 response. one time all the patients were calling the nurse and the nurses phone wasn't on those patients. tons of mistakes. 

if you have a loved one please refer a different hospital. the hygiene is my biggest concern. i changed the linens on day 5 of her being there for the first time. the rodeway motel next door changes bed sheets everyday i bet, why doesn't the hospital? 

this hospital is not proactive. its only reactive. you have to ask for every little thing. i'm afraid to see the conditions of the patients that don't have lived ones visiting teling them to clean, change the sheets, change her gown, help her to the restroom when the nurses don't respond for 15 min, 20 min. i'm sure they are going on themselves.

my wife has worked at hca hospitals for nearly 40 years. i have been very happy with all aspects of care i have gotten up to 3 years ago. (and i have been a frequent guest at palms of pasadena). my last several visits have fallen very short of there historical level of care. the last time i was in the pcu i was literally ignored both in terms of attendance by the care givers (and apathy) and no one seemed to listen to what i or my family was saying. i left worse of than when i went in, but i could no longer tolerate the atmosphere so i said all was well just so i could get out. at this point if it was not for the only insurance we can afford (hca united health) then i would never go back. as a matter of fact, i will have to be near death for me to ever go back. if you can go somewhere else then i recommend you go there. david bowen

on new year's day and due to a  painful canker sore under my tongue, i visited the er. the moment the nurse saw the sore, he expressed his concern of being an oral cancer symptom. days before, i saw a doctor for this matter and was asked to visit er if not feeling better within 2 weeks. i could not believe, i was asked by dr. williams, to make a follow up appointment with my primary doctor for her to give me a referral for a biopsy. i was expecting something to be done in a more promptly matter, especially after disclosing other chronic health issues. my doctor was fully booked until tomorrow, which is one week after my visit to your facilities. hopefully, it will not be cancer. if it is, i have lost one week of treatment.

took a bad fall last night at a restaurant, wet tile and heads don't mix. 
   since i know enough regarding concussion care, i chose to go in for a scan this morning. 
  i can't say enough about the care i just received in their er!  everyone was fast and caring about my head issue.
pa heather is top notch as are all the others i encountered.
   wonderful experience! 
though the head  will hurt awhile longer, the team there didn't make it worse!

had heart catheterization this week. registration was easy, prep
and instructions were efficient, procedure was on time and painless. a big thanks to nurses lisa, monica and mary for taking
good care of me and my family. a very grateful heart to dr.chris
hadad for his expertise and bedside manner!

just to be clear... zero stars

spent 6 hours in the er tonight. 6. was having chest pains and went in - got into a room straight away and was told to expect a 3 hour visit with all the testing and everything. i waited 2.5 hours after my second cardiac enzyme test and finally got fed up so i hit the nurse call button to get an update because no one came by to check on me or anything. it would be amazing if shannon er could make sure that their patients feel noticed and cared about. 3 hours after the final test i finally told my nurse (who was very sweet) to please take the iv out of my arm, i was leaving. anyway, don't just leave us with a call button and not come back for hours. it's really uncalled for.

(update)

and to top of the lack of concern for my well being.. i just received a call from shannon. an automated voice call from pam bradshaw to follow up and see how i'm doing. i didn't stick around on the line to hear "press 1 for great, press 2 for not so great." do better shannon!

they gave my boyfriend stitches because he gashed his leg, but they did a really poor job. some of them fell out, and some of them wouldn't come out. the nurse said she's never had so much trouble removing stitches. now he has to have plastic surgery to get the remaining ones out. there is one all the way under his skin and the have to cut him open to get it out, which means he has to get more stitches after that. nice job leominster

thank you to all the staff at la habra convalescence hospital for making our stay here a very productive recovery. special thanks to the physical therapists romel and robert for getting my wife up and mobile after her knee replacement. also, thanks to lupe, laura and maria s. for the extra special care. thank you to monique for all of your hard work.

finally, thank you to the rns klaudia, darcy and gina for understanding and respecting the pain management regimen from other issues. the occasional nurse who didn't and thought they should override the pain management doctor's regimen are the reason for the four stars and not five. 

we will definitely hope to stay here when she gets the other knee done.

dad was here for about 2 weeks following a hospital stay at pih. staff were great from day 1 and honestly felt like they cared. rehab team were amazing and right away started getting him back to normal. according to him only complaint would have been noise level some nights but got better after mentioning to front office and administration. thank you to all la habra staff for taking care of dad.

i had a surgical operation to remove chronic otitis media and restore the eardrum in january 2018.
during the operations when i was under the anesthesia they inserted the urinary catheter. after the operation was completed and i was released home, i started to have severe bleeding from my penis. they didn't tell me that a urinary catheter was inserted in the hospital .i was very scared and thought that maybe i started having kidney problems due to anesthesia or drugs.my family urgently took me to the emergency room. there the doctor told me that during the surgery  the urinary catheter was inserted and my bladder was damaged, and the catheter was inserted incorrectly. ear surgery was also unsuccessful.eardrum perforation has not been eliminated and hearing has not improved .

review: the worst medical center ever! i don't understand how it's still in business. dawn (head nurse) is the most unprofessional thing walking the halls. the sense of care and urgency is not on the rating pile when it comes to this er department. georgetta was the nicest and sweetest person. not sure why the military refers soldiers here, however this will be the last time. this review is just the beginning of the complaint process.

from the time i first checked in with the admitting desk, throughout my entire time in the emergency room and finally upon being admitted for observation, my experience was seamless and without flaw.  the group of doctors, registered nurses, nurse's assistants, registered therapists, nutrition services and servers along with all others employed at the florence/steward hospital are amazing!  their professionalism, medical knowledge, compassion, integrity and genuine people skills are rare and unique to find assembled under one roof. 

i would not hesitate to refer anyone to the florence/steward hospital.  i know this is the third owner, but possibly the third time is the charm.  the attention and care i received was very good!!

i'm writing this bc my husband and i are sick to death of the legal system and medical system. my husband has a daughter who is type one diabetic. we live in texas and his daughter in arkansas. we have to do almost all our interactions by phone or my chart. currently his daughter is being seen by dr hutchison. i am writing this under the hospital name for a lot of reasons and will write under any name that is associated with her to get the word out there.  he has standard custody where he gets her one weekend a month and every summer, holidays blah blah!! jan 13 his daughter was hospitalized for dka, blood glucose of over 700 . which was after we sent numerous messages to get help from her endo here in texas and then to the endo there in arkansas hoping they could work together. also so we could let them know how poorly his daughters diabetes was going after all we have access to her blood glucose 24/7 bc of an amazing ap. something was obviously wrong. sadly all that effort went ignored by them and every other medical person!  then our daughter ends up in picu for two days. since then we have been trying to wrap our mind around. how this could happen with all the contact we have been giving them. now we are told they can't talk to us , we have to use our attorney to talk to their attorney, and that he can only know stuff about his daughter when she is in his care!  yes we will use our attorney, but i guarantee you it won't only be for his daughters health from now on... it will be to su them for keeping his daughters health from him which is super illegal. not only have we found out his daughter has been hospitalized numerous times prior to this one , cps has been involved, yet we have never been contacted by anyone! we find this out after we recieve the requested 302 pages of medical records! 
the other guardians swear that dr huthison recommended our daughter get a type one diabetic tattoo, so they got her one. we asked the doctor and she has yet to deny it.  let's not forget she is 14 years old.  we are quite sure a bracelet would suffice. 
so on top of horrible medical practices and illegal medical practices, while his daughter was in the hospital we spent a good hour of our life in the record dept - jessica the original person we spoke to - we emailed and she uploaded our custody agreement stating we can have access to her medical records, sent us the mychart info, they made copies of our license , and got our forms filled out with our socials, and find out we can't take the medical records home til our child is checked out of hospital. which at that time she wasn't. so we are told to call tomorrow and they can mail them back to texas. we called back 2 days later and spoke to wendy, who mind you was rude as all get out, at one point refusing to help us bc i was upset that all our personal information was lost, and we are now in texas, we were just in arkansas! 6 hour drive! they wasted our time and lost important information. who wouldn't be upset. on top of this your child was just in picu. zero understanding coming from these folks. 
they could not locate our documents, anywhere!  i spoke to the manager diane, and she was more helpful, i explained the situation to her and she did her best to right a wrong but still our personal information was lost in space.  we did end up getting the records but this just shows that every aspect of this hospital is just awful and it's the blind leading the blind. 
oh, i failed to mention virginia, who works on the child picu floor, i assume is a greater of some kind really has a way with words. she sits at her little desk as you come off the elevator and thinks she's pretty important. she offended me more than once. they seem to favor one parent over the other at this hospital, they  kept referring to my husband as a visitor and not her father, and even when i told her , he is her father and he is on the custody agreement - she has to throw  her opinion in on the subject when i asked her why she did that. she said "evidentially y'all did something wrong not to have guardianship of your child" wow. just can't believe my ears . at this point - this hospital just sucks. i am blown away at how divisive it is towards mixed families! i blacked out the names but circled the rights my husband has to info on his daughter, that the docs and hospital claim he doesn't have !  please if you live out of state and your child goes here, pray as hard as you can , bc you won't know or hear anything about your child from them, until a shes dead! sad day in america and for our family. 
btw(some pics i uploaded aren't showing up) if you want to see something or share this post, hollar and i will be happy to send you more details. hoping this will go viral.

this review is for the ob/gyn office. 

i understand that we live in bfe and that there is more need than there are providers to provide for it. however, this is not the fault of the patient and they are the ones who suffer for it.

it is not the patient's fault that there is one ob for the entire area. when someone moves to fallon and is pregnant, there is no option but to go here. the doctor seems to play a bait-and-switch game with patients after initially meeting and it can ruin the experience for a pregnant woman.
 
i am one such pregnant woman. i have an extremely anxious personality and am no getting no help from this practice. the main doctor who is assigned to me is never available to answer questions or concerns and i am always fobbed off to the physician's assistant, who also has no time or concern to help. i have seen the actual doctor exactly once in 33 weeks of pregnancy. i have seen the physician's assistant for every other appointment that is scheduled for the doctor and she is brusque and unfriendly. every concern i have is condescended and brushed off with a general air of "just deal with it." 

now i have anxiety to the point of not being able to function and no one will do a thing. i have called and insisted that i want to meet with the doctor and been flat out refused. i have requested medication and again been refused. i have been to the er with panic attacks for weeks and begged to just talk to a doctor to calm my fears of delivery and been told no.

the doctors in this practice don't care about the health of pregnant women and just show up to deliver and then disappear again. we are nothing but vessels for babies and not worth helping in their eyes.

if you have tricare, my advice to you if you're pregnant is to make sure you hang out near reno when's it close to your due date and then just go to the nearest hospital there. banner churchill is the worst thing to happen to pregnancy in fallon and no one cares to do anything about it.

administration at this hospital is substandard to other hospitals i've used.

lost records,  lost faxes, lost doctors orders from my oncologist.  

then there's the matter of where to park here...

in summary: i hope the medical care is better than their office procedures.

do not go here if you ever want to see your medical records. i've been working to get my medical records from winter haven sent to another facility for two months now. winter haven has refused to share my medical records. this is hindering my ability to receive treatment from the second medical facility. even with the second facility's efforts to request my records, winter haven will not release them.

this is unethical, defeating, and the opposite of patient-centered care. go anywhere else.

i came into the er with terrible pain in my neck. i have dealt with chronic pain for many years. i wasn't sure what had caused the increased severe pain in my neck, but i suspected it was something i'd done at the gym. from the moment i walked into the er until the moment i left, the care and treatment at wakemed north was superb! in particular, jon c., a rn there, adam z., a pa there, and sarah l., another pa provided outstanding and exceptional care! i have been suffering for so long without the proper pain management and care for my spine, and probably the most valuable thing i received during my visit (in addition to the medications they gave me for pain) was a referral from adam z., pa to cary orthopedics to see dr. sameer mathur. after reviewing dr. mathur's education and his practice in cary, i was thoroughly impressed by the cutting edge procedures he offers. i now have an appointment to see him this upcoming monday. i was treated kindly, compassionately, and respectfully by everyone at the wakemed north er. the facility was very clean and very comfortable. i would go back to wakemed north er in a heartbeat, and it will be the only emergency room service i will go to, should i need to go to the er in the future.
fac_name: WakeMed North Family Health & Women's Hospital

review: had to come here for my daughter to get a mri and some other medical procedures. the staff working in radiology and mri were all very professional and caring, doing everything they could to make sure my daughter was comfortable and not worried. every time we have had to come to this hospital, i cant remember anything bad to complain about. if you ever have to come to atlanta for the children's hospital, this is the place to go.
fac_name: Children's Healthcare of Atlanta - Egleston Hospital

review: i came here because my 4 month old had been crying in pain inconsolably, and i believed she may have had an ear infection. it was past my pediatrician's hours, so the er was our only option. when i checked in, i said it was for an ear infection. when the first nurse saw us, i told her i thought it was an ear infection. when the second two nurses took us back, i told them i thought it was an ear infection. when the doctor came in, i told her i thought it was an ear infection. she barely looked in her ears and said that because she was so little, she couldn't really see in her ears to tell if it was an ear infection or not, so she instead diagnosed her with a cold. they suctioned her nose and sent us on our way. we got through the night, and i wasn't convinced it was a cold, so i took her to her pediatrician. he looked in her ears with no issue and determined that she in fact did have an ear infection. i paid $260 here for the doctor to tell me she wasn't qualified to diagnose my baby. if i had not gone to the pediatrician, i wouldn't have been able to treat my baby correctly, and who knows what would have happened. i literally told them from the second i walked in what i thought was wrong, and they still couldn't figure it out. the only reason i'm not giving one star is because they got us in and out really quickly and everyone was very friendly.
fac_name: Children's Healthcare of Atlanta - Egleston Hospital

review:
awful, awful, awful overall experiences over an almost 5 years time. i switched from family health center due to never having the chance to form a real bond w/a doctor. now, 5 years later, i have had 4-5 different practitioners & i'm tired of it. dental has helped but also have not. i was in a bike accident & lost a lot of teeth & crowns. they made partials, only one works. i'm now waiting for a new crown & then i'm going to a specialist.

now, let's talk about behavioral health. for five years, i have been seeing dr. melissa deer. it is mostly for my chronic insomnia. i used to be able to come in & talk to her, now all she does is type & refill prescriptions. right now, today, i needed her help & she refused. i have tried for months to get a therapist appt to no avail or mismatch or more therapists leave.

i have had enough, this is not medical care, this is not supportive care, they operate to save their jobs not for the patients.

i'll be searching for a new provider!

review:
my wife and i delivered our baby here on 1/22/2020. we were floored by the service we received here. the nursing staff, devonie, amy, tonya, emma, and alicia were all amazing and godsends. dr. bergman, our ob doctor was also fantastic. we had such a great experience here. being that this was our first baby they really made us feel really comfortable and relaxed. 

the l&d unit is really nice. they have the whirlpool tubs which was an added bonus. they allow four visitors at a time in the postpartum unit and also require an id or dl in order to visit. 

overall our experience here was great and we'd definitely deliver here again!  thank you to the amazing staff.

i had a great experiance with the whole staff recently for some routine tests, but i want to give special recognition to the phlebotomist frankie. completely painless blood draw, smooth as silk! and frankie was a kool cat as to boot. props!

i was seen here after having a power tool accident and and the staff were so awesome and friendly. dr. soper was extremely friendly and kept me and my family comfortable. extremely grateful for dr. soper and the sutter health staff for turning my traumatic accident into a delightful visit to the er.

great experience. my husband dropped a angle grinder on his foot and we got in quickly. rachelle soper was our doctor and she was amazing, nice and very professional. beautiful stitches, she also noticed a cut tendon so she recommended us to a great orthopedic doctor.

i am writing this review on behalf of the er staff nights. my mother was in an emergency situation and brought in for cardiac arrest. the entire staff was awesome. the charge nurse morris managed our expectation and checked in with us often. winnie the rn and the other staff worked so hard for mother. dr. rond was very professional and compassionate, he genuinely cared for my mother's well being as well the family. we will forever  remember how much empathy the staff extended to us all. even the er security innocene, treated us with care . truly unforgettable. thank you!

this hospital looks like a welfare clinic bad service, i was waiting for 3 hours never got admitted i left the waiting area and went to urgent care. next time i'll go to john muir hospital better staff. no wonder this hospital ain't rated top 5 sutter health hospitals. very poor service

been in the er over 3 hours. nurse came out  and said we don't have a room for you yet and hopefully another md starts soon and then things will pick up. i'm in pain but  probably going home this is ridiculous

front desk rn spends her time yelling at everyone & having a bad attitude in front of all the patients in the waiting room. she always gets the security dude in trouble for no damn reason and it's annoying to have to hear her complain the entire time. we were in a car accident and didn't get to see a nurse till 2 hours after.

my wife gave birth here and my son was in the nicu for nearly 3 weeks. the staff, from the valet's to the security to the nurses and doctors, were all wonderful and made a hard experience far easier to deal with. 

not only was everyone very professional, kind, and compassionate but they took wonderful care of my wife and son. my wife ended up having to have an unplanned c-section and they helped to make what was a scary situation as easy as possible and made us feel like we were in great hands through the whole experience. 

when my son was born he ended up having some complications and had to spend some time in the nicu. the nicu nurses and doctors were without a doubt some of the most profession and caring individuals i have ever had the pleasure to work with. they took wonderful care of my son and made sure no stone was left unturned in making sure he was healthy by the time that he came home. 

i cannot thank the wonderful staff at this hospital enough for all that they did for my family.

this review is specifically for the physical therapy office at 18111 brookhurst, suite 2400. last thursday, my wife went to see a doctor at memorialcare for neck pain. after receiving a referral from the doctor, we contacted physical therapy. we were happy that they had a same day appointment since we were already there, but then were informed we could not be told how much it would cost, their insurance person wasn't there. so instead, hey gave an appointment for the following day. after arriving and asking, how much the treatments would cost, we were told, our insurance person wasn't there. so my wife asked, could someone call us and tell us how much the sessions would cost. during the 15 consultation, the therapist recommended six sessions. when checking out and trying to schedule those appointments, we were informed that they had no appointments available for over 10 days. a week later, when we received the call from john the manager of the facility, we were informed the 1 hour consultation (which again, took about 15 minutes) would be $315, $300 of which we would have to pay, because of our deductible. when i protested and recommended we only be charged maybe a half hour, although sympathetic, he said no, they had things they had to do for the appointment, such as figuring our the insurance (?). when i asked about cost of future appointments, they were also $315, which (with insurance) we would have to pay $60 in closing, how is it that to see a physical therapist even with insurance can cost three times more than what it cost to see the doctor that recommended the therapy?

review:
this review has nothing to do with the great doctors and nurses here at cedars. 
it has to do with the cleanliness of the waiting area. 
nicu waiting room is disgusting.  we've been here for 4 days, and the trash has not been taken out, chairs and tables are filthy. i had to ask the secretary to call for cleaning and for gloves and wipes to clean where i was going to sit.  chairs look like they haven't been cleaned in months. 
cedars-sinai needs to up their game with cleanliness. nothing like ucla. their employees actually respect management.

cedars-sinai medical center is the closest medical facility to me in beverly hills. there are two towers on beverly bl: the north and south towers. the emergency room is in the south tower, with entry on gracie allen drive.

have been coming to this medical center for over twenty years. as recently as last week, i did not feel good, and had symptoms synonymous to a heart condition with shortness of breath. historically, and with family history, i had a genuine concern and checked into the emergency room. my vitals were taken shortly thereafter, but after that, i waited nearly 4 hours before i was admitted, not happy, zero star!

the emergency room was crowded with patients and severely under staffed. fortunate to be physically fit but even athletes can suffer heart related issues, and i didn't want to take a chance. 
i checked in on a friday early afternoon and needed  medical treatments, tests and procedures and ended up staying for a week. that week was probably one of the worse experiences i had to endure with relentless injections, to administer medications and or draw blood for more lab work. i felt as though my blood was being sold, with the multiple amounts of blood taken from me. my arm was bruised where injection needle poked me. also, for nearly 6 days, i was feverish, as high as 104 and was freezing, yet was not allowed to have anything more than a bed sheet...i could have contracted pneumonia as a result.  i was freezing, dehydrated and desperately lacked rest and sleep...all of which added to my illness.

the nurses were attentive and seemed genuinely caring and they deserve a 5 star. the nurses seem to be more aware of department schedules and special units. most of the doctors that checked on me seemed to be clueless, promising me one treatment and no being able to deliver, due to schedule conflicts and just pure ignorance of the medical facility's political processes. in my observation, most of my attending  doctors looked to be recent graduates and lacked systematical training. also, lots of these doctors seemed to have been imported other countries and continents and lacked communication skills, some barely spoke english. did cedars compromise patient care with cheaper quasi doctors from other countries to lower their overhead salaries? i had better dialogue with the nurses who all spoke english clearly.  many of the treatments i received were administered by nurse practitioners, who were all very efficient and respectful and again deserve 5 stars. 

cedars-sinai is regarded as among the best medical facilities in south california for having almost any complex procedures not offered by many hospitals. many celebrities often come here for medical attention. although i am sure the staff are instructed and trained to maintain patient privacy, i am not convinced lots of the star struck staff adhere to those rules. i am not a celebrity, but i insisted my personal information remain private and insisted on mostly female staff as much as possible and was accommodated 85% of the time.
despite my request for privacy in a private room, i had no privacy, with constant gawkers of male staff coming into my room, pretending to do something to take a peek. i had a sheet over my head to mitigate that bothersome parade of gawkers, so unnecessary and very annoying. i didn't even have the energy to scream them out of my 'private room.'

this last weekend was not my first or last time at this medical facility but hope that any future visit will be much improved, the overall rating is more deserving of a sad pathetic 2 star...with as much funding cedars-sinai received from generous donors, room for improvement with better quality trained doctors, staffing is desperately needed, so patients receive care asap and not have to wait a long suffering 4 hours, which is unacceptable.

$5300. this is not a typo. i cannot image how the services provided warrant a bill this large. stunningly ridiculous.

dr. kosari is a terrible, careless, incompetent surgeon. do not trust him. i've made that mistake twice, so i'm not sure which of us is the bigger idiot. i've tried to summarize my experience with him below, but happy to describe in more detail through message for those considering a surgery with dr. kosari.

in 2013, i started to develop an umbilical hernia just above my belly button. it was never that noticeable, but in the spring of 2019, it had grown just enough to always be noticeable to me. i was referred to dr. kosari. i thought that the reputation of cedars-sinai would hold, but i was wrong.

in the examination, dr. kosari was friendly, but clearly rushed. he let me know he only had about 10 minutes. i explained i'd had the hernia for a few years and, while seated, he asked me to lift my shirt, briefly touched the belly button (literally for less than a second) where it was visible and that was it for the exam. he said he'd recommend doing the surgery with stitches, not mesh. knowing nothing about the difference, i trusted his judgment.

the day of the surgery, i was a bit tense as this was my first surgery. i was also concerned he had not adequately inspected the hernia (and he had not ordered any type of ultrasound). i waited for about 2 hours and then they took me in to prepare me. when i saw dr. kosari before the surgery, i explicitly asked him, "so you are going to be able to fix not only the part below the belly button, but also above it, right?" dr. kosari responded, "yes, don't worry. once we're in, we'll be able to check it all to see what we're dealing with."

i woke up after the procedure and went home. i had the surgery on friday, sep 13. i removed the bandage (which was covering the belly button and surrounding area) and showered on sunday, sep 15. by monday, i felt the hernia above my belly button exactly as before the surgery. panic immediately struck. i called cedars-sinai and was able to tell dr. kosari's nurse i felt a bulge exactly like the hernia, and she told me to just come in for my checkup in 2 weeks for dr. kosari to examine it.

when dr. kosari examined me, he tried to say there was nothing wrong, or that it was something else (like a result from the surgery or a problem with "skin" being "detached"). i told him, "no...i am 100% sure this is the same hernia i've had...it feels exactly the same." he told me to come back in 4 more weeks after the recovery period "to see if it's still there." that really aggravated me, i left the appointment knowing i still had the hernia, but he wouldn't acknowledge it.

at the next appointment, he acknowledged i still had a hernia, but never acknowledged it was because of his carelessness. compared to the first surgery, he was pushing much more strongly for not operating again. i think it's because it would make him look bad to have to repeat the exact same surgery, but i scheduled a follow up surgery for dec 3 anyway to get it dealt with once and for all (had already pretty much met my out of pocket max, so thought why not - and couldn't get in to ucla before the end of the calendar year - book ahead!).

on dec 3, i had the second surgery, and this time we did an ultrasound before the surgery. again, he did not recommend mesh, just a single stitch he said. this time, i didn't notice the hernia for a few weeks, but could definitely feel a slight bump, which i thought might be the stitch or something. now, just over 6 weeks since the second surgery, i still have the hernia. i can feel it exactly the same as i used to.

after one surgery, i'd expect a hernia to be fixed, at least for a few years before it might recur. after two surgeries, i would really expect a hernia to be fixed. now, after spending thousands of dollars, taking months off from the gym for two separate recoveries, and still having the problem that was supposed to be fixed, i'm so filled with anger and frustration about this "doctor." he is careless, negligent, or uses poor judgment in making choices for his patients' care. 

please, do not select this doctor. i will be seeing dr. chen from ucla instead....happy to compare my experience after my third hernia surgery for the same hernia. in my last check-up after the second surgery, dr. kosari told me, "if it comes back let me know and we can go back in there with the mesh." to myself, i thought this moron will never touch my body again. don't let yourself become another one of his mistakes. i will forever regret it, but hopefully i can get a successful surgery from ucla and eventually put this behind me. but i'm sure i will continue to live with the nightmares about the hernia problems that i've had ever since the first surgery was unsuccessful, i hope you can learn from my pain and experience to avoid the same experience with this terrible doctor. cedars-sinai should not allow this man to be operating under their name.

as they say, "fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice shame on me." he won't be fooling me a third time.

i am an rn with a master's degree and was also an aprn for 10 years. having been a healthcare provider for many years, i am saddened to write a negative review of a hospital.

i was sent to the er by my primary doctor's office. when i arrived at ascension seton hays county er in kyle, the waiting room was not overly crowded, and it was evident some of the people were not patients but family members of patients. i was optimistic for a quick visit. 

i made sure to confirm that not only the hospital but all related to my care would be in-network with my medical insurance. i knew seton was in-network, but i did not want anyone involved in my care who was not in-network. i know seton has not been very good about this in the past.

after i was triaged, i was told to sit again in the waiting room. since i had to use the bathroom, i was directed to collect a sample. sitting in the waiting room holding a container of urine on my lap felt incredibly awkward. in fact, i was so embarrassed that for part of the time, i felt compelled to put it in my handbag. 

when i was called to the back, i was led to a stretcher in the hallway. that is where i remained throughout my care from assessment through treatment through discharge. 

way back in nursing school, i was taught to always introduce myself by name and role to each patient, for instance, "hi. i'm sandra, and i will be your nurse today." i consistently did this throughout my career regardless if i was wearing a name tag or id, and i strongly believe that every provider in healthcare should do the same, from technicians to nurses to physicians. during my visit at seton's er, some staff did introduce themselves to me such as ashley (the triage nurse) and the er doctor. however, there were others involved with my care who did not. 

from my place in the hallway, i had a front row seat to everything. the patient in the room next to my stretcher was obviously dying. family members sat next to and stood near my stretcher. i felt like i was intruding on their grief. as a caring person, i wanted to reach out and provide support, but i kept quiet since i really should not have even been aware of what was going on with them and the patient.

at another point, i heard a commotion going on behind the head of my stretcher. it was not particularly loud, but i heard security involved, and i felt frightened. i did not dare turn around to see what was going on, but i did watch as security walked a man in handcuffs down the hallway. i hope i had not been in any danger.

when my iv was removed, a band-aid was placed in my antecubital space where the iv had been located. shortly after, i noticed my arm felt wet and cold. i looked down and saw that i was bleeding profusely and that my beloved sweater was getting soaked with bright red. a nurse (well, i assume she was a nurse; she never introduced herself) brought over a bottle of hydrogen peroxide and a stack of gauze to remove the blood. she started the process pouring the peroxide on my sweater, but it would take a while to remove such a quantity of blood, so she left me with the supplies to continue working on it myself. finally, i got my sweater mostly clean, but i was left very wet and cold.

it was taking a long time to get final lab results, and then i learned that the lab had lost my specimen! how does that even happen? is the lab not in the same building? a mishap like that does not instill confidence. hopefully the lab does not also accidentally mix up samples or misread them or misreport them.

i spent almost 4 hours at ascension hays seton to have a few simple tests done (no imaging) and a medication administered (a push, not a slow drip). it was not like the er was chaotic. in fact, i watched many staff sitting behind the desk for much of my time there.

close to the time of my discharge, i was approached to sign a consent to treatment. it seemed quite late to be asking for that. i was feeling so frustrated by that point that i signed the various forms without reading anything. i was also told that with insurance i owed $*** just for walking into the er (the amount did not include tests, etc.). she wanted to collect money right there on the spot. i handed over my credit card, thinking this trip to was the biggest waste of money and time i could have imagined. i dread thinking about the remainder of my bill still yet to come.

every staff member i encountered was nice, and i appreciate them. still, i would not recommend ascension seton hays er in kyle. obviously, i strive and wish for good health and hope i never have to go to an emergency room again. however, if i do, i will first check into my other options before heading to seton.

i am waiting in the lab after waiting for 45 minutes to register.  so far just to have labs done, i have waited over an hour.  the lab person greeted me with "have a seat it is going to be a wait." not a pleasant greeting,  just the unpleasant way. they do not recognize how to protect your privacy. the lab teach asked questions in front of other patients that i would have preferred to not share with strangers. if you have to come to this lab, try to avoid it. terrible experience.
the worst experience ever. stay away from this place if you value your life or your loved ones life.
fac_name: Huntington Beach Hospital and Medical Center

review: i'm here tonight because i'm struggling to breathe. i've felt like i've had the flu for past week. i've done nothing but listen to every employee bitch about their job and their co workers. i got pissed at the young xray dude because he came to get me without a wheelchair, ran to get one for me, and decided to take the pretty young girl with the same flu as me in the next room first. passed me right up while i got up to get in the chair and told me he would be right back for me.  when i scolded him, he totally ignored me and showed no remorse. i've now been here for 2 1/2 hours and they have yet to do anything to releive my struggle to breathe. but i can hear the breathing treatment going on in the next room (did i mention she came in a good half hour after me?). they had me do a urine test when i first came in and my piss is still sitting by the sink.

my son had to come in due to he was dehydrated, all cramped up, got here at 3pm not really busy at all,  several people have come in after us and been in and out as we still sit here and it's now 6:05 pm, more frustrated at how many people have come and gone already and they were here for "colds", "flu like symptoms.  bad, very bad service, shouldn't even be one star.

my husband had gotten bitten by a feral cat and we needed to find a clinic or er that evening after everything was closed. they were great and took good care of him and he did not have to wait and it was just an all around decent experience.

i was quickly checked into the emergency room. i received great care while there and when it became evident that i would need surgery the next morning i was given a room upstairs. the care there was even better. the nurses and cna's who assisted me during my 2 days & 2  nights stay were attentive and kind. the food was pretty good for hospital food (except for the chicken soup don't order that). overall i received excellent care.

i've had several issues with banner health, and i try to avoid them at all costs. however, last week, i dislocated my knee while ice skating and the ambulance took me to this hospital. it was a generally pleasant experience at first, they were nice when my roommates came to visit and the nurses were sweet. however, two days later, i went back to banner for a follow up appointment and i got hardly any information besides a " you're fine and keep doing what you're doing". i had to get an mri as well, they weren't going to schedule me one for another week but i pushed to get one the next day. there was no after-visit summary or anything. when i got there the next day to get an mri, they weren't ready, they were still turning on lights in the waiting room, and overall it seemed incredibly unprofessional. three days after my mri, i still hadn't received my results that they said they would call me for. after calling them myself, they informed me that they've had my results since about an hour after my mri, but they never told me. when i went to pick up my results, they didn't have a copy yet, were unprepared for me to come even though i called ahead, and overall communication didn't seem to be a priority. when i went to a different orthopedist (at a different location), i was told that i needed a new brace, possibly surgery if it didn't improve, and physical therapy, which i was not told at banner health. overall, my biggest flaw with this company is that they are very unprofessional and not very good with time-management. the nurses at this location are very sweet though, as well as the security guards. i've never had an issue with them, and they supported me when i was angry at the rest of my visit. thank you to them! however, if you can help it, stay away from northern colorado medical center.

i absolutely cannot say enough about how well i've been treated in my 3 visits to this er.. i'm not really sure how you leave a review for an emergency room.. i'll just say that everyone i've dealt with has been professional and courteous.. they have gone out of their way to take care of and comfort me.. i know that there were more pressing emergencies, but i've never been made to feel like i wasn't important.. let's hope that you never need an er, but if you do, you are making a mistake if you dont come here!

great place to receive outpatient physical therapy. therapist are very well trained and considerate and listen to any issues that you have. the pool area is checked throughout the day and evening for cleanliness. dressing room is very clean. someone was in shower area so no pictures of that but i've found it to be clean on every visit. thank you brandon for the fantastic service it feels great walking without my walker and cane!!!

of all the hospitals in the metroplex, tx health is the place i'd be if in need. my wife had gone in for a simple procedure, and was very well taken care of. the staff and attendants are professional and friendly, and the facility is spotless. best around!

my wife and i were taken to this hospital in may 2019 due to a car accident.  the medical/er care seemed adequate.

the customer care followup to resolve billing issues or questions is pretty weak.  after finding out that they do not bill your medicare part d plan for meds that they get from the local pharmacy, i tried to pay online at the site on the invoice that i received.  that url is no longer valid.  i found the correct site, but it would not accept my zip code as a valid zip code.

after multiple messages to the customer care email with no response to the zip code issue, i finally gave up and found and dusted off my checkbook and paid via mail.

my grand children (twins) were born at this hospital, the team in labor and delivery were amazing! that was nine months ago. my second child had his baby at the at the same hospital two months ago and ended up having complications, the hospital and all of the teams that helped her did a fantastic job.  the hospital is clean, organized, modern, and staff could not have been more helpful, and kind.  thank you to a wonderful hospital!!

i had scheduled an appointment and canceled well before the 24 hour notice and canceled due to me finally getting service from my primary doctor in stafford. low and behold i keep getting a $25 no cancellation fee bill in the mail. of course when i called they said i never called. i just paid the fee and i still get bills! so i'm furious

this is the absolute worst er in all of cypress dare i say houston. i took my wife in because she was complaining about pain in her abdomen. we walk in around 3:30am talk to the front desk and fill out some paper work. the first red flag was the urine sample. i know it's standard for women when it comes to the lower abdomen, so i tried to ignore it. the guy at the front desk was very helpful. but he was the only one. an admin came to see my wife and asked if she would pee in the cup to which she said no because it isn't an obligation. the admin then replied "that's ok you're going to be here a while". it's sunday morning there were maybe 7 people in the er so i ignored it and she finished her paper work. a few minutes later the admin comes back for more general information. my cue to take my wife and leave should have been right after her first comment. she proceeds to ask for information like her address and social, but while doing so she was making snarky remarks and snide comments while trying to laugh them off as a joke. i let it slide seeing as how i just wanted her to get the care she needed. but the admin wouldn't let up. she was dropping inappropriate comments about our children and the fact my wife was "young" shes 22. we know the process of an er you have to wait because it's typically full on the weekends. another young girl walks in with her sister for the same issue and they immediately take her to the back. i noticed she wasn't handed a cup either and they gave her the utmost care to the point even my wife pointed it out. they took her ahead of us. this is an er you can't set an appointment smh. whatever. we waited 4 hours eventually i went to the front and asked what was going on because there were about seven more people that arrived after with non life threatening injuries (nobody came in an ambulance) that went before her and the front desk clerk assured us we would be next. they finally call my wife for her scan and rudely denied me going back with her. "you cant come!" and wheeled her off. she was a little worried. i waited for her return and when she came back she informed me that not only was the tech not professional she was very rough and ignored my wife's request that she be gentle all the while asking personal questions that did not pertain to her reason for visiting. she even told me at one point the tech told her she wasn't sick without a scan or examination first! when she was called for blood work (which she denied because she's anemic) the nurse was rude saying "so youre denying the bloodwork?!" very loud and very unprofessional. i stepped in and said yes she is and we requested the dr. let me say this dr vu is hands down the worst er practitioner in the state of texas. he talked over my wife. denied her feelings of pain and told her it was all in her head before she even fully explained what the problem was. i stepped in and politely but forcefully told him to listen to her! to which he finally shut the hell up and listened and had her taken to the back for a bed. 


this is where it gets absolutely terrible. we waited in a wing with no patients for another hour i guess it was the shift change no big deal. the nurse comes in and asks for a completely different person who was a male. they finally get it together but the entire time my wife is being talked over and dismissed by multiple nurses. at this point i'm getting upset so i step in and have to tell the nurses and dr vu again, to pipe down and listen! 

dr vu tried to press my wife about denying the blood test which i tell him to make it happen. we waited for 5 more hours to get her blood results when we were told it would be 45 minutes. meanwhile my wife kept pressing the call button due to the pain and she got no answer. i walked to the nurses station and they were texting and joking. when i asked for their attention i was met with a "what?!" i had to walk away. luckily one of the professional nurses rushed over and helped my wife. upon her helping suddenly dr vu was available again and told us (after my wife told them she didn't want the blood test) that her results were inconclusive. we received her discharge papers and found she was charged for a completely different scan than what we asked for. 

i stood in the hall way for hours watching nurses walk by while she was writhing in pain without even checking or asking if we were ok. she was rushed through her paperwork and nobody explained anything. 

hca cypress discriminated against her because of the color of her skin. i found their instagram and sent a message about her mistreatment and they blocked me. 


this is the most racist unprofessional prejudiced er in houston please do not bring a loved one here they will waste your time disregard your feelings and dismiss your claims of pain. 

hca cypress should be shut down! 

i wish i could give them no stars

dr. cooper was awesome and treated my children very well. i just love how they cater to your children regardless of the illness. they have always been my first choice since they specialize in all illness dealing with children.

the nurse are always prompt and very courteous and very emphatic to your situation. they always listen and some go above and beyond to make sure you and your children are comfortable as possible. the doctors were very attentive to cupcake situation due to us not being able to pin point what set off the severe reaction of hives and swelling.

the place is always clean when i go so never had a problem there.  there's always ample parking and valet if you choose . they were packed so many babies, toddlers, adolescents and teens were sick. so you know we all had to wait patiently. kudos to the er nurses who kept their cool, made their rounds and continued to check up on everyone who was still waiting to be seen.

our experience has been less than stellar. let's start with we were over billed at check in. we had an extremely long wait time even though we showed up early to our appointment. the procedure my son had done wasn't terrible so there's that. 

what i can't understand is why it's taken two months for the billing department to rectify their mistake. i had to bring this to their attention. children's did not take ownership  and proactively address their mistake at all. they allegedly cut a check actually blamed the usps and said that maybe it could take weeks for a check to go from plano to allen?!?  

i absolutely would not recommend this place and after chatting with a few medical professionals about this whole awful experience i've learned this hospital isn't even that great!

the 8 hour wait time (documented)in the er waiting room was appalling! i'm pretty sure if those hospital workers were in my shoes, they'd be pissed as well. my family and my child should have been treated with better care and compassion from the health care professionals there; along with the other patients waiting with their ailing child. not saying that my childs' illness superseded any other child there, but having your pediatrician call the er ahead and advising you to quickly get your child to the hospital, arriving within the hour and having to wait 8 hours to be seen by a doctor is piss poor! the senior leadership team may need to be aware of this.

the wait time here is terrible. i went with my son who hurt his actual eyeball, and they didn't exactly take life, limb or eyesight very seriously. i get that they are busy, but we waited 6.5 hours to be seen!!!!!

my grandmother had an appointment at 1:30 pm for an mri; she was seen at 3:45 pm. she was not told what paperwork she needed to bring and had to go back home to get it. this is absolutely ridiculous and completely avoidable.
they do the best they can. people don't understand the healthcare worker side of it sometimes, hence the bad reviews.
took forever to be seen and nurses didn't know how to take blood pressure.  waited  an hour+

having a close relative in the hospital can be a miserable experience - - unless you feel like your relative is getting the best medical care available, from an experienced, caring physician. that's what i experienced at southern california hospital in hollywood.  the doctor's name is salam alkasspooles. 

my daughter was recently hospitalized for two weeks, and dr. alkasspooles was assigned to her case. after a few days, i had become increasingly distressed because test results were inconclusive. every time i spoke to dr. alkasspooles, he made me feel better. i felt like he was listening to me. he made it a practice to return every call i made to him - - usually on the same day. i felt like he cared about my daughter, as if her health and her progress really mattered to him. she wasn't a number to him; she was a person. he listened respectfully to everything i had to say. he went waaay beyond duty to make me feel like he cared for my daughter, and for my concerns.

if every physician could be as competent, sensitive and caring as dr. alkasspooles, the world would be a very different place. don't hesitate to go to southern california hospital at hollywood. if their physicians are all like dr. alkasspooles, you'll be in the very best of hands, and have the most caring, responsive and competent medical care available.

0 stars
rude staff. no formal training in patient care or customer service. avoid this hospital
i was born at this hospital almost 50 years ago. i would like to know how to talk to someone at the hospital privately to express my gratitude.

walked up to the front door and security sent me around to the other entrance.  went to the other entrance and they sent me to the front door.  finally an employee smoking on the side let me in..  both doors were locked during business hours.  no one working here actually wants to work.

outpatient: 
i mostly come for surgical specialities. i followed my surgeon from bwh. 
notes : i love the front desk staff ! very efficient. they work hard to get you in for radiology appointments. nice , clean waiting area. 

nurses: heather is my favorite. 

registration: so nice ! sometimes it takes a while but they are friendly and will make nice small talk with you. 

outpatient radiology : nice staff ! great techs who remember you as an inpatient and are glad to see you showered - haha. i've only had a few outpatient appts in radiology. most of my experience is inpatient. 

er: had to come once when my feeding tube clogged post discharge. i paid a $150 copay and my insurance paid $$$$$ for ginger ale and a huge syringe. it worked ! but ugh.  

inpatient : so i had major surgery here february 2019. total gastrectomy. this is the reason for my lack of yelp reviews this year. :)

5 stars for my wonderful surgeon and residency team. 
5 stars for my nurses and cnas (maybe one nurse and one cna gets one star- the rest were amazing.)
0 stars for the nurse/patient ratio !! my lung was collapsing and i was sitting up and i had to wait 45 min for my nurse to lie me down. she literally told me she couldn't help me until she was done with intake and had help!
5 stars for all the techs and docs in radiology. a little tiring to be asked if i am pregnant when my body was ripped apart and sewed back together but whatever. i wasn't asked once -  i was asked every time!! sorry but there is no way the story has changed. yay protocols. 

i was lucky to have a private room. i have no complaints of my accommodations. my son liked my bed better than i did. he mainly liked my tv. he wants me to go back so he could watch tv!!!!

that damn icu bed though. that's supposed to be a better bed. my tiny bony body hated it. it felt like lying on a giant bag of raw carrots. !!! if i wasn't so wiped from my inability to breathe and having my back cut open for a chest tube , i'd cry about it.  i mainly cried about the chest tube and having to use the bed pan. 

and bedside phlebotomy! the phlebotomists were nice (and really great patient advocates when it comes to telling nurses when drawing blood isn't safe) but it was rough those mornings! i had 2 ivs in each arm which is apparently not safe for blood draws without that central line. so one arm would have to be turned off and then they'd have to come back later to poke me. you don't want to know what my arms looked like with 3 weeks of daily pokes!! 4 stars. for torturing me they lose a star. ha. 

transport would get on my nerves because it was as if they never had to transport a patient with multiple machines before. it was always a debacle to get me ready to go to radiology , etc. 

some would even let visitors be on the same elevator as me. my 1, 2 and 3 week dirty hospital patient self on the elevator with random people avoiding eye contact with me. not fun. made me feel more subhuman than i already felt with a large scar splitting me in half, connected to tubes and lines galore. very rarely able to wash my hair, at least in the first 2 weeks. i didn't want other people seeing me. i had a ton of transport services so this wasn't the norm but when it did happen it was upsetting. 

waiting for them after my scans to take me back sucked too. ugh. they were nice though.  so 3 stars ?

after all my other surgeries i was walking the next day. this hospital doesn't give walking epidurals or something (i can't remember the reason). but i was in bed for like 4 days before i could walk. i did not like this. 

i can't comment on food because i was npo. 

if you have a feeding tube , don't let the nurses put that sticky protein crap in your tube. it will always clog it. fight the reasoning. nutritionists mean well but they aren't feeding tube savvy. and they don't have to deal with being rudely awoken by the beeps of your pump not working anymore. get your surgeon involved. i was discharged with a bunch of packets and told my surgeon i refused to use it. he agreed. 

pt is fine. they are helpful. 

you have students coming in and out. let them in. it's a teaching hospital! 

a lullaby plays every time a baby is born! (i personally know several cha obgyns and if you are looking to have a baby you are in amazing hands. my experience is surgery only !)

i honestly only came to cha for my surgeon. i wouldn't come otherwise for surgery. nothing against cha. but the nurse to patient ratio is enough to keep me away.

my mom was a patient at 6 north and it was horrible. i noticed many safety violations happening throughout stay on floor, as well as hippa violations, and negligence. management was no help, was promised "safety is #1 priority" by laurie bausk, nurse manager only to see patient safety disregarded repeatedly. 
there was a great and knowledgeable nurse there gina but she was outnumbered by bad nurses like krista who told my family "she may never be the same again and may end up in rehab for the rest of her life." thankfully she was wrong, as they were wrong about a lot of things during her stay. i also had a safety issue and asked if the nurse station would screen visitors and that we only wanted certain people to come in the room, i was told no. my mom was roomed near loud nurse station were patients were talked about poorly. the kitchen and housekeeping staff were more uplifting than the floor nurses. i won't even touch on the way we were treated and talked down to by internist megan b. callahan, md who misdiagnosed my mom and just wanted us to be happy they were wrong. she had a preconceived notion about us and it showed on everything she did. thankfully she was replaced by jeremy sylvan, md who knew his stuff and also cared about the people he treats. they were more concerned about which insurance was paying for the stay and were going to discharge her without treating the reason she was admitted. it made a scary experience worse.  1 month later and myself and my mother haven't heard from patient relations although we have contacted them numerous times, my emails have gone ignored. maybe the not caring about patients comes from the top? also finding our more bad things about my mothers care and treatment during stay. if im lucky i will get her in a new hospital system that cares about patients and knows what they are doing. my mother had no insurance at time it was pending if she did i believe she would have been treated a lot better.

the doctor was being a complete dick head. as soon as we got to the hospital he greets us at the ambulance and is genuinely concerned. i tell him what was going on with my mom(she has messed up her back, and her pain tolerance isn't high so she was in tears) and his attitude isn't the greatest, but i just brushed it off before maybe he was having a bad day. but what happened after we got in the room is very unnaceptable, and highly unprofessional. i hear him mumble to the nurse and i quote "let's see how full of shit she is about all this". i try to remain cool and not smack his shinny ass bald ass fucken head because talking to someone of higher power in the medical facility would be more professional. his name is joe leary, and we already asked if we can have another doctor but he was the only doc on shift tonight.

i went into the hospital er for abdominal pain and rectal bleeding today friday 2/1/2020 around 10pm.

waiting room had about 8 people; patients, friends, and family included. i had my vitals taken with in 15 minutes. one patient gave me the stink eye because i was called in just before them. the triage nurse that took my vials asked if i had a history of hemorrhoids, i said yes but 12 years ago after having my daughter but i had surgery to remove it and have not had an issue since.  i added that i had 4 bowl movements in the day and the started normal then turned into diarrhea with severe burning and bright red blood.  

she diagnosed me with a hemorrhoid and suggested that i take a laxative. 

then i waited two and a half hours. 

i went to the triage desk, no one to befound. i could smell chick-fil-a so i looked into the other bay windows where the triage nurse popped her head out. i asked how much longer, she said let me look. she had a two minute conversation with the other nurse about being short staffed. she then walked around the corner with a full mouth of food telling me it'll be another twenty minutes, maybe. then she went back to her meal. i left.

dr t newton advised to do chest x-rays without examining my son. he then said " what do you want me to do then".  me: "examine him like a doctor does; and tell me if his lungs are clear, as i am not a doctor", "my son has asthma". 

this seton is exactly the same as i remembered 15 years ago when my son was born, absolutely horrible care. was praying for improvement since it's so close and convenient. dr. t newton is sarcastic and just plain rude.

i arrived this afternoon right at 5pm. i had a blockage in my stomach called a good bolis. i was in a ton of pain. i was taken back to a room within 30 minutes. professional and caring nurses took very good care of me, very quickly! not to mention a doctor that made everything move fast. i had lab work, fluids for dehydration, x ray within an hour and was on my way to have an edg to remove the blockage. surgeon and staff in the or were just as amazing. i'm from fort worth and completely out of my comfort zone. they made me feel important and cared for! i can't thank them enough!! out of the hospital and back at my hotel within 3.5 hours.

excellent experience in the surgical center (cataract  surgery). everyone we encountered was friendly, helpful, and professional. many hospitals have programs to ensure that patients have a good experience, but this often  results  in inane checklists, canned questions, etc. but seton nw is getting it right. their people provide top quality care with excellent personal attention. well done!

you want to see one of the most tone-deaf hospital, visit this. sad. as soon my son was taken to er twice, they want to do every test possible. worse when the staff came and asked "have you signed up to give your organs?" my son had anxiety attack and this question only makes it worse. there is no commonsense here. they will ask a person in shock questions that will worsen the situation. most of their doctors are on contract. they will bill the heck out of you. i am trying to resolve the billing issue but no one is willing to talk. endless hold and then "sorry we cant speak to you" since my son is just above 18 years. they took co-pay and miraculously that is not taken out of the bill and their system doesn't track it. the same happened 4 months ago and after talking over a month they took it off. how much worse do you want to make the patients and their family? you want really bad then visit this place. the doctor and some nurses were fine.
sibley is a part of johns hopkins in dc right at the maryland border. has a rehab center too.

i'm not a big fan of hospitals but planning for my twins' birth, i knew it had to be at a hospital. 

i had a scheduled c section (at 38 weeks) prior to thanksgiving so i had to stay through the holiday. the labor and delivery department and postpartum department were all great! i believe sibley already has a good reputation for delivery and i feared going into labor before week 34 because then i would've had to go to gw or georgetown university... whichever one has the nicu. i'm so thankful for making it to term and being able to deliver here. 

i loved the team that worked with me ... even though different nurses had different ways of doing things. i recommend sibley for future mamas!

if the apple store and chick-fil-a had a baby who said "i want to be a hospital when i grow up," this would be that baby's dream fulfilled. 

it's the nicest and cleanest hospital i've ever been in with the nicest people. the er waiting room (sponsored by marriott according to the placard on the wall) had phone charging stations. the rooms in the back looked like something off of a medical drama. i was half expecting house to walk by. 

i have never had so many medical professionals treat me like i was the first sick person they'd ever encountered. 

"i'm so sorry you're not feeling well."
"i sincerely hope you feel better." 

i was laying on the bed outside the ct machine room when a random nurse passed by and asked me if i was cold and if i wanted him to bring me a warm blanket. i already had a blanket, but he brought me a piping hot one and folded it over me like my life depended on it. the only thing missing was "have a blessed day" and some waffle fries. 

everything was fast too. the last dc emergency room i visited left a lot to be desired...like medical care. after three hours of waiting for a bed and six hours of waiting for an ekg, i was asked to leave at 2 in the morning and come back the next day, so they could "free up some beds." 

not here. they literally called me back after 30 minutes, and still two nurses and a doctor repeatedly apologized for "the long wait." they did all my labs and even got a ct scan done in about two hours. when i was discharged, the doctor took her time explaining everything and repeatedly asked if i had any questions as if i was the only patient there. the nurse came in after her and did the same thing "just in case." 

little baby chick-fil-apple turned out to be a damn fine hospital.

the sweetest staff members ever. from the moment i walked in ... no one likes having to go to the er but when you do, you'd like to be accommodated and feel cared for or at least like your health is a priority, and they did nothing less than. above and beyond, service is immaculate. i came in with chills, high heart rate due to dehydration and horrible abdominal pain caused by food poison. my uber driver had recommended sibley memorial over the er i was initially going to, and i am so glad that he did. i highly recommend sibley hospital i wish i had gotten the names of all of the helpful nurses. thank you
wow! sibley is the best hospital i've ever been to. the hospital is extremely clean and the staff is out of this world phenomenal!
no wait. i came in at 8:30 and they admitted to see me at 8:15. the people are super nice and they actually know how to stitch. i avoided gw hospital, paid for an uber to come here, well worth it.

i waited for 9 hours in the er and wasn't seen until 1am by a doctor to address severe abdominal pain. very disorganized and no communication. there was no one available to answer questions. they did a blood test, urine test, ultrasound, and ct scan and provided me no updates on any of those and just proceeded to the next one. i would not recommend this hospital if you have a serious emergency that needs to be met immediately.

recently, i went to sibley memorial hospital with acute shortness of breath and received excellent, caring, courteous care! dr. louis piper, the attending physician, alison mackin, nurse, and yodit kassa, ultrasound tech, were all outstanding, friendly and did a great job of communicating what was going on and answering my questions. i was seen for an initial screening in a matter of about 10 minutes and, once they determined my symptoms didn't pose an immediate threat to life, i had to wait another half hour or so. in the end, i spent all day in the er getting lots of tests, which wasn't much fun, but the team did a great job of checking into the possible causes of my shortness of breath. my only complaint about the er is very minor: i was sent home after getting a single tablet of blood-thinners and a prescription for more--but i needed that prescription filled before the next morning. filling a prescription on a sunday evening is challenging and it would have been nice if they had been able to give me a one-day supply--but apparently hospital protocols don't allow that.
thank you, everybody at sibley. i'm so grateful!

this review is for the cafeteria only. i went down to get breakfast and they had food but no workers  to serve it to you (hot food behind glass). after waiting for 5 min and nobody willing to work or do there job i left. on my way out i saw the back door open and a group of workers hanging out in the back talking and laughing. i have no problem with that but when you have customers trying to get food you should take 2 min to do your job.

it used to be easy to schedule an appointment in the sibley imaging center.  today it took 40 minutes wait time, listening over and over to the message saying how busy everyone was.  then they offer to return your call if you want to leave a message, and promise to return the call within 24-48 hours.  are you supposed to sit at home and wait for their call? a silly offer.  clearly the staff is shorthanded, and hopkins is economizing.

i would highly recommend to stay out of this hospital at all costs. go through the extra trouble and get yourself or a loved one over the bridge to philadelphia hospital. 
one star is extremely generous for this absolute disaster of a dump. the staff will leave you or loved ones in feces for hours, along with dozens of other major issues. thumbs down to this crap hole
would not recommend the obgyn or birthing unit here. the anesthesiologist gave a high spinal epidural and almost killed me and my baby. still have nightmares about it.

i've been bringing my little one to this hospital for their feeding program since the last two weeks of december 2019.  they have been nothing but great!  

i've been very fortunate to land a feeding slot quicker than i expected for my little man.  we met with one of their nurses for the second part of the evaluation and explained what they were doing for each test.  not only that but she answered all questions that we had. afterward, they told us that we were going to get contacted on the next available feeding therapist and their available schedule. 

i'm not going to lie, i was a devasted that we were not going to schedule that moment at the hospital but was completely shocked at how fast the turnaround time was when they contacted me (that afternoon) of the next available time slot we could initially start our feeding therapy sessions.  the first week of jan 2020!

since then, we have been assigned to one feeding therapist and she has been fantastic! we meet with her one a weekly bases and it has been another helpful and informative therapy session added onto my son's list of therapy sessions.  they really are great at their job and i cannot thank them enough for helping me and families facing these struggles.  my son has only gone through 3 sessions and he has improved so much in his chewing abilities.  

this program was through the vcu feeding program and sent us over to this location for their feeding program. for the short amount of sessions, i've brought my little one to already, i am so thankful for this program.  keep up the awesome work!!!

oh and the front desk guys (actually ladies) that we've encountered have been freaking awesome as well.  i really enjoy and appreciate the positive attitude that they have for us who have came to this location early in the morning and later afternoon.  thank you!

after getting the run around they would not reduce or remove the charge.

mishi (head o.r. nurse) and all intake and o.r. prep staff were amazing. the facilities were clean, staff pleasant and it was almost stress-free getting prepped for surgery. the anesthesiologist (dr. nyberg, md) and the vascular surgeon (dr. gonzalez, md) were personable and very clear about surgical procedures and how they could make the medical experience more comfortable based on specific needs (history of nausea, history of past procedures, etc...).
