we had already previously toured the facility and really liked what we saw! clean and big rooms, friendly staff, and loved that their labor and delivery is completely separate from their emergency building! if you're planning on having your baby in the valley, please go here! we had a scheduled induction for 01/18 at night and i have to say, their staff took the best care of us from start to finish. after 24 hours of trying to induce my labor, i was actually sent home because my body just wasn't ready to give birth and the staff new isn't more comfortable at home. after being home for 3 hours, our baby boy changed his mind and we headed back to the hospital! it was a very long labor but thankfully all the nurses took such great care of us! always checking in on us and being super tentative, reminding us or meal times and making sure we got fed, made sure i got the medication i needed and wanted and when i wanted it, always offering a hand once baby boy was here, helping me through my first few days of postpartum, and making sure my all baby and my testing got done in a timely yet still respectful manner. i know it seems like a no brained than a hospital should already do these things but usually they're so busy and hectic that this just isn't the case. not with honorhealth osborn. if i could give them 10 stars, i would! as happy as i was to go home and start our "normal lives", i was sad to their their amazing staff.
the absolute best hospital in america! from the check in staff, to the nurses and doctors.

while on a casual evening walk christmas eve, admiring some nearby lighted landscape, i failed to see the gnarly, prickly, cactus as i reached out my hand to point to a holiday decoration.  in doing so, i pointed my finger directly into a cactus needle, which quickly imbedded itself under my fingernail and broke off in between my skin and nail.  not realizing at the time it had actually broke off inside, i thought it was just a puncture. as the pain continued, and my attempts at self-treatment to try and remove it failed, it was evident that i needed professional medical help. we called honorhealth scottsdale osborn about 10:00 pm christmas eve and they said come in. we were professionally and warmly greeted by the er staff and seen immediately. i cannot say enough great things about the professional medical staff here. the nurses, er admit, and er dr nichols, are the best. after numbing, and cutting my nail away from the skin to get that prickly cactus needle out from my nail bed, and a tetanus shot, rx for antibiotics, we were on our way just after midnight christmas morning. i am so thankful for the nurses and doctor who were on call this christmas night. they were all so kind and compassionate. i'm truly grateful for their time and commitment to being there for people like me. there were, indeed, emergencies far worse than my cactus catastrophe, but all the same courtesy and care for all.

i had outpatient surgery here this week. what a rollercoaster 

i had to arrive at 530a for a 730a procedure. i haven't had surgery since i was a child, but that seemed fine. until we got there and they didn't start calling patients back until almost 545a! seemed a little unprofessional. 

the nurses and techs who helped prep me were fantastic. super sweet and talkative which really helped quell my nerves. the anesthesiologist also came in and he was fun to talk to. (i'd had a pre-op call with an anesthesia nurse the friday prior, which was also good.) different techs came in to do different prep tasks, then my surgeon came in just to chat through things one more time. he seemed to be in a bit of a rush which wasn't the case at my consultation, but it put me a little on edge again.

as soon as he left, it was like the green berets of rns came in and things were in motion extremely quickly. there was also a high school student from gpnhs in there?? they must have given me the happy juice before she came in because in retrospect that's freaking weird. anyway, very little chatting and then i was on my way to the or. 

there were tons of people in there which i assume is normal. but that hs student was in there too! (oh, what gpf money can buy!) i barely remember anything past moving to the operating table. it would have been nice for my surgeon to stop in again before i was asleep.

when i woke up in recovery all i could hear was a nurse telling me to breathe deeply, and telling me that my surgeon couldn't find my husband. nice wake-up call but whatever. i couldn't breathe well because i was in a lot of pain. her only response was "that's normal, you just had major surgery". whuh?? i get that i had to get the anesthesia out but the total disregard for my pain and comfort was really frustrating. it's also so bright in there. i had to ask for a towel to put over my eyes. that nurse and another were concerned about my oxygen levels at one point, but i literally couldn't breathe deeply. i was really sad that they couldn't give me any tips/tricks for taking better breaths, but just kept snapping at me.

i then went to my private recovery room. my husband came back (he was at home, which is just around the corner). from this point on i was still in a lot of pain and kept telling the nurse there. her only solution was to "go get the doctor so he could admit for pain management". giant eye roll. maybe you could just be patient and give me an hour to 1. wake up and 2. let the meds kick in? so rude. surgeon came in again to follow up on one issue that came up, but he was in a huge rush again. not that i needed him to stay by my bedside but it was literally like "went well. put ice on the incision. bye." 

the initial recovery room nurse went on break evidently, so then a nurse named nan (pretty sure. i was a little high still, lol) came in. she was great. finally someone who helped me breathe normally, and recommended that i sit up in a chair to help with both the breathing and the pain. nan was so wonderful. she took my vitals one more time.

my rating is based on the fact that this level 3 hospital is the primary facility serving the capital city of washington state.  until i entered the emergency room in mid november, i had only seen patients being treated in hallways on television shows.  i had never dreamed i would be one of those or that i would hear physicians breaking hipaa laws next to me so carelessly as they went over patient's medical history after confirming their 1st and surnames and continuing with incredibly personal information i would love to forget.

let's start with the g6 sensors themselves and the fact that since october 2018, the average amount of time a sensor lasts on my son is a paltry 4.33 days (only 8 sensors since then have lasted the full 10 days!)i've tried everything to get them to last longer, from listening to all the (often contradictory) advice that support reps give - one person tells me to pinch the skin at the attachment site before attaching, another person tells me not to do that. we've tried hydrating him more, that didn't work. someone even told us to try not to calibrate if we can avoid it, because that throws the sensor into a tailspin and eventually it will fail. more on what a messy situation that is later. what i had been doing about all these sensor failures up until a few months ago, was when i got a chance, i would call in with the information i captured in a spreadsheet (lot #, attachment date, attachment location on the body, whether or not i applied an overpatch, the date it was removed and the reason for removal) and the support specialist would take the total number of days i should have gotten out of x sensors, subtract out the number of days i did get, and round up to the next number of sensors, and 3-5 days later, i'd have the sensors replaced. for instance, if 7 sensors lasted 34 days, the support rep would say "7 sensors should last 70 days. they lasted 34, so we owe you 36 days, which you can get out of 36/10 = 3.6 or 4 sensors." it wasn't ideal, but as a very busy person, being able to call in when i could to get sensors replaced was the only thing that made all these sensor failures halfway tolerable.

then, they instituted a policy that they would replace only 3 sensors per call, and the rest would have to be approved, adding a new dimension to the dysfunction that is the g6. customer support reps continually assure me that i am not the only one having these issues, so why in the hell would they institute a policy like this when there are so many problems with the g6? now instead of waiting to do this when i can, i have to call every time one fails? i just don't have the time to do that! the same person who first apprised me of this policy  told me i could send email instead of calling. great! but then i get a return email asking me to take more time i don't have to fill out a patient request form (the description field of which accepts 126 characters max!), and then after i've done that, now i have to wait an additional 2-3 business days to get a call back, and even if that happens on time (which it doesn't always) over the course of all of this, 2 more sensors have failed. they've created a bottleneck with this 3-sensor-limit policy. most of the time, they approve the 3 sensors and leave any remaining sensors in limbo waiting for "approval."  i had needed 6 sensors, the rep who i was on the phone with sent 3, and told me i'd have to wait for the other 3 to be approved. after not hearing back for about 3 weeks, i called in and the rep just sent the sensors. so what was the fucking point of that? they didn't even need to get approved! they just added a layer to make it more difficult for me. i patronize the company because it is supposed to provide working devices, and when they don't work, to have them replaced swiftly, not to create impediments for every type of problem i could have and then not even stick to those policies. dexcom should be creating solutions, not problems.

finally, dexcom g6 has this habit of asking me to recalibrate every 15 minutes if the fingerstick calibration value is too far off from the sensor reading. on christmas night at about 11:35pm the sensor reported my son's bg was low, and before i go throwing glucose down his throat, i did a fingerstick. the fingerstick came back with 93, and when i calibrated, it told me to recalibrate after 11:50pm. it's almost midnight and i'd really like to go to sleep, but i figured i'd play along. at about midnight, i fingerstick again,106. i put that in the dexcom app. now it wants me to calibrate after 12:05am." so then i do it again, and it says calibrate at 12:20m.  i don't have time to jerk this thing off.  dexcom openly admits it is for information purposes and may not be accurate and also admit that the fingerstick is the more accurate indicator of what the blood sugar actually is. then why on earth do i have to keep doing this for hours even at 1 in the morning when i want to sleep because the fingerstick doesn't agree with dexcom!? when i put in the fingerstick value it should adjust to that, period. this calibrate over and over again is pure horseshit and it goes against everything we know about which is the accurate one and which is to be used for information purposes! now support would say "after the 2nd or 3rd calibration, you should just replace the sensor." but you can see why i want every sensor to last as long as possible, because every sensor failure is is another addition to the boondoggle that is the sensor replacement process.

the mount sinai hospital provides a miserable patient experience
mount sinai has many fine doctors and many wonderful nurses.  i am not here commenting on the medical care that may be received at this hospital.  rather i am talking about the hospital culture and approach to the patients - which is execrable.  

my 97 year old mother, alert and bright, was taken there with a broken hip two weeks after an emergency heart surgery.  she sat up all night in an overcrowded, overworked and understaffed er (see ny post of december 9, 2019: https://nypost.com/2019/12/09/mount-sinai-hospitals-emergency-department-is-a-war-zone-workers-say/ ) before being loaded on a gurney and taken to an overflow facility.  in the course of her transfer all of her clothing, shoes, jewelry, outer- and under-wear disappeared.  the following day, when i first learned of the loss, i notified security and the patient ombudsman and provided an itemized list of missing items.  those two offices supposedly conducted an investigation.  they found no sign of the goods but would reveal nothing of their efforts nor share any of their report.  i have no basis to know whether any investigation was conducted or any report generated.

after 6 weeks of a run-around within the hospital proper i wrote to the general counsel who referred me to an outside law firm.  the outside law firm allegedly referred the matter to be investigated - and had me wait another month before telling me, more than 9 weeks after the loss, that they would offer us pennies on the dollar to go away.  

while in the hospital, my mother was served a diet erroneously prescribed by the hospital nutritionist.  it took daily efforts, with the help of doctors, nurses and the nutritionist, for more than ten days, to have that corrected - during which time my mother was largely unable to eat the food provided to her.  i brought in food on a regular basis to be sure she had adequate nutrition and a hot meal she could stomach.  

due to repeated surgical delays, poor communication, aggressive medication, and general abuse by the hospital my mother, who arrived at the hospital bright and optimistic, left it feeling depressed and defeated.  

my family has recorded additional examples of incompetence and broken promises from the hospital during this stay, but this may be sufficient to bring home the point that the patient experience at mount sinai is one of insouciance and disrespect.  

finally i would note that my mother's late husband was a surgeon at mount sinai, an emeritus professor in their medical school, their historian and archivist, a recognized author and historical contributor to various medical disciplines - and she, known to be his widow, was still treated in this uncaring manner. (she does not deserve better treatment for that relationship, but it might have been offered.)  based on direct, repeated and anecdotal experience, the description of the mount sinai er in the post article and my mother's experience were neither isolated nor unique.  

if you have a choice of hospital facility, and you care for the mental state and dignity of your "patient", i would strongly suggest nyu, cornell or another hospital would provide a far preferable environment and a comparable medical experience.

review: i have had kaiser medical insurance coverage for quite a few years.  during that time, i have come across both good and bad doctors.  because the overall care and convenience kaiser provided in the past was fairly good i never considered switching to another health insurer.  however, in the past 3 years i have seen the quality of medical care and their doctors' concerns for their patients deteriorate.  six weeks ago, i accompanied my neighbor as she visited the kaiser hospital emergency room 3 times during a 48 hour period of time.  she was suffering with severe abdominal pain and swelling but did not have a fever.  the first 2 times the er doctors sent her home without offering any help because the abdominal cat scan did not show anything.  the er doctors totally ignored the fact that she was in a lot of pain, unable to eat, and also had a distended stomach.  as a result, she contacted the people in management at the hospital.  they told her that they would call the er department and for her to return to the emergency room immediately.  this time, under pressure from management, the er doctors consulted with a specialist.  although nothing showed up in the ultrasound or cat scan, the specialist figured out that she had an intestinal blockage.  as a result, they pumped out a huge amount of bile that had pooled in her stomach.  she had to spend the next 6 days in the hospital for additional treatment and testing.  during that time, they also discovered that she was bleeding internally.

on my first visit, before surgery, i had to physically get up and go to the front desk, since no one had answered the "red light" signal, and ask for assistance for her, since she couldn't walk or get out of bed without help.  because of this, she had to wear diapers.  the first day i went to visit, i had to go find someone to come in and change a very soaked and dripping diaper she had had on for more than two hours, because no one answered her "red light" signaling that she needed help.  she has constantly had to lay and wait for someone to bring her ice for her warm water that has been sitting all day.  the workers are up and down the corridors a lot, and won't stop and look in on her unless they see that i am in the room with her, then they "might stop in" and ask if she needs anything.  i have had to find the attending nurse or person in charge more than once, to get her pain medications to her when she has been in "moaning worthy" pain of them!  they keep it so hot in the rooms that i have even had to start shedding or loosening clothing to stay comfortable.

the actual care i received was very professional, however the billing has been a complete nightmare, i will not go back.  after siting down with their fiance rep and going over my healthcare plan in great detail with her, she had me sign a document saying that my responsibility for a diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound would be $669.89.  the paper i signed even states, "to help, we have contacted your health plan to estimate the out-of-pocket expenses (copay, deductible, and/or co-insurance you will be responsible for".  during the procedure i was asked if i wanted a 3d ultrasound at a cost of an additional $75, which i agreed to.  
in the end they charged my insurance $1,535.00 and i received a bill for $1,1113.87, not including an additional bill from the doctor who reviewed my ultrasound results.  this facility is in-network and has negotiated pricing with my insurance, there should be no discrepancy between price and bill.
i have literally spent months trying to get a real explanation of this billing discrepancy.  the only solution they offered was a payment plan.  i would like them to honor the pricing i signed for with the addition of the 3d charge.

review:
we had a less than favorable experience a few days ago at the lcom er. the er was a mess and seemed no better than what i'd expect harbor general to be like. we have very little experience in an er setting so maybe my expectations are unrealistic.

for starters, the was place filthy. the sheet on the triage nurse's intake bed was dirty.  people, we're in the middle of the corona virus problem! that thing should be changed after every patient. just so you know, i went back the next day almost 24 hours later to get some paperwork and that same dirty sheet was still on there with the same identifiable dirty shoe marks and stains. at the time of admittance, i was happy my husband was even being seen so i didn't make a fuss. in hindsight, i should have said something. 

most important however, was the lack of care he received by the attending physician dr. lu. he was impersonal and spoke very condescendingly to us. my husband was treated on a bed in the hallway the entire time hooked up to a heart a portable heart monitor!  here's a person with a heart condition and skyrocketing blood pressure, dizziness and whose been vomiting.  no blood work done, urine taken but not evaluated, and no fluids given.  and yes, i do feel entitled to decent care - i'm going to pay my bill! 

i think the main problem is too many people in our community use the er like a doctor's office with common ailments because they can't be turned away for lack of insurance or ability to pay. the staff are like robots with the barrage of problems that walk through the door. 

i'm sharing my experience because we are concerned at the level of healthcare available to us in our community during an emergency situation. is what we experienced an isolated event or is this the norm at our community er?

review:
besides couple regular check ups, this was my very first actual experience with both the er and inpatient care. fortunately, it wasn't for me. unfortunately, it was for my mom. then again, super fortunate that everything was more than i could hope for her. 

long story short, i had to take my mom to arlington memorial er after having been to md arlington er just right before. there wasn't anything wrong with md arlington, but per my mom's doctor recommendation, based on which specialty doctors they had on staff that night vs arlington memorial. needless to say, it was a very long friday night of emotional rollercoaster.

when we arrived at tham er, i immediately told the front desk my mom's symptoms and how we were told by her doctor to come here, in less than a min after filling out the 1, possibly 2 page document, they took my mom in right away, started running several different tests on her. she was seen by a doctor, x-ray technician, a nurse, all within 20mins. 

it took them a little longer after that to do a few more tests, go over the findings, and complete administering her to inpatient, before they could move her upstairs to settle in. never been to any inpatient room before, i was quite surprised to see how nice and spacious her room is. besides all the necessary medical equipments, it comes fully equipped with 2 sinks, private bathroom with shower, a couch, 32in tv, and a closet. honestly, i wouldn't mind having to spend a week or 2 here.

i never gotten a chance to meet her doctors since i could only stay with my mom at night, and all doctors do their rounds during day time. however, her nurse, annie, was excellent, extremely helpful, and informative. not only did she attend all of my mom's needs during her night shift, she was very informative and patient with all of our questions.

just like most hospital, it could be a bit confusing to navigate around. luckily, they have a lot of signs to tell you what is what and which direction to go, also, they have an information desk with volunteers that would be more than happy to walk with you to where you need to go. there are also 2 big garages that provide plenty of free parking for your convenient.

all in all, our experience was much more than i could hope for. it definitely wasn't a good thing we had to come to the hospital, but i'm glad we came to tham!

was 302 earlier this month. i had a psychotic episode, so please believe me when i say i needed inpatient admission.   during the initial 120 hr stay, i was told that there would be a hearing on the 5th day and that the hospital was going to recommend a 303 and keep me for 20 more days.  when i almost broke down, i was told that it was standard practice and that the court would make the final decision.  was told i would have a public defender to represent me.  to prepare, i made sure i took my meds, attended each group therapy session (where i told my story umpteen times to the same  therapists and fellow patients) practiced good hygiene, basically anything that i could possibly do to prove that i was compliant and would remain compliant if disharged.  the 5th day came, and the psychiatrist called me out of a therapy session, and introduced me to the attorney appointed for me.  when the word "hearing" is used it is common knowledge that you go to either a court house (or other venue where a judge of some level conducts legal proceedings) and that your attorney will brief you as to what to say and when to say it.  its also good when the attorney is on your side, hence the word defense.  this was not the case.  the attorney told me on the spot that he was going with the hospital's recommendation of a 303 with a maximum of 20 days.  i felt sick.  i asked "what about the hearing?"  he told me "there is no actual hearing.  i just submit a recommendation to a judge.  but that doesnt mean you will be here all 20 days.  thats just the maximum".  he then said goodbye and both he and the psychiatrist walked away.  i was overwhelmed with anxiety and could not return to the group.  i went to my room and cried for hours.  nothing else was said.  anytime i had questions, they were met with a terse "just keep going to group and take ur meds and we'll see what happens"  i actually, by chance, found out from another patient what the real story was.  they base your discharge date on how well your insurance pays, and if you are being discharged to a recovery house or some sort of residence. i was being discharged to my wife, that was the plan.    all i could do was be compliant, don't give anyone a hard time, and they might shave some time off.  well, the fact that i am writing this means that im out.  7 days shy of my max.  i think my insurance questioned them and they relented.  the psychiatrist i saw shaved my medication regiment to her own form, and had nothing positive to say to me.  i think its also telling that even though she saw me every single day since my admission, she did not see me today.  not to even finalize discharge instructions.  they keep you cooped up, not allowed outside (even though i was told that sleeping late everyday when at home robbed me of vitamin d and fresh air, lol)  like i said, about the meds, the dr. cut down my night meds and i couldnt get a full night sleep with people popping in and out of your room at night (even though all patients are on candid camera) the food was half decent and they did have 3 times a day where you could get a snack, so if your meal was gross, you wouldnt starve.  unfortuneatly, things were tightened down this past week because the state was doing an inspection.  i dont blame the nurses or the techs.  i blame the program.  if i ever suffered another crisis, i would ask to be taken to horsham house.  atleast you can smoke/go outside.

i've considered taking this post down, but i can't. it's been 5 months since my baby was born, but i still feel like my baby and i were not taken care of properly. this article helps explain what i experienced.

st. rose, i really think you should consider not being a baby friendly hospital, or at the very least having a more hands-on policy for mothers who have a c-section surgery. looking back, i really struggled breastfeeding after a major abdominal surgery because i couldn't sit up all the way... and to me that sounds like common sense. i could barely move and i struggled to walk. my baby lost weight, and i was recovering from a major surgery. anyone with common sense would've given me a bottle of formula so i could rest and recover. i'm not sure why a trained nurse didn't see my baby lost 10% of her weight and was dehydrated. she needed  something to eat, but i was pushed to only breastfeed. someone dropped the ball here. i hope this doesn't happen to any mother again. please review your processes to protect your moms and babies.

this hospital claims to be a "baby friendly hospital", but it doesn't seem like they really care about my baby at all. i ended up having a c-section, and i have been trying to breast feed on schedule, but my baby lost over a pound because i'm not producing enough milk. the doctor told me i need to supplement my baby's feeding with formula. which is so devastating to hear because i really want to breast feed her and i have been trying so hard to make sure i'm doing it right. so today when we are about to be released to go home, i asked them for some formula to get us through the next feeding...  the nurse and the charge nurse refused to give me even one bottle. the charge nurse had the audacity to shame me by asking me if i'm even breast feeding! i've been doing everything i can to feed my baby. my milk simply hasn't come in yet. she kept telling us that my nurse was correct to follow hospital policy, and there is nothing she can do for us. my husband tried to reason with the charge nurse, and she didn't want to talk to him. she just kept saying, "can i just talk to her (me)." i also tried to reason with her by telling her how concerned i am for my baby's weight loss, and that i'm not asking for a box of formula, just enough to get us through the next feeding so we can settle in at home and my husband can go to the store to buy some. her response was, "just to make you happy i'll give you one bottle, but just so you know it's against our baby friendly policy". her attitude, condescending tone, and over all mom-shaming really breaks my heart. i'm a first time mom who needed an emergency c-section. i am devastated that my baby lost weight, and here i have these nurses making me feel bad that i haven't been able to produce enough milk to nourish my baby. they don't want to give me formula to help my baby, and made me feel like i'm begging for one bottle of formula just to get me through one feeding. all the other nurses have been over the moon, but to see that management can't make a reasonable call on giving a struggling mom some formula and that hospital policy is more important than the health of my baby is unbelievable. i cannot believe how a "baby friendly" hospital won't actually help my baby. i'm devastated and heart

if i could give it 0 stars, you got it!  abusive to my family member. let him sit in poo for an hour 3 times. don't respond to alarms. aspiration dangers. physical therapy is a joke. held him against hhis will. lack of rn knowledge as they dont  know the proper name of generic meds. don't know proper medical condition names. god help you if you ask to stay the night to keep an eye on your family member.

i came to presbyterian with a clogged ear drum. i wish i hadn't, because they made my problem significantly worse and resulted in losing complete hearing for about 5 days. i eventually was able to solve the problem myself. avoid like the plague.

this hospital is ridiculously expensive!!!! i was charged 15k that's right 15k for a doctor to try and drain my thumb that's right "try" to do it. i want to know where in god's name do they expect me to fined 15k working a average job,with bills and also a family. they should really feel a shame of themselves! just ridiculous they didn't even fix the problem. i had finally did it myself the next day for free. i'm so upset it's causing me great anxiety..

i just wish practicing doctors had a more appealing bedsmanner. i also wish that insurance would allow doctors to do their job in a more practical way. which might allow for things to move smoothly.

my boyfriend  and i went to the er the  beginning of july 2019.  we were at home and he went to having a seizure, then wet himself. i took him to this hospital because it was the closest one to us. dropped him off at the emergency drop off no one person came out to help me to get him in a wheel chair. took him to the front desk and went back to the car to go park. as soon as i got in  they were already giving him attitude because he was not responding. they took an hour and a half to get us back to a room and that was because i was complaining. the guy was watching something on youtube, the other person was face timing her son. we finally got to the back and of course he started complaining about his head hurts. the nurse was trying to talk to him but he was in and out of sleep. he was trying to talk but wasn't getting far. so i was speaking for him letting her know what happened, he started shaking and wet himself, hours before. after an hour or so in the room i get up to go use the restroom. wasn't gone for more then 3-4 minutes. i get back to the room and the nurse tell me were discharging him because he's no incorporating. he tells her please giving me something for my head and i'll talk. he stated to her that something popped in my head. she also said the dr came in 3/4 time and tried to talk to him bs!!! keep in mind, they do not accept medicare. but they do offer free flu shots...and snacks. winning! ;)

she makes me want to change surgeons and hospitals. i don't feel safe leaving my life in the hands of medical professionals who do not value their patients rights or uphold their ethical oaths.

the doctor's, nurses, technicians are world class.

is zero stars even an option? i would first like to say that if you are coming here for an elective surgery, joint replacement or others, do not come here, run as far as you can. 

my grandmother was scheduled 12/18/19 @7am for a total knee replacement, preop, or & pacu were awesome.

once she was admitted to the ortho floor (3rd floor) we were welcomed by the nursing manager, daniel bernstein, my grandmother is rolled into the corner of the hallway where we wait hours for her to get into a clean room. the hallway was "equipped" with a call light (silver desk bell), a pulseox monitor that was not being monitored at the nurses station because she is in the hallway, a privacy curtain that did not cover or provide any privacy and the list goes on (all pictured below). this not just a privacy concern but a real safety concern. the cords from the bed and all the machines she was hooked up too were crisscrossing along the floor where my handicapped grandfather almost fell! i asked for my concerns to be escalated when daniel said "we escalate this all the time", just blowing me off, noooo daniel i want to speak to someone else regarding this issue, so here i am writing this review as i wait. 

according to the academy of medsurg nursing: the practice of admitting patients to hallway beds while they await appropriate room assignments is patently unsafe and should never be used.

patients must be provided adequate space, privacy, comfort, and safety at all times. hallway beds do not provide clinicians with bedside access to equipment, such as oxygen, suction, and call lights, needed for safe provision of care. patients are at greater risk for falls and other adverse events if they cannot access a call light or be monitored appropriately by nurses.

she wanted the lights to be off, the thermostat adjusted, non of which can be done because this is a hallway. it was no surprise that my grandmother would be admitted to the hospital following her surgery so why was the hospital so poorly prepared? they have signs plastered every where saying "a quiet environment is a healing environment", well when you are in a hallway you can't just close the door. you are exposed to the chaos of the unit, the chemicals from house keeping, the constant call lights & phones ringing.

my last concern is for the nursing staff. how do you expect your nurses to provide adequate care if they can't even get to the patients bed. "your safety and health is our main concern", well then get patients out of the hallways then, safety is not a concern, money is. value money over patient safety, satisfaction & health.

you need to really ask how this is safe, how can you provide care to a patient in the hall, what if an emergency occurs then what? how about fire code violation? hipaa? i'm sure joint commission would love this....

but i will end this on a good note, our charge nurse hoang & primary nurse laura are the only good thing about this place. way to go hoang & laura. you are both worth 10 stars!

i came here to the er 5 hours ago with chest pain, heart palpitations and sky-high blood pressure. i was seen immediately and had an abnormal ekg and then a chest x-ray and blood work followed. that was 4.5 hours ago. no updates- nothing. everyone else that arrived at the same time as me have come and gone but i've received no update.

i asked the doctor if she ever had put a shoulder back in the socket and was told she had done it many times and that every week someone comes in with a shoulder dislocated.  i soon found out she had no idea what to do and wondered if i was her first patient.  she had to ask the attending doctor how to put in lidocane. the attending doctor was instructing her.  when she was twisting my arm up and all around she kept asking the attending doctor if she was doing it right.  after 10 minutes of no luck and pain i told her i wanted an ortho doctor called in.   i told her an ortho doctor could do it.  i see on tv all the time where doctors put the shoulder back in the joint in a minute.  she refused to call out to the ortho doctor on-call and said they now have to try weights.  the tech tried to put weights around my elbow.  it caused a lot of elbow pain, so he then tried around my wrist.  extreme pain on my wrist.  i told him why don't you attach to my upper arm since that is closer to the dislocation.  he went out and  created the device to wrap around my upper arm and that worked.  that tech did a great job.  i wondered if they do this all the time how come no one knew how to relocate my shoulder and they would not call-out to an experienced doctor that would know what to do.  
the doctor also had another set of x-rays to see if after all her twisting it was now in the socket.  i told her it was not and that i did not want all the extra radiation when i knew it was still out.  she said radiation was low.   results showed shoulder was not in the socket.  i also told her those weights are not going to work and i want an ortho doctor.  she said we need to go in order and weights is the next step.   as the weights were hanging from my arm dr matonis told me to yell out when the shoulder goes back in the joint.  i told her i did not know it was out to begin with so how an i suppose to know when it goes back in.  she said i will know which is ridiculous because after they finally got my shoulder back in the joint the pain was still the same.  she kept telling me it would feel better.  it is now a week later and i still could not tell you if my shoulder is in the joint.  the pain in the middle of the upper arm is exactly the same.    
when the weights did not work she asked me if i wanted her to try again to force my arm in the joint.  i told her again i want an ortho doctor.  she said after weights the next step is to put me under in the trauma room.  i said what makes you think you can to it when i'm asleep, if you can't do it when i'm awake.  she said my arm will be easier to manipulate.  i again told her to try.  another male resident was pushing on the back of my shoulder as hard as he could.  his hard pushing would have hurt if he did that on any part of my body.  meanwhile, she was twisting my arm trying to get it in the socket.  the uci ladies (two) that would alternate sitting in the room across from my room (watching the patient in that room) kept turning their chairs around so they could watch.  they stared as if watching tv.  it was so rude! ! the doctors - resident, attending, rn, never thought to close my door a little so i could have privacy. 
after pushing/pulling, weights, pushing/pulling, she said we now should put you under. i again told her i want an ortho doctor and that an ortho doctor could have resolved this a long time ago.  she again told me she could do this. she said she was having such a hard time getting my shoulder back in because i waited so long to come in (i came in 5 hours after the fall).  this is a typical response from a woman that cannot get the job done and so blame their lack of expertise on the patient.  while waiting for a trauma room i asked the rn about getting an ortho doctor.  he said he did call-out.  dr matonis never told me that.  the trauma room was finally available.  it did not look to me like anyone was in any of the trauma rooms to begin with.  she told the tech to put a mask on me, but he told her is was not needed, since i had the nose tube. she then told others in the room that they will learn a lot when the ortho doctor comes.  after it was over the tech told me ortho, dr choi, was there and assisted.  dr matonis never told me anything.  never saw her after.  they wrapped  shoulder stabilizer around my bra under my clothes.  my belly showed. no one helped.  now x-rays show a possible fracture which did not show in 1st set.

horrible and predatory pricing and billing system. had a colonoscopy at their offsite endoscopy center in irvine. the center charged $5,000 and the gi doctor, carlos saad, charged $5,000! i have excellent ppo insurance and it paid 90% of charges for the actual colonoscopy and the same percentage for the doctor so i'm stuck with a $1,000 bill for these ridiculously over priced tests. guess what medicare pays for these same tests??? the ambulatory center would have been reimbursed $615 and the physician $588. america - we are all getting scammed by the healthcare system. as of today i'm all for medicare for all!
my husband was in the hospital for weeks in the icu. the care was very good and the nurses were very attentive, especially the nurse amber. all the staff, doctors, and everyone was so helpful.

omg - i don't even know where to begin in expressing my dismay over the treatment provided by these doctors here. from very poor committee decisions on how to treat a serious condition to worthless appointments with young doctors who clearly do not know what they are doing to long wait of two hours for the oncologist, i am truly stunned. my husband and i are used to the hoag medical and hospital system and some wonderful doctors that we have experienced with hoag. he was referred to this uci 'teaching hospital' for his complicated condition. boy, do they have a lot to learn yet.

i would give uci no stars if possible. referrals take too long and are mishandled, specialists are over booked, i couldn't even get appointments with my primary care provider who recently left the practice along with another doctor because they couldn't stand the way patients were treated. don't go to the ed unless you're a trauma patient. they're always busy with trauma and have no time or patience for anything else. i had my privacy violated in the ed and witnessed other patients being mistreated. you're better off down the street at st. joesph:s hospital where you'll be treated with compassion by actual doctors, not unprofessional, arrogant, immature medical students.

if i could give this place a zero, i would. don't come her for solutions, come here if you want to be shuffled around without a resolution. if you even attempt to ask an intelligent question, don't hold your breath for an intelligent response. a patient if even had a possibility of survival, they would kill that patient here due to there long hours of wait time. i'm talking about 4 to 8 hours of wait time.

on november 8, 2019, i went to the uci er because i had right side lower abdominal pain. i spent approximately 4 hours and 30 minutes there grand total, including the medical assesment, blood pressure and temperature taken with accompanied mri. the experience was traumatic and nightmarish. the er is too small for the amount of people it services. blood work was taken off a corridor in the er. people were seated closely one after another, some in noticeable pain. there seems to be no method of triaging, no place to treat people, too little staff. not that i want to go to any emergency toom, i  know i will never return to the uci er. it is traumatic, chaotic, too small, understaffed and disorganized. i would rate it a minus 1.

i hate the a kokomo st vincent they are rude and misdiagnosis. i'm a electrician and they're telling me that for over 2 years that i y numbness is due to drinking but now after two years now it's up in my stomach and everything in my i can't wiggle my toes so is that right is something else i know i don't have a doctor no i can't see a doctor because i don't have one that's reason why you go to the emergency room so they can tell you something's wrong they ain't s*** they ain't doctors either they nurse practitioners
fac_name: St. Vincent Kokomo - St. Joseph Hospital

review: after reading some reviews i was really concerned about having my kids surgery done at this facility. honestly i have zero complaints. i had three kids that had tubes and adenoids out on the same day. the staff was nice, nurses were great and doctors were great with amazing bedside manners. i'm a registered nurse who used to work in the recovery room and i was very impressed with the care my kids received. the center provided me with my insurance benefits and explained what i needed to pay and what was covered and i came prepared. i was very stressed out about having three kids scheduled on the same day but the staff made everything smooth sailing. my family and i had a very good experience.

though ridgedale is well enough run, and my procedure (a screening colonoscopy went fine) the anesthesiologist was inattentive.  he place the nose piece for oxygen incorrectly, so only one part was in a nostril.  i mentioned it to him and he corrected it.  he also placed my arm in a position where it would lose circulation - i also had him correct that.  with little to do, the anesthesiologist made 2 mistakes.

i had the unfortunate need to visit an er after speaking to the nurse helpline over the weekend.   i didn't want to spend all day and be around a bunch of sick people, so i opted to try phoenix er on dobson.  
check in was quick as i was the only person! i was taken to a private room and met the doctor.  she was super friendly, thorough and helpful. after a series of questions, i was taken to a private examining room.  everyone: nurses, radiology tech and doctor were all female! and very knowledgeable and personable! 
within 2.5 hrs, after tests, i was out the door without ever coming in contact with another sick patient. hopefully i'll never need to go again, but if i do, i'd return without hesitation.

a friend recommended phx er & medical hospital to me as she had just taken her 5 year old in for stitches. she said there was no wait, minimal paperwork and everyone was super nice.

of course a week later i needed to take my 6 year old in and my girlfriend was right - this er is the best! everyone from the lady at the front desk to the nurses and doctors were all so incredibly sweet! every single one of them! they got us right in and even offered my daughter and i a snack while we waited for test results. our room even had a great tv setup with hulu to keep us entertained.

and the other great thing?! it is actually clean!! everything is spotless and you can really tell they take care of the place. i actually wasn't afraid to sit down haha. 

so if you're ever in need of an er - this is your place!

my 37 year-old daughter visited phoenix er medical hospital about a two months ago. as her father, i was really worried as she never gets this sick. felisha, the director of registration, got her in really fast with minimal paperwork which i truly appreciated and they started treating her right away, quickly getting an iv in her arm.

keep up the good work phoenix er & medical hospital and i'll definitely come there should i need medical attention in the future.

doctors and medical emergencies always give off the scariest feelings.  you're not sure what is going on with your health and you're afraid of what comes next.  the staff at phoenix er care about making patients feel heard and taken care of.  everyone was so kind to us.  i got a chance to chat with our nurse and she told me how even though they're busy, they want to give off the opposite feeling to people so they feel properly cared for.  

within 5 minutes of checkin we were pulled back to be seen and within 20 minutes of checkin we were with a doctor.  their rooms have 50"+ tellys to keep people occupied while they wait.  fully stocked with netflix, hulu and roku. 

overall, the place is incredible.   simply put - no one likes to be in a medical emergency but you can be assured you're taken care of if you come here.  phoenix er isn't owned by the bigger hospitals so their commitment to  tender loving care really does shine through.  it's physician owned.  i hope we don't have a situation where we need emergency services again but if we do this will be the place we go.


mary makes the best hot chocolate too.  she deserves praise.  dr. alimov was very personable and spoke candidly which is always appreciated in situations like that.

not an urgent care...much better. what an amazing micro hospital, i found them on facebook.  it is everything a hospital has, just smaller. state of the art equipment, they seem to all communicate with walkie talkie system . no waiting while the disappear to look for someone. checked in with one form, walked back, quick room service, went for x-ray on my elbow.   never going to big hospital or urgent care.  this is the place and the future of healthcare.

i took a chance on this hospital and i was thoroughly impressed. went in with severe back pain and they were attentive and polite from the start. the facility is clean and felt comfortable. dr. stump was amazing and very understanding that i wanted to get imaging done to make sure it wasn't a re injury, which it was. i will definitely be going back! thank you all!

never in my life have i been treated so well in an er. the wait time was nothing. i got a room immediately. the staff was warm and welcoming and kind. the rooms were comfortable with a tv that provided netflix. they had delicious food and drink for myself and my family members with me. they truly made a horrible experience just a little bit better. thank you to all of the amazing staff there!

usually for my emergency needs i'll go to chandler regional, well today when my daughter started feeling ill and emergency services were needed i decided to go a different route and give this place a try. i called in to see if my insurance was accepted felisha answered the phone and assured me my insurance was taken there, she also let me know that they offered self pay discount plans. we arrived and were promptly greeted, signed in and within 5 minutes my daughter was in a room and being cared for. that's the quickest i've ever had medical services received. the nurses were super nice they were all on the same page it wasn't just nurses coming in the room reading papers and giving services. they all work together as a team with the doctors to make the experience comfortable and make you feel assured. it's  a smaller facility, not crammed with people. no waiting room full of sick people or anything like the regular er rooms it was accommodating and convenient and extremely clean! as long as this place exists it will be my go if i need emergency services

do not visit this location because you will be treated rudely by a staff member.
the staff member will ridicule you about your hygiene. will state that you reek of
urine and spray you with disinfectant.
while waiting i witnessed the staff member
spraying another patient with disinfectant.
she will also give lessons on incontinence
without being scheduled to do so.
another patient canceled her appointments due to being humiliated about bladder problems. you should avoid
the popular level road location and find another location.
fac_name: Baptist Health Medical Group Kentucky Heart Specialists

review: i'm truly surprised why anyone would or could give this place anything other than 5 stars. it's easy to drive to, (yes there is construction but it's clear where you need to park), the staff is unbelievably competent and kind (from reception to the surgeons to the discharge nurses), the facility is clean, discharge instructions are clear, and the food is good. the waiting area is incredible - you get to watch the status of whomever you are there with at the hospital. i was there for major surgery and i felt calm, informed and most of all cared for the entire time. also leading up to the surgery the phone calls for registration and billing we're professional and easy. this place is  5 stars all the way.

avoid elective imaging here.  go to a different imaging center when you make an appointment for a ct, mri, or bone scan.  the radiology dept at this inova location is immature, lies, gossip, and talks about patients in front of other patients.  scans are not done accurately.  lead radiology technicians lack ethics and engage in name calling of patients.

our little guy had his first er visit last night and i am so pleased with his care i had to write a review. specifically to give kudos to katie who was not our assigned pediatric er nurse but was someone our toddler latched onto. katie sat with him and played with him off and on for the four hours we were in the hospital which really made his experience (and ours) a lot less stressful. the entire staff was amazing but katie was particularly great. the only reason why i'm giving it four instead of five stars was the wait time. we were there for four hours just for a vital check and a ct scan. this did seem to be a particularly busy day for ct scans and i am sure preference was given to those in more traumatic situations than ours but for the little guy, the wait was rough. the radiology team was fantastic as well. thank you again for making our first er visit a lot less traumatic

be careful with the hospital billing.  they will run up your bill and do unneeded tests.  loudoun county needs another hospital to keep patient costs under control.  the use of the emergency room is $2,200.  the minimum er dr charge is $1,200.  something needs to be done with inova robbing patients.

i came in with a gastrointestinal flare up and all the staff were amazing!! 
they were very kind and took care of me right away.
even reception was amazingly nice and super supportive in getting me seen as soon as possible and super nice at check out as well. 
very caring staff i can't say enough thank you's!
fac_name: Dignity Health Arizona General Hospital - Mesa

review:
it took me a lot to go into an er. i've been dealing with these flair ups for a while. i went in cause i felt like i was having chest pains, dizzy, and couldn't breath. i was trying to explain to them that i have had this feeling in the past before and went to the urgent care where they did an ekg and chest xray, but at that time they didn't know if it was my pancreas or not and told me to go to er. 

the doctor came in and said well i'm not sure we will have the answers but we will do some labs. i was explaining with the nurse what's been going on with me cause i feel like the whole story would help. she kept cutting me off saying multiple time "well what brings you in today?" 

they forget to close the door and i can hear them talking about me. all in condensing tones saying things "like she too young". "she says chest pains and funny thing now she has stomach pain" "i like how people say that so they can be seen sooner". it was awful and embarrassing. i didn't even know that was a thing. did they think i wanted i be in there wasting my money giving them a job? after that i mentally checked out and didn't care about being there. the doctor came in for just a few secs said didn't find anything. of course they didn't they just did an ekg and chest x-ray like i already had. he didn't have any ideas or thoughts on anything. just said we are only here to make sure your not dying. since then i have had more symptoms of other things in the last week. found a doctor who had a test done and have found out what may be the start of what causing this. 

doctors and nurses should not be writing off people from their possible experiences in the past. that's how things go missed and people leave the er not better. just because someone is young doesn't make everything an anxiety attack. plus talking about someone like that when they already feel bad for coming in is unacceptable. why do they care. i have insurance and now i have to pay loads of money to them for nothing. 

i only gave 2 stars cause the front desk ladies and x-ray lady were super kind and helpful. she allowed me to fill out paperwork afterwards because in that moment i don't think the paperwork was gonna happen.
fac_name: Dignity Health Arizona General Hospital - Mesa

review:
beware the barranca surgery center.
on july 26 2018 a surgical procedure was performed on my left eye at the barranca surgery center by dr. nadeem vaidya. during the surgery someone threw a bottle or something hard into a metal garbage receptacle which as you can imagine made a loud report sounding much like a gun shot. now remember this was in a very quiet operating room environment. the sound startled the doctor and me as i was only under local anesthesia so i saw the doctors whole body wiggle with surgical tools in my eye. bottom line is i have a blind spot in that eye which i noticed the very next day. the result of this is a blind spot impairing the vision in my left eye.
i wanted to sue the barranca surgery center so something like this would never to anyone else. i felt the person who through the object just was not thinking, and i wanted management to caution its people that the actions they take can cause serious damage. not being litigious i did not know how to go about the task and did not know there is a one-year limit for filing a case.  so bottom line is i have very poor vision and lots of headaches and cannot do anything about it.

anesthesiologist dr steve p lee was an absolute nightmare of a doctor.  after taking my wife's history, he was judgmental, petulant, impatient and sadistic/tortuous trying to start an iv.  his anger and contempt showed immensely while trying and failing miserably.  i could not believe a doctor treated her this way.  she and her history evidently "made his day difficult." she was respectful and honest with him, did not give him a hard time.  she reported this to the staff and admin and no one followed up.  this place is ill-equipped and the staff is incompetent.  none of the nurses could get an iv and he couldn't either.  she didn't even continue with the procedure.  he backed up the chair(rolling), put up his hands in anger when i stopped the mistreatment and torture on my wife, and exclaimed "okay, if that's what you want to do, fine!"  i could not believe it.

warning: do not go to this emergency room. 

they did nothing to help resolve my ongoing headache. they fed me a bunch drugs( tylenol, benadryl and other drugs at the same time as if they were trying to kill me) and the nurse popped a blood vessel trying to take blood out of me in my veins. and the worst part is that they didn't even bother to let me know my insurance expired before taking me in so they're now charging me 6k for this ridiculous emergency room visit. again, they did nothing to resolve my ongoing headache.

update: to that guys response about the emergency rooms not checking insurance before them checking you in is complete b.s. i had to go to another e.r. and they first hand told me that my insurance had expired(yes i had to go to another one because of the fine job these idiots did). this has got to be the most crooked e.r. in the l.a. county. again, do not come here. they are a schemed crooked e.r. who will not resolve your health problems.

bloodstained curtains and dirty smocks in the rooms. nurses admit to ignoring doctor's orders. security and nurses are rude and dismissive.

also completely disorganized and chaotic. lost my husband's belongings and the phones in his room didn't work so they left him after surgery with no contact method for anyone and no way to get in touch with me or his family. they had 5 different people, and eventually called me in, to come look for his phone, wallet and clothes. then had the audacity to offer to keep them for us in a safe. hell no.

and the worst for last. husband woke up after surgery and had a panic attack from the heavy meds. nurses screamed at him instead of helping or being even moderately empathetic. 

lights in the rooms don't even work. the place itself is very dirty. and read the contract...the hospital forces you to sign an agreement saying if they **** up in any way, you foot the bill. we came here because it was an emergency and it was close to home. now we will drive the extra half hour to ceder just to avoid this deathtrap.

this was the worst hospital stay!!!! go somewhere else!!!

they literally forgot about me for over 24 hours!!! they also misdiagnosed me, which was brutal. the whole stay was awful. the iv in my hand left a scar and was extremely painful damaging my vein. i kept asking them for extra blankets, which they refused me due to my fever until it turned out....the air conditioning knob was installed incorrectly so when it said it was off, it was actually on high! i had 104.3 fever with high a/c on me and 1 hospital blanket. ridiculous! if my friend hadn't gotten me balloons we would have never been able to prove it. when they forgot about me, they didn't do any vital checks, didn't feed me, and i even ran out of toilet paper/extras, to which i had to call the nurse button from the bathroom - humiliating. there was also no remote for the tv in my room so i had to stand up and walk over to the tv with my iv bag every time i wanted to turn it on/off, volume up/down, or change the channel. really ridiculous. also, they don't have full time doctors on staff here. they have doctors from other professions come in, so i had a doctor, who was technically a sleep doctor, that would only come in after 11pm (when i finally got to sleep and was getting some rest), and then he was gone within the half hour. i learned this because when he misdiagnosed me, and i called the front desk to ask questions (within 10 minutes), they told me he was already gone and couldn't talk to me about it the next day, which i said was unacceptable. i'm lucky i made it through my stay there. my first hospital stay and it was absolutely the worst. the staff is bad, the doctors are bad, the facilities are somehow even worse. go somewhere else!!!

my visit today was not what i expected. i like to come here because the times that i have needed an er , so no one plans to tell me other ers are closed and this hospital is swamped taking in all of the other patients...... 
6 hrs for nothing

ughh. when i was there it was awful.  i think the mental health iop is a drop-off point for  l.a. county jail inmates who are required to take  therapy as a part of their probation.  jesus.  there are these menacing street gang jailbird type women there  that like to play "let's bully the newcomers", and the feckless staff doesn't seem to mind.  i stayed there for longer than i probably should have.  i complained  about the bullshit middle school harangue i was getting from the "mean girls"  ("don't sit there! so and so sits there!; assigning themselves lunch monitor duty and accusing me of leaving a mess at the coffee machine, etc), and i got gaslighted.  that is what an incompetent "care" center does.  avoid if you value your sanity.

dr. payam shadi most compassionate doctor i've ever had the pleasure of knowing. he has been my primary doctor for over 8 years. he is incredibly knowledgeable, caring, compassionate, and he exceeds all expectations. he is kind and professional with a bedside manner that puts one at ease. he is also very responsive, helping me with time-sensitive questions and issues when they arise. thank you dr. shadi for everything you have done for me and my family. i highly recommend dr. shadi, he forever touches the lives of all of his patients.

terrible place, it's dangerous. i had a friend here a few times and their negligence despite knowing she had cancer resulted in it spreading. they did not treat her for it and would not schedule any appointments as they "don't have" social workers. save the life of yourself or your loved one and go somewhere else.

chesapeake regional medical center is a pretty decent hospital. i've never actually been a patient but i've taken family members here and visited friends and relatives on many occasions over the years. i have also visited this hospital countless times during all hours of the day and night in the course of my job duties. all the staff and employees i've encountered have been friendly and professional. things don't always move at the pace one would desire but that's kind of par for the game in the healthcare industry. 

the hospital is always very clean and organized. they seem to have all the latest and greatest equipment and plenty of knowledgeable and competent staff to use it. hospital walls can be thick so i always appreciate the free wi-fi available throughout the facility. signage is good so you can easily find your way and parking is pretty decent. i've never had an issue finding a parking spot. if you are in need of quality healthcare i can recommend this hospital.
this hospital sucks rude staff nurses are very rude doctors sucks i would rather die next time i go to this hospital again

i went to the hospital recently on a saturday afternoon after work, i thought i had a bad rash from a antibiotic, it was on my backside so i could not see it. turns out it was a major infection from a small wound that i did not know about or any clue how i got it. so instead of the two hour wait i was figuring on i was admitted and spent five days getting major antibiotics. all the nurses were great, i was able to joke and laugh with them, my doctor came in everyday to check on me and see how i was doing. it was boring of course but the tv was ok, only problem i had the entire time was a room mate from hell, but as all the beds were occupied there was little they could do. i did not have to wait long in the er, it only took about a hour to get a room, luckily the room mate didn't arrive until the next evening. other than the room mate the only thing that was annoying was the alarm on my bed so i couldn't get up to go to the bathroom whenever i wanted, as i was completely ambulatory it was frustrating but i know that there are rules they have to follow and the nurses and techs have no say in them. as i wasn't in pain and i missed the ice and snow storm it was not a terrible experience.

the 2 stars are because everyone was friendly and fairly quick to see me and get me out of the er. unfortunately, those are really the only positive experiences.
in may of 2018, i went to the er and was seen quickly. x-rays were taken of my lungs and a diagnosis of left-lung pneumonia was given. however, i've never had pneumonia and didn't know what antibiotic is typical for that. the er doctor prescribed z-pak. i continued to be sick for another week and ended up back in the er. the er doctor on-duty that night was confused as to why the previous doctor gave me z-pak instead of levofloxacin. he mentioned that levofloxacin is the standard for a diagnosis of pneumonia. (so, there went $600+ down the drain on my first visit due to the doctor's error. in addition, after speaking to my cousin who is a physician's assistant, she didn't understand the z-pak prescription either.)
a little over a week ago, i was back in the er for a broken radial head. the er doctor looked like she was in a hurry and overwhelmed. (trust me, i don't think i'm the most important patient with a broken arm.) however, she was so rushed and talked so fast that i didn't really process the information and then she ended it with, "any questions?" i was just perplexed and i said, 
"i guess not...???" also, i *think* she said i had multiple fractures (i don't know, she rushed through it so fast) which i later found out at the orthopedic specialist that was untrue. i just have a bitter taste in my mouth. i will go to another er next time i have an emergency.

when my child was taken to the er in fairfield california for what would be the first day of new lifelong diagnosis, i insisted that he be transferred to ucd children's hospital. the northbay er doc refused (he wanted to send him to oakland children's hospital) but i am so glad that i insisted. i knew that this hospital has received a lot of awards for care and i only wanted to best for my child. my son received wonderful care from the nurses and doctors at ucd. the nurse was very respectful of my son's independence and encouraged him to give his own shots. we got to see are specialist that we ended up staying with for the past  7 years (my son adores  lindsey loomba-albrecht, m.d. and alex the dietician).the room was clean, spacious, and our care was excellent. my only complaint was having to share a room. the other little guy was in so much pain and he cried often so it was hard to get rest. thank you ucd pediatric unit-we will never forgot our stay there.

first let me start off with the positives: i'm glad this hospital exists.

if you need it to go to the hospital, and this was your only option, go ahead.

customer service in certain departments is stellar. in other departments it really stinks.

the lobby has a gross, dirty, overcrowded vibe.

when you go to other floors, the gross vibe does go away, but at times it does still have that old musky appearance to it.

again, it's a hospital. the requirements to be a doctor anywhere, including here, are rigorous. i'm not sure you can blame the staff themselves for the behavior and life situations of their clientele.

the staff in the express care clinic in this hospital are some of the worst.
prior to arrival, i looked up the services that are provided by the clinic and it was the closest hospital to me in that moment so i said, why not? 
when i arrived, the nurse/assistant who's meant  to help me is on his phone, that's already a no. 
i inform him what i'm feeling and he takes me into a room to take my vitals and he informs me that they can't help me there and that i have to go to the emergency room? 
excuse me? he didn't even try to help me out, just ushered me out.
what's the point of an express care clinic if you're just going to send the patients to the emergency room?  
so disappointed and angered by the treatment of this clinic in lincoln hospital.

pray you are never in a car accident with lincoln hospital as the closest trauma center. it took me calling the adn after being here for 5 hours, 3 hours of which i got s new nurse. it took 3 hours and me calling the adn, for me to actually meet my nurse. when i mentioned to the clerk that i been in that section for 2.5 hours, her response was, "you're in an emergency room, what do you expect."

i've been a cancer patient since 2012. after brain radiation in december, my brain became swollen and i lost use of my left side, sort of like a stroke. i spent 12 hours in 2 different ers before being admitted on nye at 11:30 pm. dr. wong added a medication to my chart that i was not taking and, in fact, hadn't been discussed with me. he indicated i needed an "acute neuro rehab" but i learned after 8 days that i'd been passed over by every rehab, due to said medication. i was shipped off to a rank, nasty nursing home where i got no rehab and was physically assaulted by a nurse, only after calling the head of case management to have the medication removed from my chart. all your medical records are available electronically to other facilities. 

after that nightmare, and my leg continuing to atrophy, i returned to dr. wong's office mid january for readmission. this time i was smart enough to bring a witness. the doctor made specific representations that he made a mistake putting that medication in my chart and assured me he knew an oncologist at ri hospital where i could get both the acute neuro rehab and the medication he wanted me to start. so i went back in, 2 weeks later no placement and i was offered another nursing home, meanwhile my left leg was completely atrophied. i went home to get nursing, ot, and pt. dr. wong clearly misrepresented his ability to place me and i had to force myself out. 

after getting services at home, i was still falling and injuring myself. dr. wong dumped my care on dr. meghan shea because he knew he royally messed up. she also assured me she would get me the help i needed if i was readmitted. after spending 19 hours in the er, i was placed on the wrong floor and then moved. once again, no appropriate placement was found after staying days and days on end. i now have anxiety attacks, which i never had before. i was shipped off to another nursing home, where i was promised physical therapy on my useless left leg. the place was set up only for elderly patients, the "physical therapy" was less than i'd done at home and the one bike had 4-5 people waiting to use it at any given time!

i have so much more negative things to say about my three stays in 3 months, pt made a false report, patient services and case management were useless and i never got the orthopedic consult i'd been asking for since january. dr. wong's fellow assured me with appropriate therapy, i'd be on my feet in a month. it's now been 5 months and i'm still on a walker and unable to do almost anything. yet, they billed a fortune to insurance for virtually no care and allowing my leg to atrophy to the point it still doesn't work over the course of 3 hospitalizations.

this is long but bare with me. this place stereotypes people with mental health history. this is strictly for their er doctors and er intake nurses (some). i have past heart problems which were corrected in high school. i was feeling close to the same way the first time i had my heart episode and went to the er in mid november. i went in for heart palpitations, shortness of breath, extreme lethargic about to pass out feeling, and weakness. when i was taken to the er by my boyfriend, because who wants to call an ambulance on their lunch break in their work parking garage and drawl that kind of attention to themselves, when i got there, the intake nurses literally did not fucking care i existed as a human. it took the nurses or security guards who help wheel people in and out to tell them to open the door and let me in. the er intake nurse didn't give rats a$$ that i couldn't breath well, didn't pay attention to my boyfriend who was literally handing her an emergency card i keep in my wallet of all my allergies and medical history. my boyfriend told them my symptoms, they didn't even think about hooking me up to a ekg until i was in the er exam room, which if i can remember correctly was about 15 to 20 minutes after i arrived. the nurses were ok that day and the nurse who put my iv in kept moving it because she couldn't get the blood out...ok we'll go somewhere else?! so much pain while feeling like i could pass out. 

next the doctor comes in. talks about my symptoms, some history, so on. the moment i mentioned i was on an anti depressant with past history of anxiety, it switched his questions. it went from asking about how i was feeling physically to asking me if i was stressed, or sad, or anxious...so on with the other related questions. look, doc, i know the difference between heart problems and an anxiety attack, this is not an anxiety attack. so instead of ordering more tests he gives me an anti anxiety med, and let's me chill out for an hour or so. of course a anxiety med like xanax is going to chill me out and slow down my heart and breathing. been on them before in high school and anyone who has a friend in their residency at a top tier hospital can tell you, "yea that med is going to make your heart slow down and relax any symptoms." never once consulted a on staff cardiologist or offering to wait to have one come down because of my past history. given my previous heart problem, if anyone remotely understands the heart knows that things can come back and not in the same way as before!!! after this i was discharged and told if i have any more symptoms to come back. 

the next day and a half i slept, no joke, 18 hours out of a 24 hour day. i could still feel heart beats skip, still had shortness of breath just doing small things like going up stairs or even getting up to go to the bathroom. i didn't want to eat or even talk. so after a day and a half of not feeling like a functioning person, i went back.

this time the intake nurses took me seriously, hooked me up to ekg right away, and got an iv in me right away. this doctor took me seriously and ordered a ct with contrast to check for blood clots and did a few blood pressure tests based on laying and standing. everything came back normal. the moment i knew she looked at the most recent visit, started the, "are you sure you're not anxious," questions came out. in my head i'm thinking, "are you flipping kidding me?! does no one take me seriously?!" the one thing i will never forget the doctor saying to me is, " if you are feeling bad and don't get answers the first time, you shouldn't come back to the er. go see the doctors we referred you to the first time." i'm sorry what!????! i was literally doing what the discharge papers said. it's not my problem ( well kinda is if i die from not well examined heart issue) if you didn't exhaust all your resources to help or passed me along because you gave up. i started to cry. the only person who gave me hope was the nurse. she literally ask me, "do you feel safe to go home?" i flat out started crying, and said no. and told her i would never return here for any emergency. i told her i rather drive to a further hospital and die on the way, than come to this hospital again. she took that seriously and comforted me. i was discharged sent home waiting to see a cardiologist 2 weeks later. 

that cardiologist was pissed no one consulted a cardiologist on staff. i got an eco, heart monitor for a week, and a stress test, i have a problem with my sinus node and will need to have surgery. something that could have been solved and found in that moment if someone didn't profile me as a depressed anxious person!!! 

seriously, tell your doctors to stop stereotyping people with mental health problems. stop thinking that someone with a valid history of cardiac problems and a mental health past is just making it up and is just "anxious."
